english: Uneven ground or variations in soil texture cause water to drain away from higher, sandy spots while collecting in low-lying areas with thicker clay soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ejaaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsakemɔi haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋã hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ebua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shikpɔŋ sũi ni mli edɔ waa yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen nutrients in the soil or is sitting in stagnant water that isn't letting the roots breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu ni ekã shi ni haaa shishifãi lɛ amu.

english: Why do some crop varieties grow taller and produce better in other regions than on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ fe miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different plant varieties are bred for specific weather and soil conditions; a seed variety that thrives in wet, cool regions might struggle in dry or hot local soils.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi anaa. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my plants if I sow seed grains too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leading to thin stalks and small, weak grain yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Is it better to plant rice seeds directly into the ground or grow them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raising seedlings in a nursery gives young plants a strong, healthy start so they can resist weeds better when transplanted into the main field, though direct seeding saves labor.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli moŋ.

english: Why do crops grow stronger when the soil is plowed deep with a machine instead of just cleared by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa waa kɛ́ akɛ tsɔnei tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni akɛ niji tsu nii lɛ?

english: Plowing deeply with a machine breaks up hard underground soil layers, allowing crop roots to grow deep, breathe easily, and absorb nutrients buried beneath the surface.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, amɛmuɔ mlɛo, ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni afu yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants already fully adapted to your soil, so they drink up moisture and nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain rot or get moldy soon after I collect it from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miifite loo ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Grain rots if it is harvested while still damp or stored without proper sun-drying, as internal moisture attracts mold and insects that spoil the crop.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa baafite kɛji akpa be mli ni edɔ lolo loo akɛto ni hulu lɛ egbiko. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, or heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can feed its growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ enɛ waa, ni eha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii etsɔ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that plant loves and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts puts good nutrients back into the land and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahelai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and fragile root systems that burn easily under strong heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees shields young cocoa from the hot sun and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to clear away the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, act like extra mouths to feed and steal water and soil nutrients from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows large, healthy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabu krokomɛi ni boteɔ mli ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ aduawai agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei he hiaa tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make their food through leaves exposed to sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight while keeping the leaves dry, which prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato tsei hoɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting instead of spreading flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites, aphids, or whiteflies feeding on the sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ latɛs lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long without good drainage, creating conditions for soil fungi to attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping soil moisture steady through regular watering helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli Sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds growing near my crops make my crop yield so much smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to build strong stems and produce big yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu lɛ baaje onibii amli waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so I do not waste it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Bɔni afee ni akafite lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when plants are actively growing and the soil is moist, usually early in the morning or after a gentle rain. Applying fertilizer to completely dry soil or right before a heavy downpour wastes it because it burns roots or washes away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli leebi maŋkpa loo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni eeeha amɛshã loo amɛho lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds in the field so they grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plant maize seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart within a row, with rows separated by about 75 centimeters. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ ŋmãa mli. Gbalamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ aaafee sɛntimita 75. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rainy season begins in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje tsei afeemɔ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady and the soil is moist to about a hand's depth. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot, rainless week follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛɛ aaafee tso kome ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: Plants intentionally curl or droop their leaves during extreme heat to reduce water loss through evaporation. As long as the soil has moisture and the plants recover by evening, this is a normal defense behavior.
ga: Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ, Enɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni akɛbuɔ he.

english: What is the purpose of the tassel at the top of my corn plant and the soft silks on the corn ear?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The tassel produces pollen, and the silks catch that pollen so seeds can form on the cob. If the silks do not receive enough pollen from the tassels, your harvest will have cobs missing many kernels.
ga: Tasel lɛ jieɔ pollen. Ni siliki lɛ mɔ̃ɔ pollen lɛ koni dumɔwui anyɛ afee yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji siliki lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli Okpamɔ lɛ hu baaha ŋmeii babaoo ahi shi ni dumɔwui bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, light, and root space directly from your main crops. Clearing weeds during the first four to six weeks of crop growth prevents them from starving your plants during their most critical stage.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hɔmɔ akaye otsei lɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Growing them alongside or in rotation with maize acts as a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for your crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa yɛ masɛi loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my soil is fertile enough to support healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains organic matter or earthworms. Pale, sandy, or hard-baked clay soils often need compost or manure to improve crop yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ŋã, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating ragged holes in the center of my young corn plants; what are they doing?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko ni miiye bu ko ni efo yɛ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ. Mɛni amɛfeɔ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys crop leaves and central shoots. You can control them by inspecting plants early, picking them off by hand on small farms, or applying recommended treatments early in their growth.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ baa ni fiteɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛteŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ mra. Ni akɛ niji baakpa yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli loo akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ

english: How do I stop insects from destroying my harvested grain while it is stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry the grain thoroughly in the sun until the seeds are hard before storing them. Keeping the storage area clean, using airtight bags, or applying safe grain-preservation dust prevents storage pests like weevils from eating your harvest.
ga: Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwraa kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛto. He ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he tsemɔ Vacuum bags ni akɛtsuɔ nii Aloo sũ ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii akaye onibii.

english: Why are my crop seedlings starting to fail when they are only three to five months old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ beni amɛye nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Very young plants are fragile and can easily suffer from soil nutrient imbalance, pest damage, or root burn caused by applying harsh, uncomposted fertilizers or improper care early in their life cycle.
ga: Tsei bibii waa lɛ waaa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna amanehulu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. loo shishifãi ni shãa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli baa. loo kwɛmɔ ni esaaa yɛ shihilɛ mli shishijee fãi lɛ amli

english: Why is it important to keep weeds away from my crops during their first few months of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsi jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In the early months, young crops have small root systems and need all available sunlight, water, and soil nutrients; weeds will easily outcompete them and stunt their growth.
ga: yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia amɛ. Ewaaa akɛ jwɛi yeɔ amɛnɔ kunim ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why did my land produce high yields three years ago, but now my crop yields are decreasing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo yibii babaoo afii etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ? Shi amrɔ nɛɛ ani minitsumɔ lɛ eba shi?

english: Farming the same land continuously draws nutrients out of the earth. Without replacing those nutrients through compost, crop rotation, or proper fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if I am applying too much chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miitsu nii tsɔ?

english: Using too much chemical fertilizer can burn the roots of young plants, turn the leaves yellow or brown at the edges, and ruin the natural balance of your soil over a few seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ yɛ bei 2-3 mli.

english: How can I revive my soil after farming it continuously for four years?
ga: Yɛ afii 4 ni akɛduɔ nii daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore exhausted soil by adding organic compost, growing nitrogen-fixing cover crops like beans, or leaving the land to rest for a season so it can naturally recover nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi, tamɔ ŋmeii, loo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be kome koni enyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it safe to use pig manure directly on my vegetable and crop farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ kpootoo fɔmɔ baatsu nii yɛ mi aduawai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh pig manure is strong and can burn plant roots or introduce harmful pests and bacteria. It must be composted and decomposed properly over time before applying it to your soil.
ga: Kplotoo ŋmei hee mli wa ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui aba. Esa akɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli dani abaanyɛ akɛwo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I prevent farm animals like pigs from damaging my growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi, tamɔ tsinabii anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ?

english: Fencing off farmland or constructing designated pens for livestock keeps animals from compacting the soil, digging up crop roots, or destroying young plants.
ga: Fɛnsi ni atswaa yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kponɔ loo kooloi ashihilɛhei pɔtɛɛ amamɔ Tsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkafee shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛkafo tsei shishifãi, loo amɛkafite tsei bibii.

english: Why should I process harvested crops like oil palm into oil instead of selling raw crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tamɔ ŋmei fɔ lɛ mafee fɔ moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ?

english: Processing raw crops into products like oil increases your profit margins, creates a product that lasts longer without spoiling, and gives you more control over market prices.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ ni ooofee nibii tamɔ fɔ lɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Bɔɔ nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee. ni ehaa onáa hewalɛ babaoo yɛ jarayeli jara nɔ.

english: What equipment do I need to start processing my harvest into oil on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii he hiaa mi koni manyɛ mabɔi mu nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ?

english: To process crops into oil, you generally need basic processing tools such as a mechanical press or digester, heating units for boiling, and clean, airtight containers for storage.
ga: yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni afee mu lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni he hiaa bo ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ compactor loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nibii amli lɛ he miihia bo. Heating unit kɛha shãa kɛ tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ.

english: How do I keep my oil palm fruits healthy so they yield a lot of oil after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-oil palm yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni maná fɔ babaoo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ensuring crops get adequate potassium in the soil and harvesting the fruit bunches at full ripeness guarantees maximum oil content and quality during extraction.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni akpa aduawai akui lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha mu ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba mli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits when the heat becomes too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants get stressed and their pollen becomes sterile. Without proper pollination, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than producing weak fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni pollen lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun, which stops them from losing too much water through evaporation until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ tsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants look completely droopy at noon but stand firm again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi koni edamɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Once the sun goes down and heat decreases, the plant catches up on drinking water and perks back up.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni latsaa lɛ ba shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots spread so quickly on my tomato leaves when the weather is warm and damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures combined with moisture create the ideal condition for fungal diseases to multiply and attack leaf tissue rapidly.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni hulutsoo be fata he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛtutua baa lɛ mli fãji oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive under full, direct sunlight and heat. They require shade trees like plantains to shelter them from burning sun rays during their early growth stages.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi?

english: Excess nutrients or high foliage growth can cause cassava to direct all its energy into growing top leaves rather than storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Niyenii babaoo loo baai ni yaa hiɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do the broad leaves of my plantain trees split naturally into shreds during dry sunny weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ fãa bibii bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally to let hot winds pass through without tearing down the entire plant or causing it to lose excessive water from large unbroken leaf surfaces.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni egbaaa tso lɛ mli loo ekɛ nu babaoo ni jɛɔ baa agbo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ baaa.

english: Will extremely hot soil affect how my pepper seeds germinate after planting?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaná mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ nɔ hewalɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if the soil becomes too hot, it can dry out or damage delicate seeds before they sprout, preventing them from germinating properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Ebaanyɛ egbi loo efite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo dani amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start shooting out green sprouts while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔji be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their resting phase when ambient barn temperatures and moisture levels shift, signaling to the tuber that it is time to start growing a new plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli beni hulutsoo ni ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: How does warm weather affect the time it takes for my hot pepper plants to ripen?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa mi-hot pepper tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Warm conditions speed up the natural biological processes of pepper plants, making them flower and ripen faster as long as they receive adequate water.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ pepper tsei amli lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwereɔ oya, kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients from the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and get yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies that suck juices from the plant leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ Nɔ ni kɛbaa Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a natural protection mechanism to reduce water loss and protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantain trees close to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees easily burn under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I sow the seeds too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the young plants to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, causing them to grow weak and thin with very small fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are getting too much direct sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ?

english: Cocoa trees receiving too much sun will have leaves that burn brown at the edges, dry up, and drop early, leaving the branches bare.
ga: Cacao tsei ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ babaoo lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshã yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Egbiɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya, ni eshiɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ efolo.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients needed during flowering.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my yams without digging them up too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni mikɛfoŋ oya tsɔ?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce weak yields even when rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and space from crop roots before the main crop can feed properly.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli dani tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I work on my cocoa farm during the off-season when there are no pods to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni abaakpa lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds, pruning dead branches, and treating pests during the off-season keeps the trees strong and healthy so they can produce a much larger harvest when the next fruiting season arrives.
ga: weeding Niji ni egboi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ Koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpa nibii babaoo kɛji yibiiwoo be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shɛ.

english: How do I know the best time of year to plant new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the major rainy season so the young plants can build deep roots with plenty of natural water before the hot dry season comes.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo yɔɔ mli dani hulutsoo be mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by a lack of water, poor soil nutrients, too much direct sunlight, or pest attacks, which prevents the flowers from turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo Enɛ haaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Will cutting unnecessary branches off my cocoa tree hurt the tree or reduce my yield?
ga: Ani niji ni he ehiaaa ni mafolɔ kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ yibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches does not hurt the tree; it actually helps sunlight and air flow through the farm, reducing diseases and forcing the tree to put its energy into growing larger pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ efiteee tso lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ. Ha helai aba shi ni onyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do experienced farmers leave big shade trees inside their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shiɔ tsei wuji yɛ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Large shade trees shield delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, help keep moisture in the soil during dry spells, and protect cocoa trees from strong winds.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hɔɔŋ, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, overly shaded conditions where water lingers on pods without drying quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nu lɛ baahi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni egbiŋ oya.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks the strength to produce a good cocoa harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛkpaa kookoo kpakpa?

english: If cocoa tree leaves turn pale yellow, grow slowly, or produce small and few pods despite getting enough rain, the soil is likely low on essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Growing plantains or food crops alongside young cocoa provides shade and early income, but growing heavy-feeding crops too close can compete with young cocoa for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Plantains loo niyenii ni akɛduɔ kɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ shika aba oya. Shi tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ kookoo ni mli wa lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: Why does letting high weeds grow under my cocoa trees lower my cocoa yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa mi-kookoo yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water from cocoa roots, and thick weed growth traps humidity while giving harmful farm pests a safe place to live and multiply.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Ni jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin changes color completely from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange, showing the beans inside have fully matured.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot withstand direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them creates a cool protective cover that keeps the soil moist and shields the young seedlings from burning until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa fɛ̃i ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block sunshine from one another. This competition results in tall, thin stalks with small, poorly filled corn cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa anáa ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a clear sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛwoji lɛ hu afee hewalɛ.

english: Why do elderly farmers say planting beans together with maize helps the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa maŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby crops like maize extra nutrients to grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, naa niyenii krokomɛi koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi aha he ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the sun from evaporating water out of the ground too quickly. It also keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons and stops heavy rainfall from washing away the good topsoil.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars destroy my young corn leaves during the night, but I cannot see them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ? Shi minyɛɛɛ mana yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the funnel of the maize stem during the hot daytime to escape the heat. They come out to feed on the tender leaves at night or early morning when the weather is cool.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛjo latsaa lɛ naa foi. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving the plants steady, regular water and shade helps the flowers stay attached and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with deep, tough root systems that can react immediately to the warm soil and rain. Because they absorb nutrients instantly, clearing them early prevents them from stealing food away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to recover. It also lets soil-borne pests and diseases built up in that specific spot, which reduces your total yield over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he pɔtɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves of the plant naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack open as the tubers expand beneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei edara kɛji tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Pests like root-boring weevils and nematodes eat away the underground bulb and roots of the plantain, weakening its anchor in the soil until the weight of the fruit bunch causes the plant to fall over.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ nematodes ni kɛ shishifãi baa lɛ yeɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi. ni eha ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛyashi aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ baaha tso lɛ akumɔ shi.

english: Where can I get clean and healthy plantain suckers to start my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana plantain tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mikɛje ŋmɔ shishi?

english: You can get disease-free plantain suckers through agricultural extension officers or by using the split-corm technique in a nursery, which ensures you do not transfer pests from old farms to your new land.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná plantain tsei ni hela bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi adɛŋ. Aloo okɛ tuber mligbalamɔ gbɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akajɛ oŋmɔ momo lɛ mli kɛya oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up before the fruit bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai akui lɛ daa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal leaf disease called Black Sigatoka, which destroys the leaves so the plant cannot capture sunlight properly to grow large fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fungal leaf disease ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka, ni fiteɔ baai lɛ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: What causes my plantain farm to produce big fruits during the first harvest but smaller ones in the following years?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii wuji yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ mli shi ewoɔ yibii bibii yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Plantain plants heavy feeders that remove nutrients from the soil quickly, so without adding compost, mulch, or fertilizer after the first harvest, the soil fertility drops and fruit size shrinks.
ga: Dumɔ dumɔwui kɛtsɔ bulk feeders, ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni aduawai lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting oil palm before I can harvest fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mu tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani okpa yibii lɛ?

english: Improved oil palm varieties usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into the field, provided they receive adequate water and weed control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ amɛna nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei fɔ ŋmɔ?

english: Oil palm thrives in deep, rich loamy soil that holds moisture well, gets plenty of sunlight, and does not remain continuously flooded or waterlogged.
ga: Mu tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni mli kwɔ mli. ni haa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Na hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nu afua loo ehiɛɛɛ nu mli daa.

english: How far apart should I plant my oil palm seedlings on my land?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu oil palm dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palm trees should be planted about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern to ensure that the mature fronds do not block sunlight from each other as they grow.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ koni baai ni eda lɛ akatsĩ hulu la lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to process my palm fruits into red oil rather than selling raw fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tso yibii ni afee lɛ fɔ tsuru lɛ hi fe tso yibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Processing palm nuts into oil adds value, allowing you to earn significantly more money per harvest and store the finished oil to sell when market prices rise.
ga: Palm ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ fɔ lɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa. Enɛ haa onáa shika babaoo kɛha okpamɔ lɛ. ni okɛ mu ni agbe naa lɛ ato koni ekɛhɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: How can joining a local Agricultural Department project help me make more profit from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe awo maŋ lɛ mli Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Extension projects give farmers direct access to high-yielding planting materials, modern farming techniques, and organized buyer networks that help lower production costs and boost profits.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni akɛyaa mli lɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ náa nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ. ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akuu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo baa shi ni ehaa sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I protect my young crops from dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli hɔmɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of young plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) retains soil moisture, prevents weeds, and cools the roots during high heat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Tsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is getting too much water from irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize gets too much water, its roots drown because they cannot breathe. You will notice the leaves turning pale yellow, growth slowing down, and the soil staying soggy and smelly.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ emu. Obaayɔse akɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. slow growth Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning while the air is still cool. This allows water to soak deep into the soil for the roots to drink before the heat of the day causes it to evaporate.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa efoɔ.

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand easily. If your soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the roots struggle to push through, causing the tubers to grow misshapen and small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ efite ni eyɛ bibioo.

english: Cassava leaves fold or droop in high heat to protect themselves from losing water. It is a natural defense, and the leaves usually bounce back once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ loo akɛwoɔ la ni mli wa nɔ koni nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight. Instead of spending energy making peppers, the plant uses all its energy to grow tall to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ́ pepper tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee chili peppers Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdara ni ekwɛ ŋwɛi koni ená la lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The tomato plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top so new leaves can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eya nɔ ekwɛ baai heei.

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when stressed by heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. The plant lets go of its flowers to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ latsaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out and burn easily in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them until they are established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛyashi amɛbaatswa amɛhe shi.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and look healthier than the crops I planted in the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be ni ehiɛ yɔɔ fɛo fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally built to grab water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves, and will it kill the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani ebaagbe tso lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which spreads in warm, humid air. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves, weakening the plant if not managed.
ga: Nakai sũ yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning brown in the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees nearby shields young cocoa seedlings, keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist so the leaves do not burn.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni akashã baai lɛ.

english: What is causing holes in my young maize leaves and soft powder inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli kɛ powda ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworms or stemborers eating the plant tissue. Inspecting the crops early and applying neem extract or approved organic sprays can control these caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning light yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and yellowing leaves on cassava plants are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting prevents this virus from spreading in your farm.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ yucca tsei anɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛ́ oodu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks nutrients for growing good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops grow slowly, stems remain thin, and leaves often turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green. Adding compost, manure, or balanced fertilizers restores nutrients and helps crops grow strong.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when I water the soil well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil usually happens because soil-borne fungi or bacteria have entered the plant stems and blocked water flow inside. Rotating tomato plots with non-solanaceous crops like maize helps starve out these soil pathogens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa ejaakɛ ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfiteɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Tomatoi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee ŋmɔshi nibii kome, tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛɛ.

english: Yam vines produce long climbing tendrils that need sunlight to create nutrients for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and reduces the risk of leaf diseases spreading from damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli, ni ebaaha baa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from irregular watering, extreme heat, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady moisture and balanced nutrients keeps flowers attached to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my plantain shoots grow strong while others produce small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi shwereɔ tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Sword suckers with narrow leaves grow from deeper roots and produce large bunches, while water suckers with broad leaves produce weak plants with small bunches. Selecting sturdy sword suckers for planting ensures good yields.
ga: Sword shoots ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ panicles agboi. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nuɔ nu ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ feɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ panicles bibii lɛ. Klante tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ahala kɛha dumɔ haa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn dusty and full of tiny holes after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Dusty maize in storage is a sign of grain weevils eating the stored crop from the inside out. Properly drying grains until they are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags stops insects from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ he okadi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmaa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii akafee babaoo.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow poorly when the water level in the field drops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishi ŋmãa lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice requires consistent shallow water to absorb essential nutrients easily and to keep weeds from smothering the young shoots. Maintaining a steady water level ensures healthy growth and full grain heads.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ biɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ daa koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ oya. kɛ koni jwɛi akatsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa Nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyitsei eyiɔ obɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure or fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly onto my vegetable garden beds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee afata mibɔɔ mli aduawai saatso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and hot for delicate plant roots, which can burn and kill the plants. You need to let it sit and decompose into cool compost for a few weeks before applying it.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa ni edɔ tsɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe tsei Esa akɛ oha eta shi ni efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ejɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight rolls during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, helping them save moisture and avoid drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, which stresses the plant and stops fruit formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear on my maize crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The warm moisture right after rain creates the perfect weather for pest moths to hatch their eggs quickly on young green crop leaves, causing sudden pest outbreaks.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛfɔ oya yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa trukaa lɛ baa

english: Why do experienced farmers say I should plant cowpeas together with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kome lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as natural food for heavy-feeding crops like cassava growing next to them.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei ni haa kooloi niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not like direct, harsh sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. Tall forest trees act like natural shade umbrellas to keep the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Koo mli tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I sow seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak stems and tiny fruits instead of big yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii yɛ yibii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients completely and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target that crop to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds hurt my farm crops if there is still open space between the plants?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lolo?

english: Even if there is open ground, weed roots spread quickly underground to steal water and plant food away from your crops, while also sheltering harmful crop-eating insects.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ moŋ shi jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi oya koni amɛju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu ahe.

english: Why do my crops produce less fruit and grow so slowly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo ni amɛdaraa blɛoo kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need a constant supply of water to transport nutrients from the soil to their leaves and fruits. During the dry season, plants enter a survival mode, slowing down growth and shedding leaves to conserve energy and moisture until water becomes available again.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Amɛhaa amɛdaramɔ baa shi ni amɛshwieɔ baai koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I keep producing fresh vegetables on my farm during the lean months when rain is scarce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ mawo aduawai heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli?

english: You can practice dry-season farming by using simple irrigation methods like drip lines or hand-watering from shallow wells, combined with heavy mulching (covering soil with dried grass) to trap moisture and protect crop roots from heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ drip loo nine ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ nubu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli okwaayeli mli. kɛfata he kɛ jwɛi ni tsii (Mulch with dry grass) koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he.

english: Why do crops like onions grow very well in northern parts of Ghana but struggle to yield in the southern rainy areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ sabolai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ? Shi esa akɛ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛná nibii ni amɛbaadu yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ yɛ anaigbɛ lɛ.

english: Different crops prefer different climates; onions thrive in dry, warm air with low humidity. Southern Ghana's high humidity and heavy rains create too much soil moisture, which causes onion bulbs to rot and encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi. Sabolai daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be fioo yɔɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: I have been planting cassava on the exact same piece of land for two years, so why are my harvests getting smaller every season?
ga: Mikɛ afii enyɔ edu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops with nitrogen-fixing plants like beans or peanuts helps restore soil health and maintain strong yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni mli wa yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and thin instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ mlɛo moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when they hit hard, compacted soil or rocks underground. Building high, loose soil mounds free of stones allows the tubers to expand easily and grow long, smooth, and thick.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni efeɔ kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience severe stress, such as intense heat, lack of water, or a shortage of essential nutrients like phosphorus. Providing shade cloth during peak sun and steady water helps them retain flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo waa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them close under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi?

english: Maize requires full direct sunlight to manufacture energy for cob development. When shaded by big trees, the plant spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach the light instead of filling out its cobs.
ga: Abele he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha cob lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ eyɛ tso agbo ko shishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and turn yellow during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kuku mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water rapidly under hot sun. Curling is the plant's natural defense to reduce sunlight exposure on the leaf surface, while yellowing indicates the plant is pulling nutrients from older leaves to survive.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shi yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihe niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and rot so quickly before I can send them to markets in other towns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes naturally produce ethylene gas as they ripen, which speeds up decay when they are packed tightly in hot, unventilated wooden crates. Harvesting them slightly early at the 'breaker stage' (pink tip) and packing them loosely in ventilated crates extends their shelf life.
ga: Tomato jieɔ ethylene gas kɛji ekwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha fitemɔ aya hiɛ oya kɛ́ akɛwo adekai ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Kpamɔ mra fioo yɛ 'breaker stage' (pink tip) ni okɛwo tsɔne mli ni efee mlɛo. Yɛ adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do pests attack my stored maize much faster during hot weather than during cooler months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ oya kwraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli fe nyɔji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grain pests like weevils reproduce much faster in warm temperatures and high humidity. Storing dried maize in airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects and stops their eggs from hatching.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafɔ.

english: After extracting red oil from my palm fruit, can I make any extra income from the leftover kernels?
ga: Beni ajie mu tsuru ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ani manyɛ maná shika kroko kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, palm kernels contain valuable oil used for making soap and cosmetics. You can dry and sell the cracked nuts to processors or extract palm kernel oil yourself for local markets.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, mu ni jara wa ni akɛfeɔ samla kɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ yɛ tsei ahe. Obaanyɛ ogbi ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo bo diɛŋtsɛ ojie ŋmeii lɛ amli fɔ lɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Can I use the leftover fibrous husks from oil palm processing directly as farm manure?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fiber ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ mu tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to compost the pressed fiber first. Decomposed fiber acts as a rich organic mulch that holds moisture in the soil and slowly releases nutrients back to your crops.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni afee fiber ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Fibers ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ organic mulch ni haa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi fiofio ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi kɛyaa oŋmɔshi nibii amli fiofio.

english: What is the main difference between the red palm oil from the fruit flesh and the oil inside the kernel?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ red palm oil ni jɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ teŋ?

english: Red palm oil comes from the outer flesh and is rich in natural vitamins for cooking, while palm kernel oil comes from the inner seed and is a clearer, harder oil mostly used for soap making and specialty cooking.
ga: Palm fɔ tsuru lɛ jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli, ni adebɔɔ mli vitamini ni akɛhooɔ nii babaoo yɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofa ni ji palm kernel fɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli, ni eji fɔ ni mli tse ni wa. Akɛtsuɔ nii titri kɛfeɔ samla kɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested palm nuts spoil quickly if I leave them stacked on the damp ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sugarcane dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh palm fruit bunches contain high moisture that attracts fungi and generates heat, which degrades the oil quality. Processing or drying them immediately prevents mold and stops the oil from spoiling.
ga: Palm tsei heei yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa. ni haa mu lɛ mli kpakpa baa shi Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo agbiɔ lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ aba ni ehaaa mu lɛ afite.

english: How long will my oil palm seedlings take after planting before I can harvest my first palm nuts?
ga: Beni midu mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani manyɛ makpa mi-palm yibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Improved oil palm varieties typically take 3 to 4 years to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches when given proper weed control, fertilizer, and adequate moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa. Kɛ aha jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce small, empty fruits without solid seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo yibii bibii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui ni wa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms require insect pollinators to transfer pollen to female flowers. Poor pollination or a lack of soil nutrients like potassium leads to underdeveloped fruits without proper kernels.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ ni pollinators lɛ ajie pollen lɛ kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ. Pollination ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my oil palm tree stop producing fresh fruit bunches during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ harmath be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms need steady water to form new flower spikes and swell their fruits. During severe dry spells, the tree conserves energy by pausing fruit production until the rains return.
ga: Nu he miihia mu tsei lɛ daa koni amɛfee fɔfɔi heei ni amɛwo yibii lɛ amli. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli Tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ aduawai ni amɛkpaa yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting oil palm trees far apart instead of close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu mu tsei yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fe he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Oil palms produce wide fronds that need full sunlight. Planting them about 9 meters apart prevents trees from shading one another, ensuring each palm gets enough sun to yield heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni biɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 9 kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ akatsi amɛhe naa. Ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii ni tsii.
