english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm turning yellow and drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a shortage of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or severe water stress during long dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: I noticed my young oil palm tree produces male and female flowers separately. Do I need to plant specific male trees to get fruits?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Ani ehe miihia ni madu tsei ni ji hii pɛ koni maná yibii?

english: No, a single oil palm tree naturally produces both male and female flower cycles at different times. Planting your trees in a group allows wind and insects to carry pollen between them naturally.
ga: Dabi, mu tso kome pɛ baawo fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important for me to till my land before planting cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani miduɔ kaabii?

english: Tilling breaks up hard, packed dirt so air and water can soak deep into the ground. It makes the soil soft, allowing young cabbage roots to spread easily and buries weeds that would otherwise steal food from your crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbálaa muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa cabbage shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo. ni ofu jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Should I mix dried animal manure into my farm soil while preparing it for cabbage?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi afutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni misaa kaabe lɛ?

english: Yes, adding well-rotted manure or compost during land preparation enriches the soil with natural nutrients and helps the ground hold onto water longer, giving young cabbage seedlings a healthy, fast start.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ aya hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa kaabe dumɔwui bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi mra.

english: How far apart should I plant my cabbage seedlings on the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kaabii dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting seedlings about 30 to 45 centimeters apart gives each cabbage plant enough room for its roots to feed and its large outer leaves to spread out so it can form a big, solid head.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 30 kɛyashi 45 lɛ, ehaa kabaaji tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye nii. ni kponɔgbɛ baai agboi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ yitso agbo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Does cabbage need full sunlight to grow well in Ghana?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be fɛɛ he miihia cabbage koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana?

english: Cabbage grows best when it gets plenty of direct sunlight every day, which gives it energy to grow thick leaves. However, during very hot days, the soil must be kept moist so the sun doesn't dry out or wilt the plants.
ga: Cabbage daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji enine shɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa gbi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi, yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekagbi loo eha tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: How do I tell if my cabbage crop needs more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo he miihia mi-cabbage tsei lɛ?

english: If the top layer of soil feels dry and dusty when you press it with your finger, or if the leaves look soft and droopy in the morning before the sun gets too hot, your cabbage needs watering.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni eyɛ sũ beni okɛ onine nyɛɔ nɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛgbee shi leebi dani hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ehe miihia ni awo o-cabbage lɛ nu.

english: Why do weeds harm my cabbage so much even after the cabbages have grown large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-cabbage lɛ awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ cabbage lɛ miida momo lɛ?

english: Weed roots are very aggressive and silently steal water and fertilizer from under the ground, while high weeds block sunlight from reaching the cabbage leaves, causing the heads to stay small.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dioo. yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ kaabe baai lɛ ahe. ha yitso lɛ afee bibioo

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves and why is that bad for the crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-cabbage leaf lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ enáa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii lɛ?

english: Holes are usually made by small insects like caterpillars eating the leaves. This hurts the cabbage because the plant relies on whole leaves to capture sunlight and build energy to form a firm head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Enɛ yeɔ kaabii lɛ awui ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ baa muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la ni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni ekɛfee yitsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing wide leaves but failing to form a hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa lɛ mli kwɔ shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This often happens if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil, if the weather is extremely hot, or if the plants were planted too close together, forcing them to focus on leaves instead of forming a center head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa Aloo kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee bulb ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ.

english: How do I know when my cabbage is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni cabbage lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cabbage is ready when the center head feels firm and solid when you squeeze it gently. In Ghana, most cabbages are ready to harvest between 2 to 3 months after transplanting the seedlings.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ efee klalo kɛji akɛ yitso ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ blɛoo. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, kaabaji babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 teŋ beni ajie dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it fine for me to plant cabbage on the exact same bed every season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu kaabii yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi?

english: It is better to rotate cabbage with other crops like maize or beans because growing cabbage repeatedly in the exact same spot allows cabbage-loving pests and soil diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake kaabii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Yɛ kaabii ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ hewɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kooloi ni sumɔɔ kaabii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need partial shade from faster-growing crops like plantains or shade trees, which act as living umbrellas to keep the young trees cool and moist until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass and leaves on the soil surface around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ashwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ? mi ŋmɔshi nibii

english: This practice is called mulching. Spreading dry organic material covers the soil like a blanket, which stops the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same field as my maize help my maize yield a better harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the special natural ability to pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it directly into the soil. The neighboring maize feeds on this extra soil nitrogen to grow bigger and produce better ears.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Side corn baaye sũ mli nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ koni ekwɛ tsei wuji ni ekɛ toi kpakpai aba.

english: Why is it important to plant cassava stem cuttings with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmeii ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds along the stalk that determine where new branches and leaves will sprout. If you plant them upside down, the plant wastes crucial energy trying to curve its stems back toward the sun, leading to weak growth and fewer tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii ni tsɔɔ he ni niji kɛ baai heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛya hulu lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa waa, ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ hu faaa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes allows maximum sunlight reaching the plant, which sends energy down to make huge tubers in the earth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ he. ni tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo ko yɛ je lɛŋ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often shed their flowers when the plants experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and ensuring proper plant spacing helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛma shi tamɔ tomato.

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves and dirt-like powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ ebaai lɛ amli kɛ powda ni tamɔ muji yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant during the day to feed on young leaves. Checking your field early in the morning and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnel controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baai lɛ amli lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites hiding on the undersides of leaves. These pests suck the sap out of the plant and spread viruses, causing the leaves to twist and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops look wilted and limp in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground, so they droop to protect themselves. If they bounce back in the evening when it cools down, it is a natural self-defense mechanism, but deep watering at the root level helps them stay hydrated longer.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ be mli ni edɔ lɛ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Shi nu ni oooha amɛ kɛya shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni amɛná nu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is ready and good enough to start planting maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni ehi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Look at the color and feel of the soil, as well as the wild plants growing there. Dark, loose soil that holds moisture without staying soaked like a swamp is rich in nutrients and ready for planting.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni enuɔ he ehaa. Nɔ ni fata he ji koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli ni esa akɛ adu

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up and look wilted during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in intense heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. As long as the soil has moisture and the leaves perk back up by evening, the plant is just protecting itself from the hot sun.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do farmers around here plant cassava and maize together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ biɛ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together makes the best use of your land and time. Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the field after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ kɛ be tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii 2 kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves of my young cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi-kaaba tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars or beetles feeding on them. Checking under the leaves early in the morning allows you to catch these pests before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baa lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the corn plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important food for growth. When food in the soil runs low, the plant moves nitrogen from its old lower leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving them steady water and protecting them from severe heat helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha amɛ nu daa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my yam plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi beni mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young yam plants have weak roots at first. If weeds grow around them early on, the weeds will steal all the sunlight, water, and food from the soil, preventing the yam tubers from expanding.
ga: Sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close, their roots fight each other underground for space and water. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko kɛ nu. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I test if my saved bean seeds are good before I waste time planting them in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji ŋmeii ni ato lɛ hi dani maŋɔ be kɛdu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Wrap ten seeds in a wet cloth and keep it damp inside a dark place for three days. If seven or eight seeds sprout small roots, your seeds are healthy and good for field planting.
ga: Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ dumɔwui nyɔŋma he ni okɛto he ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ gbii etɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui kpawo loo kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ shishifãi bibii Odumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛhi kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why should I wait for two good rains before planting seeds at the start of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a dry season often dries up quickly, leaving the hot soil to scorch young seeds. Waiting for two steady rains ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni eshã dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so I do not waste my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Koni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite?

english: Cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange when they are fully ripe. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside have fully developed sugar content for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa nɛɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar ni fa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa.

english: What will happen to my cocoa crop if I delay harvesting the pods for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ sɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Delaying harvest causes beans to germinate inside the pod, which destroys their market quality. Overripe pods also rot on the branch and attract diseases like Black Pod that quickly spread to healthy trees.
ga: Nikpamɔ be lɛ ni akɛbaa sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni fiteɔ jarayelihe lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsobii ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ hu fiteɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ ni egbalaa helai tamɔ tsei diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I use a sharp knife or cutlass to break open my harvested cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni mli wa tsuɔ nii? loo tsɔne kuku ni akɛgbeleɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ

english: Using a sharp blade can easily slice the cocoa beans inside, which ruins their appearance and allows mold to grow during fermentation. Using a heavy wooden stick or blunt tool opens the pod safely without damaging the beans.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Abaanyɛ afo kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mlɛo. Enɛ baafite bɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Ni ŋmeii baanyɛ adara yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tso ni tsii loo nibii ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii Ebaagbele ŋmeii lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does harvesting cocoa take so much physical care compared to other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ni akpaa lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ kwɛmɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods must be cut carefully off the trunk with a sharp tool without damaging the flower cushion beneath the stalk. Damaging this cushion prevents the tree from growing new flowers and pods in future seasons.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ dɛŋdade ni mli wa afo kookoo tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni efiteee fɔfɔi akutso ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Kushɛ nɛɛ ni afiteɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, a fungal infection caused by excess humidity and lack of sunlight. Regular weeding and pruning unwanted branches allow air and light into the farm to stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do very tiny, young cocoa pods dry up and turn dark before they ever grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as 'cherelle wilt.' It is often a natural way for the cocoa tree to shed extra pods it cannot feed due to insufficient water or nutrients in the soil.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ ‘cherelle wilt’ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ atsu he nii yɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing flowers but failing to grow into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ cacao ŋmɔji diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers. If the farm is too dry, lacks leaf litter where midges live, or has been sprayed heavily with harsh chemicals, poor pollination prevents pod formation.
ga: Kookoo tsei yeɔ kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ Baai amli jwɛi bɛ he ni kooloi lɛ hiɔ lɛ. aloo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa miifɔ nɔ Pollination ni ehiii lɛ tsiɔ pod feemɔ naa.

english: Why is it important to check on my cocoa farm regularly instead of waiting until harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Frequent visits allow you to spot early signs of pests, diseases, or nutrient shortages while they are small. Catching problems early prevents major losses and makes farm maintenance much easier and cheaper.
ga: Saramɔi ni yaa nɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa onaa mra be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he okadii lɛ yɔɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Naagbai ni ayɔseɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nibii wuji ni elaaje lɛ anaa. Ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni ejara waaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Yellowing usually means the plants need temporary shade crops like plantain or shade trees to protect them while they establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni abu tsei ahe beni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does pruning branches actually help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches so the tree sends its energy and nutrients directly to pod growth. It also opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can circulate, reducing disease risks.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni tso lɛ atsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya tsei niji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ hu koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. ni haa helai srɔtoi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away, preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or dry, or when the plant lacks key soil nutrients like phosphorus, causing stress that stops fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni ekɛ haomɔ ni haa aduawai lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the dirt when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive rain leaves water trapped in the soil around cassava roots, cutting off oxygen and encouraging root-rot diseases that cause the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni enɛ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa lɛ baa.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when there is standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa beni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in flooded fields because standing water blocks weed growth, keeps soil temperature steady, and keeps plant nutrients dissolved for easy root absorption.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ ahi shi daa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa saplings die when I clear all the tall trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Mashi miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller trees to protect their fresh leaves from harsh sunlight and retain soil moisture; direct sun burns young saplings before they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni ebu baai heei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã tsei bibii dani amɛdara.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in tall, weak stalks that cannot produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to place wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to make food; staking keeps leaves clean, prevents diseases from damp soil, and allows underground tubers to grow larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ he tseɔ. Tsĩɔ helai anaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree, which leads to smaller bunches and takes much longer for fruit to mature.
ga: Suckers loo shoots babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain wulu lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha niji lɛ afee bibii, ni ebaahe be babaoo dani aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bloom above the ground but the nuts mature under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant sends down long stems called pegs that push into the dirt, where the nuts can grow safely hidden from sun and pests.
ga: Beni tso lɛ ekɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beans lɛ baanyɛ adara shweshweeshwe ni hulu la loo kooloi gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my pepper leaves more quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids reproduce much faster in warm, dry weather and feed on leaf sap to get water, which dries out and weakens pepper plants quickly.
ga: Kplukai, tamɔ aphids, fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni oye baai lɛ amli nu lɛ koni ona nu Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ agbi oya ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to protect them from intense heat while their roots settle into the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and rot during the peak of the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain makes the soil waterlogged, which prevents air from reaching the root system. When cassava roots cannot breathe, the plant reacts by shedding its leaves to survive the excess wetness.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the branch before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp environments. Pruning heavy leaves and branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and keep the fungus away.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji kɛ baai ni tsii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose all their flowers before any fruits start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fɛɛ miifite dani yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to sudden heat stress or unpredictable soil moisture. Maintaining steady watering and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa latsaa loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ he. Kɛ́ afɔ nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves show that the soil is low in nitrogen, a vital food for leafy growth. The plant pulls nutrients from its older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the leaves above ground look healthy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: If the soil is too hard or contains too much leaf-boosting nutrients, the plant invests all its energy into growing top leaves instead of pushing roots outward to store food.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa baai lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeetsi eshishifãi lɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ato.

english: Why do my corn stalks fall over easily after a short storm or strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya yɛ ahum kuku loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn stalks fall when their supporting roots are planted too shallowly. Heap soil around the base of the stems (mounding) to anchor the plant firmly against strong winds.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Okɛ sũ abɔle tsei lɛ ashishi (pile) koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to fruit than those on neighboring farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plantains require massive amounts of water and nutrients. If weeds are stealing their food or dead leaves aren't cleared away, the stem grows slowly and delays fruiting.
ga: Plantains biɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo babaoo. Kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii loo ajieee baai ni egboi lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daaa fiofio ni ehaa yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do weeds come back so much faster than my planted crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weed seeds are already resting in the soil and are naturally adapted to grow instantly with moisture, drinking up water and sunlight before young domestic crops can catch up.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui miijɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. Ni atsake lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eda amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, nu kɛ hulu la dani maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he.

english: How does leaving dry leaves and grass around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni mishiɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering soil with dried plant matter (mulching) acts like an umbrella that holds moisture in the soil, blocks weed seeds from receiving sunlight, and feeds the soil as it rots.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like NPK will restore the green color and improve your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: How do cowpea plants help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina tsei aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant's sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil solution or an appropriate insecticide early helps protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem fɔ mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is under severe stress from direct heat and drought. Keeping shade trees in your farm helps maintain the cool, moist environment midges and cocoa trees need.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ kɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahiamɔ nii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, rotten patches at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It often happens when watering is irregular, which prevents the roots from taking up calcium from the soil, even if calcium is present.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ calcium yɛ moŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack due to the swelling tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni efuu lɛ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my plantain tree leaning heavily and falling over during moderate rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots supporting heavy bunches. Microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects often weaken the roots and stem base. Supporting heavy trees with wooden props and using healthy planting suckers prevents lodging.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi wɔɔhe naa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than at afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the cool morning allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply so roots can drink before the heat sets in. Afternoon watering causes most water to evaporate quickly in the heat before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anu nu dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to keep clear weeds around my young yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mi yams bibii ni ato lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than yam vines and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping mounds clear during the early months ensures the vines get full sunlight to produce large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe sweet potato wain tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse yɛ shishijee nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa wain tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be fɛɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer upper leaves, turning the bottom ones yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and becoming thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought stress as the plant tries to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in heavy rain when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Without oxygen in waterlogged soil, fungi grow quickly and destroy the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji oxygen bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my planted yam setts taking so long to sprout out of the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-sweet potato lɛ miikwɛ̃ kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam setts delay sprouting if the soil is too dry, if the seed yam was harvested recently and is still in natural dormancy, or if planted too deep away from soil heat.
ga: Sweet potatoes baaha ekwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ mli lolo. aloo kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ hewɔ

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers dry up and drop off without forming tiny pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, shade imbalances, or damage from tiny sucking insects like capsids/mirids.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, kɛ hulutsoo ni ejaaa mli. loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids/mirids lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms as soon as the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ pɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when day temperatures get too high because extreme heat prevents proper pollination and forces the plant to conserve moisture.
ga: Pepper tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa ni enyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do black bugs cover my cowpea pods as soon as they start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji haa mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee pɛ?

english: These black bugs are aphids that suck the sweet sap out of young pods. They are attracted to fresh green growth and reproduce very quickly in warm weather.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii diji nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ wuo mli nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Amɛsumɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ni amɛfɔɔ oya waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does Striga weed make my maize stay stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miigba mi-ŋmã lɛ naa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to maize roots underground, stealing water and nutrients before the maize plant can use them.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruits start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms (nematodes) or stem borers often weaken them underground, leaving the tree unable to support the heavy weight of a maturing bunch.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii (nematodes) loo stem borers lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni eda kwraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my rice growing tall and dark green in some spots of the farm, but short and yellow in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ? Shi yɛ be ko mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ bafee kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Uneven growth happens when land is not leveled flat, causing water and nutrients to pool in low spots while higher spots remain dry and nutrient-poor.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etseee. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. yɛ be mli ni hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ kã he amɛgbi ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before they even produce ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet, stopping the plant roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ashishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does applying animal manure help my crops differently than synthetic chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he?

english: Synthetic fertilizer feeds the plant quickly, but animal manure feeds the soil. Manure improves the soil structure so it holds water and nutrients longer, keeping your field productive over many farming seasons.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi kooloi ashishifã lɛ haa sũ lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii yɛ okwaayeli bei srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are there tiny holes appearing on my young maize leaves with small worms hidden inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Kplukai bibii je kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ. Akɛtee kone mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds on the growing leaf center. If left untreated, they eat the growing point of the crop and greatly reduce your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ lɛ Amɛbaaye hei ni onibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ ni amɛbaahã onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil, leaving your crops hungry and unable to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara waa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, plants compete heavily for sunlight, water, and nutrients. They waste their energy stretching high for light instead of developing strong stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ la nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rainfall of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a prolonged dry heat spell. Planting too early can scorch the seeds or dry out young sprouts before the main rains set in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut off some of the side branches and shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ afã kɛ suckers kɛjɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots allows the plant to direct its food and water into developing larger, healthier fruits rather than growing extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe baai krokomɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my cassava and leave the roots in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ kpamɔ be sɛɛ ni mishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If left in the ground past maturity, cassava roots become tough, woody, and lose their starch content, making them poor for eating or processing into gari.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni Cassava shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaafee tso ni amɛmli starch lɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haaa anyɛ aye loo afee lɛ curry.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack that crop to build up in the soil, leading to poorer harvests every season.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ mli woɔ wu daa be.

english: How do I know if my farmland is dead and cannot grow good crops anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ egbo ni enyɛɛɛ edu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Soil is considered degraded or dead when it becomes very hard, pale, and dry, and crops planted on it turn yellow, stay small, or give very poor yields. You can bring it back to life by adding organic manure, compost, and planting cover crops like cowpeas to restore nutrients and moisture.
ga: Abuɔ shikpɔŋ akɛ efite loo egbo kɛ́ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa, efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbi, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efee bibioo, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Obaanyɛ oha amɛhi wala mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa amɛhe tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu koni niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aku sɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the easiest way for me to make tired soil fertile again without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can restore tired soil naturally by adding dry animal manure, leaves, or compost, and by letting crop remains rot in the farm instead of burning them. Rotating crops with legumes like groundnuts or beans also puts vital nutrients back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni egbi, baai, loo kooloi amli ŋmei ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ashãa amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fata he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad for me to burn my farm bushes before planting a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli dani madu tsei heei lɛ?

english: Burning bush destroys rich organic matter, kills useful earthworms and soil organisms, and leaves your land exposed to dry sun and soil erosion. Clearing the weeds and letting them decompose on the field creates natural fertilizer that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsoi ni ashãa lɛ kpataa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ hulu ni egbiɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni aŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant lacks essential food like nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are choked by flooded water. Adding chicken manure or nitrogen fertilizer and ensuring rainwater drains easily will help the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he ni akwɛ koni nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin but produce very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops grow tall and weak when seeds are planted too close together, causing plants to stretch up and fight one another for light and food. Giving your crops proper spacing allows each plant to get enough sunlight, water, and nutrients to build strong stalks and big fruits.
ga: Tsei daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛyeɔ la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen food. Watering your plants regularly during hot periods and providing mild shade helps flowers stay on the plant and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen babaoo kpe amɛ. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ni oha amɛná hulutsoo fioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are not getting enough water during dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves roll inward, droop, or look dull during the hottest part of the day. You can also test the soil by digging your finger a few inches deep; if the soil feels dusty and dry, your crops need watering.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli, amɛgbeeɔ shi, loo amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe efee shoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ hu okwɛ kɛtsɔ onine ni oootsɔ mli kɛyashɛ inchi fioo ko nɔ kɛji onuɔ he akɛ sũ ebɔle ehe ni egbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo onibii amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits around the base of the plant for too long, drowning the roots and encouraging soil diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to flow away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shishigbɛ lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ewoɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I keep harmful insects from destroying my vegetable leaves without spending too much money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-vegetables baai lɛ ni mikɛ shika babaoo efiteee?

english: You can protect vegetables by spraying them with cheap natural sprays made from crushed neem tree leaves mixed with water and a little soap. Picking large bugs off by hand and keeping the weed population down also prevents pests from multiplying.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu aduawai ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni jara waaa ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa ni akɛ nu fioo kɛ samla efutu mli lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nine ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi wuji kɛ jwɛi ayibɔ ni aba shi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I choose the best time to plant my seeds when the rains keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply at least twice before planting so the ground holds enough moisture for seeds to sprout. You can also consult local agriculture extension officers who receive weather forecasts tailored to your district.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ dani odu. Enɛ ji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Obaanyɛ oyabi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ hu koni ona kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa ni sa okpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food for the plant, resulting in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa tso lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baafee wuji.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plant, they steal water and food nutrients from it. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring your main tree produces a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Tsei titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná plantains babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or cause waterlogging.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ekɛ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have giant bushy leaves but very small tubers when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikpaa cassava lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava plants spend all their energy growing tall stems and big leaves instead of storing energy underground to swell the cassava tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi konɛ e ha nɛ kasava sisifã ɔmɛ nɛ a bli.

english: Why do experts say planting cowpeas or beans helps improve my soil for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit, often made worse by irregular watering. When watering is inconsistent, roots cannot transport calcium to the fruit properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small green caterpillars to eat holes right through the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. They lay eggs on young maize leaves and crawl into the center funnel of the plant to feed. Spraying natural neem extracts or approved bio-pesticides early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii anɔ ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛyaye niyenii. Kɛ́ afɔ adebɔɔ mli neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa enɛɛmɛi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking juice from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid watering my vegetable crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ ahe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot sunlight causes water droplets on leaves to evaporate too quickly or act like hot magnifying glasses that burn the leaves. It also wastes water and creates damp heat that encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ glase ni mli edɔ ni shãa baai lɛ. Efiteɔ nu hu ni ehaa hulutsoo ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ baa.

english: Can I just pick a dried coconut that fell from my tree and plant it in my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmeii ni egbi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds directly from fallen fruits often leads to low yields or late fruiting. Certified nurseries grow specific improved varieties that are selected to grow faster, resist diseases, and bear plenty of fruit every year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi loo aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei amli ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ duɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ krɛdɛɛ ni ahala koni amɛdara oya, ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How do I know which specific variety of crop is best to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different varieties are developed for specific goals, like producing heavy harvests, growing short for easy picking, or resisting drought. You should ask an extension officer to recommend a certified variety that matches your soil and climate.
ga: Afeɔ srɔtoi kɛha otii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ ŋmaa babaoo ni abaakpa. Amɛdumɔ kuku koni akɛto mlɛo. loo hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ Esa akɛ obi o-extension agent lɛ ni etsɔɔ bo srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Are all dwarf coconut trees better to plant than the tall coconut trees?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei bibii fɛɛ hi ni aduɔ fe ŋmei tsei ni kwɔlɔ?

english: Dwarf varieties start bearing fruit much faster and are easier to harvest, while tall varieties usually live longer and survive harsher conditions. Choosing the right one depends on whether you want fast production or long-term farming.
ga: Dwarf henɔi lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa, ni ekpamɔ waaa. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Nɔ ni sa ni obaahala lɛ damɔ kɛji oosumɔ ni afee nibii oya loo okwaayeli ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the benefit of buying crop seedlings from a nursery instead of planting my own seeds directly?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ahe ni ooohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe moŋ fe ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaadu amɛ?

english: Nursery seedlings are raised under carefully controlled conditions using high-quality parent trees. Buying from a nursery ensures you get healthy, uniform plants that are guaranteed to give high yields.
ga: Akɛ nyɛ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ehaa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yaa nɔ daa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ akɛ amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if a seedling from a nursery is good quality before I buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani mahe?

english: A good seedling has dark green, spot-free leaves, a thick and sturdy stem, and a strong root system. Avoid seedlings that look pale, weak, or show signs of insect damage.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, nɔ ko bɛ he, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse, ni amɛhe wa. kɛ shishifã ni mli wa Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni jieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some coconut trees yield lots of fruit every single year while others hardly bear anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoshi tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni eshwɛ fioo ni tsei komɛi wooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Fruit yield depends mostly on the plant's genetic variety and soil care. Improved varieties are bred specifically to produce heavy harvests continuously every year, unlike unselected local trees.
ga: Yibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ tso lɛ mli fɔmɔ nii srɔtoi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ babaoo. Henɔi srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo nibii ni tsii, ni yaa nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ejeee tamɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni ahalaaa lɛ.

english: Why do tree crops sometimes stop bearing fruits after producing heavily for one season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei kpaɔ yibiiwoo beni amɛwo yibii waa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Trees can drain all their stored energy after a massive harvest. Using high-yielding varieties combined with good soil feeding keeps the tree healthy enough to bear heavy crops every year without taking breaks.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ ajie hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo fata he ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpa fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo daa afi ni amɛkpaaa.

english: How does choosing the right crop variety increase the money I make at harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso henɔ ni sa ni mihalaa lɛ baanyɛ aha shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: The right variety produces significantly more fruits per tree using the same amount of land and labor. Higher production per tree directly increases your total harvest and profit.
ga: Nɔ ni sa lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kwraa yɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtsɔ he kɛ nitsumɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli babaoo lɛ baaha okpamɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some tree crops take many years to produce fruit while improved varieties start bearing so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi oya waa lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred for early maturity, meaning they focus their early energy on producing flowers and fruit rather than just growing tall.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ amɛmra be mli hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee shwiili.

english: Why do some coconut trees dry up and die from diseases while neighboring trees remain healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi gboɔ ni helai gbeɔ amɛ shi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Certain plant varieties have natural resistance to common diseases. Planting a disease-resistant variety obtained from a trusted nursery protects your farm from major crop losses.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Kɛ́ odu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct, strong sunlight damages their soft leaves and dries out the soil before their shallow roots can absorb enough water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ dani shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into narrow tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from extreme heat and save water by reducing the surface area exposed to the hot sun.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus its energy on growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending stored food down to develop the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní nɛ a to ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee tubers ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow down the middle while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency; the plant moves the limited nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to keep the growing top leaves healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ aha.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any peppers begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by high heat, sudden dry spells, or poor soil nutrition, shedding the flowers to conserve energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. trukaa ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant several seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together compete against each other for the same limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all the plants to grow weak.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes with tiny powder that looks like sawdust inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ? Etamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf shoot during the day, feeding on young leaves and leaving behind its waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ye baai bibii ni oshi jwɛi yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like a rock after the rain stops and the hot sun dries the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ egbi ŋmɔji lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like rotten plant material or manure, which normally acts like a sponge to keep the soil loose and easy for crop roots to grow through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsei ahe nibii loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are my cassava leaves developing light green and yellow patches and twisting sideways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtee afã lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that damages the leaf greenness, preventing the plant from making food efficiently.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ baai lɛ aŋɔli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the lower stems of my tomato plants turn soft and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When tomato plants grow too thick with leaves near the muddy ground, moisture gets trapped and blocks airflow, creating a wet climate where soil fungi easily attack the stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ he lɛ, nu lɛ baamɔ mli ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa tsei lɛ ahe mlɛo.

english: Why should I cover my cleared farm land with dried grass or leaves before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture underneath so your maize seeds have water to grow, even when the hot sun shines directly on the field.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shishi. Enɛ baaha o-abele dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ po
