english: Is it a bad idea to leave my field soil completely bare after clearing the bushes?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaashi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving soil bare allows the hot sun to dry out all the moisture and bakes the ground hard, which makes it very difficult for young seeds to sprout and survive.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ agbi ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ais. Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa dumɔwui bibii akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die when I plant them late in the year around November or December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ aaafee November loo December lɛ?

english: In Ghana, November and December mark the dry season and Harmattan when rains stop. Crops planted during this time cannot survive on rain alone and will dry up unless you water them manually.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, abuɔ November kɛ December akɛ hulutsoo be, ni abuɔ Harmattan akɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaa. Tsei ni adu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ pɛ mli, ni amɛbaagbi ja okɛ onine wo amɛ nu.

english: How can checking the local weather forecast help me decide when to put my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ he?

english: Weather forecasts give you advance notice on when the rains are likely to start and stop, helping you plant at the exact right time so your seeds get continuous water to grow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa lɛ tsɔɔ bo be ni nugbɔ lɛ baaje shishi kɛ be ni ebaakpa. Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do the usual rainy months keep changing, making it difficult to know the right time to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ yaa nɔ etsakeɔ lɛ? Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaale be ni sa kɛha okwaayeli.

english: Shifting climate patterns are altering the traditional wet and dry seasons in Ghana. Following weather updates helps you adjust your planting calendar instead of relying only on past habits.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake blema nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni ooonyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua bo ni otsake odumɔ kalanda lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ tsutsu sui pɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during dry spells as a self-defense mechanism to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly from their leaf surface.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu naa koni ekajɛ baa lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ.

english: What happens to corn seeds if I plant them in dry soil and the rain stops right after?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa?

english: If seeds get just enough moisture to sprout and then rain stops, the tender young roots will dry out in the hot soil and the plant will die before establishing itself.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ dani enyɛɔ etswaa shi.

english: Can I still grow corn during the dry season if no rain falls at all?
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ be mli lɛ lolo?

english: Yes, but only if you use irrigation like pumping water from a river, well, or borehole, because corn needs a steady water supply throughout its growth to produce cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa mli, nu bu loo nubu mli lɛ tsu nii pɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ edalɛ be fɛɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmãa aba.

english: Why do my crops look withered even though rain fell a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures cause water to evaporate quickly from both the soil and the plant leaves, causing crops to show heat stress even shortly after a rainfall.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ po.

english: If I plant a very large plot of land, does it mean my corn will automatically produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu shikpɔŋ ni da waa lɛ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baakpa babaoo kɛjɛ ehe?

english: A larger plot gives you more space, but crops on big farms still need proper water, healthy soil, and care. If dry weather hits, a large field will fail just like a small one if it lacks water.
ga: He ni da lɛ haa onáa he babaoo. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ he miihia nu lolo. sũ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Ni kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ agbo ko baafite tamɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni nu bɛ mli.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the soil the nitrogen your maize needs.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ bei pii amli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or recommended insect spray helps clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ mli atse.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a gentle cover that protects them from harsh heat while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa anáa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛma shi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest if the tubers are under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months, the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni miduko tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry or when there are not enough insects to move pollen between flowers. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps save the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely makes crops fight each other for food and sunlight, resulting in thin plants with small fruits. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow full and yield more.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ niyenii kɛ hulu la he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni edara jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to provide long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa niji kakadaji lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting them off the ground stops the leaves from rotting and helps the tuber below grow very large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ owó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even after I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water from their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. Drooping is their natural way of saving water, and they usually stand back up by evening.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi gbɛkɛ

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rains will wash the fertilizer away off the top of the soil before the roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade plants like plantain or cassava grown beside them to shelter their leaves while their root systems grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni akɛwo baai lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess rain combined with heavy leaf cover creates high humidity, which causes a fungal sickness called black pod disease to multiply and attack the growing pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni akɛ baai ni mli edɔ fataa he lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ faa babaoo ni etutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miida lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow at the tips when the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient required to keep the plant green and growing fast.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni tsei ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does my maize plant develop flowers at the top before I see any corn ears on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ hiɛ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛyiteŋ dani ŋmãa toi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The flower at the top produces pollen, which needs to fall onto the silks below so the cob can fill out with healthy corn kernels.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ woɔ pollen. ni esa akɛ egbee siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ emuu ahi mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small ears when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ toi bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving each plant with less energy to make food.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava plant shed almost all of its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops leaves to conserve water during dry weather. The plant is not dead; it is protecting itself and will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Enɛ ji koni obu ohe he ni obaaná baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in the sun. Sunlit leaves produce the energy the plant needs to expand the tuber underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ e-bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do groundnut plant flowers bend down and push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers naturally send out growth stalks called pegs that push into the dirt because the actual nuts develop and mature hidden underground.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii tsuɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ahewɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyaa hiɛ ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or dry soil, which prevents the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi akawo yibii.

english: Why do the outer leaves of my plantain trees turn brown and collapse against the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves brown and drop naturally as they age, but rapid browning happens when the plant lacks water or essential nutrients like potassium in the soil.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ baa oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food in the soil. It can also happen when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and refusing to grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji kuku ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants stay stunted when the soil lacks enough nutrients or when the earth is packed too tightly for roots to spread. Adding compost or well-rotted animal manure gives the roots room to expand and provides food for growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ amli alɛɛ ni ebaaha niyenii aha amɛdalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close together on the ridge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ yucca tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space for its leaves to catch sunlight and for its underground roots to grow big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ebaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la, ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hu anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil stays moist a few inches deep after two or three good rains, rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry up and die before they can establish roots.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ 2-3 inches yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa fioo komɛi asɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛfee shishifãi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants. Removing weeds early leaves all the soil resources for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ejuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This naturally feeds the maize growing next to them, acting like a free fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmãa ni damɔ shi ekome.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plants do not get enough water. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛha amɛhi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Leaves droop in strong sunlight because the plant is losing water through its leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. It rolls or wilts its leaves to hide from the sun and slow down water loss until the evening cool.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efoɔ koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ hulu la he ni ekɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars hide deep inside the whorl of the maize plant to shield themselves from hot afternoon sun, heavy rain, and birds. They stay inside where the leaves are tender and soft enough for them to chew easily.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛhiɔ hei ni baai lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds bought in a store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred in a laboratory to have high vigor and yield in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose that special vigor in the next generation, producing smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni ehi shi shiŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛi krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo fioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under full sun. They require shade trees or fast-growing plantains to act as natural umbrellas to keep the soil moist and block harsh sunlight during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni daa oya koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during peak afternoon heat to save water and reduce moisture loss through evaporation. If the plant recovers in the cooler evening, it is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves on maize usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves available nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them alongside maize enriches the soil naturally, helping the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: How does spreading dried poultry manure or leaf compost on my farm help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi loo baai ashishifãi ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Poultry manure and leaf compost add organic matter to the land, which acts like a sponge to hold moisture in the soil during dry spells while slowly feeding essential nutrients to your crops.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei kɛ baai amli ŋmei kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa haa onibii

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the center whorl of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on the tender young leaves inside the center of the maize stalk. Detecting them early allows you to treat the crop before the pest destroys the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohereɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the field, reducing yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tamɔ tsei ni miida lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to insert long wooden stakes into the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Staking helps the vines catch sun and fresh air, which encourages larger tuber growth underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ. Enɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting, signaled by the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off and the base of the plant stem becoming thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata okadii lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni tso lɛ shishi bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebatsɔ tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller grains and tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛ bulbs lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for vital resources like sunlight, water, root space, and soil nutrients, stealing the nourishment your crops need to build big grains or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ hulu la, nu, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ dumɔwui wuji loo ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa seedlings from hot sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa tsei he hiaa koni amɛwo baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops the disease from spreading in your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow well together because cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize and improves overall soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning excess shade branches allows light and air to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them with thin stems and small, poor roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni ehiii lɛ feɔ bulb agbo najiaŋ.

english: Why should I leave a portion of my land to rest for a season without planting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko koni mihe ajɔɔ mihe be kome ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akadu nii?

english: Leaving land to rest, or fallow, gives the soil time to naturally replenish the nutrients and organic matter that previous crops took away, making it fertile again for future planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ koni ejɔɔ ehe loo ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jie lɛ baawo mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before any tomatoes can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: High heat causes tomatoes to drop their blossoms to survive heat stress. Watering early in the morning and providing light shade helps protect the flowers so fruit can grow.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How deep should I place my yam pieces inside the soil mounds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ awo gɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Yam pieces should be planted about 10 to 15 centimeters deep. This protects the seed from hot sunlight while leaving enough space in the mound for the new yam tuber to grow long and thick.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato fãi lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 10 kɛyashi 15 koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa hu yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli koni ŋmeii heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder when I store it in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: The powder is created by tiny insects called weevils eating the grain from the inside out. Properly drying the corn to low moisture before storage prevents weevils from destroying the grain.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ powda nɛɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei ni yeɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi dani akɛto lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer recommends a foliar application for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ extension nitsulɔ ko wo ŋaa akɛ akɛ foliar spray awo mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: A foliar application means spraying liquid nutrients or treatments directly onto the leaves of the crop rather than putting them into the soil. Leaves have tiny pores that can absorb these liquids quickly to help the plant grow healthy.
ga: Foliar spraying tsɔɔ nu mli niyenii loo tsofafeemɔ nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. No baanyɛ aŋɔ nu nɛɛ oya koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can my crops really feed and protect themselves through liquid absorbed by their leaves?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye niyenii ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, plant leaves have small openings called stomata that can take in liquid treatments directly. This method often works faster than root fertilization, especially when a crop needs quick nourishment.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe baai yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni atsɛɔ lɛ stomata ni baanyɛ aná nu mli tsofafeemɔ tɛ̃ɛ Gbɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii oya.

english: Does applying spray treatments directly to cocoa leaves damage them?
ga: Ani kookoo baai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baafite kookoo baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Under normal conditions, spraying properly diluted products on leaves helps the plant. However, damage occurs if you spray during extreme sun, use the wrong concentration, or use products not intended for leaf application.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni sa mli lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaafite. Nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo nibii ni esaaa kɛha foliar spraying lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why is it harmful to spray my cocoa farm in the middle of the day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo ŋmɔji anɔ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: When you spray under a hot sun, the water droplets on the leaves act like small magnifying glass lenses, burning the leaves. High heat also stresses the tree, causing leaf pores to close so the spray cannot be absorbed.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ Nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni haa baai lɛ shãa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɛɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply liquid spray on my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu afɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon. During these cooler hours, the sun is gentle, and leaf pores are open to absorb the treatment without burning the leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse ji leebi loo shwane. Yɛ fɛ̃i ŋmɛlɛtswai nɛɛ amli lɛ Hulu lɛ baafee blɛoo. Ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baagbele waa koni amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ ni amɛshãaa baa lɛ.

english: What happens to liquid sprays on plant leaves if I apply them in the bright afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni baaba nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: The heat evaporates the liquid rapidly, leaving concentrated chemical residue behind that scorches leaf surfaces and causes heat stress to the cocoa plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Eshiɔ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yɛ esɛɛ. ni haa baa lɛ hiɛ shãa ni ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How does spraying my cocoa farm in the cool morning benefit my trees compared to afternoon spraying?
ga: Te mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ? Kɛ akɛto shwiemɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ he

english: Cool morning spraying allows droplets to sit on open leaf pores longer without evaporating or burning, giving the tree maximum time to absorb the nourishment before heat sets in.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai lɛ hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛshwieee shi loo amɛshãaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ be babaoo ni amɛkɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani latsaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves look scorched or burnt after I apply leaf treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã loo eshã beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛtsaa baai lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves look burnt when treatments are applied during high heat, when liquid concentrations are too strong, or when harsh sunlight heats up wet chemicals on the leaf surface.
ga: Baai lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Beni nu lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofai ni efɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are suffering from heat stress?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Signs of heat stress include leaf yellowing, drooping, brown edges, curling leaves, or leaf shedding shortly after hot weather or improper midday spraying.
ga: Nɔ ni fata hulutsoo he haomɔ he okadii ahe ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, baai ni shwieɔ shi, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, baai ni shwieɔ shi, loo baai ni laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. loo hulutsoo be mli tsofa ni esaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ

english: Why do cocoa trees react so sensitive to weather conditions when receiving crop inputs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe waa kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally prefer partial shade and cool conditions. Strong direct sunlight combined with wet chemical sprays shocks the tree's natural cooling mechanisms, leading to leaf damage and plant stress.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ shade fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni mli efɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ baakpokpo tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: How do I know if the size of the land I am clearing is too big for me to farm properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mijieɔ lɛ dalɛ da tsɔ ni manyɛ matsu okwaayeli he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: A farm is too large if you cannot weed, fertilize, and harvest it on time with your available labor and money. Managing a smaller plot thoroughly often yields a higher profit than planting a huge plot that ends up overgrown with weeds.
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ da tsɔ kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ okɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shika ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛjie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa nii yɛ be naa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ fe shikpɔŋ agbo ni jwɛi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ni ooodu.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting cassava too close forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the tubers enough room underground to grow large and thick instead of producing thin, weak roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ shishifãhi nɛ a he wa we.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil is ready for me to plant my seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist a few inches deep for several days. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then wither if a dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi gbii babaoo. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing well when big trees shade them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei wuji ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full, direct sunlight to make food and produce flowers. Heavy shade from large trees starves the plants of energy, causing them to grow tall and thin without producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which target the soft, growing funnels of young maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended organic or chemical controls into the leaf funnels stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ organic loo tsofai ni akɛwo baa mligbalamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before they produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering and balanced nutrients help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes my farm soil to dry out and harden so quickly after clearing?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ ni ewaa oya nɛkɛ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Exposing bare soil directly to the hot sun burns off organic matter and dries out moisture fast. Covering the soil with dried leaves or crop residue as mulch protects it from heat and keeps moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko wo hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves turn yellow and dry up, and when you pull up a sample plant and see that the inside of the pods has dark markings with plump seeds inside.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni kɛ́ ogbala tso ni akɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ nɔ ni ona akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ yɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Why should I buy improved seed varieties instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and weaker plants. Improved seeds are specially bred to produce higher yields, grow faster, and withstand common local pests and drought conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa yibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. edaa oya ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist while the young trees grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow before the ears even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the growth stage helps the leaves stay green and strong enough to produce good corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii mra Yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly damp after a light rain, rather than right before a heavy rain storm. Applying it to damp soil allows the plant roots to absorb the nutrients quickly before heavy downpours can wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo dani ahum ni naa wa aba. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater stays trapped in flat ground, the roots drown and rot; planting cassava on raised earthen mounds allows water to drain away naturally.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes inside the growing leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ baai ni miida lɛ mli

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft growing centers of corn plants. Spotting them early and applying organic or recommended sprays inside the leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the entire stalk.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tsɔɔ hei ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ona amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaafite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently watered and cool helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ eha tomato tsei lɛ efo amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant corn on the exact same spot on my farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Alternating corn with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches and shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can circulate through the tree canopy. Good airflow keeps the tree dry, preventing fungal diseases like black pod from spreading to your pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Tsi fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ naa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã o-pods lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my cassava help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas spread along the ground to block weeds and keep the soil moist. Additionally, their roots fix nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the nearby cassava plants so they can grow bigger roots.
ga: Cowpeas gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni haa ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii koni eshishifãi lɛ adara

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and dropping off during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot survive under strong direct sunlight without protection. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain alongside young cocoa creates shade and keeps the air cool and humid, which protects the young cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo aba ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruits start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil, making them top-heavy when carrying big bunches. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo props or wooden poles prevents strong winds from uprooting or snapping the trees.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ otere ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie tso lɛ shishi loo ekagbee shi.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow big ears. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like NPK, urea, or decomposed poultry manure restores the green color and improves grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ toi wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK, urea, loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni efite fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for the next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have microscopic helpers on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plants decay after harvest, this nitrogen stays behind as natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpea yɛ yelikɛbualɔi bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, wet soil, depriving the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark brown and soft while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni mikɛkpeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a small water mold that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments. Trimming extra branches to let sunshine and fresh air reach the pods helps dry out moisture and prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nu mli ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ atsake tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or when soil moisture changes back and forth between dry and wet. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the ground cool and moist, helping flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and pass viruses to the plant. Spraying neem seed extract or safe insecticides early before severe damage occurs stops these insects and protects new leaves.
ga: Kooloo bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei amli Neem dumɔwu mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra dani fitemɔ ni naa wa baa Ehaa kooloi nɛɛ kpaa ni ebuɔ baa heei ahe.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and dark powdery dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage comes from Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide and eat inside the central leaf funnel of young maize. Applying recommended control treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots even when I keep them inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔji eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their sleeping period and start growing shoots when storage temperatures rise and humidity builds up. Storing tubers in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn off the bare ground keeps them cool and delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes gbalaa adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. ni amɛjeɔ ŋmeii adumɔ shishi kɛ́ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Kɛ tubers lɛ ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhe jɔɔ ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Good cocoa soil must be deep, dark, and well-drained so roots can grow deep without getting waterlogged. If water sits on the land for days after rain, cocoa roots will rot.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni nu akabote mli. Kɛji nu tee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Cocoa shishifãi baanyɛ agbo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and prevent itself from drying out. The plant is not dead, and new leaves will grow back as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu akafite ni amɛkagbi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers if they lack water or nutrients, or if there are no tiny midges (insects) in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: How do I know when it is the right time to reduce shade trees as my cocoa grows older?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ji be kpakpa ni esa akɛ mafo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ anɔ be mli ni mi-kokoo lɛ daa lɛ?

english: When young cocoa trees grow tall and their branches start touching each other to form a thick canopy, you should slowly thin out shade trees so the mature cocoa gets enough direct sunlight to produce pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa ni amɛniji jeɔ shishi amɛtaa amɛhe koni amɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ hulutsoo awo tsei lɛ anɔ fiofio bɔni afee ni kookoo ni eda lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is beneficial because beans trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my young maize crop in the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ mi-baby corn lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before the maize grows tall enough to shade the ground. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks allows the maize roots to establish strongly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Dani ŋmãa lɛ baada bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ baawo ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Clearing surrounding weeds helps reduce these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning black and dying before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Black spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly during heavy rains and slows down tuber growth underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Rotten spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular during dry spells.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: I want to farm on a piece of land near our town that hasn't yielded good crops in years, so how can I make this soil fertile again?
ga: Miisumɔ ni matsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ wɔmaŋ lɛ ni wooo yibii afii babaoo nɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ nɛɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ?

english: Overused or exhausted soil lacks essential nutrients and organic matter. By clearing the land, spreading decomposed organic manure or soil improvers, and tilling them into the soil before planting, you restore vital nutrients like nitrogen and organic material that crops need to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine loo ni efite ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsakemɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani okɛdu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I properly prepare my farm land before planting to make sure my crops grow strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing weeds, loosening the topsoil so roots can spread easily, and working organic matter into the ground. This improves the soil's ability to hold water and gives young seedlings quick access to air and nutrients right after they germinate.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli ni ajieɔ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli babaoo, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii oya yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grow tall and healthy in some parts of my farm, but remain small and weak in other parts of the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi amli lɛ? Shi eji nɔ bibioo hu ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli hei krokomɛi.

english: Soil quality varies naturally across a field due to differences in soil depth, water drainage, and past land use. Areas where organic material naturally accumulates or where water settles without waterlogging will naturally have richer soil, causing crops in those spots to grow much better.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ jɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ mli. He ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi bɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baahi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai hei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: If I spread manure or soil improvers on my field, how does it actually make the farm fertile?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ tsakemɔi shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Soil improvers feed beneficial soil organisms that break down organic material into nutrients that plant roots can absorb. This process also creates a spongy soil structure that holds both water and nutrients close to your crop roots instead of letting them wash away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakemɔi haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛfeɔ niyenii ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ niyenii. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ bɛŋkɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛho amɛhe lɛ

english: Should I just scatter soil nutrients on top of the ground, or do I need to mix them into the dirt?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashwã sũ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛfutu sũ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to mix soil nutrients directly into the top layer of dirt. Leaving them exposed on top of the ground allows hot sunlight and heavy rain to burn off or wash away valuable nutrients before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afutu muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ashã loo efo niyenii ni jara wa lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: When is the best time to apply soil improvers or manure to my land before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ tsakemɔi loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata mishikpɔŋ lɛ he dani adu nii?

english: The best time is during initial land preparation, about one to two weeks before planting your seeds. This gives the soil time to absorb the organic material and moisture, creating a nutrient-rich environment ready for new roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishijee. Aaafee otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ dani adu dumɔwui. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha shishifãi heei ni baaje shishi.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer or animal manure to my farm actually harm my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, adding too much nutrient material at once creates high salt levels in the soil that can burn plant roots. This prevents roots from absorbing water properly, causing the crops to wilt, turn brown, or die.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛfataa he shikome lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aahu akɛ ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egboɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ brown loo gbo.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn pale or yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen-rich compost or fertilizer helps the plant build chlorophyll and regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee chlorophyll ni amɛha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground, causing temporary wilting to conserve moisture. Soil enriched with organic matter holds water better and helps reduce this heat stress on plants.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ tso lɛ agbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa dɔlɛ ni tsii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does clearing weeds completely during land preparation help my main crop grow better later?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them thoroughly before planting ensures that all the fertility you add to the soil goes directly to feeding your main crop rather than wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie mli jogbaŋŋ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha nibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ aya oniyenii titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe koo mli tsei lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, full sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out quickly. They need partial shade from faster-growing trees like plantains to protect them while their roots grow strong enough to pull enough water from the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe. Beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small ragged holes in them with powdery dirt sitting inside the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni egbɛ eshwa ni nibii bibii ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the center shoot of the maize plant during the day to eat the soft young leaves and leaves behind droppings that look like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai ni mli tse lɛ. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called thrips often attack and drink the juice from young flower buds before they can turn into pods. When the flowers are damaged this way, the plant drops them to save its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ tutuaa ni amɛnuɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji fɔfɔii fite yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ Tsei baagbee shi koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the farm and stays on top for too long, water fills up all the empty spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ lɛ eyiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehiɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu baayi he ni efee efolo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy wind after carrying big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ewo ŋmeii wuji sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay shallow in the top layer of the soil rather than going deep down. When the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots out of the soil.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛmli kwɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ko ni mli wa kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why does my tomato plant suddenly wilt and die within two days even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboi trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This rapid wilting is caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that enters the plant's roots and blocks the internal tubes that carry water up to the leaves, causing the plant to dry out from the inside while standing in wet soil.
ga: Bacteria ni shwieɔ shi oya nɛɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni eboteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Gbimɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli be mli ni odamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of turning them into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme soil heat, lack of regular water, or a shortage of essential plant food like calcium and nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. nu ni faaa daa loo tsei niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning purple on the leaves and remaining very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwɛɔ kuku waa lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize indicate that the plant is struggling to get enough phosphorus from the soil. Phosphorus is the nutrient responsible for early root development and stem growth.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fosforo ji niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ daa mra ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: How do my stored seed yams know when to start sprouting shoots even before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ ebɔi shweremɔ dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams go through a natural sleep period called dormancy after harvest. Internal chemical triggers inside the tuber act like a natural alarm clock, waking the yam up to sprout when storage temperatures and time indicate the rainy season is coming.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni tswaa ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ Teɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba.

english: Why do tomato plants grown near tall grass stay thin and fail to produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni adu yɛ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɛŋkɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Weeds and tall grass have aggressive root systems that quickly suck up water, fertilizer, and light before the tomato plant can reach them, effectively starving the crop of the food it needs to make big fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la oya dani tomato tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa niyenii tsei lɛ he hiaa ni amɛwo yibii wuji ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some high-yielding maize seeds produce so much more food than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ wo niyenii babaoo fe ŋmãa ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Specially bred seeds, like hybrids, are designed in laboratories to resist local diseases and absorb nutrients more efficiently. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Afee dumɔwui srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii, yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: If I buy a cheaper seed variety instead of the expensive government recommended seed, how will my crop behave differently?
ga: Kɛji mihe dumɔwui ni jara waaa yɛ dumɔwui ni jara wa ni nɔyeli lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ najiaŋ. Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cheaper traditional seeds may grow well, but they often take longer to mature, are more easily damaged by dry spells, and produce smaller cobs compared to improved varieties that are bred specifically for high yield and climate resilience.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui ni jara waaa lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ. Efiteɔ oya fe tsutsu lɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be nɔ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔse amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe shifimɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves are a signal that the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential food plant roots take from the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can feed itself and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi jieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ aye ehe niyenii ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has become too tired for crops to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops stay small, turn pale, or yield much less than they used to despite good rainfall, the soil has lost its nutrients and needs green manure, compost, or fertilizer to restore its power.
