ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa, amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛji tsutsu lɛ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni ehe hiaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aha ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the stalks of my maize plants thin and falling over easily during light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their stalks are weak due to overcrowding, a lack of potassium in the soil, or damage from soil pests that eat the roots that anchor the plant.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Rolling leaves is the crop's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water inside its stem.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he tsɔne kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akahi tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize cobs have many missing kernels when rain stops around the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii babaoo fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs plenty of water when producing silks and tassels. If dry weather hits during flowering, the silks dry up before catching pollen, leaving empty spots on the cob where grains should have grown.
ga: Abɛi biɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛfee siliki kɛ tsɔji. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Siliki lɛ gbiɔ dani eŋɔɔ pollen. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why are the seeds I planted failing to shoot up out of the soil after a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ otsi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if heavy rains buried them too deep, or if soil insects like ants and worms ate the seeds before they could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do the leaves at the top center of my maize plants look ragged and chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ayiteŋgbɛ lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni atsɔ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms, which hide deep inside the funnel of the plant during the hot day and come out at night to eat the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What actually happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. This competition makes all the plants tall, thin, and weak.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa.

english: If maize becomes too expensive or hard to find in my area, what other locally grown crops can I use as a substitute to feed my animals?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa jara wa tsɔ loo ewa akɛ aaana yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi manyɛ mikɛtsu nii ni adu yɛ maŋ lɛ mli moŋ kɛha kooloi aniyenii?

english: Cassava roots and peels, sorghum, millet, and sweet potatoes are excellent local alternatives to maize. They grow well in Ghanaian soils and provide high energy for livestock when dried and processed properly.
ga: Kasava, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi kɛ amɛhewolo ji maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa najiaŋ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ ni amɛhaa kooloi hewalɛ babaoo kɛji agbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsu he nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an important plant food, or that heavy rain has flooded the roots and prevented them from taking in nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni haaa amɛná niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants give signals above ground when ready: the main stem turns dark brown, lower leaves naturally yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ feɔ okadi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji efee klalo. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any pepper fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them shed their blossoms to save water and energy for survival instead of using it to grow fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Ha amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ aduawai

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow well when I plant cassava and maize too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil food, while their big leaves block sunlight from reaching one another.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same farm patch every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛfɔɔ daa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops in the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes in their roots that suck nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small worms suddenly start eating tiny holes in my maize leaves right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ shishi amɛyeɔ bu bibii trukaa lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, whose moths lay eggs on tender young green leaves right after the rains start because soft seedling shoots are easy food for hatching caterpillars.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ji niyenii ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why do my crops wilt and die even after a few days of very heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much water standing in the soil smothers plant roots so they cannot breathe, causing the roots to rot and preventing the plant from drawing up nutrients.
ga: Nu babaoo ni tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted seeds right after I clear and weed my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni midu beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and adapted to local conditions, holding dormant seeds in the soil that sprout instantly once exposed to rain and direct sunlight.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii waa, ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Ekɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ toiŋjɔlɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plant lacks water or nitrogen in the soil, but in Ghana, it is often a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ okadi nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus, or the roots are struggling to absorb nutrients because the soil is too wet and cold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ naa naagba yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy seasons when humidity is high and sunlight cannot reach through dense branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. ni hulu la nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried from farm to farm by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my maize producing flowers at the top when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yɛ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Maize flowers early when it faces severe heat or drought stress. The plant senses it might dry up and tries to make seeds as quickly as possible to survive.
ga: Abele fɔ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haomɔ ba. Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ekolɛ egbi ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo dumɔwui oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when rainfall is irregular. Without steady moisture, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ lɛ Tsei hu baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds even when the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests like nematodes or stem borers. When a heavy fruit bunch grows, the weak roots cannot hold the tree up.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ afite. Beni aduawai lɛ da Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua tso lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and dying long before the harvest season reaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by Yam Anthracnose disease, a fungal infection that ruins the leaves, or when soil nutrients and moisture are completely exhausted.
ga: Atomɔ wein tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ anthracnose hela ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ tutua amɛ. Fungal hela ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ baa loo be mli ni niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa

english: Why do my crops produce better yield when I plant them in straight lines with proper spacing instead of scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures every crop gets its own share of sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients, while reducing weed competition and stopping diseases from spreading quickly.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi akaŋshii baa shi, ni ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ kpaa.

english: Will using heavy tractor machinery to clear my new land affect how my cassava roots grow underground?
ga: Ani trakta tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛbaatsu nii koni akɛjie shikpɔŋ hee lɛ baaná bɔ ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Heavy machinery packs the soil tightly, creating a hard ground layer that makes it difficult for tuber crops like cassava or yam to expand. Loosening the soil after clearing helps roots spread out and grow large.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni haa ewaa ahaa tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ be mli ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout so much faster than my planted crops right after clearing a new plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni miduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie shikpɔŋ hee ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for years. Clearing the land exposes them to full sunlight and rain, triggering quick growth because wild weeds naturally adapt to raw soil faster than cultivated seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ fɛɛ kwraa. kɛ dalɛ baa oya Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives two to three steady rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting after only one light rain leaves seeds in warm, semi-dry dirt, which burns or rots the seeds before they sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ sɛɛ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi fioo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shãa loo amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do crops take longer to mature during the minor rainy season compared to the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heɔ be fioo dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli kɛ akɛto be titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season provides fewer hours of strong sunlight and reduced rainfall. Crops depend on sunlight to manufacture their food, so reduced light slows down plant growth and fruit production.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi lɛ baaná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, ni nugbɔ hu baanɛ fioo. Dumɔwui damɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛná niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ la ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade, like plantain suckers or shade trees, to shield them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni abu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawo shishifãi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into fruit during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their blooms to save moisture and energy for basic survival rather than spending effort on making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ koni onine ashɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land without them stealing food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛjuuu niyenii kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, because they feed at different times and depths. Maize grows fast and draws nutrients from near the surface, while cassava grows slower and feeds deeper, taking over the space after maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ nii yɛ bei kɛ mlibotemɔi srɔtoi amli. Abɛi daa oya ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ nii babaoo. Amɛtsakeɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers sit in the soil for weeks without producing new top leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ eta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii babaoo ni baai heei ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Newly planted suckers focus their energy on building strong underground roots first. Once the roots are established enough to take in water and food, new leaves will shoot up rapidly.
ga: Akɛ jwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa amamɔ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ, Baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow after heavy downpours wash over my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni eha miŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes essential soil nutrients like nitrogen below the root line. Without nitrogen, plants lose their deep green color and struggle to produce food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ ahe yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛhe su ni tsuɔ waa ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfee niyenii.

english: If I put extra fertilizer around my young crops all at once, will it make them produce food faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he kɛbɔle Dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ he shikome Ani ebaaha amɛwo niyenii oya?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer at once burns tender plant roots by drawing moisture out of them. It is better to apply smaller amounts in stages so the plant absorbs nutrients safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ fioo fioo mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin but give small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ shi ewoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, space, and soil food. The plant spends all its energy stretching high to reach light instead of putting energy into growing large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow much faster if I plant right after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first major rains soak the dry earth and release a sudden boost of nutrients stored in the soil, giving fresh seeds the strong water supply and food they need to sprout rapidly.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli fũu ni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo trukaa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei lɛ náa nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing fruits during very hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the sun gets too hot, the plant gets stressed and tries to save water to survive. To do this, it drops its flowers so it doesn't waste energy trying to grow fruit.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi. Bɔni afee ni afee enɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekafite hewalɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni edu aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava yields get smaller every time I plant them on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot year after year drains the specific plant food that crop loves from the soil, leaving the land tired and unable to nourish new tubers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni nibii ni aduɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ bulb heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are natural soil healers. Their roots trap good air underground and convert it into plant food, which feeds the soil and helps neighbor crops like maize grow greener.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tsalɔi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkafite shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots start spreading across my cocoa pods when the rainy weather stays too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ miibɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ? Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ

english: Continuous rain and heavy shade create damp conditions where tiny plant sicknesses, like the Black Pod fungus, thrive and travel easily from pod to pod through water drops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa haa hulutsoo baa. ni tsei ahe helai bibii tamɔ blackpod fungus Edaa ni efãa gbɛ mlɛo kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and spread so much faster than my main crops right after a rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher than farm crops. Their seeds can lie dormant in dry soil for a long time and instantly wake up and grab water the moment rain touches them.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛteɔ shi koni amɛyajie nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy windstorms near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not dig deep into the earth, and the heavy bunch of fruit at the top makes the tree top-heavy. When soil gets soft from rain, strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni aduawai ni tsii yɛ yiteŋ lɛ baaha tso lɛ yiteŋ atsɔ tsii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetables turn yellow and rot when water stays pooled on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like human beings do. When water covers the soil completely for days, it drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up food and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa gbii komɛi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haaa amɛnyɛ amɛye nii. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: After clearing my land, why do my crops sometimes fail even if I planted at the right time?
ga: Beni mijie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ?

english: Clearing land removes topsoil protection and natural shade. If the soil becomes too hard or dry right after clearing, young roots cannot spread; adding compost or leaving cleared weeds to decay as mulch helps the soil retain water and feed young crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ, ejieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hebuu kɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Does burning cleared grass and bushes on my farm help or hurt my crops before planting?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajie kɛ brɔshi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui dani miduɔ?

english: Burning gives a quick burst of ash nutrients, but it destroys healthy living organisms in the soil and makes the ground dry out much faster. Clearing without burning keeps the soil moist and fertile for longer.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Shi ekpãtãa nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya kwraa. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If I buy seeds to plant, how do I know if they are good quality seeds that will actually sprout?
ga: Kɛ́ ohe dumɔwui ni okɛbaadu lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji amɛji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ŋ?

english: Good certified seeds come in sealed bags with official government tags. You can test them before planting by wrapping 10 seeds in a moist cloth for three days; if 8 or 9 sprout, the seed batch is healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ni awo he odase lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni maŋ nɔyeli lɛ kadiɔ nɔ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ oka dani odu kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii etɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to buy new certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye kpami nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ mi.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to withstand local heat, resist common diseases, and yield much more food compared to saved seeds, which lose strength and produce less over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ naa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ewoɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe Amɛhewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do farm input credit programs work when I need seeds and fertilizer but don't have cash upfront?
ga: Te Fam Input Credit Program lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ beni dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi lɛ? Shi shika ko bɛ hiɛ

english: Input programs supply you with quality seeds, fertilizers, and chemicals at planting season on credit, and you pay back the cost after you harvest and sell your crops.
ga: Data entry program lɛ haa bo dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ credits mli. Ni obaawo nyɔmɔ ni okɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ beni okpa onibii ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting crops like beans alongside your maize helps feed the plants and restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting damaged by too much sun and dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water in strong sunlight, their leaves curl up or roll tight during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing water.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of flowers but fail to grow actual fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii babaoo shi jeee aduawai loo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers need insects like bees for pollination to form fruit, and they need soil nutrients like phosphorus. Strong drought, heavy rainfall, or poor soil when flowering begins can stop fruit from setting.
ga: Fɔfɔi he miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛha pollination koni amɛwo yibii. Ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs he miihia amɛ. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii beni fɔfɔi jeɔ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo akpa.

english: What should I do if I followed all your planting instructions but my farm is still not growing well?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mikɛ odumɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni miŋmɔ lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Crops can struggle due to hidden issues like bad soil acidity, underground pests, or irregular rainfall. When instructions don't give expected results, invite an extension officer to visit the field so they can inspect the soil and crop roots directly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa yɛ naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acid ni ehiii lɛ ahewɔ. shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Kɛji ŋaawoi haaa nɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ aba Fɔ̃ɔ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ nine ni amɛbasara jɛmɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛdu tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How often should I go into my farm to inspect the crops after planting them?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ agbe naa?

english: You should check your field at least twice a week during the early stages. Young plants are delicate, and visiting often allows you to catch weed invasion, pest attacks, or dry soil before the crops die.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oyale mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli yɛ shishijee mli. Tso bibioo lɛ waaa. Ni bei pii lɛ, saramɔ baanyɛ aha jwɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi aba onɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture needed for healthy growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ agbi.

english: What is eating small holes in the center shoots of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot of maize plants and eats the fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni eyeɔ baai heei lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, which thrive in hot, dry weather and suck the sap from tomato leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi lɛ amli, ni ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ tomato baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots decompose, they leave natural plant food in the soil.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite lɛ Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is running out of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ?

english: You can observe your crops for signs like pale yellow leaves, thin stems, slow growth, or smaller fruit yields compared to previous harvests.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli kɛha okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, amɛdalɛ blɛoo, loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the fruits are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be damaged underground by microscopic pests called nematodes. Weak roots cannot support the heavy fruit bunch, causing the tree to collapse.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the direct sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground and helps the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ awo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller individual fruits.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko bafeɔ bibioo.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plant without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, heavy rains that soak the soil too long, or a lack of insect pollinators.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi, tamɔ trukaa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kpe. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo koolooi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa

english: When water collects around cassava roots without draining away, it starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efooo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atswa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct heat. Plantain plants grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade to shield young cocoa from the sun while also providing quick food and income for your household.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni dɔlɛ fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii oya kɛ shika aha oshiabii lɛ.

english: What crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting several years for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii babaoo koni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Fast-growing food crops like plantain, cassava, maize, and cocoyam can be planted between young trees. They provide immediate food and harvestable produce during the three to five years before trees like cocoa or citrus start bearing fruit.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ. Amɛhaa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nibii ni abaanyɛ akpa afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani tsei tamɔ kookoo loo citrus jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Can I grow mango trees and cashew trees together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu mango kɛ cashew tsei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, you can intercrop mango and cashew trees, but you must leave enough space between them. Both develop large, wide canopies as they mature, so proper spacing prevents them from blocking sunlight from each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu mango kɛ cashew tsei. Shi ehe miihia ni oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa. Mɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmei agbo ni mli kwɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi hulu la ni baa amɛhe lɛ naa.

english: How long does an orange tree take to start giving fruit after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akutu tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grafted orange seedlings usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years. If you plant orange trees directly from seeds, they will take much longer—about 6 to 8 years—and may produce lower quality fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛji akɛ odu o-citrus tso lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaahe be babaoo, aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many flowers before the fruits actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally drop excessive flowers due to environmental stress like sudden dry weather, strong winds, or insect pests. Ensuring adequate soil moisture during early flowering and controlling pests helps more flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi fe nine yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do cashew trees survive dry seasons better than most other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei yeɔ wala yɛ fɛ̃i be mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cashew trees possess deep taproots that reach deep underground water supplies, along with tough leaves that conserve moisture, making them naturally drought-resistant and suitable for dry regions.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛfata baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ he. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehi kɛha hei ni hɔmɔ yɔɔ.

english: Can cocoa trees grow directly under full open sunlight without shade?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Mature cocoa trees can survive in full sun if well-fertilized, but young cocoa requires shade to prevent leaf burn. Even for adult trees, light canopy shade protects against heat stress and helps trees live longer.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji akɛ awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Shi esa akɛ afee kookoo bibii lɛ shade koni baa lɛ akashã. Tsei ni eda po Ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: What causes the leaves on my orange trees to turn yellow and curl up?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on citrus trees are usually caused by a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, attacks from sap-sucking insects like aphids, or root damage from waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tsofai ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ tutuamɔ, loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ citrus tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa.

english: Is it safe and beneficial to keep goats and sheep on a farm with crop trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaakwɛ tooi kɛ tooi yɛ ŋmɔji ni adu tsei yɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Yes, raising sheep and goats alongside tree crops is beneficial because their manure enriches the soil with nutrients. However, you must construct fences or tether them away from young crops so they do not eat the foliage.
ga: Hɛɛ, tooi kɛ tooi ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ otswa gbogbo loo gbogbo kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkaye baai lɛ.

english: How can I prevent weeds from overtaking a large orchard of mixed tree crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye tso yibii abɔɔ agbo ko ni akɛ tsei ni efutu mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cover crops like leguminous ground plants or intercropping with short-season food crops suppresses weed growth, keeps the soil moist, and enriches the soil with nitrogen while your main trees grow.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo nibii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii ni heɔ be kuku lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa nitrogen kroko baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni otso titri lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do imported maize seeds often get ruined by weevils faster than local maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii gbeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ oya fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Imported seeds are usually bred for specific weather conditions and high yields in their native countries, but they often lack natural resistance to local pests like the weevils found in Ghana. Local varieties have adapted over time with tougher outer skins that make it harder for weevils to bore into them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛbɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmei ni anaa yɛ Ghana lɛ. Kuu lɛ mli henɔi lɛ etsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli kɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni mli wa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmei lɛ akɛ eeebote mli.

english: How can I tell if the seed maize I buy in the market is good quality for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ?

english: Good quality seed maize should be clean, whole, free from small holes or powdery dust, and uniform in size. Check for signs of mold or dark spots near the tip, and make sure the seeds are hard and completely dry when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe atse, ni efee muu, ni bu bibii loo sũ bɛ mli, ni elɛɛmɔ afee ekome. Kwɛmɔ tip lɛ nɔ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela loo he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ he. Ni kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa kɛ́ okɛ onineshi tsɔne miimɔ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant maize seeds that have already been slightly damaged by insects?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ŋmeii efite fioo lɛ?

english: Insects often eat the inner part of the seed called the germ, which holds the embryo of the new plant. If the germ is destroyed, the seed will not sprout at all; if it is only partially eaten, the seedling will grow very weak and produce a small yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mligbɛ fã ni atsɛɔ lɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. ni toɔ tso mli fɔmɔ kotokui heei Kɛji akpata helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahiɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kwraa. Kɛji akɛ aye fã ko pɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ waa ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Why do small insects like weevils keep appearing in my harvested maize even after I tie the bags tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo lolo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the maize grains while the crop is still on the farm. When you harvest and bag the grain, those eggs hatch into larvae inside your sealed bags and eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Beni okpaa dumɔwui lɛ ni okɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: What is the best simple way to protect my harvested maize from weevils without using expensive chemical powders?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mi-abele ni akpaa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Make sure your maize is thoroughly sun-dried until it is hard and snaps when bitten. Storing the dry grain in airtight (hermetic) bags or mixing it with clean wood ash or dried neem leaf powder prevents weevils from breathing and attacking the crop naturally.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ o-corn lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni ebaakumɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ lɛ ŋmɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli loo akɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo neem baa ni egbi lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkatutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does leaving maize to dry on the stalk in the field increase the chance of bug attacks?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni ashiɔ ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ kooloi baatutua amɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Yes, leaving mature maize in the field for too long exposes it to wild weevils, beetles, rain, and mold. It is better to harvest as soon as the husks turn brown and dry the cobs on raised wooden platforms at home.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ni ashiɔ ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaatsɔɔ koo mli ŋmeii, ladybugs, nugbɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ ni ogbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso ni akɛdamɔ shi yɛ shia lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I prepare my harvested maize so that local institutions like the school feeding program will buy from me?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ koni maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhei tamɔ skul niyenii hamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ midɛŋ?

english: Large institutional buyers look for clean, weevil-free maize that is properly dried and free of stones or mold. Sorting your maize into clean, uniform bags and ensuring low moisture content makes your grain reliable and preferred over poor-quality alternatives.
ga: Nitsumɔhei wuji ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ ŋmãa ni he tse ni ŋmeii bɛ mli ni agbi jogbaŋŋ. Tɛi loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ o-ŋmã lɛ to kotokui ni mli tse, ni yaa nɔ daa, ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha o-ŋmã lɛ afee nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni asumɔɔɔ fe nɔ krokomɛi ni baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do buyers offer me very low prices for my maize right after harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa jara ni baa shi waa haa mi yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Right after harvest, many farmers flood the market with maize at the same time, driving prices down. Grain with high moisture content also spoils quickly, forcing farmers to sell fast at lower prices instead of drying and holding it for when demand increases.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ ŋmãa miiwo jara lɛ nɔ, ni enɛ eha jara miiba shi. Dumɔwui ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hu fiteɔ oya. Enɛ nyɛɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ jara ni baa shi. Mohu ɔ, a gbiɔ mɛ nɛ a kɛ toɔ ke a hia ní ɔmɛ fuu.

english: Why do many maize farmers in my community struggle to make money even when they work hard every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná nɔ ko eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtsuɔ nii waa daa afi lɛ?

english: Low earnings usually come from using low-quality or damaged seeds, losing large parts of the harvest to pests during storage, and selling produce immediately at low harvest prices instead of storing good grain to sell when market prices rise.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shika ni baa shi lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo ni efite ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Nibii ni akpaa lɛ ateŋ babaoo laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ hewɔ. kɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa jara ni baa shi nɔ Yɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ni akɛtoɔ koni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara nɔ jara tee hiɛ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Is it better for me to buy fresh certified seeds every season or save seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi loo makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Saved seeds are free and adapted to local pests, but their yield decreases over time. Fresh certified seeds give much higher yields in the field, but they must be bought from trusted sellers and stored carefully to keep them safe from pests before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ aheee nɔ ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli. Shi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi esa akɛ ahe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ dɛŋ, ni akɛto jogbaŋŋ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite lɛ dani adu.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without big cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This makes them stretch high and thin to reach the sun, leaving them too weak to form big, healthy corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛfee mlɛo koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa.

english: How deep into the ground should I bury my maize seeds during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about two to three fingers deep (around 3 to 5 centimeters). If you plant them too deep, the young shoot gets tired before reaching the surface; if too shallow, birds might eat them or the hot sun will dry them out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3-5. Kɛji odu amɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui dani amɛshɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji amɛmli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbi.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops roll inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward as a natural survival trick to protect themselves from losing water. By rolling up, the plant shrinks the area exposed to the strong sun, saving moisture until the evening cool arrives.
ga: Oyitsɔi ni oootsɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa yɛ ohe lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ hei ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young plants usually mean the crop is missing nitrogen, which is essential plant food for staying green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the roots will help the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ baafata he Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my maize even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-abele lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are like unwanted guests that eat your food—they quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your maize all the nutrients it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ yɛ oniyenii nɔ—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop yields drop if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows maize diseases to build up. Swapping maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil's strength naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be ni ekɛ hela baaba abele mli. ŋmãa tsakemɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, a heavy rainstorm will wash away the fertilizer before the plant roots can swallow it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp or just before a light shower so the nutrients sink gently into the ground.
ga: Dabi, ahum baatswa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ ami lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo fioo dani nugbɔ anɛ koni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio.

english: Is it helpful to plant cassava and maize together on the same small plot?
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ Ani nakai nɔŋŋ he baaba sɛɛnamɔ loo sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together is good because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the field after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ hi ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillars hiding inside the top folds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli

english: Those holes and tiny caterpillars are caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm that eat young leaves. Spraying early with recommended treatments or applying neem water into the leaf funnels helps stop them from destroying the growing cob.
ga: bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii Mɛi ni ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛbaatsu nii mra lɛ ashwie nɔ. Aloo, kɛ akɛ neem nu fata baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa ŋmei ni miida lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise making soil mounds or ridges before planting root crops like yams or groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii dani adu shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii?

english: Loose soil mounds make it easy for tubers and pods to grow big underground without pushing against hard, packed dirt. It also helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ haa bulbs kɛ pods lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛtsɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my crops produce so many flowers, but many of them fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when they are not pollinated. If insects or wind do not transfer pollen from male to female parts, the plant sheds the unfertilized flower instead of growing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ashɛɛɛ amɛhe. Kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ pollen kɛjɛɛɛ nuu lɛ mli kɛyaaaa yoo lɛ mli Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ yibii ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell with my own eyes if a flower on my farm was successfully pollinated?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mihiŋmɛii ana akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eye omanye yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: After successful pollination, the flower petals will naturally dry up and fall off, but the base stem will stay green and start swelling into a small, firm fruit.
ga: Yɛ pollination ni eye omanye sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Shi shishigbɛ tso lɛ baakã he ahi eŋɔli ni ebɔi shwiemɔ ni etsɔ aduawai bibii ni mli wa.

english: How do I perform hand pollination on my crops to make sure they produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ miniji awo fɔfɔii amli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo?

english: You can use a small soft brush or carefully pick a male flower and gently rub its pollen onto the sticky center of a female flower early in the morning.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ brɔsh bibioo ni yɔɔ blɛoo atsu nii loo okɛ blɛoo ajie fɔfɔi hii lɛ. Okɛ pollen awo pistil fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ mli leebi.

english: Why are some of the fruits on my crop growing out misshapen or unevenly formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ efite loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Uneven or crooked fruit usually means the flower only received a small amount of pollen on one side, which causes only part of the fruit to develop fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni ejaaa loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ efã kome. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fã ko pɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is early morning the best time for me to check and pollinate my farm flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaakwɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛ amɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: In the early morning, flowers are fully open, pollen is fresh and sticky, and the heat of the sun has not yet dried out the flower parts.
ga: Leebi lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi. sticky fresh flower pollen Ni hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ fãi lɛ agbi lolo.

english: Will hand pollinating my crops actually increase my total harvest compared to relying on natural insects?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ haa miyibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: Yes, because natural insects often miss many flowers. Hand pollination ensures almost every healthy flower gets fertilized, leading to significantly higher yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi srɔtoi babaoo. Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baa.

english: How many days after pollination should I expect to see tiny fruits starting to form?
ga: Yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, yɛ gbii enyiɛ mli esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana aduawai bibii ni baabɔi feemɔ?

english: For most crops, you will start seeing visible swelling at the base of the flower within 3 to 7 days after successful pollination.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Obaaje shishi ona fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ ni efuu yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 7 mli yɛ pollination ni ye omanye lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell that my fruit is fully mature and ready for harvesting just by looking at it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi yibii lɛ ekwɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can spot readiness by changes in skin color, drying up of the tendril or stalk closest to the fruit, and a full, filled-out shape.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona hesaamɔ kɛtsɔ hewolonɔ su tsakemɔ lɛ nɔ. Tendrils loo stems ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai ni egbi lɛ kɛ mfoniri ni eyi obɔ lɛ

english: What is the best way to harvest my crop without damaging the rest of the plant for future yield?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mifiteee tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ koni mikɛfee wɔsɛɛ?

english: Use clean, sharp shears or a knife to cut the fruit stem cleanly rather than pulling or twisting forcefully, which can tear the plant bark and invite diseases.
ga: Kɛ sɛkɛs ni he tse ni naa wa loo kakla afo aduawai lɛ ashishifã lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbala loo oootsɔ mli waa Enɛ baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli ni ekɛ hela aba.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I harvest the pods too early before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ dani amɛshwere kwraa?

english: Harvesting too early results in lower weight, poor flavor, and seeds that are not fully developed, which reduces both market value and quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa mɔ he waaa, ehaaa ehiɛ afee fɛo, ni dumɔwui lɛ hu shwereee jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jarayeli mli jara kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block direct light and retain soil moisture, the harsh sun scorches the leaves and causes them to dry out.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ni baatsi la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi.

english: This is caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and humid conditions. High moisture stays on pods when trees are overcrowded or surrounded by weeds, allowing the fungus to spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Fungal tutuamɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli Fɛ̃i babaoo hiɔ tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo jwɛi ebɔle ehe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every year make the tubers smaller each harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy-feeds on specific nutrients in the ground. Planting it repeatedly without resting the land or rotating with crops like cowpeas exhausts the soil, leaving fewer nutrients for new tubers to grow big.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, bulb heei lɛ daa ni amɛnáaa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and chupons from my cocoa trees when they are growing fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ be mli ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Extra branches and chupons waste the tree's food and water on leaf growth instead of pod growth. Removing them allows air and light to circulate through the tree, which prevents diseases and directs energy into forming bigger pods.
ga: Niji kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe pod dalɛ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ pods wuji.

english: Why did my maize leaves burn and wither after I put chemical fertilizer right against the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ shãa ni egboɔ beni akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated mineral salts that draw moisture directly out of plant tissues if placed too close. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in a small ring or row so the roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi inchi fioo ko pɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii amli. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why are my cocoa tree flowers falling off before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from lack of water, insect attacks, or poor soil nutrients. Trees naturally drop surplus flowers they cannot support with available food and water.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni faaa amɛmli, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ mli baa. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do improved hybrid maize seeds perform better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred for high yield, fast growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose these strong genetic traits in the next generation, producing weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsɔse amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛdara oya ni amɛnyɛŋ helai aba. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do mirid insects attack my cocoa trees more during the transition from rainy season to dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mirid kooloi lɛ tutuaa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ kɛyaa fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mirids, or akate, prefer soft new shoots and young pods that develop after the main rains. As dry weather starts, they feed heavily on these fresh green parts, sucking juices and causing dieback on branches.
ga: Mirid loo Akate sumɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ je shishi Amɛyeɔ nɛkɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ nɛɛ babaoo, ni amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ nine lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn pale and the plant falls over when water sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu edamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water starves plant roots of oxygen, causing them to rot under the soil. When the root system rots, the plant cannot support itself in the wind or absorb nutrients, leading to yellowing and collapsing.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aye oxygen. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shwiemɔ he okadii baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off during the peak dry season without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization from happening. When pollen fails due to high temperatures, the flower dies and drops off without developing into a tomato.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni haa fɔmɔ baaa Kɛji pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛtsɔko tomatoi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or floods the roots so they cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli, ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ dumɔ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can trap nitrogen food directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, they leave that free food in the soil for future crops like maize or yam.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nakai niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade plants like plantains around them when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni aná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle ehe lɛ beni adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that shield young cocoa trees from direct heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce bigger, heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. When the plant feels stressed by drought or extreme heat, it drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ hɔmɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa miihao lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know if worms are eating my maize, and what signs should I look out for?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii miiye mi-ŋmãa lɛ? Ni mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ okwɛ ohe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he?

english: Look inside the central leaf funnel of your maize plants for small ragged holes and fine crumbs that look like sawdust. Worms like fall armyworms hide deep inside these leaves during the day, eating the newest plant growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ o-corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli. koni ana bu bibioo ko ni etse kɛ fãji bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai nɛɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ tsei heei ni miida fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my cassava roots from rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dani akpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, wet soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni mli wa lɛ ajo foi kɛya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when there is enough land space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal water, fertilizer, and light before your crops can reach them. Even if space looks open, the roots of weeds under the soil take food away from your crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Eyɛ mli akɛ jɛmɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ Shi jwɛi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hu gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it risky to plant all my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry period before the heavy rains start properly. If your seeds sprout after that first rain and then face weeks without water, the young shoots will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni okɛ hiɛ ni nu bɛ mli otsii babaoo. Tsobii bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds sprout well, but the seedlings grow thin, tall, and weak before dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ? Shi ani dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɔ, ni amɛhe waaa dani amɛgboiɔ?

english: Seedlings stretch out thin and tall when they do not get enough direct sunlight. They waste all their energy reaching upward for light instead of growing thick stems and strong roots to support themselves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee shɔŋŋ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkwɔ kɛya la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, mo tsɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ o kɛ ye bua o he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an important food element in the soil. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away from crop roots, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ shwiemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps feed the maize plants growing alongside them.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer right next to my seed when I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ emasɛi lɛ? Dumɔwui be mli ni adu?

english: Concentrated fertilizer acts like salt on tender young plant roots and seeds. If placed directly against the seed without enough water, it can burn and destroy the seed before it has a chance to sprout.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ dumɔwui anɔ. Kɛ akɛwo dumɔwui anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ ashã ni amɛfite dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear, wide-open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their foliage and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ buɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which ensures larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi, ni no baaha plantains lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe afee mlɛo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on as many leaves as possible to make energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they might rot and helps the plant produce large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I build soil mounds across a sloped piece of land instead of down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo gɔŋ lɛ shishi?
