english: Building mounds across a slope acts like mini-dams that catch rainwater and hold soil in place. Digging them down the hill creates pathways for rain to wash away fertile topsoil and roots.
ga: Gɔŋ ko ni ama yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ faa bibioo ko ni mɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ atsa amɛ kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ tsɔɔ gbɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishifãi ni jara wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves and fruit during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai kɛ aduawai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and wet leaves create the ideal environment for plant fungi to grow and spread. Spacing plants further apart and clearing weeds allows air to circulate, keeping the leaves dry and reducing spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha tsei amli ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. He ni tsei kɛ jwɛi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stunting the growth of the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ edaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. As they suck out the plant's juices, they inject a fluid that distorts leaf growth and slows the plant down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ Amɛshwieɔ nu ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to turn soft and rot if left in wet soil too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava roots stay in overly saturated, waterlogged soil for extended periods, roots cannot breathe and soil bacteria take over, causing the starch to decompose into water and rot.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu fe nine ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ nu mli ni egboɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of small holes and looking ragged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai eyi kɛ bu bibii ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed inside the leaf whorls when the plant is young. Spraying recommended organic or chemical pesticides early in the morning or late evening helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning light yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or compost will help restore healthy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why will my maize yield be small if I plant seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, offering necessary shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I test if my stored seeds will sprout well before I plant them on my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing ten seeds on a damp paper towel or wet cloth for four days. If eight or more sprout, your seeds are fresh and healthy enough to plant in the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Anáa enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛwoɔ wolo ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo mama ni mli efɔ gbii ejwɛ Kɛji ŋmeii 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai je kpo lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ efee ehee ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu yɛ osɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop in intense afternoon heat to reduce water loss through evaporation. If the plant springs back up by the evening or early morning, it is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe ni egbee shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi Kɛji tso lɛ da ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big green leaves above ground but very thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ?

english: This often happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen makes leaves grow large, while potassium is needed for root and tuber growth, so balancing your fertilizer will improve tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ daraa. Yɛ be mli ni potassium he hiaa kɛha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tuber lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my field early when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔji amli mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal essential sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks ensures your crops get a strong start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la ni he hiaa, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ mli niyenii oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower stem leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ yitso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a critical nutrient for crop growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure helps restore healthy green leaves and grow bigger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmãa toi lɛ adara.

english: Planting cassava too close creates competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, leafy plants with very small cassava tubers under the ground instead of thick, harvestable roots.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before they can grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or when pests attack the blossoms. Keeping soil moisture consistent and protecting plants from extreme heat helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my corn seeds when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady, wet rain for a few consecutive days before planting. Sowing into dry soil causes seeds to rot or sprout weakly if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani oduɔ nii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ fioo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids transmitting a plant virus. Spraying recommended organic or chemical insecticides early prevents insects from ruining the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I not just save and replant seeds from my last hybrid maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ kɛkɛ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their high yield strength and disease resistance in the second generation. Purchasing fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong germination and high production.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stunted even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients to grow tall and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miifite oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvesting or stored in hot, unventilated spaces. Handling yams carefully and keeping them on raised racks in cool, shady structures helps them last for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato tsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto shwɛmɔhei ni awó nɔ yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and suckers from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra side branches forces the tomato plant to direct its energy into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on useless extra leaves and stems.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baabi hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ dɛŋ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils when the sun gets very hot around noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to trap moisture inside and prevent the plant from drying out.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off before turning into fruits during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when under heat or water stress because they do not have enough energy and water to support developing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewalɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ bɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big green leaves, but producing small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or water, it spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmei baato ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, so it strips nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growing shoots at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why can't I grow cool-weather crops like apples on my farm here in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ tamɔ apolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ biɛ lɛ?

english: Certain crops require a long cold winter season to trigger flowering and fruit development, which does not happen in tropical, warm climates like Ghana.
ga: Tsei komɛi biɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo he hewalɛ. Enɛ baaa mli yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Ghana.

english: Why do my okra seeds take so long to sprout when I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Okra seeds have hard outer shells that need steady soil moisture to soften before the seedling inside can break through and sprout.
ga: Okra dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be koni efee blɛoo dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot so fast during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and cool humidity during the rainy season allow the fungus that causes black pod disease to multiply and spread quickly across cocoa trees.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ babaoo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a light wind blows through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily rot in overly wet soil or get damaged by soil pests, making the heavy plant unstable in windy conditions.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni baanyɛ afite oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine nɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afite lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii ni ehiɛɛɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do my yams rot quickly when I store them inside a closed room after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are living roots that continue to breathe; without proper air circulation in a cool, ventilated shed, heat and moisture build up and cause decay.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ ŋwɛitsu ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa amɛhe naa ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow so slowly when weeds are left around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from cowpea roots, starving the crop of the resources it needs to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tsina shishifãi amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nibii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or has too much water sitting around the roots. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling and pale cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and prevents the plant from growing large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná yitsei wuji ni wa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to trim off extra branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning allows fresh air and sunlight to flow through the tree, which stops moisture from building up and prevents diseases like Black Pod from destroying your cocoa.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ abua naa, ni ehaaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ afite kookoo lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans restores the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni akɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three consecutive heavy rains that soak deep into the earth, ensuring young roots will not dry out if rains pause for a few days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil food, leading to thin stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with aggressive roots that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my harvested grains get ruined by insects so quickly when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ lɛ, ŋmeii fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects and mould thrive when grains are stored with trapped moisture inside them. Sun-drying your grains thoroughly until they are completely hard before bagging keeps pests away.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to ni nu emɔ amɛmli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe wa kwraa dani awo amɛ kotoku mli lɛ, no tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK will help the leaves regain their deep green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cassava roots even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone isn't enough; hard or compacted soil stops roots from expanding, and lack of nutrients like potassium keeps them small. Loosening the soil deeply before planting and adding organic compost gives tubers the space and nutrients they need to grow large.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee bibii. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches and clearing surrounding weeds allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and develop yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings obtained from certified extension officers is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Tsoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni aduɔ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during strong winds. Propping up the main stem with strong bamboo poles or branched wooden forks helps support the weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni niji yɔɔ mli lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ muji lɛ atsu nii kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get soft rotten spots at the bottom while still on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ soft rot yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom end rot, happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching with dry grass helps prevent the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ akafite.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or lack of water. Watering your tomato plants consistently at the base early in the morning keeps the soil cool and helps the flowers stay on to produce fruit.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tomato tsei lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my watermelon plants grow plenty of big leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon tsei lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes watermelons spend all their energy growing thick leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set more flowers and grow bigger melons.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha watermelon lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni mli tse. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai adumɔ najiaŋ lɛ Kɛ́ otsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔii babaoo ni eha omelons lɛ afee wuji.

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and start to dry up. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings rather than a clean white color, your crop is ripe.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ egbɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if the soil is soaked with too much water or damaged by dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ efite.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem burns the plant's skin and roots because the chemicals draw water out of the tissue. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem in the soil where side roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofai gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ fãji amli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in hot, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun rays and keep the air and soil humid during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ amɛnaa. ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants need as much sunlight on their leaves as possible to create food and swell the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, preventing rot and allowing leaves to capture sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fitemɔ naa ni oha baai lɛ aná hulu la lɛ.

english: Why is it best to plant my seeds immediately after the first major rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting after the first good rain gives the seeds the steady water they need to sprout quickly and build deep roots before any brief dry spell returns.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant will begin to crack open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop uses and allows pests and diseases that love maize to multiply in the soil. Changing crops or planting beans helps rest and feed the land.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and produce small fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, sunlight, and water that your crops need to grow. When weeds overcrowd the field, your crops starve and cannot produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Beni jwɛi ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ miiye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to survive instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like material in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi-baby corn baai lɛ kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: This is a sign of caterpillar feeding, such as the Fall Armyworm, which eats its way through the center leaves of young maize. Treating the crop early protects the plant before the growing tip is destroyed.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he dani eshishifãi ni miida lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that dry out easily under harsh, direct heat. Shade trees or plantain plants shield young cocoa from scorching sunlight and help the soil retain moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei loo plantains ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do many farmers plant maize and cassava together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground. Intercropping allows you to harvest food twice from the same plot without the crops competing for space early on.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ fiofio yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe wooo he ko he akaŋ mra.

english: Why do my crops grow much better on land where I previously planted groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they die, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil and feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ amɛgboi lɛ, nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Rolling leaves is a protective habit maize uses to save water. By curling its leaves inward, the plant exposes less surface to the sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji su ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ hulu la fioo nɔ. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up soil air pockets, drowning the roots. Without oxygen, the cassava roots weaken, allowing fungi in the wet soil to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa ni egboɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or late at night?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before heat rises, and wet leaves dry quickly in the sun, which stops leaf rot and fungal diseases from growing overnight.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Why shouldn't I pour granular fertilizer right against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. Placing it right against the main stem can burn the plant's skin and shallow roots; it should be buried a few inches away where roots can stretch out safely to drink it.
ga: Mineral salts ni mli wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofu lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ bo teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe shweshweeshwe koni amɛnu nu.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck the plant's juice, they inject chemicals that cause the leaf to warp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ Amɛshwieɔ tsofai ni haa tsei lɛ ahe baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I know that my underground yams are fully grown and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams indicate maturity above ground when their vines and leaves stop growing green and begin to turn dry and yellow, showing that the plant has finished storing energy into the root.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni wain tso lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy rain wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep woody taproots; instead, they have shallow underground mats. When soil gets soft from heavy rain, strong winds easily pull these shallow roots out of the mud.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ tsei. Mohu ɔ, a ngɛ zugba a sisi ngmahi nɛ a mi kuɔ we. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛɛmɛi jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep turning yellow and dying when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the seedlings while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when planting them into the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the plant to waste energy trying to correct its growth direction, leading to weak shoots and smaller tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni akɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ajaje gbɛ ni tso lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni faaa.

english: How do I choose the right plantain suckers from an old field to plant on my new land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a broad, heavy base. Avoid 'water suckers' with wide, flat leaves, as sword suckers grow much stronger, resist wind better, and produce healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante tu’ ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni tsii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘nu tso’ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Ejaakɛ klante lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa fe no kwraa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves in a V-pattern is a clear sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer, such as urea or well-decomposed animal manure, helps the leaves turn green again and supports stalk growth.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛaawo mli. Enɛ baaye abua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black, dry spots at the bottom of tomatoes are known as blossom-end rot, caused by inconsistent watering and a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni egbi ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium awo aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or damage from tiny pests like thrips. Ensuring the soil stays moist and providing mild shade during peak dry periods helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nibii bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao amɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha ŋmɔlɔ fioo ko. Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe fɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the middle leaves of my maize plants and leaving small green powder inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central leaves (whorl) of young maize. Applying early treatments like neem leaf extract or recommended biopesticides directly into the plant whorl destroys the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii mra lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I suppress weeds on my farm without buying expensive chemical weedkillers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Planting fast-growing cover crops like cowpea or egusi melon between your main crops creates a leafy ground cover that blocks sunlight from weed seeds, stopping weeds from sprouting while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ cowpea loo egusi melon yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa yɔɔ mli ni haa hulu lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anɔ lɛ baa. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to go to the extra trouble of placing tall stakes for my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa haomɔ kroko ni ji tsei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni mikɛwoɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the roots. It also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil diseases, which helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tsu nii kɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu mli egbiɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ kpaaa gbee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make the soil richer for the crop I plant next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei dumɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha tsei ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts have beneficial soil microbes living on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the roots break down after harvest, they leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fã yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the crop runs out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the primary plant food needed to build strong green leaves and produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso mli niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ ni eha toi wuji ni wa aba.

english: Cassava tubers need loose, breathable soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the ground for too long, the roots drown from lack of air and fungal diseases move in to cause rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mumɔ baanyɛ ashɛ he koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baabote mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baaba.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out completely, pepper plants experience high stress and drop their flowers to save energy, preventing fruits from forming.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ waa. ni okɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same land where I harvested yams last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa sweet potato yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yams take a massive amount of nutrients out of the earth during growth. Planting cowpeas afterwards naturally traps nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, restoring fertility for future crops.
ga: Sweet potatoes jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tight and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viral diseases, which cripple normal leaf expansion and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it better for me to sow my maize right after the first major rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sowing immediately after the first major rain allows seeds to absorb maximum soil moisture and capture the quick surge of natural nutrients released by the dry soil when it first gets wet.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa babaoo, ni amɛŋɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ oya beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds hit the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the surface. When heavy bunches grow at the top and the ground becomes soft from rain, strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi ku we nɛ e kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Beni jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why must I clear weeds away while my groundnut seedlings are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop seedlings and steal precious water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, choking the young groundnut plants before they can build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu ni jara wa, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmei dumɔwui anaa dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees produce sour fruit even though the tree looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli edɔ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Citrus fruit turns sweet only when the tree receives plenty of direct sunshine and key soil nutrients like potassium while the fruit matures, allowing the plant to convert natural acids into sugar.
ga: Citrus aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei tsakeɔ adebɔɔ mli acids lɛ amɛfeɔ sugars.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newest growth at the top, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants losing all their leaves during the dry season? Are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ani amɛmiigboi?

english: Cassava plants shed leaves during the dry season to save water and protect themselves. The roots underground stay alive, and the plant will grow new green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baahi shi. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei eŋɔli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do people say I should plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before I plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans, cowpeas, and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that land later, the maize feeds on that leftover plant food and grows stronger.
ga: Beans, cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye tsei aniyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and tiny dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji bibii ni tsuɔ waa yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That damage is caused by young caterpillars, such as the fall armyworm, that hide inside the funnel of the plant and eat the tender leaves. Catching them early with simple remedies or targeted sprays prevents severe damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii tamɔ cutworms. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ tsei akutsei amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii Amɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ mlɛo Aloo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nibii ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ.

english: Why must I clear all the weeds around my crops before putting fertilizer on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer away from your plant roots. Clearing the ground first ensures your crops get all the food you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Kɛ́ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛtsu nii lɛ.

english: Why should I stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need lots of sunlight to feed the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines off the dirt onto stakes allows all leaves to get sun while keeping them away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baa fɛɛ baa nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot days, very dry soil, or insect damage. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ, tamɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔji yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the dirt with dry plant material, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the soil. It holds water in the ground longer and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why did the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest grow much smaller cobs than the seeds I bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmãa bibii kwraa fe nɔ ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only during their first planting. Saving and replanting seeds from those crops leads to weaker plants and smaller yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia planted beside them to act as natural umbrellas until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu la ni fa lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with thick bushy leaves, but the tubers inside the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded closely together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo beni tsei ebua amɛhe naa babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Giving them consistent moisture and proper organic manure helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ baa daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crop have ragged holes and small dark droppings inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip (the whorl) of the maize plant during the day and eats the tender leaves from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered when the soil dries out completely and then gets flooded with water suddenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua baa trukaa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the same soil nutrients every season, so planting it continuously drains the soil completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu abele be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hoɔ kwraa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support vegetables without buying expensive chemical testing kits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ aduawai anɔ ni miheee tsofa ni jara wa ni akɛkaa tsofa lɛ?

english: Healthy soil feels crumbly in your hands, holds moisture without becoming sticky clay, smells fresh like dark earth, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter that show active life under the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ oniji amli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ. Eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni egboi ni eshwɛ ni tsɔɔ wala yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a heavy storm hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni ahum ni naa wa baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread sideways rather than deep into the earth. If insects bore into the root base or if the soil is too loose, the weight of heavy fruits causes the entire tree to tip over during strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kooloi bibii bote shishifã lɛ shishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse tsɔ. Yibii lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do I need to erect long bamboo stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight powers the leaves to create energy, which is then sent down into the ground to make large, fat yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfee hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni efee ŋmeii agboi ni mli ewo fɔ.

english: Why did my seeds fail to come up after I planted them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch of hot weather. If the soil dries out completely right after seeds sprout, the delicate tiny roots die underground before they can reach the surface.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why should I water my cocoa trees in April when it is not the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ nu yɛ April mli? Be mli ni jeee nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ?

english: Watering your cocoa farm during dry periods like April keeps the trees healthy and encourages them to grow pods outside the traditional harvest season, giving you extra income throughout the year.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ April mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdu ŋmɔji yɛ kusum naa ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa onáa shika kroko yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Which months of the year do cocoa trees normally give the highest harvest in Ghana?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ nɛɛ mli ji be ni cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce their largest main crop between September and December because of the main rainfall patterns, followed by a smaller light crop earlier in the year.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli kookoo tsei woɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni fe fɛɛ yɛ September kɛ December teŋ. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ni adu yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. This color change shows that the beans inside are fully mature and ready to be picked.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to work with community leaders or farmer groups when selling harvested cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ okɛ akutsoŋbii ahiɛnyiɛlɔi loo okwaafoi akui baatsu nii kɛ́ oohɔ̃ɔ kookoo ni akpa lɛ?

english: Selling through trusted community leaders or cooperatives helps combine harvested crops into larger batches, making it easier to arrange certified weighing, transport, and reliable buyers.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ kɛtsɔ akutsoŋ hiɛnyiɛlɔi loo nitsumɔhe nine ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ feɔ ekome kɛfeɔ kui wuji. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaha shwiili ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, nibii ni akɛmajeɔ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aha.

english: Will applying water to my farm during hot months keep young cocoa pods from falling off?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ akagbee shi?

english: Yes, extreme heat and dry soil cause trees to drop young pods to save energy. Giving the soil moisture during hot periods helps the trees keep their pods attached so they can grow to full size.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Is it possible to get pods on my cocoa trees outside the usual harvest months?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akwɛ pods yɛ cacao tso nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Yes, using modern farming methods such as dry-season irrigation allows cocoa trees to flower and produce healthy pods outside the standard major harvest season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I tear cocoa pods off the branches using my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ minine shwieɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Plucking pods by hand damages the flower cushion on the tree stem where future pods grow. Using a sharp hook or tool protects the cushion so the tree can produce more flowers next season.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niji jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ, efiteɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ baajɛ mli aba lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo dɛŋdade ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ matrɛs lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some cocoa farms yield abundant pods while neighboring farms yield very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Farms produce more pods when they receive consistent water, good shade, and proper soil care. Farms that suffer from dry soil or poor management produce far fewer pods.
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ baawo pods babaoo kɛji amɛná nu daa. eyɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Okwaafoi ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: What happens after all the harvested cocoa from our farms is brought together in one place?
ga: Mɛni baa beni abua kookoo ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ wɔŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa yɛ he kome sɛɛ?

english: Once harvested, the cocoa beans are pooled together after fermentation and drying so they can be accurately weighed, graded for quality, and sold off in bulk to licensed buying companies.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ, akɛ amɛ feɔ ekome yɛ be mli ni amɛfee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ esusu Precisely graded yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ naa ni ahɔ̃ɔ babaoo aha nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni amɛheɔ nii lɛ.

english: How does hot, dry weather affect the growth of cocoa pods early in the year?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ saa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: High temperatures dry out the soil quickly, which can slow down pod growth and cause leaves to drop, making artificial watering essential for maintaining steady growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha pod lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha baai lɛ afite. Enɛ haa nu ni akɛfee lɛ he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. This often happens in exhausted soils or after heavy rains wash nutrients away, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce mostly leaves and very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put their energy into growing vines instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so they require very little added fertilizer compared to maize.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, cowpea biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he.

english: Young cocoa trees scorch easily under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create living shade umbrellas, protecting cocoa seedlings from heat and heat stress during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to put up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato tso ko he gbɛjianɔ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high off the ground so they can capture maximum sunlight to feed the underground tubers. It also improves airflow around the leaves, preventing moisture build-up that leads to fungal diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying with organic neem oil or soapy water helps clear these pests before they stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛha tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet without proper drainage, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack the tubers. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates too drastically. Keeping soil evenly moist with grass mulch protects the roots and encourages the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cabbages staying soft and leafy instead of forming hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of nutrients like phosphorus during their early growth stage.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ ewaŋ kɛji akɛ ekɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ yɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainy weather even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches in water-softened soil. Staking the main stem with strong bamboo props provides external support to prevent trees from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fĩ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ koni ekaje tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects them from sun scorch, keeps the soil moist, and gives the seedlings the shelter they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akashã he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa he ko ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller fruit bunches when I let many small shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he.

english: When too many suckers grow around the main plant, they compete with it for food and water in the soil. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to direct all its energy into growing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ plantains agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn pale yellow in a V-shape down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and make food; adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores the nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eye niyenii. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they feed nitrogen into the soil naturally, which helps the maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why should I wait for rain before spreading dry chemical fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ dani mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can absorb. Putting fertilizer on dry ground can scorch and burn the roots, and much of the fertilizer will be wasted before the plant can use it.
