ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia nu koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hei ni egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fiteɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves inside the center fold of my young maize plants full of holes and small dirt pellets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the center funnel of young corn to eat the soft leaves. The dirt pellets are its droppings; early treatment is needed before the caterpillar destroys the plant's main growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Muji lɛ ji efɔfɔi. Ehe miihia ni aná tsamɔ mra. Dani ŋmeii lɛ baafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ titrii lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and getting small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or viruses carried by insects. These pests drain the leaf juices and cause distorted growth, which slows down fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ŋmeii kɛyaa lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes when the hot sun is very harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Very hot temperatures make the pollen inside tomato flowers sticky or sterile, preventing pollination. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it to save energy rather than letting it rot on the stem.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Bɔni afee ni akafee pollination Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei lɛ baashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and turn it into energy, which is then stored underground to build big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhe hulu la ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulb agboi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni eji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if heavy rain falls continuously near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yaa nɔ ebɛŋkɛɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water for too long, air cannot reach the root zone. The waterlogged tubers suffocate and soft rot fungi in the soil quickly invade and decay the tubers before they can be dug up.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifã lɛ he. Tui ni efɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua tui lɛ oya ni amɛfite dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo amɛhe.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top, showing that your soil needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni dara yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves, or by intense heat stress. Checking under the leaves and using neem oil spray can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mlikwɛmɔ kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out quickly, or if there are no insects around to pollinate them. Mulching the soil to keep it moist and cool helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya Aloo, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and leafy instead of forming a hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ baai moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form solid heads if they suffer from high heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer early on. Consistent watering and adequate plant spacing encourage the inner leaves to wrap tightly into a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji akɛ edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Aloo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he mra. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee bulb ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the tips of my maize ears bare without any seeds on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi bɛ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Bare ear tips happen when maize suffers from dry weather or lack of nutrients during the flowering period, which prevents the silks at the tip from getting fully pollinated.
ga: Toi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa siliki ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ anyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to reach direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, giving them better airflow and sunlight while protecting the plant from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ miiho baai dani eyibii lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall over because they have shallow root systems that can be weakened by underground pests like nematodes or heavy rain, making them top-heavy when the fruit bunch grows. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden fork prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni kuu lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and inspecting for pests much easier than when seeds are scattered randomly.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akwɛmɔ hu feɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning heavy tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu lɛ ashɛ he kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava under the ground is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ eda ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees always fall over or break when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo efoɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, soft trunks, and heavy fruit bunches, which make them very top-heavy. Strong winds can easily snap their stems or pull them out of the soil if proper measures are not taken.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. ni haa efeɔ mlɛo Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tso lɛ shishi loo ejie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do to protect my plantain plants when the windy season is approaching?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe beni kɔɔyɔɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: When you know strong winds are expected, you can support fruiting plantains using wooden props or bamboo stakes (propping) and ensure you have trees around your field to break the force of the wind.
ga: Beni ole akɛ akpaa gbɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei loo ŋmei tsei (nibii ni fiɔ sɛɛ) aye abua dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ, ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni oná tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe. ŋmɔji amli koni akɛfo kɔɔyɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do plantains seem to suffer more wind damage than many other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ plantains fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Plantains have large, wide leaves that catch the wind like sails. Because the plant holds a lot of weight near the top, even moderate wind gusts can cause severe lodging or stem breakage.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ lɛlɛ mli tsɔnei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ atere muji babaoo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fioo po baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ahi shi waa loo amɛkumɔ.

english: Is it better for me to clear all tall trees off my farmland before planting plantains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: No, clearing all trees leaves your crops completely exposed to harsh winds. Keeping a good balance of tall trees on your land creates a protective barrier that slows down destructive winds.
ga: Dabi, tsei fɛɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi lɛ baa.

english: How do tall trees scattered on my farm help protect my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei kakadaji ni egbɛ eshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ minibii ahe?

english: Tall trees act as natural windbreaks. Instead of strong wind hitting your delicate crops directly, the trees absorb and scatter the wind's force across the farm.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa onibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛjaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can leaving trees on my land prevent my plantain farm from being destroyed during a storm?
ga: Ani tsei ni mishiɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ ahum ko mli?

english: Yes, having a strong network of trees across your land breaks up high-speed wind currents, drastically reducing the chances of your plantain stems snapping during heavy storms.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ ni ooona lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa oya lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ plantain tsei lɛ baakumɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: How does having many trees integrated into my field affect the breeze blowing through my farm?
ga: Te tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Multiple trees disrupt direct wind paths, transforming strong, damaging gusts into a gentle breeze that passes safely over your crops without knocking them down.
ga: Tsei babaoo tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsakemɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ owo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ ni tswaa shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni etswaaa amɛ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to understand when strong winds usually occur in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni manu be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa baa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Knowing the timing of seasonal winds allows you to plan ahead—such as timing your planting dates, installing plantain props early, or planting windbreak trees before the stormy season hits.
ga: Kɛ́ ole be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa yɛ be mli lɛ baa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oto gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ, tamɔ gbii ni ooodu nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ. Dumɔwui ahe nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra loo tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ adumɔ dani ahum be lɛ aba

english: How does understanding local wind patterns help me prevent farm losses?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shishinumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni elaaje lɛ akafite?

english: Once you learn when and where strong winds blow, you can make smarter decisions on where to place sensitive crops like plantains and take protective steps before the weather causes damage.
ga: Kɛji okase be kɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa Obaanyɛ okpɛ oyiŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ plantains baawo lɛ he ni ofee nɔ ko ni baatsi enaa dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ naagbai aba.

english: How can I set up my farm layout to protect delicate crops from sudden wind storms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa trukaa lɛ he?

english: You can design your farm by planting or leaving sturdy trees along the borders and scattered within your fields to block incoming winds, shielding fragile crops like plantains underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto oŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooodu loo oooshi yɛ husu lɛ he lɛ nɔ. ni nyɛgbɛ nyɛshwã nyɛŋmɔji amli koni nyɛbu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ he. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa tamɔ anaigbɛ plantains ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and energy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the plants will help them turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ he Enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ ni eda oya.

english: Why is my cassava yield low when I plant the sticks very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ faaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava sticks are planted too close together, the roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Spacing them at least one meter apart gives the roots enough room to expand into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mita kome lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: What is eating small holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi kaabaji baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae. Spraying early with natural neem leaf extract or approved insecticides kills these pests before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Egbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree lacks water, lacks nutrients like potassium, or if there are no tiny insects (midges) around to pollinate them. Keeping leaf litter around the tree retains soil moisture and creates a good habitat for these beneficial insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu efo tso lɛ mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli, loo kɛji kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) bɛ he ni amɛbaawo amɛhe fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ náa shihilɛhe kpakpa.

english: Replanting seeds from hybrid maize leads to much lower yields and weaker plants because hybrid seeds lose their special vigor after the first generation. It is best to buy certified fresh hybrid seeds every season for a big harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi waa ni tsei lɛ baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots on the bottom during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium during irregular watering or heavy rain. Staking plants off the mud and adding lime or organic matter to the soil helps prevent this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ kɛjɛ muji lɛ mli ni akɛ lime loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground. When you harvest them, the decaying roots and leaves leave behind natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ shiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my pepper plants more when the pepper plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui babaoo beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young pepper plants have small, weak root systems that cannot easily fight against fast-growing weeds for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early gives the pepper seedlings the space and food they need to establish strong stems.
ga: Chili tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ awu ashi jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ oya koni amɛná nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa.

english: Why does my stored corn turn into fine dust and powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn turns to powder because tiny insects called grain weevils eat the insides of the kernels. Properly drying the corn until it is very hard and storing it in airtight storage bags or treated silos prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ sũ yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli nibii. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa waa ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo ŋmãa ni atsa mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Why should I remove the tiny extra branches growing out of the sides of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ sɛɛ

english: Removing those extra side shoots (suckers) forces the plant to send all its water and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on growing excess stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ (ŋmeii) lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ lɛ, ookwɛ tsei kɛ baai krokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or plantains planted next to them to block the harsh sun and keep the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Enɛ ji koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots, keeping them safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Is it good for me to plant beans in the same farm where I planted my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps your soil. Beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better while giving you two different harvests from one farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afeɔ nibii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: How do I know if caterpillars are eating my maize before the whole farm gets destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-ŋmãa lɛ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baafite?

english: Look inside the center leaves of young maize plants for tiny holes, ragged edges, or saw-dust-like dirt. Finding these signs early allows you to treat the fall armyworms before they damage the entire crop.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli kɛha bu bibii, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii, loo muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa fall armyworms dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that naturally react fast to rainfall and steal nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the water and food they need to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha otsei ni miida lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plants experience extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Watering your plants regularly and keeping the soil evenly moist helps flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially tested to resist local diseases and handle drought better. Saved seeds lose their strength over time, which leads to smaller harvests compared to certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard and cracked after a few sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ gbii babaoo ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves or compost. Covering your soil with dry grass or compost helps trap moisture in the ground and prevents the earth from baking hard under the sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ, ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows them room to expand and produce maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ha gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need space between them instead of being planted tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tubers lɛ yɔɔ gbɛ yɛ amɛteŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaabɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their underground roots do not have enough room to expand into large tubers. Planting them with proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough nutrients, water, and soil space to grow thick roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ bɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli tse baa.

english: Why should I avoid planting my cassava directly under the thick shade of big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ tsei wuji ni mli ewo muji lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy and grow tubers. Under heavy shade, the plant spends its energy growing tall, thin stems toward the light instead of developing food underground.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs. shishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ baaná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔji ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted when my soil is hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ais lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand downward into the earth as they grow. If the soil is hard or compacted, it is too tight for the root to push through easily, resulting in stunted, misshapen tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How deep should I bury my plantain suckers when setting them up in my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu plantain tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted in holes about 30 centimeters deep. This depth ensures the roots are deep enough to anchor the heavy plant against strong winds while still allowing the underground corm to sprout easily.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 30 mli. Nɛkɛ mlibotemɔ nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tso ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up into tight tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural protection mechanism to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, helping the plant save water when the soil is dry.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree shed many of its leaves when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, the air becomes very dry and soil moisture drops. Cocoa trees drop some leaves to reduce water loss, surviving the dry period by resting until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ye omanye yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high temperatures, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops the flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack the middle center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer the tender, young leaves inside the central whorl of the maize plant because these soft leaves are easiest for them to feed on and offer shelter from sunlight and predators.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ sumɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ejaakɛ nɛkɛ baai bibii nɛɛ ji nɔ ni niyenii yeɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ, ni amɛhaa hulu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ náa abobaahe.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes rot quickly when I pack them tightly inside plastic sacks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ nii lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested tubers breathe and release moisture. Packing them tightly in sealed sacks traps heat and wetness, creating an ideal environment for mold and rot to destroy the food.
ga: Tuber ni akpa ehee lɛ muɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ niyenii.

english: Does leaving weeds around my tomato plants hurt them if I am already watering them regularly?
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ebaaye mi tomato tsei lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa?

english: Yes, weeds aggressively compete with tomato plants for nutrients in the soil and root space. They also trap humidity and harbor insect pests that can carry diseases to your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ tomato tsei yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ toɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Why does my soil seem to lose its strength and produce smaller harvests after a few years of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa ni ewooo yibii yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops continuously pull nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you do not replenish the soil with organic material or give it time to rest, the land loses its vitality and cannot support heavy crop yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo ohaaa lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How can I help my farm land regain its natural strength without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can rebuild the land by adding organic material like animal manure, compost, and dead plant leaves. These feed the living organisms in the ground, which naturally restore the soil's fertility over time.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma oshikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egboi ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi haa bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens to my farm if I plant the same crop on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating crops or letting the land rest helps keep the soil balanced and strong.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does letting a portion of my farm lie fallow help my future crops?
ga: Te miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko ni mishiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miwɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When land rests, wild plants grow and rot back into the dirt, returning valuable nutrients to the earth. This quiet period allows the natural soil life to rebuild so the land is fertile again for your next planting.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihe ejɔ ehe lɛ, koo mli tsei daa ni amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ. Okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa aku sɛɛ aba je lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ be ni yɔɔ dioo nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ebɔɔ su ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect their leaves while their roots grow deep enough to handle the sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm's soil has enough life and vitality to produce good pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii kpakpai aba?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds moisture after rain, and is full of living earthworms and insects that break down dead leaves into plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Haa ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni hiɛ ka ni fiteɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa tsei lɛ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that thrives when the air around the tree is too damp and dark. Pruning excessive branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ duŋ. Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi fe nine lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekatsɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are the earthworms and small insects crawling under my plants damaging my crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: No, most small soil creatures are very good for your crops. They digest fallen leaves and turn them into natural fertilizer while digging tunnels that let air and rain reach your crop roots easily.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii babaoo hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha onibii. Amɛfoɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ashɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe mlɛo.

english: Should I clear and burn all the fallen leaves beneath my cocoa trees to keep the farm clean?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie baai ni egbee shi yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni mashã amɛ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse?

english: It is better to leave the fallen leaves to decay naturally. They act like a protective blanket that keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry spells, and decomposes into rich food for your cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha baai ni egbee shi lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni efite ni etsɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant food crops like plantain alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Food crops like plantain grow quickly to provide necessary shade for the young cocoa while also giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature and produce pods.
ga: Tsei ni akɛyeɔ niyenii tamɔ plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa aha kookoo bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil or that the ground is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies that damages the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to save water during long dry spells. The plant is not dead; it is resting and storing energy inside its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when the plant lacks calcium. Without steady water and warm weather, the plant rejects the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ calcium Kɛji nu bɛ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakpoo fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dry in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot survive direct burning sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to act as living umbrellas until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aya mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Yam vines climb stakes to spread their leaves high in the air for full sunlight. Sunlight gives the leaves energy to manufacture food and feed the growing tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with poor yields when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, spending all their energy growing tall to reach the light instead of producing food.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawuu amɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛshɛ la he moŋ fe ni eeefee niyenii.

english: Why should I cut away small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why does my field yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up crop-specific pests. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko he tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough, with seeds already adapted to take immediate advantage of early water, while farm crops take time to break out of their seeds and establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni amɛhe wa. Dumɔwui ni atsake koni akɛ nu ni yɔɔ mra amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ atsu nii yɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and retain moisture, giving the young cocoa plants time to establish strong root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ naa be ni ekɛmaa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why does my maize crop fall over easily when strong winds and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks buckle when planted too closely together or when root systems are shallow due to poor soil depth. Adding extra soil around the base of the stem (earthing up) strengthens root support and prevents wind damage.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ fãa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛfataa he kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ kroko ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni baafite lɛ naa.

english: If I spray medicine to kill insects on my crops, why do I still need to apply fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii lolo?

english: Pest spray protects the crop from being eaten, but fertilizer feeds the crop so it can grow strong and recover. Just like a person needs both medicine to cure sickness and food to build strength, crops require both chemical protection and soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni akaye amɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei niyenii bɔni afee ni amɛda waa ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Taakɛ tsofa kɛ niyenii fɛɛ he hiaa wɔ koni wɔná hewalɛ lɛ. Tsofai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow when there is plenty of rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right stage helps restore green leaves and crop vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick stems but yield very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive excess nitrogen or are planted too closely, the cassava puts all its energy into growing stem height and leafy branches instead of sending food down into the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids underneath the leaves. Spraying an appropriate insecticide or neem oil kills these pests so new leaf growth can emerge normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baagbe kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal infection that spreads in cool, wet conditions. Clearing weeds and removing diseased pods promptly stops fungal spores from spreading across the farm.
ga: Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ helai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die early before the harvest season reaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho dani akpa lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam vines is often caused by root rot from poor drainage or leaf spot disease. Planting on high mounds and rotating crops helps roots stay healthy until full maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo baa mli hela ni haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing flower pollen to dry out and fail to set fruit. Shade netting or regular morning watering lowers heat stress so flowers can form tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋshɔŋloo loo nu wo mli daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi. koni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ tomato

english: Why are my watermelons rotting from the bottom end while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ? Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Bottom rot on watermelons is caused by calcium deficiency, often triggered by inconsistent watering. Keeping soil moisture steady throughout fruit growth allows roots to continuously absorb calcium.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ watermelon shishi fitemɔ baa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛŋɔ calcium.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant from making food properly, leading to small cobs and poor root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, cob tsei lɛ daraaa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them directly in an open field without big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantain planted nearby to act as natural umbrellas until their roots and leaves are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll upwards during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛshwieee amɛhe lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense trick tomato plants use to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling their leaves inward, they expose less surface area to the sun and reduce the amount of water escaping from their tissues.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ fãji lɛ amli lɛ baa shi

english: If one plant in my garden gets a virus, can it spread to the rest of my crops?
ga: Kɛji hela ko mɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko mli lɛ Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, plant viruses spread very easily across a farm, mostly carried by sap-sucking insects like aphids and whiteflies, or transferred through dirty cutlasses and hands when moving from infected plants to healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ mlɛo waa. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies ji mɛi ni woɔ amɛ babaoo. Aloo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ dade kɛ niji ni mli ewo muji nɔ kɛ́ ojɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning dark purple instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple ni mli edɔ yɛ eŋɔli najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is short on phosphorus, a key plant food. This happens when the soil is deficient in nutrients or when cold, wet soil stops the roots from absorbing phosphorus properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná fɔsfɔs jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience sudden temperature spikes, extreme drought, or when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant grow extra leaves instead of holding onto fruit blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in high humidity and damp shade. If weeds are overgrown or tree canopies are too thick, moisture gets trapped and allows the fungal spores to multiply and destroy the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ni ehaa fungal spores lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: Why do the tubers of my yam plants have rough skin and strange swollen lumps on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ hewolo yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efuu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen lumps on yam tubers are caused by microscopic worms called root-knot nematodes living in the soil. They attack the root skin, making the tubers unsightly and reducing their storage life after harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root-knot nematodes ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Amɛtutuaa shishifã hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ fɛo, ni ehaa be ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close forces the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Hybrid seeds lose their vigor and high-yield qualities after the first harvest. If you replant seeds saved from hybrid crops, the resulting plants will grow unevenly and produce much lower yields than the original seeds.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ du ekoŋŋ Tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure will help the leaves turn green and produce better grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the ground every season. If you do not replenish the soil with manure, fertilizer, or by rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts, the soil becomes exhausted and yields will drop.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafo ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I cut off the big leaves of my plantain suckers before planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain baai wuji dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming the leaves stops the sucker from losing too much water through evaporation while it forms new roots. This helps the new plant establish faster and prevents it from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ beni amɛfeɔ shishifãi heei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei heei ni amɛmaa oya ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly due to extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be, ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, which is usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ.

english: What causes fall armyworms to appear so suddenly and destroy my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa cutworms baa trukaa ni efiteɔ mi-baby corn lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths fly into fields during warm, rainy weather and lay hundreds of eggs on young leaves at night. The eggs hatch quickly into caterpillars that eat the heart of the maize plant.
ga: Fɛ̃i be mli ŋmeii fɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmeii ohai abɔ fɔɔ baai bibii anɔ gbɛkɛ. Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready for harvest under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants designed to survive tough conditions. Their seeds lie hidden in the soil and absorb water and sunlight faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when I store them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when they get wounded during harvest, or when stored in hot, poorly ventilated places where fungi grow. Storing undamaged yams on raised racks in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated barn prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji epila yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteko lɛ to adeka ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the early rains begin in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady rain for several days rather than planting after the very first light drizzle. Planting too early in dry soil can scorch seeds, while waiting for adequate soil moisture ensures high germination rates.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ babaoo aba lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete intensely for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for root expansion and leaf growth, resulting in healthier plants and a larger total yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or root damage caused by waterlogged land. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore leaf color and crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ kɛbaa lɛ efite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: This typically happens when soil contains excess nitrogen relative to potassium, causing the cassava plant to direct its energy into leaf growth rather than storing starch in root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe potassium. Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa baa lɛ dalɛ mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi yibii babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that can be easily damaged by wind or soil pests like nematodes. Supporting the fruiting stalks with sturdy wooden props prevents the trees from collapsing under heavy weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ aduawai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ akagbee shi yɛ muji ni tsii shishi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies transmitting plant viruses, or by extreme dry heat. Controlling these pests early helps preserve normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni mli egbi waa mli Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra Ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my young crop plants with dry grass help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves retains moisture in the ground, keeps root temperatures cool, and stops weeds from growing. As the material decays, it also adds rich organic nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Beni nibii lɛ fiteɔ Ebaakɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to high temperature stress, irregular watering, or a lack of natural pollinators. Maintaining consistent soil moisture helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni wa.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Blackened cocoa pods are usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, humid conditions. Pruning dense tree branches to let in sunlight and fresh air reduces moisture and prevents the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the tip down the center, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure restores the green color and helps the plant develop full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil is too acidic, plant roots become locked and cannot absorb the nutrients in the fertilizer. Applying agricultural lime balances the soil acidity, allowing the crop roots to feed properly.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Okwaayeli mli lime ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli acidity lɛ feɔ ekome. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii ni sa

english: Will planting my maize seeds very deep in the ground help them build stronger roots?
ga: Ani mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ?

english: Planting seeds too deep starves them of air and uses up all their energy before they can break through the soil surface. Planting at a shallow depth of about 3 to 5 centimeters allows quick sprouting and healthy early growth.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee amɛ ni amɛbaafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my soil and harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize, while giving you two different crops from the same piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do the soil and leaves dry out so fast in my vegetable garden during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct heat from the sun evaporates soil moisture quickly. Covering the soil around your crop stems with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps soil moisture and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ atswa otsei lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dirt looking like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? Ni muji bibioo ko hu yɛ jɛmɛ. Etamɔ nɔ ni eji ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying approved treatments or neem extract early in the morning directly into the central leaf funnel controls the pest before it destroys the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo leebi neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ dani ekpata tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my pepper plants so they do not spoil quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mi-pepper tsei lɛ koni amɛkafite oya?

english: Peppers are ready for harvesting when they feel firm to the touch and have fully changed to their bright mature color, such as red or yellow. Harvesting at this stage ensures the best taste and a longer shelf life for market.
ga: Pepper lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji etswa shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi eta he ni etsɔ su ni mli tse kwraa, tamɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fã nɛɛ haa anáa ŋmɔlɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛha jara nɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow—often starting at the tips and moving down the center—when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ ejeɔ shishi yɛ naagbeehei ni eyaa shi yɛ teŋgbɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhefɛo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly due to stress from high heat, dry soil, or lack of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and adding organic fertilizer encourages the flowers to stay on and set fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper blossom ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves and cause the whole plant to wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dark spots on tomato leaves are usually caused by fungal diseases like leaf blight, which spread when water sits on leaves in hot, humid weather. Spacing plants for air movement and watering close to the roots helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai, tamɔ late blight, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nu ba baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni kã tsei kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the middle parts of my young maize plants before they tassel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the funnel of young maize plants to eat fresh leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying targeted biological treatments or recommended pesticides protects the growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baabu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the young green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and shrivel up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air through, along with picking infected pods early, keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji ni ahala pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Seeds should be planted after the soil receives enough steady rain to stay wet several inches deep for consecutive days. Planting after just one light shower causes seeds to germinate and then dry up and die.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ inchii babaoo gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce skinny, small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space, sunlight, and underground room to expand. When planted too close, the leaves shade each other and the roots fight for nutrients, resulting in low yield.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko, hulu la kɛ tsũ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baa shi

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield much less grain than the seeds I bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa fioo kwraa fe nɔ ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation. Seeds harvested from those crops lose their special strength in the next generation, producing smaller ears and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why does wild grass keep growing back faster than my crops even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds and underground stems survive in the soil and sprout rapidly once sunlight hits bare earth. Mulching the soil with dry grass or leaves blocks light and stops weeds from taking over your crop rows.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ sũ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaatsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot quickly after I store them in the barn?
