ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, exposed to hot sun, or stored in a warm room without airflow. Storing unbruised tubers on raised, well-ventilated wooden racks keeps them fresh for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ Aloo okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei ni efite lɛ ato tso shɛlɛf ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides shade and keeps the air humid until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fail to produce big cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ mli tseee ni amɛwooo ŋmãa wuji kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing gives every maize plant enough space to build thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmãa ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that stored food remains in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the soil stays wet after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for a long time without draining away, it chokes the roots and lets fungi attack them, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaakã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmei lɛ atutua. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha sweet potato wain tso lɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high toward the sun so their leaves can trap sunlight and make energy, which is sent down into the ground to make the yam tubers swell bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee hewalɛ. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ

english: Leaf curling on tomato plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that spread crop sickness, or by heat stress. Keeping the field clean and spraying safe treatments helps keep leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the cool soil absorbs water deeply before the afternoon sun can evaporate it, allowing the roots to drink enough water to stay strong all day.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves or grass on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from drying out quickly, and blocks weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why does the soil in my field become hard and cracked after I irrigate it during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa beni mikɛ nu wo nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare clay soil packs tightly when water dries off under hot sunlight, forming a hard crust. Mixing manure or decomposed leaves into the soil keeps it soft so water can sink in easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ buaa ehe naa beni nu lɛ gbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. cause a hard crust Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo baai ni egbo futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha efee blɛoo bɔni afee ni nu anyɛ abote mli oya.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get easily scorched under harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains around them to shield them from the heat until their root systems grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi shishifã lɛ mli baawa.

english: Trees shed their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. With fewer leaves, the plant loses less moisture to the hot air, keeping the trunk and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and soft while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fĩ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Trimming heavy branches to let in light and fresh air helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ mli Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ, ni afolɔ waa koni ekɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do crop leaves develop yellow spots and rot faster during long rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria love damp environments. When moisture sits on leaves for days without sunshine to dry it off, fungal spores germinate easily and infect the leaf tissue.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria sumɔɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Beni ŋmɔtɔ ta baai lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo ni hulu la bɛ ni haa amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Fungal spores lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted suckers and overgrown branches stops the tree from wasting water and energy on leaves that don't produce fruit. It directs all the tree's food straight into growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei ahe tsei ni ataooo kɛ tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite nu kɛ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. Akɛ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny without bearing much fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight for sunlight and stretch upwards to reach the light. They spend all their energy growing taller instead of building thick stems and strong fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛshɛ he. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa tree falling off instead of turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is under stress from heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. If the plant feels it doesn't have enough water or food to support pods, it drops the flowers to save itself.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ eshishifãi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Ebaajie fɔfɔii ni ekɛtsa ehe.

english: How do I know if my crops are turning yellow because the soil is tired or because of a sickness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Tired soil usually turns whole fields of leaves a uniform light green or yellow color over time, whereas disease usually causes patchy spots, dark streaks, or rotting on specific plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ po yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ kɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ŋmeii baa tsei komɛi anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing around the base of my trees reduce my final crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ haa minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds act like thieves under the soil—their roots drink the water and eat the natural plant food meant for your crops, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi julɔi Amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kɛha onibii lɛ. Shimɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: Why does clearing away rotten pods and old dead leaves from the farm floor keep my living trees healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni egboi kɛ baai momoi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Old, rotting plant material acts as a hiding place for pests and fungal spores. Clearing them away removes the sickness source so it cannot jump back onto your healthy growing trees.
ga: Tsei ahe nibii ni egbɔ ni miifite lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaajie he ni hela lɛ jɛ lɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ eku esɛɛ efo kɛya otsei ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaves turn yellow from the bottom when the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for green plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting legumes like cowpeas before maize restores soil nutrients and keeps leaves green.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he loo adu ŋmei, tamɔ tsina ŋmei, dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas together with my maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen, so growing both crops together enriches the soil naturally without requiring as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ nitrogen babaoo haa ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and dry winds during their first few years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby shields the young leaves from sunburn and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds or wet soil conditions. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo poles or wooden stakes prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi eshishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Excess water sitting around cassava roots starves them of air, causing fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows surplus rainwater to drain away safely from the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cassava shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. haa ŋmeii fiteɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks for them to yield big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ koni maná bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch maximum sunlight, which generates energy for tuber expansion underground. Staking keeps leaves dry and elevated off the ground, reducing disease and boosting yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni ewo amɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai baa shi ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady, deep watering and placing dry grass mulch on the soil keeps the roots cool and helps flowers stay attached to produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛwo tomato.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading plant diseases that permanently stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni haa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ daa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my garden egg plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli eggplant lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the sun, lowers soil temperature, and prevents weeds from taking light and food from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that scorches newly germinated seeds in the dry ground. Waiting for regular, continuous rains ensures young roots have steady water to establish strongly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni no shãa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu ni haa amɛnáa hewalɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil and prevent roots from taking in air and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot weather, dry soil, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than fruiting.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are wilting because of disease or just because of the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbo yɛ hela hewɔ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ pɛ hewɔ?

english: If plants are just thirsty, they will droop in the afternoon heat but bounce back fully in the cool evening or after watering. If the wilting is caused by a disease, the plant will remain wilted even overnight and may develop brown streaks on the stems.
ga: Kɛji kumai ye tso lɛ kɛkɛ Ebaagbi yɛ shwane mli. Shi ebaaku esɛɛ kwraa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Kɛji hela ji nɔ ni kɛ shwiemɔ ba lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ egbo nyɔɔŋ kome po ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block direct heat and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller yields than crops given proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee ni sa.

english: Why does my soil produce lower yields every year even though I plant the same crop on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi fɛɛ afi lɛ? He ni miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same land every season drains the specific nutrients that crop uses. Rotating your main crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen and nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hoɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water or fertilize my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu loo mawo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time is early morning or late afternoon when the air is cooler. Applying water or fertilizer during the hot midday causes water to evaporate too quickly and can cause the fertilizer to burn the plant roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds steal growth away from my main crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiju dalɛ oya kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are hardier than cultivated crops, so they quickly soak up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your plants, effectively starving your crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii amli kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Is there a way I can make more money from my cassava harvest instead of selling the raw tubers immediately?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maná shika babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni makpa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can process fresh cassava tubers into value-added products like gari, high-quality cassava flour, or dried chips, which last much longer without spoiling and sell for higher prices.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei shishifãi heei afee nibii ni jara wa tamɔ gari, ni ji ŋmei shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. loo crispy potato chips Amɛbaahi shi be babaoo ni amɛfiteee ni ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How do I stop insects from eating my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects need moisture and air to thrive. Drying your maize until it is completely hard before storing it, and using airtight storage bags or sealed containers, starves pests of moisture and oxygen so they cannot survive.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia koolooi koni amɛdara. Aŋmãa ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ebaawa kwraa dani akɛtoɔ Ni akɛ vacuum storage bag loo nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ atsu nii. Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants drop leaves mainly due to intense heat and direct sunlight. Cocoa seedlings need shade crops like plantains to shelter them from hot sun until their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ titri. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ hia tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɛɛ toi wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They use all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of forming large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why do flowers drop off my crop plants before turning into fruit or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants suffer from water stress, high heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. It can also happen if helpful insects like bees are not visiting the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu he haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crop leaves suddenly wilt and dry up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting during rainy periods usually happens when fungus or tiny pests attack the roots underground. Damaged roots cannot absorb water from the wet soil, causing the plant above ground to dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii tutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do worms attack my young maize leaves right in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi-baby corn baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually the Fall Armyworm, which prefers the tender young leaves hidden inside the center whorl of the maize plant. Spotting them early allows you to protect the growing tip before the crop is ruined.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni sumɔɔ baai bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does my soil lose its strength and produce smaller harvests after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa ni ewooo yibii yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and minerals out of the dirt every season. If you do not add manure, compost, or fertilizer back into the soil, or rotate different crops, the soil becomes exhausted and yields drop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tsakeee Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens if I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so roots can drink it. Applying fertilizer to dry dirt leaves it useless on the surface and can even burn the crop roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, planted in bone-dry or waterlogged soil, or eaten by insects and mice before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of tiny insects when I store it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Be ni akɛtoɔ kotoku mli?

english: Maize gets insects like weevils if the grain is bagged before it is fully dried, or if stored sacks touch damp ground. Grain must be dried until hard before bagging and kept off the floor on wooden pallets.
ga: Abele lɛ naa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ awo ŋmaa lɛ kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. aloo kɛji akɛ kotoku ni ato lɛ kɛ he ko ni mli efɔ lɛ kpe Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ.

english: Can I plant maize under mature cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize cannot grow well under full-grown cocoa trees because the heavy branches of mature cocoa block out the sunlight that maize needs to grow strong and make cobs.
ga: Abɛi kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo niji ni eda lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa ni ebatsɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block harsh sunlight, the hot sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to build healthy foliage, and when food is low, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to its newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. ni kɛ́ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause water to stand on the farm for a long time, the roots drown, allowing soil fungi to enter and turn the tubers soft and rotten.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu ta ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, groundnuts feed the soil and make extra nutrients available for the maize to grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Peanuts lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ aba koni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow during the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out shallowly near the top of the soil. When heavy bunches grow at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots out of wet, soft ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, beni panicles lɛ daraa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear and destroy my maize farm right after a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa trukaa ni amɛfiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo ko ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm thrive in dry, warm conditions. Their eggs hatch quickly after mild rains, and the young caterpillars hide inside the plant leaves where they feed rapidly before you notice them.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbi. Amɛwuji lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ baate amɛhe oya yɛ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ he ni amɛnaa niyenii yɛ lɛ dani oyɔse amɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the earth, keeps the soil cool, and preserves water around the crop roots for a longer time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they feel stressed by irregular watering or extreme heat. If the plant does not get steady moisture while flowering, it drops the buds to save its remaining energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔii ashishi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to train my yam leaves to climb up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛkwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which is then sent down into the ground to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so root systems can drink it in. If applied to dry soil under heat, the concentrated salts in the fertilizer can scorch and burn your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ la shishi Nuŋ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni amɛshã amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no plantains or big trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei wuji bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides living shade, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the cocoa can establish roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can recognize when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse enɛ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do other farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass and coconut husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ ŋmei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the soil protects it from drying out under the intense sun, reduces weed growth, and slowly decomposes to enrich the soil with organic matter.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas naturally restores nitrogen back into the soil, making the land fertile again without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ebaaku sɛɛ ekɛ nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do we need to heap soil into high mounds to plant yam instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua sũi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anaa koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and wide underground; high, soft soil mounds give the tubers space to expand easily while allowing excess rainwater to drain off so the yams do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli shwereɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it dangerous to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain in early rainy season is often followed by long dry hot weeks; if seeds germinate immediately, the young shoots will dry up and die from lack of continuous soil moisture.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before turning into green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, causing stress to the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: Why shouldn't I drop solid fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is high in concentrated mineral salts that can burn the stem and feeder roots of the plant; it should be applied a few inches away in a ring so the roots absorb it safely.
ga: Mineral salts ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do caterpillars and fall armyworms suddenly attack my farm in large numbers when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: The fresh green leaves that emerge with the early rains attract adult moths to lay hundreds of eggs, which quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars that feed on tender plant leaves.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ni jeɔ kpo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ohai abɔ. Enɛɛmɛi fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them directly in full sunlight without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, intense heat. They need shade plants like plantains or cassava around them to block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air humid while their root system develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni ebɔle amɛhe. Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of leaves but no peppers when grown under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi pepper ko bɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to produce energy for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy shade, the plant uses all its energy just trying to grow taller leaves to reach for light, leaving no energy to make peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná la babaoo. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee chili.

english: How do I know if my farm plot receives enough sunlight to grow crops like okra and garden eggs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ okra kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii?

english: Most vegetable crops like okra and garden eggs need at least six hours of unblocked, direct sunlight every day. If big trees or buildings cast deep shadows over your field for most of the day, those crops will struggle to grow well.
ga: Aduawai babaoo tamɔ okra kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni atsĩii enaa lɛ aná ŋmɛlɛtswai ekpaa daa gbi. Kɛji tso agbo ko loo tsu ko ha hulutsoo ba oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli. Nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is a defense response. Tomato plants roll their leaves inward during extreme afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sun, which helps the plant conserve internal water.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ toɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up when there is too much intense sunshine and no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When intense sun combines with dry soil, maize plants cannot draw enough water to cool themselves down. The heat breaks down the green matter in the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and dry up to save energy.
ga: Beni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ. Abɛi tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ. Dɔlɛ lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ha etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do young orange fruits fall off my citrus trees when the weather gets very hot and bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmeii tso lɛ nɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit during intense heat and drought to survive. The tree sheds the fruits so it does not have to feed them, allowing the tree to keep its remaining water for its own trunks and roots.
ga: Citrus tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Tsei shwieɔ amɛyibii, ni no hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni aha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ toɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it necessary for me to walk into my field every day to inspect my crops instead of checking once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ?

english: Daily visits allow you to spot early warning signs like leaf wilting, pest attacks, or disease spots before they spread across the farm. Catching issues early under the sun saves your crop before damage becomes permanent.
ga: Daa gbi saramɔi yeɔ ebua bo ni ona kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra tamɔ baai ni egbo, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. loo spot hela dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Naagbai ni ooomɔ mra Hulu shishi lɛ baaye abua ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani nɔ ni efite lɛ baahi shi daa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava sticks are planted too close, the leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. The plants waste energy stretching upward to fight for sunlight instead of storing energy underground to form big cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hulu la akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ toɔ zugba sisi konɛ a kɛ pee kasaa sisi agbohi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops after bright sunshine follows a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants with deep root systems. They absorb rainwater very quickly and use the direct sunlight to produce energy faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower your field if left unchecked.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ. Amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu oya waa. ni ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops burn and wither when I apply fertilizer on a very dry, sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is made of chemical salts that need soil water to dissolve safely. Applying it under hot, direct sun without water causes the fertilizer to suck moisture out of the plant roots, scorching the crop.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni haa nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei ni shãa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special natural pods on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like a free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant in that field next.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plant roots to drink up the moisture before the sun gets strong. In the hot afternoon, most of the water evaporates into the air quickly before reaching the roots, which wastes your water and stresses the crops.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu babaoo shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ fiteɔ nu ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy soil without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding on the underside of the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Spraying the leaves with organic neem leaf extract or mild soapy water helps clear these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baafɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The soil contains thousands of tiny weed seeds lying dormant underground. When you clear the land, sunlight and rain reach those hidden seeds and wake them up to sprout quickly. Covering bare soil with dry grass or cover crops blocks sunlight and stops weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni kã shikpɔŋ shishi Kɛ́ otsi jɛmɛ lɛ Hulu kɛ nugbɔ shɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe ni etswaa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la naa ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do young cocoa plants grow better under plantain trees than in direct open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi fe hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences a sudden dry spell without enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant turn flowers into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ trukaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli etsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight to make food for the plant. When the vines climb upward on stakes instead of tangling on the ground, the plant leaves get more light and grow much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tso lɛ baai lɛ kpɛɔ waa ni bulbs lɛ dara kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground, while the stem holds heavy water and big fruit bunches. Supporting the plant with a strong wooden prop pole under the fruit stem keeps the heavy weight from pulling the roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ tso lɛ hiɛɔ muji ni ewoɔ yibii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ, no tsiɔ muji ni tsii lɛ naa koni ekagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn yellow during the dry season even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need enough water to reach deep into the soil to dissolve plant food so the roots can drink it. Small amounts of surface water evaporate quickly under the sun, leaving the soil dry underneath and causing plants to starve and heat-stress.
ga: Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni he hiaa tsei koni eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛjie tsei lɛ amli niyenii koni shishifãi lɛ anu. Nu fioo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli gbiɔ. ni ekɛ hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tsei anɔ.

english: Is underground borehole water safe for watering my vegetable crops continuously throughout the year?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Borehole water is generally very good for year-round farming because it is clean and reliable. However, some underground water contains high levels of salts or minerals, so testing the water helps ensure it won't damage your soil over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha afi muu lɛ fɛɛ okwaayeli ejaakɛ ehe tse ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii loo minerals babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nui komɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ kaa baaye abua ni nu lɛ efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my yellowing maize leaves are asking for fertilizer or asking for water?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa baa ni ji yellow lɛ miibi ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu?

english: If maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip down the center while the plant stands tall, it is hungry for nitrogen food. If the plant wilts, curls its leaves, and browns from the bottom, it is thirsty for water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii. Kɛji tso lɛ egbo lɛ, baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo kɛjɛɔ shishi. ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye lɛ

english: What happens to my crops if I put chemical fertilizer on the soil when there is no moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer requires moisture to dissolve and become food. When applied to dry soil under hot sun, the un-dissolved chemical salts will draw water out of the crop's roots, burning and damaging the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛye niyenii. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsofai ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. shãa ni efiteɔ tsei Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tsei ni amɛdara

english: Why do some fertilizers make my plants produce big green leaves without giving me many fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi haa mi tsei lɛ baa agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛhaaa mi aduawai loo dumɔwui babaoo lɛ?

english: Fertilizers high in nitrogen encourage leaf and stem growth. If crops get too much nitrogen without balanced amounts of phosphorus and potassium, they spend all their energy making big leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa baa kɛ tsei lɛ daraa. Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ yibii.

english: Why did my farm give me a huge harvest in the first year, but yields dropped significantly in the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi waa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Newly cleared bush land has rich nutrients built up over time. The first harvest consumes these nutrients, so without adding organic manure or fertilizer to replenish the soil, the soil gets tired and yields drop in following seasons.
ga: Niyenii nibii babaoo ni ebua naa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hei ni ajie tsei bibii lɛ ehee lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ biɔ nɛkɛ niyenii kpakpai nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he koni akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ sɛɛ mli bei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay shallow and spread out sideways instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spread sideways near the surface to catch quick rainfall, but if the soil beneath the surface is hard and compacted, the roots cannot push deep and will stay shallow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa he kroko ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ koni nugbɔ anɛ oya. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaahi shi yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, sudden drought, or lack of moisture, because the plant drops flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo hulutsoo ni bɛ Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Can I keep harvesting from the same tomato plant for a whole year if I continue watering and feeding it?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa tomato tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji mitee nɔ miwo lɛ nu ni miha lɛ niyenii?

english: Most tomato varieties are short-season crops that naturally age, weaken, and become vulnerable to diseases after 3 to 5 months of fruiting. It is better to plant new seedlings in cycles than trying to keep old plants alive.
ga: Tomato henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji tsei ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛhe waaa ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni amɛwo yibii lɛ. Ehi akɛ ooodu dumɔwui heei yɛ sɛɛkuu mli fe ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha tsei momoi ahi shi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and greener than my crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to survive in local soils with very few nutrients. They naturally absorb available rainwater and soil food much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji ni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying when the sun is too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade trees like plantains or shade crops planted nearby to protect them from heat and help keep moisture in the soil until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny flowers before they can grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ pods?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support with water and food. The tree intentionally sheds extra flowers and small pods to save energy so that the remaining pods can grow big and healthy.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii akwɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ jwɛŋ ni ejie fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Afee lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree when I want it to yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the tree sends food and water straight to the healthy pods instead of leaves. It also lets air flow through the tree, which prevents damp diseases from forming.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii kɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ akafee.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my cocoa farm has lost its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he wa efo mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: When farm soil becomes weak, crop leaves turn pale yellow, plants grow slowly, and the cocoa pods produced are much smaller than usual. Applying fertilizer replaces the missing nutrients the plants need to grow well.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo. Ni kookoo ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do black spots spread over my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots during rainy weather are usually caused by a fungal attack called black pod disease, which loves wet and damp conditions. Clearing weeds and spraying recommended fungicides helps protect your pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa. ni sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ŋaawoo baaye abua ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cocoa trees very close to each other just to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Trees planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small yields. Overcrowded farms also trap moisture, which encourages diseases to spread rapidly.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo. Gbɛjegbɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ hu hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni woɔ hela lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa oya lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower mostly after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain signals to the plant that water is available to sustain new growth. The tree uses this water to produce flowers and feed developing pods through the growing season.
ga: Nugbɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɛha dalɛ hee. Tsei kɛ nu nɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do tall weeds around my crops prevent my plants from giving me a good harvest?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he fɛɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crops. They also hide harmful insects that can bite your crops and spread diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Amɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ akɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛgbɛ hela amɛshwã lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why do I need to ferment my cocoa beans under plantain leaves before I dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation stops the bean inside from germinating and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that cocoa buyers demand. Unfermented beans remain bitter and sell for a lower price.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛnáa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ. Beans ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo, ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: How can getting agricultural financial support from a bank help me get more cocoa from my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he shika ni maná kɛjɛɔ shikatoohe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná kookoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Financial support allows you to buy inputs like fertilizers, good seeds, and crop protection sprays at the right time, as well as pay for farm labor to manage your field properly for maximum yield.
ga: Shika yelikɛbuamɔ haa onyɛɔ oheɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui kpakpai. ni okɛ tsofa abu tsei ahe yɛ be ni sa mli Plus wo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔ koni okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni oná yibii babaoo.

english: If my farmland usually gets a lot of rainwater flowing through it during the rainy season, can I rely on that water alone to grow my crops all year?
ga: Kɛji akɛ bei pii lɛ, miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nakai nu lɛ pɛ nɔ koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: No, rainwater flow is unpredictable and will stop when the rains end. Crops need steady, regular water to thrive, so relying only on natural rainwater runoff can leave your crops dry and dying during hot or dry spells.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni ebaakpa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba naagbee. Nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hɔmɔ baa waa lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant my crops in low areas of my farm where rainwater naturally flows and collects?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni nugbɔ nu hoɔ ni ebua ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Low areas give crops easy access to water, but if too much water settles there without proper drainage, it can flood the soil, drown the roots, and cause diseases like root rot.
ga: He ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii náa nu mlɛo. Shi kɛji akɛ nu babaoo fa tsɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ gbɛ kpakpa nɔ hu? Ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu, efite shishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ aba.

english: How does heavy rainfall flowing quickly across my field affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fast-flowing rainwater can wash away the rich topsoil your crops need for nutrients. It can also weaken or uproot young seedlings before they settle into the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii hu agbɔjɔ loo egbala amɛ kɛjɛ mli dani amɛdu amɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers use a water pumping machine on their land instead of waiting for rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ nu pɔmpii tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaamɛ nugbɔ lɛ?

english: A water pump allows a farmer to draw water from a river, well, or pond whenever the crops need it. This gives crops a reliable water supply so they keep growing even when rain does not fall.
ga: Nu pɔmpii haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ faai, nubui, loo kpaakpoi amli be fɛɛ be ni amɛ dumɔwui lɛ he baahia amɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: When is the best time of day for me to pump water onto my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ nu baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Early morning or late evening is best. If you water crops during the hot afternoon sun, much of the water evaporates before the roots can soak it up.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Kɛji okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Can I use water pumped from any nearby stream or pond for my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa loo nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: Most natural water sources work well, but if the water is extremely muddy or polluted with chemicals, it can damage plant leaves, block soil air holes, or introduce plant diseases.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu jɛɛhei babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ nu lɛ mli eyi kɛ muji babaoo loo tsofai ewo mli. Ebaanyɛ efite tsei ahe baai. Tsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ bu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa loo ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahelai aba

english: When crops lack water, their leaves droop, curl, or turn yellow. When they get too much water, the leaves may turn yellow and drop off while the stem feels soft and waterlogged.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ baagbee shi, amɛbaakpãtã, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up during hot weather even when the top of the soil still looks dark and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo duŋ ni edɔ lolo moŋ.

english: Crop roots absorb water deep beneath the surface. Even if the surface soil looks damp from light rain or morning dew, the deeper soil around the roots may still be completely dry.
ga: Tse shishifãi gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo, loo leebi ŋmɔtɔ hewɔ moŋ Shi ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe shɔŋŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lolo.

english: Which crops need a continuous water supply the most if I have a water machine on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei he hiaa nu ni yaa nɔ fe fɛɛ kɛji miyɛ nu tsɔne yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, cabbage, and garden eggs need steady water to yield well. Staples like maize and cassava can handle short dry periods better than soft vegetables.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kaaba kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ adamɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli. Ehi fe aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo

english: Why do my neighbour's crops grow better than mine even though we farm in the same area and get the same rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔtsuɔ okwaa yɛ he kome ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he kome moŋ?

english: Your neighbour may be using extra watering tools like pumps during dry spells, or managing soil moisture better. Giving crops extra water at critical growth stages makes a big difference in harvest size.
ga: Okutsoŋnyo lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ nu shwiemɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ nu pɔmp atsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. aloo akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Nu kroko ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ bei titrii amli lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer near the base helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist during hot days. It also stops weeds from taking root and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi lɛ akawo shishifãi ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Is it good to apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain falling?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer away into streams before the plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or when only light rain is expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ fioo pɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to multiply. Alternating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people tell me to cut off the small shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mifolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ajie?

english: If too many small shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they fight over food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, which makes the main tree produce larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ ŋmeii titrii babaoo he lɛ Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji.

english: Why should I prune or cut off the small shoots from my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Extra small branches, called water shoots or chupons, drain energy from the main cocoa tree without producing pods. Removing them lets the tree direct all its food toward producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Nine bibioo krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nu tso loo chupong. Etsuɔ nii koni ejie hewalɛ kɛjɛ cacao tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ efeee. Kɛ́ ajieɔ kookoo yibii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wood poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can catch full sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber below. If left on the ground, the leaves shade each other and get diseased, resulting in tiny tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai yeɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji yitso bibioo

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the juices. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water or neem extract solution helps get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem mli tsofa ko shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime heat is too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Providing steady watering at the root level helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off naturally. Cracks may also appear in the soil around the base of the stem as the roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi baanyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why is my cocoa farm giving me fewer bags of harvest every year even though the trees are still alive?
