ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui fioo daa afi lɛ? He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Over time, cocoa trees pull nutrients out of the soil to grow pods. If you do not add nutrients back into the dirt through fertilizer or manure, the soil becomes empty and hungry, resulting in lower yields year after year.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Cacao tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee efolo ni hɔmɔ hu baaye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How does putting fertilizer or manure into the ground actually help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Just like food gives a person strength to work, nutrients in fertilizer feed the soil so the roots can drink them up. This gives the tree the energy to grow stronger branches, hold onto its flowers, and produce mature pods.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii haa wɔ hewalɛ ni wɔkɛtsu nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ niji ni mli wa, emɔ fɔfɔi amli, ni efee pods ni eda.

english: How will I know by looking at my cocoa trees that the soil is running out of food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛtsɔ cacao tso ko ni mikwɛɔ lɛ nɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ miiho yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When cocoa trees are starving, their leaves often turn yellowish instead of deep green, they drop their flowers early, and they produce very few or small pods compared to healthy trees.
ga: Kɛ́ hɔmɔ ye kookoo tso lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi oya. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo bibii kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my cocoa trees with dry leaves and farm waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground keeps the soil cool, traps rainwater so the roots do not dry out quickly, and slowly rots into natural food that feeds the soil.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi oya ni amɛfite fiofio ni amɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Is it really possible for a small cocoa farm that gives only three bags to start giving ten or twenty bags?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli diɛŋtsɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli? No haa kotokui etɛ pɛ ni akɛjeɔ shishi kɛ kotokui nyɔŋma loo nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni akɛhaa?

english: Yes, standard cocoa trees have the capacity to produce much more than three bags. When you feed the soil properly, prune bad branches, and protect the crop from pests, the trees unlock their full potential and multiply your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tso ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo nɔ ni fe kotokui etɛ. Kɛji okɛ niyenii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni ehiii lɛ ahe ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe Tsei lɛ baagbele amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply plant food to my cocoa farm so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsei aniyenii awo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkafite?

english: The best time is at the beginning of the rainy season when the ground is damp. The rainwater helps the soil absorb the nutrients so the tree roots can drink them easily.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nugbɔ nu yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ mlɛo.

english: If I add nutrients to my soil today, how quickly will I see a change in my cocoa harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ŋmɛnɛ Etsɛɛɛ ni mana tsakemɔi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli?

english: You will notice greener leaves and new shoots within a few weeks, but the big increase in cocoa pods usually shows during the next main flowering and harvesting season.
ga: Obaana baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. Shi bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni etee hiɛ waa lɛ jieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ kpamɔ be titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers that just fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support big pods. Feeding the soil gives the tree the energy needed to keep the flowers attached until they grow into full pods.
ga: Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii wuji lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods dry up and turn black while they are still tiny on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny pods shrivel up when the tree is stressed by lack of soil nutrients, excessive shade, or diseases. Keeping the soil healthy and cutting away unwanted branches reduces this loss.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shade loo hela babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ nɔ ni laajeɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kooloo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are like unwanted guests at a feast—they quickly steal the water and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa trees, leaving your crop weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ yɛ okpɔlɔŋmɛɛ ko shishi. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ oya. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ bo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties from extension officers is the best way to keep the crop healthy.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni jɛ extension officials lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when the soil gets too dry, when heat is extreme, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shading during hot days help the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Beni latsaa lɛ mli wa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, very wet, and shaded conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning thick cocoa leaves to let in sunlight, and removing infected pods helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ waa kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ. Kookoo baai ni mli tse ni afolɔ koni afee hulu la kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers deep in the soil instead of near the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mabɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Planting plantain suckers deep helps their roots anchor firmly into the ground so strong winds will not blow the heavy tree over when it starts bearing large bunches of fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ etswaŋ tso lɛ beni ebɔi aduawai wuji womɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings fall over and rot right at the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by soil fungi when seedling beds stay too wet and crowded. Giving seedlings enough space and avoiding overwatering protects young stems from rotting.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛji dumɔwui asaji lɛ edɔ tsɔ ni amɛmli edɔ. Kɛ́ oha dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and full of branches instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bibii ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ niji moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become small and misshapen when the soil is hard and stony or when tiny worms in the soil attack the roots. Building high, loose soil mounds allows the tubers to expand freely without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji bibii ni efiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni efeɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough nourishment to grow strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my pepper farm producing plenty of green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth with few fruits usually happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer. Switching to fertilizers richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to make flowers and fruits instead of just leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni aduawai fioo pɛ woɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai moŋ fe baai kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants start producing flowers early when the dry season approaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally respond to changes in day length and moisture. When days get shorter and drier, the plant speeds up flowering to produce seeds before water runs out completely.
ga: Cowpeas tsuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ gbi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni gbii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi oya koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani nu lɛ baaho.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or spreading a plant virus. Spraying with organic neem oil solution or recommended insecticides helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem oil solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing central leaf whorl of young maize plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baai ni miida lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within a few days even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden collapse is usually bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters the roots and blocks water channels inside the plant stem. Rotating your field with non-solanaceous crops like maize or cassava helps reduce the bacteria in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni eboteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Okɛ tsei ni jeee solanatic tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baatsake odumɔ nii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bacteria ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi

english: Yam plants need to spread their leaves out in direct sunlight to make the food that grows the tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to light and preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kane yɔɔ ni otsi baa hela ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young shoots to grow around one plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they compete with each other for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main stem produces a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, dumɔwu titri lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni ena nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha plantains ni tsii ni eyi obɔ aba tso lɛ yiteŋ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: How does covering the ground around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves inward usually means the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure restores green growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When harvested, the remaining roots decay and naturally enrich the soil with free fertilizer for the following maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ baafite ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees or plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly to provide shade umbrellas, maintaining higher air moisture and protecting the tender cocoa leaves during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛha hulutsoo. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni oooha eya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves yellowing and falling off, and the ground around the base of the stem will begin to crack open as the tubers expand below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why won't my crops grow well on land that was previously dug up for illegal gold mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining destroys the dark topsoil layer where plant food and organic matter live, leaving behind infertile subsoil, packed sand, or chemicals that prevent crop roots from taking in nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ, ni haa tsei niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ pɛ ni eshwɛ ji shikpɔŋ shishi ni wooo yibii lɛ. ŋã ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsofai ni tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts helps restore soil health.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leafy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to slow down water loss through transpiration. As long as the soil has adequate water, the leaves usually recover once the midday heat cools down.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛtsɔ latsaa ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is eating holes in the middle of my young corn shoots overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye bu ko ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the tight center whorl of the corn plant during the day and chew on tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii dani ojie

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and thin even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively consume sunlight, soil nutrients, and water before your main crops can reach them, effectively starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ hulu la. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu mli lɛ waa dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aba. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more plants in my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, root space, and soil food, resulting in weak, tall, thin stalks with small yields.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛkwɛɔ, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Clearing all shade trees leaves young cocoa leaves exposed to harsh heat and sun exposure, which scorches the plant and dries out root moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ehaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la. Enɛ baashã tso lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried plant matter, called mulching, keeps the sun from drying out ground moisture too quickly, keeps roots cool, and blocks weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la akagbi sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I delay harvesting after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mikɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ ni akpa lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills air spaces around cassava tubers with standing water, cutting off oxygen to the roots and encouraging soil fungi that cause tubers to decay rapidly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli obɔ. Cassava shishifãi ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekanyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their roots are small and their leaves burn easily. They need shade crops, such as plantain or cassava, to cover them and keep the moisture in the ground while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that there is too much water drowning the roots and preventing the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ abɛi tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo miiha shishifãi lɛ mii shi. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do some cocoa farms produce a huge harvest while others nearby yield very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: High yields come from regular effort and proper management practices, such as timely pruning, weeding, pest control, and feeding the soil, rather than leaving the trees to grow on their own.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa tamɔ tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eda

english: Why do cassava plants drop their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed leaves during the dry period to conserve water and survive the heat, focusing their remaining energy on resting and storing starch in their underground roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ haa hejɔɔmɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main stem, which prevents damp fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli edɔ tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ anaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak stalks and small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil can burn the roots and ruin the fertilizer before the crop can benefit from it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tso lɛ aná he sɛɛ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast in my cocoa farm when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod is a water-loving fungus. Raindrops splash the disease spores from damp soil or infected pods onto healthy ones, spreading the infection rapidly across humid, overcrowded farms.
ga: Black pod ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ sũ ni mli efɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving it time to replenish, causing the soil to become tired and reducing plant growth.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops after the first rain arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to react instantly to rain and grab sunlight and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crop seeds can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Amɛheɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the cocoa trees from direct heat and keeps the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii ewo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I pare or clean the bottom of my plantain suckers before planting them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo matsumɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishi dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Paring the bottom of a plantain sucker by trimming off the outer layer removes hidden weevil eggs and microscopic worms. Cleaning them prevents you from introducing pests into a clean field that would destroy the roots of your new crop.
ga: Ni afoɔ plantain sucker lɛ shishi kɛtsɔ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ni afoɔ koni ajie ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsumɔ amɛhe lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite otsei heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. As the heavy bunch grows, the top-heavy weight makes the tree unbalanced, meaning a strong wind can easily pull the roots out unless you support the trunk with a sturdy wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ da lɛ, Muji ni tsii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafee nɔ ni sa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. When nitrogen is lacking, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the upper growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water sitting around the roots without proper drainage, the roots drown, rot, and decay underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ nu hoɔ yɛ gbɛ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagboi, ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do black spots appear and quickly spread across my cocoa pods during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Water drops carry the fungal spores from pod to pod, so keeping the farm thick and unpruned makes it easy for the disease to spread.
ga: Black pods ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ hiɛɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ ato.

english: Why are the roots of my tomato plants full of strange swollen bumps when I pull them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni efuu lɛ? Be ni mikɛbaawo ŋwɛi?

english: Swollen bumps on tomato roots are caused by tiny microscopic worms in the soil called root-knot nematodes. They bore into the root tissues, causing swelling and blocking the plant from absorbing water and food.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ root-knot nematodes lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ tomato shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Amɛboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni ehaa fuumɔ baa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ gbɛ koni ekamɔ nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry leaves stop the soil from drying out fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ baai ni egboi shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or straw creates a blanket called mulch. This layer shades the soil from direct sun, keeping it cool and trapping water underneath so it doesn't evaporate quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu yɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, efoŋ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and naturally adapted to wake up and soak up nutrients faster than domestic crops. They quickly spread roots and take advantage of the wet soil before your crops have a chance to settle in.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛte shi ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwãa oya ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi.

english: Why do I need to till and loosen the soil before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani adu ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil creates space for roots to spread and grow thick. Hard soil stops the roots from expanding, resulting in small, thin cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ baa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow if I plant them too deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds only have a small amount of stored energy to push their shoots up to the light. If planted too deep, the shoot runs out of food and dies before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa la lɛ mli. Kɛji adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ Niyenii baaho amɛ ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain stems planted next to them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ plantain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big umbrella-like leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heat gets extreme, pepper plants enter survival mode to conserve water. They drop their flowers to save energy so the main plant doesn't dry out and die.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaya shihilɛ mli koni amɛbu nu he. Amɛkɛ fɔfɔii woɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Koni tso titri lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce smaller fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to build large, healthy fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and act like thieves, taking up the soil's moisture, light, and nutrients before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Amɛheɔ sũ mli nu, la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani tsei shishifãi shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, reducing future harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni abaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, naturally enriching the land for the next crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to harvest since they grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts show maturity when the lower leaves of the bush turn yellow and drop off. You can also sample a pod; if the inside lining has dark veins and seeds fill the shell, it is time to dig them up.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni jwɛi lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ pods lɛ hu akwɛ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ lɛ, be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: If I spend my money on quality farm inputs, am I guaranteed to make a profit?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ shika lɛ tsu nii yɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ Ani miyɛ nɔmimaa akɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Investing money in inputs like good seeds and fertilizers boosts yield potential, but you must monitor your field carefully because poor management or pest damage can still cause financial loss.
ga: Ni oookɛ shika awo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui kpakpai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaye abua ni oha onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ nibii ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha shika afite.

english: Why do some farmers lose money even after spending a lot on their fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi fiteɔ shika babaoo yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli po lɛ?

english: High spending alone does not ensure success; if you do not pay close attention to proper planting times, weeding, and pest control, your investment will be wasted.
ga: Shika babaoo ni afiteɔ lɛ pɛ haaa mɔ aye omanye. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ emaaa dumɔ be lɛ nɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ baafee yaka.

english: How can I make sure I get back the money I invest in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ maná shika ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You recover your money by managing your field closely from planting to harvest, ensuring that every cedi spent translates into high crop yield and quality.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná shika kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa kɛjɛ dumɔwui kɛyashi kpamɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akwɛ koni atsake pagoda fɛɛ pagoda ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize plant usually yield only one good cob instead of many?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmei kpakpa kome pɛ shi jeee ŋmei babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize plants naturally channel most of their absorbed nutrients into developing one large, fully filled cob rather than multiple weak ones under standard spacing.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛfee abele ŋmeii wuji ni eyi kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ cobs ni yɔɔ blɛoo babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, Cob yɔɔ shishitoo mla shishi

english: What causes maize cobs to remain small even when the stalk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: If the plant lacks sufficient water or soil nutrients during the flowering and grain-filling stage, the cob will not develop fully despite a tall stalk.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni awoɔ mli lɛ mli. Cob lɛ edaŋ kwraa yɛ eshishifã ni kɛlɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crops yield less if I do not visit and inspect my field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji miyasaraaa ŋmɔji lɛ ni mikwɛɛɛ amɛ daa lɛ?

english: Crops require active care; without regular inspection, weeds, pests, and nutrient deficiencies quietly steal resources and reduce your final yield.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ mli daa lɛ, jwɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ juɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ dioo. ni okɛ naagbee nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I arrange my farming so that I have crops to harvest continuously?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi okwaayeli lɛ nɔ koni maná ŋmaa ni yaa nɔ?

english: By using staggered planting, you sow seeds at different times so that as one harvest comes to an end, the next crop is ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Obaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. koni kɛ́ agbe kpamɔ kome naa lɛ, ŋmaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Should I start planting a new crop immediately after harvesting the old one?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi tsei heei adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa tsei momoi lɛ?

english: If moisture and soil nutrients are available, starting a new cycle right as the old harvest finishes keeps your land productive and provides steady income.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii heei ni ooobɔi beni agbe ŋmaakpamɔ momo lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii ni eha shika ni yaa nɔ daa aba.

english: Why is constant field observation so important for crop success?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aye omanye lɛ?

english: Early detection of issues like insect damage or disease allows you to fix problems quickly before they destroy your crop and ruin your financial investment.
ga: Naagbai ni anaa mra, tamɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo hela Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsuɔ naagbai ahe nii oya Dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ shika ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does careful management turn a small harvest into a profitable business?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ahe nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ baanyɛ aha nikpamɔ bibioo ko afee jarayeli nitsumɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he?

english: Consistent care maximizes the yield of every single plant, allowing you to cover your production expenses and save profit to fund your next planting cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso awo yibii babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ toɔ ni okɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ ato koni okɛwo dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: What actually is pruning, and why does my cocoa tree need it?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi cacao tso lɛ?

english: Pruning is the careful cutting away of dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches from a tree. It allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk and inner leaves, which keeps the tree healthy and helps it produce more fruit.
ga: Tso niji ni egboi, hela emɔ amɛ, loo niji ni he ehiaaa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ wajeɔ tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: When is the best time for me to prune my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ?

english: The best time to prune cocoa trees is right after you have harvested most of the ripe pods. Waiting until after the major harvest ensures you do not accidentally disturb or damage young, growing pods.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛfolɔ cacao tso lɛ ji beni okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ateŋ babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ kpeteŋkpele lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha okɛ oshara akagbala loo okpãtã ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How does removing overgrown branches after harvesting help my cocoa trees produce well for the next season?
ga: Te niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni ajieɔ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing out extra branches after harvest allows the tree to stop wasting energy on old foliage. Instead, the tree directs its nutrients toward resting, growing strong new leaves, and flowering for the next crop.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai momoi amli lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ kɛ niye níhi baa hwɔmi mi. Ha baai heei lɛ awa ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to regularly observe the way my cocoa trees grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni mi-kokoo tso lɛ daa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Observing your cocoa trees helps you understand their growth cycle so you can time your farm activities correctly. Watching the tree shows you when pods are forming, when branches are overgrown, and when it is safe to prune.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ cacao tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onuɔ bɔ ni cacao tso lɛ daa lɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni okɛ be ni sa atsu oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi lɛ ahe nii. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee. Niji lɛ dara tsɔ. Ni mɛɛ be ehi akɛ abaafolɔ tsei lɛ?

english: How do small young cocoa pods develop into big ones ready for harvest?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Small cocoa pods grow bigger over several months as the tree supplies them with water and nutrients from the soil. With good light and care, these small pods steadily expand and change color as the beans inside mature.
ga: cocoa pods bibii Amɛdaraa yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli be mli ni tsei lɛ haa amɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ kane kpakpa kɛ hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yaa nɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some small cocoa pods fail to grow big and instead dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ ekomɛi edaaa ni moŋ amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Small pods often dry up or fail to grow if the tree is stressed, lacks nutrients, or if branches are cut off at the wrong time, depriving the small pods of the shade and food they need to expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛdaraaa kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ehe, loo kɛji akɛ afolɔ eniji yɛ be ni esaaa mli. make pods bibii Shade ni bɛ kɛ niyenii he miihia ni alɛɛ mli.

english: What happens if I cut branches from my cocoa trees while they still have small pods on them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo cacao tso nine ko yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Pruning while small pods are still on the tree can shock the tree and expose delicate pods to harsh sunlight, causing many of those young pods to fall off or die before they can mature.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lɛ, tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akpokpo ni eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii bibii babaoo shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell that my cocoa trees are ready for a major harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ wulu lɛ?

english: Your cocoa trees are ready for a main harvest when most of the full-sized pods on the trunk and branches turn from green or red to a bright yellow or orange color, showing the beans inside are fully ripe.
ga: O-cocoa tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ beni ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: What makes cocoa pods become plentiful on a tree during the main season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii babaoo feɔ tsei anɔ yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: Pods become plentiful when trees are pruned at the right time after harvest, giving them space and sunlight to produce many healthy flowers that develop smoothly from small cherelles into large mature pods.
ga: Pods lɛ fa babaoo kɛji akɛ afolɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ha amɛ he ko kɛ hulu la koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ cherries bibii amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni eda kwraa lɛ amli.

english: Can trimming my cocoa trees at the wrong time reduce the total weight of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo tso lɛ ni mifoɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, trimming at the wrong time can destroy developing flowers and young pods, directly reducing the total number of mature pods available for you to collect at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata fɔfɔi kɛ tsei bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni edara lɛ ayibɔ baa shi ni obaanyɛ obua naa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl up, the crop is protecting itself from losing too much water. By rolling its leaves, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun and dry air, helping the plant hold onto moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ miibu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: It is always best to water early in the morning. Morning watering allows the soil to absorb moisture before the sun heats up and evaporates it, giving your plants the water they need to survive the heat of the day.
ga: Nu lɛ be fɛɛ be leebi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ dɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ lasu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nu ni he hia amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Heat makes the pollen sterile, so the flower cannot form a fruit, causing the plant to drop the flower to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during heavy rain and high winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil rather than going deep. When the ground becomes soaked with water, the soil softens, and heavy bunches make the top of the plant too heavy to stay upright in strong winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee blɛoo. Ni niji ni tsii baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee tsii tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves up to the young growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa baa bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and dropping off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing water through them and enters a quiet resting state until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ kpaɔ nu ni amɛlaajeɔ lɛ ni amɛboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete like people sharing a single bowl of food. They fight for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants that produce small harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa akaŋ tamɔ gbɔmɛi ni jaa niyenii tsɛnsi kome. Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni no haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow out of the ground when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored energy. If buried too deep, the young sprout uses up all its energy pushing through the heavy soil and dies before it can reach sunlight to start making its own food.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he koni amɛje amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii feemɔ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even if I give my crops fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild and aggressive growers that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. If weeds are left near your plants, they will drink the water and feed on the nutrients intended for your harvest.
ga: Weed ji koo mli tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni eyɛ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji jwɛi ashi yɛ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Amɛbaanu nu lɛ ni amɛye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha okpamɔ lɛ.

english: Pruning cocoa trees opens up the branches so air and sunlight can flow through the leaves. Sunshine and airflow reduce moisture where fungal diseases like black pod thrive, while directing the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo kokoo tso lɛ, egbeleɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ baai lɛ amli. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ daa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted poultry manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry organic matter, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, preserves soil moisture during hot days, and stops weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Is animal manure good enough to replace chemical fertilizers on my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani kooloi ashishifãi lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsake tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, dry animal manure adds nutrients naturally and improves the soil structure so it holds water better. While it releases nutrients slower than chemical fertilizers, it keeps your soil healthy for a longer time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii fataa he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii feɔ fɛo koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii blɛoo fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ, Shi ebaaye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, protecting the young cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it bad to plant peppers in the exact same bed where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot back-to-back lets pests build up in the soil, while rotating with crops like maize or beans starves those pests.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei yɛ he kome ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that produce very small yields or fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii loo yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and yellowish dust inside the growing tip?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ sũ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant, eating the leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, uneven watering, or dry soil. Giving your plants consistent moisture during hot periods helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do I need to stick wooden poles into the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to prevent leaf diseases and maximizes exposure to sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi foliar hela naa ni eha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa trees on my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct sunlight while they are small. Plantains grow very fast and provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive and grow well.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn light yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged or too dry. Adding organic compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady rainfall for at least a week so that the ground becomes deeply moist. Planting immediately after the very first light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ anɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be otsi kome koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: What type of plantain suckers should I select from an old farm to start a new plantain farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mahala kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje plantain ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should select maidenhead or sword suckers, which have narrow, sword-like leaves and strong, broad bases. Avoid suckers with wide, fully developed leaves because they grow weaker and produce smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala oblayoo bulbs loo klante ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ baai ni mli kwɔ, tsei ni eda lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa ni amɛbaafee plantain jwɛi bibioo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops after I clear and plant my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing land exposes weed seeds hidden in the soil to sunshine, causing them to sprout quickly before your crops establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jɛmɛ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa hulu la. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing on the leaves of my crops, and how does it hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by insect pests like beetles and caterpillars feeding on the crop. Leaves are the plant's food factory; when they are eaten and damaged, the plant cannot produce enough energy, resulting in poor growth and smaller yields.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Baai ji tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛ aye ni efite lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa shweremɔ ayaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can identify readiness when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, or by carefully digging around one stand to check root size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ hesaamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ Stand one lɛ he ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifã lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my plantain suckers too close to one another on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for water, soil food, and sunlight. This causes the plants to grow tall and weak, making them easily blown over by wind and resulting in small, thin plantain bunches.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la he, ni no haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya Enɛ haa plantain tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why should I leave dried leaves and cut weeds on the ground around my plantain stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni mafo jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving dead plant material on the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch prevents the sun from drying out the soil, keeps weeds from growing, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Mulch yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my plantain leaves and make them dry up early?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii diji miigbɛ eshwa mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ni eha amɛmiigbi oya?

english: Black spots on plantain leaves are usually caused by leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka, which thrive in humid and warm weather. Cutting off infected leaves and maintaining clean farm conditions helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai tamɔ Sigatoka, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni akwɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni he tse nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ.

english: What should I do if I notice a strange crop disease spreading rapidly across my pepper field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina tso hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? Ani egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You should immediately remove and destroy the infected plants away from your field to stop the spread, and contact an extension officer to help identify the disease before applying any chemical.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ koni okpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. ni okɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ abɔ koni amɛye amɛbua bo ni oyoo helai dani okɛ tsofai komɛi atsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when there are no trees above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tso ko bɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight; without shade crops like plantain to cover them, the hot sun dries out their leaves and scorches the plant.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ekãa ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaashã tso lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular water supply, which stresses the crop and prevents proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa pollination ni sa aba.

english: When maize is crowded, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting beans in the same farm help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmeii lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby maize plants.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant yams on the exact same mound every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing yams on the same spot continuously exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets yam-specific pests and diseases build up permanently in the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa sweet potato nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die when rainwater sits around their stems for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates the roots by blocking oxygen, which causes root rot and stops the plant from taking up food and water.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii kɛ nu nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to trim some leaves off my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming lower leaves stops ground diseases from jumping onto the plant, increases air movement, and forces the plant to send its food energy into growing bigger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akaho kɛya tso lɛ nɔ. ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii hewalɛ amaje koni amɛwo yibii wuji

english: Why do seeds I saved from my previous maize harvest give me less yield than certified seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni shwapo lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor and disease resistance over generations, whereas certified store seeds are specially bred to produce strong plants and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ shwapoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed young growth.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eye ebua tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and excess shade. Pruning overhead trees and clearing weeds helps airflow and reduces wetness on pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up with light yellow spots and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by small whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early vine drying is often caused by Yam Anthracnose, a fungal leaf disease triggered by heavy rains, or underground pests attacking the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ wain tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ mra. Fungal baa hela ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛbaa. loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is a lack of bees and wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wrinkle up into tight cups and stop growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on young leaves and transmitting viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize each year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every season drains the soil of specific nutrients and builds up pests. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over at the root even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain roots can be weakened by tiny worm-like pests called nematodes or weevil borers that eat the underground corm, causing the whole stem to tip over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii anɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Ha tsei lɛ fɛɛ agbee shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantain suckers next to young cocoa seedlings?
