ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and provide wide leafy shade to protect the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of hot weather or because of a disease in the roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ loo shishifãi ahe hela hewɔ?

english: If crops droop in the hot afternoon sun but recover overnight, it is heat stress. If they remain wilted in the cool morning and soil is moist, it indicates a root rot disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko gbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi ehiɛ ba shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ, Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Kɛji akɛ egboɔ lolo yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ eji shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. This often happens in poor soil or after heavy rains wash nutrients away. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps moisture in the ground during hot days. It keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and turns into natural manure as it rots.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo

english: How does planting beans alongside my main crop help my soil grow better food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa niyenii kpakpa?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby crops extra nutrients to grow better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees creates gentle shade and moisture, helping the cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni ashi amɛdamɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground stays soaked with water for too long, the roots suffocate and rot. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain plant, they all fight for the same water and food in the soil, leading to small bunches. Leaving only one or two strong shoots allows the main plant to produce large, heavy plantains.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ mli tsei 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do yam farmers put long wooden sticks in the ground for the yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato okwaafoi kɛ tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii lɛ? Fuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, exposing them to light and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enaa la ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai anaa.

english: What causes tiny worms to eat the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on corn leaves. The tiny caterpillars crawl deep into the central leaves to feed, leaving visible holes; catching them early with natural or recommended treatments keeps them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ. Kplukai bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛyaye nii, ni amɛshiɔ bu ko ni anaa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the heat is too extreme, when the plant lacks consistent water, or when tiny pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a plant virus. Controlling these small pests early stops the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tso mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɔ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up in the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them protects the cocoa until it gets older and stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plant uses to stay green and grow fast. This happens when the soil runs out of nutrients or during heavy rains that wash nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Enɛ baa mli be mli ni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa niyenii mli nibii laajeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava yields get smaller every time I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same soil every year drains specific nutrients without giving the land time to rest or rebuild. Rotating crops or letting the land rest restores soil health.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ koni ená shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce smaller fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Leaves curl up or droop as a survival trick to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping the plant hold onto water. Once the heat cools down in the evening, the leaves usually bounce back.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe loo amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa yiwalaheremɔ koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop due to extreme heat stress, lack of water, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering and avoiding heavy chemical sprays during flowering help save the blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do weeds actually stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your plants. They also hide dangerous insects that can attack and damage your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Amɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ atutua ni amɛfite onibii lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my crops or if it is a disease making them sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii loo hela ko miiha amɛmiiye hela?

english: Insects usually leave clear physical damage like holes in leaves or bitten stems, while diseases often show up as strange spots, molds, wilting roots, or unnatural color changes without visible bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ bu yɛ baai amli loo tsei ni emɔ amɛ. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Ejieɔ ehe kpo bei pii akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ŋmeii, kɛ shishifãi ni egboi. loo su ni tsakeɔ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often heats up dry soil without soaking it deep enough, creating a warm, damp environment that rots seeds. It is best to wait for steady, consistent rains so the ground stays wet and cool.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ ni haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches or suckers from plants like tomatoes or garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine tamɔ tomato loo abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra leaves and weak branches forces the plant to send its energy and nutrients straight into producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary stems.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Can I use one chemical spray from the market to solve every pest and disease problem on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jara nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛtsu tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii?

english: No single chemical can cure all crop problems. Insecticides only kill insect pests, fungicides treat fungal diseases, and fertilizers feed the soil. Using one spray for every issue wastes your money and can damage your crops.
ga: Tsofa kome pɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ atsu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahe nii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii pɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa ŋmeii helai. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome tsu nii kɛha naagba fɛɛ naagba lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika ni ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If my plant leaves are turning yellow, does that mean I should buy a chemical spray right away?
ga: Kɛji mi tso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are not always caused by a disease. They are often a sign that the plant is missing soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that it is getting too much or too little water. You must find the true cause before buying sprays.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be hela kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. Esa akɛ otao nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa dani ohe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different bottle medicines together in my knapsack sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baafutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: No, mixing different farm chemicals without expert guidance can cause a chemical reaction. This can destroy the medicine's effectiveness or create a harsh mixture that burns your crop leaves.
ga: Dabi, tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ŋaalɔi akudɔɔɔ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko afee nɔ ko. Enɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ loo efee nɔ ko ni mli wa ni baashã otso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off so easily when I touch them or when it gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ mita amɛhe loo kɛ́ edɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers are very delicate. When the plant suffers from high heat, lack of water, or rough handling, it experiences stress and drops its flowers to save energy, which stops fruits from growing.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa. Kɛ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitsumɔ ni wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Enɛ ɔ ma ha nɛ yiblii ɔ kpa wami.

english: Why are my young pepper fruits dropping off the plant while they are still tiny and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby peppers lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Young pepper fruits are very sensitive to sudden environmental changes, insect attacks, or irregular watering. If the plant feels under threat or lacks water, it sheds the young fruit to stay alive.
ga: Pepper yibii bibii lɛ nuɔ shihilɛ mli tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa, kooloi ni baatutua amɛ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he waa. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ awo ehe gbeyei loo nu efo emli lɛ Ewoɔ yibii bibii bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: People tell me that putting double the recommended fertilizer will make my maize grow twice as fast. Is that true?
ga: Akɛɛ mi akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛwo mli lɛ wo mli lɛ shii enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha mi-abele lɛ ada oya shii enyɔ. Ani eji anɔkwale?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn your crop's roots and kill the plant. Crops can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients at a time, so extra fertilizer ruins soil balance and wastes money.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ni ebaafite shika.

english: Why does my garden egg plant have plenty of big green leaves but no fruits growing on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yibii ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ?

english: Giving your plant too much nitrogen fertilizer causes it to spend all its energy growing heavy leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Crops need a balanced feed to produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei ni tsii ni miida lɛ ahe. yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ Niyenii ni ja he miihia Dumɔwui koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, heavy shade. It is an infection that requires you to prune shade trees and remove diseased pods so it doesn't spread to healthy trees.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo, shade ni mli wa mli kɛbaa. Eji hela ko ni biɔ ni afo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my crops wither and die after I spray weedkiller around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Many weedkillers are non-selective, meaning they kill any green plant they touch. If even a light drift of the spray touches your crop's leaves or stems, the crop absorbs the poison and dies.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ halaaa mɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaagbe tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakpe lɛ. Kɛji aerosol ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tswa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai loo amɛshishifãi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaŋɔ poison lɛ ni egbo.

english: While cassava leaves curl slightly to conserve water, yellow patches and heavy twisting indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease. This virus is spread by tiny whiteflies, so you need to plant disease-resistant stems rather than just relying on rain.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei baa lɛ ebɔle ehe fioo koni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli moŋ, shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni etsake waa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmei mosaic hela. Nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct heat and strong winds. Clearing all trees exposes them to intense sun, which scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots can grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Tso fɛɛ tso ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa aba enɔ. Enɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnaa nu.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts on my land before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial bacteria on their roots that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the dirt. Planting them first feeds the soil with natural fertilizer that your next maize crop needs to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni he baahia o-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why does putting chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my tomato plant make it wilt and burn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tomato tsei ahe lɛ haa amɛgboɔ ni amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts. Putting them directly on or next to the main stem sucks moisture straight out of the plant's skin and burns its roots. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso titri lɛ nɔ loo ebɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni eshã shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, koni amɛtsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, blocks the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do fall armyworm caterpillars always hide deep inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall caterpillars lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on maize leaves at night, and once the caterpillars hatch, they head straight for the central funnel because it is dark, moist, and filled with tender leaves that are easy for them to chew safely away from predators.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ gbɛkɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyaa gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ eyɛ duŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eyi kɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaye shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tiny and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or thrips, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects feed on the sap, they weaken the leaf tissue and cause it to distort as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nu nu lɛ Amɛhaa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhaa efiteɔ beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do I get very small cassava tubers when I plant my cassava sticks close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he kome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves fight for sunlight and their roots fight for space and food. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough soil area to swell its roots into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Leaving too many plantain shoots on one plant forces them to share the food brought up from the roots. Cutting off extra shoots leaves only one strong follower, allowing the main plant to direct all its energy into producing a giant, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi plantain ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛja niyenii ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsofɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa shwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and rolling up tightly into tubes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll into tight tubes during dry weather to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which keeps moisture from escaping. The yellowing happens because the plant cannot absorb nitrogen from dry soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa tsɔnei ni mli wa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli. Yellow baa ejaakɛ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off the plant without forming any fruit when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato pollen becomes sticky and sterile when daylight temperatures get too high. When pollen fails to fertilize the flower due to heat stress, the plant simply sheds the unfertilized flower to save its energy.
ga: Tomato pollen lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollen nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔfɔi yɛ latsaa hewɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When the soil runs low on nutrients, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally and restores its fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each cassava plant enough room to spread its leaves and develop large, healthy tubers below ground.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei tso he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ ŋmei wuji ni mli wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: How do I know if the first rainy day of the season means it is time to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: The first rain often just wets the surface soil, which can trick seeds into germinating only to dry up and die when the sun returns. It is best to wait until the rains become steady and the soil is moist several inches deep before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ shi amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ inchii komɛi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my corn plants and leaving small holes and brown powder behind?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu bibii? Ni powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides deep inside the growing tip of maize plants. Checking your farm early and spraying safe insecticides or applying neem extracts can protect your crop before the damage spreads.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted on my cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to sprout quickly and grab open sunlight and soil moisture before cultivated seeds can get established. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the head start they need to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛhe hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ dani amɛdu dumɔwui. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná akaŋshii hegbɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving some big trees gives the young cocoa the soft shade and cool moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ amɛ ni amɛhe bɛ nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha kookoo bibioo lɛ aná su ni mli tse kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lack of nutrients, or attacks by pests like mirids (capsids). Ensuring proper soil moisture, shade, and pest control helps the flowers turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa, hulutsoo, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Tubers rot when water stays trapped around the roots for too long due to heavy rains and hard soil, or from fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa hewɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and dry up during the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by small organisms in the soil called bacteria or fungi that block the water pipes inside the plant's stem. Once infected, the plant cannot draw water up to its leaves, so planting resistant seeds and avoiding waterlogged soil is key.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ bacteria loo fungi ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ trukaa nɛɛ baa. Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ agbala nu kɛyashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe hia ni adu dumɔwui ni wa ni ajie shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. Shade trees act as a natural blanket, protecting the young cocoa from intense heat, keeping the soil moist, and helping the leaves stay green and healthy until the crop matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential food it needs to build green leaves and grow big cobs. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its strength.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli ni akwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Crop roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil leaves the plant unable to take in the food, and concentrated fertilizer touching dry roots can actually burn and damage them.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni kɛ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ kpeɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite nii.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have tiny natural helpers in their roots that pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the dirt to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot caused by damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ hewalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni etsĩɔ baai ni sũ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa

english: Black pod is a disease caused by microscopic fungi that thrive in cool, damp, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into the farm, which dries out the wet conditions the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ adara lɛ agbi.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus to the plant. The virus disrupts the plant's food movement, causing leaves to twist and preventing the fruit from reaching full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Virus gbalaa niyenii ni tsei yaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ ashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying until moisture and temperature conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa baaya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if heavy rain stays on my farm too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the farm for too long, the soil suffocates the roots, causing fungal rot to set in underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni afuɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my fruits drop off the tree before they are ripe enough to sell at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit drop usually happens when trees lack water or nutrients like potassium during fruit development, or when pests attack the stems. Keeping the soil moist during dry periods and adding organic manure gives the tree the strength to hold onto its fruits until full maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium bɛ tso ko mli yɛ tso yibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua tso lɛ yibii lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni okɛ tsofa ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔ tso lɛ yibii amli kɛyashi ebaada.

english: What causes my watermelons to crack open in the farm before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa watermelon lɛ tswaa yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Watermelons burst when they receive a sudden surge of water after a long dry period. The inside grows faster than the skin can stretch. Providing regular, balanced watering prevents this sudden pressure build-up.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nu ni fa trukaa yɛ be mli ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ naa.

english: How can I stop my harvested tomatoes from rotting quickly before I get them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Tomatoes rot fast if picked during the hot sun or packed in deep, heavy baskets where bottom fruits get crushed. Harvesting early in the morning while it is cool and packing them in shallow, ventilated crates prevents bruising and slows down rotting.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛwo tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔ ni tsii amli he ni ashwieɔ aduawai lɛ yɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni akɛwo adekai ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil within two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli beni atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots react quickly to air once severed from the stem, causing dark veins and rapid spoilage inside. Leaving a small piece of the stem attached to the root when harvesting and keeping the roots in cool shade helps them stay fresh longer.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he nii oya kɛji afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa lá ni hoɔ yɛ lá mli lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ fitemɔ ni yaa oya yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ashi tso bibioo ko ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe beni akpaa shishifãi lɛ ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I keep insects from destroying my harvested maize while waiting for prices to go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni jara aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils thrive in stored maize that still holds moisture. Drying your maize until the grains are very hard and storing them in sealed hermetic bags cuts off oxygen, preventing insects from surviving without using harmful chemicals.
ga: Weevils lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni ato ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they suffer from high heat stress or lack of soil moisture. Spreading dry grass as mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi afɔ shi. tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do black spots appear on my garden eggs while they are growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Black spots are typically caused by fungal diseases that grow in humid, overcrowded farms. Spacing plants properly allows air and sunlight to pass through, keeping the leaves dry and stopping fungal spot diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why are my plantain bunches much smaller than what other farmers produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibioo kwraa fe nɔ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi woɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain bunches remain small when the main plant has too many suckers growing around it, competing for nutrients and water. Cutting away extra suckers so that only two or three grow alongside the mother plant leads to larger bunches.
ga: Plantains kuu ko ji bibioo lolo kɛ́ tso titri lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ ehe, ni amɛmiitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni fioo loo etɛ pɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso nyɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ afee niji wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning dense shade tree branches to let in sunlight and removing affected pods early prevents the rot from spreading across the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni ojie ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Clearing all shade trees leaves them exposed to intense heat, which dries them out and kills them before they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni egbeɔ amɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, light, and nutrients from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem grows strong and produces larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ adara ni efee panicles wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen feeds green leaf growth, so when the soil lacks it, the plant draws nitrogen from its oldest leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daalɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my rice crops produce fewer grains when I sow the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When rice plants are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding weakens the individual stalks, causing them to produce smaller grain heads.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmeii aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui ayitsei bibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when we get heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water blocks air from reaching the roots. Without oxygen in the soil, the roots suffocate and rapidly decompose.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaafite oya.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight to make food for the plant. It also keeps leaves away from damp soil, preventing leaf fungal diseases and resulting in bigger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba amɛnɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do groundnut flower stems push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but once pollinated, the stem grows downward into the soil. The actual groundnut pods need the darkness and moisture of the earth to grow and ripen.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee pollination lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut pods diɛŋtsɛ Ehe miihia duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures get extremely hot or when watering is irregular. High heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tsei agbo koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or from viruses carried by those insects that twist the leaves as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii ni tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ mli kooloi kɛ helai ni baa lɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually mean the plant has cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant varieties and pulling up infected young plants stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii anɔ. Kɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hela lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbala dumɔwui ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my young maize leaves overnight while leaving nearby grass alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kpata mi-baby corn baai lɛ ahiɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli, ni amɛshi jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ pɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer young maize leaves because they are soft, sweet, and rich in nutrients that help caterpillars grow fast. Inspecting crop leaves early in the morning helps you catch the caterpillars when they are actively feeding so you can apply targeted treatments.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe tsei ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni amɛmli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do red Striga weeds only grow attached to the base of my maize and sorghum stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi tsuru lɛ pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Striga seeds stay asleep in the dirt until they smell specific liquid chemicals released by maize or sorghum roots. Once awakened, Striga roots attach directly into your crop's roots to steal water and food, which weakens the stalk.
ga: Striga dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɛ efeee nɔ ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnuɔ tsofai ni ji nu ni ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi jieɔ lɛ he. Kɛji ote shi lɛ, Striga shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow taller and stronger when I plant cowpeas in between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waa kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are natural soil restorers that absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When planted alongside maize, cowpeas release this nitrogen into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the hungry maize plants.
ga: Cowpea ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the fruit bunches on my plantain trees getting smaller when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves and large root systems that need plenty of sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Planting them too close forces the suckers to fight each other for food and light, which reduces the size of the final fruit bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi wuji ni biɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa naagbee kuu lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines produce many green leaves on top but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen fertilizer, the sweet potato plant spends all its energy growing lush foliage above ground instead of food tubers below. Balanced soil with more potassium encourages the plant to store energy underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baatsu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their young flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi bibii lɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience high heat, low air humidity, or insufficient shade during dry spells. Providing tall shade trees keeps the farm moist and cool so the cocoa tree can hold onto its flowers until pods form.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ni baa shi loo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves of my hot pepper plants turn brown and drop off during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants suffer from root rot when water collects around their roots for too long without draining. Excessive water in the soil chokes the roots and breeds fungi, making the leaves wilt and fall off. Planting on raised beds helps surplus water run off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa. Shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni nu shwieee. Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ebaaha ŋmeii aba. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many bright yellow flowers that fall off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers require gentle movement from wind or bees to transfer pollen inside the flower so fruit can grow. Extremely hot weather can damage pollen, causing flowers to drop off unpollinated before fruit can develop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ ni ajie amɛ blɛoo. Kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii amli koni ekɛ pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pollination bɛ mli dani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin sprouting green shoots inside the barn before I take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akɛba jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plants that naturally wake up from their resting state when exposed to warmth and light inside the storage area. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated, and shaded barn slows down this natural sprouting so tubers stay heavy and firm.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛji akɛ amɛna hulutsoo kɛ la ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Sweet Potatoes ni Akɛtoɔ Atoohe ni Mli Ejɔ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ yitso lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dying when the heat comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight in their early years. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a cool environment and shields the young leaves from excessive heat until the cocoa canopy develops.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my young maize crop, and how does it hurt the harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa abifao lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te enáa ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are typically caused by leaf-eating caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. These pests feed on the central shoot, which weakens the plant's growth and reduces the number of full corn cobs produced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ajie ŋmãa ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ lɛ ayibɔ shi

english: Why does my maize turn light yellow and remain short even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize turns yellow and stays stunted when the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth. Applying appropriate fertilizers early in the growth period helps the plant regain its deep green color and vigor.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest without digging them up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛtsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and cracks begin to appear in the soil near the base of the stem where the tubers are swelling.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛdalɛ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ, he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to erect stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which is transferred underground to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: Dark patches on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by Blossom End Rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering during fruit development.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji Blossom End Rot, ni baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and look distorted?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap and transmitting plant viruses, causing leaves to twist and growth to slow down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdalɛ hu baa shi.

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, take water and soil nutrients away from the main mother plant. Removing extra shoots ensures the main plantain receives full nourishment to grow a large, heavy cluster of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo baajie nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa plantain titri lɛ náa niyenii jogbaŋŋ koni ewo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural food for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I water them early in the morning or during the midday heat?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because low temperatures allow the roots to soak up moisture before the heat of the day causes the water to evaporate quickly from the dry soil.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it that when I plant cassava sticks upside down in the soil, they do not grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ekwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni etsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have natural directions for water and food transport. Planting them upside down forces the roots to grow upwards before bending back down, which confuses the plant, delays growth, and produces weak, small tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya ŋwɛi dani amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shi. ni futuɔ tso lɛ lɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa yitso bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: When maize is planted too closely, the roots fight each other for the same soil food and water, while the leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. This competition starves the plant, leaving it without enough energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for green color and strong leafy growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash food out of the soil or waterlogs the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji tsei aniyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha niyenii jɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant conserve water so it doesn't dry out. However, if the leaves stay curled and yellow, it can also be a virus spread by tiny whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ehaaa egbi. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress, such as long dry spells, excessive heat, or insect attacks. The tree sheds flowers as a survival mechanism to preserve water and nutrients for itself rather than spending energy on pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ mli, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkɛtsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ pod lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my watermelon fruits rot and turn black at the blossom end before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering—such as letting the soil dry out completely and then flooding it with water.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa ni no sɛɛ lɛ afɔseɔ nu awoɔ nɔ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have tiny natural factories on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food in the soil. When you harvest groundnuts, this left-over nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why must I clear weeds away from my crops even when the weeds are small and not shading my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhaaa mitsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ.

english: Even small weeds have roots beneath the ground that drink water and steal plant food meant for your crops. Removing them early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and provide wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni masaa tsei ni mikɛbaakwɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves fully into the sunlight, which fuels tuber growth underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I avoid watering my garden vegetables in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ he yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot sun causes water to evaporate into the air before the plant's roots can drink it. Additionally, water drops left on leaves can act like magnifying glasses in intense heat and scorch the leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo kɛ́ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the stems grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so the soil stays wet longer during dry days, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges helps rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when bees fail to visit the flowers to help them form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ ayasara fɔfɔi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects hiding under the leaves or by a virus they spread. Spraying the plants with neem water or insect spray helps protect new leaves.
ga: Koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ baai lɛ akumɔ baa. Akɛtee baai ashishi loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they catch sunshine and avoid rotting from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la ni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ sũ mli helai ni baa lɛ ahe fitemɔ he.

english: Why are small worms eating the leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms that hide in the growing tip of the plant to feed. Putting clean wood ash or recommended crop medicine in the leaf funnel destroys them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ ni he tse loo tso tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛwo baai lɛ amli lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the harvest I get from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and space intended for your crops, which starves the crops and lowers your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ni otsei lɛ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Which maize plants on my farm should I pick seeds from for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi esa akɛ mahala yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: You should only save seeds from the healthiest, strongest plants that produced the largest cobs and showed no disease, ensuring your next crop inherits those strong traits.
ga: Esa akɛ obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni he wa fe fɛɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ pɛ amli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aná nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ gboshinii.

english: When my plantain stool grows many small suckers around it, how do I choose which one to keep?
ga: Kɛ́ mi-plantain stool lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala nɔ ni mikɛto?

english: Look for the single strongest, healthiest shoot with thick stems and wide leaves, then cut away the weaker ones so the parent plant can give all its nutrients to that best one.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli tse kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, afoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ koni tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ anyɛ aha tso ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ niyenii fɛɛ.

english: How can I prepare my weak tomato seedlings in the nursery so they survive when I plant them out on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa tomato dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can strengthen fragile seedlings by gradually exposing them to direct sun and slightly reducing water a week before transplanting, building their toughness to handle field shock.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookwɛ amɛ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Okɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ nu lɛ aba shi fioo yɛ otsi mli dani okɛwo kroko mli. Koni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛkpee shoofeemɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and burn easily under strong sun; planting temporary shade crops like plantains gives them the shelter and cool moisture they need to grow roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa wɔɔhe kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why do some of my planted yam setts sprout very early while others take a long time in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ekomɛi miikwɛ̃ oya nɛkɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi yeɔ be babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam setts sprout based on their moisture content and natural dormant period; setts stored in cool, shaded conditions wake up evenly and sprout much faster.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa ha kɛ be ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ naa. Nibii ni ato yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baate shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why should I pull out healthy shoots if three or four maize seeds sprout in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii etɛ loo ejwɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Removing the extra seedlings leaves only the strongest plant per spot, stopping them from fighting for soil food and light so that single plant can yield a large cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi he fɛɛ he. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawuu yɛ niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he koni tsei komekomei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves but gives me tiny tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When cassava puts too much energy into branch and leaf growth, it neglects root development; trimming excess side shoots helps direct food down into growing big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo wo tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ Ekuɔ ehiɛ eshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii baa shi kɛyaa bulb ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: What special attention should I give to my pepper plants once they start producing flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ jwɛŋmɔ krɛdɛɛ esa akɛ mikɛha mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni amɛbɔi fɔmɔ?

english: When crops begin flowering, they need regular watering and rich nutrients so the delicate blossoms do not drop off before turning into hot peppers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ Ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akagbee shi dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: If I see one cassava plant on my farm with weak, stunted, and yellow leaves, what should I do to it?
ga: Kɛji mina ŋmei tso ko yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni baai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, egbɔjɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: You should uproot and remove that weak, diseased plant immediately so insects do not transfer the virus to your remaining healthy crop.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shishifãi awo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kooloi bibii lɛ akagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, forcing the plant to drag food out of its older leaves to support its growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛfi ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so that the crop yields well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Spacing maize properly (about 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between plants) ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors.
