ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ateŋ (aaafee 75 cm yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ 40 cm yɛ tsei ateŋ) yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot and die when I plant them in a low flat field where rain water stands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes cannot survive in waterlogged soil because standing water cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to rot and preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Tomato nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient crop leaves need to produce food and maintain a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe baai koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛhiɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, lack of soil moisture, or insufficient nutrient levels during the flowering phase.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb while my cassava grows straight up on its own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-cassava lɛ diɛŋtsɛ miida.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines with soft stems that require physical support to spread leaves toward the sun, whereas cassava naturally develops a thick, self-supporting woody stem.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni he hiaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni cassava lɛ feɔ tsei ni mli tse ni yeɔ ebuaa ehe lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen, the plant directs its energy into producing leaf growth above ground rather than storing energy in root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato shishifã bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops lead to a much bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haa yibii babaoo baa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and fertilizer away from crops; removing them ensures all soil nutrients and moisture go directly to building your crop's fruit or grain.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, kane, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ yaa onibii loo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions when heavy rain and dense shade trap humidity around the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa ni hulutsoo be lɛ mɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds after the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: You should sow after the soil has received two or three thorough rains so there is enough deep moisture to support germination without the seed drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ odu nii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa 2-3 sɛɛ koni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves drooping and turning yellow before the plant even produces fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ po woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Drooping yellow leaves in plantains usually point to root damage caused by tiny soil pests called nematodes or a severe shortage of potassium in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ plantains nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kɛbaa loo potassium ni faaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cashew trees on the same farm together with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ cashew tso yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ cocoa tso?

english: Cashew trees prefer full sunlight and drier conditions, whereas cocoa trees need shade and high humidity. If planted too close together, the cashew trees will outgrow the cocoa and block the moisture cocoa needs, so it is best to give them separate sections on your farm.
ga: Cashew tsei sumɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei. Kɛji akɛ adu Cashew tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛdaraa oya fe kookoo ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kookoo he hiaa lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbala fãi srɔtoi lɛ amli. Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How does keeping my farm neat and organized help my cocoa trees yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: A well-spaced and cleared farm allows air and sunlight to flow freely between trees. This reduces excess dampness that causes black pod disease, makes pest control easier, and allows trees to direct their energy into producing healthy pods.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli wa.

english: What are these tiny insects called 'abobɔ' on my cocoa flowers, and are they harming my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘abobɔ’ ni yɔɔ mi kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: The tiny 'abobɔ' (midges) are good friends to your farm. They pollinate the cocoa flowers by transferring pollen from one bloom to another, which is what actually causes the flowers to turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Abobɔ’ (teŋgbɛ gbɔmɔ) Tiny ji naanyo kpakpa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛhaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ muji ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only the ones visited and pollinated by tiny insects like midges will grow into pods. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off the tree.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii saraa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What can I do on my farm to attract more of these pollinating midges?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛgbala nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ babaoo?

english: Midges breed in moist, cool places. Leaving rotting plant leaves, banana stems, or old cocoa husk piles on the soil under the shade provides a perfect breeding ground for them to multiply.
ga: Midges fɔɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Tso baai ni egboi, akwawa tsei, loo kookoo momo ni abua naa lɛ ni ashwieɔ shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ nɔ Eji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees take a few years to bear fruit while crops like maize produce in months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ heɔ afii fioo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli.

english: Tree crops like cashew spend their first few years developing deep root systems and strong trunks to withstand harsh dry seasons. Once mature, a single cashew tree will continue producing harvest for many decades.
ga: Tso tsei tamɔ cashew heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa naa. Kɛji eda kwraa lɛ Cashew tso kome baaya nɔ awo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color distinctly. Pods that are naturally green turn bright yellow when ripe, while reddish varieties turn an orange-yellow color, showing the beans inside are mature.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods, ni ji eŋɔli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi tsuru lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃.

english: What is the proper way to harvest cocoa pods without damaging the tree?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa kookoo ŋmeii ni afiteee tso lɛ?

english: Always use a sharp harvesting hook or cutlass to cleanly cut the pod stem. Pulling or twisting pods off by hand damages the flower cushion on the trunk, preventing new flowers and pods from growing there in the future.
ga: Kɛ hoo loo kakla ni naa wa atsu nii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ onine gbala loo otsi fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. shwere yɛ jɛmɛ wɔsɛɛ

english: Why is it necessary to pick up cashew nuts immediately after they drop to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie cashew ŋmeii kɛji amɛgbee shikpɔŋ pɛ?

english: Cashew nuts drop naturally when fully ripe. Leaving them on the ground exposes them to soil moisture, rain, and insects, which rots the nut inside and reduces the price you can sell them for.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii baa amɛnɔ, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ mli, ni ebaaha jara ni obaanyɛ okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What preparations should I make before the main cocoa harvesting season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ hesaamɔi esa akɛ mafee dani kookoo kpamɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before harvesting, clear pathways through your farm for easy movement, sharpen your tools, clean your pod-breaking area, and prepare clean baskets or sacks so you can collect and ferment your beans without delays.
ga: dani abaakpa kpamɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni gbɛfaa afee mlɛo. sharpen tools Tsumɔ he ni pods lɛ fã lɛ. Ni saa tsɛnsi loo kotoku ni mli tse koni onyɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato ni okɛwo mli ni okɛwo mli oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil or getting too much water around their roots, which stops them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and smaller if I plant maize on the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize heavily feeds on specific soil nutrients every season; planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and lets soil pests build up.
ga: Abɛi nine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli kɛyaa be kroko mli. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: How do groundnuts help make the soil richer for other crops planted after them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots work with friendly soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanut shishifãi kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to stop losing water through the leaves, keeping its underground tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛkpa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ. ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do many small flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only flowers visited by tiny insects get pollinated; the tree also sheds extra flowers if it lacks enough water or food to support them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe. Tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi hu kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua lɛ bɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make the energy needed to grow thick, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves get white powdery spots on them during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and damp leaf surfaces create the perfect condition for fungal micro-organisms to grow and spread across the leaf surfaces.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually triggered when soil moisture swings quickly from dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant too many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Overcrowded plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them thin and weak instead of healthy and strong.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start to rot quickly when I stack them in a big pile inside my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛtoɔ ŋtayaa agbo ko mli yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When yams are piled high without space between them, heat and moisture get trapped. Crops still breathe after harvest, and trapped heat creates damp conditions that make fungi and bacteria grow fast, causing the tubers to spoil.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eto ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni gbɛ ko bɛ amɛteŋ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i emɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni egboi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil within a few days if I leave them out in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji mishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to ripen after picking. High heat speeds up their natural breathing process, causing them to lose water, turn soft, and rot quickly. Keeping them in a cool, shaded, and airy place slows down decay.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa adebɔɔ mli mumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nu shwieɔ amɛmli, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛgboiɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfite fiofio.

english: Why is it bad to store my freshly harvested maize in tightly sealed plastic bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa ehee lɛ baawo plastic kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain natural moisture that needs to evaporate. Sealing them in plastic bags traps this moisture inside, creating a warm, damp environment where mold grows rapidly and ruins the crop.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu ni esa akɛ etsɔ la yɛ ŋmaa ni akpa ehee lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo plastic kotoku mli lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Fɔ̃ɔ lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leafy stems above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, the cassava plant sends all its energy into growing thick leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food below ground to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni mli tse kɛ niji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi konɛ a pee ngmɔkɔ nguahi.

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This makes the stalks weak and produces small, poor-quality cobs compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield fewer pods when I cut down all the large trees around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni bɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa trees need partial shade from larger trees to protect them from intense sunlight and harsh winds. Without shade, the cocoa plants suffer heat stress, drop leaves, and produce fewer flowers and pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, Cocoa tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ mli, amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly due to stress caused by high temperatures, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. When the plant experiences extreme heat or thirst, it drops flowers to preserve its own survival.
ga: Nɔ ni haa pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi fe fɛɛ ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kumai ye amɛ lɛ Eshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛkwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my plantains so they don't spoil while still on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain lɛ? Enɛ ji koni ekafite be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Plantains should be harvested when the fingers are full and plump, but still completely green. If left to turn yellow on the plant, hot sunlight, insects, and birds will damage them before you can take them to market.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa plantains be mli ni niji lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo. Shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lolo. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ, ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi baafite lɛ dani akɛwo jara nɔ.

english: Why do my okra leaves curl up and turn yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Okra leaves curl to conserve moisture when the soil is too dry or when tiny sap-sucking insects attack them under the bright sun. Giving the plants adequate water helps them keep their leaves open and green.
ga: Roselle baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii miinu nɔ. Tutua amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi ni efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do my sweet potato roots split open under the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato shishifãi lɛ tswa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato roots split when there is sudden heavy rainfall after a long dry period. The roots absorb water too fast and expand quicker than their skin can grow, causing the tuber to crack open.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ada. ha yitso lɛ atswa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct sun and their roots cannot yet drink enough water to keep up with intense heat. Providing shade keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves while the plant builds a strong root system.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuuu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa lolo. Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ maa shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Planting maize too close forces the plants to fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving them enough space allows each plant to grow thick stalks and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji baa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crops you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is bone dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can swallow it. If you put fertilizer on dry soil without moisture, the concentrated chemicals can burn and kill the plant roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ami lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by using sunlight captured through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and airflow, which helps the plant make larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of proper soil nutrients. Without steady water and good soil food, the plant discards its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai bɛ daa lɛ, Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling is usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the sap out of the leaves, or that they have infected the plant with a virus. Treating the insects early stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Aloo kɛɛmɔ akɛ amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yeɔ tsei. Kplukai ahe tsamɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots get watery and spoil fast if a heavy rain falls right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain falls after a dry period, the cassava plant quickly drinks up water to start growing fresh leaves, transferring water into its root starch and making the roots watery and quick to rot.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ baanu nu oya koni ebɔi baai heei kwɛ̃mɔ. Okɛ nu awo shishifã lɛ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops even when I do not take care of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mikwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with naturally tough root systems that suck up food and water much faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear them early, they steal the nutrients meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa. ni baaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni eda lɛ Kɛji okɛjieee amɛ mra lɛ, Amɛbaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow well inside standing water while my maize rots if water sits around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle he.

english: Rice has special internal tubes in its stems that carry air down to its roots under water, whereas maize roots drown and rot because they cannot get air when covered in standing water.
ga: Omɔ yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni amɛbaagboi yɛ bɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛji akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ha amɛhe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and lose their leaves during the cold Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind rapidly pulls moisture out of leaves faster than roots can pull water from the ground. Mulching your soil with dry grass helps hold moisture near the roots to keep plants alive during cold, dry weather.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni eha tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: How can I protect my cassava plants so they stay healthy through the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping root crops survive long periods without rain.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the weather becomes very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme dry heat stresses the plant, making its pollen dry up before it can produce fruit. Watering deeply around the base of the plant early in the morning helps maintain healthy flower set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he waa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and rot when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain leaves soil waterlogged, which prevents plant roots from breathing. Constant dampness also encourages waterborne fungal diseases that break down leaf tissue.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ hu woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ nu mli ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my plantain leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa plantain baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black spots are usually fungal infections that thrive in wet, damp weather. Giving your crops enough space between each plant helps wind blow through and dry the leaves faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves look wilted even when my farm field is completely full of rainwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nu eyi miŋmɔji lɛ amli obɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits on top of soil for too long, it suffocates the roots. Damaged or drowning roots can no longer absorb water, causing the plant to droop as if it were in a drought.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Shishifãi ni efite loo ni egbo lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei gboiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do my tender young seedlings die when a heavy rain falls right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa beni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Very young plants have soft stems that can easily snap under heavy rainfall or rot in soggy soil. Building simple palm-frond shades over nursery beds protects small seedlings until they grow stronger.
ga: Tsei bibii waa lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baanyɛ akumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa shishi loo amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ afee ŋmei tsei ahe mfoniri ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. kɛyashi be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ

english: Is it good to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. A single light rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which will dry out and kill seeds right after they sprout.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in dry soil, ready to sprout instantly at the first drop of water. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the water and nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji nu klɛŋklɛŋ shwie shi pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field without tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate and need protection from harsh sunlight during dry periods. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby provides leafy shade and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee hulutsoo ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my land very well before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Proper land preparation removes weeds, loosens hard soil, and allows plant roots to spread easily. If the initial land clearing is done poorly, weeds will choke your young plants and cut down your final harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akabote mli. shwiemɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo Kɛji akɛ afeee shishijee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ Jwɛi baagbe otsei bibii lɛ ni ebaaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: What should I do if my farmland soil is very hard and difficult to dig?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ewa akɛ abaafo?

english: Hard soil usually lacks moisture and organic matter. You can soften hard land by adding compost or animal manure, clearing weeds without burning the bush, and digging to break up the soil so plant roots can breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛshãaa jwɛi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsaa koni akɛgbala shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu

english: Why do my crops grow weak and yellow when I plant them on an old farm site?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ shikpɔŋ momo nɔ lɛ?

english: Old farm sites usually lack nutrients because previous crops have used them up. Adding organic manure or compost helps restore soil fertility so new plants can get enough food to grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ŋmɔji momo amli ejaakɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ efo mli. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni akɛha tsei heei lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: How do I know when my old plantain trees need to be uprooted and replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehe baahia ni ajie mi dumɔwui momo lɛ ni akɛtsake?

english: When plantain stems become thin, produce tiny bunches, or fall easily in strong winds, the plant is too old. Uprooting old plantains frees up space and nutrients to plant fresh, healthy suckers that produce big yields.
ga: Beni plantains lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ Efoɔ mli efeɔ tsei bibii loo egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara tsɔ. Dumɔwui momo ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ kɛ niyenii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a broad, strong base. Avoid suckers with wide leaves because they produce weak plants with small fruit bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante tu’ ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo yibii bibii.

english: Can I get a good harvest if I plant plantains on a small piece of land?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa kpakpa kɛji midu plantains yɛ he ko bibioo?

english: Yes, plantains yield very well on small plots if you space them correctly and manage weeds. Because plantain is always in high demand across Ghana, even a small plot can produce a profitable harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains woɔ yibii waa yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ kɛji oto he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi miitao plantains waa yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko po baanyɛ ana sɛɛnamɔ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain buried in the soil for a long time and sprout instantly when sunlight and rain hit them. Main crops take longer because they spend their early days building roots underground before growing big leaves.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nibii titrii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ be babaoo yɛ shishijee mli. Koni afee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi dani adu baai wuji

english: What happens to my plantains if I leave them overgrown and do not harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantains lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ fe nine ni mikpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa?

english: Leaving ripe plantains unharvested causes fruits to rot on the stalk, attracts pests to your farm, and drains energy away from the young suckers growing around the main plant.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi plantain lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaaa lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ agbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Gbalamɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ojie hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my seedlings die off after sprouting well in the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young plants often die if the soil dries out quickly, if underground pests eat their soft roots, or if hard soil prevents their roots from pushing deeper to find water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu.

english: How does leaving old crop roots in the ground affect my new plants?
ga: Te tso shishifãi momo ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ saa mitsei heei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Old crop roots can hide pests and soil diseases from the previous season. They also block new roots from spreading and steal room that your new seedlings need to take firm root.
ga: Tso shishifãi momo baanyɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato. Amɛtsiɔ shishifãi heei hu anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛju he ni ehe hiaa ni odumɔwui heei lɛ atswa shishifãi shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my young seedlings are mature enough to be moved out of the nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings need time to build strong roots and sturdy stems. Waiting a few weeks gives them time to form a solid root structure so they can survive being lifted and replanted without dying.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ be koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa. Otsii fioo komɛi ni amɛbaamɛ lɛ baaha amɛná be ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi kɛji ajie amɛ ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛgbooo.

english: What will happen if I uproot my crops and plant them out when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mijie miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni midu be mli ni eji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Very young seedlings have weak, fragile roots that break easily when handled. Giving them extra time in the nursery ensures they are strong enough to handle the stress of transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii waa yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egbɔjɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ aha amɛ be kroko yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsu haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli baa lɛ he nii.

english: Should I water my seedbed before uprooting plants to move them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo dumɔwui lɛ ashishi nu dani majie tsei lɛ koni mikɛwo he kroko?

english: Yes, moist soil makes it easier to lift the plant cleanly. It allows the soil to stick to the roots and prevents delicate roots from tearing when you scoop the seedling out.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaawó tsei anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbala kɛji okɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwie shi.

english: What is the proper way to lift a young seedling from the soil without causing damage?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ awóɔ tso bibioo ko nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni afiteee lɛ?

english: Slide your hand gently under the soil beneath the root zone and lift the plant along with its soil block. This keeps the whole root system intact and undisturbed.
ga: Okɛ onine awo shikpɔŋ shishi blɛoo yɛ shishifã lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ awo nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Should I shake off the nursery soil from the roots before putting my plant in its new spot?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani mikɛ tso lɛ awo he ko hee?

english: No, you should keep the nursery soil attached to the roots. Leaving that original ball of soil around the root system protects the delicate roots and helps the plant recover faster after moving.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shishijee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ buɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi oya kɛji eshi.

english: How deep should I set my plant when transferring it into a new container or farm bed?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mitsei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miiwo tsɛnsi loo shikpɔŋ hee ko mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Set the plant at the same depth it was growing in the nursery bed. Make sure all the roots are completely covered with soil so they do not dry out.
ga: Okɛ tsei lɛ awo he ni mli kwɔ tamɔ bɔ ni adu amɛ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds directly into a large bucket right from the start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ tanki agbo mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ?

english: Starting seeds in smaller nurse beds allows you to give them close attention while they are weak. Once they develop strong roots, moving them into a big bucket gives them plenty of room to expand and produce food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni oooje shishi yɛ fɔmɔ saatso bibioo ko mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni saatso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee tanki agbo ko mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná he ko babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: How does moving a crop into a bigger bucket help it grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛyaa tanki agbo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: A larger bucket provides more space for the root system to spread out and collect water and food, which allows the plant above ground to grow taller and yield more.
ga: Tanki ni da fe tsutsu lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii amli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops look weak or wilted right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Crops experience a natural shock when moved to a new environment. Keeping the root ball complete and watering them immediately helps them recover quickly and start growing again.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli shoofeemɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee he ko hee. Kɛ́ okwɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu wo amɛmli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ oya ni amɛbɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to check the roots under a seedling before planting it out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi dani adu lɛ?

english: Checking underneath the seedling lets you confirm that the root system is healthy, fully developed, and holding the soil together, which guarantees the plant is ready to feed in its new position.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ona nɔmimaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ amli wa, amɛdara kwraa, ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaye nii yɛ he hee lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which the plant needs to build food and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, but legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves or spreading a virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and fall off naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to build big soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to grow long and thick, and elevated mounds prevent rain from drowning the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekabote shishifãi lɛ amli ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot or when the plant does not receive consistent water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when dark, dense branches stop sunlight and air from drying out the pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ediŋŋ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekaha tsei lɛ agbi.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or mulch stops heat from drying out the earth, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop fertilizer right next to the seed when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly on or next to a seed can burn the tender tender root shoots as soon as the seed tries to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwu lɛ nɔ loo emasɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛji dumɔwu lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do my young maize seedlings need a different type of fertilizer than full-grown plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants need special starter fertilizers high in phosphorus to build deep, strong roots early on, while mature plants need more nitrogen and potassium to grow tall leaves and fill out heavy grains.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa mra. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ehe miihia nitrogen kɛ potassium babaoo koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai kakadaji ni ewo dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing the crop lacks soil nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted compost or a balanced fertilizer restores the soil nutrients needed for green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji bolɔmɔ ni akɛbiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I apply vitamin and micronutrient boosters when my tomato plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ vitamini kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ mi-tomato tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ?

english: Flowering requires extra energy and nutrients like calcium and boron. Adding boosters at this stage prevents flowers from dropping off and stops the bottoms of the fruits from rotting.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium kɛ boron krokomɛi. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli fata he yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni ekagbee shi, ni ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why do my pepper plants need much more water when they start flowering than when they were small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ shwiemɔ fe be mli ni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Plants use extra energy and water to carry nutrients into flowers and growing fruits. If they dry out during flowering, the plant will shed its blossoms to survive, leaving you with fewer peppers.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛji amɛgbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Ehaa chili fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ bo.

english: Why should I trim off the extra small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nɔ ni fa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing them allows all the soil nutrients to go directly into producing one big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛhe koni amɛya tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee plantains ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I treat my crop seeds with protective powders before planting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ powda ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu aduawai dumɔwui ahe nii dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ mli lɛ?

english: Treating seeds coats them with protection against underground insects and fungal diseases, ensuring the tender young seed can sprout safely without rotting in the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, bibii nyɛɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbooo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in harsh, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist for young cocoa plants.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my maize plants grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This natural nitrogen feeds the nearby maize plants just like an added fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii tamɔ bɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Is there a difference between the yellow maize grown for poultry feed and the white maize I plant for food?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni miduɔ koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni miduɔ koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, feed maize is bred to be hard and rich in specific fats and nutrients needed by animals, while white human-food maize is bred for softness, taste, and easy pounding into local dishes like banku.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse ŋmãa koni efee nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ fɔ pɔtɛɛi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa kooloi babaoo. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, atsɔse ŋmãa yɛŋ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ blɛoo, ehiɛ ŋɔɔ ni abaanyɛ atswa lɛ mlɛo ni afee maŋ lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ banku lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does adding dried poultry manure to my farmland help my vegetables grow stronger roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi fata nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa lɛ?

english: Poultry manure adds organic matter that loosens hard clay soil, acts like a sponge to hold moisture, and slowly feeds roots with essential nutrients over a long time.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ fataa he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa haa shishifãi lɛ fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Is chicken manure really good for making my soil fertile and helping my crops grow?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmei ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa?

english: Yes, chicken manure is rich in nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter. It improves the soil structure, helps the soil retain water longer, and releases nutrients slowly to nourish your crops naturally without harsh chemicals.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni ojie niyenii mli hewalɛ kpo fiofio Koni oha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: How should I handle fresh chicken manure before putting it on my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsu tsina ŋmei hee he nii dani mikɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very hot and concentrated, which can burn plant roots. You need to let it dry out or compost it by mixing it with dry leaves or soil for a few weeks before applying it to your farm.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli edɔɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi Ehe miihia ni oha egbi loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ nɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time to apply chicken manure to my farm land?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ awo miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to apply composted chicken manure a few weeks before planting during land preparation. This gives the manure time to blend into the soil so the young crop roots can easily access the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ baatsu nii otsii fioo komɛi dani adu yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa be ni ekɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ oya.

english: Why does my farmland become hard and poor after using artificial fertilizers for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miifee basabasa yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Artificial fertilizers feed the crops quickly but do not feed the soil. Over time, heavy use reduces natural organic matter and beneficial soil organisms, leaving the soil hard, dry, and less productive.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I collect and sell chicken manure to other farmers as a business?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua tsina ŋmeii anaa ni mahɔ̃ɔ maha okwaafoi krokomɛi akɛ jarayeli nitsumɔ?

english: Yes, gathering, drying, and packaging composted chicken manure is a great farm enterprise. Many farmers prefer buying affordable, ready-to-use organic manure to boost their crop yields naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni abua naa, ni agbiɔ, ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ ji ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ wulu ko. Okwaafoi babaoo sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara waaa ni afee klalo akɛ akɛbaatsu nii koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens if chemical fertilizer touches the leaves or stems of my crops directly?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai loo amɛshishifãi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Direct contact with strong chemical fertilizer can scorch or burn the plant tissue because of its high salt content. Always apply fertilizer to the soil around the base of the plant, keeping a short distance from the stem.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã tsei ahe fãji yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli, ni oha he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahi shi fioo.

english: Can using improper or toxic fertilizers make my family and me sick?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaaa loo ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha mi kɛ miweku lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, handling dangerous farm chemicals without protective gear or consuming crops heavily sprayed with harmful chemicals can cause skin irritations, breathing problems, and long-term health issues.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he bɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara eshwie nɔ babaoo lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hewolo nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. mumɔ mli naagbai kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are my crops wilting even after I gave them strong chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer pulls moisture away from the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing fertilizer burn. This weakens the crop and makes it look like it is wilting or drying up.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashãa lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha efee tamɔ eegbo loo eegbi.

english: What basic protective steps should I take when handling farm fertilizers and chemicals?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Always wear gloves or cover your hands, wear long sleeves and a nose mask, avoid touching your face while working, and wash your hands thoroughly with soap and clean water immediately after finishing.
ga: Wo glɔvs loo ha oniji ahe be fɛɛ be. Wo atadei ni nine kakadaŋŋ ashɛ nɔ kɛ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa hiɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ohiɛ ni oootaa he beni otsuɔ nii lɛ he. Ni kɛ́ ogbe nitsumɔ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ oniji ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can heavy use of harsh fertilizers cause my vegetables to rot or get diseased?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ agbo loo helai aba amɛnɔ?

english: Yes, excessive chemical fertilizers can weaken the plant's natural defense systems and damage root tissues, making it easier for soil-borne diseases and rot to attack your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii baatutua onibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nutrients like nitrogen. When the soil lacks proper plant food or fertilizer, the plant cannot make enough chlorophyll to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to invest in feeding my soil with fertilizer if I want a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mishika awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji miitao yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Just like humans need good food to grow strong, crops consume nutrients from the soil to produce fruit. If you harvest year after year without replacing those nutrients with fertilizer or compost, the soil becomes empty and your crops will produce very little.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa adesai koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ewo yibii. Kɛji okpa nii afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the hot sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why will my harvest be smaller if I plant my crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots and leaf branches to spread out and produce larger fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ewoɔ yibii loo bulbs wuji.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads quickly during damp and rainy weather. Clearing weeds, pruning extra branches for light, and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. weeding Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni akɛha la kɛ mra ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars suddenly destroying my maize leaves, and how do I spot them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi-abele baai lɛ trukaa lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mana lɛ mra?

english: This is often Fall Armyworm. They lay eggs on the leaves, and when the worms hatch, they eat the inner funnel of the plant. Checking the middle leaves of your young maize weekly for small holes allows you to treat them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji Fall Asraafoi A-Worm. Amɛwoɔ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ tsei amli gbɛi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ gbekɛbii abele baa lɛ teŋgbɛ daa otsi kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa lɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my cassava tubers grow bigger?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crop. By keeping your field clean, all the food in the soil goes directly into feeding the cassava roots, making them grow bigger and heavier.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni aaaha ehe atse lɛ nɔ Niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛtsiiɔ.

english: Pruning removes weak branches that drain energy from the plant without producing good fruit. It also opens up the plant to sunlight and fresh air, which prevents diseases and directs the plant's food into growing larger tomatoes.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baaa. Ehaa tsei hu naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni ehaa tsei niyenii ni akɛduɔ tomatoi wuji.

english: When a plant experiences severe water stress from heat or drought, it drops its flowers to save energy and survive. Mulching the soil with dry grass helps hold moisture near the roots and prevents flower drop.
ga: Beni tsei naa nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kɛjɛɔ latsaa loo hɔmɔ mli lɛ. Tsei baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite ni amɛhi shi. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I save hybrid maize seeds from this year's harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yield in the first generation only. If you save and replant those harvested seeds next season, the new plants will grow unevenly and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ, Tso hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops fail even when I plant them at the exact same time as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miifee nɔ ni ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ be kome too mli kɛ afi ni eho lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana change from year to year. Relying strictly on a calendar date is risky because rains may start late or pause mid-season, so you must check soil moisture levels and local weather forecasts before sowing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi. Kalanda gbii ni akɛtsuɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Enɛ ji akɛ nugbɔ baanyɛ aje shishi blɛoo loo ekpa be kuku yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ dani odu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: If I add extra fertilizer to my tomatoes, will it make them produce twice as many fruits?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata tomato lɛ he lɛ Ani ebaaha tomato lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ?

english: Too much fertilizer can actually burn the roots or cause the plant to grow only big green leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Plants only take up what they need, so extra fertilizer often damages the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha tso lɛ baa agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji pɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the yellow leaves on my pepper plants spreading to the healthy leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɛ eshwa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean a fungal or bacterial infection. These diseases spread through wind, splashing water droplets, or farm tools, which is why removing affected leaves early protects the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa. Helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie baai ni ena hela lɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why didn't half of the maize seeds I bought at the market sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ fã ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Market seeds may have been stored improperly in hot or humid conditions, or damaged by insects, which kills the living embryo inside the seed and prevents it from growing.
ga: Ekolɛ abaato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. loo kooloi bibii efite Enɛ gbeɔ fɔmɔ kotoku fɛɛ fɔmɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look dead during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl to protect themselves from losing water through extreme heat. It is a natural survival trick to conserve moisture until the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛkwɛɔ koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi hulu lɛ baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How come caterpillars are still eating my cabbage even after I sprayed chemical pesticide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-cabbage lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Insects can build resistance if the same chemical is used repeatedly, or sudden rain might have washed the spray off the leaves before the insects could consume it.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ aye amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall but yield almost no peppers under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ shi nɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni baajɛ mli aba yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to produce flowers and fruit. When trapped in shade, the plant wastes all its energy stretching tall to search for light instead of making peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni etaoɔ la moŋ fe ni eeefee chili.

english: Why are my tomato roots turning soft and black when I water them twice every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ shii enyɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Overwatering drowns plant roots by filling up all air spaces in the soil. Without air, roots rot and fungi multiply, so soil should remain moist but never waterlogged.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii baafa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ shi esaaa akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants dropping off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant undergoes sudden heat stress, dry spells, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips that feed on delicate flower buds.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa, be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutua amɛ.

english: Why did my cassava plants choke out the groundnuts I planted between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miifo ŋmeii ni midu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava grows taller and faster, spreading broad leaves that block sunlight and deep roots that steal soil nutrients from smaller crops like groundnuts if they are planted too close together.
ga: Cassava baakwɛ̃ ni ebaafee oya. Amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa, kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli, kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect their underground tubers. Once the rains return, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism tomato plants use to reduce the surface area exposed to intense heat, which slows down water loss. If the plant recovers in the evening, it is simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Leaf curling ji hebuu gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba ŋwɛi he ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the surrounding soil and helps your maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Pale yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged from heavy rain, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ naatsii

english: How can I tell if my maize is being destroyed by Fall Armyworm caterpillars?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle mi-abele lɛ he?

english: Check the central leaves (the whorl) of the maize plant. If you see ragged holes, ragged leaf edges, and yellowish-brown powdery waste that looks like wet sawdust, Fall Armyworm caterpillars are feeding inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai (rings) lɛ mli. Kɛji ona buji ni etse, ŋmeii ni etse, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye nii yɛ mli.

english: Why do my sweet pepper fruits get dark, sunken spots on the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii ni ebote shishi dani amɛshwereɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad, leafy shade that protects cocoa seedlings from sunburn and retains soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa baa lɛ mli hulutsoo, ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and thicker in my field than my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so their seeds germinate faster and their roots spread deeper than domesticated crops to snatch water and sunlight first.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe shia tsei koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand downward smoothly. If the soil is hard, compact, or full of stones, the developing tuber struggles to push through and becomes stunted or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli ejɔ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy wind or rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that hold heavy fruit bunches. If underground pests like nematodes or weevils damage those roots, the plant loses its grip in soggy soil and topples over easily.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni haa aduawai akui ni tsii feɔ ekome. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo ŋmeii fite nakai shishifãi lɛ, Tsei hu nyɛŋ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the young leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can drink, causing them to burn, turn brown, and curl up.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Koni atsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshãa. Tsɔɔmɔ brown ni okɛ curl
