english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without turning into fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress and dry air. When daytime temperatures get too high, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can fertilize the plant, so the tree drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ jɛɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli baa lɛ mli titri. Beni hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani enyɛɔ ekɛ tso lɛ woɔ fɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip, it is a clear sign that the soil is low on nitrogen food. The maize plant takes nitrogen away from its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmãa kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and rolling upwards like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from the underside of young leaves. As the damaged leaf grows, it twists and curls upwards into a cup shape.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛji baai ni efite lɛ dara Ebaatsɔ ehe ni ebaatsɔ kɔɔpoo su mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood clay or low-lying soil, water fills up all the air spaces, suffocating the tubers and causing rot-causing fungi in the ground to destroy them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ nu. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer right against the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the stem or main root burns the plant tissues and draws water out of the root, which can stunt or kill the crop. Fertilizer should always be buried in a ring a short distance away.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ fioo ko mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I see holes and dark, sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibi lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar crawls inside the growing funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the soft hidden leaves and leaving behind its droppings, which look like wet sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni eshiɔ eshishifãi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut roots have tiny round balls attached to them when I pull them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔɔlu bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ekã shi beni migbala lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Those tiny balls are called root nodules, and they are very good for your soil. Friendly bacteria live inside them, taking nitrogen gas from the air and trapping it in the roots to feed your groundnut crop and fertilize the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ bɔɔlu bibii nɛɛ akɛ shishifãi. ni ehi waa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Naanyobɔɔ helai hiɔ amɛmli. Amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmei tsei lɛ niyenii ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a strong wind blows, even when the trunk is thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa yɛ etso lɛ ni etse lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread out near the top of the soil rather than growing deep down. When heavy bunches form at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for strong winds to pull the shallow roots out of wet earth.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaada kɛya shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu ko ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start growing green sprouts inside the barn before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato kpamɔ lɛ je shishi ekwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Yams naturally go to sleep after harvest, but as warm and humid air increases, the tuber senses that rain is coming. It uses its stored food and water inside the skin to push out new green sprouts so it can grow again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes yaa wɔɔhe beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Yitso lɛ baale akɛ nugbɔ miiba. Ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni ato yɛ ehewolo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ koni enyɛ eda ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat, which causes them to dry out and die. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them acts like a canopy, providing the cool shade and soil moisture needed for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ gbiɔ ni egboɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ kɛ sũ mli nu ni he hia kɛha kookoo bibii wala.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little food it has to the newest leaves at the top, causing the older leaves at the bottom to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point my cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani obaatsɔɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny plant buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems have to bend around to grow toward the light, which wastes energy and leads to very low root yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni eda kɛya la lɛ he. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa shi waa baa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain plant, they compete with the main tree for water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning away extra suckers leaves just one or two shoots, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to produce big plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ. Nɛkɛ tso lɛ niji nɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi koni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear land and cut sticks to stake up my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafolɔ tsei aniji koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to create food for the underground tubers. Raising the vines on tall wooden stakes spreads out the leaves to catch sunlight and keeps them off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia kane tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ baagbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã koni hulu lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat or water stress stops the flower from pollinating correctly, so the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my maize help my soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally adds free nutrients to the soil that the neighboring maize crops can feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko fataa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and turn small?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or from viruses spread by these insects. Spraying organic controls like neem leaf oil can help kill these pests and protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ neem baa fɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu shweremɔ hee he.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow better when there is standing water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa folo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water stops weeds from growing because most weed seeds cannot germinate underwater. Rice plants are unique because their roots can breathe in waterlogged conditions, allowing them to grow without competing with weeds for soil nutrients.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ haaa jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ ejaakɛ jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nu shishi. Omɔ tsei yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ jwɛi akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is burning my farm land after clearing bad for my crops in the long run?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni mishãa yɛ be mli ni mijie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ náa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, burning clears the farm quickly but destroys essential organic matter and friendly soil organisms that feed your crops. Leaving the cleared weeds to decompose on the surface naturally adds rich food back into the soil and keeps it moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa baajie ŋmɔ ko oya shi ebaafite nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ naanyo ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the crop even produces ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and healthy. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaves and improves crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the plant to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo plantain ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant maize on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally back into the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by excessive heat. Protecting young plants and using natural sprays like neem extract can reduce insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ he kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do helpful insects like bees die when I spray chemical pest medicine on my flowering crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie mitsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays kill beneficial insects along with harmful pests. Bees visit flowers to help them turn into fruits, so it is best to spray early in the morning or late evening when bees are not actively visiting flowers.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara. Wuobii saraa fɔfɔi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii eyasaraaa fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the tree lacks water, if pests like mirids damage the blossoms, or if there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli, kɛji kooloi tamɔ pollen fite fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my mango tree when it is already big and growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ mango niji komɛi amli be mli ni amɛdara momo ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Trimming overcrowded branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the inner parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and encourages the tree to grow bigger, sweeter fruits instead of just dense leaves.
ga: Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ. Yɛ baai ni mli edɔ kɛkɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my papaya fruits start rotting on the tree before they even turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya yibii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ po lɛ?

english: This pre-harvest rot is usually caused by fungal diseases that spread fast in warm, humid air. Harvesting papayas as soon as the first yellow strip appears prevents the fungus from destroying the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni baa dani akpaa nii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akpa papaya lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ je kpo lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekafite aduawai lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains planted alongside them to block the intense heat, the leaves burn and dry out because the plant loses water faster than its roots can absorb it.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee Baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to the newer top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings facing the right direction in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the cassava stem where leaves used to grow. These buds should always point upwards toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for roots and shoots to sprout, delaying growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or a lack of pollination. When temperatures are too high or water is scarce, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the maize plants growing nearby, improving soil health without extra artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmei tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground, giving the leaves full sunlight exposure and protecting the crop from fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛaawo he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Why should I cut down some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many shoots (suckers) growing from one plantain stem compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant produces larger bunches.
ga: Tso kome mli tsei babaoo (tsoji) kwɛ̃ɔ koni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from growing well even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for fertilizers, water, and space. Even with enough rain, crops will starve and remain small because fast-growing weeds absorb most of the nutrients in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ he ko, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ lolo ni amɛji bibii lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ji mɛi ni shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun even after I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in the hot afternoon sun is a defense mechanism tomato plants use to protect themselves. By rolling up their leaves, they reduce the leaf area exposed to the hot sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ amɛhe he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my harvest yields drop if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, and pests or diseases that target that specific crop build up in the soil, leading to poorer harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni kooloi loo helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do some crops like maize take exactly three months to harvest while crops like cassava take up to a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa, heɔ nyɔji etɛ dani akpaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmei heɔ afi kome?

english: Different crops have different growth cycles. Fast-growing crops like maize mature quickly because they focus their energy on producing seeds above ground, whereas root crops like cassava need a longer time to store starch in their roots underground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkɛ starch toɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop yields drop if I plant immediately after clearing the bush without giving the land proper preparation time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu beni mijie jwɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni mihaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni sa ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Proper land preparation clears competing weeds and loosens the soil so roots can breathe and absorb nutrients easily. Planting without giving time to prepare the field leaves crop roots struggling against weeds for nutrients and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ kɛyaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ ni be bɛ ni akɛsaa he lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: If I spend my money buying fertilizer for my farm, how exactly does it make my crops produce more yield?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ shika lɛ he ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like targeted food for soil that has lost its richness over time. It gives crops essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, which plants use to grow stronger leaves, build deeper roots, and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai ni mli wa Efee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ yibii wuji baa

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the field, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai nibii lɛ ahe lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily get scorched under full direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the cocoa with shade and moisture during its first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight over the same soil water and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with lower overall yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and drop their flowers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants face intense heat and limited water, they drop their flowers and curl their leaves to reduce water loss and save energy just to stay alive until water becomes available again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ kpe lɛ, Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ kɛyashi nu baaba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmeii ni ato lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around crops with dry leaves acts as a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly under the sun, and suppresses weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu la shishi. ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do improved seeds from the agricultural extension office produce better harvests than seeds I save from last season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ Agricultural Extension Office lɛ wo yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified improved seeds are specifically bred in laboratories to resist local diseases, withstand dry periods, and yield uniformly, whereas saved seeds lose these strong traits over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ laboratorii amli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ yibii ni yaa nɔ daa baa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow lots of tall green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants grow excess leaves at the expense of flowering. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to switch energy from growing leaves to producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná baai babaoo ni ebaaha ewo fɔfɔi. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni ekɛtsake hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛbaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major plant food in the soil. Heavy rains can wash this food away, or the soil might be tired, so adding compost or fertilizer gives the plant the nutrient it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo niyenii nɛɛ kɛya. Aloo ekolɛ sũ lɛ etɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and die if I do not plant plantains or shade trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu dumɔwui loo mihaaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains around them creates living umbrellas that shade the young cocoa from hot sunlight and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the soil when the rains are too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the plant for too long, the roots drown from a lack of air, allowing rot diseases in the soil to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ he. tso lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ekɛ hela ni fiteɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. When the plant feels conditions are bad, it sheds its flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eshihilɛ lɛ ehiii Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks instead of letting them lie on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot soil where they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf diseases caused by damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni etsiɔ baai ahe helai ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: What happens if I put my maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ wo bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that take natural plant food from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop dies, that stored food remains in the soil to help feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by very tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaf and sucking its juices. This damages the leaf tissue, causing it to distort and curl as it tries to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa efoɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda lɛ.

english: The main plantain stem needs massive amounts of water and nutrients to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit. If you leave too many small suckers attached, they steal that food away, leading to small and light bunches.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ biɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo koni ewo yibii wuji ni tsii. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛbaaju nakai niyenii lɛ kɛya. Efeɔ kui bibii ni waaa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rain shower of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of dry earth, and a long hot dry spell may follow it. Seeds need steady, continuous moisture to grow roots; if the soil dries out completely after sprouting, the tender young seedlings will die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ni hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni mli edɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa koni shishifãi lɛ ada. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ shweremɔ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagboi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a protective umbrella, providing shade and keeping the soil cool while the trees mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, overly damp, and shady conditions. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, hei ni edɔ tsɔ, kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin, but produce very small corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa bibii waa ni akɛhaa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the maize plants have to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows them to grow strong roots and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmei agbo.

english: Does it matter which way I push a cassava stem cutting into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashɛre ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems have small raised buds that must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the plant to waste energy trying to sprout correctly, leading to delayed growth and weaker yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Dalɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my farm producing less food every year even though I plant the same crop each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli niyenii faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ?

english: Growing the exact same crop in the same soil year after year drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating your main crop with legumes like beans or cowpeas helps restore vital nutrients naturally back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so it works best?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil right after a light rain or early in the morning. Covering it lightly with soil stops heavy rains from washing it away before the roots can drink it in.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. loo leebi maŋkpa Light mulching Enɛ baaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho dani shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the center funnel of young maize. Checking your farm early and applying recommended controls into the plant's center destroys them before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ nibii ni yɔɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baafite nakai ŋmɔji lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds when my crop seedlings are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the sunlight, fertilizer, and water intended for your seedlings. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the food they need to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni ebaaju hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu oya kɛha odumɔwui lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in hot weather is a plant's natural way of saving water and protecting itself from intense heat. As long as the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baatse kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛkɛ.

english: How can I stop insects from eating and ruining my harvested maize while it is stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛfite be mli ni eyɔɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grains. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is completely hard before storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates pests and prevents mold from destroying your crop.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when there has been no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl up, the plant is trying to protect itself from losing water. Rolling the leaves reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant hold onto moisture until it gets water.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enine shɛɔ nu nɔ.

english: Which vegetables can I grow during the dry season that will still give a good harvest and sell fast at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai abaanyɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni woɔ yibii kpakpai lolo ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, hot peppers, and okra do very well in the dry season if given a little water. They fetch high prices at the market because fewer farmers are able to harvest crops during dry periods.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, chili, kɛ okra tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu fioo. Amɛheɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jara nɔ ejaakɛ okwaafoi fioo ko pɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How do improved seed varieties from agricultural officers help my farm when the rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni atsake kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specifically bred to mature faster or withstand dry spells, allowing the crop to produce good yields even with low or irregular rainfall.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya loo koni amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo loo enɛɔ daa po.

english: Why should I plant drought-resistant rice varieties instead of traditional rice in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa najiaŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-resistant rice varieties need much less water to mature and can survive sudden dry spells, helping you get a reliable harvest even when rainfall is low or comes late.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ biɔ nu fioo ko pɛ dani ekwɛ̃, ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni baa trukaa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ hekɛnɔfɔɔ kpaa nii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ nɛ fioo loo ebaa sɛɛ po.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or a lack of consistent water. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants from excessive heat keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody instead of soft when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tamɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become tough and woody if left in the ground too long past their maturity date or if the plant suffers through severe dry spells followed by sudden heavy rain.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaafee tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni amɛho amɛhe. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early yellowing of yam leaves usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients or the plant is suffering from root damage caused by dry soil or pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miifite tso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants in the early morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots take up water before the day gets hot. It also gives wet leaves time to dry in the sun, which stops fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni shishifãi lɛ aná nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ hu be ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or soybeans make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo soybeans ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and soybeans have roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer, feeding the maize you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ soybeans yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy tops. Planting them deep enough and mounding soil around the base gives them a stronger grip in wet soil so wind cannot push them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Tsei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa kɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatsɔ mli

english: How do I choose crops that will be easy to sell in my market after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ jarayeli mli?

english: Crops like maize, cassava, and fresh vegetables always have constant daily demand in local markets. Choosing fast-moving food crops or standard cash crops ensures you will not struggle to find buyers when it is time to harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai heei ji nɔ ni ataoɔ daa gbi yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya loo shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ ni ooohala lɛ haa onaaa nɔmimaa akɛ onaaa mɛi ni baahe nii kɛji kpamɔ be lɛ bashɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and grow weak even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants turn yellow when the soil lacks essential plant food, especially nitrogen. Applying the correct fertilizer gives the soil the missing nutrients so the crop can produce deep green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akafee nɔ ko. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo baai eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so my crops can use it properly?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing. If you apply it when the ground is too dry, it can burn the plant roots, and if you apply it during heavy rains, the water will wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi ashã. ni kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Nu lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick with a disease or just suffering from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo hulu lɛ eshɛ amɛhe kɛkɛ?

english: Heat causes leaves to wilt in the hot afternoon and recover at night. Crop diseases show spots, white powder, rotting, or yellow patterns on the leaves that remain even when the weather cools down.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ. Tso hela jieɔ ŋmeii, powda yɛŋ, fitemɔ kpo. Aloo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni eshwɛ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ moŋ.

english: Why does a disease spread so fast from one crop to the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Crop sickness can travel through wind, rain drops, insects, or even on your farm boots and cutlasses. If sick plants are not removed early, the sickness easily moves to healthy plants next to them.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔshiimɔi, kooloi bibii, kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔɔtui kɛ dadei po amli. Kɛji ajieee tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, Hela lɛ yaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ. mlɛo

english: Why do government certified seeds yield better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to grow strong, resist common field diseases, and produce high yields. Seeds saved from past harvests often get weaker over time and can carry diseases from the old farm.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛdara waa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ fɔɔ gbɔjɔmɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba kɛjɛ ŋmɔji momo amli

english: Why is it necessary to clear all weeds before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani wɔdu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your young crops. Clearing the land completely before planting gives your new seeds space and food to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui heei náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How does joining a local farmer group help me keep my crops healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Working in a farmer group makes it easier to get advice from extension officers, buy genuine seeds and fertilizers in bulk, and learn from neighboring farmers how to spot crop diseases early.
ga: Okwaafoi akuu mli nitsumɔ haa onine shɛɔ ŋaawoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ okwaafoi agbɛfaŋ lɛ adɛŋ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooohe dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni okase bɔ ni ooofee ona ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra kɛjɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops need shade trees while others need direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ahe hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Some crops have delicate leaves that burn under hot direct sun and need shade trees to stay cool and retain soil moisture. Other crops need full sunlight all day to make food and produce healthy yields.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei krokomɛi hu he miihia hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛhoo nii ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster in the major rainy season than in the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops depend on consistent rainfall and ground moisture to feed. The major rainy season provides steady water for heavy-feeding crops, while the minor season has less water, which is better suited for fast-growing crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛha niyenii. Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ haa nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa kooloi niyenii ni tsii. Yɛ be mli ni yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nu baafee fioo. ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni daa oya lɛ

english: Why are my young crop seedlings wilting and dying when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are delicate like human babies and dry out quickly under direct, intense sunlight. Creating shade or planting them under larger nurse plants protects them from heat stress and keeps the surrounding soil moist enough for them to survive.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo mli loo okɛ amɛ wo nurse tsei wuji ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: What can I put around the stems of my plants to stop the soil from drying out so fast in the heat?
ga: Mɛni mikɛwoɔ he? Tsei ahe tsei koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a protective shield. It blocks direct sunlight from heating the soil, helping it retain moisture much longer.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ akpã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa sũ lɛ mli adɔ. No hewɔ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes when there is no rain and the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism against extreme heat. By curling up, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss and helps the plant survive dry periods.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: How can I tell if the fertilizer or seeds I am buying at the local market are genuine and good quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ji anɔkwale ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Genuine seeds come in sealed, certified bags with official tags from government agricultural boards or reputable suppliers. You can test seed quality before planting by placing a small sample in a damp cloth to see if most of them sprout within a few days.
ga: Dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa ni awo he odaseyeli ni nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli ajinafoi akuu loo mɛi ni kɛ nibii nɛɛ haa lɛ ni yɔɔ gbɛi kpakpa lɛ aŋmala nɔ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ ahe okwɛ dani odu kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. yɛ mama ni mli efɔ mli Koni ana kɛji dumɔwui babaoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to sort through my saved crop seeds before I plant them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala dumɔwui ni ato lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sorting your seeds helps you throw away cracked, insect-damaged, or small, weak seeds. Planting only the strongest, whole seeds ensures uniform growth and gives you a much better harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ooohala lɛ baaye abua bo ni ojie dumɔwui ni ekumɔ lɛ. Kplukai loo dumɔwui bibii efite Abaanyɛ ajie nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa amɛdaraa po ni ehaa onáa ŋmaa kpakpa kwraa.

english: How does continually adding animal manure or compost to my farm help my crops over time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ maya nɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Adding compost or animal manure gradually builds up organic matter and nutrients in the soil season after season. As the soil structure improves, it holds more water and feeds your crops continuously for higher future yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli fiofio. Tsɔɔmɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ naa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ hi lɛ Ebaahiɛ nu babaoo ni ebaaya nɔ eha onibii lɛ niyenii koni amɛná yibii babaoo wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables shed their flowers and drop leaves when the weather stays hot for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops experience severe heat stress, they drop flowers and lower leaves to save energy and water just to stay alive. Feeding the soil well and providing adequate water helps the plant withstand these hot spells without losing its yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe lɛ Fɔfɔi kɛ baai baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔ nɛkɛ hulutsoo bei nɛɛ anaa ni amɛyibii lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do crops grow much better in soil that was left to rest for a year compared to land farmed every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ashi lɛ pɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto okwaayeli shikpɔŋ he daa afi?

english: Leaving land to rest (fallowing) allows wild plants to decay and naturally refill the soil with nutrients. It restores the soil's strength and water-holding capacity, making it far more productive when you return to plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ koni ekɛ ehe ajɔɔ ehe (tillage) lɛ haa koo mli tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ oku osɛɛ oyadu.

english: Is it helpful to plant bigger, fast-growing crops like cassava or plantain next to my delicate young crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsei wuji ni daa oya, tamɔ yucca loo plantains yɛ mitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, larger companion crops act as living umbrellas that block harsh sunlight and strong winds. They create a cooler, protected environment underneath that allows tender young crops to establish themselves safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, nanemɛi tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ susuma ni hiɛ ka ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa. Amɛfeɔ shihilɛ ko ni mli ejɔ ni abuɔ he yɛ shishigbɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that insects like weevils do not destroy it while it sits in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Koni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii akafite lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ.

english: Make sure your maize is completely dried in the sun until the grains are hard before storing. Keeping the dried grain in clean, airtight bags or sealed containers stops insects from entering and prevents moisture from ruining your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ o-abele lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛto. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ awo kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nibii krokomɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli amli. Enɛ baaha kooloi akabote mli, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to make food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso titri ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer right before a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the topsoil or washes it too deep into the ground before the crop roots can absorb it, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo efoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa oshika kɛ onitsumɔ fiteɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing tip of young maize plants to feed on the tender leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays too wet for too long or gets infected by fungal water-molds, which cut off air from the roots and cause them to decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ mɔ amɛ. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too close, plantains fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for each plant to form a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ Amɛfeɔ ekãa ni amɛkɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛfeɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when I leave weeds growing right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi lɛ yɛ afã lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive thieves—their roots spread quickly to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, stunting their growth.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni he wa waa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. ni ha amɛdalɛ ba shi lɛ

english: Why should I keep some tall trees on my land when planting new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsei kakadaji ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu kookoo tsei heei?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Tall trees act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my garden crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts as a blanket that stops heat from evaporating moisture out of the soil, keeping the root area cool and wet.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines off the hot ground allows the leaves to spread out into maximum sunlight to make energy, which directly feeds and enlarges the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aye nii tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients, saving their energy for survival instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa trukaa lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛhiɔ shi lɛ baa shi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my maize leaves and small worms eating the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Yeli yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Those holes and worms are caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the central funnel of the maize plant where new leaves grow. Catching them early and applying appropriate control methods protects your crop before the pests destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni baa heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni gbɛi ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okwɛ amɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni obu onibii ahe dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during severe dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from burning. Planting shade trees like Gliricidia or intercropping with plantains keeps the microclimate cool and helps soil hold moisture during the dry months.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ gliricidia loo akɛ plantains adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks nutrients without sending it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa ni mikɛmajeee laboratori?

english: You can observe your crops' behavior: if the lower leaves turn yellow while the rest of the plant remains pale green, the soil is low in nitrogen. Stunted growth or purple leaf edges often mean a lack of phosphorus.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa: kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni eshwɛ lɛ Tso lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lolo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni baa shi loo baai ni yɔɔ purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds or ridges before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mawo gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil to expand into large tubers. Planting on ridges or mounds prevents water from pooling around the roots, which stops tuber rot and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei wuji. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ, no haaa nu abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why is it important to use wooden stakes to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii kɛfi mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that relies on leaves exposed to full sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from damp soil, increasing sunlight exposure and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe aaajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in small fruit bunches. Leaving only one active sucker alongside the main stem ensures all energy goes into producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. Kɛ́ ashi sucker kome ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Mulching the base of the plant to keep soil moisture steady and ensuring balanced watering prevents flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ ashishi ni akɛhaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Weeds act as silent competitors that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's growth cycle ensures your planted crop gets all the resources needed to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni efee dioo, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ haa otso lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ agbo.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested maize crop to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains harvested from high-yield hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, resulting in uneven plant growth and lower yields. Buying fresh, certified seeds every season guarantees strong plants and maximum yield.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Can crops get sick like people do, and what causes it?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná hela tamɔ gbɔmɛi? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: Yes, crops get sick just like humans. Plant diseases are usually caused by microscopic organisms like fungi, bacteria, or viruses that enter the plant through rain, wind, insects, or infected soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hela tamɔ adesai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nibii bibii ni anaaa tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, loo muawai ni boteɔ tsei amli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, koolooi, loo sũ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsei helai baa.

english: Do plants breathe like humans, and can a sickness affect their breathing?
ga: Tsei baanyɛ amu tamɔ adesai. Ni ani hela baanyɛ aná mumɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Plants breathe through tiny, invisible pores on their leaves called stomata. Certain leaf diseases can block or damage these pores, making it hard for the plant to take in air and create energy to grow.
ga: Tsei muɔ kɛtsɔɔ bu bibii amli. Atsɛɔ nibii ni anaaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ akɛ stomata. Foli helai komɛi baanyɛ atsĩ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa loo amɛfite. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaana kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do new types of crop sicknesses keep appearing on farms that our elders never talked about?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai heei No hewɔ lɛ ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni wɔ onukpai lɛ ewieee he kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Changing weather patterns, higher temperatures, and moving seeds or soil between different regions can introduce new plant diseases or cause existing ones to behave differently.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ kɛ dumɔwui loo shikpɔŋ ni nyiɛɔ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai heei aba loo eha tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ.

english: Why are dark or black spots suddenly appearing on my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ miije kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Dark or black spots are early warning signs of a fungal or bacterial infection. The spots form where the disease is destroying the plant tissues and feeding on its nutrients.
ga: He ni edɔ loo he ni edɔ ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli loo bacteria mli lɛ eba. He ni hela fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni eyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I explain a plant disease to an extension officer if I do not know the English or official name for it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ tso hela ko mli matsɔɔ extension nitsulɔ ko? Ni kɛji akɛ mileee Blɔfo gbɛi loo maŋ gbɛi lɛ hu?

english: You do not need to know official names. Simply describe the visible signs—like black spots, rotting stems, or wilting—or bring a freshly infected leaf or fruit sample wrapped in paper to show the officer.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ole gbɛi ni akɛtsɛɔ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ hei diji, tso lɛ shishi egbo, loo egbo. Aloo okɛ baai loo aduawai heei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛwo wolo mli lɛ eko aba ni okɛtsɔɔ nitsulɔi lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if a black spot on the fruit keeps growing?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ tee nɔ eda?

english: If left untreated, the spot will expand until the entire fruit turns black, rots, and dies, completely destroying the harvestable produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsaaa he lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ aduawai lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, egboɔ, ni egboɔ, ni efiteɔ ŋmaa lɛ kwraa.

english: If one plant gets black spots, will it spread to the other healthy crops near it?
ga: Kɛji tso kome yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji Ani ebaagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, many plant diseases spread quickly to nearby crops through rain droplets splashing off infected leaves, strong winds, or contaminated hands and farm tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni tswaa baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo niji kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does crop sickness seem to get worse during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai tamɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria thrive in wet, damp environments. High humidity and splashing rain help disease spores multiply rapidly and travel easily from leaf to leaf.
ga: Mold kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ babaoo oya ni amɛyaa kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ mlɛo.

english: This is commonly caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that attacks the pod surface in cool, wet conditions, turning the outside dark and ruining the beans inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ feɔ duŋ ni efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Should I pick off leaves or fruits that turn black and dry up, or should I leave them on the plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maŋɔ baai loo aduawai ni etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi loo esa akɛ mashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You should carefully remove and destroy infected plant parts immediately. Leaving diseased leaves or fruits on the crop allows the sickness to spread to remaining healthy parts.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ ashi baai loo aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã hei ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can scorch or dry out easily. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide broad leafy shade, keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa trees while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa shade kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ.
