english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni mli wa lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central funnel of my maize plants and chew holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves and growing tips. Detecting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnels can control them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni daraa lɛ ahe ŋmeii. Ni aaana amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting in the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in flat, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Okɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ awo tsei lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards and the plants remaining small without fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni tso lɛ kã he eji bibioo ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with insecticidal soap sprays and removing severely infected plants stops the virus from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kudɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do I get a smaller maize harvest if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaaa ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is completely dry or right after a rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, usually right after a rain. Applying it to bone-dry soil can burn plant roots, while applying it during heavy downpours can cause the fertilizer to wash away before plants can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, awoɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the seed store produce bigger yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ dumɔwui ashwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought commercial seeds are often specialized hybrids bred for high yields, disease resistance, and vigor. Seeds saved from hybrid plants lose these special traits in the next generation, producing smaller and less uniform crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, kɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ baa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my vegetable crops help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It blocks the sun from evaporating water from the dirt, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my coconut trees need full sunlight to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo he hiaa mi ŋmei tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees are tropical plants that need direct sunlight to make their food efficiently. Sunlight gives them the energy required to grow strong trunks, stay healthy, and produce big, sweet coconuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei ji tsei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Hulu la haa amɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni wa. Ha ohe ajɔ bo ni ofee ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ

english: What happens to my coconut seedlings if they get sunlight but not enough water?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ shi enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Sunlight helps the seedling make food, but without water, the leaves will dry up and turn yellow. Water is essential to carry nutrients from the soil up into the leaves and keep the plant hydrated.
ga: Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Shi kɛji nu bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nu he hia koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya baa lɛ nɔ ni eha tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted coconut tree to start producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: It depends on the type you plant; dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 8 years.
ga: Edamɔ tso henɔ ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8.

english: How can I protect my crops during the dry season around January?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni miihe ashɛ January mli lɛ he?

english: During dry periods like January, cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to retain moisture, and water them regularly in the early morning or evening to reduce evaporation.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ January mli lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha onibii ahe koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Ni okɛ nu awo mli daa leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: When is the best time of the year to start planting new crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ maje ŋmɔshi nibii heei ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is usually at the start of the major rainy season (around April or May) so your young plants get continuous natural rain to establish deep roots before any dry weather sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Abaadu tso lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli (aaafee April loo May) no hewɔ lɛ odumɔwui lɛ baaná adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why is it important to leave enough space between my coconut trees when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni kã ŋmei tsei ateŋ lɛ he hiaa beni aduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Spacing gives each tree its own room to spread its leaves and roots. If they are planted too close together, they will fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsu ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ baagbɛ eshwa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Can I grow other small crops underneath my mature coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, you can grow shade-tolerant or short crops like ginger, pineapple, or cassava under mature coconuts as long as enough sunlight filters through the coconut branches and the soil has enough water for both.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo loo tsei kukuji tamɔ aŋmei, anana loo sino. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei ni eda atsu nii. Shii abɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baakpɛ yɛ ŋmei niji lɛ amli, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds around my young crop plants slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, soil nutrients, and sunlight that your young crops need to grow, effectively starving your plants if left unchecked.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut palm turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is short on soil nutrients (like nitrogen or potassium) or is lacking enough water during hot and dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli (tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium) loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are my young coconut fruits falling off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Coconut palms often drop young fruits due to extreme dry weather, uneven watering, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil during the fruiting stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛyibii bibii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plant turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to keep leaves green and help the crop grow strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná baa ni mli wa.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on my land after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing your land for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I remove all the tall shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Mashi miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade trees to act as living shields that protect their tender leaves from scorching and help keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni hiɛ kã ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my oil palm trees stop producing big fruit bunches when I cut off too many green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii wuji kɛji mifo baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ?

english: Green leaves act as energy factories for the tree using sunlight to make food. When you trim off too many healthy leaves, the oil palm starves and cannot produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ nitsumɔhe kɛha tso lɛ, kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ Oil palms lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the ground, standing water pushes all the air out of the soil, suffocating the tubers and causing fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does my swamp rice grow well in flooded fields while my maize rots in the same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli shi mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that carry air from the leaves down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots drown because they cannot transport air underground.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ amɛbai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aya shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is scarce, because the heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to discard flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign of tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves or spreading a virus that stunts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi, loo hela ko ni miitsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ miigbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch starts getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and weak stems filled with water rather than hard wood, so they struggle to support the heavy weight of growing fruits without wooden prop supports.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ tsei ni wa najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛye amɛbua tso yibii ni miida lɛ ni tsii lɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni akpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months of dry storage, using their internal moisture and nutrients to push out new growth for the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto he ko ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha dalɛ hee aba yɛ dalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the crop lacks nitrogen, a key plant nutrient, or when heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the root area.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ wala beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching cassava roots, causing them to suffocate and allowing soil fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, when tiny insects damage the blossoms, or when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients to support pod development.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Beni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plants from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or whiteflies that transmit viruses and steal nutrients from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. ni tsɔɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can make energy, which travels down to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli koni ebaai lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyatao niyenii ni egbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Removing extra suckers stops them from competing with the main plantain stem for water and fertilizer, resulting in larger and heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ plantain tso titri lɛ akatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: In intense afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can pull from the ground, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry organic matter keeps the ground cool, preserves soil moisture so you water less, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akafɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for roots to drink it; applying dry fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efite shika.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions, so their seeds wake up instantly and consume nutrients faster than domesticated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shia mli lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting my maize instead of planting right after the first rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu ŋmãa? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: Planting after just one shower is risky because the deeper soil is still dry. If dry weather returns for a few days, the newly sprouted seeds will dry up and die. Waiting for regular rains ensures the soil holds enough moisture deep down for roots to grow strong.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ku osɛɛ oya gbii fioo krokomɛi. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hia ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is essential food for leaf growth. This happens when the soil is poor, washed out by heavy water, or when manure or fertilizer hasn't been added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii. ni nu lɛ hoɔ loo beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ

english: Why is it bad if I put three or four maize seeds together in the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ to ŋmãa ŋmãa bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli waa. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food. To save energy and survive, the plant drops its flowers instead of feeding young fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi shi Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii bibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land where I grew tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the soil. Changing to a different crop, like beans or maize, starves those soil pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ abɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ni oootsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (called mulching) shields the ground from the hot sun, keeps the soil moist for longer so you irrigate less, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and feeling dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies carrying a virus to the plant, or by extreme heat stress where the plant curls its leaves to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ hela lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu akafite lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and brown if I leave them in the ground too long after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots store high amounts of starch and water. When wet soil stays soaked for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing water rot and fungal diseases to breakdown the tubers inside the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ toɔ ŋmeii kɛ nu babaoo. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai akpata ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines. Staking lifts their leaves off the damp ground into sunlight, which helps the plant make food efficiently for bigger tubers while protecting the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I plant plantains first when starting a new farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that protect delicate young crops like cocoa from harsh sunlight, while also giving you food and income long before your main cash crop matures.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa bo dani oshika ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Will my plantains be ready to harvest before my main crop like cocoa starts bearing fruit?
ga: Ani mi-plantains lɛ baafee klalo akɛ akpa dani mi-ŋmɔshi nibii titri, ni ji kookoo lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Yes, plantains produce food within 12 to 15 months, giving you an early harvest while your main tree crops are still growing and maturing over several years.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli, ni ehaa okpaa nii mra yɛ be mli ni otsei titrii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ miida lolo ni amɛmiidara yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ.

english: What is the best way to move plantains from an old farm to start a brand new farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ momo mli koni akɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You dig up healthy suckers—the young shoots growing at the base of old plantain plants—and replant those shoots directly into prepared holes on your new farm land.
ga: Ofoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ—ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain momo lɛ shishi lɛ—ni okɛwoɔ bu ni asaa he yɛ he hee ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why am I getting very small cocoa harvest from my farm during the crop season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni minine shɛɔ kookoo fioo pɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Low yields usually happen when the farm lacks steady maintenance like regular weeding, pruning, and disease control, which cocoa trees need to produce healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ bɛ saamɔ daa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ kɛ helai ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa Ehe miihia ni cacao tso lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: How does keeping my farm clean and maintained help my cocoa trees yield more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Clearing weeds and brush stops unwanted plants from stealing water and nutrients from the soil, allowing your cocoa trees to get full nourishment to produce more pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tsei ni ataooo amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Does having large forest trees on my land guarantee that my crops will produce a large harvest?
ga: Ani koo mli tso agbo ko ni miyɔɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo?

english: No, non-cocoa trees help provide shade and protect the soil, but you still need active farm maintenance and care to get a good crop harvest.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Shi ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli he miihia bo lolo koni yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do farmers leave big forest trees inside a cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shiɔ koo mli tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafolɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Forest trees act as protective umbrellas that shade cocoa plants from excessive sun, help retain soil moisture, and create a good environment for long-term cocoa growth.
ga: Koo mli tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔnɔ, ni amɛbuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha kookoo shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Do non-cocoa trees on my farm need any management, or do I just leave them alone?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akwɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ? Aloo mashi kɛkɛ?

english: They need occasional maintenance like pruning heavy branches so they don't cast too much dark shade or break and damage your lower crops during high winds.
ga: Amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ yɛ bei komɛi amli, tamɔ tsei niji ni tsii ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Bɔni afee ni ekafee duŋ tsɔ. loo efite otsei lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How do I know when it is time to harvest my cocoa pods during the crop season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when they change color completely from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛtsake amɛhe kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Can I harvest plantain suckers from my old farm while still harvesting food from it?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa plantain tsei kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mikpaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo?

english: Yes, you can harvest ripe plantain fruits for food while carefully separating side suckers to plant in your new farm field.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa plantains ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛha niyenii. Agbɛnɛ hu, gbalamɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni okɛdu yɛ oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen or waterlogged by heavy rains. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves produce green food for strong plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha nu eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and balanced water helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nu ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on soil ridges instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil ridges keep the earth loose and raised, giving cassava roots space to expand into big tubers while preventing water from pooling around the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ehe nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why does my farmland soil get hard and dry like concrete after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure. Spreading animal manure or dry crop waste onto the field keeps the soil soft so water can soak in easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if my land is fertile enough to plant yams without using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu sweet potatoes ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Dark, crumbly soil that feels moist and smells fresh like forest soil is full of natural plant nutrients, making it ideal for raising large yam mounds naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni su diŋɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ koo mli shikpɔŋ eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves scorch and dry up when I cut down all the nearby big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct hot sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides a cool umbrella that protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, dark conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight into the farm and removing rotten pods prevents the sickness from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli kɛbaa. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ajie tsei ni egboi lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly spread by tiny insects like whiteflies or caused by severe heat stress. Spraying plants with organic neem oil and keeping them watered helps protect them from insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo hulutsoo ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ gbɛɔ baa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ ni aha tso lɛ nɔ nu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni baafite lɛ ahe.

english: Why do tiny black bugs bore holes into my stored maize grain a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni ji diji lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, afo bu ko awo mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Those bugs are grain weevils that multiply in warm, damp maize. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are completely hard and storing them in airtight bags suffocates pests and protects your crop.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni fɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni edɔ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why is it useful for me to group and weigh my harvested crops before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mafee mikpamɔ lɛ kuu ni masusu he dani mikɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting and weighing your produce lets you know your exact harvest yield, allows you to separate high-grade crops for top prices, and protects you from buyers underpaying you on bulk estimation.
ga: Kɛ́ ohala onibii lɛ amli ni osusu he lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ ŋmaa pɔtɛɛ ni obaakpa. Ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ mli. Ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi ni woɔ bo nyɔmɔ fioo yɛ akɔntaabuui wuji amli lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in a smaller total harvest compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Does burning dry bushes on my land before planting help or hurt my soil?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni egbi ni mikɛshãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it burns away natural organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the ground, leaving the soil dry and less fertile for future crops.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hu, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed those nutrients away from the roots. Adding compost or fertilizer helps the plant turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nakai niyenii lɛ kɛjɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown next to them to act as natural umbrellas and protect them from sun scorch.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering stress the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the tender leaves inside my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called fall armyworms, target the fresh, growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and treating the plant prevents them from destroying the growing stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Akɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ ŋmãa tsei heei lɛ adalɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by crop diseases in the soil that attack the roots and block water from traveling up the stem, causing the plant to wither despite plenty of soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa nu hoɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei gboiɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough land for all of them to grow?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil that your main crop needs to grow strong, effectively starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. ni okɛ hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When water collects around cassava roots without draining, it suffocates the tubers and causes rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess rain to drain away safely.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ Cassava shishifãi ahe ni nu shwieee lɛ Enɛ baaha cassava shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I water them in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot, preventing the water from evaporating before the roots can use it.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: How do I know when my maize crop has reached full maturity and is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize shows it is fully mature when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and a tiny black spot forms at the base of each kernel where it joins the cob, showing that the plant has stopped sending food to the grain.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu shishi he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa niyenii ni ekɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up and turn brown on the stalk instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: As maize nears the end of its life cycle, it naturally transfers all its remaining water and stored energy into the kernels to harden them, causing the outer leaves and stalk to dry out naturally.
ga: Beni ŋmãa miihe ashɛ ewala be lɛ naagbee lɛ Ekɛ nu ni eshwɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ fɛɛ woɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli koni ekɛha dumɔwu lɛ mli awa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ tsei lɛ agbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants curl up into tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat as a natural defense to shield their surface from direct sunlight and reduce the amount of moisture evaporating from the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ ŋwɛi la he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, forcing them to stretch upwards for light instead of developing thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛmɔ la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize ears have missing kernels or empty spaces on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ bɛ ŋmãa loo he ko ni bɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Empty spots happen when pollination fails during the flowering stage, usually because dry winds or extreme heat prevented pollen from reaching every silk strand on the ear.
ga: Void spot baa kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haaa pollen lɛ ayashɛ siliki fɛɛ siliki ni yɔɔ toi lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever there is wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when brace roots are weak or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium, which are needed to build strong, solid stems that anchor the plant securely.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ potassium, ni he hiaa koni afee tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni fiɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Can I use any type of maize to make flour for bread and dough, or do different varieties behave differently?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa henɔ fɛɛ ŋmãa afee ashikishaŋ kɛfee blodo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Aloo gbɛ kroko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii?

english: Different varieties serve different uses; floury or dent maize has soft starch that grinds easily into fine flour for baking, while sweet corn contains high sugar and is meant for fresh eating rather than milling.
ga: Srɔtoi yɛ nibii srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Abɛi ni akɛ ashikiŋsha loo ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni etsɔ ashikishaŋ kpakpa ni akɛshãa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli ŋɔɔ lɛ mli sugar fa babaoo, ni afee koni aye lɛ ehee moŋ fe nɔ ni atsɔ mli.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize grains thoroughly before taking them to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛya ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Drying hardens the grain kernels so they break down evenly into powder without sticking, while also removing moisture that would cause mold and decay during processing and storage.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ehaa ŋmaa lɛ mli waa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fãa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛfeɔ powda ni amɛkpɛtɛɛɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba beni atsuɔ he nii kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some types of corn break down into fine powder easily when ground while others stay hard and coarse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ atsɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi anɔ lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efeɔ ŋmãa kpakpa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi wa ni amɛhe wa lolo lɛ?

english: Corn kernels contain different ratios of hard starch and soft floury starch; varieties rich in soft starch crush into smooth flour, whereas varieties with thick, glassy starch resist fine milling.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mlijaa srɔtoi yɛ. Akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse nɔ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni yɔɔ powda ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ glase lɛ teɔ shi woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small holes to appear in my harvested maize grains after storing them in bags?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ baagi mli lɛ mli

english: Small holes are caused by grain weevils, tiny insects that bore into dry kernels to eat the inner starch and lay eggs if the harvested crop is not treated or stored in airtight containers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa ji dumɔwui bibii, ni ji kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛye mligbɛ fã ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch lɛ ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ahe nii loo akɛtooo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is an important plant food. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster when I leave weeds growing in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and soil nutrients away from your crops. During dry periods, weeds drink up the underground moisture before your crop roots can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with low harvest when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward fighting for light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe, ni amɛwuɔ koni amɛná la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch sunlight better and stay away from dirt-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. ni ekɛ helai ni muji kɛbaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: Why are my growing cocoa pods turning black and drying up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal sickness that spreads rapidly in wet, humid, and heavily shaded farms. Trimming extra tree branches lets air and sunlight in to dry out the farm and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Tsoi krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekpaa ŋmeii.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and lacks air circulation. In waterlogged soil, the roots cannot breathe and become weak, allowing fungal decay to set in during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the inner leaves of my young corn plants full of small holes and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋwɛigbɛi ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center leaves. They hide deep in the plant whorl where soft young leaves grow, damaging the corn before it forms ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni baai bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Kpatamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ dani eda ni etsɔ toi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat or water stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does my field produce less corn if I plant maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and builds up corn-specific pests. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ebɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to produce high yields only in the first generation. Saving seeds from that harvest results in plants that grow unevenly and produce much smaller cobs in the next planting.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ahiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers plant seeds in sand or nursery beds first instead of planting them directly in the main farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋã loo ŋã nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Sand or nursery soil provides a soft, loose environment that allows delicate new root shoots to grow easily without fighting hard dirt, helping seeds sprout faster and stronger before being transplanted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ daa oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhe wa dani aduɔ amɛ.

english: Can I grow my crops directly in sandy soil, or do I need to mix it with something else?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ nɔ kroko afutu mli?

english: Pure sand holds very little water and food for plants. Mixing sand with compost or decomposed animal manure helps the soil hold moisture and provides essential nutrients for crop growth.
ga: Ŋã ni he tse lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ kɛhaa tsei. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã futu ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ baaha.

english: Why do extension officers recommend covering the soil around young plants with plastic sheets or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ plastic loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil traps moisture in the ground so it doesn't dry out quickly in the sun, prevents weeds from growing, and protects delicate roots from extreme heat.
ga: Mulching lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni hulu lɛ akagbi oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: How does covering my seedbed with plastic or palm leaves help my seeds sprout better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛ plastic loo ŋmei tsei aha dumɔwui ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Covers create a warm, moist climate while shielding fragile seeds from harsh sunlight, heavy rains that wash soil away, and hungry birds or insects.
ga: Veil lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ okpoi loo kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ

english: How do I know when my seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are usually ready for transplanting when they have grown 3 to 4 true leaves and developed a strong, sturdy stem that can withstand field conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ́ amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baanyɛ adamɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi anaa.

english: Will my crops produce any harvest while still in the nursery stage, or must I wait until after transplanting?
ga: Ani abaakpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi be mli ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ awo mli sɛɛ?

english: Nursery beds are only for young seedling development; crops need the extra space, sunlight, and root room of the main field to fully mature and produce a harvest.
ga: Afee ŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ pɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia he ko ni fata he, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmaa.

english: Is it possible for me to farm and harvest crops continuously all year round, even during dry months?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafee okwaayeli ni makpa ŋmɔshi nii be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ? Yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli po?

english: Yes, with a reliable water source or irrigation system, along with proper soil care, you can plant and harvest crops continuously from January through December.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ nu jɛɛhe loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. kɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa he Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii daa kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December.

english: What is the benefit of planting my crops in small batches every few weeks instead of planting my whole farm at once?
ga: Mi tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ kui bibii amli Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ otsii fioo fɛɛ otsii fioo mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Planting in batches spreads out your harvest dates, allowing you to sell fresh produce regularly throughout the year rather than having all your crops ready at one time.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ kui amli lɛ baaha okpamɔ gbii lɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii heei ni anáa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ afee klalo shikome lɛ

english: In the early weeks, crops spend most of their energy growing roots underground to anchor themselves and search for food; once roots are established, leaf and stem growth speeds up rapidly.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi koni amɛkɛma amɛhe shi ni amɛtao niyenii. Beni abɔ shishifãi lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ oya.

english: What daily or weekly work do I need to do to make sure my crops give a good yield?
ga: Mɛɛ daa gbi loo otsi nitsumɔi esa akɛ mafee koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Regular care involves watering during dry spells, clearing weeds so they do not steal food from crops, checking for harmful pests, and applying fertilizer at the right stage of plant growth.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ he ji nu ni awoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ koni akaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Kwɛmɔ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli

english: How does nearby galamsey or illegal mining water affect the health of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te Galamsey ni bɛŋkɛ loo nu ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Galamsey introduces toxic chemicals like mercury and heavy metals into the soil and water sources. These pollutants damage the tree's root system, stopping it from taking in clean water and nutrients, which eventually stunts growth or kills the cocoa tree.
ga: Galamsey woɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ mercury kɛ dade ni tsii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛ nu gbɛi lɛ amli. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaaa amɛná nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha cacao tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaafite cacao tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to protect them, heat scorches their leaves and dries out soil moisture before their roots can establish.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close forces them to fight for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. It also creates a dark, damp space that encourages diseases to spread easily between trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ feɔ ekome. Ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ hu baa ni ewoɔ helai hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ateŋ oya.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without forming pods if the trees are under stress from high temperatures, lack of water, or poor pollination by tiny insects like midges in the area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long does a newly planted hybrid cocoa tree take before it starts giving fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees generally begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years if given proper shade, weed control, and soil nutrients, whereas older traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ amɛwo amɛhe hulutsoo. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: How does cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ni mi cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii babaoo baa?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. It allows more sunlight and air to flow through the farm, reducing humidity while directing food straight into pod production.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hoɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa hulutsoo baa shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ niyenii yaa pod feemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning shade trees, and removing infected pods helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What is damaging the tender green shoots and leaves on my cocoa trees during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni fiteɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids). They bite into young shoots and feed on the plant's sap, which dries out the new growth if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii ni amɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my cocoa trees to turn yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po?

english: Yellow leaves during rains often indicate a shortage of essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, or waterlogged soil where roots cannot breathe properly to take in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is the topsoil on my farm washing away whenever heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil without plant cover or mulch gets easily swept away by rain runoff. Growing ground cover crops or leaving plant leaves on the soil keeps moisture in and holds the fertile topsoil in place.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ hoɔ oya. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ loo tsei ahe baai ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from strong sunlight. Without shade from plantains or shade trees, intense sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil moisture, causing the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei amli lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy leaves but tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing lush leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding the tuber roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, tuber sisije ɔmɛ lɛɛɔ kɛ yaa sisi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves high up into the light and keeps them off the hot ground, preventing rot and disease.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ yɛ la mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: Yellowing starting from the tip along the main rib of lower leaves means the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on heavily to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ fãi wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmãa kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmãa wuji lɛ nɔ waa yɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism. By rolling up, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe koni ekɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when temperatures get extremely high or when the plant experiences stress from either too little water or sudden heavy watering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu fioo tsɔ loo nu ni fa babaoo trukaa lɛ mli.

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when irregular watering prevents the roots from taking up calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to move my tomato seedlings from the nursery bed to the main farm in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tomato dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanting in the cool evening gives seedlings the entire night to heal their roots and absorb water without the stress of hot afternoon sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛmɔɔ nu gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool in dry weather, and blocks weed seeds from receiving light to grow.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do my crops actually make their own food to grow?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Crops produce their own food using energy from sunlight, water from the soil, and air trapped by their green leaves. Fertilizer and manure act like vitamins to help the plant perform this process more efficiently.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli, nu ni jɛɔ sũ mli, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ vitamini ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsuɔ nɛkɛ nitsumɔ nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when it is raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking a vital nutrient called nitrogen. Even with plenty of water, plants need soil nutrients to maintain green leaves and develop healthy grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ nu babaoo po yɛ Tsei hu ahe miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ ni amɛná ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up in full sunlight while plantains do fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, plantains lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate tender leaves that easily scorch under direct sun. Plantains grow broad, tough leaves quickly, making them ideal living umbrellas to shade young cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni wa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa akɛ hulutsoo kɛha kookoo tsei bibii yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, crops lose leaf moisture to the air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant droops temporarily to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and save water.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ baa lɛ mli nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛba baa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni amɛbu nu he.

english: Plants shed flowers when stressed by high temperatures, erratic watering, or low soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for its own survival until growth conditions improve.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cutting off extra side branches on tomato plants help produce bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo niji krokomɛi ni fata he yɛ tomato tso nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Excess branches consume water and soil food to grow leaves instead of fruit. Removing small extra branches directs the plant's energy into developing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni baai akwɛ̃ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. niji bibii amlijaa Kpojiemɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts improve the soil for my next corn crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this naturally enriches the soil with food for future crops like corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block light from each other, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why can cassava survive long dry spells while my corn crop dries up and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow deep to search for underground water, and the plant can drop its leaves to stop moisture loss during dry seasons while storing energy in its thick tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Ni tsei baanyɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛkpa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are growing in the same farm ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. They also crowd crop roots and can harbor pests and diseases that attack your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Amɛhaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi hu feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: How does heavy rain damage my mature crops right around harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Excess rain on fully grown crops introduces high moisture that causes mature fruits and grains to rot, mold, or sprout prematurely, which quickly ruins their quality and market value.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni edara lɛ fiteɔ, amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ baafite nɔ ni hi kɛ jara nɔ oya.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my crops so they don't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?
