english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as leaves turning yellow, stalks drying out, or pod shells hardening; harvesting at this sweet spot prevents pests and wet weather from destroying them.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbi, loo pod lɛ yibii ni mli wa. Nikpamɔ yɛ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni amɛkafite amɛ.

english: Why do crops decay much faster once they are cut compared to when they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya kɛji afolɔ amɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni eda lolo lɛ he lɛ?

english: When a crop is harvested, its living defense mechanisms shut down, leaving the harvested produce unable to protect itself from rot-causing fungi and bacteria that thrive in damp weather.
ga: Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, wala yibii lɛ ahebuu gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ kpaɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni akpaa lɛ nyɛɛɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa ŋmeii baa ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is matching my crop schedule to seasonal weather patterns so critical for success?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ be ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ be mli lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ he hiaa koni aye omanye lɛ?

english: Crops require specific moisture levels at different growth stages, so aligning your schedule ensures heavy rains hit during growth rather than during the sensitive drying and harvest phase.
ga: Tsei biɔ hulutsoo be pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ amɛdalɛ bei srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, be ni okɛtoɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ baanɛ waa yɛ shweremɔ be mli. Mohu ɔ, e ji be nɛ e he hia wawɛɛ nɛ e ngɛ hɛ mi kpatami kɛ ní kpami be.

english: What weather signs should I look for before spending money to hire labor for harvesting?
ga: Mɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he okadi esa akɛ makwɛ dani mafite shika yɛ kpamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for a predicted stretch of dry, sunny days so your harvested produce can be gathered and dried properly without wet downpours trapping moisture in your crop piles.
ga: Taomɔ gbii ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ abua nibii ni akpa lɛ anaa ni agbi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ onibii ni ato lɛ amli.

english: What causes my freshly harvested grains to mold so quickly after I gather them?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui heei ni mikpa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya beni mibua amɛnaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly gathered grains carry internal moisture; if they are bundled or stored without sufficient sun-drying, trapped humidity creates a breeding ground for destructive mold.
ga: Nibii ni abua naa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ abua naa loo akɛto ni hulu lɛ mli egbiko bɔ ni sa lɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ afee he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: How can I protect my gathered crops from spoilage if rain starts while I am harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mikpamɔ lɛ he koni ekafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni mikpaa nii lɛ?

english: Cover your collected produce with tarpaulins elevated off the damp ground using raised wooden platforms, allowing air to circulate while keeping rainwater out.
ga: Kɛ tarp ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ aha nibii ni abua naa lɛ ahe. koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli yɛ be kome mli ni nugbɔ lɛ akabote mli

english: Why do ripe crops begin to rot on the plant if left unharvested during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akpaaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fully ripe crops stop absorbing nutrients and naturally open up, allowing rainwater to collect inside pods or skins where dampness causes fungal rot.
ga: Tsei ni edara kwraa lɛ kpaɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ pod loo hewolo lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it risky to spend all my savings to harvest my entire farm at one time during unpredictable weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ okɛ shika fɛɛ ni okɛto lɛ baakpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting everything at once exposes your entire yield to sudden rainstorms before it can be dried or sold, risking both the entire harvest and the money spent on labor.
ga: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni oookpa shikome lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baa oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ amli dani abaanyɛ agbi loo ahɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ kɛ nikpamɔ lɛ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ yɛ nitsumɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ woɔ oshara mli.

english: How does waterlogged soil affect mature crops right before harvest?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani akpaa nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Waterlogged soil smothers roots by cutting off oxygen, causing stalks to weaken, fall over into the mud, and expose the harvest to damp ground rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛgbeeɔ mulu lɛ mli, ni ehaa sũ ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does the topsoil on my farm wash away so easily when it rains ever since the big trees were cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni afo tsei wuji lɛ?

english: Tree roots act like nets that hold the soil tightly together, while their leaves break the heavy force of falling rain. Without trees, heavy rain hits the bare ground directly and easily washes away the fertile topsoil your crops need to grow.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni fiɔ sũ lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewalɛ naa lɛ. Kɛji tsei bɛ lɛ Nugbɔ ni naa wa baatswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa ni he hiaa ni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo.

english: How can planting trees help keep my farm soil moist during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Tree roots create deep channels that help rainwater soak deep into the ground during the wet season instead of running off. Trees also shade the ground from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating too quickly from your crops' soil.
ga: Tso shishifãi feɔ gbɛi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli, moŋ fe ni eeejo foi. Tsei hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni oduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do trees naturally add fertilizer to the soil for my crops?
ga: Te tsei baanyɛ afee tɛŋŋ amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: When tree leaves fall onto your farm, they rot and break down into natural manure rich in organic matter. Additionally, certain trees pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, naturally feeding nearby crops.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Egboɔ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Tsei komɛi hu gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crops dry up and heat up so quickly now compared to years ago when we had more trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbi ni edɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he beni wɔyɛ tsei babaoo lɛ?

english: Trees create a cooler local climate by releasing moisture into the air and providing shade. When trees are cut down, the surrounding air gets much hotter and drier, causing crops to lose their moisture rapidly and dry out.
ga: Tsei haa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa hulutsoo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli woɔ la ni egbiɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do strong winds keep snapping and blowing down my tall crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yaa nɔ etswaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ shi lɛ?

english: When land is completely cleared of big trees, there is nothing to block strong winds as they sweep across the land. Planting a line of trees around your farm acts as a windbreak, slowing down harsh winds before they reach and destroy your crops.
ga: Beni ajie tsei wuji fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nɔ ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi dani eba ni efite onibii.

english: Why do crops like cocoa grow much better under shade trees than in open bare sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and prefer cool, humid conditions. Shade trees filter the hot sunlight, lower the surrounding temperature, and protect the cocoa plants so they can produce healthier pods.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. ni esumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ Shade tsei lɛ shwieɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aba shi ni ebuɔ cacao tso lɛ he koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow and look stressed during the dry hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni haoɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct afternoon heat forces plants to lose water faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Without scattered trees nearby to break the heat and lower atmospheric temperatures, crops suffer heat stress, causing leaves to yellow and wilt.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei komɛi egbɛ eshwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni ejie dɔlɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpeɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Will planting trees alongside my food crops reduce my farm yields?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Not if you select the right beneficial tree species and space them properly. Choosing deep-rooted trees that do not compete with crop roots for surface water will protect your crops from heat and improve soil health, leading to better long-term yields.
ga: Jeee nakai kɛji ohala tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni sa ni oto he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ohala tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How long will it take for newly planted trees on my land to start protecting my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani tsei heei ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aje shishi amɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Fast-growing trees start offering basic shade and wind protection within 2 to 3 years. By 5 to 7 years, their roots and fallen leaves will significantly improve the soil structure and local climate around your crops.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛhaa shishijee hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Yɛ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 sɛɛ lɛ, amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai ni egbee shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi. Abaanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ waa.

english: Is it true that clearing all trees from my land will make it unusable for my children in the future?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsei fɛɛ ni mijie kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha miwɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛtsu nii?

english: Yes, removing all trees leads to rapid soil erosion, loss of organic nutrients, and harsh local heat that dries out the land. Over time, the soil becomes too poor to support crops, making it difficult for future generations to farm successfully.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei fɛɛ ni aaajie lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ oya. niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni laajeɔ kɛ jɛmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbiɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa yinɔi ni baaba lɛ Yaa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu okwaayeli he nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees like umbrellas, while also providing food and income while waiting for cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta, yɛ be mli ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete for soil food and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and overcrowded farm conditions. Removing infected pods and trimming excess branches lets sunlight in to slow down the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, duŋ, kɛ gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do insects attack my crop plants more during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high air moisture and soft green shoots, which pests need to feed and breed quickly. Checking your farm frequently during wet months helps you spot and manage pest outbreaks early.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Ehe miihia ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aye niyenii ni amɛfɔ oya. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ, obaanyɛ ona ni okwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ anɔ mra.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from dry weather, lack nutrients, or lack tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers. Keeping shade trees helps maintain soil moisture so pollination can happen.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Tsei ni akɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni pollination aba.

english: Why is it important to prune or cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo loo ajie niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or overgrown branches that suck energy away from fruit production. It redirects tree food toward flowers and pods while allowing air flow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni eda fe nine ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do cassava leaves fall off during the dry season, and will the crop die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagboi lɛ?

english: Cassava drops leaves naturally during dry periods to save water and prevent drying out. The plant is not dead; its roots stay alive underground and will grow new leaves when the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi hulutsoo naa. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and turn yellow even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizers, soil nutrients, and water directly from the roots of your crops. Keeping the field clear ensures your main crops absorb all the food and water in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do hybrid cocoa seeds give better yield than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hybrid cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially developed to resist local diseases, grow faster, and produce more pods. Saved seeds gradually lose these strong traits, resulting in lower yields over time.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. shwereɔ oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ fiofio Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers fall over easily during heavy winds and rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can loosen in wet soil when carrying heavy fruit bunches. Planting suckers at the right depth and supporting heavy stalks with wooden props prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ ajie ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛ́ ehiɛ aduawai ni tsii. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii yɛ he ni sa ni akɛ tsei ni tsii lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's growth helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ni akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli awa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough to plant cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: Healthy cocoa soil is dark, soft, holds moisture well after rain, and contains decaying organic leaves and earthworms. If your soil is very sandy, dry, or hard like rock, you need to enrich it with organic compost before planting.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni baai ni fiteɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã, egbi, loo tɛi ni wa Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu.

english: Is it better to clear my land by burning the bush or by clearing it manually without fire?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ashãa nɔ loo akɛ niji aaatsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ la tsuuu nii?

english: Clearing without burning is much better because burning kills useful soil organisms and destroys topsoil nutrients. Leaving cleared grass and leaves to rot back into the soil creates natural compost that feeds your future crops.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ hi kwraa fe no. Ejaakɛ la ni ashãa lɛ kpataa nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni efiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do other farmers advise me to plant cassava together with maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava with maize lets you harvest two crops from one piece of land at different times. Maize grows fast and is ready for harvest in about three months, while cassava grows slower underneath and matures months after the maize is harvested.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa duɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Abɛi daa oya, ni aaafee nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, daa blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ ni ekwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How deep should I bury cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 10 to 15 centimeters deep, placed at a slanted angle with the growth buds pointing upward. Planting too deep makes tuber formation difficult, while planting too shallow causes the stick to dry out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu Yucca niji lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15, ni akɛto he ko ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu nii jogbaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha bulb feemɔ afee nɔ ni wa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cocoa nursery seedlings die shortly after I move them to the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings often die from heat shock and sudden direct sunlight when moved to the field. To help them survive, plant temporary shade crops like plantain ahead of time and transplant during the main rainy season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, kɛtsɔ hiɛ. ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli

english: What is eating small holes in my tomato leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ tomato baai lɛ anɔ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small holes in tomato leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. You can manage them by spraying a natural neem leaf water extract or an approved agricultural insect spray early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ tomato baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo okwaayeli mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any pepper fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, hot dry air, or uneven watering. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass helps keep the soil cool and moist, encouraging fruit to set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Wo yibii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and crooked instead of large and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ agboi ni etse amɛhe lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil is hard, stony, or packed down, preventing the roots from expanding freely. Making high, soft soil mounds or ridges without big stones gives the yam tubers space to grow smooth and long.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tɛi wuji bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent insects from ruining my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects attack stored maize if the grains are still damp or easily accessible. Make sure the maize is thoroughly sun-dried until the grains are hard, and store them off the ground in dry, airtight bags or improved cribs.
ga: Kplukai tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ mli edɔ lolo loo anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he oya. Kwɛmɔ ni hulu lɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛto kotoku ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ gbekɛbii amli ni asaa lɛ mli.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Groundnuts and cowpeas are special crops that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing your land for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow and curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or a sign that the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Aloo eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do armyworms keep attacking the inside center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The inner center (or whorl) of young maize is soft, moist, and sheltered from hot sun and predators, making it the perfect protected feeding ground for fall armyworms.
ga: Abɛi abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ (loo ring) lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eyɛ hebuu kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii feɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abuɔ he kɛha fall armyworms.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves up into tubes to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any tomatoes during dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato wooo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the air is very dry, tomato plants experience heat stress that prevents flower pollination, causing the plant to shed its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Tomato tsei naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I still add organic animal manure to my farm if I already bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afata miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji mihe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ momo?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the crops directly, but organic manure improves the soil itself by helping it hold water longer, keeping it soft, and feeding healthy soil organisms.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to yield well only in their first planting; saving and planting seeds from that harvest results in weak plants with smaller, irregular yields in the second generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil in raised mounds or ridges so their roots can easily push downward and expand outward into thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii amli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ashɛ shi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse ni wa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, the main stems turn woody, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ bafeɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Is there a strong market demand for tomatoes in Ghana right now?
ga: Ani jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli wa bianɛ?

english: Yes, local tomato farmers currently produce less than 20% of the total market demand, which leaves a huge market gap for local growers to supply.
ga: Hɛɛ, amrɔ nɛɛ, maŋ lɛ mli tomato okwaafoi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ 20% yɛ jarayeli nibii fɛɛ ni ataoɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa jarayeli gbɛ agbo ko baa kɛha maŋbii ni duɔ nii lɛ koni amɛkɛha.

english: Will I struggle to find buyers if I start growing tomatoes on my farm?
ga: Ani mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mana mɛi ni baahe mi kɛji mibɔi tomato dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, because local tomato production satisfies less than 20% of the high demand in the market, meaning there are plenty of buyers seeking supply.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ maŋ lɛ mli tomato ni afeɔ lɛ haa jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ 20%, ni tsɔɔ akɛ jarayelɔi babaoo yɛ ni miitao nibii ni akɛbaaha.

english: Which vegetable crop currently has a huge supply shortage in Ghanaian markets?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni aduɔ lɛ he ehiaaa waa amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have a severe supply shortage because current local production meets less than 20% of what the market requires.
ga: Tomato yɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ he naagba waa ejaakɛ amrɔ nɛɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ nɔ ni jara lɛ biɔ lɛ mlijaa 20%.

english: How long can tomatoes stay fresh after harvesting if I do not have a fridge?
ga: Be enyiɛ tomato baanyɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ? Kɛji mibɛ friji

english: With the right tomato varieties, harvested fruits can stay fresh and firm on a simple kitchen table for up to three weeks without refrigeration.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tomato henɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ lɛ, yibii ni akpa lɛ baahi shi ehee ni ehi shi shiŋŋ yɛ o-rustic kitchen okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi otsii etɛ ni fridge bɛ mli.

english: What kind of tomato variety should I plant if I want to reduce spoilage after harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ tomato henɔ esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni mahã nɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ aba shi?

english: You should select high-quality tomato varieties known for long shelf life, as they can naturally stay good for up to three weeks at room temperature.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tomato henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ale akɛ amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato baanyɛ ahi ebɔɔ su lɛ mli kɛyashi otsii 3 yɛ ŋwɛi fɛ̃i mli.

english: Why do some tomatoes spoil quickly while others last for weeks without cold storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato komɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi otsii babaoo ni akɛwooo friji mli lɛ?

english: Certain tomato varieties have better firm traits and post-harvest resilience, allowing them to remain fresh on a table for up to three weeks without rotting.
ga: Tomato henɔi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa amɛ. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ hiɔ okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ otsii etɛ ni efiteee.

english: Do I need to buy expensive cooling equipment to store my harvested tomatoes?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe friji ni jara wa koni mikɛto tomato ni mikpa lɛ?

english: No, if you grow good-quality tomato varieties, you can store them at normal room temperature on a table for up to three weeks without needing a fridge.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa kɛji akɛ oduɔ tomato henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛto okpɔlɔ nɔ yɛ ŋwɛi fɛ̃i ni sa mli kɛyashi otsii etɛ ni okɛwooo friji mli.

english: Can I hold my harvested tomatoes at home for a few weeks before selling them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tomato ni mikpa lɛ ato shia otsii fioo komɛi dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, provided you cultivate the right variety, you can safely keep the tomatoes on a table for up to three weeks without them going bad.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ odu tomato srɔtoi ni sa. Obaanyɛ okɛ tomato ato okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi otsii etɛ ni efiteee.

english: How does growing long-lasting tomato varieties help me make more profit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tomato ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Long-lasting tomatoes give you up to three weeks of shelf life without spoiling, allowing you flexibility to sell into a market that currently lacks 80% of its needed supply.
ga: Tomato ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛtoɔ otsii etɛ ni efiteee. Ehaa onáa hegbɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe ko ni amrɔ nɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ 80% bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are market women and traders interested in specific locally grown tomato varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei kɛ jarayelɔi lɛ yɔɔ tomato henɔi ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miishɛɛ titri lɛ?

english: Traders prefer resilient tomato varieties because they can be kept at room temperature for up to three weeks without spoiling, helping fill the massive 80% market deficit.
ga: Jarayelɔi sumɔɔ tomato henɔi ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi ejaakɛ abaanyɛ akɛto ŋwɛi fɛ̃i mli kɛyashi otsii etɛ ni efiteee. Enɛ ye ebua ni awo jarayeli mli shika babaoo ni ji 80% lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is like food for the crop. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni tamɔ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo abele toi agboi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings need to be planted at a slant rather than flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle helps the roots grow deeper into the soil to find water during dry periods, while keeping the buds near the surface so sprouts can easily reach the sunlight.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Ha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la lɛ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars feeding on the plant. Spraying a natural neem leaf water mixture or suitable pesticide protects the leaves so the cabbage can grow into a solid head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baai loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efutu mli lɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe koni kaabe lɛ anyɛ adara ni etsɔ yitso ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out their pollen, causing flowers to drop before fruit can form. Mulching around the stems and watering at the base keeps the soil cool and helps fruit set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ he kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ baa shi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural food from the air and put nitrogen back into the soil, refreshing the field for the next season after heavy crops like maize have used up the soil nutrients.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ he jɔɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ beni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ efite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around them or when tiny worms in the soil attack them. Planting yams on high mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Aloo beni ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, they steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from one another, resulting in thin, weak roots instead of big, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji cassava tsei miidara yɛ he kome lɛ, amɛshiɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slow and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. If you do not clear them early, the weeds eat the plant food first, leaving your crops weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli kɛji ojieee amɛ mra. Jwɛi yeɔ tsei klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛfee bibioo.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly under the sun before storing it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Storing wet maize traps moisture inside the bag, which causes mold to grow and attracts insects that spoil the grain. Sun-drying makes the grains hard and safe for long-term storage.
ga: Abele ni efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kotoku lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Hulu ni egbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli waɔ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize crops are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni hɔmɔ miiye mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: When maize plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, their lower leaves start turning yellow from the tip inward in a V-shape. Applying fertilizer at the right time restores their healthy green color and increases grain yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, amɛshishi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbee mli kɛyaa mligbɛ, ni amɛfeɔ V su. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it harmful if I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them safely. Applying concentrated fertilizer to dry soil can burn and severely damage the crop's root system.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: The best time to spray is early morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. Hot midday sun makes liquid chemicals evaporate too quickly and can cause leaf burn on your plants.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei.

english: Why do I need to follow exact dosing instructions when applying pesticide to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Using too little medicine makes pests resistant so they won't die, while using too much can poison your crops, burn leaves, and waste your money.
ga: Tsofa fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛ koni amɛkagboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛyeɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii amli awui, baai ashã, ni afite shika.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces its leaf surface area to prevent losing water, and they usually recover when temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu akafite. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with few leaves when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa shi ebɛ baai fioo beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they stretch upward to fight for sunlight, spending all their energy on height instead of growing strong leaves and big underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa Moŋ lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ baai ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning overcrowded tree branches helps air circulate to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ. Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds damage my young crops even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal fertilizer nutrients, sunlight, and root space, effectively starving your young crops even if water is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ shishifãi gbɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii bibii lɛ kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest if I plant the same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground; rotating with legumes like beans recharges the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, atsake koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How will planting my crops in straight rows help me compared to planting randomly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ he?

english: Straight row planting gives every plant equal space to capture light and nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply medicine, and harvest without damaging plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ náa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ tsofa awo mli, ni okpa nibii ni ofiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. As the plant grows, it starves its older leaves to push whatever available nitrogen it has to the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ koni amɛtsi nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛya baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow lots of tall green leaves but produce no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi fɔfɔii bɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing stems and lush leaves instead of flowers. Adding phosphorus fertilizer helps trigger blooming and fruit production.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Fosforo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to shrink their surface area and prevent water from evaporating too quickly. It is the plant's natural shield against drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do my maize plants roll their leaves into thin tubes when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Rolling leaves into tight tubes protects the plant's leaf pores from direct sunlight. This reduces water loss through heat until the soil receives moisture again.
ga: Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo tsɔnei ni mli wa mli lɛ, ebuɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in soaked soil because excess water fills the soil pockets and cuts off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds allows rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ sũ kotokui amli ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by intense dry sunlight, extreme heat, or a lack of small pollinating insects. Providing banana or plantain shade shields the tree and keeps moisture around the blooms.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ o-banana loo plantains lɛ wo hulutsoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does cutting off extra small branches from my mango tree make the remaining fruits grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni ajie kɛjɛ mango tso lɛ nɔ, ni eha yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ dara?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches stops the tree from spreading its food too thinly. The tree can then direct all its water and nutrients into a smaller amount of fruit, making each mango larger and healthier.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha tso lɛ akagbɛ eniyenii lɛ eshwa tsɔ. Tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli yɛ fioo fioo mli. Enɛ haa mango fɛɛ mango feɔ agbo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: How can I tell when my yams under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This signals that the plant has stopped feeding the vine and transferred all its food into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa wain tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Extra suckers compete with the parent plantain tree for nutrients, water, and light. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to bear heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ la. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛye ŋmei ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in the same plot as my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that can pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. The nearby maize uses this extra soil nitrogen to grow stronger without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ sũ mli nitrogen ni fa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is flooded with water, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Too much shade and high rain let water drop onto the pods and spread the fungal spores easily.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Shade ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nu baajɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni egbɛ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do I see tiny holes and powdery dirt inside the central shoots of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the funnel) during the day and chew on tender leaves before the cob grows.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei yɛŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Ani agbee shi ni efeee pod kwraa?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry weather, insect attacks, or lack of pollination by small midges in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni nu egbi, kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ, loo nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haaa amɛhe afee fɛo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before pepper fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, water is scarce, or when insects like thrips damage the delicate flower parts.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, nu faaa, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips fite fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily destroyed by soil pests like root nematodes and weevils. Weakened roots cannot support the heavy bunch, so the plant needs bamboo props for support.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes kɛ weevils lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ he miihia nibii ni akɛ ŋmei fee koni ekɛfi esɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soils because standing water suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green sprouts in the barn before I am ready to sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani mifee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and sprout when they sense heat and moisture changes after harvest. Storing them in a cool, dark, well-ventilated barn slows down this natural sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ wɔɔhe ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa tsakemɔi amli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my yams spoil so quickly if I leave them exposed to direct sunlight after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ beni mikpa amɛ nii lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight heats up harvested yams and burns their skin, causing them to lose moisture rapidly and rot from the inside. Keeping yams shaded protects them from heat damage and extends their shelf life.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni akpa lɛ mli adɔ. ni eha ehewolo lɛ shã. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni efiteɔ kɛjɛɔ emli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes wo shĩa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dɔlɛ akafite amɛ, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover their harvested yams with fresh leaves at the market or on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai heei haa ŋmeii ni amɛkpaa lɛ ahe yɛ jara nɔ loo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering yams with leaves creates a cool barrier against harsh sun rays, helping to keep temperature down and reduce skin damage so the tubers stay firm and fresh.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ha sweet potato nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fɛ̃i kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa hewolo nɔ fitemɔ baa shi. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi ehee ni eha ehe ajɔ lɛ

english: What happens to my yams if I dump them roughly on the ground when unloading them at the market?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Rough dumping cracks the inner flesh and bruises the outer skin of the yams. These invisible wounds allow bacteria and fungi to enter, causing the yams to rot much faster.
ga: Kɛ́ ashwie nɔ ni mli wa lɛ, ebaagbala sweet potato lɛ mligbɛ ni ebaafite sweet potato lɛ kponɔgbɛ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi ni anaaa nɛɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa.

english: Can leaving yams directly on hot bare ground ruin them even if they are covered on top?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ nɔ ko ehà nɔ po?

english: Yes, hot bare ground or concrete transfers heat into the bottom layer of the yams, causing the underside to soften and spoil. Placing a bed of leaves or straw underneath provides insulation from the ground heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo kɔnkrit baajie dɔlɛ kɛya atomɔ shishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi saatso wo shishi lɛ, ebaatsi ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Does drying yams under the bright midday sun help preserve them or cause harm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe loo ekɛ naagba baa?

english: Harsh midday sun hurts yams by burning their tissue. While yams need gentle curing in a well-ventilated, shaded place to heal surface scratches, intense direct sun speeds up spoilage.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ sweet potato kɛtsɔ fãji ni shãa lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni atsa sweet potatoes lɛ blɛoo yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahe moŋ, shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How can I protect my yam pile from heat damage while waiting all day for buyers at the market?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe koni hulutsoo lɛ akafite lɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jara nɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can shield your yams by placing a cushioned layer of dry grass or leaves under them and covering the top with clean leaves or shade cloth to keep cool air circulating around the crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-sweet potato lɛ he kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛbaawo amɛshishi ni okɛ baai ni he tse loo mama ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ aha nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ abɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do market authorities ask us to sweep away old leaves after selling our crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli he nitsulɔi biɔ ni wɔjie baai momoi beni wɔhɔ̃ɔ wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Old, decaying leaves collect dirt, attract pests, and trap unwanted moisture, which creates an unhygienic environment that can spread rot to fresh produce brought into the market.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ ni miifite lɛ buaa muji naa. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni emɔɔ nu ni ataooo ni haa shihilɛ ni he tseee lɛ baa Enɛ baanyɛ agbala fitemɔ kɛya nibii heei ni akɛba jara nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do yams rot faster during the hot dry season compared to cooler weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ akɛto hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry air cause yams to lose water quickly and stress the crop tissues, making them far more vulnerable to internal rot if left unprotected.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni ekɛ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛyɛ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaafite yɛ amɛmli kɛji akɛ abuuu amɛhe.

english: Will buyers offer me lower prices if my yams show sun heat marks or soft spots?
ga: Ani mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ baaha mi jara ni baa shi? Kɛji mi sweet potato lɛ yɛ hulutsoo he okadi loo he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo

english: Yes, buyers look for firm, smooth yams without soft spots or discoloration, because sun damage indicates that the yam will rot quickly after purchase.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ ahe sweet potato lɛ, ebaafite oya.

english: Is it okay to store my harvested yams in an open field without any cover for a few days?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli, ni ahaaa nɔ ko nɔ, gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Leaving yams uncovered in an open field exposes them to sun scorch during the day and dew at night, both of which shorten storage life and encourage early rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulu ashã amɛ yɛ shwane mli, ni ebaaha ŋmeii aba amɛnɔ gbɛkɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshihilɛ be lɛ feɔ kuku ni ewoɔ fitemɔ oya he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow well even after I plant them properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops often fail to thrive due to poor soil nutrients, lack of consistent water, soil diseases, or pests. Checking your soil condition and adding organic compost or manure can help feed weak crops and prepare the soil for future planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni bɛ daa, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ niyenii ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: If the crop I planted fails to grow, should I plant the same crop again or switch to a different one like groundnuts?
ga: Kɛji tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ Ani esa akɛ makwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ loo matsake kɛya tso kroko nɔ tamɔ ŋmei?

english: It is usually better to switch to a different crop like groundnuts rather than planting the same crop again. Switching crops breaks the cycle of soil pests and diseases, and crops like groundnuts actually help restore nitrogen to poor soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, moŋ fe ni ooodu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell early on that my young plants are not thriving so I can save them?
ga: Matsɔɔ bo kɛjɛ shishijee. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni midumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, manyɛ maye mabua amɛ.

english: Look out for yellowing leaves, slow height growth, or wilting during cool times of the day. Spotting these signs early allows you to apply organic manure, adjust watering, or clear surrounding weeds before the plants die completely.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kaadi ŋmɔŋ ni daa blɛoo loo egboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli hulutsoo be mli Okadii nɛɛ ni onaa mra Ehaa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli, otsakeɔ nu ni okɛhaa lɛ, loo ojieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Dani tso lɛ baagbo kwraa

english: Is it okay for me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I already have fruit trees growing?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ aduawai tsei momo lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant groundnuts between fruit trees, especially when the trees are still young. Groundnuts grow low to the ground and do not block light, and they enrich the soil with nitrogen which benefits your fruit trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii yɛ aduawai tsei ateŋ. Titri lɛ, beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ehaaa hulutsoo. Ekɛ nitrogen hu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ, ni enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha otsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Will planting groundnuts between my fruit trees steal water and nutrients from the trees?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli?

english: Groundnuts actually work well with fruit trees because their roots draw nutrients from shallow soil while fruit trees reach deeper. In addition, groundnuts add natural fertilizer back into the soil, helping nearby plants thrive.
ga: Peanuts tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ aduawai tsei anɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai tsei lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ. Peanuts hu kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How close to my fruit trees can I safely plant groundnuts without damaging the tree roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ aduawai tsei ahe shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Leave a space of about 1 to 2 meters around the base of young fruit trees. This prevents groundnut roots from crowding the tree and gives you room to dig up the groundnuts during harvest without damaging the tree's main roots.
ga: Shi mita 1 kɛyashi 2 kɛbɔle tso bibioo lɛ shishi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ tso lɛ. Ni ehaa onáa gbɛ ni okɛfoɔ ŋmeii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. ni efiteee tso lɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ

english: Can groundnuts still produce good yield if my big fruit trees cast shade over them?
ga: Ani ŋmeii baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji mi tso agbo ni woɔ yibii lɛ wo amɛhe shade?

english: Groundnuts need plenty of direct sunlight to make flowers and pods underground. If your fruit trees create heavy shade, trim some upper branches to let light reach the ground, or plant the groundnuts in the sunny patches between trees.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛji o-fruit tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo waa lɛ, Kpãa niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo dumɔ ŋmeii yɛ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do groundnuts help improve soil that is not working well for my farm?
ga: Te ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they take nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food inside the soil. This acts as free natural fertilizer for your land, making the soil healthier for other crops later on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What type of soil do groundnuts need to make plenty of large nuts underground?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ he hiaa koni ŋmeii agboi babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts prefer loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water easily. Soft, loose soil makes it easy for the plant's pegs to push into the ground and swell into full, healthy pods.
ga: Peanuts sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsi amɛhe kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfuu ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time during the rainy season for me to plant groundnuts?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Plant groundnuts right after the rains become regular and steady. They need warm, moist soil early in their life to germinate quickly, but they require dry conditions when it is time to harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia amɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Shi shihilɛi ni mli egbi he miihia amɛ beni kpamɔ be shɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize stalks fall over whenever a strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over (known as lodging) when their roots are not deep enough or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium. Heap soil around the base of the plants (earthing up) to give the roots strong anchorage against heavy wind.
ga: ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ roosting) kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium. Okɛ shikpɔŋ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afata he) koni eha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How can I protect my young cabbage seedlings from insect pests without spraying expensive chemicals all the time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa shwieee nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: You can cover your nursery beds with fine mesh protective netting. The netting acts as a physical barrier that stops moths and flying pests from laying eggs on your young plants while still allowing air, sunlight, and rain to pass through.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ aha o-nursery saatso lɛ he. Net lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ otsei bibii lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ nugbɔ tsɔɔ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing twisted and deformed instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe efee shoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become deformed when the soil is too hard, compacted, or full of rocks. Loosening the soil deeply by ploughing or mounding before planting allows the roots to expand freely and grow straight.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo akwɛɔ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes crack open when water intake is irregular, such as heavy rain following a dry period. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to tear. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering prevents this.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. cause tearing Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are some of my pepper plants remaining very tiny while others planted at the same time grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ be kome mli lɛ dara waa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when plants are sown too close together, forcing them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough soil room and light to mature evenly.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch and dry out under intense direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that protect the young trees until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata kookoo he lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and rot when heavy rain sits on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water collects around plant roots without draining, it starves the roots of air and causes root rot. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso shishifãi ahe ni nu ejeee mli Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The corn plant moves available nitrogen to its upper leaves to survive. Applying well-decomposed manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant instead of growing into full tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as severe hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or sudden flooding. Giving plants consistent water during flowering helps save the blossoms so they can set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu afua ni baa trukaa Nu ni akɛhaa tsei daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes white dusty spots to cover my garden egg leaves and make them dry up?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa eggplant baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ?

english: The white dusty spots are caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives in humid, crowded farm conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming overcrowded leaves improves airflow around the plant to stop fungal growth.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ sũ yɛŋ baa. Eshwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ. tsei koni amɛkpa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does maize grow and yield harvest so much faster than tree crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa daa ni ewoɔ yibii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Maize is a seasonal grain plant with a short life cycle that naturally matures in just 3 to 4 months, whereas tree crops spend years building trunk and leaf structures before producing fruit.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɔ shi be kukuoo ni ekwɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛmaa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Which short-season crops can I plant to give me quick cash while I wait for my long-term crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ lɛ?

english: Fast-growing crops like maize, vegetables, and legumes complete their harvest cycle in a few months, allowing you to generate income to fund farm activities while long-term crops like cassava or fruit trees develop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai, kɛ ŋmãa Egbeɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Ehaa onáa shika ni okɛbaatsu ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ahe nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai tsei lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants curl up their leaves when the sun gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu lɛ miitso waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce surface area exposed to heat, which helps conserve moisture inside the plant during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn turn yellow and fail to grow tall if I don't feed the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haaa niyenii lɛ?

english: Maize grows very rapidly and requires high amounts of nitrogen from the soil. Without adequate nutrients, the plant cannot produce enough green chlorophyll, causing yellowing and stunted growth.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ebiɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting seeds too close causes the maize plants to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season, why does my harvest keep decreasing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be Mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing maize on the same soil strips away specific nutrients. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas returns vital nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to intercrop fast crops like maize with slower crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa?
