english: Maize grows tall and harvests early without shading out young cassava, allowing you to make efficient use of soil space and harvest two crops from the same land at different times.
ga: Abele daa ni ekpaa oya ni ekɛ shade haaa ŋmei bibii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: How can I store my harvested maize properly so it feeds my household for the entire year without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato jogbaŋŋ koni mishiabii lɛ aná afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni efiteee?

english: Drying maize thoroughly until the moisture is low and storing the grains in airtight hermetic bags protects them from pest damage like weevils and prevents mold growth.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Ni kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmãa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are maize prices usually very low during the harvest period compared to the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli kɛ akɛto hulutsoo be lɛ he lɛ?

english: During harvest time, most farmers are selling their fresh produce at once, creating a large supply in the market that drives prices down until supply decreases months later.
ga: kpamɔ be mli Okwaafoi babaoo hɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii heei yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii babaoo baa jara nɔ ni haa jara lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young maize seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to quickly absorb available soil moisture and nutrients faster than domesticated crops, which is why clearing them early is essential for maize survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhe shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia koni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi.

english: Where is the safest place for me to get quality maize seeds for this planting season?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni maná ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nɛkɛ ŋmãa be nɛɛ?

english: It is best to buy certified seeds from registered agro-dealers or your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) office. Seeds bought from general market sellers are often meant for eating, not planting, and may produce weak crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ loo okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe (MoFA) nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi babaoo adɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛyeɔ, shi jeee dumɔwui, ni ebaanyɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Can I just take maize grain from my kitchen storage and plant it on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ mli ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting grain stored for cooking usually leads to poor yields and stunted plants. Seed maize is specially produced, treated, and certified to grow strong and resist diseases, unlike regular grain from the market.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ŋmaa ni aduɔ lɛ haaa yibii kpakpai kɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ. Afeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsuɔ he nii ni ahaa amɛ odaseyeli akɛ amɛhe wa ni helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ. Ejeee tamɔ dumɔwui krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Is it fine to plant seeds saved from my previous harvest, or should I buy new ones every year?
ga: Ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ. Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei daa afi?

english: If you are growing hybrid crop varieties, saving seed from last year's harvest will cause your next crop to grow unevenly, stay small, and produce far less grain. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees the best crop performance.
ga: Kɛji oodu tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he Dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookɛto lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee, afee bibioo ni ebaawo dumɔwui fioo kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very short and stunted while my neighbor's farm looks tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when you plant low-quality or fake seeds, when the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or when crops face early drought. Using certified seeds and applying the right fertilizer at the right time prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ehiii loo amalei. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ loo be mli ni tsei kɛ hɔmɔ kpeɔ mra Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: If my rice crops are already looking small and stunted, will adding extra fertilizer fix them?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ tamɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔ momo lɛ Ani ŋmãa babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baatsu naagba lɛ he nii?

english: Fertilizer helps if the soil lacks nutrients, but if the stunting is caused by genetically poor or bad seeds, fertilizer will not turn them into high-yielding plants. Good crop growth starts with good seed quality.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shweremɔ lɛ baa hu? Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haŋ amɛfee tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Tso lɛ dalɛ kpakpa jeɔ shishi kɛ dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: Why did my rice seeds sprout out of the ground but then stop growing after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi no sɛɛ lɛ ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: This can happen if the seed variety was not suited for your land, if pests attacked the young roots, or if poor-quality seed lacked enough stored energy to keep growing strong after sprouting.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ esaaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua shishifãi bibii loo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ.

english: How can my local agricultural extension officer help me before I start planting my farm?
ga: Te maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ dani mije ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Extension officers can help you select the best crop varieties for your soil, guide you to trusted seed sellers, teach proper planting distances, and show you how to test seed quality before you plant.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ohala tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Mikɛ bo miitsɔɔ dumɔwui ahɔ̃ɔlɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni otsɔɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ.

english: Is there a simple way for me to test my maize seeds at home to see if they will grow before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ maka ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ makwɛ yɛ shia koni mana kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can do a simple germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet cloth for a few days. If 8 or more seeds sprout healthy roots, your seed batch is good to plant across your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa. Odumɔwui lɛ hu sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do different maize seed varieties perform so differently on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Seed varieties are bred for specific soil types and weather conditions. Improved certified varieties are developed to resist local pests and dry spells, whereas local or mixed seeds vary wildly in quality and strength.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Afee tsofai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ srɔtoi babaoo yɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha lɛ mli.

english: What signs should I look for when buying seed packages to know they are genuine?
ga: Mɛɛ okadi esa akɛ matao beni miheɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ koni male akɛ eji anɔkwale?

english: Look for an official certification tag or seal from the seed inspection division on the bag. Genuine seeds are usually clean, uniform in size, treated with a protective color coating, and sealed in branded packaging.
ga: Taomɔ nɔmimaa wolo loo naatsii ni jɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ he tseɔ. Ha ni akɛ pɛnte ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ awo dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mli ni akɛwo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning swollen and yellow, and why are the trees slowly dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ efuu ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ tsei gboiɔ fiofio lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus clogs the tree's internal channels, making branches swell, leaves turn yellow, and eventually killing the tree over a few seasons.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛi lɛ anaa. haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ fũɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli.

english: Is there any spray or fertilizer that can cure swollen shoot disease once my cocoa tree gets it?
ga: Ani tsofa ko loo tsofa ko yɛ ni baanyɛ atsa bud swelling kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ ná?

english: No chemical spray or fertilizer can kill the virus inside an infected tree. Sprays can only kill the insects that spread the disease, so cutting down the infected tree is the only way to stop it from killing the rest of your farm.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ agbe helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ bɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Spray lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okpa amɛ koni amɛkagbe oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does an extension officer say I have to cut down my cocoa tree even if only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ afolɔ cocoa tsei lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛbaai fioo komɛi pɛ hela mɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: The swollen shoot virus spreads throughout the tree long before all the leaves show symptoms. Leaving a partially sick tree standing allows insects to carry the disease from that tree to nearby healthy ones.
ga: Bud swollen virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ dani okadii lɛ fɛɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ fã ko lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ helai kɛjɛɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does the government send teams to cut down whole sections of cocoa farms during a disease outbreak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ miitsu kui koni amɛyafolɔ kookoo ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ yɛ hela ko ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When swollen shoot disease spreads across a district, cutting down infected trees and nearby contact trees creates a safe boundary. This stops the outbreak from destroying whole farming communities and allows the land to be replanted safely.
ga: Beni ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa jɛmɛ fɛɛ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa husu ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa. Enɛ haaa helai ni baa lɛ akafite okwaayeli akutsei muu fɛɛ, ni ehaa anyɛɔ aduɔ shikpɔŋ ekoŋŋ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot where a diseased tree was cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, but you must first clear out the old infected roots and wait for all remaining mealybugs to die. Planting improved hybrid cocoa varieties along with shade crops helps the new seedlings establish safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. ni omɛ ni mealybugs ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ agboi. Cocoa hybrid henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni aduɔ kɛfataa tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ahe lɛ haa dumɔwui heei shwereɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Are the replacement hybrid seedlings offered by the government better than the cocoa seeds I collect from my own trees?
ga: Ani nɔyeli lɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni akɛto najiaŋ lɛ hi fe kookoo yibii ni mijie kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yes, government-supplied hybrid cocoa seedlings are bred to grow faster, produce pods much earlier, yield more cocoa per tree, and resist common diseases better than traditional seeds collected from old farms.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse hybrid cocoa dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ he lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Ehaa pods baa oya Ehaa cocoa yibii babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ. ni amɛhe wa fe blema dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal systems become less efficient at absorbing nutrients from the soil, making them produce fewer pods and more susceptible to pests and diseases.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ, ni ŋmeii kɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: How does a crop disease move from my neighbor's farm into my own cocoa farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko jɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee mi diɛŋtsɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Diseases move across boundaries through tiny insects blown by the wind, ants carrying mealybugs between trees, or when shared farm tools like pruners and cutlasses are not cleaned after use on infected plants.
ga: Helai tsɔɔ kooloi bibii amli kɛtsɔɔ husui anɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa Aŋmeii ni hiɛɔ mealybugs yɛ tsei ateŋ loo be mli ni atsuuu ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛhaa tamɔ pruners kɛ daggers lɛ ahe nii beni akɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ sɛɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I abandon my farm and leave it without care for a year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmɔ lɛ ni mishi amɛ afi kome ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ?

english: An untended cocoa farm quickly becomes overgrown with bush and weeds, which block light, steal soil nutrients, and create a breeding ground for pests like capsids and diseases like black pod and swollen shoot.
ga: Oya nɔŋŋ ni tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi shwereɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni asaaa amɛhe lɛ amli, ni no tsiɔ la naa, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni efee hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efee diŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why do my young replacement cocoa plants wither and die when left in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa najiaŋdamɔlɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small roots that dry out quickly under strong heat. They require shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees to shield them from burning sun while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant produce more energy, which results in larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Maize leaves curl during hot afternoons to reduce water loss. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself and save moisture when the sun is at its hottest.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe he ni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during heatwaves helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ la ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ dɔlɛ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning light yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do farmers say that planting cowpeas or beans helps improve soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, they release natural fertilizer into the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rain drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves with small brown specks inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ kɔni lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing tip of the plant to feed away from heat and birds. Early detection and targeted control are needed to save the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ehe miihia ni ana mra ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why do my pepper plants stay short and weak when grass grows around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food faster than pepper plants can get them. Removing weeds regularly allows the pepper crop to absorb all available nutrients and grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔtɔ tsei. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa pepper tsei lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa amɛhelɛtemɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are tiny young fruits dropping off my mango tree before they get a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii shwieɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees shed excess baby fruit when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support all of them to maturity. Watering during dry periods and applying compost helps the tree hold onto its fruit.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi amɛdara lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why do my maize seeds start sprouting little green shoots inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ lɛ? yɛ mi nitoohe kotoku lɛ mli

english: Maize seeds are alive and stay asleep until they touch moisture and warmth. If rain or humid air leaks into your storage bags, the seeds think they have been planted in damp soil and begin to grow.
ga: Abele ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo he. Kɛji nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ho kɛtee kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ Asusuɔ akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn black and soft when I pile it in a big heap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ato ŋmãa agboi ahe lɛ?

english: Harvested corn still holds natural water inside the grains. When piled together wet without airflow, heat builds up and creates damp mold that turns the grains soft and rots them.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lolo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ato he kome ni efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does corn left touching the ground rot faster than corn kept off the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpaa gbee lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Moisture constantly rises out of the soil and gets absorbed by the bottom layer of corn. Raising your crop off the floor lets dry air circulate underneath, keeping dampness and ground fungi away.
ga: Fɛ̃i teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ shwieɔ mli. Wo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ abɔle amɛshishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to spread my harvested corn under the sun before packing it away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi dani mijara mli lɛ?

english: Sunlight bakes out the hidden moisture deep inside the corn kernels. Dry corn grains become too hard for mold to grow on and too tough for many insects to chew.
ga: Hulu la lɛ shãa nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃, ni ewa tsɔ ni ŋmeii babaoo nyɛŋ amɛye.

english: Why do small beetles start eating powdery holes in my corn grains after a few weeks in the shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ladybugs bibii lɛ bɔi powder bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ yeli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs on the corn while it is still in the field. If the stored corn is warm or slightly damp, those eggs hatch into insects that eat their way out from inside the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmãa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli edɔ fioo loo edɔ Nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tall corn plants fall over flat on the ground whenever a heavy rain storm hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Corn plants have shallow roots holding onto the dirt. When heavy rain softens the soil into mud, strong winds easily pull the roots out or break the heavy stalks near the base.
ga: Abɛi tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli oya loo akumɔ tsei ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my corn is fully mature and ready to be picked from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When the green husk leaves wrapped around the cob turn dry and brown, and the grains feel hard when you press your fingernail into them, the corn has finished growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ, egbiɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa kɛ́ okɛ onineshi tsɔne mii mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do my corn plants stay thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When corn plants grow too close to one another, their roots fight over the same water and food in the soil, leaving the plants weak and without enough energy to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmãa wuji.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key plant food that keeps leaves green. The plant moves whatever green food it has left up to its new growing leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii eŋɔli fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing grains with empty gaps on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Corn needs wind to blow pollen from the top flowers onto every single silk thread on the cob. If dry winds or heat spoil the pollen, the unfertilized silks will leave empty spaces instead of full grains.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ atswa siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi loo latsaa fite pollen lɛ, Siliki baai ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, offering the shade and moisture needed for cocoa to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo ahi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall stakes to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up toward the sunlight to produce energy. Staking keeps leaves exposed to light and away from damp soil, which prevents diseases and helps the underground tubers grow larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant starves its older lower leaves to send whatever food it has left to the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmã tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni ji baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with lush leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots to build thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ ebaai ni tsii kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiiwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or water supply is uneven, which prevents proper pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during intense heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant's sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for hungry crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up dry soil without providing enough lasting moisture. Seeds absorb a little water, start growing, but then dry out and rot before the real rainy season fully begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa. Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu fioo, amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, shi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baashɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers allows the main mother plant to direct its energy into producing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tso agbo ko mli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings collapse at the stem line and die in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering during the hot midday sun can heat up moist topsoil and damage delicate stems, or encourage soil fungi that rot the stem at ground level. Watering early in the morning or late evening prevents stem collapse.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ adɔ ni efite tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. aloo ekanya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nu ni oooha amɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do I need to clear a firebelt around my cocoa farm before the Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie la ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Cocoa ŋmɔ dani Harmattan be lɛ jeɔ shishi

english: During the dry Harmattan season, crops and weeds dry out completely and catch fire easily. Clearing a wide strip of bare land around your farm stops wildfire from jumping onto your field and burning your crops.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa, ni la shãa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi koo mli la naa koni ekatu kɛba oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni ekɛshã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning dry and brown after I spray them for pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves burn if chemical sprays are mixed too strong or applied during the hot afternoon sun. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening protects your crops from chemical burn.
ga: Baai lɛ baashã kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo akɛwo shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ tsofai ni shãa amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Will spraying insecticides directly on open flowers prevent my crops from producing fruit?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii?

english: Yes, heavy chemical sprays on open flowers kill beneficial insects like bees that pollinate the crop. Without pollination, the flowers drop off instead of turning into fruits.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ babaoo lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the young leaves on my new cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct, intense sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or plantains planted nearby to act as umbrellas and protect their tender leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni amɛtsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Why are my plantain suckers growing very tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight and stretch upward rapidly. Spacing them properly ensures they grow thick trunks that can support heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ebaatsɔ oya. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa amɛnáa tsei ni mli tse ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ ekwɛ baai heei ni ekwɛ shishifãi.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much standing water fills all the air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots. Without air, the roots decay quickly underground.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafite oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do black pods spread so quickly through my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp shade and spreads through rain splashes. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air in to dry out the pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli Dense pruning haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have small holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: Small holes in maize leaves usually mean fall armyworms are feeding inside the plant's growing funnel. Early identification and spraying protects the main shoot from being destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fall armyworms lɛ miiye nii yɛ tso lɛ gbɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ayɔse tso lɛ mra ni afɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu tso titri lɛ he kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves shows that the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older leaves to keep the new growth green, signaling a need for fertilizer.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. ni ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green and healthy. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to protect themselves from losing too much water. Placing dry grass mulch around the base of the tree keeps the soil cool and moist, reducing leaf loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi fɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Ha baai ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the soil dries out completely. Regular watering at the root level and providing light shade helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants that yield very small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight so the plant can make energy to grow big tubers under the ground, while also keeping leaves off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ afee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no ji helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ jɛɛhe.

english: Covering the ground with dry materials, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil, stops weeds from growing, and breaks down into natural soil food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite akɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are filled with water and become top-heavy when they carry a large bunch of fruit. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents the tree from breaking.
ga: Nu eyi plantain tsei lɛ amli obɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ kɛ́ amɛwo aduawai babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ.

english: How do weeds growing on my farm actually harm the growth of my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in the soil by stealing water, light, and nutrients that your crops need to grow, leaving your crops weak and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young crops get scorched when I put all the fertilizer at once instead of applying it in small portions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome moŋ fe ni mikɛbaatsu nii fioo fioo lɛ?

english: Feeding young crops too much fertilizer at once burns their delicate roots. Just like giving small meals to a growing child, applying fertilizer in small, gradual doses helps the plant build strength steadily without getting damaged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tsei bibii amli babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaashã amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nakai eji yɛ niyenii bibii ni akɛhaa lɛ hu he. kɛha gbekɛbii ni miida lɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi baafata he Fiofio lɛ, enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etswa ehewalɛ ema shi fiofio ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when I plant them in direct sunlight without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily under strong sun. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby gives them early shelter and moisture until they grow tough enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it recommended that I cut off some of the lower branches and extra leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ mifolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning away excess or weak branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on foliage. This allows the crop to direct its strength and nutrients toward producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better for me to pick my pepper fruits bit by bit as they turn red, or wait to harvest the entire field at once?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii lɛ fiofio kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ? Aloo ooomɛ ni obua ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa shikome?

english: Harvesting ripe peppers bit by bit encourages the plant to produce new flowers and continue fruiting. Leaving mature peppers on the plant tells it to stop growing new produce.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwie shi fioo fioo lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekpa nibii heei ni ebaa lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I miss the required schedule for spraying pesticide on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo be ni ato akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop treatments work best when given at specific stages of pest growth. Missing your spraying schedule allows pests to multiply rapidly, causing severe damage that cannot easily be fixed later.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛji akɛ akɛha yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ daraa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ atooo be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Enɛ fiteɔ nibii waa ni anyɛɛɛ asaa mlɛo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: If I see one sick crop in my field with yellow spots, why should I pull it out immediately?
ga: Kɛji mina tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mitsi mihe kɛjɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Removing a single diseased plant stops the illness from spreading through insects or wind to healthy crops, protecting the rest of your farm from getting infected.
ga: Tso kome pɛ ni hela emɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Buu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn brown and burn after I spray chemical medicine on them during a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals under intense sun causes the liquid to evaporate quickly and concentrate on the leaves, burning the plant tissue. Spraying should be done early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cool.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni ekɛ ehe awo baai lɛ anɔ. shã tso mli fãji Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and weak even after I apply fertilizer late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ po lɛ?

english: If a plant suffers severe starvation or stress during its early stage, its development becomes permanently stunted. Late fertilizer application cannot fully reverse early damage suffered by the crop.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ye hɔmɔ loo haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Eshweremɔ sɛɛ foɔ daa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsake nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn weak when I delay weeding my farm for a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ beni mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi nyɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. When weeds overtake the field for a month, crops starve and their growth comes to a halt.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Beni jwɛi lɛ ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔŋ kome lɛ Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop their flowers when there is a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they drop their flowers to conserve energy and survive. Once regular watering or rainfall resumes, the plant will slowly regain strength and flower again.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi hu koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nu loo nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba hewalɛ fiofio ni ebaawo fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh direct sunlight and extreme heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the sun, the soil loses moisture quickly and the seedlings get scorched.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la naa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni dumɔwui lɛ shãa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the corn plant lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to the top leaves to keep growing, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Should I apply my NPK fertilizer on the same day I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ gbi kome nɔ ni mikɛduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is better to wait about 10 to 14 days after planting until the seeds germinate and form early roots. Applying fertilizer on planting day can burn tiny seeds or get washed away before the young plant has roots to absorb it.
ga: Kɛji odu ogbe naa lɛ, mɛ gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛ shishifãi ba oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ gbi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui bibii akwɛ̃. Eshãa loo efoɔ ehe dani tso bibioo lɛ náa shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ.

english: Will cutting off the top leaves of my cassava plant make the roots underground grow bigger?
ga: Ani kɛ́ afo ŋmei ko yiteŋ baai lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adara?

english: No, cutting top leaves actually reduces tuber size. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food for the plant, which is then stored in the tubers underground; removing leaves starves the roots.
ga: Dabi, ŋwɛi baai lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaha yitso lɛ dalɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii kɛha tsei. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruits during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain and high humidity make flower pollen wet and heavy, preventing proper pollination. Rain stress also causes the tomato plant to drop blossoms to save energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe wa. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli baa lɛ hu haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my pepper plants even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than pepper plants and aggressively steal plant food, soil space, and sunlight. Even with enough water, your crop will starve because the weeds take up the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe pepper tsei ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la waa. Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: If I plant my yam mounds closer together, will I get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes yam roots compete for nutrients and space, resulting in many tiny yams. Proper spacing gives each vine enough soil volume and sunlight to grow full-sized tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ he ko. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii babaoo. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha wain tso fɛɛ wain tso aná shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulb ni dalɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes and powdery droppings inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo muji yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center (funnel) of the corn stalk and eats the fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli (cone) ni amɛyeɔ baai heei dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas inside my maize farm without reducing the amount of corn I harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli ni mikɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, cowpeas add nitrogen into the soil through their roots, which actually helps feed the maize. When spaced correctly, intercropping corn and beans maintains maize yield while providing an extra harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest grow weaker than new hybrid seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred for high vigor and yield in their first generation only. Replanting saved seeds causes genetic breakdown, resulting in weaker stalks, higher disease risk, and smaller ears.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛhe wa ni amɛwo klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha fɔmɔ nii afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Helai ahe oshara ni yaa hiɛ kɛ toi bibii

english: Why should I avoid burning all the cleared weeds and grass when preparing my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ ni mikɛshãa lɛ he beni misaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. Leaving cleared vegetation to rot naturally returns nutrients to the soil and helps keep the ground moist during dry spells.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning light yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua.

english: Is it good practice to leave cut weeds on top of the soil around my crops after weeding?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? Miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cut weeds on top of the soil acts as a protective blanket called mulch. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents new weed seeds from getting sunlight to sprout.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui heei ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to grow thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely between waterings, or when there are no bees around to pollinate them. Regular watering helps protect the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that dry out quickly under direct heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or forest trees to shelter them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ko kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my maize when the first rain of the season drops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain. Wait until the rain has soaked the soil at least finger-deep multiple times, ensuring there is enough stored moisture so your seeds do not dry up if the rain pauses.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ shii abɔ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Can I plant beans together on the same mound with my yam, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmei kome nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: You can plant them together safely. Beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which actually enriches the ground and helps your yam grow better.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii diɛŋtsɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide inside the center of my young maize leaves and eat them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks young maize plants. They hide deep in the plant leaf funnel, so checking your farm early allows you to apply recommended treatments like neem leaf extract or targeted sprays before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ. Akɛ amɛ tee tsei ahe baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo spot sprays awo mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my last maize harvest yield less than the packaged seeds I buy from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo mli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Agro-dealer seeds are often hybrid seeds carefully bred for high yields and disease resistance. When you plant saved seeds from a hybrid crop, those special traits break down, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Beni oduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ. Nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: If I harvest my okra pods today, how many days do I need to wait before picking new ones from the same plant?
ga: Kɛji mikpa okra ŋmeii ŋmɛnɛ Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mafo ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Okra plants produce new pods rapidly during warm weather. Picking mature pods every 2 to 3 days forces the plant to continuously produce fresh flowers and new pods instead of putting its energy into ripening old seeds.
ga: Gumbo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii heei oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli tsei ni eda lɛ daa gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aya nɔ awo fɔfɔi heei kɛ tsei heei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛwo dumɔwui momoi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why don't my cocoa trees produce ripe pods continuously every month of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ eyaaa nɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ daa nyɔŋ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally follow seasonal cycles triggered by rain and temperature changes. Flowering and pod development peak after the major rains, followed by periods of rest where the tree stores nutrients for the next cycle.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ be mli nibii ni nugbɔ kɛ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi kɛbaa lɛ asɛɛ. Fɔfɔi kɛ pod shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa sɛɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji hejɔɔmɔ be ni tso lɛ toɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛha sɛɛkuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause high stress in tomato plants, preventing successful pollination. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tomato tsei anɔ. ehaa pollination nyɛŋ aba mli Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination Tsei baashi fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi amli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava plants to spend their energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves above ground. For thick tubers, cassava needs balanced nutrients, particularly potassium, which directs growth into the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛha ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ, ŋmei he miihia niyenii ni sa. titri lɛ potassium ni baaha eda kɛya shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants take much longer to form ears when rain does not fall for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ toi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants rely on steady soil moisture to transport nutrients throughout the plant. When water is scarce, the plant slows down its metabolism and delays ear formation to save water for survival.
ga: Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Beni nu faaa Tsei lɛ haa amɛ niyenii ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛhaa toi lɛ afeemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning pale yellow after heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Excessive water can wash away soluble nitrogen from the topsoil and reduce oxygen levels around the roots. Without nitrogen and breathing roots, the plant cannot produce chlorophyll, making the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni ehaa oxygen ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi kɛji nitrogen bɛ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee chlorophyll. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune extra shoots growing around my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to yield heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sucker kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii aha.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight for food production while keeping them off damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant channel energy into developing bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce very few pods when planted directly under dense tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are sun-loving crops that require direct sunlight to make energy for flowering. Under deep shade, the plant puts all its limited energy into stretching its vines toward the light rather than forming flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu ni biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔi. Yɛ hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ shishi Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa ewein tso lɛ mli kɛyaa la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a viral infection spread by insects. These pests disrupt the leaf cells, causing the leaves to distort and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key plant nutrient needed for green leaves and strong growth. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist and the weather is cool. This prevents heat from burning the plants and helps the roots absorb the nutrients easily.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekashã tso lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves and tops of my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛyitsei anɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of the maize plant and eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential minerals like calcium.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛ́ sũ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds from my farm before I plant my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water away from your crops. Clearing them before planting gives your young crops a clean environment to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná shihilɛ ni mli tse ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yam plants need their leaves exposed to maximum sunlight to produce big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing rot and disease.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce smaller pods when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their branches block sunlight from each other and their roots fight over water and food in the soil, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsoi aniji haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is direct sunshine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shield them until they grow mature and tough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the midday heat, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to protect themselves and usually stand back up when the evening cools down.
ga: yɛ shwane mli Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe he be kukuoo ko, ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛte shi kɛ́ amɛhe jɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and begin falling off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ daraa beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or when water sits around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with small yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. They stretch upwards to catch light instead of using their energy to grow thick stems and healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the ground time to recover. It also allows pests and diseases that feed on cassava to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmei lɛ hu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground moist by slowing down evaporation under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why is it good for me to leave some big shade trees standing on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow best under forest canopy. Leaving large shade trees shields young cocoa from burning in direct sunlight, maintains air humidity, and protects soil moisture during dry seasons.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kooi lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for planting my maize after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: One quick rain is usually not enough because the heat will dry out the top layer fast. You should wait until rains become steady and moisten the soil to about the depth of your hand so the seeds do not dry up after germinating.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kuku kome pɛ faaa ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi fã lɛ gĩɔ oya. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ he ni onine shɛɔ he. Koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving powdery dirt inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing center of the maize plant during the day and chew on young leaves as they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni ekɛ baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the cocoa tree experiences water stress during dry spells, lacks key soil nutrients, or gets attacked by tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids that damage flower stems.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu mli nu lɛ, tamɔ ashwishwɛi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday sun, pepper leaves lose water through their leaves faster than roots can pull water up from the soil. Drooping is a natural defense to reduce exposure to the sun, and the plant usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ohiŋmɛii ni oootsi kɛjɛ ohe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni baaha hulu ni okɛkpeɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When persistent heavy rains soak the ground and leave it waterlogged, the water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing rot-causing microbes to multiply.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ tee nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni nu shwieɔ shi. Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii bibii ni kɛ rot hela baa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, a main food plants need to grow strong. When nitrogen is short, the plant moves what little it has to the new upper leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
