ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baa hee lɛ nɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and gives pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply in your field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa Na shia ni baahi shi daa kɛha fɔmɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why are small worms eating the heart of my young maize leaves and stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ tsui baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds inside the growing funnel of the plant. Spotting them early and applying safe control measures like neem oil or recommended sprays helps protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ tsei ni daraa lɛ anɔ. Ni ooona amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that grows in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air into your farm helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni ooofee koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaf, or from a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: How can I keep my soil moist for longer during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the dirt around your crop stems with dried grass or leaves—called mulching—blocks the sun from evaporating water out of the soil.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime heat is too intense, when water supply is irregular, or when there is a lack of bees or wind to shake the pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni baatswa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my watermelon fruits turn black and rot while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni edaa lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to dry soil or irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize for dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Maize is mature when the outer husks turn fully brown and dry, and a tiny black mark appears at the base of the grain where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa kwraa ni egbi. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I leave them past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are full of starch and water, making them easily attacked by rot-causing fungus when heavy rains make the soil waterlogged.
ga: Akɛ starch kɛ nu eyi cassava shishifãi amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when left directly under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings require shade because direct harsh sunlight overheats their tender leaves and scorches them before their root systems are mature enough to draw sufficient water.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baadɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ fe nine ni amɛshã amɛshishifãi lɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I leave openings for air to flow when I cover my seedling nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli beni mikɛhaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh air circulation prevents trapped heat build-up and reduces excess humidity, which stops fungal diseases from killing delicate young plants.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do we cover fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for several days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii heei anɔ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans traps the heat and moisture needed for proper fermentation, which breaks down the bean pulp and develops the rich chocolate flavor before drying.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa baa dani egbiɔ.

english: Plants curl their leaves during peak afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping them conserve internal moisture until temperatures drop.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni fɛ̃i lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it helpful to spread dried grass or leaves around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture, and protects crop roots from extreme sun heat.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi, ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I keep my nursery beds tightly sealed with thick plastic tarpaulin all day long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plastic tarp ni mli wa haaa gbekɛbii askul saatso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tightly sealing nursery beds prevents fresh oxygen from reaching the plants, which can cause seeds and young shoots to suffocate and rot from excess trapped heat.
ga: Tso lɛ mli saatso ni atsĩ naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ hee ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ babaoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too deep lack access to enough air and exhaust their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa he ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ waa dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow when the soil remains flooded with water for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil blocks oxygen from reaching plant roots, effectively drowning them and stopping them from taking up essential soil nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings grow tall, thin, and weak when kept under heavy tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: When shade is too dense, seedlings stretch aggressively upward searching for light, resulting in weak stems that easily break or fall over.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efoɔ loo egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do I need to remove weeds from around my young cassava plants as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi-cassava tsei bibii lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal water, sunlight, and plant food from young cassava crops, stunting root development during critical early growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ tsei niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow strong. It can also happen when too much water saturates the soil and starves the roots of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa babaoo koni enyɛ eda waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with plenty of big leaves, but when I harvest, the tubers underneath are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi beni mikpa bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, no mli lɛ eji bibioo kwraa?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of root expansion. Balanced soil nutrients and loose soil are necessary for big tubers to develop.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. yɛ shishifãi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ he miihia koni bulbs wuji lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cold, damp, and shaded conditions. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods helps control the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, edɔ, shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Sir, why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted and stunted?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies that suck the sap from the leaves and sometimes pass viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai amli nu ni bei komɛi lɛ ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei amli

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my maize and leaving saw-dust like dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Eyaa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ ŋmeii tamɔ muji yɛ ŋmãa lɛ yitsei lɛ amli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing point of the maize plant during the day and feed on young leaves, which requires early intervention with approved pesticides or neem extracts.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ he awo mli mra. kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when the weather gets extremely hot, or when the plant experiences water stress from irregular watering during the flowering period.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewɔ.

english: How come my plantain trees keep falling over just when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi lɛ? He ni jwɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, making them top-heavy when carrying heavy fruit. Root damage from tiny worms (nematodes) can also weaken their anchor, so propping the stems with strong wooden poles is essential.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ehaa efeɔ muji kɛ́ ootere aduawai ni tsii. Shishifãi ni ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei ni wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines, or can I just let them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso mli? Aloo obaanyɛ oha egbɛ eshwa hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Staking holds yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which directly fuels the growth of big tubers below ground. Leaving leaves on hot, damp soil increases the risk of leaf diseases.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ ŋtayaa mli koni hulu la lɛ aná babaoo. ni haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ashi baai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa helai baa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to keep big trees scattered on cocoa farms instead of clearing every tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ mɛi hewalɛ ni adu kookoo tsei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie tso fɛɛ tso lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive in forest environments where shade protects young pods from direct heat stress, prevents moisture loss, and reduces attacks from major pests like capsids.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo mli shihilɛi amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa koni ebu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni he hiaa tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuamɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during dry spells even when I gave them plenty of water a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miha amɛ nu babaoo gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ.

english: Sandy soil loses water very quickly because it cannot hold onto moisture for long. Adding organic matter like animal manure or compost helps the soil act like a sponge and hold water near the crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya waa ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji ni ehiɛɔ nu yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, erratic watering, or poor soil nutrients, causing the plant to save its energy by shedding blossoms instead of making peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ kɛjɛ latsaa he haomɔ mli. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ha tsei lɛ akwɛ hewalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee chili.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions, especially when air cannot flow freely through overgrown tree branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni edara fe nine lɛ amli oya.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is worn out and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, remain short, have pale yellow leaves, and produce smaller yields than in past seasons, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo waa, eyɛ kuku lolo, ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ewoɔ yibii fioo fe nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater cannot drain away, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that soft-rot fungi need to destroy the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni anyɛɛɛ ajie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni soft rot fungi he hiaa koni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam mounds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting yam mounds too close together forces the crop vines to block each other's sunlight and cause the underground roots to compete for soil nutrients, which leaves you with very small tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha wain tsei lɛ atsĩ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ Enɛ baaha oná yitso bibioo waa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow, weak root systems and very heavy tops, which makes them unstable and easy for strong winds to uproot if they are not propped up or protected by windbreak trees.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa. Enɛ haaa ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baafo lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ fiii esɛɛ loo ebuuu he.

english: Why do weeds reduce the amount of groundnuts I get at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nourishment directly from your groundnut plants, while also physically blocking the flowering stems from pushing down into the soil to form pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-peanut tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What quick crops can I plant to earn income while waiting for my new cocoa trees to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu oya koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei heei akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like plantains, cassava, and vegetables grow quickly to provide fast income while also acting as useful shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from the harsh sun.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains, cassava kɛ aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni ekɛ shika aba oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ hulutsoo be ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why does my maize produce small cobs when I plant it under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight all day long to manufacture its food. Big trees block the light and drink up the water and nutrients that the maize needs to form large, full cobs.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni ená niyenii. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni abele afee ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: When the soil gets flooded with water, the plant roots cannot breathe or take up nutrients like nitrogen from the ground, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under strong sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ baafee blɛoo ni amɛbaashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: You will notice ragged holes eaten into young leaves and dark green droppings clustered inside the center funnel of the growing maize plant.
ga: Obaana buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni aye yɛ baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the ground to be wet before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it; putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots and waste the nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a widespread virus carried by tiny whiteflies that prevents the plant from growing big cassava roots underneath.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Why shouldn't I bury my maize seeds very deep in the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they use up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil to reach light and may rot or die before sprouting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ koni amɛná la lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ egbo loo egbo dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside the tomato flowers, which prevents fertilization, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. ni tsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as natural food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds saved from last year's harvest yield less food than fresh certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli hewalɛ faaa fe dumɔwui heei ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid crop seeds lose their special strength and high-yield qualities after the first season, so planting saved seeds results in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Hybrid tsei dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why is it important to weed my farm early during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ani ehe hiaa?

english: Young crop shoots are fragile and will lose the battle against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food, leading to permanent stunting if weeds aren't cleared early.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaaye ta ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ daa kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ mra.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients or getting too much water around their roots. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my cassava stems when planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu?

english: Leaving about one meter between cassava plants gives their roots enough underground space to expand into big tubers without fighting each other for soil food, water, and sunlight.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my cabbage leaves, and what is causing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ Ni mɛni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa?

english: Holes on cabbage leaves are usually eaten by small green caterpillars like diamondback moth larvae. Spraying neem tree leaf extract or using safe crop protection early in the morning stops them from destroying the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli, tamɔ diamondback moth lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ cabbage baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe wo ohe leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni neem baa lɛ akafite.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out very quickly even after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter or high sand content cannot hold water easily. Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass (mulching) and mixing compost into the soil helps hold moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔji ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ loo ŋã babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them acts like an umbrella, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry weather, or uneven watering. Regular watering at the base of the plant during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishi daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my pepper seeds taking so long to sprout out of the ground after sowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have tough skins and need constant moisture and warm soil to wake up, which can take two to three weeks. Keeping the nursery bed damp every day speeds up their germination.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baanyɛ ahe otsii fioo komɛi. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ edɔ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong roots that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny prevents them from choking your crops and stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni wa waa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafo oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛkaju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of bushy leaves, but the potatoes underground are very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes sweet potatoes spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of tubers below. Using fertilizers richer in potassium encourages the plant to grow big, heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha sweet potatoes lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I start a small vegetable farm if I have very little money to buy expensive chemicals and tools?
ga: Mi baaje aduawai ŋmɔ bibioo ko shishi. Te kɛji akɛ miyɛ shika fioo ko pɛ ni mikɛbaahe tsofai kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ni jara wa hu?

english: You can start small by clearing a simple plot with a hoe, using free animal manure to enrich the soil, and planting hardy seeds like okra or pepper that yield quickly and bring early returns on small investment.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ko ni okɛ ŋmei baatsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ kooloo ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni odu dumɔwui ni wa tamɔ okra loo pepper ni woɔ yibii oya kɛ shika fioo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli nyɔmɔwoo oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade trees because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root system is deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I loosen the soil deep underground before planting instead of just clearing the surface weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mifo shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ dani midu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows young plant roots to penetrate deep into the earth easily, giving them better access to underground moisture and stored nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants automatically draw stored nitrogen from older leaves to keep new leaves growing, showing that your field needs fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai heei. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout or die soon after I apply chemical fertilizer directly into the planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ loo amɛgbooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo dumɔ bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed too close to a seed burns the tender young roots as they try to emerge. Fertilizer should always be placed a few centimeters away from the seed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo dumɔwu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi bibii lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛje kpo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the afternoon sun even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The leaves wilt temporarily to save moisture and will bounce back once temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni efoɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too high or water supply is irregular, as the plant tries to save energy rather than support new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ bɔ ni sa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ aduawai heei.

english: Why do my crops stop growing quickly whenever I delay clearing weeds for even two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni mafo jwɛi lɛ ashwiemɔ mli kɛyashi otsii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the inner leaves of my young maize plants filled with holes and small dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, hiding inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant where they eat new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil. Trapped water suffocates the tubers and creates ideal conditions for fungal rots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing smaller and lighter bunches of fruit every new year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni waaa daa afi hee lɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it produces multiple young suckers around its base. If you do not cut back excess suckers, they compete with the main tree for nutrients, leading to smaller fruit.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaawo ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ eshishigbɛ he kɛji ofolɔko ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why does spraying chemical pesticides on my cocoa trees during the dry season burn their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa kookoo baa lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: During the dry season, cocoa trees are already stressed from a lack of water. Applying chemicals in hot, dry weather causes the water in the spray to evaporate rapidly, leaving high concentrations of chemicals on the leaves that scorch them and weaken the tree.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ haoɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya. Eshiɔ tsofai babaoo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni shãa tso lɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if agrochemicals arrive late after the rainy season has ended?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ agrochemicals lɛ bashɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: When chemicals arrive late after the rains end, cocoa trees have already entered a dry survival state. Spraying them during this period causes severe stress, often making flowers and young pods drop off prematurely, which reduces your total harvest.
ga: Beni tsofai baashɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Cocoa tso lɛ hu ebote hɔmɔ shihilɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Bei pii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Is it safe for me to spray my cocoa farm when the dry Harmattan wind is blowing?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi miitswa kɛmiijɛ Harmattan lɛ?

english: No, spraying during Harmattan winds is risky. Strong dry winds carry the chemical drift away from your target crop onto unintended areas, and the extreme dryness causes cocoa leaves to absorb harsh chemical drops too quickly, resulting in leaf burn.
ga: Dabi, shwiemɔ yɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ yɛ oshara. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ woɔ tsofai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hei ni esaaa. Ni ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine lɛ haa kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa.

english: What should I do if my government spraying chemicals arrive when the weather is already very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nɔyeli lɛ shwie tsofai anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ momo lɛ?

english: Do not spray immediately during the hottest part of the day. You should consult your extension officer, spray only in the cool early morning or late afternoon, or safely adjust the dilution so the hot sun does not turn the chemical into a severe burn hazard for your trees.
ga: Kaashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Esa akɛ oyabi mɔ ni kwɛɔ bo nɔ lɛ. Okɛshwie nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso pɛ. loo dilute safely Enɛ baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akahã otsei lɛ ashã tsofa ni naa wa.

english: Why do cocoa trees shed their leaves after being sprayed in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛshwie amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf shedding is a natural defense mechanism. When a tree experiences double stress from drought and hot chemical spray, it drops leaves to save precious water and keep its main trunk and roots alive.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he haomɔ ni ji shii enyɔ kpe lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu ni jara wa lɛ he. ni okwɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do young cocoa pods wither and turn black after dry season chemical spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ beni akɛ tsofa eshwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young pods have thin, delicate skin. High temperatures combined with strong chemical spray break down this protective layer and drain moisture out of the pod, causing it to dry up and die before maturing.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni waaa. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ ni ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: How does intense afternoon sun affect the chemicals I spray on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ saa tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Intense heat and direct sun break down chemical compounds rapidly, making them less effective at killing pests while simultaneously accelerating spray evaporation, which concentrates the chemical on leaves and burns them.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbemɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshãa amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree leaves are suffering from chemical damage or a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai efite mi-kokoo baai lɛ loo tso hela ko yɛ amɛhe?

english: Chemical damage appears rapidly—usually within 1 to 2 days after spraying—as widespread brown, dry patches on all sprayed leaves. Disease symptoms typically develop slowly over weeks and spread gradually from branch to branch.
ga: Tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa oya—bei pii lɛ, yɛ gbii 1 kɛyashi 2 mli yɛ be mli ni afɔse tsofa lɛ sɛɛ—tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni egbi yɛ baai fɛɛ ni afɔse tsofa lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ he okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo fiofio. Yɛ otsii babaoo mli ni egbɛ eshwa fiofio kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe nine kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day to apply spray chemicals on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: The ideal time is early morning (between 6:00 AM and 8:30 AM) or late afternoon. During these hours, temperatures are cooler and humidity is higher, allowing the leaves to safely absorb the treatment without burning.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ji leebi maŋkpa (yɛ 6:00 AM kɛ 8:30 AM teŋ) loo shwane mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees nearby when chemical treatments are applied?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii?

english: Shade trees lower the temperature on your cocoa farm and keep the air humid. This reduces heat stress on the cocoa trees, making them much stronger and less likely to suffer leaf burn when chemical sprays are applied.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ okkoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni baa cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ ahe wa waa, ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, enyɛŋ ekɛ baai lɛ ashã.

english: How can a crop disease move across my field if plants cannot walk around?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya he fɛɛ he?

english: Crop diseases move through tiny spores or germs carried on your boots, cutlasses, farming clothes, soil on your hands, water runoff, or by insects. Cleaning yourself and your tools prevents you from carrying sickness from one plant to another.
ga: Tse helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii anɔ. No ŋmɛɔ atadei, dadei, okwaayeli atadei, muji ni yɔɔ oniji anɔ, nu ni hoɔ, loo kooloi bibii anɔ. Ohe kɛ onitsumɔ dadei lɛ ahe ni oootsumɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Should I wash my cutlass and farm boots before going into a healthy crop field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-daggers kɛ mi-boots lɛ he dani maya okwaayeli ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, dirty cutlasses and soil stuck to your boots carry crop diseases and worm eggs from infected areas. Washing your tools and boots with clean water and soap stops you from infecting healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, muji ni afo kɛ muji ni kpɛtɛɔ o-boots lɛ he lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla tsu onitsumɔ dadei kɛ o-boots lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ hela akatswa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on plant sap. Using disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers prevents this sickness from destroying your harvest.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni yeɔ tso mli nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my tomato plants to droop and dry up suddenly even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often bacterial or fungal wilt caused by small germs living in the soil that block water movement inside the stem. Rotating your tomato crops with maize or grass crops prevents these germs from building up in your land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ muawai bibii amli kɛbaa. ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa Tomato ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa loo jwɛi tsei tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ akabua amɛhe naa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to heat and burn under harsh sunlight. Plantain trees or shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing the damp shade and cool climate young cocoa plants need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are starving for food, particularly nitrogen, or that their roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Applying well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores nutrients so the leaves can turn green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo afu amɛshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and very small cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets full sunlight and enough food to grow large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmãa toi wuji akwɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting yams on the exact same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Planting yams continuously exhausts the specific nutrients yams need and allows yam pests and rot-causing soil germs to multiply in that spot. Moving yams to new ground allows the soil to recover and starves the pests.
ga: Atomɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa sweet potato mli helai kɛ sũ mli helai ni fiteɔ lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii kɛtee he ko hee lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: How do weeds growing near my vegetables harm my crops besides taking up space?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛfata he ni amɛheɔ he ko lɛ he?

english: Weeds steal water and soil nutrients away from your crops and serve as safe hiding spots for harmful insects and plant diseases. Keeping your field weed-free reduces pest attacks and gives crops full access to soil moisture.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli, ni efeɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why is it helpful to trim off the lower leaves touching the soil on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves stops soil-borne disease germs from splashing onto the plant during heavy rain and allows fresh air to blow through the leaves, keeping the plant dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli Ha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I start my seed crops in a nursery first instead of planting them directly in my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Tiny seeds like tomatoes and peppers are very delicate; a nursery acts like a protected baby room that shelters them from heavy rain, pests, and harsh sun until they are strong enough to survive in the open farm.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa. Gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbekɛbii atsu ni abuɔ he ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my crop seedlings in the nursery are ready to be moved to the main farm area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting when they have grown 3 to 4 strong leaves and reach about the height of your index finger, which usually takes 3 to 4 weeks after sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ 3 kɛyashi 4 ni amɛlɛɛmɔ ji aaafee inchi kome. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie wooden stakes to my tomato plants while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fĩɔ tomato tsei ahe beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Staking keeps tomato leaves and heavy fruits off the wet ground, which prevents fruit rot and fungal diseases while allowing the leaves to capture maximum sunlight.
ga: Staking baatsi tomato tsei kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ aduawai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden poles instead of spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food; keeping the leaves high off the ground prevents leaf diseases and directs the plant's energy into growing big tubers under the soil.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ tee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ahe helai anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is the importance of clearing weeds and bushes from my land before planting my crops?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ha tɛŋŋ akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Clearing removes aggressive weeds that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops, giving your young plants a clean environment to establish strong roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni baa shi ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi ni baa shi lɛ. Ha odumɔwui lɛ shihilɛ ni mli tse koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the grass and bushes after clearing my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and useful soil organisms, whereas allowing cleared plant material to rot on the farm feeds the soil and helps keep it moist during dry days.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I plan my farm so I have enough food for my family while still making money at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni maná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni mináa shika kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: You can divide your land by growing fast food staples like cassava or maize for house meals, alongside cash-earning crops like vegetables that sell quickly at the local market.
ga: Obaanyɛ oja shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni oooye yɛ shia lɛ nɔ. Kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shika baa tamɔ aduawai, ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani mikɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables spoil fast if harvested in the hot afternoon heat or bruised during transport; picking them early in the morning and keeping them in a cool, shaded place keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Aduawai fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa loo kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala amɛ leebi maŋkpa ni okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water stays on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe; when soil stays flooded, the roots choke and cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow from lack of food.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miifite dani eda ni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer stress from heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to grow leaves instead of developing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miipiŋ amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land instead of just planting one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ kome pɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together is called intercropping. Maize grows quickly and can be harvested in a few months for quick food or income, while cassava grows slowly over a full year. This allows you to maximize your limited land and get two harvests from the same space.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ akɛ intercropping. Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli kɛha niyenii loo shika ni anáa oya. Beni ŋmei daa fiofio yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo ni onáa ŋmãa enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: How do I choose between buying improved seed varieties or using saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ ahemɔ loo dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Saved seeds are free, but they tend to produce smaller yields and are more easily damaged by pests over time. Improved seeds cost money upfront, but they are bred to resist local diseases, withstand drought, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ aheee nɔ ko. Shi amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ amɛ oya yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ biɔ ni awo he nyɔmɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Shi atsɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ anɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa

english: How can I tell if a piece of land I want to farm has good soil for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni matsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nɔ?

english: Good soil for maize is dark in color, crumbly to the touch, and retains moisture without turning into heavy mud. Dark soil contains rich organic matter from decayed leaves, which feeds maize plants so they grow tall and produce large ears.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji ni tsii Sũ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni jɛɔ baai ni egboi amli lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛwo toi wuji.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food is left in its older lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young upper leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyakwɛ ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra branches from your cocoa trees lets in sunlight and air movement, which dries out the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kookoo tso niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha nu ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, dry soil, or poor nutrition. Providing steady moisture and mulching around the roots helps cool the soil and protects the flowers so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have naturally adapted to local soils over many years. They grow aggressively to steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil before your farm crops have time to establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool while the cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling inward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defence mechanism tomatoes use to protect themselves from losing water during intense heat. By rolling up their leaves, they reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to survive until temperatures cool down.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni tomato kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting in the storage barn after just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvesting or kept in a hot room without fresh air. Storing yams on raised racks inside a well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them cool and dry, preventing rot-causing germs from taking hold.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Sweet potatoes ni akɛtoɔ shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha edɔ ni egbi. Etsiɔ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool while your young cocoa plants get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ be mli ni o-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Which direction should I plant my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You must plant cassava cuttings with the growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for stems to sprout, leading to weak growth and lower root yields.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni odu yucca tso lɛ nine ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the wet ground and lifts them into direct sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture more energy, which leads to larger, healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni ewo nɔ kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field improve my soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When left in the ground, they naturally fertilize the soil for other crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to dry soil conditions. Watering your plants consistently allows them to pull up calcium from the ground smoothly.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop early when plants face heat stress, lack of water, or over-fertilization. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants light shade during mid-day heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha tso lɛ ná hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out seeds or kill newly sprouted seedlings before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, be kuku ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui agbi loo efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my garden reduce the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow strong. Leaving weeds in your farm starves your main crops, causing small plants and low harvest yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, fɛ̃i, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How can I prevent insects from eating up my stored maize after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni ato yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ensure your maize is dried completely in the sun before storage, as weevils multiply quickly in damp grain. Storing dry maize in airtight bags prevents insects from getting inside and destroying your stored crop.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ faa oya yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi wo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi akabote mli ni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the cocoa seedlings until they are strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant maize and beans together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa?

english: Yes, planting maize and beans together helps both crops. Beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while maize stalks give bean vines support to climb, allowing you to harvest two different crops from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bean wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plant the essential nutrients it needs to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when water sits around the roots for too long in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering. Providing consistent water and light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji haomɔ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be Nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning twisted like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or by a viral infection spread by these pests. Managing insects early prevents leaf damage and stops viruses from spreading across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Mra be mli kooloi ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I select the right yam seed sets so that my farm produces large tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato dumɔwui ni sa koni miŋmɔ lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji?

english: To grow large yam tubers, choose seed sets from healthy, high-yielding vines that show no signs of rot, holes, or disease spots. Clean seed pieces give the young shoot plenty of stored energy to develop a strong root system.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ sweet potato tubers wuji Halamɔ dumɔwui akui kɛjɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ejieee ŋmeii, bu loo helai ahe okadi ko kpo lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ato koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear and weed my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in the soil for years and sprout as soon as clearing exposes them to sunlight and rainwater. Covering the soil with a layer of dry mulch blocks sunlight and stops weed seeds from germinating easily.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my young maize crop, and how can I stop it?
ga: Bu bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Small holes inside the funnel of young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. Inspecting crops weekly and applying approved organic bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnels keeps the caterpillars from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa. Otsi fɛɛ otsi ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli kɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmeii lɛ ayitsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle properly before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rainfall is risky because the soil can quickly dry up during subsequent hot days, killing germinating seeds. Waiting until rains are regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow roots safely.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ ni efiteɔ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ atswa shishifãi shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the farm and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans pull natural plant food called nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the maize and keeps your soil healthy for longer.
ga: Beans gbalaa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the shade and coolness they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps water so you water less often, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akafɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry hot spell that can dry out and kill delicate young sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ ni egbeɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ asɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more food the plant makes to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ náa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa fioo ko kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight each other for plant food and water in the soil, while their leaves fight for sunlight, making every plant grow weak.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná tsei niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes completely dry, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms before the fruit can start growing.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii eba lɛ Kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani aduawai aba.
