english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves, or a plant disease spread by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo mites, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei ahe helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their soft leaves from intense heat and soil drying out. Clearing all large trees exposes them to harsh sunlight, causing them to scorch and die before their root system is fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ he. Tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa waa aba tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shãa ni egboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight and away from wet soil. More sunlight exposure helps the leaves produce energy, which directly increases the size and weight of the tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ hulu la mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ akabɔ he. Hulu la babaoo ni anáa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ adaramɔ kɛ amɛhewalɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain and wind just when the fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ewo yibii pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles supports the extra weight so winds do not uproot them.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ panicle ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni fata he lɛ sɛɛ. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why does my cassava drop all its leaves during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ fite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Your cassava is not dying; it naturally sheds leaves during dry periods to conserve water. As soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue growing its underground roots.
ga: O cassava ɔ gbo we lolo. Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: Why do so many of the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees produce many more flowers than they can support with food and water. The tree naturally drops unpollinated or weak flowers so it can direct its energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu aye abua amɛ. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ lɛ afee ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decay in the ground, they release free fertilizer into the soil that nourishes the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and improves ear size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa toi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your crops consistently prevents the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves are caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from the underside of leaves. Applying safe insecticidal soap or neem oil spray removes the pests so flat leaves can grow back.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like someone shot holes through them with chewed saw-dust inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko efo bu ni ekɛ ŋmeii efo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the growing shoot. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended pest controls protects the central stem from destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe ŋaawoo lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs or no harvest at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii waa loo akpaaa nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to direct all its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the cassava plant is hungry for key soil nutrients like nitrogen. Even with enough water, plants need food from fertile soil or fertilizer to keep their leaves green and grow healthy roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ po. Tsei hu he miihia shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the dirt so roots stay cool during hot weather. It also blocks weeds from growing and turns into rich soil food as it decays.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests naturally lose their vigor and produce smaller yields each season. Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, withstand dry spells, and yield far more grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do my weeds grow so much faster than the tomato seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe tomato dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants that are naturally adapted to grab sunlight, water, and soil food much faster than farm crops. If they are not cleared early, they will crowd out your tomatoes and starve them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛji akɛ ajieee mra lɛ, Tomatoi lɛ baawo mli ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my maize leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms miifite mi-corn baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths fly into fields at night and lay hundreds of eggs under the leaves. Once hatched, the caterpillars feed constantly and hide deep inside the center of the leaf whorl where they are hard to spot initially.
ga: Autumn caterpillar ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai ashishi. Beni ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ewa akɛ aaana amɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black spots and rot when the weather is very humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves allow fungal diseases, such as late blight, to spread rapidly from leaf to leaf. The fungus chokes the plant's internal sap flow, causing leaves and fruit to blacken and decay.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ blight, gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. Fuji lɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ehaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa saplings burning and curling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitso ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them, the intense heat dries out their delicate leaves faster than the roots can drink water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni akɛbu he lɛ bɛ lɛ, tsei ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baagbi amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat or water stress. To save its own life, the plant sheds its flowers so it doesn't waste energy trying to grow fruit during tough weather conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala Bɔni afee ni ekafite hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for plant growth. As the plant grows, it pulls stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, signaling that the crop needs fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Egbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small green pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: This early pod loss is called cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree lacks enough nutrients or water to support all its pods, or when small insects like mirids bite the young pods and damage them.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mra nɛɛ akɛ cherel wilt. Ebaa beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi lɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids lɛ ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from the swollen tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and split instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbala yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend or split when they hit hard, compacted soil or underground stones as they expand. Softening the soil deeply and building high, loose mounds or ridges allows the tuber to grow straight down without resistance.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baabɔle loo ebaagbala kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ beni amɛmli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ blɛoo waa ni afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers but no actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi pepper diɛŋtsɛ ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off without forming fruit when temperatures become too high or when there are not enough insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow lots of leafy vines but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air. If you add too much nitrogen fertilizer to the soil, the plant uses all its energy to grow heavy green leaves instead of making flowers and bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The plant wilts on purpose to shrink its leaves and save water, then recovers in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaahã baai lɛ afee bibioo ni amɛbu nu lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my rice plants fall flat on the ground just when the grains start filling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛbɔi dumɔwui ayimɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over, or 'lodge,' when their stems are too thin and weak to carry the heavy grain heads. This usually happens if seeds were planted too closely together or if too much nitrogen fertilizer was applied late in the season.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo ‘efoɔ’ kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm cause my young maize to stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-abele bibioo lɛ feɔ gbekɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your maize needs to grow. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa bo koni o-abele lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical medicine to mix for spraying my crops so I do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite lɛ?

english: Crop chemicals work just like human medicine and require precise measurements. Using too much can burn crop roots and leaves, while using too little makes the treatment ineffective against pests.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adesa tsofai ni ebiɔ susumɔ ni ja. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ he.

english: Why is it dangerous to mix two different farm chemicals together if the containers do not say to do so?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ baafutu kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ afee nakai lɛ?

english: Combining chemicals without instructions can cause a reaction that ruins their effectiveness, produces fumes that harm your health, or creates a strong mixture that damages your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfataa he ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni fiteɔ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ aba. Ejieɔ lasu ni yeɔ ohewalɛ nɔ awui. loo ofee nibii ni mli wa ni fiteɔ onibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade plants like plantains to protect them and keep the soil moist until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp weather. Excess moisture on the pods allows the fungus to spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to turn yellow and curl up?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies are feeding on the plant or spreading a plant virus, or that the soil is low in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ miiye tso lɛ loo amɛmiigbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ nɔ. loo etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. If they are not removed early, they steal the food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛji ajieee amɛ mra lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my farm even after I spray my crops properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Pests can easily fly or crawl over from nearby farms that were not sprayed. If surrounding farm owners do not spray at the same time, pests will shelter there and return to your crops later.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afã loo amɛfo kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni afɔɔɔ amɛ tsofa lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmɔtsɛmɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Kaafɔ yɛ be kome mli. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baahi jɛmɛ ni sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba onibii amli.

english: Why does my maize produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight over the limited food and water in the soil, preventing the plants from getting enough nourishment to form big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni faaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra unneeded branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Extra branches, often called chupons, consume the tree's food and energy without producing good fruit. Cutting them off allows the tree to focus its energy on growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fata he, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ chupons lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko kwraa haaa. Kpojiemɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize in the same field without harming the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is helpful because beans trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as natural food for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees protect the young plants from drying out and burning, acting as a shield until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkashã. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa ni ewaɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How long will I have to wait for my new oil palm trees to start giving me fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni ŋmei tso hee ko aje yibiiwoo shishi beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Oil palm trees generally take between three to four years after planting to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches, requiring continuous care and weeding in the early years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ dani amɛkpaa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the soil has become waterlogged, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or during heavy rains, which stops the flowers from pollinating properly and forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems with very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important for me to spread dry leaves around the base of my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi ashwie mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Okɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why should I prune or trim off some branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches directs the plant's energy away from making leaves and forces it into growing larger, healthier peppers.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni ekɛbaa lɛ mli. ni enyɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my cassava help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like cassava.
ga: Peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid planting yam on the exact same plot of land two years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Planting yam repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil nutrients yam needs to grow, while allowing pests and root diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Sweet potato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa sweet potato lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does leaving weeds on my cassava farm slow down the growth of the tubers underground?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ aba tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal the soil's moisture and plant food, leaving cassava roots starved and preventing them from expanding into thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping the soil moist and protecting the seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves toward the sun so they can make food for the plant, while also keeping leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal leaves and roots from rotting.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni anyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ŋmeii akafite baai lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth found in manure or fertilizers. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating the central leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: This damage is often caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides in the center funnel of young maize plants to feed on soft new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How can I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top, and when the base of the stem swells up thick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. kɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ fũuɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a sudden lack of water, causing it to discard blossoms to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashwie fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under leaves and suck out juices, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: The first rain usually cools down dry land temporarily without wetting the soil deep enough. If a long dry period follows, germinated seeds will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa hei ni egbi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji ashi ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does adding animal manure help my crops grow bigger fruits than planting in untreated soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa fe shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds beneficial soil organisms and slowly releases essential nutrients while holding moisture around crop roots for a longer time.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã ji niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha wala yibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni fiofio lɛ ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your crops, leaving less energy for your crops to grow healthy roots and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai.

english: What actually happens to my maize plants when I apply chemical fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer provides concentrated plant food containing key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Nitrogen helps the leaves grow dark green and lush, phosphorus builds strong roots, and potassium helps the plant resist drought and produce full, heavy grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni tsiimɔ fa.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and bushy after fertilizing, but sometimes fail to bear heavy fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ? Shi bei komɛi lɛ, etsuuu nii waa nakai?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus or potassium, they put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of flowers and fruits. Plants need a balanced mix of nutrients to produce heavy yields rather than just tall leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tsei amli ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai ŋmeii yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei koni amɛwo yibii babaoo moŋ fe baai kakadaji kɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops after I put fertilizer in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, quick-growing root systems that consume water and fertilizer nutrients faster than your main crops can. If you do not clear weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will swallow up the food and outgrow your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa ni kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii oya fe otso titri lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii lɛ ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend spraying chemical medicine on cocoa trees before the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afɔse tsofai yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and humidity create damp conditions where fungal diseases like black pod spread rapidly. Spraying protective fungicide medicine before the rainy season coats the pods in a shield that stops disease spores from taking hold.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo baa. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya Tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akɛshwieɔ shi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe, ni ehaa gbɛtsii nii ko baa koni hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai akakpɛtɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my crops are being eaten by insects or if they are sick from a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii eye miŋmɔshi nibii loo tso hela ko miiye amɛ?

english: Insect attacks usually leave visible physical damage, such as chewed holes in leaves, rolled leaves, or bite marks on stems. Plant diseases usually show up as discoloration, brown or yellow spots, rotting stems, or sudden wilting without visible insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni anaa lɛ yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ bu ni atswa yɛ baai amli, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmɔtɔ he okadii yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jieɔ amɛhe kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. tso ni egbo loo ni egbo trukaa ni anaaa kooloi bibii

english: Can applying too much crop medicine or fertilizer actually damage my plants instead of helping them?
ga: Ani tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye mitsei lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes. Applying too much fertilizer or agrochemical can burn the roots and leaves of plants. High concentrations of chemical salts draw water out of the plant roots, causing the leaves to dry up, turn brown, and potentially kill the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo agrochemicals tsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai. Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli, ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale green or yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is exhausted of essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks nutrients, the plant cannot produce chlorophyll, which is what keeps leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ nitrogen, nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do some fertilizers need to be buried in the soil near the roots instead of just thrown on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi awo sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni aaashɛrɛ ashwie sũ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Some fertilizers evaporate quickly into the air when exposed to direct sun and wind. Burying the fertilizer under a thin layer of soil keeps the nutrients trapped where root systems can easily drink them up without loss.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ́ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ bibioo ko shishi Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ oya ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl in the bright afternoon heat but stand straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane latsaa be lɛ mli lɛ? Shi edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the dry soil. Curling or drooping reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the sun to save water, and the plant recovers once the temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ ebɔle ehe loo egbee shi lɛ, ebaa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: How does spraying crop medicine directly onto leaves protect the rest of the plant underground?
ga: Te tso tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ abu tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Certain crop medicines are systemic, meaning the plant absorbs the chemical through its leaves and circulates it through its sap down to the roots and stems. When insects bite any part of the plant, they consume the medicine and die.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ tsofa lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛtsɔɔ nu lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ tso lɛ fã ko Ebaaŋɔ tsofa lɛ ni egbo.

english: What is that strange green plant growing directly on my cocoa branches that I didn't plant?
ga: tso eŋɔli ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Mɛni miida tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mi kookoo nine lɛ nɔ ni miduuu lɛ?

english: That plant is called mistletoe. It is a parasite that attaches its roots inside your cocoa branch and steals the water and nutrients that your tree needs to grow and produce pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tso lɛ akɛ mistletoe. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa kookoo niji ahe ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: How does mistletoe end up on the high branches of my cocoa trees in the first place?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mistletoe lɛ ba naagbee yɛ mi-cocoa tso lɛ niji kakadaji lɛ anɔ yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Birds eat the sticky berries from mistletoe plants on other trees and drop the seeds onto your cocoa branches when they land. The seeds stick to the bark, sprout, and start growing into the tree.
ga: Okpoi yeɔ tsei ayibii ni shwieɔ shi ni jɛɔ mistletoe ni yɔɔ tsei krokomɛi anɔ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ kookoo niji anɔ beni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he, ekwɛ̃ɔ, ni ebɔi dalɛ ni etsɔ tsei.

english: Can mistletoe actually kill my cocoa tree if I leave it alone?
ga: Ani mistletoe baanyɛ agbe mi-cacao tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mishi amɛ?

english: Yes, if left unchecked, mistletoe can grow into a huge plant that steals too much food and blocks sunlight, eventually causing the cocoa tree branches to die and lowering the tree's lifespan.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ Mistletoe nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eda ni etsɔ tso agbo ko ni juɔ niyenii babaoo ni tsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa yɛ naagbee lɛ, kookoo niji lɛ gboiɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ wala be baa shi.

english: If I just pluck off the leaves of the mistletoe, will that stop it from growing back?
ga: Kɛ mifolɔ mistletoe tso lɛ baai lɛ Ani ebaakpa shweremɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: No, plucking only the leaves leaves the mistletoe roots embedded inside the cocoa bark, so it will grow back quickly. You must cut off the mistletoe right at its base where it joins the tree, or remove that small branch completely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha mistletoe shishifãi lɛ ahi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ ebaada oya. Osumɔɔ ni ofo mistletoe lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ he ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Aloo ŋɔɔ nine bibioo ko No fɛɛ eje kpo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut branches off my healthy-looking cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted branches, known as pruning, removes dead wood, useless shoots, and mistletoe. This allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree, encouraging more flower and pod growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ akɛ pruning. Abaajie tsei ni egboi lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii kɛ mistletoe ni he ehiaaa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: When is the best time of year for me to prune my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mafo kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best time to prune cocoa is right after the main harvest season, usually around April to June before the heavy rains start, so the tree can direct its energy into new, healthy shoots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo kookoo ji yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛyashi June mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jeɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ saji heei ni mli wa.

english: Why is it recommended to hire trained labor to prune my cocoa trees instead of doing it all myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ aŋɔ nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛfolɔ cacao tsei lɛ moŋ fe ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaafee fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trained pruners have specialized tools like long-handled pruners to safely reach tall mistletoes without damaging the main trunk or flower cushions, saving you time and protecting your yield.
ga: Mɛi ni atsɔse amɛ ni amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ yɛ dɛŋdadei krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ tso ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni akɛ niji kakadaŋŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ, koni amɛkɛshɛ mistletoe tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo fɔfɔi lɛ akushin lɛ. Ekɛ be baa shi ni ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods this season even though the trees look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ?

english: Your tree might be feeding unneeded extra branches or parasites like mistletoe. When nutrients are diverted away from flower cushions to feed parasitic plants, pod yields drop significantly.
ga: Ekolɛ otso lɛ miiye tsei tsei krokomɛi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mistletoe niyenii ni he ehiaaa. Enɛ ji be mli ni ajieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi akushɛi amli koni akɛha tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ niyenii. Pod yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How does clearing mistletoe and overgrown branches help me make more money from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mistletoe kɛ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Removing mistletoe ensures that all the fertilizer and soil nutrients go directly into forming bigger, heavier cocoa pods, giving you a higher total harvest to sell.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie mistletoe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into pods when the top of the tree is very thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli etse waa?

english: A bushy tree top blocks sunlight and traps moisture, creating humidity that causes flowers to rot. Opening the canopy through pruning lets light in so flowers can develop into pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yiteŋ ji jwɛi ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa fɛ̃i baa ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ agbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha la abote mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ fɔfɔi baanyɛ atsɔ pods.

english: Why is it important for me to make my field flat and even before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee ŋmɔ lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ dani madu nii po lɛ?

english: Level ground ensures that rainwater spreads evenly across your farm instead of pooling in low spots or washing away topsoil, helping every crop get an equal amount of water and nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ebaafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does breaking up hard ground help my young crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni migbala lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Breaking hard soil loosens the earth so soft tender roots can push deep into the ground to find water, while also letting air and rain soak in more easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akumɔɔ lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ boteɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why are my root crops like cassava growing small and crooked in some parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: When the soil is too hard and tightly packed, roots cannot expand freely. Loosening hard ground allows root crops to swell evenly and grow large.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Can a hard crust on top of the ground stop my seeds from sprouting up?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ midumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Yes, when heavy rain is followed by strong sun, the soil surface can bake into a hard shell that delicate young sprouts cannot break through, trapping them underneath.
ga: Nakai eji, kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa nyiɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu baanyɛ afee ŋmei ni wa ni tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. ni okɛto shishi

english: What happens to my crops if rainwater stays standing on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo?

english: Excess standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off their air supply, causing the roots to rot and the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Will removing extra water from my soggy field give me a better harvest?
ga: Ani nu ni fa fe nine ni mijie kɛjɛ miŋmɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Yes, draining excess water protects roots from rotting and prevents fungal diseases, allowing the plants to grow strong and produce their full yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akafite, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni fa.

english: How can I check if my ground has too much water before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball. If water drips out easily or the mud turns into a sticky lump that won't break apart, the soil is too wet and may rot your seeds.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ oya loo sũ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni etseee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: How can I remove standing water from my low land without using costly equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie nu ni damɔ shi kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can dig simple shallow ditches or channels across your field sloping away from the crops so gravity naturally drains the excess water off your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu loo nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Yɛ ŋmɔji ni baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my farm ground crack open when the weather becomes dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ gbeleɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soils shrink as water evaporates in the hot sun, causing large cracks to open up which can tear roots and let remaining soil moisture dry out faster.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii lɛ mli shwieɔ shi beni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji gbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ amli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my harvested grains split and crack open when I dry them in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli fãa ni amɛtswaa kɛ mikɛ amɛ wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If wet grains lose moisture too quickly under intense sun, the rapid shrinkage creates stress inside the grain, causing it to crack open.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ, Rapid shrinkage kɛ haomɔ baa dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ tseɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and maintaining soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam plants create tubers underground using food made by their leaves in the sunlight. Staking gets the vines off the ground where leaves can catch maximum sun and stay safe from rot and pests.
ga: Sweet potato tsei feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛ baai fee yɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ he ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main element plants use to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji nɔ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm make crops produce better than planting in bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with essential plant foods like nitrogen and organic matter. It acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer so the roots can drink during dry periods.
ga: Koolooi agbo haa tsei niyenii ni he hia shikpɔŋ lɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my seeds rot or die if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a temporary shower followed by several hot, dry days. Sprouted seeds dry out quickly in the hot soil if continuous rains have not fully set in yet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo ko kɛkɛ. Gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baagbi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛko lolo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat gets too high, tomato plants experience stress and shed their blossoms to save energy and water. Without the flower staying on the stem, the fruit cannot form.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɛji fɔfɔi bɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nyɛŋ afee.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves to suck out sap, which damages the leaf tissue and distorts its shape as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ni etsakeɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger in my field than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they absorb soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated farm crops, allowing them to outgrow your crop quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots under the ground are ready to harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava signals maturity when its bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem, and the ground right around the base of the stem begins to crack open from swelling tubers.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ efolo. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ yitso ni efuu lɛ mli.

english: What is the main difference between NPK fertilizer and Urea fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ urea ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: NPK provides three essential nutrients—nitrogen for leaf growth, phosphorus for strong roots, and potassium for fruiting—while Urea supplies a concentrated boost of nitrogen only, which helps plants grow green and lush quickly.
ga: NPK haa niyenii mli nibii etɛ ni he hiaa waa: nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ; Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha yibiiwoo yɛ be mli ni urea haa nitrogen ni mli wa pɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops need Urea fertilizer just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ he miihia urea kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When leaves turn pale green or start yellowing from the lower part of the plant upward, it usually means the crop is short on nitrogen and needs Urea to regain its healthy green color.
ga: Beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni aná urea koni enyɛ ená eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is flowering the best stage for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Ani fɔfɔii afeemɔ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Flowering is a key stage when plants need energy to form fruits or grains, but crops actually need nutrients at different times; base fertilizers like NPK are best applied earlier at planting, while Urea is often applied around flowering.
ga: Fɔfɔii afeemɔ ji be ko ni he hiaa waa ni tsei he hiaa hewalɛ koni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, tsei he hiaa niyenii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Esa akɛ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK atsu nii kɛjɛ dumɔ shishijee mli. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ akɛ urea tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just put all my fertilizer into the soil at the same time I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: If you apply all the fertilizer at once during planting, much of it can get washed away by heavy rain or burn young crop roots before the plant grows big enough to absorb it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ wo mli yɛ be kome mli yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo loo tso shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã amɛ dani tso lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ.

english: What happens to my yield if I wait too late after flowering to apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mimɛ be ni miwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ koni mikɛwo mli?

english: If you wait until after flowers have already set into fruit, the plant has already passed its major growth spurt, so the late fertilizer won't increase your fruit size or crop yield as effectively.
ga: Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi fɔfɔi lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsɔ dalɛ kpele be ko mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ naagbee nɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ehaŋ aduawai lɛ ayibɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I place Urea fertilizer directly at the base of my plant stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ urea awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can scorch or burn the plant; it is better to place it a few inches away from the stem near the roots and cover it lightly with soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã loo eshã. Esa akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni akɛ sũ aha he fioo.

english: Why do my crop flowers sometimes fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when a crop lacks adequate nutrients or water during the flowering stage, which is why feeding plants properly right before or during flowering helps retain the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I know when crop varieties like Amankwaatia are ready for top-dressing fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni tso ko tamɔ Amanquatia efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: You should apply top-dressing fertilizer like Urea when you see the very first flower buds forming, as this gives the crop the energy boost required to develop plenty of healthy fruits.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ urea, awo mli kɛ́ ona klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔii lɛ ni miifee, ejaakɛ enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kroko ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crop plants producing plenty of green leaves but taking long to show flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen early on encourages them to focus entirely on foliage growth, which can delay the appearance of flowers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛaaha tsei mra Ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo.

english: What makes improved crop varieties like Champion different from my regular local varieties?
ga: Mɛni haa tso henɔ ko ni atsake lɛ tamɔ Champion lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ mimaŋ tso lɛ he?

english: Improved crop varieties like Champion are developed to give higher yields and grow faster, but they require proper feeding with fertilizers at specific growth stages to achieve their full potential.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ Champion, koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛdara oya. Shi amɛbiɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why do some of our local crop varieties take up to nine months to mature on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ nyɔji nɛɛhu dani amɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Long-duration crops spend those extra months building deep root systems and storing energy in their stalks, which helps them survive dry spells and produce bigger, heavier yields at harvest time.
ga: Tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baa ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni tsii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: What kind of soil conditions do I need to get plenty of rice produce from my land?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ he hiaa mi koni maná ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rice grows best in clay or silty soils that hold water well, especially in low-lying areas, because constant soil moisture helps the plant absorb nutrients and form full grain heads.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hiɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some farmers in my community harvest large amounts of rice while my crop yield stays low?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ miikpa ŋmãa babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: High yields depend on using quality seeds suited for the area, planting at the right spacing, controlling weeds early, and ensuring the crop gets adequate water throughout its growing period.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni sa kɛha jɛmɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ tsei lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Which crops can I plant before or alongside rice to make my land yield more produce?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu dani loo yɛ ŋmãa masɛi koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts before rice enriches the soil with natural nitrogen, which feeds the rice plants and increases your total harvest without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dani adu ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli nitrogen babaoo. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha ŋmãa fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: How do I know when my local rice crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is mature when about eighty to eighty-five percent of the grain heads turn golden yellow and the grains feel hard when you bite or press them.
ga: Omɔ lɛ eda kɛji akɛ ŋmaa yitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ kɛ enumɔ batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmɔ loo onyɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant short-season crops or ones that take a full nine months to grow?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo loo nɔ ni heɔ nyɔji nɛɛhu muu lɛ fɛɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Short-season crops give you food and quick income early, while nine-month crops take longer but often yield larger harvests that can sustain your family and market sales through the dry season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya mra. Yɛ be mli ni nyɔji nɛɛhu mli ŋmɔshi nibii heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, amɛfɔɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ aha weku kɛ jarayeli nibii ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why does my rice crop require so much water compared to other local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Rice plants have shallow roots and large leaf surfaces that lose water quickly in the sun, so keeping the soil wet prevents the plants from stressing and producing empty husks.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekahao ni eha eshishifãi lɛ afee efolo.

english: How can I safely store a large harvest of local rice produce so it doesn't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa babaoo ato shweshweeshwe koni ekafite?

english: Drying the harvested rice grains thoroughly in the sun until they are dry and brittle before storing them in clean, sealed bags keeps mold and insects away.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbiɔ ni ebaafiteɔ dani akɛwoɔ kotokui ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my young rice crop during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive and quick to take up sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Clearing them within the first three to four weeks lets your young rice plants grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha omɔ tsei bibii lɛ adara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How does a long rainy season of up to nine months affect how my crops behave?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be ni heɔ nyɔji nɛɛhu lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended rains allow crops to stay green and keep feeding for longer, which leads to fuller harvests, but it also means you must watch out for fungal diseases caused by excess humidity.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha niyenii aba be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ babaoo. Shi etsɔɔ hu akɛ esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops need flowers before they can produce any fruit or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers are the plant's reproductive parts. Tiny grains called pollen must move from one part of a flower to another, or between flowers, to trigger the plant to start growing seeds and fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji tsei afɔmɔ fã. Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pollen lɛ ajɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fã kome mli kɛya fã kroko mli. loo fɔfɔi ateŋ Koni ewo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛje dumɔwui kɛ aduawai adumɔ shishi.

english: Can my crops produce a high harvest on their own without insects or wind visiting them?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ basaraaa amɛ?

english: Most crops need help moving pollen. While some plants rely on the wind, many valuable crops like cocoa and vegetables depend heavily on tiny insects like midges and bees to carry pollen so flowers can turn into healthy fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni amɛkɛjie pollen. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei komɛi damɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ moŋ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni jara wa, tamɔ kookoo kɛ aduawai kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii anɔ waa koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii amli. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ afee aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it possible for a farmer to pollinate crops by hand, or is that something only nature can do?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ okwaafoi kɛ amɛdɛŋ baawo amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔtɔ? Aloo eji nɔ ko ni adebɔɔ pɛ baanyɛ afee?

english: Farmers can actually pollinate crops manually by using small tools or brushes to transfer pollen between flowers. While nature usually does it, hand pollination can boost fruit production significantly when natural insects are scarce.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwo amɛ tsei lɛ amli fɔfɔi kɛtsɔ nibii bibii loo brɔshi ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ fɔfɔi lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ sumɔɔ ni efee nakai moŋ. Shi nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai aya hiɛ waa kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii faaa.

english: Why is clearing weeds and undergrowth around my crop trees so important?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ojie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei lɛ ahe miihia waa.

english: Weeds and thick bush steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing undergrowth ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Does clearing all the bush and leaves under my cocoa trees affect the insects that help my farm?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ baai fɛɛ ni abua naa yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baaná kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, it can. While clearing weeds helps crops grow, completely removing all leaf litter can destroy the damp shady homes where tiny pollinating insects live and breed.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ afee. Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa moŋ, shi kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ amli jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shia ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ. ni ji he ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollin lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛfɔ bii lɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my trees sometimes fall off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off mainly when they fail to get pollinated by insects, or when the plant suffers from environmental stress like severe drought, extreme heat, or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi babaoo yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛŋ afee amɛ pollin lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei miipiŋ yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ahe, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haaa mɔ he waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do insects know when my farm flowers are ready for them to visit?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii leɔ be mli ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaasara?

english: When flowers are mature and ready for pollination, plants produce sweet scents, bright colors, and sweet liquid called nectar to attract pollinators like bees and midges.
ga: Beni fɔfɔi lɛ eda kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha pollination. Tsei jieɔ tsofai ni ŋɔɔ, sui ni mli tse kɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my farm have plenty of flowers during the rainy season but very few pods later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii babaoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away pollen or prevent tiny flying insects from visiting flowers. If insects cannot visit the flowers during bloom time, those flowers will not turn into pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli muji loo etsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafo. Ba ni obakwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ayasara fɔfɔii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Nakai fɔfɔii lɛ tsakeŋ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will spraying chemical insecticides on my farm stop my flowers from turning into fruits?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi mi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai?

english: Yes, if applied incorrectly. Spraying strong chemicals while crops are flowering kills beneficial insects that pollinate your flowers, which can lead to a smaller harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Tsofai ni mli wa ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa ofɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kpamɔ bibioo aba.

english: What simple activities can I do on my farm besides clearing weeds to help my crops produce more?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛfata jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ he koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Besides clearing weeds, you can preserve shade trees, avoid spraying chemicals during peak flowering hours, and leave a light layer of organic mulch to keep the soil moist and encourage helpful insects.
ga: Kɛfata jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ he lɛ Obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ hu anɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ fa babaoo lɛ he. ni okɛ jwɛi ni ji organic jwɛi bibioo ko aha nɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crop plants need to stay green and healthy. The plant moves limited nitrogen from older leaves to feed new upper leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs organic manure instead of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: If your soil hardens quickly after rain, dries out fast, or feels light and sandy, it needs organic manure to build up soil structure and hold moisture. Chemical fertilizers supply fast nutrients to plants but cannot fix dry, hardened, or degraded soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, egbi oya, loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋã. Organic fertilizers he miihia koni akɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ mli. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya. Shi enyɛŋ esaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ni wa loo ni efite lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. It can also happen as a self-defense reaction when the crop loses water too fast during hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he kɛji tsei fite nu oya tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is eating ragged holes into my young maize leaves and leaving dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni ashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that burrows into the center funnel of young maize. Checking your field early allows you to spot caterpillar egg masses or caterpillars before they destroy the crop's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ehaa onaa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii akui babaoo dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When day temperatures get too high or soil moisture swings from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot pollinate properly and sheds its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli. Tsei nyɛŋ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive intense, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living canopy that shelters seedlings from heat sunburn and keeps soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?
