english: Cassava roots rot when water sits stagnant in the soil due to poor drainage. Excessive water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungal diseases to attack and decay the tuberous roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua amɛ ni amɛha tuber shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out thin, short, and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛfeɔ kukuji, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow crooked when planted in hard, compact, or stony soil that physically blocks the tuber from pushing downward. Creating tall, loose earthen mounds gives the growing tuber space to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shi lɛ nɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee lɛ haa bulb ni miida lɛ he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees fall over because they have shallow root systems that are easily weakened by root-eating pests like nematodes or stem borers. Propping heavy bunches with strong wooden stakes helps support the weight and prevents wind damage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei bibii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ amɛtsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he.

english: Why is my swamp rice turning pale yellow and growing slowly even though the field has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni eedara blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Rice can turn yellow in flooded fields if the water remains stagnant, which prevents oxygen from reaching the roots and stops the plant from taking up food like nitrogen. Draining stagnant water periodically allows roots to breathe and absorb soil nutrients.
ga: Omɔ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli kɛji nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are very sensitive. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them provides protective canopy shade and soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa kwraa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ebaaye ebua ni eha shade kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibioo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ dalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin without producing big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ toi wuji kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This forces them to stretch upward for light instead of storing energy to form large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛhe la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato koni amɛkɛfee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil even though the leaves on top look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds water for too long without draining properly. Excess moisture suffocates the roots and creates a place for underground fungus to attack the tubers long before the leaves show signs of dying.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa gbɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ dani baai lɛ jieɔ gbele he okadii akpo.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground allows the plant to produce more food through photosynthesis, which leads to bigger root tubers under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ haa tsei feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. High afternoon temperatures can dry out the pollen inside the flower, preventing the fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛbuaa naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) growing around the base will steal water and food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough nutrients to grow heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Konii babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ plantains babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread plant viruses. The virus distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from producing new flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Virus lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei.

english: Why is it wrong for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes away granular fertilizer from the soil surface or carries it deep past the plant's roots before they can soak it up. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil after rain, not immediately before a severe downpour.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ dani enyɛɔ eshɛɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Jeee dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and stop growing quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiikpa shweremɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal moisture, sunlight, and essential soil nutrients directly away from your crops. When weeds crowd your field, your crops starve and cannot produce the food they need to stay green and strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I make sure my crops have enough water during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Digging a farm well or shallow water retention pit on your land captures rainwater during the wet season, giving you a reliable water source to keep your crops hydrated when the rains stop.
ga: Kɛ́ otsa nubu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabua nugbɔ nu naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: How do I know the right place on my land to dig a farm well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafo nubu?

english: Observe where rainwater naturally flows and settles during heavy rains. Digging your well along these lower pathways makes it easier to collect and store groundwater for your farm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hei ni nugbɔ nu hoɔ yɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu bu ni oootsa yɛ shishigbɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooobua shikpɔŋ shishi nu naa ni okɛto kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use the rainwater flowing across my farm to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, by digging small channels or contour trenches along the natural water paths across your land, you slow down flowing rainwater so it soaks deep into the soil for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋshɔ bibioo ko ni atsaa. loo ŋshɔkei ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nu gbɛi ni foɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does heavy rain keep washing away my rich topsoil and young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Rainwater creates fast-moving paths across unprotected land, stripping away fertile soil. Constructing contour drains across the water's path slows down runoff and keeps your topsoil in place.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ feɔ gbɛ ni yaa oya kɛtsɔɔ hei ni abuuu he lɛ. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ ama paipii ni akɛtsɔɔ nu lɛ mli yɛ nu lɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is a contour drain and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji Contour Drain ni te ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A contour drain is a trench dug across the slope of your field. It intercepts running rainwater, stops soil erosion, and holds moisture near crop roots so your plants stay healthy.
ga: Nu paipii ni tamɔ bu ni atsa yɛ oyale lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu, ni ekpaa shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ehiɛɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ Koni otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow on the sloped parts of my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Rainwater moves too quickly down sloped land, taking plant nutrients with it. Building low earthen barriers across the slope stops nutrients from washing away and helps soil retain water.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yaa oya tsɔ yɛ hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ ni okɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ gbogbo ni baa shi ni atswaa Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ ni atsĩɔ lɛ haaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akaho ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Where should I construct drainage channels on my farmland?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ matswa nu homɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Drainage channels should be placed right along the main paths where water naturally travels through your field, safely guiding excess rain away from plant roots without causing erosion.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nu homɔ gbɛi awo gbɛi wuji ni nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ anɔ. Koni ajie nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli shweshweeshwe ni ekɛ shikpɔŋhosomɔ baaa.

english: How do I prevent heavy rainfall from waterlogging and rotting my crop roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha nu afua ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ akafite?

english: Digging clear pathways and trench drains through your field directs excess water off the land, preventing stagnant water from suffocating your crops' roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔji amli lɛ ni oootsɔ mli lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekatsi otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Without trenches or barriers to hold water back, rainwater runs off the surface instead of sinking in. Creating water retention structures on your land helps rain soak deep into the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔkei loo gbɛtsii nii komɛi bɛ ni baaha nu ahi Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote mli. Nu ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oootswa lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What simple land preparation should I do before the rainy season begins?
ga: Dani obaabote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ nibii bibii esa akɛ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ oha?

english: Before the rains start, identify the natural water paths on your farm and dig retention ditches or small wells so your land is ready to catch and store water for the growing season.
ga: Dani nugbɔ baabɔi nɛmɔ Kwɛmɔ adebɔɔ mli nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni otsa nubu loo nubu bibioo ko. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaamɔ nu ni ekɛto kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillars feed on the growing point of young maize plants, which reduces yields if not controlled early using safe insect pest management techniques.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra. Kɛtsɔ ŋaai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards like tiny cups and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or by a virus they carry. Controlling these tiny pests early keeps the plant healthy and prevents severe stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and rotting before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when soil moisture fluctuates sharply between dry spells and heavy rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ateŋ.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way up in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ miidu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem; they should always point upward toward the sky. Planting stem cuttings upside down causes weak, stunted leaf shoots and significantly reduces tuber development.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Niji ni miida ni amɛmiikwɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛhe afee shoo. ni ehaa yitsoŋ dalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and leafy green but fail to produce large tubers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi enyɛɛɛ ewo bulbs loo aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: This happens when there is excessive nitrogen in the soil and not enough phosphorus or potassium. High nitrogen encourages leafy top growth, whereas balanced nutrients are required for root expansion and fruiting.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni fɔsfɔs loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ daraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni ja he miihia kɛha shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that restores soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops turn pale yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifee midumɔwui lɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your young crops, making early and regular weeding essential for crop nutrition.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa otsei bibii lɛ. Ha efee nɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. ni daa lɛ he miihia kɛha tsei aniyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and dry heat. Fast-growing plantains provide essential temporary shade and maintain soil moisture during the cocoa plant's first two critical years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli egbi he. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before planting my main maize crop instead of planting after the first single rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu mi ŋmãa titri lɛ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rains are often followed by hot dry spells that dry out the topsoil, causing newly germinated seeds to scorch and die before the true rainy season established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines off the ground using wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee ŋtayaai adu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air to capture maximum sunlight for plant food production while keeping leaves away from damp ground diseases, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni emɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha tsei aniyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and drooping down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or receiving too much water. Nitrogen gives plants their rich green color, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea helps the plants regain their health and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu babaoo miiná. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my chili pepper plants curling up into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. When they suck the plant's juice, it deforms the leaf, which can be treated by spraying a recommended pesticide or neem oil solution.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji oonu nu kɛjɛ tsei amli lɛ Baai lɛ baatsake amɛhe. Abaanyɛ atsa enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If one cassava plant in my farm gets dark brown spots on its leaves, can it spread to the rest of my crops?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, spots on leaves are usually fungal or bacterial diseases that spread easily to healthy plants through wind, rain splashes, or farm tools. Removing and burning affected leaves early stops the sickness from spreading across your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ahe tsɔi ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ shãa mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops look completely lifeless and wilted during the afternoon heat even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They wilt temporarily to save moisture and will usually stand back up when the sun goes down and temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: How do I safely mix and spray liquid chemicals on my crops so I do not burn the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafutu tsofai ni ji nu ni mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shweshweeshwe? koni akashã baai lɛ

english: Always mix liquid chemicals strictly using the recommended water ratio on the label. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening prevents the sun from heating up the chemical on the leaf and scorching the plant.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, futumɔ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu mlijaa ni atsɔɔ yɛ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu lɛ haaa tsofai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ adɔ ni ekɛshã tso lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best time to spray liquid fertilizer is early morning before 9 AM when the leaf pores are open to absorb nutrients and the soil is cool enough to retain moisture.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa dani 9:00 a.m. be mli ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbele koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and soil moisture to protect the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo bibioo lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather is extremely hot or when they lack adequate water and nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots underneath are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of tubers. Using a fertilizer higher in potassium encourages the plant to store energy underground and grow bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: What is making small, neat holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Neat yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are typically caused by young Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's funnel. Checking the center leaves early and applying targeted controls prevents them from eating the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nɔ ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii yɛ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting stems from healthy, disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aaakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in high humidity and excess shade. Pruning tall shade trees and weeding around cocoa trunks allows air to dry out the pods.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Tsei kakadaji ni afolɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ. Kookoo tsei lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ mli gĩɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots that cannot absorb enough water to keep up with intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong stems and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: If your maize leaves turn light green or pale yellow instead of deep green, or if the lower leaves turn yellow starting at the tips, your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji o-corn baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting cowpeas after maize helps restore natural fertility to the soil without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Cowpeas ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait for steady rain before planting my seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting for the major rainy period ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, which is usually caused by long dry spells, excessive heat, or a sudden lack of nutrients in the soil during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli trukaa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: What happens if I do not trim the extra leaves and small branches off my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifolɔɔɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ? kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli

english: Leaving extra leafy branches causes the tomato plant to send its food energy to the leaves instead of the fruits, resulting in smaller yields and damp conditions that attract fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei niji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ akudɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly after I put them in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they were cut or bruised during harvest, or if the storage barn is hot and lacks fresh air. Storing undamaged yams in a raised, well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them dry and safe from rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ shĩa lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe koni amɛkafite.

english: How does heavy rainfall actually help my crops make fruit instead of just growing leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii moŋ fe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves nutrients in the soil so roots can drink them easily. When a plant gets consistent water, it has enough energy to stop spending all its strength on growing green leaves and start producing flowers and healthy fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni eha shishifãi lɛ anu nu oya. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu daa lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakpa ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaatsu nii yɛ baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ he. ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ

english: Why does the soil on my plot dry up so fast even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to the hot sun through evaporation. Adding organic matter like dry grass or compost traps the rainwater deep in the ground, keeping it moist for your crop roots long after the rain stops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛyaa hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaamɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my small green mangoes fall off the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Young mangoes drop when the tree gets stressed by dry spells, sudden lack of nutrients, or attacks from pests like fruit flies. Keeping the soil moist during fruit growth helps the tree hold onto its harvest.
ga: Mango bibii baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. niyenii ni esaaa ni anáa trukaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni baa lɛ tutuamɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ aduawai adalɛ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my harvested mangoes spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Mangoes keep breathing and ripening rapidly after being picked, especially in the heat. Storing them in a cool, shade-covered, and airy space slows down spoilage and keeps them fresh for buyers.
ga: Mango lɛ muɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji ajie lɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfite fioo, ni ebaaha amɛfee ehee aha mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best spot on my plot to plant new crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni madu tsei heei?

english: Look for a spot with deep soil that gets plenty of sunlight and where rainwater doesn't collect into a muddy swamp. Plants need sunlight to make food and good drainage so their roots don't rot.
ga: Taomɔ he ko ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli. ni nugbɔ nu ko bɛ ni abua naa yɛ ŋshɔkei ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli. Hulu la he miihia tsei koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kpakpa. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin but give me very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight and stretch upward instead of growing strong stems. Giving each plant proper spacing allows light to reach all parts, encouraging more fruit to grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ebaafee kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa la shɛɔ efã fɛɛ fã he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ daa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water can wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, leaving crops hungry. Also, if roots stay soaked in water logged soil for too long without air, the leaves will turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛji shishifãi lɛ tara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crop fall off without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress, water shortages, or lack of pollination. Keeping the root area moist during flowering helps the plant hold its blossoms until they turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni faaa loo pollination ni bɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Can I leave old crop leaves and plant waste on my land, or will it ruin the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ ni madu jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Aloo ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving clean crop waste on the land acts like a blanket that cools the soil and holds rain. As the waste rots over time, it turns into free natural fertilizer that feeds your next crop.
ga: Nibii ni he tse ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ. Beni jwɛi fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, atsakeɔ nakai jwɛi lɛ afeeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How does timing my planting with the first rains help me make more money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shika ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Planting right at the start of the rains allows your crops to grow fully using free natural water. Harvesting early allows you to sell your produce in the market when supplies are low and prices are high.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ. early harvest Ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii yɛ jara nɔ be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to cover them, harsh afternoon sun scorches the fragile leaves and causes the young plants to wither quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Gbi gbɛkɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Can excessive direct sunlight reduce the number of cocoa pods my farm produces?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo ŋmeii ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, too much direct sun stresses cocoa trees, causing them to drop flowers and young pods prematurely to save water, which ultimately reduces your total harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi mra koni akɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi yɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants struggle to survive when I clear all the large trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing all forest trees leaves cocoa seedlings completely exposed to intense sun and wind. Keeping moderate shade trees keeps the soil cool and preserves the ground moisture seedlings need to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa aba kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni akɛaaha hulutsoo be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower, but the flowers drop off without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Unpredictable rainfall combined with sudden hot weather creates heat stress, which forces fragile cocoa flowers to drop before they can successfully develop into pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa kookoo fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛyeɔ omanye ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if unexpected heavy rains start during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Sudden rains during dry periods create high humidity, which promotes the fast spread of black pod disease if the farm is not properly pruned and weeded.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ ŋmɔji amli jogbaŋŋ ni ajieee jwɛi kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do small cocoa pods shrivel and turn black on the tree during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni tsei lɛ agbo ni amɛfee ediŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. During severe heat or periods without rain, the cocoa tree intentionally sacrifices its youngest pods to conserve limited water and survive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshaa amɛ ŋmeii bibii fe fɛɛ lɛ afɔle koni amɛkɛbu nu fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: How does extreme direct sunlight affect my cocoa beans while they are drying?
ga: Te hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ saa mi-kokoo yibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Overexposing wet cocoa beans to intense heat can dry the outside shells too quickly while leaving the inside moist, leading to poor fermentation and lower bean quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ tsɔ lɛ wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya tsɔ, yɛ be mli ni emli lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haaa kɔfi yibii lɛ afee fɛo jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa kɔfi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hu baa shi.

english: What should I do to protect my cocoa beans when rain suddenly falls while they are drying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-kokoo yibii lɛ ahe kɛ́ amɛkumɔ trukaa? Nugbɔ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: You should immediately cover the drying cocoa with plastic tarpaulins or mats to stop rain from rewetting the beans, which prevents mold from growing.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tarp loo plastic tsɔne aha kookoo ni egbi lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni nugbɔ akahanɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad to dry harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare ground under hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaagbi kookoo yibii ni akpa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa on bare ground exposes beans to extreme heat absorbed by the soil, uneven drying, and contamination from dirt and insects.
ga: Kookoo ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa baa ni muji kɛ kooloi bibii woɔ mli

english: How can I prevent my soil from drying out too fast when the sunny weather lasts too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Spreading dried crop leaves or plant waste around the base of your cocoa trees acts as mulch, covering the soil from direct sun rays and trapping moisture in the ground.
ga: Tso baai ni egbi loo tsei amli sũi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving water drainage helps the plants turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea, loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are developing tubers under the soil without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ miifee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mikɛfooo amɛ?

english: As cassava tubers grow big underground, they swell and push the dirt upwards. You will notice small cracks forming in the soil right around the base of the plant stem, which shows the roots are swelling well.
ga: Kɛji cassava shishifãi lɛ dara agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Ebaafuu ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aya ŋwɛi. Obaayɔse ŋmeii bibii. ni baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efuu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my groundnuts so they do not spoil in the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying up, and the inside of the pods shows dark brown or black markings when you crack a test pod open.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni pod lɛ mli baafee okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛji ogbele kaa pod lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops very close to each other on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same soil food and water, while their leaves shade each other from sunlight. Spacing them properly allows each plant to get enough food and light to yield well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do crops grow better on raised soil mounds during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Raised mounds loosen the soil so roots can spread easily, and they lift the crop roots above standing water, preventing the roots from rotting when heavy rains fall.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. ni tsei ashishifãi baate shi yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo nɔ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akafite kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in strong sunshine to reduce the amount of water escaping from the plant. However, if the leaves stay curled in the early morning or evening, it could be a sign of sap-sucking insects or disease.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii loo nu ni shwieɔ nu lɛ miiye.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if the soil stays soaked with too much water?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When soil stays completely wet, roots cannot breathe and begin to drown. This causes tomato leaves to turn yellow, droop, and can cause the tomato fruits to split or rot on the vine.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tomato baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbee shi, ni ebaanyɛ eha tomato yibii lɛ mli agbala loo amɛgbo yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I leave dried leaves and plant waste around my crops to help them grow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mashi baai ni egbi kɛ tsei amli sũ ni etse ehe banee. Nibii ni aduɔ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, spreading dry leaves or grass around your plants acts as mulch. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer that feeds the crops without costing extra money.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fiofio ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii ni efiteee shika babaoo.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves have many small holes in them, and will it stop them from producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii babaoo nɛkɛ ni ani enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee ŋmeii?

english: Holes in the leaves mean leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars are feeding on your plants. Since leaves make food for the crop, losing too many leaves makes the plant weak and produces fewer pods.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii miiye otsei lɛ. Ejaakɛ baai lɛ ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ baai babaoo fite lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baawo.

english: Why do my crop plants suddenly wilt and die even when there is moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When plants wilt in wet soil, underground pests or soil fungi are usually attacking the root system, damaging the plant's ability to drink water from the ground.
ga: Beni tsei gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Do crops actually sleep at night, and what do they do during the day when the sun comes up?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii wɔɔ gbɛkɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni mɛni amɛfeɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ te shi?

english: During the day, crops use sunlight, water, and air to produce their own food (photosynthesis) so they can grow and produce fruit. At night, they rest and focus on using that stored energy to build new roots, stems, and leaves.
ga: Yɛ gbi mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. (photosynthesis) koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛwo shishifãi, ŋmeii, kɛ baai heei.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my young seedlings on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu?

english: Early morning is the best time to water seedlings. This allows the roots to absorb moisture deeply before the hot afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate from the soil.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ dumɔwui anɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do crop roots absorb fertilizer from the soil, and when is the right time to feed them?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Ni mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aha amɛ niyenii?

english: Plant roots can only drink up fertilizer that has dissolved in soil water. The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rains when the soil is moist, allowing roots to easily absorb the nutrients.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: How long does a young oil palm tree take before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso bibioo ko jeɔ yibii akui awomɔ shishi?

english: High-yielding hybrid oil palm varieties usually start producing their first harvestable fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into the field, reaching full production around 7 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni ji hybrid oil palm henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. ni ebaada yɛ aaafee afii 7 mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my palm trees turn yellow during dry weather, and should I be worried?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mahao?

english: Yellowing leaves during drought usually mean the tree is short on water or nutrients like nitrogen. The tree naturally slows down its work to conserve moisture, which causes older leaves to yellow and die back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Is it necessary for me to cut off old or dried palm leaves, or should I leave them on the tree?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ tso ni egbɔ loo ni egbi lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Pruning off old or dead fronds helps the tree direct its strength into growing fresh leaves and bigger fruit bunches, while also making it much easier for you to harvest and inspect the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai momoi loo ni egboi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ baai heei kɛ aduawai wuji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaakpa otsei lɛ ni okwɛ mli.

english: Why is it recommended to plant my oil palm seedlings in batches rather than all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kui amli moŋ fe ni aaadu fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Planting in planned batches helps you spread out your installation costs, manage farm labor more effectively, and ensure a continuous sequence of harvest and income over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kui amli taakɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ogbɛɔ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli oshwaa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ akɛ kpamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ kɛ shika ni anáa yɛ be mli.

english: How can I tell if spending more money on certified oil palm seedlings is better than using seeds from wild trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehi akɛ mafite shika babaoo kɛhe oil palm dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ fe ni makɛ koo mli tsei amli dumɔwui atsu nii?

english: Certified seedlings are specially bred to produce significantly more oil and withstand common diseases. Although they cost more upfront, the higher fruit yield over their 25-year lifespan yields far greater profits than wild seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo amɛhe odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná mu babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shika ni fa fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ moŋ. Shi yibii ni anáa babaoo yɛ afii 25 wala be mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo fe koo mli dumɔwui.

english: What happens to palm trees if I plant them too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ kɛji midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients. As a result, they grow tall and thin but produce very small and few fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kwraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young palm trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop with short-term crops like maize or vegetables during the first 2 to 3 years to get food and cash flow, as long as you keep the crops a few meters away from the palm tree base to avoid competition.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli koni eha niyenii kɛ shika aba. Shii abɔ ni obaahã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ninetalɔi fioo pɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi koni akaŋshii akafee nɔ ko lɛ,.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn yellow when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the soil loses moisture too quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a living canopy that protects the seedlings while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants full of small holes and covered in white sawdust-like stuff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni akɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ehà nɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center growing point of the maize plant. The sawdust-like material is caterpillar waste, which signals that you need to act quickly with proper controls before the pest destroys the growing stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji ŋmei ŋmei. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni otsu nii oya kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata tsei ni miida lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves. Controlling these insects early stops them from stunting the plant and spreading leaf curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafee mɛi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛkagbɛ leaf curl virus lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating your maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restore vital nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing nutrients before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your soil is pale, very sandy, or if weeds and past crops grow slowly with yellowish leaves instead of dark green ones, the soil lacks plant food and requires manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ŋã yɔɔ mli waa, loo kɛji jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Proper planting distance ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can process energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ atsu hewalɛ he nii koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat causes tomato plants to shed their flowers to save water and protect themselves from heat stress. Mulching the soil and watering at the roots during dry hot spells helps keep the plants cool enough to hold fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ ashɛreɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni awoɔ amɛ nu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkpa.

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation (mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps soil moisture so you water less, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly rots into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ nu fioo nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi ni haa nɔ lɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves showing yellow patches and twisting into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsɔ amɛhe amɛfee srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting stems taken from sick plants. Using certified disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does maize grow differently on newly cleared forest land compared to old farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ fe okwaayeli shikpɔŋ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly cleared forest land is rich in organic matter and nutrients accumulated over many years, which makes maize grow tall and green quickly. However, the soil can be naturally acidic or contain buried roots, so proper clearing and soil testing help ensure uniform crop growth.
ga: Kooi amli hei ni ajie ehee lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa abele lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni efeɔ eŋɔli oya. Shi kɛlɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo eyɛ shishifãi ni afu. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to remove tree stumps completely before using tractor machines on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei akutsei lɛ kwraa dani mikɛ trakta lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hidden tree stumps and thick roots can break machine blades, puncture tractor tires, and prevent plows from making straight, clean rows. Removing them completely ensures seeds are planted at an even depth for balanced crop development.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse baanyɛ akumɔ tsɔne mli ŋmeii. trakta taii ni efo mli ni etsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni he tse. Dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is a combine harvester, and how does it help with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ?

english: A combine harvester is a large farm machine that cuts, threshes, and cleans mature grain crops like maize all in one continuous operation. It saves weeks of manual labor and prevents crop loss caused by sudden rains or pests while ripe maize sits in the field.
ga: Combine harvester ji ŋmɔ mli tsɔne agbo ko ni akɛfoɔ, ashwieɔ, ni atsuuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ nitsumɔ kome ni yaa nɔ daa mli. Enɛ haa akɛ niji tsuɔ nii otsii babaoo. ni atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can heavy harvesting machines damage the soil where I want to grow my crops?
ga: Ani nikpamɔ tsɔne agbo baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa mi koni madu nii lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy machinery can pack the soil tightly together, which is called soil compaction. Compacted soil makes it difficult for crop roots to penetrate deep for water and nutrients, so farmers often loosen the ground after heavy equipment use.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nibii ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ amɛkɛ tsɔnei ni tsii tsu nii.

english: Are crop harvesting machines made in other countries able to work well on Ghanaian farm soil?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Most imported farm machinery is designed for specific crop types and field conditions. Foreign equipment often needs minor modifications or height adjustments to handle local soil conditions, moisture levels, and Ghanaian crop varieties effectively.
ga: Afee okwaayeli tsɔnei babaoo ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi. Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ biɔ ni atsake amɛ fioo loo atsake amɛhe ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni akɛtsu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he nii. Humidity level kɛ Ghana tsei srɔtoi lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I plant a very large field of maize all at once if I don't have harvesting machines ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ agbo ko shikome lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii ni asaa he hu?

english: Maize planted at the same time will mature all at once across the entire field. If you lack the machines or labor to harvest quickly, mature maize will sit in the field and rot, suffer pest attacks, or spoil under rain.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli Amɛbaakwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Kɛji obɛ tsɔnei loo nitsulɔi ni okɛbaakpa oya Abele ni eda lɛ ta ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni egboɔ. Nɔ ko ni gbeɔ mɔ loo egbo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ

english: How does the timing of the dry season affect when I should clear forest land for planting?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ ajie koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛdu nii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Forest land must be cleared during the dry season so cut trees and brush can dry out and be cleared easily. Attempting to clear land during the rainy season turns the soil into mud, making it difficult for machinery or workers to prepare the land on time.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie kooi amli hei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni afo lɛ baagbi ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ abaajie amɛ. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni ajie shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ muji. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsɔnei loo nitsulɔi akɛ amɛbaasaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be naa.

english: Why does maize require exact row spacing when I move from manual farming to machine farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ aná sɛɛkpee ko beni mijɛɔ nine mli okwaayeli mli kɛyaa tsɔne mli okwaayeli mli lɛ?

english: Machine farming requires uniform row spacing so tractor wheels and machine headers can pass through the field without crushing plants. Proper spacing also ensures every crop gets equal sunlight, air flow, and fertilizer.
ga: Okwaayeli ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ biɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ daa. No hewɔ lɛ traktɔ lɛ shwiili lɛ kɛ tsɔne lɛ yitso lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni ekɛ tso lɛ ekpãtãaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ hu haa tsei fɛɛ náa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ

english: What causes maize crops to fall over easily when planted in large open fields?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔji wuji ni mli tse lɛ amli?

english: Strong winds can easily push down tall maize plants, especially in open fields where natural forest windbreaks have been removed. Using strong-rooted maize varieties and planting at recommended depths helps support the crop against high winds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa ŋmãa tsei kakadaŋŋ ashwie shi mlɛo. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni afo adebɔɔ mli koo mli kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni shishifãi lɛ wa tsu nii ni adu yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why does ripe maize spoil quickly if it stays in the field too long before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ehi ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Once maize reaches full maturity, the stalks stop feeding the ears and the grains begin to dry. Leaving ripe maize on the stalk exposes it to field insects, birds, mold growth, and unexpected rains that can cause seeds to sprout directly on the cob.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kpaɔ toi lɛ niyenii ni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa kooloi, okpoi, kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before the corn is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which acts as main food for the plant. Applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer in small stages helps the maize stay green and produce bigger ears.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe titri. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ bei bibii amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ewo toi wuji.

english: Why does my land produce good crops the first year, but yields drop if I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop prefers and allows specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ajɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense heat because their roots are shallow. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade umbrella protection and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden Y-stakes prevents the wind from pulling them out of wet soil.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and stop the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni baanyɛ aha pepper baai lɛ abɔle ehe ni ekpa tsei lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves. Spraying early with natural neem oil or soap solution keeps these insects under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo samla baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I am even ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifee klalo po akɛ makpã lɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by poor soil drainage that keeps too much water around the tuber, allowing soil fungi to attack. Planting on high mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa. ni haa nu babaoo hiɔ eyitso lɛ he Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering stresses tomato plants, causing them to shed their blossoms to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow very tall and leafy, but the roots underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of swelling the roots. Balanced soil nutrients encourage big tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my farm make the soil stronger for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants die, that trapped food stays in the soil to nourish future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni atsĩ naa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it better to burn cleared weeds on my field or let them rot on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo maha amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving weeds to rot creates natural organic cover that retains soil moisture and turns into free food for your crops over time, whereas burning destroys good soil bacteria.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebafeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaaa onibii yɛ be ni sa mli. yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kpakpai.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make leaves green and grow fast. Feeding the soil with organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with plenty of big leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Adding wood ash or potassium-rich fertilizer encourages the tubers to swell.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which naturally feeds your maize crop without buying extra chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground, causing lower yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate stems and leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.
