english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sun to make food for the underground tuber. Keeping vines off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and catching fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekafite ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes right inside the center funnel of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that hides in the tender heart of maize plants. Catching them early by dropping neem extract or recommended insecticides into the funnel protects the plant before it is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ titri ni yɔɔ mli ji akɛ, enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ekɛ ehe ewo ŋmãa tso ko tsui ni mli jɔ lɛ mli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni oooshɛrɛ awo tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he dani efite.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or insufficient insect visits for pollination. Providing mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool and hydrated.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rains truly begin. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then quickly scorch to death in the hot, dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ afi lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu oya tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛshã oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak even when there is enough soil for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and fertilizer away from your crops. Clearing weeds early lets your crops get the full food supply they need to grow thick and productive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop almost all their leaves when the dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during the dry Harmattan season to save water. Losing leaves reduces the amount of moisture the tree loses through evaporation, helping it survive until the rains return.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni tso lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Should I sweep away and clear all the dry leaves lying under my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egboi ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɛɛ?

english: No, you should generally leave them on the ground. The fallen leaves act as a natural carpet that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating, and slowly decays into rich organic fertilizer for your crop.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ esa akɛ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kapɛti ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does leaf shedding mean my cocoa tree is sick or dying?
ga: Ani baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛgboi?

english: No, leaf shedding is a normal survival mechanism during dry periods. Once the rains return, your cocoa trees will use their stored energy to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Dabi, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Okoko tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ.

english: Why does the soil under my cocoa trees dry out so fast once the Harmattan winds begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: The combination of hot sun and dry Harmattan winds pulls moisture directly out of bare soil. Keeping a thick layer of leaf litter on the ground acts as a shield to block the sun and trap moisture.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni Harmattan feɔ ekome lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni mli tse ni etse ehe lɛ anaabuamɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he.

english: What happens if I burn the dry leaves I gather from my cocoa farm floor?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishã baai ni egbi ni abua naa kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Burning leaf litter destroys valuable organic matter that feeds the soil, leaves the ground bare and dry, and exposes your entire farm to the risk of uncontrolled bushfires during the dry season.
ga: Baai amli jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi. Ni enɛ haa oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ woɔ koo mli la ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he oshara mli.

english: Can the thick layer of dry leaves on my farm floor cause bushfires?
ga: baai ni egbi ni mli tse Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha koo mli la aba?

english: Yes, dry leaves catch fire easily. Instead of clearing the whole farm, create a clean border around your farm perimeter (a firebreak) to stop fires from entering while keeping the leaf cover inside to protect the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbi lɛ shãa oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, Feemɔ husu ni he tse yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he (la ŋmɔ) koni la akabote mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ ahi mli koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Is it good to heap all the fallen leaves directly against the trunk of the cocoa tree?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ato kookoo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is better to spread the leaves evenly across the whole farm floor. Piling them right against the main trunk can trap moisture against the bark and attract unwanted pests or diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbɛ baai lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ni egbala kooloi loo helai ni ataooo lɛ kɛba.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa trees from wilting in the severe dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbo yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: You can protect young trees by providing shade crops like plantains, placing temporary palm fronds over them, and keeping the soil covered with fallen leaves to preserve moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe. Abaanyɛ ana enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni akɛbaawo nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do young cocoa pods dry up and turn dark during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, the tree prioritizes its own survival over the fruits. It cuts off moisture to younger pods, causing them to dry up and stop growing.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei susuɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he fe amɛyibii. Ebaafo ŋmɔtɔ kɛya ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa egbiɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: How do large shade trees help my cocoa farm when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kookoo ŋmɔji beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Shade trees block harsh, direct sunlight, lower the surrounding air temperature, and reduce the strength of dry winds, stopping your cocoa trees from drying out too quickly.
ga: Tsei haa hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hewalɛ aba shi Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ.

english: Groundnuts produce flowers above ground, but once pollinated, the stems bend and push themselves downward into the soil so the peanut pods can grow and mature safely underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee lɛ pollination lɛ, tso lɛ baakoto ni ekɛ ehe baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose as many leaves as possible to direct sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba tsei lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cassava tubers staying small even though the leaves on top are very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and heavy leaves instead of expanding their underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛbaakɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips is a clear signal that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient the plant needs to build strong, green foliage.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus, which prevents the flowers from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily in full sunlight, which is why planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them protects them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl inward and wrinkle up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by uneven moisture in the soil during dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cowpea pods growing long but staying completely empty inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ miidara kakadaŋŋ shi amɛmli efee efolo kwraa lɛ?

english: Empty cowpea pods happen when tiny insects suck the sap out of young green pods, depriving the developing seeds of the food they need to swell.
ga: Afeɔ cowpea ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ beni kooloi bibii shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii dumɔwui ni amɛduɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why does my plantain plant fall over just when the bunch of fruit starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbee shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over under heavy fruit weight when microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects weaken the root system and base of the stalk.
ga: Akɛ plantains shwieɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashishi beni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo kooloi bibii lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants shooting up tall and growing flowers instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni edaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage shoots up to flower, or 'bolts', when exposed to high temperatures or drought, tricking the plant into thinking its life cycle is ending so it produces seeds early.
ga: Cabbage baakwɛ̃ kɛyashi fɔfɔi loo ‘bolt’ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo hɔmɔ mli. Elakaa tso lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ ewala be lɛ miiba naagbee no hewɔ lɛ eyaa dumɔwui amli mra.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each maize plant grows strong stems and yields larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ náa ŋmãa ni wa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but only produce tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when cuttings have too many buds, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tso lɛ nine lɛ mli ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eniji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf rot and encouraging bigger tuber growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from nurse plants like plantains to keep them cool and retain soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu mli be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves wilt and curl up in the hot afternoon even when the ground isn't dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, pepper plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. The leaves curl to protect themselves from losing more water, and they usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation on hot days, and stops unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn getting ragged holes with small caterpillar dirt inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It burrows deep into the center leaves of the young corn plant to feed on tender tissue, which leaves visible holes as the leaves unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni eye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ haa buji ni anaa kɛji baai lɛ gbele.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores onto pods, and high humidity allows the disease to penetrate and ruin the pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa helai boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same field every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that love tomatoes to build up in the dirt, reducing your harvest over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tomato lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my maize crop so it works best?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Fertilizer works best when the crop is actively growing and the soil is moist. Apply a small amount a few weeks after planting when leaves appear, and a second portion just before the plant starts flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Okɛ fioo ko awo mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. Ni okɛ tsɔne ni ji enyɔ lɛ awo mli dani tsei lɛ aje fɔfɔi abɔi.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the soil give the maize the nutrients it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔji ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to support good crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy farm soil is dark, feels crumbly in your hand, holds moisture well without staying soggy, and often contains earthworms. If the soil is pale, hard, or dry, mixing in organic compost or animal manure will improve its fertility before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ enine mli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ehiɛɛɛ mli. ni bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egbi lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha ewoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight because their foliage dries out quickly. Planting tall shade crops like plantain or banana trees alongside cocoa creates natural shade and keeps the soil cool and moist for the young seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get a larger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small ears of corn. Giving each plant proper spacing allows every stalk to grow strong and yield bigger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ tso lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this disease from reducing your yield.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young corn leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant foliage. Inspecting your field regularly and applying approved bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts early stops them before they ruin the entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo mli mra. Abaatsi enaa dani ekpata kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot or when they do not receive a steady supply of water. Watering your crops consistently and putting dry grass mulch around the plant roots helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ sũ awo hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil happens when heavy rainfall stays pooled around the roots for too long or when underground pests damage the tuber skin. Building high soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the yams stay dry and safe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ sweet potato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ hewolo lɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to quickly absorb moisture and soil food faster than domesticated crops can. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures they do not steal vital water and nutrients away from your growing plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe esa akɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkajuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of small insects during storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni akpa lɛ efite loo eyi kɛ kooloi bibii bibii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested grain spoils in storage if it is put away while still damp, which attracts mold and insects like weevils. Drying your grain thoroughly under the sun until it is completely hard and storing it in airtight sacks protects it from pests.
ga: Abaato dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa, ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungus that spreads in cool, wet weather, especially when cocoa trees are too crowded and sunlight cannot reach inside the farm to dry the branches.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen fertilizer, or the field has too much standing water which prevents the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to focus all their energy on growing tall leafy vines instead of flowering and producing seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha cowpea kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama wain tsei ni baai kakadaŋŋ akwɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a fɔɔ fɔfɔi nɛ a woɔ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egboi?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss. The plant is not dying; the tubers underground stay alive and will sprout fresh leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gbooo, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baahi shi ni amɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all leaves to feed the tuber underground, and keeping vines off the wet ground prevents leaf diseases from destroying the farm.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Ni kɛ́ wein tsei lɛ tsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni baa wain tsei anɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and watery instead of big and firm at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni wa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain watery if harvested too early, if planted in heavy waterlogged soil, or if shaded by big trees that block sunlight from feeding the roots.
ga: Nu yɛ cassava shishifãi amli lolo kɛji akɛ akpa mra tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛji onine shɛ hulutsoo nɔ kɛjɛ tso agbo ko ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaba koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures become too high, when the air is extremely dry, or when the plant experiences irregular watering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni afɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants rolling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbages stay loose and soft instead of forming hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ mli etse ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if they get too much heat stress, lack sufficient full sunlight, or receive excess nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Kaabage baagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hao lɛ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to keep your crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: If my crops get sick, can I just buy any plant medicine at the store to fix it?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ mahe tsei ahe tsofa yɛ shwapo mli koni mikɛsaa?

english: No, because different plant illnesses require different treatments. Chemical sprays meant for insects will not cure a fungal rot or viral sickness, so you must identify the exact sickness before buying medicine.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsei ahelai srɔtoi biɔ tsamɔi srɔtoi. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa fungal rot loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔɔ hela ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli faŋŋ dani ohé tsofa.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dying from a plant sickness or just from a lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ miigbe mi-ŋma lɛ?

english: Drought usually causes the entire plant to wilt and roll up its leaves during hot periods. A crop disease typically creates spots, streaks, or strange colors on specific leaves first, even when the ground is damp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai haa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo sui ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai lɛ eko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and shady conditions. You can prevent it by pruning tree branches to let sunlight through and removing infected pods from the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ koni hulu la atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: If I see a few sick plants in my field, should I pull them out immediately?
ga: Kɛ mina tsei fioo komɛi ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani Esa akɛ Matsi mihe kɛjɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing and safely destroying infected plants early stops the sickness from spreading through the air or soil to the healthy crops nearby.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Ehaa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can plant diseases stay hidden in the soil and attack my new crops next season?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtutua miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many fungi and bacteria survive in the soil long after harvest. Practicing crop rotation—like planting beans or peanuts after maize—helps starve and break the disease cycle in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ baa shi ni efoɔ helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when an officer tells me to buy a disease-resistant crop variety?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ onukpai kɛɛ mi akɛ mahe tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ?

english: A disease-resistant variety is a crop bred by researchers to naturally fight off specific common plant illnesses, allowing it to produce a good yield even when disease is around.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji tsei ni niiamlitaolɔi efɔ koni amɛkɛwu amɛshi tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji hela yɛ po.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants compared to buying new certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do some tomato varieties rot easily while other varieties stay fresh on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato komɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi ehee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different tomato varieties are developed with different strengths; some have natural defenses and thicker skins bred into them to withstand fungi and bacteria better than older varieties.
ga: Tomato henɔi srɔtoi Afee lɛ koni ehiɛ hewalɛi srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni baanyɛ ashi ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe henɔi ni etsɛ.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my field even after I spray chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔji lɛ amli beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Pests return if the chemical is washed away by rain, applied at the wrong time, or if the insects have become immune to a spray that has been used repeatedly without changing chemical types.
ga: Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji nugbɔ ho tsofai lɛ, ni akɛwo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli, loo kɛji akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ. ni tsofa lɛ henɔ lɛ tsakeee

english: Why do my yam vines need high soil mounds instead of just planting them directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downward and need loose, soft earth to expand into large, straight roots. High mounds loosen the soil so the tuber grows easily without hitches, while also allowing extra water to drain away so the tuber does not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kɛyaa shi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ shishifãi wuji ni ja. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni tsiɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu kroko atsɔ mli koni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves into full light so the plant can make enough energy to feed the tuber underground, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la ni mli kwɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ moŋ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems that go through a temporary resting period after harvest. Once that resting period ends, the tuber naturally wakes up and uses its internal water and stored energy to grow new shoots.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni esa akɛ amɛyawɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Bulbs lɛ teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen. Because nitrogen is mobile inside the plant, the crop steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves and moves them to the top shoots to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi tsei lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why are my cassava leaves dropping off during the long dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry weather to save water and stay alive. The plant is not dead; its roots remain safe under the ground and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense daylight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the shade and cooler air they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands more flowers than it can feed. The tree naturally drops most of its flowers so it can save its water and nutrients to mature a smaller, healthy batch of full-sized pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛfɔmɔ nii amli bɔni afee ni amɛbu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ afee bibii ni amɛhe wa.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the mother plant for food, light, and water. Removing extra suckers leaves one strong follower shoot, allowing the main stem to produce a much larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome pɛ ni he wa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee ŋmei ni da ni tsii kwraa.

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feed under the leaves, or when the plant experiences extreme afternoon heat and curls its leaves to stop water from escaping.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ na niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Aloo be mli ni tso lɛ naa latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli.

english: How can I learn how to farm yams if I have no experience with farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makase bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ahaa kɛji mibɛ okwaayeli mli niiashikpamɔ ko tsutsu?

english: Beginners usually learn best by pairing up with experienced local farmers in their community who can demonstrate step-by-step techniques for land preparation, planting, and crop care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ kaseɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛ feɔ ekome lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ, dumɔ nii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli fitsofitso.

english: Why is it important to learn directly from experienced farmers before starting my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okase nii kɛjɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ dani obɔi bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Experienced farmers understand local soil types, weather patterns, and crop habits, which helps you avoid common and expensive mistakes when starting out.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ shishi. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ tsei adamɔ sui Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tɔmɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni jara wa lɛ ahe beni ojeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: What happens to my yam crop if the rains fail during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yams need consistent moisture to develop tubers underground; without rain, the tubers remain small, leading to poor yields or complete crop failure.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akpãtãa kwraa.

english: Why do yam plants need so much soil moisture to produce a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo he hiaa sweet potato tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam tubers store water and food reserves as they grow, so adequate rainfall is essential for the underground tuber to swell and reach a healthy size.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa he miihia koni ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛshɛ dalɛ ni sa he.

english: Can yam crops recover if a drought happens while they are growing?
ga: Ani sweet potato tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji hɔmɔ ba be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: While young yam plants can survive brief dry periods, prolonged drought during the main tuber growth stage permanently reduces the size and quality of the harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛgbiɔ moŋ, shi hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ kɛ ehilɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: How can I find good seed yams to plant when there is a shortage in the community?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hi ni mikɛdu yɛ akutsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: During seed shortages, you can source clean seed yams from specialized seed producers, local agricultural officers, or by saving healthy, smaller tubers from previous good harvests.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui faaa lɛ Obaanyɛ oyaná sweet potatoes ni he tse kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe nilelɔi adɛŋ. maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kpakpa ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛbuɔ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does a bad harvest in one year make it difficult to plant crops in the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nikpamɔ ni ehiii yɛ afi kome mli lɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nii yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A poor harvest means fewer tubers are produced overall, leaving farmers with fewer healthy seed yams saved to plant for the following season.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni ehiii tsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ fɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, okwaafoi lɛ bɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaadu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do yam prices become so high in major markets like Accra after a dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato jara yaa hiɛ waa yɛ jarayeli hei titrii tamɔ Accra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lack of rain reduces the overall harvest across farming regions, creating a shortage in city markets where high demand drives up prices.
ga: Nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa yɛ okwaayeli kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ eba shi. Enɛ haa nibii ni faaa yɛ maŋtiasei amli jarayeli hei ni nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo lɛ haa jara yaa hiɛ lɛ baa.

english: When is the right time to plant seed yams to make sure they get enough water?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui koni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Seed yams should generally be planted just before or at the very beginning of the major rainy season so the soil has enough moisture for root growth.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui dani loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What steps can I take to protect my crops if the rain does not fall as expected?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can use techniques like mulching to trap moisture in the soil, plant early-maturing crop varieties, or seek advice from extension officers on drought-tolerant planting methods.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋaai tamɔ mulching atsu nii koni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adumɔ Aloo bi ŋaawoo kɛjɛ extension officers lɛ adɛŋ yɛ bɔ ni ooofee odu tsei ni hɔmɔ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi lɛ he.

english: What causes the leaves of my crops to turn brown and dry up during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Intense sunshine and strong heat scorch plant leaves, forcing the crop to lose moisture faster than its roots can absorb water from the ground.
ga: Hulu lɛ miitso ni baai lɛ miitso kɛ dɔlɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops from getting damaged when the afternoon sun is too harsh?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshinii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: You can reduce sun stress by placing shade nets over vulnerable plants, planting taller shade crops like plantains nearby, or applying mulch on the ground to keep the roots cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha hulutsoo haomɔ aba shi kɛtsɔ shade netting ni okɛaawo tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Is it good to pour water on my crops in the middle of a very hot afternoon?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late evening because midday sun evaporates water too quickly and hot leaves can suffer stress when wet under direct sun.
ga: Esa akɛ awo mli nu leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ kɛ́ edɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What can I put on the ground to prevent the hot sun from drying out my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—known as mulching—blocks direct sun rays, keeps the soil cool, and traps moisture.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my seedlings look wilted and weak inside my shade house during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ mishia ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Heat builds up and gets trapped inside farming structures when the sun shines intensely, creating high temperatures that stress young plants even if the soil is wet.
ga: Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa ni eboteɔ okwaayeli nibii amli kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni naa wa ni haa tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ baa.

english: How do I stop my nursery building from becoming too hot inside for my vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi gbekɛbii askul tsu lɛ naa koni ekafee nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ kɛha aduawai lɛ?

english: You can manage the heat by opening side vents, lifting shade nets, or allowing fresh air to flow freely through the structure so hot air can escape.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ dɔlɛ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni ooogbele lɛ nɔ. Wo hulutsoo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tsɔne lɛ mli oya koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes stop producing fruits when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat puts pressure on crops, causing them to drop their flowers before setting fruit so the plant can save energy to survive the heat.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ato hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Does strong sunshine make my crops yield less food at harvest time?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Yes, extremely intense heat and sun cause stress that forces the plant to spend its energy staying alive rather than developing large fruits or healthy leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ hulu la kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛfite hewalɛ koni amɛhi wala mli lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nguahi aloo tso yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: How do I know if the hot weather is causing too much stress to my farm crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ miihao miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsɔ?

english: Signs of heat stress include leaves curling upward, yellowing foliage, stems drooping during the day, flowers falling off early, and slow crop growth.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be miiba lɛ ahe ji baai ni shwieɔ shi, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why do some of my crops handle the hot sun better than others on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different natural tolerance to weather; some have deep roots or thick leaves that hold water, while sensitive crops require extra shade and care.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he tsuishitoo srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli tse ni toɔ nu. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ.

english: What special care should I give to my cocoa trees once they start forming pods?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛbɔi ŋmɔtɔ?

english: When cocoa trees begin pod formation, they need extra nutrients and protection. Applying recommended fertilizers gives the tree energy to grow large pods, while regular pruning lets in sunlight and air to prevent fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmeii lɛ Amɛmiitao niyenii kɛ hebuu krokomɛi ni fata he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if the tree lacks sufficient water, soil nutrients, or insect pollinators like midges. Ensuring good soil moisture and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during flowering helps pods set successfully.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ midge. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: What makes cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Pods turn black mainly due to Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and shade. Clearing weeds, removing infected pods early, and pruning branches allows air to circulate and keep pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pods lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. weeding Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa pods are growing healthily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy cocoa pods show steady growth with smooth, unblemished skin that gradually turns from green or reddish to yellow or orange as they mature, without dark spots or soft rotting areas.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he ni fiofio lɛ etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu mli beni ekwɛɔ lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ loo hei ni fiteɔ bɛ mli

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry and need support from fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni aye abua mi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Crops show hunger through their leaves. Pale yellow leaves, slow growth, or purplish stems usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus needed for strong growth.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni daa blɛoo, loo tsei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus, ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool and the soil is damp. Applying it under hot midday sun can burn the plant roots and waste nutrients.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akaje mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my crops turn yellow when fruiting begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Fruiting takes a massive amount of energy from the plant. If the soil does not have enough nutrients, the plant pulls food from its older lower leaves to nourish the developing fruit, turning those leaves yellow.
ga: Yibiiwoo biɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ dɛŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii. ni eha nakai baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very bushy leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes the plant to put all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of feeding the roots below. Balanced nutrients are needed to encourage big tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Niyenii ni ja he miihia koni eha bulbs wuji lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling, the leaves reduce their exposure to the hot sun and slow down water loss through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does heavy rainfall right after my crops bloom affect my harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efɔ lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away pollen from open flowers before insects or wind can pollinate them. This prevents fruits or grains from forming properly, leading to a smaller harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli muji lɛ ahe dani kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ afee amɛ muji. Enɛ baatsi aduawai loo ŋmaa lɛ naa koni ekafee jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce far more pods during the major harvest season than in the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli fe kpamɔɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to weather patterns. The major harvest season follows the main rainy period when the trees have absorbed plenty of water and nutrients, giving them the strength to flower heavily and grow many full-sized pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ. Nikpamɔ be titri lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ fɔfɔii babaoo ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: What happens to the quality of my cocoa if I leave mature pods on the tree too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii ni edara lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: If you wait too long to pick mature pods, diseases like black pod rot can set in, and the beans inside may start to sprout. Sprouted or rotten beans reduce the quality class and overall weight of your final harvest.
ga: Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni okɛjie ŋmeii ni eda lɛ, helai tamɔ black pod rot baanyɛ abote mli. Ni ekolɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Beans ni ekwɛ̃ loo ni egbo lɛ baaha onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ etsitsinɔnii fɛɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my crops when planting on a 10-acre plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ mikwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 10 nɔ?

english: Crops need enough personal space for their roots to gather nutrients and their leaves to catch sunlight. For cocoa, planting about 3 meters apart ensures the trees do not fight each other for food and light as they grow big.
ga: Tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ abua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa, ni baai lɛ hu aná hulu la. Kɛha kookoo lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ akatswa niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants lose their leaves and dry up when there is no shade on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baa shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa crops have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains nearby to block the sun, the young plants lose water too fast and burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu lɛ naa lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Will using heavy machines to clear my farm land harm how my crops grow later?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Heavy machinery can press the topsoil down too hard, creating a tight layer that roots cannot easily push through. Hard soil also prevents rainwater from soaking in well, which can slow down crop root growth.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ anyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni shishifãi nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: How does bad soil health affect the way my crops grow and bear fruit?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops show warning signs like yellowing leaves, slow growth, and small stems. Without rich soil food, the crop cannot produce strong flowers or healthy fruits.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ Tsei lɛ baajie kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ awo fɔfɔi ni mli wa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is often caused by a natural condition called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops extra pods it cannot support, or by fungal diseases like black pod. It shows the tree is either short on water/nutrients or fighting an infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni etsɔ diŋ lɛ amli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu/niyenii loo ekɛ hela ko miiwu.

english: How long does it usually take for new hybrid cocoa crops to start bringing in a harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso hee ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ shishi?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to mature quickly and usually start bearing their first fruits within 2 to 3 years after planting, compared to older types that took up to 5 years.
ga: Akwɛɔ kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni bei pii lɛ, amɛjeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛ akɛto afii 5 ni heɔ kɛha kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast around my crops and make them look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni miha amɛfee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds take over, your crops starve and struggle to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni baaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa trees produce better pods?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes weak or dead branches so the tree does not waste energy on them. It opens up the tree so air can flow and sunlight can reach the pods, which keeps disease away and grows bigger fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egbɔjɔ loo egboi lɛ ajieɔ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ. Egbeleɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger trees or plantains because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil before their roots can grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a essential food plant need to grow leaves; adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point my cassava stems when I push them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ otsi ŋmei lɛ owo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani etsɔɔ he ko?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the stem buds pointing upward so the new shoots can easily grow up toward the light while strong roots form downward in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii heei anyɛ adara oya ni amɛná la yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni wa lɛ woɔ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less corn if I plant it on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the ground and allows pests to build up in the soil, whereas swapping crops like maize with cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving tiny droppings?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, tiny pests that hide inside the central funnel of young corn plants; checking crops early and applying neem extracts or recommended sprays early in the morning stops them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi bibii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo spray ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii leebi ni okɛkpa amɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass and fallen leaves on top of the soil around my garden crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbo kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry materials, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from evaporating water, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do seeds I buy from the agricultural officer give a better yield than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and bred to resist local diseases, handle heat better, and grow uniform, high-yielding crops, whereas saved seeds lose their strength and quality over seasons.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ naa kɛ tsei ni aduɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe kpakpa yɛ bei lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away the good topsoil on my hilly farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Making planting ridges or planting grass strips across the slope rather than up and down creates natural barriers that slow down running water and keep the rich topsoil in place.
ga: Kɛ́ adu jwɛi ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied a few weeks after planting when crops are actively growing, and when the soil is already moist so the plant roots can soak up the nutrients quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu tsei lɛ, be mli ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: How does planting cover crops like beans or mucuna help reduce the time I spend weeding my farm?
ga: Dumɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo mucilage. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ehaa be ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi?

english: Cover crops grow fast and spread wide across the ground, forming a thick green carpet that blocks sunlight so weed seeds underneath cannot sprout or grow.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Efeɔ kapɛti eŋɔli ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ kwɛɛɛ loo amɛdaraaa.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are sick or if they are just thirsty from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo kumai miiye amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Thirsty maize leaves usually roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon and recover by morning, whereas diseased plants develop persistent yellowing, spotty leaves, or dry patches that do not improve overnight.
ga: Abɛi ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ leebi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ daa, baai ni egbɔjɔ, loo hei ni egbi ni ehiii kwraa nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: What early signs should I look for on crop leaves in the morning to catch diseases before they destroy my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe leebi koni mana hela dani efite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Look out for unusual dark spots, powdery white spots underneath the leaves, or sticky liquids, as these are early signs of fungal infections or insect attacks that need fast treatment.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ, hei yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. loo nu ni shwieɔ shi Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo kooloi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ etutua lɛ ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ oya.

english: Can dumping household trash or rotten food near my garden cause my crops to rot?
ga: Ani shĩa mli jwɛi loo niyenii ni efite ni mishiɔ yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ afite?

english: Yes, unmanaged rubbish dumps attract destructive pests like flies and host fungal spores that can travel into your farm soil and cause stem or fruit rot on healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ana gbɛ kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni ekɛ stem loo aduawai fiteɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Is it safe to leave dead crop stems and weeds in my farm after clearing the land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi tsei ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ajie jɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving dead plant stems around can harbor pests and plant diseases over the dry season, allowing them to jump back onto your fresh crops when the rains start.
ga: Eshiɔ tsei ni egboi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ha amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote onibii heei lɛ amli kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants get weak and sickly when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, and moisture gets trapped between tightly packed leaves, creating the perfect warm environment for mold and rot.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yam on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in one spot allows crop-specific soil diseases and pests to multiply in that earth, leading to weaker plants and poorer yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa nakai je lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If one tomato plant in my garden gets a leaf sickness, can it spread to the healthy plants?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome yɛ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ hu? Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli?

english: Yes, plant diseases spread quickly through wind, splashing rain droplets, and even on your hands or farming tools when you touch a sick plant and then a healthy one.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ oniji loo okwaayeli nibii po nɔ kɛji ota tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings keep falling over and dying right after popping out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal sickness in damp soil called damping-off, which attacks the soft, fresh stems of young seedlings right at ground level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Damping-off, ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetables develop leaf diseases more often during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai náa baa helai shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains keep crop leaves wet for long periods and cause high moisture in the air, creating ideal conditions for fungi and bacteria to grow and invade crop tissues.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei ahe baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo babaoo baa Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adara ni amɛbote tsei amli fãji amli.

english: Can diseases from my neighbor's farm travel over the boundary and affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã husui amli ni ena mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, crop diseases travel on the wind, through flowing rainwater runoff, or via shared equipment, which is why keeping a clean field border is important.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fãa gbɛ. kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ tsɔne ko ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ Nɔ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa hetsemɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food for green growth. This often happens when the soil is depleted or when heavy seasonal rains wash nutrients deep into the ground beyond the roots' reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap beneath the leaves, or by viruses they spread. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee shoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛjieee cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as prolonged dry weather, nutrient shortages, or attacks by pests like mirids. The tree drops its blooms to save water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuamɔ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni wala ahi shi.

english: Why are my garden egg plants dropping leaves and bearing very tiny fruits this season?
