ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbee shi ni ewo yibii bibii waa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Garden eggs lose leaves and yield small fruits when the soil lacks organic matter or water during flowering. Extreme heat paired with dry soil forces the crop to shed foliage and reduce fruit size to survive.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni fataa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ baa shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the ground and cannot drain away. Standing water starves the roots of air and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases to break down the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo kɛya. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my yams grow out small and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become misshapen when planted in hard, compacted soil or shallow mounds that stop the roots from expanding downward. Soft, deep, well-mounded soil allows the tubers to stretch out naturally.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo yɛ gɔŋji ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni ebɔle ehe jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my maize grow weak and stunted whenever that purple-flowered weed appears in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ beni jwɛi ni fɔfɔii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That weed with purple flowers is Striga (witchweed), a parasite that attaches itself directly to maize roots underground. It steals water and nutrients straight from your crop before the maize can use them.
ga: Jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ ji Striga (witchweed), ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmã shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right when the heavy fruit bunch starts to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over because microscopic worms called nematodes or banana stem weevils destroy their roots underground. Without a strong root anchor, the tree cannot support the weight of the ripening fruit in the wind.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana stem moths lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifã ni mli wa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get full of tiny holes and caterpillars right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii dani akpa

english: The holes and caterpillars are caused by pod borer pests that hatch from eggs laid on the flowers and young pods. If left untreated during the flowering stage, the hatched worms bore inside the pods to eat the seeds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii baa ji kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that clogs the water vessels inside the plant's stem. Adding more water cannot save the plant because its internal pathways are blocked.
ga: Bacteria ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ kɛbaa. Nu babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei lɛ ejaakɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsĩ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to block the intense heat, the leaves burn and dry out faster than the roots can supply water.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ bɛ. Baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ aha nu jɛɛhe.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps the underground tuber grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move down the center stem are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen from fertile soil or compost to stay dark green and produce full cobs.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ ni yaa shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Abɛi he miihia nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas helps improve my land for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with natural soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, this nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot in the ground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe in the soil. When heavy rains cause water to pool in flat or clay soils, the trapped water starves the roots of air and allows rot fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni ahiɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the farm right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when they receive a sudden heavy watering after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water rapidly and expands faster than the outer rind can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings rapidly between very dry and soaked. This stress prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ teŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have a deep taproot; their root system is shallow and spreads near the surface. As the heavy bunch forms at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily pull out of wet soil.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ hu baafee tsii ni abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants look shredded like someone shot holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni atse mli bibii bibii, tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko efo bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This leaf destruction is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central funnel of the young maize plant, eating the tender folded leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai ni afolɔ mli blɛoo lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Curled and wrinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, which causes leaf deformation and can spread stunt viruses to the plant.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli.

english: When maize plants are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each seed proper space ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to grow big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I wait to plant my crop seeds instead of planting immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ koni madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out and kill new sprouts. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the ground stays wet enough for your seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa plants from burning in the hot sun and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the dirt, spreading the leaves out to catch light while keeping them safe from rot and hot soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbalamɔ baai lɛ amli koni emɔ la lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛ koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ sũ ni fiteɔ kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots get watery and rot if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava roots stay in overly wet soil for too long during the rainy season, they absorb excessive water, which causes the starch to break down and leads to fungal rot.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ebaaŋɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores nitrogen so the leaves can green up and feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts put vital food called nitrogen back into the dirt, naturally refreshing your soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kuɔ sɛɛ ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so rapidly right after I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plant life in the dirt, not just your crops. Clearing all weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get to drink the food instead of the weeds stealing it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Jeee oŋmɔshi nibii pɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi fɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anu nu moŋ fe ni jwɛi lɛ baaju bo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They target the soft, young growing point of the maize plant. If they destroy the center leaves, the plant cannot grow new leaves or form cobs properly, leading to severe crop loss.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛkwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpãtã teŋgbɛ baa lɛ hiɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ baa heei loo efee kui jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ waa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot and dry or when they do not get enough water. Giving the plants consistent moisture and light shade during hot spells helps flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ Kɛ́ tso lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I properly extract seeds from my harvested crops so they do not get damaged for the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbala dumɔwui kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ? Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Extracting seeds requires gently separating them from the pulp or pod and drying them in a shaded, well-ventilated area. Using wrong tools or leaving moisture on the seeds causes mold and ruins their ability to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ajiemɔ biɔ ni agbala dumɔwui lɛ amli blɛoo kɛjɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛfɔ̃ shi koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu abote mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii loo ashi ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How do I know when a crop is mature enough for me to collect good seeds from it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ dumɔwui kpakpai?

english: Seeds should only be collected when the fruit or pod is fully mature or naturally dried on the plant. Harvesting seeds too early means they will not have enough energy stored to germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ abua dumɔwui anaa pɛ kɛji akɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa loo amɛgbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃.

english: Should I wash off the pulp or fruit juices from my seeds right after extracting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ni jɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie lɛ?

english: Yes, removing sugary fruit pulp and washing seeds clean prevents fungal growth and stops rot from destroying the seed coat while it is stored.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ahoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akpa be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved will actually sprout before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing a sample of 10 seeds in a moist cloth; counting how many sprout after a few days tells you the strength and quality of your seed batch.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛwoɔ mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okane bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni odumɔwui akuu lɛ mli wa ha kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha.

english: Why is it important for me to test my seed germination rate more than once before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka bɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa lɛ makwɛ fe shikome dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Testing seeds twice gives you confidence in your results and helps you catch any drop in seed quality caused by changes in heat or moisture during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui akasemɔi enyɔ haa onáa hekɛnɔfɔɔ yɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe nibii ni baa shi ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: If my germination test shows that only half of my seeds sprout, what should I do when planting?
ga: Kɛji mi kwɛ̃mɔ kaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fã pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji midu?

english: If only 50 percent of your seeds grow, you will need to plant extra seeds per hole or source fresh, higher-germinating seeds so your field does not end up with empty spaces.
ga: Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli oha mlijaa 50 pɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, ehe baahia ni odu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli loo okɛ dumɔwui heei ni shwereɔ babaoo aha. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔji lɛ akafee efolo.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them in good soil and give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ ni mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were damaged during extraction, stored in hot or damp conditions, or harvested before they were fully developed inside.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji amɛfite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Kɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. loo akpaa dani edaa kwraa yɛ emli

english: How can agricultural extension officers assist me with improving my seeds?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi koni midumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers can teach you correct seed extraction methods, demonstrate how to perform germination tests, and advise you on which crop varieties perform best in your area.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee ojie dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni akaa shweremɔ akwɛɔ. ni okɛ ŋaawoo aha yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the best way for me to store my extracted seeds so insects do not eat them before rains start?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mli egbala lɛ ato? Koni kooloi akaye amɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ.

english: Store thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers or sealed bags kept in a cool, dry place to keep out moisture and destructive pests like weevils.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni atsĩ mli mli. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why do crops grown from poorly extracted seeds often turn out weak or yield poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni ajieee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are damaged or cracked during extraction, the young embryo inside loses protection and vital food reserves, resulting in weak seedlings that cannot produce a full harvest.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ fite loo amɛgbala yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ hebuu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ egbɔjɔ kwraa, ni no hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akpa amɛ kwraa.

english: Why does the crop medicine I spray smell so strong, and does a stronger smell mean it kills pests better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbemɔ mli?

english: A strong smell does not always mean a chemical is stronger. Some medicines release vapors that drive away or suffocate insects hiding under leaves, while other effective medicines have no smell at all but kill pests when eaten.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be tsofai ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ tsɔɔ tsofai ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Tsofai komɛi jieɔ lasu ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ loo ehaa amɛmuɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai krokomɛi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Abɛ ŋmɔlɔ kwraa. Shi kɛ́ aye lɛ, egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why do some insects die immediately when I spray them, while others take a few days to die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi komɛi gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi heɔ gbii fioo dani amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Contact medicines kill insects instantly when the spray touches their bodies. Systemic medicines are absorbed into the plant leaves first, so insects only die a few days later after they chew or suck on the treated plant.
ga: Kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ kɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ kpe pɛ kɛkɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ abɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Akɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ ni kooloi lɛ gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛye loo amɛnu tsei ni atsa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can the pest medicine I spray on my crops end up damaging or burning the leaves?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite loo eshã baai lɛ?

english: Yes, if you mix the medicine stronger than recommended or spray during the hot afternoon sun, it can scorch crop leaves. It is best to mix accurately and spray early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni mli wa fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ futu mli loo okɛwo mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eha tso baai lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofutu lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: How can a spray kill pests that are hidden inside plant stems where the liquid cannot touch them?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ ni nu lɛ nyɛŋ ata amɛhe?

english: Certain medicines travel through the plant's sap system, turning the entire plant poisonous to chewing insects. When hidden pests feed on the stem from the inside, they ingest the medicine and die.
ga: Tsofai komɛi tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ye tso lɛ shishi kɛjɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaaye tsofa lɛ ni amɛgboi.

english: How do insects know when my maize is producing grains so that they attack it all at once?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi leɔ akɛ mi-abele lɛ baawo dumɔwui? No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtutua amɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Insects have a strong sense of smell and can detect natural scents released by crops when they bloom or produce sweet grains. They travel long distances following these smells to feed and lay eggs.
ga: Kplukai yɛ henumɔ ni mli wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ kɛji amɛfɔlɔ loo amɛwo dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ. Amɛfãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ amɛnyiɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ asɛɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my farm even after I have sprayed chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Even though I had already injected chemicals.

english: Chemical protection wears off after a few days or weeks due to sunlight, air, and rain washing it away. Once the smell or chemical effect disappears, new insects can fly in from surrounding bush or neighboring farms.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ gbii loo otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni hulu la, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, kɛ nugbɔ hoɔ tsofai lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo tsofa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ, kooloi heei baanyɛ ajɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli aba. loo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that carry plant diseases, or by a lack of nutrients in the soil. Inspecting under the leaves helps identify the cause.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa Kɛ́ akwɛ baa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ana nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Is it better to spray my crops before I see any insects, or should I wait until the pests appear?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani ana ŋmeii lɛ? Aloo ehi akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi tsɛŋemɔ helai baaje kpo?

english: It is best to inspect your farm regularly and spray as soon as you see the first signs of pests. Spraying too early without pests wastes money, while waiting too long allows pests to destroy the crop.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ kɛji ona klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛ. Shika ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ oya tsɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ ji shika fitemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Will the pest medicine I use on my cocoa trees also kill the friendly insects that help produce fruit?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ hu?

english: Yes, many broad-spectrum chemical sprays kill both harmful pests and beneficial insects like pollinators. Spraying late in the afternoon when friendly insects are less active helps protect them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ shwane mli be mli ni kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ tsuuu nii tsɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why is the same chemical medicine I have used for years no longer killing the caterpillars on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii afii babaoo lɛ nɔŋŋ egbeee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you use the exact same medicine repeatedly, the surviving pests build up resistance over time. Rotating between different types of crop medicines prevents insects from becoming immune.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ wala lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsofai ni atsakeɔ kɛtsaa tsei ahe helai srɔtoi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa kooloi ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ akaná hewalɛ ni gbeɔ helai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I do not plant shade crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive under rainforest foliage. Direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out topsoil, whereas shade plants like plantains shield them from excessive heat and help maintain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ baai ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ koo lɛ mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains lɛ buɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures become extreme, pepper plants experience heat stress and drop their blossoms to conserve water and energy, preventing fruit formation until milder conditions return.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ baakpe ni amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Tsi yibiiwoo naa kɛyashi shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, which is the primary nutrient crops need to stay green and build leafy biomass.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛma baai lɛ amli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I grow maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my farmland better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water trapped in heavy soil cuts off air to the cassava roots, causing root suffocation and creating ideal conditions for soil-borne fungal rots to destroy the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves starting near the ground after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops bounce off the soil and splash fungal spores onto the lower leaves, where wet conditions allow leaf-spot diseases like blight to infect the plant and spread upward.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ haa baa mli helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny fruits when I sow the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no individual plant with enough energy to grow strong stems or large fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo tsei ni wa loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do yam vines grow larger tubers when they are trained to climb up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high above ground level so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for tuber growth, while keeping foliage dry and clear of ground diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi ni hela akafee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding deep inside the center whorl of my maize plants eating the young leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ miiye baai bibii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, such as Fall Armyworms, seek out the tender funnel of the maize plant because it offers young tissue to feed on while hiding them from sunlight and predators.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ, taoɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ agbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ amɛhe teeɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: If I apply fertilizer to my crops but there is no rain, will the crops still grow well?
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shi nugbɔ enɛɛɛ Ani tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can drink it in. Without water, crops cannot absorb fertilizer nutrients, and dry fertilizer left in hot soil can even burn and damage plant roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Will adding extra fertilizer help my maize crop survive if drought comes?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋma lɛ ahi shi kɛji hɔmɔ ba?

english: No, extra fertilizer actually makes plants need more water and can dry them out faster. Crops need reliable water first before they can safely use fertilizer to grow.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, no haa nu babaoo he hiaa tso lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eha egbi oya. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia tsei dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly when the sun gets very hot and rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up as a defense mechanism to reduce their surface area facing the hot sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and stop water from evaporating too quickly during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi kɛji akɛ eshɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is wilting because of lack of water or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni bɛ loo hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Water deficiency makes the whole plant look soft, droop, and turn yellow evenly from the bottom leaves up. Plant diseases usually show up as spotted leaves, mold, or rotting parts on specific areas rather than overall wilting.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ, egbɔjɔ, ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ po. Kɛjɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ kpo akɛ baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi, ŋmeii, loo fãi ni egboi yɛ hei komɛi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbo fɛɛ

english: How can I keep my soil wet for a longer time after it rains so my crops do not dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akagbi?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass, leaves, or crop leftovers (mulch) shades the ground. This traps moisture in the earth and stops the heat of the sun from evaporating the water quickly.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ onibii amli. (Mulch) haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hulutsoo. Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekpa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ ni eha nu lɛ akaho oya.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil instead of soaking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard or bare ground cannot quickly absorb sudden heavy rainfall, causing water to rush over the surface and sweep soil away. Planting along ridges across slopes or keeping crop cover helps slow down rainwater so it can sink deep into the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ oya nɛkɛ. Enɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe loo nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I plant that will survive better if the rains stop early in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu ni baahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep roots or drought-hardy leaves that allow them to endure long periods without rain much better than crops like maize or rice.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds in dry soil before the rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi?

english: Seeds in dry soil stay dormant waiting for moisture, but if heat or pests attack them before heavy rains come, they may rot or fail to sprout. A tiny drizzle might trigger them to sprout, only to wither if regular rain does not follow immediately.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ehi shi ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ batutua dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu? Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbo loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ fioo ko baanyɛ aha amɛkwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to water my crops so the water doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu koni mikafite nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives the soil time to soak up moisture before the hot afternoon sun can evaporate it away into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Is there a simple way to keep water near my plant roots without buying expensive equipment?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha nu abɛŋkɛ tsei ashishifãi ahe ni aheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can bury small, perforated clay pots or plastic bottles filled with water next to your crops. Water will slowly seep out directly to the roots over several days without wasting a drop on the surface.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofu shikpɔŋ sũ tsɛnsi bibioo ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ plastic tsinsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Nu lɛ baaho fiofio kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbii babaoo mli ni efiteee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa yɛ nɔ.

english: Why is the ground under my mature cocoa trees always so soft and covered with dark leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ blɛoo be fɛɛ be ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: The falling leaves from cocoa trees decompose into rich organic matter, forming a natural protective carpet. This layer holds soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and feeds your crop naturally without requiring expensive fertilizers.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Efeɔ adebɔɔ mli kapɛti ni buɔ mɔ he Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why is it bad for my cocoa farm if the soil becomes hard and stiff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ ehiii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Hard, compacted soil prevents cocoa roots from breathing and spreading easily to gather water and nutrients. Keeping the ground soft and covered with leaf litter allows root systems to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛbua nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee bɔdɔɔ ni akɛ baai shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: I notice green moss growing on the soil under my cocoa trees; does this mean my soil is safe for farming?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii eŋɔli ni miikwɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Moss usually shows that the soil is moist and shaded, which cocoa roots like. However, if the area stays too wet and dark, it can lead to fungal diseases like black pod, so you need to make sure enough sunlight passes through the canopy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kookoo shishifãi sumɔɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ he lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ duŋ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji hu aba, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ abote tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm soil is healthy without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛteeee laboratori?

english: Healthy cocoa soil is dark, soft underfoot, holds moisture well, smells fresh, and has a thick layer of rotting leaf litter with earthworms visible near the surface.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Naji shishi ni yɔɔ blɛoo Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee. ni baai bibii ni egboi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi.

english: Should I clear away all the small plants and fallen leaves lying on the soil under my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei bibii lɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ? Ni baai fɛɛ ni egbee shikpɔŋ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: No, you should keep the soft layer of fallen leaves on the ground. This leaf cover stops the hot sun from drying out the soil and prevents heavy rain from washing away the good topsoil.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fã ko ato shikpɔŋ. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ nɛɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us not to let tall weeds and undergrowth grow high under cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkaŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi shwere yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Tall undergrowth steals water and fertilizer away from your cocoa roots. High weeds also trap moisture around the tree trunks, creating a wet environment where black pod disease spreads easily.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ okkoo shishifãi lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ. tso shishi Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa plants need gentle shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and hot winds. Without shade trees, intense sun burns the cocoa leaves and dries out the topsoil too quickly.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli jɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã kookoo baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why is it important to prune low branches under the main canopy of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning low branches allows fresh air to move freely through the farm. Better airflow lowers the moisture trapped under the trees, which stops pod diseases from taking over.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni jɛɔ pod mli lɛ akamɔ mɔ.

english: How deep do cocoa roots go into the ground to find food?
ga: Te kookoo shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii?

english: Most of a cocoa tree's feeding roots grow very close to the surface of the soil, right beneath the layer of leaf litter. Protecting the top few inches of soil is essential for feeding the tree.
ga: Kakao tsei babaoo ashishifãi ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ waa. Yɛ baa lɛ shishi jwɛi lɛ shishi pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi inchi fioo lɛ nɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ he miihia kɛha tsei niyenii.

english: Why should I space my cocoa seedlings far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fe bɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough room underground for its roots to feed and enough space above for leaves to catch sunlight without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii. Ni he ko yɛ ŋwɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baa lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand intense, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose moisture fast. They need overhead shade trees or plantains to shield them from high heat until their roots and branches grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa lɛ shãa oya, ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ ni haa amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing my maize seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the land receives two or three heavy, steady rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry period immediately follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baaná. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli shikome lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural food from the air through their roots and trap it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind rich fertilizer that helps future crops grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava and maize too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Cassava and maize both feed heavily on the same nutrients and moisture in the upper soil. Planting them too close makes them fight for food, which leaves both crops stunted with smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa waa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii he. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people spread dry grass or cocoa pods on the soil around their vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai aŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry materials, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil too quickly. It keeps the roots cool, saves water, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehaa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers from my plantain tree instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: When a plantain tree produces many suckers, the main stem has to share its food and water with all of them. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant yields a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Esa akɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ amɛ fɛɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of fresh air and direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and increasing tuber size.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by small whiteflies. Planting disease-free cassava cuttings is the best way to prevent the sickness from taking over your field.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Mɛi ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Kasava ni helai bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa koni ekaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there holes in the centers of my young maize leaves with dark powdery dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu yɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize plant to feed. Treating the field early protects the growing center before the whole stem is ruined.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he dani tso lɛ tso lɛ fɛɛ akpata hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its food and needs fertilizer or animal manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, remain short, turn pale yellow instead of dark green, and produce tiny harvests despite good rain, your soil has run out of essential nutrients and needs plant food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa, eyɛ kuku, etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni ekɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ wo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsei niyenii he miihia lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily whenever heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain softens the topsoil and weakens the grip of the roots. When the base of the soil becomes muddy and weak, strong winds during rainstorms easily push the root foundation out of the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛɔ he lɛ hu gbɔjɔɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ bafeɔ muji ni egbɔjɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre shishitoo nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my yam mounds crumble and wash away after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ shwie shi ni eho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Loose soil without organic matter breaks down easily when heavy rain hits it directly. Mixing compost into the soil helps bond the earth together so the mounds hold their structure against rain erosion.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpɛtɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni abua naa lɛ haa tsũ lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni nugbɔ akafite lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down when the soil around their base gets soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and rely on firm soil for support. When heavy water turns the earth into soft mud, the soil loses its strength and can no longer hold up the heavy weight of the plantain tree.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛdamɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ kɛha yelikɛbuamɔ. Kɛ́ nu ni fa babaoo lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɔ muji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa, ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ atsu nii dɔŋŋ.

english: How does flowing rainwater destroy the soil around the base of my crops?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When rainwater runs quickly across bare soil without ridges or grass to slow it down, it eats away the topsoil, exposing the roots and leaving plants with no solid foundation to absorb nutrients.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nu hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii loo jwɛi bɛ nɔ ni baaha egbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ nu baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ ajiemɔ Ni enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when too much water sits on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the land without draining, it starves the roots of air, causing them to decay underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off when the soil stays flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Flooded soil starves cocoa roots of oxygen. Without air, the root system fails and can no longer send water and food up to the leaves, causing the leaves to yellow, dry out, and fall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ anáa kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ No lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt even when there is plenty of water sitting in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miigbo eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Standing water suffocates and destroys the fine root hairs that drink water. Once these root tips die from lack of air, the plant can no longer take up moisture, causing it to wilt even in wet soil.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ gboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po.

english: Why do seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after a big rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ sũ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a mix of air and moisture to sprout. Too much standing water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the seeds and encouraging fungal rots before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni akɛfee ekome dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from eating away my raised vegetable beds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaye mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Digging small drainage channels between your raised beds directs excess water safely away from the soil walls, keeping the bed structures firm and protecting young root bases.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ gbɛ bibioo ko ni aaafo yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ gbogboi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa saatso lɛ shishitoo lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ebuɔ shishitoo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does soil that holds too much water cause my crop roots to decay in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Soil with poor drainage acts like a soaked sponge that traps water around the base of the plant. This constant wetness weakens the plant's natural defenses and allows root-eating fungal diseases to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni efɔ, ni emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I avoid putting my bags of harvested rice directly on the bare floor in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ kotokui ni mikɛbaawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Putting rice bags directly on the floor exposes them to dampness trapped in the ground. Placing wooden pallets underneath creates a gap so air can pass under the bags, keeping your rice dry and preventing mould.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kotokui wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni mli edɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ wo shishi lɛ, ehaa gbɛ ko baa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ kotoku lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ egbiɔ ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmãa naa.

english: How should I arrange my crop bags inside my storeroom so I can inspect them easily?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mato mi tsei ahe kotokui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ mli mlɛo?

english: You should leave clear walkways between the stacks of bags and the walls. This creates easy access to move around, inspect for dampness or pests, and carry bags out without disturbing the entire store.
ga: Esa akɛ gbɛ ko ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ahi kotokui ni ato lɛ kɛ gbogbo lɛ teŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaanyɛ aya he kroko. Kwɛmɔ kɛji hulutsoo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ mli. ni ojie kotoku lɛ ni okɛgbaaa shwapo muu lɛ fɛɛ naa

english: Is it bad practice to stack my bags of grain right against the storehouse walls?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ akɛ dumɔwui kotokui baawo tsũ lɛ gbogbo lɛ he?

english: Yes, building walls can draw dampness from rain outside. Stacking bags against walls transfers that moisture to your grain and blocks the airflow needed to keep the crop cool and fresh.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbogboi ni ama lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ gbogbo lɛ he lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmaa lɛ mli, ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ehee lɛ naa.

english: Can I use raised wooden platforms to hold my harvested crops inside the storage room?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ ato mikpamɔ lɛ he yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yes, raised wooden platforms or pallets are ideal. They lift the grain above floor dampness and allow fresh air to blow beneath and around the bags to protect your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni awo nɔ loo pallets lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atswa yɛ kotokui lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛhe koni ebu onibii ahe

english: Why is it important to leave space for air to blow around my stacked rice bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi he ko koni kɔɔyɔɔ atswa kɛbɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-ŋmãa kotokui ni ato lɛ he miihia.

english: Air movement helps remove trapped heat and sweat that naturally come off stored grain. Without good airflow around the bags, moisture builds up and causes the rice to spoil quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa ni jɛɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ kotoku lɛ he lɛ, Fɛ̃i baabua ehe naa ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afite oya.

english: What does 'moisture content' mean when officers talk about storing harvested grain like rice?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘muji ni yɔɔ mli’ lɛ shishi beni onukpai lɛ wieɔ ŋmaa ni akpa tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he?

english: Moisture content is simply the amount of water trapped inside the grain. If there is too much water left in the rice when you store it, the grain will heat up, rot, or attract insects.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ ji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ pɛ. Kɛji nu babaoo eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli beni okɛtoɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baadɔ, ebaagbo, loo ebaagbala kooloi bibii.

english: How does proper drying help my harvested rice last longer in storage?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa baanyɛ aye abua mikpamɔ lɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Drying reduces the moisture content inside the grain to a safe level. Low moisture stops fungi, mould, and insects from growing, allowing your rice to stay good for many months.
ga: Gbimɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Fɛ̃i ni baa shi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ koolooi adalɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo.

english: What usually causes stored rice to turn black, smell bad, or rot after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni haa bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, efuɔ, loo egboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Spoilage usually happens when rice is put into storage with too much water inside it or packed tightly without airflow. The trapped moisture creates heat and mould, which ruins the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa wo tsɛnsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli loo akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ

english: Why does damp or humid air inside a storage room harm my dried rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Dry grain acts like a sponge and will suck up water from humid air. Good airflow inside the storage room keeps the air fresh and prevents the rice from soaking up moisture again.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested rice is dry enough for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a kernel with your teeth or cracking it with your fingernail; if it breaks with a sharp snap without feeling soft or sticky, the moisture content is low enough for safe storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onyanyɔji loo onineshi ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛji etswa oya ni enuuu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does clearing neat lines on my farmland help my plantain crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ linei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ midumɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing neat rows reduces weed competition for sunlight and soil nutrients, makes it easier for you to walk around and care for your crops, and ensures each plantain plant gets enough space to stretch its roots and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ akaŋshimɔ kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Ha onyiɛ ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ koni dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakpa eshishifãi kɛ ebaai lɛ.

english: Why does leaving heavy weeds around my crop stems cause them to produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi ni tsii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mi stems lɛ haa amɛwoɔ yibii fioo?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal water, fertilizer, and light directly from your crop's roots, leaving your plants weak and unable to build big fruits or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efee aduawai wuji loo bulbs.

english: Can I plant other smaller crops between my plantain rows, or will that damage my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei bibii krokomɛi? Ani abaanyɛ afee enɛ yɛ mi plantains ni ato lɛ ateŋ? Aloo no baafite mi-plantain lɛ?

english: You can safely plant short crops like legumes or vegetables between wide plantain rows when the plantains are young; this maximizes your land use without choking the plantains, provided the smaller crops do not shade them.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai yɛ plantain ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ ateŋ shweshweeshwe beni plantain lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Enɛ baaha okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ akafo mli. he ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ bɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take almost a whole year before they start producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani amɛjeɔ aduawai akui afeemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require 9 to 12 months to develop a solid root system and grow massive leaves capable of capturing enough solar energy to feed and support a heavy cluster of plantain fruits.
ga: Ehe miihia ni plantain lɛ aná nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ená shishifãi ni wa ni ekwɛ baai wuji ni baanyɛ ato hulu hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛye plantain yibii akui wuji lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua amɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up as the plant gets taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, older bottom leaves naturally die off to send energy up to newer leaves, but if many leaves turn yellow early, it signals that the plant is thirsty or lacking nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Beni okɛ ekãa kwɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ gboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha baa heei. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ, no lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ loo niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ehe.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and healthy on one side of my farm but stay stunted on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome shi amɛmiiya hiɛ yɛ fa kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality and moisture vary across the same plot of land; areas with shallow soil, poor water retention, or fewer natural nutrients will cause crops to stay smaller unless organic manure or fertilizer is added.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he kome mli. He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nu nyɛɛɛ ahi mli jogbaŋŋ Aloo he ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo. ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so fast when it takes two or three days to transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni eheɔ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops continue to breathe and lose water after harvest; heat and rough handling during long trips accelerate this process, causing fruits to soften, dry out, and rot much faster.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo, egbiɔ ni egboɔ oya kwraa.

english: What happens to plantains if I harvest them and leave them lying in the open sun for a few days?
ga: Mɛni baa plantains nɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ ni mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Direct sunlight bakes harvested plantains, causing them to ripen uncontrollably fast, turn mushy, and lose their freshness before you can sell them.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã plantains ni akpa lɛ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ, egboɔ, ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my plantains so they do not ripen before I reach my buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mi-plantains lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ekakwɛ̃ dani eshɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ?

english: Harvest plantains when the individual fingers are plump and rounded but still completely green, as this gives them maximum shelf life during travel before they turn yellow.
ga: Kpãa plantains lɛ beni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ kokroo shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lolo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaaha ehi shi be babaoo yɛ gbɛfaa mli dani etsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I store my harvested crops safely for a few extra days if I cannot immediately find a buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ minibii ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe gbii fioo komɛi krokomɛi? Ni kɛji akɛ minaaa mɔ ko ni baahe mi amrɔ nɔŋŋ hu?

english: Keep your harvested crops off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated, and shaded area away from direct heat to slow down natural ripening and prevent premature rotting.
ga: Ha okpamɔ lɛ aka shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo, ni hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ akashɛ he. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo ni ekɛtsi fitemɔ ni baa oya lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth, or that the soil is waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when daytime temperatures get too high, when the soil lacks water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, or when soil-dwelling fungi attack the roots in flat ground without proper mounds or ridges to drain excess rain.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tutua shishifãi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gɔŋji loo ŋmeii ni sa bɛ ni amɛkɛjie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rain starts falling in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje tsei afeemɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become regular for a week or two to soak the soil deeply, rather than planting right after the first rain, which can stop quickly and dry out your seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa otsi kome loo enyɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. ni baanyɛ akpa oya ni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Why did the seeds I stored from my last maize harvest fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ lɛ?

english: Stored seeds can lose their ability to sprout if they were kept in a warm or humid place, damaged by insects like weevils, or if the original seed was a hybrid variety designed for single-use planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii efite loo kɛji akɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii shikome pɛ.

english: Why is it wrong to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the farm or pushes it too deep into the ground where the roots cannot reach it, wasting your effort and investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ekɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the corn and vegetables I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to survive tough conditions; they have stronger root systems that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your planted crops can get them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ baanyɛ aná.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sun; fast-growing plantain trees have broad leaves that act as green umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil cool while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi eŋɔli. Ha kookoo lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to construct tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kakadaŋŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight; the more sunlight the leaves capture, the more energy the plant produces to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni hi. Hewalɛ babaoo ni tso lɛ jieɔ lɛ koni ekɛgbala tuber lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to appear suddenly and destroy the leaves inside my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa ni amɛfiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which come from eggs laid by moths on the corn leaves; the larvae hide inside the central leaves of the plant to feed in safety where heat and birds cannot reach them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ amli. Lalai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ okpoi nyɛɛɛ aya jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water during dry or hot periods. It is the plant's natural way of surviving high heat until it gets moisture again.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite babaoo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli ni enáa fɛ̃i ekoŋŋ.

english: Too much water drowns the roots by pushing out air from the soil. Without air, roots begin to rot and cannot absorb nutrients, causing the plant to wilt even though the soil is wet.
ga: Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ ŋmɔtɔ po.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving some shade trees or planting shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and protects the seedlings.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo odu hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: When plantains are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them enough space ensures each plant gets full nutrition to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee tso ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to sticks instead of letting them grow on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei aniji ahe moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds tomato plants off the wet soil, which prevents soil-borne diseases from splashing onto the leaves and stops the fruit from rotting. It also helps the plant get better sunlight and airflow.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tomato tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekashwie baai lɛ anɔ, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ akafite. Ehaa tsei hu naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?
