english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape mean the plant is short on nitrogen, which gives leaves their deep green color. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the crop recover.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ V-shape, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen in the soil. Maintaining steady moisture helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava draws a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Growing it continuously in the same spot exhausts the soil and allows cassava-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmei pɔtɛɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava crop has the mosaic disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ mosaic hela?

english: Cassava mosaic disease makes the leaves look twisted, yellow, and patchy instead of smooth and green. Affected plants cannot grow proper tubers, so removing sick stems stops whiteflies from spreading it to healthy plants.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etsilɛ, ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, baai ɔmɛ ngɛ tsɔe nɛ a ngɛ ŋmɔŋ. Tsei ni ena hela lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ bulbs ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need both moisture and warmth to sprout. If they are buried too deep, they run out of stored energy before reaching the surface, and if the soil is too dry, they stay dormant until rain falls.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, ebaakã shi ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hottest part of the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During scorching afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. Wilting is the plant's natural defense mechanism to curl its leaves, reduce its exposure to the sun, and conserve water until the heat drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ebaa hulu la shi, ni ekɛ nu toɔ kɛyashi dɔlɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is growing fast, causing the bottom cells of the fruit to break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo enaa nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This can happen due to Cherelle Wilt, where the cocoa tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot support, or due to Black Pod fungal disease caused by high humidity. Good pruning and spacing help clear extra moisture and protect healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli yɛ Cherelle Wilt hewɔ, he ni cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ebɔɔ su naa lɛ. aloo yɛ black pod fungus hela ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ sɛɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aya hiɛ ni ebu pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by plant viruses spread by insects. It can also happen when plants try to save water during severe heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need full sunlight to produce energy to swell tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, increases sunlight exposure, and prevents leaf rot caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ koni bulbs lɛ adara. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni edɔ lɛ, hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaatsi baai ni sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and natural cracks will appear in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii baaje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Stem base beni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops before putting down fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that will drink up the fertilizer before your crops can reach it. Clearing weeds first ensures that your crop roots absorb all the expensive food you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni baaye ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is my plantain farm taking so long to produce bunches compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ ŋmeii baa kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require rich soil full of potassium and constant moisture. If your soil is poor, dry, or full of competing weeds, the plant will focus only on leaf survival and delay flowering.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli daa. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii, egbi, loo jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaha baai lɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ ni ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why is it better to mix decayed manure into my farm soil instead of relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo baafata ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Decayed manure acts like a sponge that improves soil structure, helping it retain rainwater and nutrients long-term. Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant quickly, but manure builds and protects the soil health season after season.
ga: Muji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii maa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the tips down the middle, it usually means the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that helps plants build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts together with maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them with maize helps feed the soil and gives the maize naturally available nutrients without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛsaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa abele lɛ náa niyenii ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when I plant them in a clear, sunny open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are naturally delicate shade-loving crops. Direct heat from the sun scorches their fresh leaves, so planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby gives them the living shelter and moisture they need to grow safely during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ji tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai heei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves fully towards sunlight to manufacture food. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground away from heat and rot, allowing the plant to direct its energy underground to grow big tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fitemɔ akashɛ he. Ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillars hiding inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ekɛ ehe ewo koni lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which feeds on the growing point of young maize plants, especially during hot and dry spells, reducing the crop's ability to develop cobs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants start wilting and rotting at the root after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ kɛ shwiemɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in the soil starves the pepper roots of air and allows harmful soil fungi to attack the stem base, causing root rot disease.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni eha sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua tso lɛ shishi. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my garden egg plants fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress—such as excessive hot weather, irregular water supply, or lack of insect pollinators like bees to transfer pollen between blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni baaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Aloo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ baatsɔ fɔfɔi ateŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready for harvesting without digging up every stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛ tso fɛɛ tso tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, the main stems show thick growth, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ yɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds in one single hole close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crowding seeds in one hole causes intense competition for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stalks with small or missing maize cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ni bɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous year's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller ears than the original seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo toi bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui akuu ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields in their first generation only. Planting seeds saved from that harvest causes the next generation to lose that vigor, yielding smaller plants and fewer grains.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ ana nakai hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when rain water sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When standing water collects around plant roots, it cuts off oxygen to the roots and promotes fungal diseases. Digging simple drainage channels allows excess water to flow away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ mli Enɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Is it possible for my crops to get too much rain during the heavy wet season?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná nugbɔ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, too much water suffocates root systems by replacing air pockets in the soil with water, which stunts crop growth and prevents plants from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛtoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ adara, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa.

english: How can I stop heavy rainfall from washing away the topsoil on my sloping land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops along the natural curves (contours) of the land or constructing soil ridges across slopes helps slow down rainwater, preventing it from washing away valuable topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta (shape) lɛ he loo ŋtayaai ni afee yɛ ŋtayaai anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ aba shi. ni etsĩ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rice thrive in low, wet areas where other crops like maize die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa gboi yɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that transport oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas crops like maize submerge and drown under wet conditions.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa boteɔ nu shishi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant rice using only rainfall without setting up irrigation systems?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ nugbɔ nu pɛ atsu nii kɛdu ŋmãa ni atooo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ko?

english: Yes, rain-fed rice farming works well in regions with high, predictable rainfall, provided you select lowland areas or river valleys that naturally retain soil moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji ohala shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo faa jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Does heavy rain wash away the fertilizers I apply to my soil?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain can wash fertilizers down below the root zone or sweep them off the farm entirely through runoff, a process known as leaching.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ ahe loo ejie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after a heavy rainstorm hits right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash seeds out of the soil completely or pack heavy topsoil tightly over them, making it impossible for tiny sprouts to break through the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kwraa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni naa wa lɛ abɔ amɛhe. feemɔ ŋmeii bibii Enyɛŋ ebote ŋwɛi

english: Why do crops grow well in my area even if the soil doesn't look very rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kwraa moŋ.

english: Frequent rainfall keeps soil constantly damp, making it easier for plant roots to dissolve and absorb whatever sparse nutrients are present in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛ baa shwie shi ni amɛ ŋɔ niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant crops like cassava on higher ground rather than down in low valleys?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tso ko tamɔ ŋmei yɛ hei ni kwɔlɔ moŋ fe jɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots swell underground and need well-draining soil; high ground prevents water from pooling around the tubers and causing them to rot before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. He ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he ni eha amɛgboi dani akpa.

english: How do I check if a piece of land holds too much water before I start clearing it for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa tsɔ dani mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Look at the wild plants growing there and test how long water sits after a rainfall; if water ponds for days or soft mud persists, the soil has poor drainage and is best suited for water-loving crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. ni oka be abɔ ni nu lɛ baahi shi yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ nubu lɛ ehi jɛmɛ gbii babaoo loo muji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away and waterlogged the roots, preventing them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why are my maize stalks remaining weak and stunted even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli po lɛ?

english: A parasitic weed called Striga (witchweed) may have attached itself to the roots of your maize underground, stealing the plant's water and nutrients before the maize can grow.
ga: Jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga (witchweed) lɛ baanyɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmã shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight because their small root systems cannot absorb water fast enough. Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without developing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is under stress from dry weather, lacks essential nutrients, or has been attacked by pests like mirids (capsids) during the flowering stage.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutuaa amɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when plants are left in waterlogged soil with poor drainage, allowing fungal diseases in the soil to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ashi tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to go through the stress of staking my yam vines high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋmɛ mitsui shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves toward sunlight so the plant can make enough food to produce big tubers, while also keeping the leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal foliage diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ koni ŋmeii akaye baai lɛ anɔ helai.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main stem for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Keeping only 2 to 3 strong suckers ensures your main plant grows big, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo tsɔ baaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and the fruit staying tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni aduawai lɛ hu ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when soil moisture fluctuates too drastically between extreme dry and wet spells, or when day temperatures become too hot for pollination to occur.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ fe nine yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa kɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa lɛ teŋ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ ni pollination nyɛŋ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and die right at the soil level shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This condition is called 'damping-off,' which occurs when soil fungi attack weak seedling stems because the seedbed is kept too wet or the seeds were planted too close together.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutua dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ashishifãi Enɛ ji akɛ, he ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, an important food for plants. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant pulls it from older lower leaves to send it to the newer growth on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛmaje ŋwɛi ŋtayaa hee lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my young corn with dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ náa muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛhe lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing leaf center. The sawdust-like matter is its waste, and catching it early helps protect your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni tamɔ ŋmei ji jwɛi. ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress, which prevents successful pollination and stops fruits from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in the same soil drains the specific nutrients that crop uses and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up and attack future harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hoɔ. ni eye ebua tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ni amɛtoɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ ni amɛtutuaa amɛ.

english: Excess water in heavy rains fills the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots due to a lack of oxygen and allowing fungal diseases to easily rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ afite oya

english: Why do my pepper plants give smaller fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too close together, their roots and leaves compete heavily for light, water, and soil food, leaving less energy for each plant to grow large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso fɛɛ tso bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why do I need to stick wood in the soil for my yam leaves to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and swell the underground tubers to a large size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la babaoo he bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyashɛɔ agbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the shade trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile like human babies and burn under intense direct sunlight; they need shade trees to regulate temperature and keep the air moist around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the wet soil, so they wilt temporarily to save moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi.

english: Why do weeds still stunt my crops even after I have already put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ

english: Weeds grow faster and take up nutrients more aggressively than planted crops, meaning they steal the fertilizer you applied before your crops get a chance to use it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. Providing consistent water and shade during very hot periods helps the plant hold its flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? lots dani etsɔ agbo

english: This is a natural process called cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree realizes it does not have enough water or soil nutrients to nourish all the pods, so it discards the extra small ones to protect the rest.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilting. Ebaa beni tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha tso lɛ mli tso lɛ fɛɛ aná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshiɔ pod bibioo ko kwraa koni ekɛbu fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but produce small ears with few kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi eyɛ toi fioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Maize planted too close together or given too much nitrogen grows tall searching for light, but lacks the space, sunlight, and balanced nutrients needed to fill out full ears of corn.
ga: Abɛi ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ni akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha lɛ baaha abɛi lɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi, ni etao la lɛ. Shi ebɛ he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmãa toi amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and feeding nearby maize crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects in heavy soil without good drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why is burning bushes on my field before planting harmful to my future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter, beneficial soil insects, and natural nutrients. Leaving cleared plants to decompose creates a protective mulch that keeps the soil cool, moist, and fertile.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaves so quickly in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miifite mi-corn tsei lɛ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: A single fall armyworm moth lays hundreds of eggs that hatch all at once. The young caterpillars hide deep inside the plant leaves where they feed continuously day and night, causing rapid damage.
ga: Moth caterpillar kome fɔɔ wuji ohai abɔ ni amɛwoɔ yɛ be kome mli. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei ahe baai amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyaa nɔ amɛtaoɔ niyenii shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ fɛɛ. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing is typically caused by a viral disease spread by tiny whitefly insects that suck plant sap. Controlling whiteflies early prevents the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. plant sap sucker Mra Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable crops in the middle of the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaaha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering in full heat causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching root systems, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch the plant or create damp heat that breeds fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei loo ekɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of holes and turn to dust inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu kɛ sũ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside maize kernels before or during harvest. In storage, those eggs hatch into larvae that eat the grain from the inside out, which can be prevented by thoroughly drying grains and using sealed Hermetic bags.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui amli dani akpa loo yɛ be mli ni akpaa, yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ vacuum kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ atsu nii

english: How do I know if the oil palm seedlings I am buying will produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ oil palm dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baawo ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: High-yielding oil palm seedlings usually come from certified sources like the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) or recognized research institutes. Seedlings bought from uncertified sellers often grow into trees that yield very small fruits or take too many years to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tso dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jɛɔ hei ni awo he odaseyeli tamɔ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) loo niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni bɛ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii bibii waa loo amɛheɔ afii babaoo tsɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I stop free-roaming cattle and animals from eating my young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsinai kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni nyiɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛheee nɔ ko lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Protecting young crops from livestock requires physical barriers like fencing with wire, planting dense living hedges around the border of your farm, or setting up dedicated paths for animals so they do not stray into your crop fields.
ga: Ni ooobu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii, tamɔ waya ni akɛwoɔ gbogbo mli kɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛdumɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa. aloo gbɛi pɔtɛɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ oha kooloi srɔtoi Enɛ baatsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkabɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow leaves and green up. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its strong green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Even with heavy rain, weeds will steal the soil nutrients before your crops can absorb them, so removing weeds early keeps your crops growing fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ, shi jwɛi hu baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua onibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are placed too close together, their roots fight over the limited soil food and cannot expand. Proper spacing gives each root enough room to swell and produce large, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ŋmei wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Is it helpful to cut off extra stems from my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, removing small side branches (called suckers) helps the tomato plant send all its energy into developing bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on making extra leaves and weak stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji bibii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ baafata he lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the middle of the day when it is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during hot afternoons as a natural way for the plant to save water and keep from drying out. If the leaves bounce back and open up in the evening or morning, the plant is doing fine, but if they stay limp, the soil needs water.
ga: Kɛ́ oha oyitsɔi shwie shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he. Kɛji baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ni amɛgbele gbɛkɛ loo leebi Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ nyiɛ lolo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia nu.

english: Can I put dry fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing concentrated chemical fertilizer directly against a plant stem can burn the stem and roots, killing the crop. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni gboiɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi.

english: What is causing tiny holes to appear all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? ni shwieɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in leaves are typically caused by destructive insects or caterpillars feeding on the crop. Spraying natural remedies like neem seed solution or safe pesticides early on controls these pests before they destroy the whole leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli tsofa loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Koni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite baa muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can visiting a local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) office help my farm?
ga: Te Saramɔ ni yaa Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) nitsumɔhe ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: MoFA officers provide free expert advice tailored to your location, help you find disease-resistant seeds, teach you correct planting techniques, and show you how to treat crop diseases before you lose your yield.
ga: MoFA nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ ŋaawoo ni he esa ni sa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ haa yaka. Ye obua bo ni ona dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui ahe ŋaai ni ja ni etsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee otsa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai dani onibii lɛ afite.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of your maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I keep planting maize on the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas gives the soil a rest and puts good nutrients back into the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi aba shikpɔji ni aduɔ nii lɛ anɔ Abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four maize seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together in the same hole, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your seeds out gives each plant enough room to grow a thick stem and yield large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which feeds the plant and allows large tubers to develop underground. Keeping the leaves lifted off the wet ground also prevents them from rotting or catching diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb agboi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛgboi loo helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, long dry spells between watering, or a lack of plant food in the soil. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ teŋ. aloo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the roots, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil moist for much longer so you do not have to water as often.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the first major rains before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Seeds planted in completely dry soil sit idle and are easily stolen by ants, birds, or rodents. Planting in moist soil right after a good rain gives the seeds the immediate water they need to sprout fast and establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ŋmeii, okpoi, loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aju amɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage us to plant beans or cowpeas together with our cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ hewalɛ ni wɔkɛ wɔ ŋmãa ni wɔduɔ lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots to feed the soil. Planting them alongside cereals like maize or millet acts as a natural fertilizer for the whole farm.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa kɛha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack. You can also dig up one root to check if it is firm and full of starch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ otsa shishifã kome hu koni ona kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily and lose water quickly under direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them provides protective shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛtsiɔ hulutsoo naa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key plant food. The plant starves and pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the afternoon temperatures get too hot or when soil moisture changes too drastically from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat or water stress damages the flower pollen, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛbai lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water up from the ground. Leaf drooping is the plant's temporary defense mechanism to reduce its surface area under the sun and conserve water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hulu la shishi lɛ shi ni amɛbu nu he.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my field grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans are legumes that can pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When these roots decay, they feed the surrounding soil, making it richer for the maize without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ji nitrogen gas lɛ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fite lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii. Ha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. This competition stresses the plants, causing them to grow weak and spindly with poor harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Akaŋshii nɛɛ maa tsei anɔ mi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbi ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ baa.

english: Why should I plant my crops on mounds or ridges instead of flat ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi anɔ lɛ? Yɛ hei ni yɔɔ kplanaa nɔ najiaŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Building ridges or mounds lifts the crop roots above standing water, preventing roots from suffocating and rotting in waterlogged soil during heavy Ghanaian rains.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi loo gɔji ni afee lɛ woɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo ni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have strange yellow patches and look wrinkled and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni efite?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using stem cuttings from infected plants will continue the disease, so you should plant certified disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aya nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ odu ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up tightly like small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juice. Spraying early with neem oil extract or recommended pesticides helps clear the insects so normal leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi bibii kɛjɛ mli bɔni afee ni baai ni yɔɔ daa lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yams rot so quickly after I store them inside my yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛto sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot typically begins when tubers get bruised, cut, or damaged by farm tools during harvesting, allowing airborne fungi to enter. Storing undamaged, dry yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn stops rot organisms from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato fitemɔ jeɔ shishi kɛ́ ŋmɔ mli nibii fite, efo, loo efite yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ abote kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potatoes ni egbi ni efiteee lɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni fiteɔ lɛ akadara.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs manure before I plant my tomato seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli dani madu tomato dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had thin stems, or produced very small fruits, your soil nutrients are worn out. Adding well-rotted manure before planting replenishes the soil food so new seedlings can grow strong quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ da blɛoo, eyɛ tsei bibii, loo ewo yibii bibii waa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei lɛ anyɛ adara oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get double the harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa lɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in weak stalks and very small cobs. Proper spacing actually gives you a heavier, higher-quality harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha oná nibii ni tsii, ni hi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before turning into hot pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper yibii ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get too hot or dry out. Keeping the soil moist and covering the base of the plant with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool so the flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during windstorms. Support your plants by propping them up with strong wooden bamboo sticks or planting them deeper in rich soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli. Fi otsei lɛ asɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni wa ni okɛbaatsu nii loo ni ooodu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce better cobs when I plant cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni hi fe be mli ni miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen food from the air and trap it in the soil. Maize feeds on this extra food, so planting them together naturally feeds your maize and improves your crop yield.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi yeɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nanemɛi ni aduɔ nii lɛ haa oŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cassava stems after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong wild roots designed to steal water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your cassava stems full access to food so they can establish deep roots.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni afee koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tsei lɛ aná niyenii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ewo shishifãi.

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce many healthy pods while nearby trees stay bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need adequate sunlight, good air movement, and tiny insects to pollinate their flowers. Trees that are overcrowded, heavily shaded, or attacked by fungal black pod disease will drop their flowers and fail to produce pods.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia kokoo tsei. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli Tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. Shade ni mli wa yɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black fungus lɛ tutua bo lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa akafee.

english: If I cut the top stems of my cassava plants before harvest, will the tubers grow bigger?
ga: Kɛji ofo ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ dani okpa Ani yitso lɛ baafee agbo?

english: Trimming the top stems late in the season forces the plant to stop spending energy on leaves and redirect all its food energy down into growing thicker, fuller cassava tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be ni shɛɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekpa hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni mli tse ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to dust and get tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Weevils and insects lay eggs in warm, damp grain and eat the maize from the inside. Thoroughly drying your cobs in the sun and storing the grains in airtight bags (PICS bags) starves the pests of air and preserves your harvest.
ga: Weevils kɛ beetles woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ ni mli efɔ mli. ni oye ŋmãa kɛjɛ mli Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu mli ni okɛ ŋmãa lɛ to vacuum bags (PICS bags) mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli ni eye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɛɛ amɛ moŋ? Ni maha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Crops need food just like humans to grow strong. Water keeps the plant alive, but fertilizers supply essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that give crops the energy to grow quickly and build healthy leaves.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, niyenii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛdara waa. Nu haa tsei hiɔ shi. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo baai ni wa.

english: Will using too much fertilizer burn my crops and ruin my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baashã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni efite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer at once can scorch plant roots and dry out the leaves. It is important to use the correct measured amount so your crops get just enough nutrition without causing damage.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Ehe miihia ni okɛ yibɔ ni sa ni asusu lɛ atsu nii koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nɔ ko akafite.

english: How do I know the best time to put fertilizer on my maize or cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli?

english: Fertilizer works best when crops are actively growing—usually a few weeks after sprouting when roots are forming, and again right before flowering—so the plant absorbs the food before rains wash it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida waa. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii dani nugbɔ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Can feeding my crops with fertilizer actually help protect them from insects?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, well-fed crops grow thicker stems, stronger leaves, and natural defenses. Healthy, properly fertilized plants are much tougher and can naturally resist pest attacks better than weak, hungry plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Baai lɛ ahe wa fe tsutsu lɛ. ni abaanyɛ abu he yɛ adebɔɔ naa Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops suddenly get full of small holes and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii trukaa lɛ? ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Holes and yellow leaves are signs that insect pests are eating your plants and stealing their nutrients. Protecting your crops early with proper soil care and pest treatment stops insects before they destroy your whole farm.
ga: Buu kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ otsei lɛ miiju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe buu mra Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ Kpa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do pests attack my farm more heavily during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pest insects multiply quickly when the weather is warm and humid or when crops are weak and stressed. Knowing when these seasons start helps you prepare pest control measures before the insects arrive.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhaoɔ. Kɛ́ ole be ni nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni osaa ohe kɛha gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani amɛba.

english: What causes some farmers in my village to get a huge harvest while my farm produces very little?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Higher harvests come from nourishing the soil with the right fertilizer, using good seeds, and protecting young crops from pests and weeds so every plant reaches its full producing power.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa babaoo lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa haa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi ahe. Bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops look fine at first but produce small or weak fruits at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi ewoɔ yibii bibii loo ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops need the most energy when forming grain or fruit. If the soil runs out of nutrients mid-season or hidden pests attack the flowers, the crop cannot produce a full, abundant harvest.
ga: Hewalɛ he miihia tsei fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛmiiwo dumɔwui loo aduawai. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ. Anyɛɛɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akpa babaoo.

english: Why does my land yield less food every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Ni mi hu midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting crops year after year removes nutrients from the ground, leaving the soil exhausted. Adding fertilizer or organic matter restores those nutrients so your land can give you rich harvests again.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nakai niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Koni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ

english: How can a small farmer like me find reliable help when my crops show signs of sickness?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi aná yelikɛbuamɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ? Beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jieɔ hela he okadii akpo?

english: You can contact local agricultural extension officers or official farm helpline numbers to get expert advice on identifying plant diseases, choosing the right fertilizer, and protecting your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ loo oŋmɔ lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ nɔmba ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ona ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ tsei ahe helai ayɔsemɔ he. Nihalamɔ ni sa ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛbu onibii ahe

english: Why do some farmers burn their land before planting, and is it bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani amɛduɔ nii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning clears brush quickly, but the intense heat destroys natural nutrients and beneficial organisms in the topsoil. Over time, burning makes the soil dry and infertile, so clearing by hand or mulching is much better for long-term yields.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ mli tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air pockets in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without oxygen, plant roots rot and can no longer take up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to die.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa bɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to my crops when I apply it to the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer acts like vitamins for plants, providing essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that are missing from the soil. These nutrients help crops grow stronger, develop deep roots, and yield bigger harvests.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ vitamini kɛha tsei. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why should I plant legumes like groundnuts or beans on my plot instead of planting maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the soil of specific nutrients. Legumes have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally refreshing the land for future crops.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii srɔtoi komɛi. Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which directly results in larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade and cool moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei bibii ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo, baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How does leaving weeds in my farm hurt my maize crop?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy thieves on your farm—they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your maize plants. If you leave weeds uncontrolled, your maize will be weak, thin, and yield small ears.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi hiɛjoolɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛji oha jwɛi lɛ je amɛhe O-ŋmãa lɛ baafee mlɛo, ebaafee mlɛo ni ebaawo toi bibii.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four corn seeds into the same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole causes the young plants to crowd each other out. They end up fighting for the same small amount of water and soil food, leaving you with weak stalks that cannot produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off or curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping or curling leaves is cassava's natural defense against extreme heat and drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces its water loss and enters a resting state so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ŋmei he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to wrinkle up, and how do agrochemicals help?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Leaf wrinkling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites that spread plant viruses. Using the right pest control spray kills these insects, allowing new, healthy leaves to grow back normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ. ni ehaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow even though there is rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is pooling around the roots and choking them. Applying proper organic compost or recommended fertilizer helps restore the leaf color and tree health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu ebɔle ehe. shishifãi ni ekɛ shishifãi ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ baa Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs extra fertilizer to help my crops produce more?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: When soil is low on nutrients, crop leaves look pale green or yellow, growth becomes slow, and the pods remain small. Looking for these signs or testing the soil helps you know when to apply fertilizer.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ baafee blɛoo. ni ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lolo Okadii nɛɛ taomɔ loo oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ole be ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii awo mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around the base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your cocoa trees. They also harbor insect pests and trap excess moisture around the trunk, which promotes fungal diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Amɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he kɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni no kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: How do I know if the chemical spray I bought will protect my cocoa pods from black pod disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi amli ni miheɔ lɛ baabu kookoo ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛ black pod hela he?

english: Fungicides effective against black pod disease usually contain copper compounds. Spraying them onto young pods at the start of the wet season creates a protective coat that stops fungal spores from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛshiɔ black pod hela lɛ hiɛ akɔɔble nibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie ŋmeii bibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply chemical sprays on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the air is cooler and calm. High heat during midday can cause chemicals to evaporate quickly or burn crop leaves under direct sun.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ dioo. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya loo eha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi.
