english: Why should I prune the excess branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to reach inner branches, which reduces dampness that breeds fungal rot. It also directs the tree's energy into pod growth instead of leaf growth.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu kɛyaa pod dalɛ mli yɛ baai adalɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does having big shade trees affect how my cocoa trees grow?
ga: Te tsei wuji ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni mɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Moderate shade protects cocoa from harsh direct sunlight and retains soil moisture. However, too much shade blocks sun energy and traps humidity, which encourages pod diseases.
ga: Shade ni mli tse buɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo babaoo tsiɔ hulu hewalɛ naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni kɛ pod hela baa

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods dry up and turn dark brown while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ekomɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the tree has more pods than it can feed, but it can also be triggered by dry spells or insect damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso ko yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. Shi hulutsoo be loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: What causes cocoa flowers to drop off before they can form pods?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ fãa?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree suffers from heat stress, prolonged drought, or when tiny beneficial insects called midges are not present to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods in some harvest seasons compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ bei komɛi amli kɛ akɛto ekrokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Pod yield changes depending on rainfall timing, tree age, soil nutrition, and disease management from the previous season. Trees also naturally rest after a year of heavy production.
ga: Pod yibiiwoo tsakeɔ yɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ, tso lɛ afii, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli Tsei hu jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ afi ni amɛfee nii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves whatever food it has left from its older lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the bottom ones to yellow and die off.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: This is a plant's natural defense mechanism against heat. By rolling its leaves into tight tubes, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the harsh sun, which stops water from evaporating out of the leaf too quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli awo tsɔne ko ni mli wa mli lɛ nɔ. Abɛi baaye abua ni eha he ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground in the farm before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy soil holds too much water around them for long periods without draining, allowing ground fungi to breed and decay the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mɔ nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Eshɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hoɔɔɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni akpɔtɔ lɛ feɔ yakayaka nii ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are my yam plants growing very bushy with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or lacks balance with other nutrients like potassium, the yam plant spends all its energy producing thick green leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build a large tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ekɛ niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ potassium lɛ kpãaa gbee lɛ, sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛba shi koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they face severe heat stress, lack of water, or attack from insects like mirids. To survive, the tree sheds its flowers so it can save its water and energy for the rest of the plant.
ga: Bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkpe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni tswaa lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa tree turn black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a water-borne fungus that spreads fast when the farm is too damp and shaded. Trimming excess branches to let air and sunlight through helps dry the farm and protect the young pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni jɛɔ nu mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain stems break or fall over easily as soon as the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ oya lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes or excess moisture. Supporting heavy bearing trees with bamboo poles and building up soil at the base helps hold them firm against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii nyɛɔ amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ nematodes loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ ŋmei tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛ sũ ni amaa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning thick and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is mostly caused by a viral infection spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and irregular watering. Keeping whiteflies off the crop and maintaining steady soil moisture keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be mli Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers right after they open, instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when soil moisture swings rapidly from very dry to overly wet, or when temperatures get too high. Consistent, moderate watering and light shade during hot dry spells help flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, ni fa fioo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are there small holes appearing all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually eaten out by caterpillars, like the diamondback moth larvae, which lay eggs on the undersides of young leaves. Inspecting under leaves early and taking pest control measures keeps the leaves whole.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ kaabii baa lɛ mli lɛ. ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii lɛ ashishi Ni aaakwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni akɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from high heat while their root system develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. Clearing them allows the cocoa roots to get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods. Factors like dry weather, a lack of soil nutrients, or poor insect pollination cause the tree to shed extra flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ bafeɔ pod. Nibii tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni ehiii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods turn dark and shrivel up long before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So minɔ lɛ batsɔ duŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It is a natural process where the cocoa tree sacrifices some of its young pods when it is stressed by dry spells, sudden weather shifts, or a shortage of plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni cacao tso lɛ kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ ekomɛi shaa afɔle kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa loo tsei niyenii ni faaa

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your trees are lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become too dry or flooded, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my farm turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly in wet, cool, and humid conditions when water droplets splash from infected pods to healthy ones.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ mli beni nu mli nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny dark spots and dry patches to appear on the young stems of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by mirid insects (capsids) that pierce and suck the sap from young branches and shoots, injecting a substance that kills the surrounding plant tissues.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii babaoo (capsids) ni tsɔɔ tsei niji kɛ tsei bibii amli nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni fiteɔ tsei ahe fãji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I see green bush-like plants growing out of the branches of my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa tsei ni tamɔ jwɛi eŋɔli ni miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ niji amli lɛ?

english: These are parasitic plants called mistletoe. Their roots sink directly into the cocoa branches to steal water and food, which weakens and eventually kills the affected branches.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ mistletoe. Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kookoo niji amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso nine ni ena naagba lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaakpata hiɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra side branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can pass through freely. This reduces the damp conditions that promote fungal diseases and directs more energy into pod production.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa hulutsoo shihilɛi ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to heap cocoa beans under banana leaves before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ato banana baai ashishi dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Fermenting beans under leaves kills the seed germ, breaks down the sweet pulp around the beans, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color required by cocoa buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Efoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he lɛ mli ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it that during certain times of the year, corn becomes so scarce and hard to buy in our local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa faaa ni ewa akɛ aaahɔ yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Corn availability follows strict harvest cycles. When the local harvest season ends, supply drops sharply until the next harvest or until traders bring in stock from other producing regions.
ga: Abele ni yɔɔ lɛ damɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni mli wa nɔ. Kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kpamɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi oya kɛyashi kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. aloo kɛyashi jarayelɔi kɛ nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baajɛ hei krokomɛi ni afeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do traders have to bring corn all the way from Burkina Faso to sell in our Ghanaian markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi kɛ ŋmãa baa kɛjɛɔ Burkina Faso koni amɛbahɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔ Ghana jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: Burkina Faso has different climate zones and dry-season irrigation systems, allowing them to harvest corn at times when local Ghanaian farms are out of season and unable to meet market demand.
ga: Burkina Faso yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hei srɔtoi kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni Ghana ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ be ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu jarayeli nibii ahe nii lɛ.

english: Why do some districts in Ghana produce so much more corn than my local area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kpokpai komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ ŋmãa babaoo fe he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions have variations in rainfall patterns, temperature, and soil fertility. Areas with longer rainy seasons and naturally richer soil can produce multiple heavy harvests per year.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi. Hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba daa afi.

english: Why does the price of corn stay high even when traders start bringing in outside supplies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara yaa hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ jarayelɔi ebɔi ŋmãa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ?

english: Bringing in crops from distant areas or across borders involves high transport costs, fuel prices, and customs fees, which keep the final market price high despite the extra supply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ loo husui asɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ biɔ gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo. fuel jara kɛ custom fees ni nɔ kwɔ Enɛ haa naagbee jarayeli jara lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my corn crop produce very small ears with missing kernels during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ toi bibii waa ni eshishifãi bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn needs adequate water during its flowering and silking stage to pollinate properly. Without enough water, pollination fails, resulting in small cobs with missing grains.
ga: Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ be mli ni egbeeɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow and dry up long before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or severe water stress, which prevents the crop from making the food it needs to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do some farmers get double the yield of corn from the same size of land that I farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ amɛ ŋmãa ni amɛwoɔ lɛ toi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Higher yields depend on using certified high-yielding seed varieties, correct seed spacing, applying the right fertilizer at the right time, and keeping the farm free of weeds early on.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ odaseyeli he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa woɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni ahaa jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil or get moldy so quickly while waiting for buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo efoɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ mɔ ni baahe lɛ?

english: If corn is harvested with high moisture content and not dried thoroughly in the sun before storage, fungi and mold grow rapidly, ruining the grain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli ni agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto lɛ, Mold kɛ mold lɛ daa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why do weevils attack my stored corn even when I keep it inside sealed sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs often lay hidden inside the grain while it is still in the field. Without proper drying and grain treatment before storage, these eggs hatch inside the sacks and eat the corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does heavy rain right before harvest time affect the corn I plan to sell?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ saa ŋmãa ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain on mature cobs in the field causes the grains to absorb water, which can lead to premature sprouting on the cob and dark spots that lower its market quality.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine yɛ ŋmeii ni eda yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei lɛ ada oya yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ, ni eha ŋmei lɛ afee diŋŋ ni haa ehiɛ ni jara wa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do pests attack my crops even when I only see a few of them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ fioo pɛ minaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Pests feed continuously once they arrive on your farm. Even a small number of insects can quickly eat through your crop's leaves and fruits, damaging the plants and reducing the overall harvest you can collect.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baaya nɔ aye nii kɛji amɛshɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kooloi bibii fioo ko po baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛyibii oya. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ obua naa lɛ baa shi.

english: How many times am I supposed to spray my farm to protect my crops from insect damage?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe?

english: In many cases, spraying your farm just once or twice at the right time is enough to prevent pests from destroying your plants and ensure you get your full target yield.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi babaoo amli lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikome loo shii enyɔ pɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, no fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite otsei lɛ, ni ekwɛ koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni okɛma ohiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will pests really lower my total harvest if I leave them on the farm without spraying?
ga: Pests haa mi yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ tsofa efɔɔɔ amɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, if pests are allowed to eat your crops even once without intervention, they will damage the plants, preventing you from reaching your maximum possible harvest output.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛ ni amɛye onibii shikome pɛ po ni amɛkɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Amɛ baafite tsei lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ bo gbɛ koni onine ashɛ nɔ ni fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ ajɛ mli aba lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my crop growth if insects feed on my plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ kɛji kooloi ye mi tsei lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra?

english: When insects feed on young crops, they weaken the plant early on. Without protecting the crops through timely spraying, the plants cannot recover enough to produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ye ŋmɔshi nibii bibii Amɛbaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ mra. Kɛji akɛ abuuu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ eyibii fɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I clear up questions about spraying frequency before the farming season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie sanebimɔ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni afɔɔ tsofa lɛ ashwieɔ shi shii abɔ lɛ he lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Knowing whether to spray once or twice in advance helps you buy the right amount of chemical treatments early and protect your crops before pest damage lowers your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ole be ni esa akɛ okɛ tsofa kome loo enyɔ awo ohe lɛ dani be lɛ ashɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohe tsofa ni sa lɛ mra. ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: How much harvest output can I get from one hectare of land if I protect my crops?
ga: Yibii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ hectare kome nɔ kɛji mibu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: With proper farm management and good pest control, a healthy crop can yield up to 5.5 tons per hectare.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ awo yibii ni shɛɔ tɔn 5.5 yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: What does 'tons per hectare' mean when measuring my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘tɔn yɛ hectare kome mli’ shishi kɛ́ misusu mikpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Tons per hectare' measures the total weight of crops produced on a standard unit of farm land (one hectare), helping you see if your farm is performing as well as it should.
ga: Tons per hectare’ susuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ okwaayeli he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. (Hectare kome) lɛ haa onaa kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: If I spray my crops twice as advised, am I guaranteed to reach my target harvest weight?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shii enyɔ taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ. Ani abaaha mi nɔmimaa akɛ mashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛma mihiɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Spraying once or twice removes the threat of pest damage, giving your crops the protection they need to grow fully and reach your target yield of around 5.5 tons per hectare.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ shikome loo shii enyɔ lɛ, ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ náa hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere. ni enine shɛ yibiiwoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ji aaafee tɔn 5.5 yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Can insect damage to plant leaves reduce the final weight of the produce I sell?
ga: Ani kooloi ni shwieɔ baai lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ naagbee tsiimɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, leaves provide energy for the crop to produce weight. When pests eat the leaves, the crop produces smaller output, reducing your final tonnage at harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, baai haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛma amɛhe muji. Beni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ baai lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baawo yibii fioo. Enɛ baaha onaagbee muji lɛ aba shi yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: How do I know if my farm is producing the maximum yield it is capable of?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ?

english: You can compare your harvest against standard target outputs like 5.5 tons per hectare; if your output is far below that, uncontrolled pests or missing spray treatments are usually responsible.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he, tamɔ tɔn 5.5 yɛ hectare kome mli. Kɛji akɛ onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi kwraa fe nakai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily and lose moisture quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living shade to cool the plants and protect them during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo aha tsei lɛ ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my maize on the same field, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo béi baaba?

english: You can plant cassava and maize together successfully because maize grows quickly and is harvested in three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize has already been harvested.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome kɛdu omanye yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay short even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellowing and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build strong green leaves and tall stems. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize recover its dark green color and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa abele ni ekwɛɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to give me a good harvest of tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha makpa tomato kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil for tomatoes feels loose, drains water well without staying soaked, and is rich in dark organic matter. It should also be soil where peppers or tomatoes were not grown in the previous season to prevent soil diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha tomato lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ efɔɔɔ. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ eyi mli obɔ Esa akɛ enɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni aduuu ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli koni akɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tiny shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these small insects early prevents leaf damage and allows the plant to produce healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ŋmeii bibii ni akudɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the bottom of my ripening tomatoes to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium inside the growing fruit, which often happens when soil moisture goes up and down unevenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Planting maize seeds too close causes the plants to crowd each other out and compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to fruit compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if they are planted with old disease-carrying roots, lack organic matter, or are competing with too many extra side-suckers that drain energy away from the main plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ akɛ shishifãi momo ni hiɛɔ helai tsu nii kɛdu. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ loo akaŋshii kɛ dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ koni ejie hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are completely mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above the ground naturally stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up, showing that the plant has finished sending energy to the tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shikpɔŋ nɔ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa amɛdalɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ emaje bulb lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off without turning into bean pods during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures cause heat stress, which makes cowpea flowers dry up and fall off before they can form pods. Planting at the right time in the season helps the crop flower when temperatures are cooler.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Leaves curl and droop to protect themselves from intense heat and conserve water. By closing up slightly, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping it hold onto moisture until the day cools down.
ga: Shi ni ebɔle ehe koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he ni ekɛ nu akafite. Kɛji akɛ agbe naa fioo Tsei lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for growth. The plant is pulling nutrients out of its old bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Tso lɛ miigbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni ji eŋɔli ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a special plant family that takes food from the air and puts it back into the soil as nitrogen. Planting them with maize helps feed the maize naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ nitrogen gbɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa abɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before spreading fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so your crop's roots can actually drink it. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil during hot weather can burn the roots or waste the fertilizer as it sits unused on top of the earth.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ejaakɛ akɛtsuuu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What actually happens to my crops if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for the same food, water, and sunlight. Instead of getting many strong plants, you get tall, thin plants with small harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona tsei ni he wa babaoo lɛ Obaaná tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my crop harvest if I leave them in the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. If left unchecked early on, they starve your crops of the resources needed to produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra Amɛbaajie nibii ni he hiaa bo koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, pull food and water away from the main plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on growing big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside of the new leaves at the top of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that prefer the softest, newest leaves inside the center fold of the corn plant. They hide in that pocket because it stays moist and protects them from the sun.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ehee fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nakai kotoku lɛ mli ejaakɛ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them in waterlogged ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground stays flooded for too long, the roots suffocate from lack of air, allowing rotting microbes in the wet soil to easily attack them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa nibii bibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet soil, which gives them more light and protects the leaves from rots and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa la babaoo baa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves. This happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight for the same soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Without enough food and light, the plant cannot generate enough energy to form full cobs.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛji niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before growing into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat or dry soil. High temperatures make it hard for the flower to fertilize itself, so the plant sheds the flower to conserve water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ akɛ amɛaafɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my pepper plants make them grow tall and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi pepper tsei lɛ miiha amɛmiikwɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients from your pepper plants. Surrounded by taller weeds, the pepper plant stretches upwards to reach light, growing thin and weak instead of bushy and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Pepper tsei ni jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Kpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. kɛtsɔ shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ nɔ Moŋ lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: What causes holes in the center leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm. They hide in the moist center part of the maize plant during the day and feed on the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii ni miida lɛ

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. As these insects suck the plant juice, the leaf distorts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu. Atsake baai lɛ.

english: The first rain usually wets only the surface soil, followed by hot sunny days. Seeds may sprout from that initial moisture but quickly dry up and die because the ground deeper down is still completely dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ nɔ. Gbi ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Shi egbiɔ ni egboɔ oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ kã he egbi kwraa.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open as the tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu Yucca lɛ, efeɔ klalo. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn brown and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that scorch easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Without living shade like plantains or shade trees to cover them, heat dries out the leaves faster than the roots can drink water, causing them to burn and fall.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni tsiɔ baai anaa lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the center of older maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or rotating your field with beans can fix this.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water for days, the soil gets waterlogged and starves the roots of oxygen, allowing fungal decay to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ha nu lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ gbii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho nu ni hɔmɔ baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out before they can be pollinated, making the plant shed the blossoms. Adding mulch to the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and preserves moisture to reduce heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani anyɛɔ ashɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tomato tsei lɛ ni woɔ fɔfɔi. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni ekɛba dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi.

english: Why do my young corn leaves have tiny ragged holes all over them as if they were eaten from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe fɛɛ tamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: This pattern is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant's central funnel and chew through tender young leaves before they unfold. Early scouting and targeted treatments help prevent severe yield loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa. Scouting mra Kɛ helatsamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ yibiiwoo ni fiteɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay stunted even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds generally grow faster and have stronger roots than crop plants, allowing them to steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients go directly to your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: As plantain trees grow, they produce multiple suckers (baby shoots) around the main stem. These extra suckers steal nutrients from the parent plant, so cutting away extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main stem to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does growing groundnuts in my field make the soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that leftover nitrogen fertilizes the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ afee ŋmei.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on in order to give big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Kwɔ ni oná yitso agbo?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which boosts tuber growth and protects the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some types of maize produce full ears faster than traditional seeds during short rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi woɔ toi ni eyi obɔ oya fe blema dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain improved maize varieties are bred specifically to mature quickly, requiring fewer weeks of rain to complete their growth cycle. This makes them ideal for areas where the rainy season ends earlier than usual.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Eheɔ otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo dani egbeɔ shweremɔ be lɛ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ gbeɔ naa mra fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under strong sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains around them, direct heat causes water loss faster than the roots can take up water, causing the leaves to yellow and drop off to save the plant.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ Direct heat haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni tso lɛ akafite.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the middle leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are a common sign of attack by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the funnel) and eat through them as the plant grows, which can slow down growth if left untreated.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (cone) ni amɛtsɔɔ mli amɛyeɔ nii be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava lets you know it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You can also gently clear away soil around one plant to check the size of the top root before harvesting.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ eshɛ kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ Ojie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso kome he lɛ hu fiofio koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ dara ha dani okpa.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the parent plant for soil nutrients and light. Removing extra shoots and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main tree to put its energy into producing large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi niji fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo plantains ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together on the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they release this nitrogen into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer to help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans shwieɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛjieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes gives the leaves maximum sunlight while keeping them off damp soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ wain tso lɛ naa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the ground absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering wastes water through rapid evaporation, and water droplets left on leaves in strong heat can scorch the leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu lɛ kɛtsɔ la ni etsɔɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Nibii ni jwɛi gboi kɛ baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material (mulching) acts as a blanket that traps soil moisture so you don't need to water as often. It also keeps the ground cool, stops weeds from growing, and eventually rots into plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed, usually by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa shwane mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops practically stop growing during the Harmattan dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Harmattan brings extremely dry air and low humidity. Crops slow down their internal growth systems to conserve water and protect themselves from dry winds, resuming normal fast growth once atmospheric humidity returns with the rains.
ga: Harmattan yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa ni hulutsoo be lɛ faaa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛmli dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he. ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ oya lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ku esɛɛ kɛ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to yield less every year even though I plow my farm with a tractor before every planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ trakta lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be baa lɛ?

english: Plowing the land too often destroys the soil's natural structure and burns out its organic strength, causing the land to gradually lose its fertility and produce weaker crops over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ shii abɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni eshãa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fiofio Fibii kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my farmland turn into dry, bare dust after I clear and plow it completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ sũ ni egbi beni mifo mli ni mitsu he nii fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy plowing exposes the inner soil directly to the hot sun and wind, drying out the moisture and turning healthy, living soil into bare, exhausted ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsuɔ waa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. egbiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hiɛ ka lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What happens to the good plant food inside the soil when I continuously till the field?
ga: Mɛni baa niyenii tsei kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ aya nɔ atsu okwaayeli lɛ?

english: Continuous tilling buries or exposes the soil's rich top layer, burning away the vital plant food and microbes that crops rely on to feed themselves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baafu loo ejie shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ kpo. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nibii bibii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops grow so well even though he does not hire a tractor to turn his soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ? Ni ekɛ trakta ko haaa koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Minimal disturbance keeps the soil firm, holds moisture better, and leaves the natural crop food intact, which can help crops thrive without expensive tilling.
ga: Haomɔ fioo ko pɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni no hewɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii lɛ efiteee. Enɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni amɛdara ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa bɛ mli.

english: How does using a heavy tractor every year affect the long-term strength of my farmland?
ga: Te trakta ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Repeated use of heavy machinery breaks down the soil particles too much, reducing the soil's overall strength and eventually making the land barren.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii lɛ akumɔ tsɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I prepare my land for planting without damaging the ground's natural goodness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔ nii ni mifiteee bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ji lɛ?

english: You can practice zero or reduced tillage by clearing weeds gently and disturbing only the small spots where you place your seeds, keeping the rest of the soil protected.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ zero tillage atsu nii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. kɛ hei bibii pɛ ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mli lɛ ni ooohao koni ebu shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ he lɛ

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of my farm so easily after I till it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mlɛo beni mikpa ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tilling breaks the soil into fine pieces and removes protective plant cover, making it easy for rainwater to sweep away the most fertile top layer of your land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bibii bibii ni ejieɔ tsei ni haa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã ni baa nii fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why are the roots of my maize struggling to stay firm in the ground after heavy plowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ ni wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over-tilled soil loses its firmness and structure, meaning it can no longer hold water well or give crop roots a strong, steady anchor to grow into.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ enyɛŋ emɔ nu jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. aloo ni eha tso shishifãi lɛ aná ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni amɛdara

english: Will disturbing my land less help my crops survive dry periods better?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ haomɔ ni baa shi lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, undisturbed soil retains deep moisture longer because its natural cover and structure block direct heat from sucking the water out of the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko gbaaa enaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ nu mli kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does a cocoa tree produce pods twice a year in Ghana, during a main season and a light season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei woɔ ŋmeii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ Ghana yɛ be titri kɛ be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to rainfall patterns, leading to a major harvest season during the heavy rains and a smaller light crop harvest during the minor rainy period.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he nii. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni anáa ŋmɔshi nii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli.

english: If my farm gave me very few pods during the main season, can the light crop season still give me a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ Ani be ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ waaa lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Yes, if weather conditions improve and you control pests and weeds, cocoa trees can recover and produce a healthy yield during the light season even after a poor main season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi ni oye kooloi kɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be ni ehiii po sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if a spraying chemical or medicine is officially approved for use on cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ akpɛlɛ tsofa loo tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli?

english: Approved cocoa chemicals are tested and certified by agricultural authorities like COCOBOD to ensure they kill pests safely without damaging the tree or leaving toxic residues on the beans.
ga: Okwaayeli nitsumɔhei tamɔ COCOBOD lɛ kaa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhaa amɛhe odaseyeli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee tsei loo amɛshiŋ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ yɛ kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together to save time when spraying my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ afutu mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: You should not mix chemicals unless the product label explicitly instructs you to do so, because combining wrong chemicals can destroy their strength or scorch your crop leaves.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai futuɔ tsofai amli ja nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ nibii lɛ tsɔɔ bo faŋŋ akɛ ofee nakai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai futu mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ loo eha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã.

english: Is it true that applying extra crop medicine will automatically give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛfata he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe?

english: No, using more chemical than recommended can damage the plant leaves, pollute the soil, and waste your money without increasing your yield.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ baai lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mujiwoo kɛ shika ni afiteɔ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but only a few of them grow into real cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Many cocoa flowers drop off naturally due to lack of nutrients, dry weather, or insufficient pollination by tiny beneficial insects in the farm.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and deep shade, which can be managed by pruning excess leaves to let in sunlight.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do trees in one part of my farm yield heavily while trees on another side produce very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Differences in soil richness, shade levels, water drainage, and soil depth across your farm cause variations in how much food each tree receives.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, hulutsoo, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni tso fɛɛ tso yeɔ lɛ tsakeɔ.

english: What basic steps should I take if my cocoa farm is giving lower yields every year?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi?

english: Pruning dead or overgrown branches, clearing weeds, applying approved fertilizers, and spraying for mirids (capsids) regularly can revive an aging or underperforming farm.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ Akpɛlɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Kɛ myrids (capsids) ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔji ni egbɔ loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does rainy weather affect the growth of cocoa pods on my tree?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ saa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain helps pods swell and mature by supplying water, but excessive dampness without sunny breaks creates an environment for fungal diseases to spoil the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Shi hulutsoo babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa bɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa kɛha ŋmeii ahe helai ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. As the plant grows, it moves available nitrogen to the top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ Ejieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava sheds leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. Once rain falls again, the plant produces fresh leaves and continues growing its roots underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil moist and cool helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and feel hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress, irregular watering, or tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit leaf curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and die if I don't plant plantains near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out quickly under direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates shade and keeps the air humid around the cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ kookoo lɛ he lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. baanyɛ atutua

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant grows strong and produces a large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi suckers babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara waa ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo aba.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning instead of midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the roots absorb water before midday heat causes rapid evaporation. Watering under hot sun can also stress warm plant leaves and waste water.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ shi oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ hu kɛ haomɔ baa tsei ahe baai ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil organisms to convert nitrogen from the air into natural plant food, leaving richer soil behind for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛtsake nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii baa shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs if I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete heavily for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, resulting in thinner stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the young leaves from getting scorched and keeps moisture in the soil while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I scatter my maize seeds closely together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops end up fighting for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly allows every maize plant enough room to grow strong stalks and produce larger corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛ nu lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji baa.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the strong Ghanaian sun, stops water from evaporating too quickly, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green so the plant can feed itself and yield a better harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye amɛhe niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally restores nutrients for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season but stay alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli shi eyɛ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive high heat. The plant rests and stores energy in its tubers underground, sprouting new green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛto nu ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Tsei jɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai eŋɔli heei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant grow bigger, healthier yam tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plants experience severe heat stress or don't get steady water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time of year keeps the plant calm enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe loo enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ dumɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi shi bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young corn plants and eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These pests, commonly called fall armyworms, target the soft green leaves inside the center whorl of the corn plant. Spotting them early allows you to treat the center of the plant with safe remedies like neem leaf oil before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ale nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akɛ fall armyworms. Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ. Spotting them early Ehaa okɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem baa mli fɔ tsuɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he nii. dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why shouldn't I sow my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ aduawai dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season usually only wet the surface soil and dry up quickly. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil stays damp enough for seeds to sprout and keep growing without dying in dry earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ kɛkɛ ni ehaa egbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the young roots establish.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, which eats the soft tissue inside the central leaf funnel of young maize. Early spraying with recommended controls protects the leaves so the plant can grow tall and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ ashɛreɔ tsofa lɛ mra kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ adara ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas on my field makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decompose, they release free fertilizer that feeds the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots under the ground are big enough and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and small cracks will form in the soil right around the base of the main stem as the tubers push outward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Efeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni bulb lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?
