english: Yam vines need leaves exposed to full sunlight to manufacture energy, which gets stored underground as tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, preventing disease and helping the plant produce much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmeii Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbo. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots that sprout around my plantain tree keep growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ yɛ Mi plantain lɛ he lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekomekomei.

english: If too many shoots, or suckers, grow around one stem, they all fight for the same water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main mother plant to yield large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo loo ŋmeii ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantain jwɛi agbo ko ni tsii aba tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark brown and rot away during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in cold, dark, and wet environments. Clearing thick weeds and pruning heavy leaves lets sunlight and wind into the farm to dry out the pods and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ tsei ni afoɔ waa Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin and fall down easily when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ shwiili kɛ shwiili ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together compete intensely for food, water, and light. Instead of growing strong, thick stalks, the plants stretch thin to reach light, making them easy for strong winds to blow down.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii, nu kɛ la he akaŋ, moŋ lɛ, amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa, ni amɛhe wa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛha la lɛ abote mli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without forming peppers during very hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee pepper yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to pepper plants. To protect itself from dying, the plant intentionally drops its flowers to conserve whatever moisture it has left in its stems.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad for my oil palm trees if I cut off all the green leaves around the fruit bunches when harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji mifo baai eŋɔli fɛɛ ni bɔle aduawai akui lɛ ahe lɛ baaná mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo beni mikpaa nii lɛ?

english: The green fronds act as the tree's kitchen, using sunlight to make food for growing the fruits. Cutting away too many healthy leaves starves the tree, causing lower yields in future harvests.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ ŋtayaai, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha aduawai ni kwɛɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni abaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade crops like plantain or shade trees growing above them, the intense sun dries out soil moisture and burns the tender leaves, which weakens the plant.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai bibii lɛ. ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects or infected stems used for planting. It stops the leaves from making food properly, resulting in very small cassava tubers.
ga: Ekolɛ o-kasa lɛ yɛ kasa mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa.

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops pull food nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you plant the same crop every year without adding organic manure, compost, or fertilizer, or without letting the land rest, the soil becomes depleted.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaafite.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients away from the main mother plantain. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to grow big, healthy fruit bunches.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ akwɛ yibii agboi ni mli wa.

english: Why do other farmers recommend that I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a free natural fertilizer that feeds hungry crops like maize growing nearby.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How does covering the bare dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te pepper tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, blocks the direct sun from baking the earth. It keeps the soil cool, holds water in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wither and die when I move them from the seedbed to the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving young plants shocks their delicate roots. If you transplant them during the hot afternoon sun, they lose water faster than their roots can drink. Transplanting late in the afternoon gives roots time to settle in cool soil overnight.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ ni oootsi lɛ baaha eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akpokpo. Kɛji okɛwo shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Ebaafite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shwane mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why are small insects eating up my harvested maize grains inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects like maize weevils multiply quickly if grains are stored while still damp, or if the storage space is warm and unsealed. Drying maize thoroughly under the sun before storing keeps insects from thriving.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. aloo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni atsĩii naa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto lɛ, ehaaa kooloi bibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: The very first rain only wets the top layer of dirt, which dries out quickly if dry weather returns for a few weeks. Waiting until the soil is deeply wet from continuous rains prevents young seeds from drying up and dying.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baagbi oya kɛji shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsii fioo komɛi. Kɛ́ mɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is my maize not growing tall even though I bought good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shɔŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ?

english: Maize roots need loose, well-aerated soil to spread out and feed. If the ground is hard and not tilled before planting, the roots get trapped near the surface, causing the plant to stay small and weak.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛye nii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni atsuuu nii dani aduɔ lɛ Akɛ shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Does clearing grass with a cutlass mean my field is ready for planting corn?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mikɛ tsɔne ŋmɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaadu ŋmãa?

english: Clearing grass only cleans the surface of your field. You still need to dig or till the topsoil so young corn roots can easily push downward to find water and nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ tsuɔ oyale lɛ hiɛ pɛ he nii. Ebaabi ni otsa loo otsu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he nii lolo bɔni afee ni ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya shi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii.

english: What will happen to my crop if I just dig small holes and plant seeds in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba minibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo bu bibioo ko? Ni adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ?

english: Hard soil blocks air and water from reaching young roots. Seeds planted in hard ground will struggle to emerge, and the surviving plants will turn yellow and produce very small cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu naa koni amɛkashɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Ni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: How does breaking up the soil before planting help my crops survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni migbala dani miduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Loosened soil acts like a sponge that drinks in rain and stores moisture deep underground. During brief rainless days, your crop's roots can reach down into that stored moisture to avoid wilting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi kuku ko mli Otso lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ he koni ekagbo.

english: Is it better to burn dead weeds on my farm or turn them into the soil before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mashã shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu?

english: Turning dead weeds into the dirt allows them to decay into natural manure that feeds your crops. Burning destroys this natural food and dries out the topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ otsake jwɛi ni egboi lɛ owo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛgbalaɔ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii. Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that your plants are starving for nutrients like nitrogen, often because the soil is too packed or poor. Mixing manure into well-prepared soil before planting prevents this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my maize crops when they sprout at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-ŋma lɛ? Ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated corn. Preparing the soil properly and removing weed roots before planting gives your crops a head start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ojie jwɛi shishifãi lɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do strong winds easily blow over my maize plants before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots cannot penetrate deep into the earth. Deep soil preparation breaks hard subterranean layers, allowing roots to anchor firmly in the ground.
ga: Abele baashwie baai lɛ anɔ beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he lɛ fiteɔ shishigbɛ fã ni wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he waa.

english: Should I plant my corn on flat ground or make soil mounds first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo mafee shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If your farm collects standing water after rain, making raised soil mounds or ridges lifts the plant roots out of the mud so they do not suffocate or rot.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ buaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ owó gɔŋ lɛ loo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaajie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni akagbɔjɔ loo akagbo.

english: What happens if I plant three or four maize seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole creates crowd competition. The young plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks that produce no ears.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa. Tsei bibii baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko ni toi bɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your soil is running low on nitrogen. When nitrogen is lacking, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to keep the younger top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni eha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ adara.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they get stressed by high heat or irregular watering. The plant drops flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When rain creates standing water, it starves the roots of oxygen and allows fungal diseases to attack and rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni amɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my groundnuts produce very few pods when I plant them under tall maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need direct sunlight to make energy and form pods. Tall maize stalks block the sunshine and steal soil nutrients and water that groundnuts need to develop properly.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii. Abɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli.

english: Which cassava variety should I plant if I want to harvest early and process it into flour or local drinks?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei srɔtoi esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa mra ni mafee maŋ lɛ mli ashikiŋsha loo nibii ni anuɔ?

english: Improved sweet cassava varieties are best because they mature quickly within 9 to 12 months and contain high starch levels, making them ideal for rapid processing into flour, starch, or local brews.
ga: Cassava ni ŋɔɔ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ekwɛɔ oya yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni eyɛ starch babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ oya ni efee ashikishaŋ, ashikishaŋ loo maŋ lɛ mli dãa.

english: Why are the grain heads of my sorghum crop completely empty instead of full of seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ efee efolo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Empty grain heads usually happen when dry spells occur during the flowering stage, preventing seed development, or when birds feed on the soft, milky grains before they can harden.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ naa Aloo kɛ́ okpoi ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tamɔ mliki lɛ dani amɛwa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural resting period after harvest, but warm temperatures and high humidity signal to the tuber that its dormancy is over and it is time to sprout new vines.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ ehiɛ ni ehiɔ shi lɛ efo. Ni be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ wain tsei heei.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by viruses transmitted by small insects like whiteflies, which suck sap from the young leaves and pass disease to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ kɛ hela lɛ baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees during the wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and cool environments where air cannot circulate freely through the cocoa canopy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and fibrous stems. As the fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs sturdy wooden props to keep strong winds from pulling it out of the wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ dara lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbiɔ tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ he. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akagbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small ears when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ toi bibii yɔɔ be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants need plenty of fresh air, sunlight, and space to grow big cobs. When planted too close, they choke each other, block air movement, and fight for soil nutrients.
ga: Abele tsei he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, hulu la kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ

english: How does good air movement in my farm prevent my crops from rotting?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akafite lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Air moving through your field dries wet leaves and stems after rainfall. Without proper airflow, trapped moisture encourages fungus and bacteria to grow and rot your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔji amli lɛ haa baai ni efɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɛ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants die off suddenly right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboiɔ trukaa dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are sensitive to soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt and fungi, which build up when wet soil lacks oxygen or when tomatoes are grown in the same plot repeatedly.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa tamɔ bacteria wilt kɛ fungus baanyɛ amɔ tomato oya. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Aloo kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ.

english: If my tomato crop fails completely due to disease, can I clear the farm and plant new tomatoes right away?
ga: Kɛji mi tomato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite kwraa yɛ hela hewɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ majie miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni madu tomato hee amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, you should not plant tomatoes in the same spot immediately because disease germs remain in the soil. You should switch to a different crop like corn or leave the land to rest.
ga: Esaaa akɛ aduɔ tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ helatsɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ani esa akɛ otsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa, loo oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛjɔɔ ohe?

english: Why is it important to know if chemicals were previously used on a piece of land before I plant fresh vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ale kɛji akɛ tsutsu ko lɛ akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ aduawai heei?

english: Some harsh chemical sprays leave residues in the soil that can stunt young plants, ruin sensitive crops like tomatoes, or prevent your harvest from meeting clean market standards.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ afite tsei bibii. Kpatamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ tomato loo tsi onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ anaa koni ekashɛ jarayeli he mlai ni he tse lɛ ahe.

english: What naturally causes my vegetables to start rotting quickly while still on the farm?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-aduawai lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Vegetables rot on the plant when there is too much wetness, poor air circulation around the base, or damage from soil chemicals and pests that weaken the crop.
ga: Aduawai fiteɔ yɛ tsei anɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, loo sũ mli tsofai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil within two days after picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fite yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot fast if they are picked while wet, packed in tight containers without ventilation, or exposed to high heat, which speeds up decay.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni efɔ. Okɛwo tsɛnsii ni mli wa mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. aloo ni akɛwoɔ la ni mli wa ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya lɛ mli

english: Why are the cobs on my standing maize turning moldy before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii dani akpa lɛ?

english: Maize cobs turn moldy when damp air gets trapped inside dense farms without enough wind and sunshine to dry out the husks.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ŋmɛ ŋmɔji ni mɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why should I ask an expert to check my soil before starting a new vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi ŋaalɔ ko ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mije aduawai ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: An inspection helps identify hidden soil problems, like chemical contamination or poor drainage, saving you from spending money on seeds that might fail.
ga: Nibii amlipɛimɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ tsofai ni efite loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ofite shika yɛ dumɔwui ni baanyɛ afite lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prepare my land so that wet crops like tomatoes do not suffer from rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ tamɔ tomato akafite?

english: You can plant on raised soil beds to let extra water drain away and space your plants far enough apart so sunlight and fresh air can reach the lower stems.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Ni oshi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain spoil my cocoa beans when I leave them outside on mats to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ mi-kookoo yibii lɛ beni mishiɔ amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ saatso nɔ koni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Rainwater adds fresh moisture back into the cocoa beans, which causes mold to grow and creates sour flavors. Cocoa beans require continuous heat and dry air to lower their internal water content safely.
ga: Nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee baa kookoo yibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Cocoa ŋmeii biɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be fɛɛ be koni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Is relying only on sunlight the best way to dry my harvested crops like cocoa and maize?
ga: Ani hulu la pɛ nɔ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mikpamɔi tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi?

english: Sunlight is free and effective, but during wet or cloudy seasons, sunshine is not strong or reliable enough, which leaves moisture trapped in the crops and leads to rotting.
ga: Hulu la bɛ hulu mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo atatu be mli lɛ, Hulu la lɛ he waaa loo anyɛŋ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Can using artificial heat or heat machines damage the quality of my cocoa beans?
ga: Ani hulutsoo ni akɛfee loo hulutsoo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, if the heat is too sudden or direct, it can smoke or burn the outer shell while leaving the inside raw. Drying needs gentle, controlled warmth to maintain high quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ latsaa lɛ ba trukaa loo tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ atswa lasu loo eshã yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ mligbɛ fã lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gbimɔ biɔ blɛoo, dɔlɛ ni akudɔɔ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so quickly across my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in damp, high-humidity environments. Raindrops splashing on infected leaves help disease spores easily jump to healthy neighboring plants.
ga: Mold yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small pods when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo?

english: Heavy rain combined with dark, cloudy skies reduces the sunlight cocoa trees need to produce food, causing the tree to drop young pods it cannot afford to feed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ŋwɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni atatu ewo mli lɛ fata he. Enɛ haa hulu la ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa ŋmeii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has too much water for my plants to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha tsei adalɛ?

english: When soil stays completely waterlogged, roots cannot get air and begin to rot, causing the plant's leaves to turn yellow and wilt even though water is everywhere.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ he fɛɛ he moŋ.

english: Why do plant leaves roll up or curl inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛshwieɔ amɛmli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants roll their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps them trap moisture inside and stop from drying out.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when the weather stays cloudy for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo atatu gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plants use direct sunlight to make their food through photosynthesis. Without bright light, they cannot produce the energy needed to grow tall or yield fruit.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛ feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛji la bɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛdara loo amɛwo yibii lɛ kpo.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops planted next to them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under intense tropical heat, so shade crops shield them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ mli waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it important for me to time my planting right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ midumɔ be lɛ ato jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: New seeds and seedlings need constant moisture to push roots deep into the ground; planting at the start of the rain gives them time to establish before dry heat returns.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui heei he miihia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishijee mli lɛ haa amɛ be dani hulutsoo ni egbi lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and build leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to turn green again.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the leaves on top look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its strength growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build thick root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: In intense sunlight, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. The leaves fold or drop slightly to protect themselves from drying out, and they usually bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi fioo koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do trees and shade plants drop all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baa fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants drop their leaves during the Harmattan to stop water from escaping through leaf surfaces in the dry winds. Losing leaves helps the plant save its moisture so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan beaŋ koni nu akaho yɛ baa lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and burn when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to shield them like umbrellas until their stems and roots grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛyashi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or dry soil stress. The plant drops the flowers to save its own life when it feels it does not have enough water to support growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛhe yiwala beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food. They stretch upward quickly to reach the sun, which makes their stems thin and easily broken by rain or wind.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli, ni amɛfeɔ oya koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize field so quickly while ignoring the cassava planted next to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ oya ni amɛku amɛhiɛ amɛshwie ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Armyworms prefer soft, sweet grass crops like maize and sorghum because they are easy to eat and digest. Cassava leaves are tough and contain natural chemical defenses that armyworms avoid.
ga: Cutworms sumɔɔ tsei ni jwɛi yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Ejaakɛ amɛyeli waaa ni amɛmli shwieɔ shi. Cassava baai lɛ wa ni adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ŋmeii tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ he lɛ yɛ mli.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops slow down their growth even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds act like hidden thieves under the soil. Their fast-growing roots steal the fertilizer and water meant for your crop, leaving your main crop hungry and slow to grow.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛshishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Ha hɔmɔ aye onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛdara fiofio.

english: Why do my plantain roots start rotting when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need air in the soil just like they need water. When water sits on the land for too long, it pushes all the air out of the dirt, suffocating the roots and causing rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia plantain shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli taakɛ nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When you put too many seeds in one spot, the growing plants end up fighting each other for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Spacing them out allows every single plant to get enough nutrition to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Beni okɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ he kome lɛ. Tsei ni miida lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to pull out some of my good seedlings after they sprout so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie midumɔwui kpakpai lɛ kɛji amɛdara lɛ?

english: Removing a few crowded seedlings gives the remaining ones enough breathing room and soil space. If you leave them all together, they will overcrowd each other and stay weak instead of growing strong and producing a high yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛmuɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji oshi amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee ekome lɛ Amɛwoɔ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Mohu ɔ, e daa wawɛɛ nɛ e woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like babies and cannot handle hot, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide broad leaves that create natural shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally feeds the soil, giving the next crop you plant fresh nutrients without having to rely entirely on bought fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hee ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than your crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and fertilizer from the soil. Even with enough water, your crop is starving because the weeds are consuming all its food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po hɔmɔ miiye amɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my land give me less cassava if I plant it in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to rest and rebuild the nutrients that cassava uses up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni ŋmei lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do diseases spread so fast across my tomato field when the plants are growing very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela lɛ miigbɛ eshwa mitato ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are packed tightly, air cannot flow between them, trapping moisture on the leaves. Fungi and rot thrive in wet, crowded conditions and easily leap from one leaf to another.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ Mold kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ mlɛo

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra leaves and shoots from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ?

english: When a plant has too many leaves, it uses up its energy trying to feed them all. Cutting off extra branches forces the plant to send its strength into making bigger, healthier pepper fruits instead.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ baai babaoo Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha lɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to spread dry grass or leaves around the bottom of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-crop bottom lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering the ground around your plants acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents rain moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, while keeping weeds from pushing through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni oookɛ muji awo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ hulu la mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa jwɛi akabote mli.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in stages throughout the month instead of planting my whole farm in one single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ? yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli

english: Planting in stages prevents all your crops from maturing at the same time. This spreads out your harvest work and stops you from being overwhelmed by too much food spoiling before you can sell it.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ tsiɔ oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa onibii ni okpa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ehaa niyenii ni efite babaoo shwieɔ onɔ dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings rot when I cover them completely with plastic sheets to protect them from rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛ mikɛ plastic tsɔne ha amɛhe koni nugbɔ akanɛ lɛ?

english: When you cover seedlings completely, heat and moisture get trapped underneath with no air moving through. This hot, damp air creates the perfect environment for fungal diseases to multiply and cause the young plants to rot.
ga: Kɛji oha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kwraa lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ŋmɛɔ shishi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I remove the palm frond cover from my vegetable seedbed once the seeds start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ mi-vegetable dumɔwui saatso lɛ nɔ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Sprouting seeds need fresh air movement and sunlight to build strong stems. Leaving the cover on traps too much heat and humidity, which makes the young sprouts grow weak, thin, and prone to dying.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la koni amɛfee tsei ni wa. Shi he ko ni okɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ awo mli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ, amɛhe afee mlɛo ni ekolɛ amɛbaagboi.

english: Why is it important to space my cocoa trees properly instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: Proper spacing allows wind and breeze to circulate between the branches. Good air movement quickly dries moisture on leaves after rain, which prevents fungal problems like black pod disease from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to trim the lower leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafo mi tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves allows fresh air to circulate around the base of the plant. Good air circulation keeps the stems dry and prevents fungal diseases that thrive in trapped, moist air near the damp ground.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: If I cover my farm soil with dry grass or mulch, will it choke my crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani ebaatsi miŋmɔshi nibii anaa?

english: No, organic mulch protects soil moisture while still letting enough air pass through. It keeps the roots cool under the hot sun without trapping suffocating heat around the base of the plant.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa tsɔɔ mli lolo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ebɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my greenhouse tomatoes drop their flowers when the structure is fully closed on hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-greenhouse tomato lɛ fɔ̃ɔ beni agbeɔ tsɔne lɛ naa yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: An enclosed structure acts like a hot box, trapping extreme heat if air cannot move. Without ventilation or air movement to cool the room, tomato flowers get heat stress and fall off before producing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adeka ni mli edɔ. Emɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ afã. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe bɛ ni haa tsu lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil faster when I keep it tightly sealed in plastic sacks right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto plastic kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still breathes and releases moisture. Tightly sealing the sacks prevents air from circulating, trapping heat and moisture inside, which quickly leads to mold growth.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Kɛ́ otsi kotoku lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Emɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn soft and rot when transported in tightly covered wooden crates during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ kɛ́ akɛwo tso adekai ni akɛ nɔ ko ewo mli shiŋŋ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering crates tightly traps the heat generated by the warm fruit and prevents air from blowing through. This heat build-up cooks the tomatoes and accelerates decay during transport.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala adeka lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ ni aduawai ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ahi shi. ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsɔ mli Dɔlɛ ni ebua naa nɛɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ ashwere ni amɛfite oya yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to store my yams on open raised wooden racks rather than piling them on the floor in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato tso adeka ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ato shikpɔŋ yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ mli.

english: Raised racks allow air to flow beneath and all around each yam. Constant air movement keeps the yams dry and cool, preventing them from rotting or sprouting prematurely.
ga: Shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ shishi kɛ he fɛɛ he. Sweet potato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa nɔ etsɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛgboi loo amɛkakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why does my harvested cassava dry faster outside in the breeze than inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli fe nitoohe lɛ?

english: Moving outdoor air constantly sweeps away moisture escaping from the cassava. Inside a closed room, stagnant air becomes saturated with moisture, slowing down the drying process.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nyiɛmɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be. Yɛ tsu ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekã shi lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa bɔ ni agbiɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp conditions. When the fungus attacks, it turns healthy green or yellow pods black and soft, destroying the beans inside and causing direct financial loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tutua Healthy green loo yellow pods lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo. efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ shika fiteɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I see a few rotten cocoa pods on a tree, can they spread the sickness to healthy pods?
ga: Kɛ mina kookoo ŋmeii ni egbo yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ, ani manyɛ magbɛ hela lɛ mashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli?

english: Yes, fungus spores from a single rotten pod can easily spread to neighboring healthy pods through rain splashes, insects, or farming tools, rapidly destroying more of your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii kome ni egbo lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kooloi bibii, loo okwaayeli nibii anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni otsuɔ nii ohaa lɛ oya.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods that have already rotted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efite ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should pluck rotten pods off the trees immediately and bury them outside the farm or take them far away. Leaving them on the tree or on the ground allows the spores to survive and infect future crops.
ga: Esa akɛ otsi tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ loo okɛya he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color changes completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Harvesting when fully ripe ensures the beans have developed enough sugar for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ mli Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ náa sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa income if I leave ripe pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba shika ni mináa yɛ kookoo mli lɛ nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ hu?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to sprout or decay. Buyers reject sprouted or moldy beans, meaning your hard work goes to waste without giving you money.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo eyɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ baaya yaka ni ahaaa bo shika.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to harvest green, unripe cocoa pods along with the ripe ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛko lɛ kɛfata kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Unripe cocoa beans do not ferment properly because they lack natural sugars. Mixing them in leads to low-quality, bitter beans that fetch lower prices or get rejected by buying clerks.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni edako lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars ni bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu mli lɛ, anáa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni mli edɔ ni jara baa shi loo woloŋmalɔi lɛ kpooɔ.

english: Why do cocoa pods seem to rot much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates constant dampness and high humidity. Water droplets resting on the cocoa pods allow fungal spores to germinate and infect the crop much faster than during dry weather.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji anɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ shwereɔ ni ekɛ hela baa tsei anɔ oya fe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my tiny, young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ gboɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is a natural tree behavior called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree naturally thins out excess young pods it cannot support so it can direct energy to healthy, surviving pods.
ga: Enɛ ji tsei ni ale amɛ akɛ cherel wilt lɛ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ. Cacao tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ hewalɛ aya pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hiɛ ka lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does having too much heavy tree shade on my farm make my cocoa pods rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Excess shade blocks sunlight and prevents wind from drying wet leaves and pods. This trapped moisture creates an ideal dark, wet environment for pod diseases to grow.
ga: Shade babaoo tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ agbi baai kɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why does leaving bushy weeds around my cocoa trees lead to spoiled pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi akui abɔle he lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao ŋmɔji lɛ miifite lɛ?

english: Overgrown weeds trap moisture around the trunk and act as pathways for pests and fungi to climb up to the lower pods, causing the fruits to decay quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii tsɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛkwɔɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shaded conditions. When rainwater sits on the pods, the fungus enters the skin and spoils the beans, which can destroy your harvest if trees are not pruned to let air and sunlight through.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ kpɛtɛ pod lɛ he lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ hewolo lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii kɛji akɛ afooo tsei lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or insect attacks. The plant naturally sheds its blossoms to conserve water and energy so it can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away from the plant roots, causing the crop to pull nutrients from its lower leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ shwieɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do buyers for international markets reject my vegetables if they have tiny insect marks on the skin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛhaa majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei lɛ kpooɔ mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛhewolo nɔ kooloi bibii yɔɔ amɛhewolo nɔ lɛ?

english: Foreign markets enforce strict quality rules to avoid introducing pests and diseases into their countries. Even small marks signal that insects might have laid eggs inside the fruit, which leads to early rot during transport.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei lɛ kɛ mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ he lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkakɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba amɛmaji amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ bibioo po Etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi baanyɛ awo ŋmeii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to spray chemical pest medicine right before I harvest my crops for market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ dani makpã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: No, every chemical needs a waiting period before harvest so sunlight and rain can break down the poison. Harvesting too soon leaves harmful chemical residues on the crop, making it unsafe for consumers and causing lab tests to fail.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ biɔ ni amɛ be dani akpa. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ anyɛ akpata tsofa fɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ni ehaa laboratori mli kaai lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes soften and rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes bruise easily when packed tightly in large wooden crates or left under direct heat. These invisible bruises break internal cell walls, allowing rot organisms to spread fast and spoil the produce in transit.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo tso adekai agboi amli jogbaŋŋ loo ashi yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ fãji ni anaaa nɛɛ fiteɔ wala yibii lɛ amli gbogboi lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die if I do not plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small root systems that easily burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade and keep the surrounding air humid, protecting the young trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli hulutsoo baa. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔji ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and full of bumps instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers deform when they hit hard, compacted soil, rocks, or tree roots as they try to push downwards. Clearing obstacles and mounding soft, loose soil helps the tubers expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtswa muji ni wa, tɛi, loo tsei shishifãi beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛ kɛba shi lɛ. Nibii ni tsiɔ gbɛ kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny beetles attack my dried maize even when I store it inside closed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ kotoku ko mli moŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the grains while the crop is still in the field. If the grain is not fully dried before bagging, residual heat and moisture cause those eggs to hatch inside the sealed bag.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ewui bibii ni anaaa lɛ woɔ dumɔwui amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani awo kotoku mli Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afɔ yɛ kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: What does adding dark compost or animal manure actually do to my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It holds onto water during dry periods, loosens hard soil so plant roots can spread easily, and slowly releases food that crops need to grow strong.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the middle leaves of my young corn stalks, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Sprinkling approved neem leaf extracts or correct pesticides directly into the center of the plant stem kills the pests before they destroy the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tso lɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ shishifã lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my green tomato fruits get black rotten spots at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egboi yɛ shishi dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and low calcium in the soil. Keeping your soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or agricultural lime around the plants helps prevent the bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime afata he Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, weak, and produce small yields. Proper spacing gives each crop enough space to grow big and healthy.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my crops even if I already applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm. They drink the water and absorb the fertilizer meant for your crops much faster than the crop roots can, leaving your main plants weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya fe tsei shishifãi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei titrii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni mafi tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need lots of sunlight to produce the energy required to swell the tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground into the sun and prevents soil diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai ni jɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ akashɛ hulu la he, ni ebaatsi helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them directly in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them creates a canopy that protects them from heat until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ ekome lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli waɔ.

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or if the plants receive too much water during root formation, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ Kasava lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I tell if my soil is too dry for my crops before the leaves start wilting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi?

english: You can check moisture by digging a hand-deep hole into the soil and squeezing a handful of dirt. If it holds its shape as a soft ball without crumbling, there is enough water; if it falls apart like dry dust, your crops need water immediately.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni sũ lɛ mli edɔ ha lɛ kɛtsɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni oootswa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni okɛ sũ fioo ko atswa shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efoŋ lɛ, no lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo. Kɛji efolɔ tamɔ sũ ni egbi Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning instead of waiting until mid-day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering early allows plant roots to drink fully before midday heat causes rapid evaporation. Midday watering leaves water on leaves that can cause scorch damage under hot sunlight.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ egbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ dani shwane shɛɔ. Ekɛ nu ni hoɔ oya baa Nu ni afɔɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ kɛ nu baa baai lɛ anɔ, ni baanyɛ aha shãa afite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to spray pesticides on my crops early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Early mornings usually have calm air and moderate heat, which stops chemicals from drifting away in strong winds or evaporating too quickly before killing the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, leebi maŋkpa lɛ, efeɔ dioo ni edɔɔ fioo. Enɛ haaa tsofai lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli loo amɛkafee la oya tsɔ dani amɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry granular fertilizer to my crop fields in the middle of a hot, dry day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ji granular lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔji amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ anɔ?

english: Without moisture, intense heat can cause chemical fertilizers to release gases into the air instead of soaking into the soil, which can burn plant leaves and waste your money.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ajie kɔɔyɔɔ fɔŋ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai ashã ni efite shika.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during the dry afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural protective response to reduce the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, which helps the plant conserve water and survive extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni haa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy and wilted in the afternoon but stand up straight again by early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi ete shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi maŋkpa.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water faster through their leaves than roots can pull from the dry soil. At night, heat drops and water loss stops, allowing roots to refill the plant.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, akpaa dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ayi tso lɛ mli obɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei ni wooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive daytime heat damages tomato pollen and prevents flower fertilization. When flowers cannot produce seeds, the plant drops them to conserve its limited energy.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ tomato pollen lɛ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ nii. Beni fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei shwieɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ fioo ko he.

english: Is it true that clearing weeds from my field in the morning sun works better than doing it on a rainy day?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ miŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli leebi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi nɔ?

english: Yes, uprooted weeds exposed to intense sun dry out and die rapidly, whereas rainy conditions allow weed roots to reconnect with damp soil and grow back quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ajie amɛshishifãi ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baagbi oya ni amɛgboi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi haa jwɛi shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpaa gbee oya ni amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the morning dew to dry off before harvesting my cowpea pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni leebi hulutsoo be lɛ agbi dani makpa tsina ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Harvesting wet crops spreads fungal diseases across your farm and introduces moisture into your harvest bag, which causes stored seeds to mold quickly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nu mli ni akpaa lɛ baagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa okpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so quickly if I leave them lying in the hot sun after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are live plant tissues that breathe faster when exposed to direct heat, causing rapid internal biological breakdown within a day or two.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ji tso fãji ni hiɛ ka ni muɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees open their flowers early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miifɔ mra lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers open early in the cool morning hours to match the active period of tiny midges and insects that pollinate them before the dry midday heat settles in.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛ kookoo fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ kɛ kooloi ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akpã gbee dani hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ shwane mli.

english: Rolling leaves is the maize plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which helps it conserve water and prevent drying out during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha abɛi tsei. Koni akɛba baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why does my local maize turn yellow and dry up faster than the improved seed varieties during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Local maize varieties often have shorter root systems or less natural resistance to drought compared to hybrid or improved seeds, which are specifically bred to retain moisture and stay green longer when rain is scarce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku loo enyɛŋ eshi hɔmɔ ni baa lɛ fioo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa loo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe. Afɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛha hulutsoo be ahi shi ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Are foreign or imported crop seeds always better for my field than the seeds I save from my own local harvest?
ga: Ani maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mimaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Not always. While imported seeds can yield high amounts under ideal conditions, local seeds are already adapted to local weather and soil, making them more resilient against native pests and dry weather.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛ ni sa mli moŋ. Atsakeɔ akutsoŋ dumɔwui lɛ hu kɛyaa akutsoŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ.

english: If I heat or roast my harvested maize seeds before storing them, will they still sprout when I plant them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ wo la mli loo mikɛshã dani mikɛto lɛ, Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ lolo?

english: No, heating or roasting maize kills the living embryo inside the seed, which prevents it from germinating, even though it helps preserve the grain for eating or selling.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ la mli loo ni ashãa lɛ baagbe ŋmãa ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. ni tsiɔ shweremɔ naa Kɛji akɛ ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ to koni aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ po.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for growing maize or oil crops like groundnuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo mu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Maize requires deep, fertile soil with plenty of nitrogen and steady rainfall, whereas oil crops like groundnuts prefer looser, sandy-loam soil that allows seed pods to expand easily underground with moderate water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni mu dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmei sumɔɔ ŋã ni mli tse. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo kɛtsɔ nu ni fa fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my white maize turn brownish or dark when I leave it in the field too long after it matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei yɛŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛ́ mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving mature maize in the field exposes it to prolonged moisture, high sun, and mold, which causes the outer husks to break down and the kernels to discolor or rot.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ ŋmãa shwieɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli fãa ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ su tsakeɔ loo egboɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so quickly if I do not dry it immediately after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji migbeee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains high internal moisture, creating an ideal environment for fungi, mold, and insects to multiply rapidly if the grain is not dried down properly right away.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ mligbɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo oya kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I use the leftover cobs and stalks after processing my maize to improve my soil for the next planting season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ beni atsu ŋmãa he nii lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, breaking down maize cobs and stalks into the soil or composting them adds organic matter back into the ground, helping the soil retain water and nutrients for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni akumɔ awo sũ lɛ mli loo afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my stored corn get warm to the touch inside the sack even when kept in a cool room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli dɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he yɛ kotoku lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ?

english: Stored corn produces heat through natural respiration, and if dampness, insects, or molds are present inside the sack, their activity generates extra heat, showing that the grain needs further drying.
ga: Abɛi ni ato lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa kɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli mumɔ nɔ. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii, loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli Amɛnitsumɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ babaoo baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni agbi ŋmãa lɛ mli babaoo.

english: Can I use plant oils to protect my stored maize grains from insect pests?
