ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ abu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, coating grains lightly with food-grade vegetable oils creates a thin barrier that smothers insect eggs and prevents pests from breeding, keeping your stored harvest safe naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmaa lɛ he nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa gbɛtsii nii bibioo ko baa. No yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kooloi bibii akui lɛ teeɔ shi, ni ehaaa kooloi bibii lɛ afɔ. Ehaa onibii ni okɛto lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my food crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miniyenii tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist after a rain, usually a few weeks after planting when young roots are ready to feed. Applying fertilizer during dry weather or right before a heavy downpour can burn the roots or wash the food away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishifãi bibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha niyenii Ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ loo eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite.

english: What is eating small holes into my young maize leaves and hiding in the stalks?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves and chewed stalks are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying safe, recommended pesticides or putting a mixture of clean dry sand and ash inside the plant funnel early in the morning can stop them from destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni aŋɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Tsofai ni Gbeɔ Kooloi ni Akɛshwieɔ Nɔ ni Akɛwoɔ Shweshweeshwe lɛ He ŋaa Aloo ŋã ni egbi kɛ sũ ni he tse ni akɛfutuɔ odumɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkafite onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whitefly insects that spread a virus to the plant, or by extreme heat and drought. Keeping the plants well-watered and spraying neem seed oil helps control the insects and protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi bibii ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water stays trapped in the soil for too long or when there is a fungal infection. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rain water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ba. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from heat, lack of water during dry periods, or attack by sucking insects like mirids. Keeping shade trees in your farm and protecting cocoa from pests helps the flowers stay on the tree and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Nu ni bɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa amɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ kookoo hebuu kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving too many young shoots causes them to steal food and water from the main plantain tree, making the fruit bunch small. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main tree to grow bigger, heavier plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli. Ha aduawai akuu lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Watering your pepper plants regularly during dry weeks and giving them light shade during scorching weather keeps the blossoms on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ daa yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli, ni okɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the ground, helping your maize grow better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy, continuous rains that thoroughly soak the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can dry up quickly and ruin your seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them survive when rain stops for weeks?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly during dry spells.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like small tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaf rolling is the crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant save water when the weather is very dry and hot.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni edɔ.

english: Why do my crops look wilted in the afternoon even when the soil still has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during long dry seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo efo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during drought to reduce water loss, surviving on energy stored in its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ ŋmei baai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and die when water sits on my farm field for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by blocking air in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients needed to keep the leaves green.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do plant diseases spread so much faster across my farm during long rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria that cause crop diseases love high humidity and wet leaves, and rain droplets splash disease spores from sick plants directly onto healthy ones.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ baai ni efɔ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside flowers, preventing them from forming fruit, so the plant sheds the useless blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young crops grow tall and skinny instead of bushy when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe be mli ni adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food; when shaded by large trees, they stretch unnaturally high to search for light, resulting in weak, thin stems.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna niyenii. Kɛ́ eyɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ekpãa ehe kɛyaa he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa ni etao la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my farm stronger during poor weather?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa adu lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ mli awa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air to naturally fertilize the soil for maize, while also covering the ground to protect soil moisture from evaporating in the sun.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aha ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akatsɔ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the bottom of the plant upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains well; when excess rainwater stays around the roots for too long, it deprives them of oxygen and creates conditions for fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafee nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni ekɛ fungal rot baa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by severe heat and water stress affecting the plant's leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ ni saa tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants suddenly dry up and die in small patches across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ miiho trukaa ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Patchy wilting in groundnuts is typically caused by soil-borne fungal diseases or the rosette virus spread by aphids, which block the movement of water inside the plant.
ga: wilting in patches Yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ loo rose hela ni ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aya.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from dry weather stress, lack essential nutrients, or lack tiny insects like midges that are needed to pollinate the flowers into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni he hiaa koni akɛwo fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii amli lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants losing their flowers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miifite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air prevent pepper flowers from successfully forming fruit, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to conserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tsiɔ pepper fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce mostly leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow lush leafy green vines rather than flowers, while tiny pests like pod borers may also be destroying young pods early.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsina tsei hewalɛ koni amɛdu wain tsei ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ pod borers hu baanyɛ afite pod bibii lɛ mra.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially if strong winds blow or if microscopic worms called nematodes damage the roots underground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa loo kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots inside the barn before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and sprout when warm temperatures and humidity rise, signaling to the tuber that it is time to start growing a new vine.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaakwɛ̃ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje wain tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: Why do my rice stalks bend and fall flat to the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over, or lodge, when the stems become weak from excessive nitrogen fertilizer or when rain and heavy winds weigh down fully formed grain heads.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ yɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa ŋmãa ni ebɔle ehe kwraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to grow green and strong, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer like urea early in the season will help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific crop pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi feɔ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and wet conditions. You can manage it by clearing weeds, pruning shade tree branches to let in sunlight, and quickly removing infected pods so the fungus doesn't spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ejɔ, kɛ fɔ́ kɛ enɛ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsa lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni oootse lɛ nɔ. Kpãa tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ mli koni hulu la lɛ abote mli. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Your cassava plants are likely suffering from Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected cuttings. The best defense is to obtain and plant certified disease-resistant cassava varieties from agricultural extension agents.
ga: Ekolɛ o-cassava tso lɛ miiye cassava mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ atsĩ naa ji ni ana ni adu ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How can I keep my vegetables alive during the hot dry season without expensive water pumps?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔbu aduawai ahe kɛji nu pɔmpii ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around your plants with dried grass, straw, or leaves—traps moisture in the ground and shields the plant roots from the direct sun, drastically reducing how often you need to water.
ga: Mulching—ni ji sũ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai shwieɔ nɔ lɛ—haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crop field so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafee yaka?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, such as after a light rain or early in the morning, and cover it slightly with soil. Never apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour, as strong rains will wash the chemicals away from the root zone.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ Kaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie tsofai kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are soft and top-heavy, and strong winds or root pests can easily knock them down once heavy bunches form. You need to stake your plantain trees by supporting the heavy stems with strong wooden poles until harvest.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe wa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ amɛ shi mlɛo kɛ́ fɔfɔii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ehe miihia ni okɛ tso ni tsii lɛ awo tso lɛ he kɛtsɔ tso ni wa ni okɛbaafi sɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Giving your tomato plants consistent moisture and light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ oha o-tomato tsei lɛ mli fũu ni okɛ amɛ awo mli daa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can I use local neem tree leaves to protect my crops from caterpillars instead of buying chemical sprays?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ neem baai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe. Ani manyɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Yes, crushing neem leaves in water and letting them soak creates a natural liquid spray that repels caterpillars, aphids, and beetles without harming beneficial insects or damaging your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, neem baai ni akumɔ awo nu mli ni aha amɛshwie shi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa. Ni eyeee kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui loo efiteee oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from sprouting and becoming soft in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto?

english: Store your yams off the ground in a raised, shaded, and well-ventilated yam barn. Inspect them regularly and snap off any young green sprouts as soon as they appear to stop the tuber from losing its energy and softness.
ga: Kɛ sweet potato ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ daa ni ofolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ koni okpa bulb lɛ koni amɛkafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: If I put a lot of extra fertilizer on my crops, will it make them grow faster and yield better produce?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Not necessarily. Giving crops too much fertilizer can burn their roots, cause excessive leaf growth without producing fruit, and lower the quality of the harvest.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Enɛ haa baa lɛ daa fe nine ni ewooo yibii. ni eha ŋmaa lɛ mlihilɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, developing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper crops very close together so I can get more peppers from a small space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for light, air, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants with smaller and fewer peppers.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture enough sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Leaving them on the ground makes them vulnerable to heat damage and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baafite amɛ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ yɛ mi plantains lɛ shishi lɛ je kpo.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients and water from the main tree. Pruning them leaves only the strongest shoots, helping the plantain produce a larger bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ, ashiɔ tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa plantains lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants fold up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat, which helps them trap moisture inside and survive dry periods.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛmli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when there is too much chemical nitrogen forcing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsofa ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I harvest them during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills the soil with water and reduces air flow around the tubers, causing the starch in the cassava roots to ferment and rot before you can dig them up.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kɛ nu ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni no haa ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ dani obaanyɛ okɛfo mli.

english: Why do experienced vegetable farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni duɔ aduawai lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the heat, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience transplant shock and are very delicate without nursery shade. In hot sunshine, excessive heat dries them out before their root systems can absorb water, so they need temporary shade and early morning or late evening transplanting to survive.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa amanehulu kɛjɛ transplant shock mli ni amɛhe waaa waa kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ amɛkwɛmɔhe lɛ. Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Dɔlɛ babaoo baaha amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni atsake amɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to cover my crop nursery bed with palm fronds or shade cloth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tso loo mama ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ aha mibii akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tender young crop shoots cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Covering nursery beds protects fragile shoots from excessive sun heat and heavy rain, ensuring high survival rates before plants are strong enough for the open field.
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei bibii lɛ eŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Nursery saatsoi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ buɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa wala yibii babaoo baa dani tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔji ni agbele mli.

english: How do I keep my crop nursery from getting too hot for tender shoots during sunny afternoons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha greenhouse lɛ mli akadɔ tsɔ kɛha mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: You need to monitor the nursery closely during peak heat hours and lift or vent the side covers to allow air movement. Good airflow lowers excessive temperature inside the nursery so tender leaves do not scorch.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. ni owó loo ojie kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha hulutsoo ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ shãaa.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defence mechanism against excessive heat and water loss. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunshine to conserve moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ he. Abɛi haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛfoɔ ehe lɛ nɔ. Koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ

english: Why do young cocoa trees fail to survive when planted in an open field without shade crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand harsh, full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains to act as natural covers, keeping the surrounding heat low and soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni akɛhaa amɛhe. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ahaa ebaa shi ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does placing dry grass around my crop roots help protect them from heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts as a protective shield. It keeps the soil cool during scorching hot days, retains moisture, and prevents high heat from damaging root systems.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai gboi woɔ Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni otsi la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafite shishifãi lɛ

english: Why is it bad for me to water my crops during the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering in intense afternoon heat causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can take it in, and warm water droplets left on leaves can burn the plant tissue. Watering early in the morning or evening gives crops cool soil and maximum moisture absorption.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni eshwɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ mli fãji ashã. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my sweet pepper plants drop their flowers and leaves during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ baai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers and lower leaves to save water and energy. Providing light shade and regular soil moisture monitoring helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa chili tsei lɛ fɔfɔii kɛ amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse haa, ni akwɛɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings take longer to sprout when the soil gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ?

english: When soil temperatures rise excessively without moisture, cassava cuttings enter a protective state to avoid drying out completely. Sprouting slows down until soil temperature lowers and moisture improves.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ tee ŋwɛi tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ Akɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ woɔ shihilɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekagbi kwraa. Nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ fioo kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants fail to form tight heads when the weather becomes extremely warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ ehiɛɛɛ dense yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cabbages are sensitive to high temperatures. When exposed to excessive heat, the plant becomes stressed and spends its energy producing loose, spread-out leaves instead of forming a solid, compact head.
ga: Kaabaji nuɔ he waa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ fe nine lɛ, tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ yi nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ kplɛɛe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning pale yellow when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves early in growth usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have logged water around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni daa oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he loo okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: I found strange worms eating the leaves and inside the stems of my maize this season; what are they and how do I deal with them?
ga: Mi na ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Mɛni ji amɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ amɛ aye?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that travels on wind currents and attacks cereal crops. You can manage them by checking your field early, putting clean sand or ash into the leaf funnels, or spraying recommended organic or chemical insecticides early in the morning.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛbaa ni tutuaa ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ kɛtsɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋã loo sũ ni he tse awo baa lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or spread when you plant cuttings from sick plants. To protect your farm, pull out and burn affected plants immediately, and plant stem cuttings from disease-resistant varieties next season.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Amɛji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ amɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛ́ ofo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii. koni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he Okɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni oshã amɛ. ni afolɔ tsei ahe shishifãi kɛjɛ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hottest part of the day even when the ground feels slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po.

english: Extreme heat causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than roots can absorb it, putting the plant under heat stress. Covering the soil around the base of your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ he (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant beans together with cassava on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baafata he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping legumes like beans with cassava is very good. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil for your cassava, while giving you a fast harvest before the cassava grows large enough to cover the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha o-cassava lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa oya dani ŋmei lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close together to fill up all the open space on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛwo he ni efee efolo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leading to thin plants and small yields. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients and light to produce a full harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest grow as strong as the certified seeds I bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ edaaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories for maximum yield and disease resistance in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in lower yields and weaker plants in the second generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni amɛná yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: My cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but most of them fall off before forming pods. What is causing this?
ga: Mi koko tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo. Shi amɛteŋ babaoo baagbee shi dani amɛje kpo akɛ pods. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: High flower drop happens when cocoa trees lack enough nutrients, face water stress, or lack beneficial insects like midges to pollinate them. Pruning excessive shade trees to allow light in and applying approved cocoa fertilizers can help flowers set into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni kɛ nu mli haomɔ kpeɔ loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ ni bɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ hulutsoo be babaoo koni la abote mli, ni okɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs fertilizer before I start planting my vegetable crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi aduawai adumɔ?

english: You can judge by observing previous crop performance or by asking an extension officer for a simple soil test. If past crops grew slowly, stayed small, or had weak foliage, your soil is depleted and requires compost, manure, or balanced fertilizers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole enɛ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni ooobi amɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo, amɛji bibii loo amɛbɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaabi ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting inside after staying in the barn for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi and bacteria that enter tubers through small cuts made during harvesting or transport. Carefully avoid wounding yams when digging them up, cure them in the shade for a few days before storage, and immediately remove any damaged tubers from the barn.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria ni boteɔ tuber lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ loo gbɛfaa be mli Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ sweet potato lɛ ni ooopila lɛ he kɛji ootsa lɛ. Tsamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi dani okɛto. ni ojie ŋmeii ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I clean and remove bad maize seeds before planting them in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ehiii lɛ ahe ni mashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cleaning removes broken, infected, or dead seeds. Planting only whole, healthy seeds ensures that most of your crop germinates evenly and stays safe from early diseases.
ga: Hetsemɔ baajie dumɔwui ni ekumɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni egboi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eye emuu pɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni helai ni baa mra lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does removing damaged seeds help protect my healthy growing crops from pests?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Damaged seeds often harbor hidden insect eggs or fungus. Sorting them out stops pests and rot from spreading to healthy seeds once they are underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni efite lɛ hiɛɔ kooloi wuji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ, ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛji amɛbote shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ.

english: What happens to my yield if I plant unselected or mixed seed varieties together?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ahalaaa loo ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Mixed seeds grow at different speeds and heights, causing larger plants to steal sunlight and soil nutrients from smaller ones, which reduces your overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efutu lɛ daa oya kɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi srɔtoi. Enɛ haa tsei wuji juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: What is 'seed rate', and how does planting the right quantity affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘dumɔwui ayibɔ’ ni te dumɔ ni sa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Seed rate is the total weight or number of seeds planted per acre. Getting it right ensures plants have enough room to draw nutrients without choking each other.
ga: Dumɔwui ayibɔ ji dumɔwui ni adu yɛ acre kome mli lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ loo ayibɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛgbala niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak when I put too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the young plants fight aggressively for limited sunlight, water, and fertilizer, making them grow tall and flimsy with tiny ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baawu waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fioo. Ha amɛdara ni amɛfee mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: How deep should my maize seeds be buried in the soil during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds should be covered with a light layer of soil so they stay moist and safe from birds, but not buried too deep or they will run out of energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sũ bibioo ko aha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okpoi akabote mli. Shi kaafu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, hewalɛ lɛ baaho dani eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: How does using a planter machine help my crops grow better than planting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ niji duɔ lɛ?

english: A planter machine places seeds at an exact depth and equal distance apart, giving every plant the same opportunity to get sunlight, water, and nutrients.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: What is the purpose of the seed cup inside a planting machine?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kɔɔpoi ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: The seed cup acts as a measure that picks up and drops the exact number of seeds needed for each spot so you do not waste seeds or overcrowd your field.
ga: Dumɔwui kɔɔpoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛsusuɔ dumɔwui ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha he fɛɛ he lɛ he ni akɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni okafite dumɔwui loo okaha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ eyi fe nine.

english: Why do I need to change planter attachments when switching from maize to another grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake midumɔ nibii lɛ beni mitsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa mli kɛyaa dumɔwu kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Different seeds have different shapes and sizes, so changing the machine's attachments ensures seeds pass through smoothly without getting crushed or stuck.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni dumɔwu henɔ fɛɛ dumɔwu yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni edara ha. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsake tsɔne lɛ nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkumɔɔɔ loo amɛkpãaa shi.

english: What basic checks should I do on my planting machine before I start planting in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee dumɔ nibii esa akɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should make sure the seed cups are clean, attachments are tightly secured, and tubes are clear of dirt so seeds drop consistently across the entire field.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni dumɔwui kɔɔpoo lɛ mli atse. Akɛ nɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ekpɛtɛ he jogbaŋŋ. ni paipii lɛ bɛ muji ko Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ agbee shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply crop medicine to my plants when the leaves are wet with morning dew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni leebi ŋmɔtɔ etsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When plant leaves are wet, the medicine gets diluted by the water or drips off onto the ground before the crop can absorb it, making the treatment ineffective.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ edɔ Akɛ nu woɔ tsofa lɛ mli loo ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ni haa tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it wrong to pour fertilizer directly into the center or mouth of my young maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ loo amɛdaaŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing strong fertilizer directly into the tender center leaves burns the growing tip and can kill the young plant. Fertilizer should be placed in the soil a few inches away from the stem so roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo baai bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso bibioo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does crop medicine fail to work if rain falls right after I spray my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the medicine off the leaves before it has time to soak in or dry. For the treatment to protect your crops, it needs enough dry time on the leaves to settle and work.
ga: Nugbɔ baaho tsofa lɛ he yɛ baai lɛ anɔ dani be ashɛ ni ekɛbaawo nu mli loo ebaagbi. Kɛha tsofafeemɔi ni baabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe Ehe miihia be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he ni etsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect medicine on my crops during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying under full, hot sun can cause the medicine to evaporate too quickly or burn sensitive leaves, and it can also kill beneficial insects like bees that help your crops produce fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofa lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eshã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa onibii ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ hu.

english: How can I tell if my soil is dry enough or too wet to begin planting seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa loo edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball. If it drips water or stays as a hard, soggy lump, it is too wet; if it holds shape gently but crumbles easily when pressed, it is ready for planting.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji nu shwieɔ shi loo ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efɔ lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ efɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afee gbɔmɔtso lɛ blɛoo Shi efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaadu.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up if I plant them too deep in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too deep run out of energy trying to push through the heavy dry earth and die before their shoots can reach the light and open air.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse he.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow when there is heavy rain early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water drowns the roots by blocking air in the soil and washes away essential food, causing the plant to become hungry and turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebaatsi niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly during sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve moisture during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their green leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ baai eŋɔlii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to stop water from evaporating through them, resting until rain returns to grow fresh leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ni baai heei kwɛ̃.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and grow faster than my planted crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native to the land and naturally adapted to collect rainwater and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛbua nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to start clearing and preparing my cocoa farm in January before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli shwiemɔ kɛ esaamɔ yɛ January mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Preparing early in January allows you to clear weeds, prune dead branches, and prepare the soil before the rains begin. This ensures the soil is ready to absorb nutrients right when the crop needs them to start growing.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa ohe yɛ January shishijee gbɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ohe. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii kpakpai amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni tsei lɛ he baahia amɛ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave clearings and dead leaves to rot on the soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi hei ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Rotting leaves and crop waste break down into natural fertilizer that feeds the soil. Burning destroys these nutrients and dries out the soil, whereas leaving them helps retain moisture and keeps the ground cool.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Shãa fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi lɛ pɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo ni egbo beni mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight or high heat. Tall trees provide necessary shade that protects delicate leaves from burning and helps keep moisture in the soil around the seedling roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu ni bɔleɔ dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and curl up around the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling and brown edges are a sign that the plantain is losing water faster than its roots can draw it from the dry ground. Adding mulch around the base helps keep the soil damp and protects the root system.
ga: Eshishigbɛ ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ plantain lɛ mli nu miiho oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers before they can grow into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can support, dropping many when they experience stress like water shortages, poor nutrients, or pest attacks. Proper fertilizing and watering help the tree keep more flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Ebaa shi waa kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔi tamɔ nu ni faaa kpe. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water and survive drought. Once the rains return, the plant will naturally grow new leaves and continue growing roots underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield a huge harvest one year, but much less the next year even if the rain is the same?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi ebaafee nɔ ni baa shi kwraa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli, kɛji nugbɔ lɛ nɛ nakai nɔŋŋ po.

english: Cocoa trees experience natural yield cycles. A very heavy harvest drains the tree's energy reserves, so it produces fewer pods the following year while it rebuilds its strength.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni efeɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo. Nikpamɔ ni tsii waa lɛ haa hewalɛ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning dense branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the fungus from taking hold.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmei lɛ amɔ mli.

english: Why do I get smaller maize ears when I plant my seeds very close together in the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa toi bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow large, healthy ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why should I cut off old and non-producing branches from my cocoa trees after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Old and extra branches waste the tree's energy without producing pods. Cutting them off allows light into the tree and directs all nutrients toward growing fresh, productive shoots for the next season.
ga: Tso lɛ niji momo kɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛwooo lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa la boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsei heei ni woɔ yibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from hot sunshine to survive. Plantain grows fast and provides big leaves for shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Beni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe waa lɛ,.

english: How should I place cassava stems in the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings slanted at an angle or upright with the growing buds pointing upwards ensures strong root growth and makes it easier to harvest big tubers later.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ miida kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa waa. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa bulb agbo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight with each other for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each crop proper space allows them to grow big and produce a better harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni sa ni akɛha tsei srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmaa kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important food for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize plants the nutrients they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha o-abele tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does putting dry grass around the roots of my plants help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa mitsei lɛ ashishi he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, leaving free nutrients in the ground for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eshiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden heat or doesn't get enough regular water. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the stem and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli dɔlɛ trukaa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa enáaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛmaa shi yɛ tomato mli.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my seeds right after a strong rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Seeds need moist soil to wake up and sprout roots. Planting in wet soil gives the seeds quick access to water so they can grow strong before the hot sun dries out the land.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu oya bɔni afee ni amɛdara waa dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole patterns in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli?

english: These caterpillars, often called fall armyworms, hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. Checking your fields early and using recommended safe treatments prevents them from destroying the growing tips of the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why must I remove weeds from my field while my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop seedlings and will steal the water, soil nutrients, and sunlight your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I planted in my farm have actually sprouted properly under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Most crop seeds sprout within 4 to 10 days after planting if the soil has enough moisture. You will see small green shoots pushing up through the soil surface; if nothing appears after two weeks, the seeds may have dried out, been eaten by insects or birds, or been buried too deep.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 10 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Obaana tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. ni tsiɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji nɔ ko ejeee kpo yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi ni kooloi bibii loo okpoi eye amɛ. loo afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why are my newly sprouted crop seedlings turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Young sprouts turn yellow when they lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when they are receiving too much water or not enough sunlight. Adding compost or well-rotted animal manure gives them the food they need to regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is healthy enough for crops or if I am wasting my time planting on it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ nii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo mikɛ mibe miifite yɛ edumɔ mli?

english: Healthy farmland has dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture without staying waterlogged. If your crops stay small, thin, or yellow despite getting enough rain, the land lacks nutrients and needs organic manure or a period of rest to recover.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni haaa nu ahi mli. Kɛji onibii ni oduɔ lɛ faaa, eyɛ mlɛo loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ be ko awo mli koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay small even when the leaves on top look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil underneath to expand into large tubers. If the ground is too hard, rocky, or compacted, the roots cannot push through to form big yams, even if the leaves above ground get plenty of sunlight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato yɛ eshishi koni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ agbo. Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ,.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers before any fruit actually grows on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miifite dani aduawai lɛ miida diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of food in the soil. Keeping the soil covered with dried grass (mulching) and keeping it moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni aha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it better to plant my crops in straight rows or scatter the seeds across the field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ loo aaagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting in straight rows allows each plant to get equal space, air, and sunlight. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier without accidentally damaging your growing crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: How far apart should I space my maize plants when putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ abɔ he beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between individual plants gives the roots enough room to search for water and nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75, ni tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ateŋ lɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 40, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛtaoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ebɔi akaŋ.

english: How do I protect my young cocoa plants from dying under the hot sun during their first year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them creates a living canopy that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Should I clear weeds as soon as they appear, or can I wait until they grow bigger?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ loo manyɛ mamɛ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: It is best to remove weeds while they are still small shoots. Small weeds are easier to pull out, and clearing them early stops them from stealing water, fertilizer, and light away from your main crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lolo lɛ. Jwɛi bibii lɛ ajiemɔ waaa. kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best because the soil stays cool. Watering in the hot sun causes water to evaporate quickly before roots can drink it, and hot leaves can get scorched.
ga: Nu ni oooha lɛ leebi loo shwane lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni baai ni yɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean the plant is under attack by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or it is lacking vital soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites emɔ tso lɛ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot, when plants suffer from dry spells, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ shihilɛi Aloo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ aduawai ni shwereɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are dark black spots spreading on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions, especially when tree foliage is too dense and prevents sunlight and air from reaching the pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale, titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ. ni etsĩ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of green leaves but no seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil or over-watering encourages the plant to put all its energy into leaf development rather than producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu baai ni baa lɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains turning into dust inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli sũ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Grain weevils and beetles eat the inside of the seeds after harvest; if the maize is not dried completely or protected properly before storage, insects will ruin the grain.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa loo abuuu he jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ afite ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava rot so quickly just two days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living tissue that react quickly to air once cut from the plant, causing internal decay within 48 hours unless processed or preserved in wet sand.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji fãji ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he nii oya kɛji afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ekɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli ja atsu he nii loo akɛto ŋã ni mli efɔ mli.

english: Is it safe to spray my vegetables with pest chemicals right before I harvest them for sale?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ dani akpa ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: No, crop chemicals need a specific waiting period after spraying to break down safely; harvesting too soon leaves dangerous chemical residues on food meant for market.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ biɔ be ni akɛshwie nɔ sɛɛ koni amɛfite shweshweeshwe. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwɛɔ yɛ niyenii ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my crops even after I spray them with pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests can become resistant if you use the same chemical repeatedly, or the spray may evaporate too quickly if applied during the hottest part of the day instead of early morning or evening.
ga: Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Aloo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. moŋ fe leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: How do I know if my soil is weak and needs manure or fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Weak soil shows when crops grow slowly, display pale or purplish leaves, and give very low yields even when there is enough rainfall during the season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ be mli ni tsei daa blɛoo. Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo purple ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water to heat. It is a natural defense mechanism the plant uses to conserve moisture until the sun goes down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving crops too much water can drown their roots by filling up all the air spaces in the soil. When roots cannot get oxygen to breathe, they stop taking up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni okɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛha mumɔ Ebaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my young crops dry up and die even when it rains for a few minutes every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ minitii fioo ko pɛ daa otsi moŋ lɛ?

english: Short, light rains only wet the surface of the soil and evaporate quickly in the sun. Crops need longer, deeper rainfall so the water reaches down to their roots underground where they drink.
ga: Nugbɔ nɛ fioo be kukuoo ko. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaatsɔ la oya kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli he ni amɛnuɔ nu yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it possible for me to grow food during the dry season when there is no rain at all?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?
