english: Yes, you can grow crops during the dry season if you practice irrigation, which means bringing water from a stream, well, or tank directly to your crops instead of relying on rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛji akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛ nu aba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ faa, nu bu, loo nu ŋtayaa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ehe aaafɔ̃ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: What is irrigation, and how can it help my farm when the weather changes?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ?

english: Irrigation is any human-made method of supplying water to land or soil to grow crops. It allows you to control when and how much water your plants get, protecting your harvest if rain stops unexpectedly.
ga: Nu shwiemɔ ji gbɛ ko ni gbɔmɔ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu haa shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ekɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ be kɛ nu abɔ ni otsei lɛ náa lɛ. Buu onibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa.

english: What is the simplest way for me to water my farm if I cannot afford electricity or expensive pumps?
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu. Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe srawa hewalɛ loo pɔmp ni jara wa hu?

english: You can set up a bucket drip system using gravity, where a raised bucket or drum slowly drips water through simple plastic pipes straight to the base of each plant without needing power.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ato nu ni hoɔ tamɔ tanki mli. Bakɛti loo tanki ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ plastic paipi ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ atsɔ fiofio. Tsɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tso fɛɛ tso shishi ni tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii

english: Can I use water from a underground well to water my crops, or will it hurt them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ nubu ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ? Aloo ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Underground well water is generally safe and very good for crops, as long as it is not salty. It provides a clean and reliable source of water when surface water like rivers dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛji akɛ ŋmei bɛ mli. Amɛhaa nu jɛɛhe ni he tse ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ faai lɛ mli egbi.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often a 'false start' followed by weeks of hot, dry weather. If seeds germinate after the first rain and then receive no water, the young sprouts will dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ lɛ sɛɛ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛnáaa nu. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: How can I keep my soil moist for many days after it rains so my crops do not suffer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite?

english: You can place dry grass, crop leaves, or straw over the soil around your crops. This practice, called mulching, shades the ground from the sun and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi awo sũ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I store rainwater on my farm to use later when the rain stops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nugbɔ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: You can dig a simple farm pond lined with tarpaulin or collect rainfall from your farm structures into large drums. This stored water can keep your crops alive during short dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ tarp ebɔ he loo obua nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛwoɔ nubu agbo ko mli. Nu ni ato nɛɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni onibii ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my yam vines grow better and give bigger tubers when I make them climb wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ miha amɛkwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes keeps leaves dry and exposed to light, which prevents leaf rot diseases and helps the plant build large, healthy yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa la. Enɛ haa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potatoes agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant are a sign of nitrogen hunger. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, telling you that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ ji nitrogen hɔmɔ he okadi. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea.

english: Why are there tiny holes and dirt like sawdust inside the young leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the leaf whorl. Spraying recommended insecticides or applying clean sand/neem powder into the central funnel early saves your farm from major yield loss.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ahe ŋmeii lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ shi loo akɛ ŋã/neem powder ni he tse atsu nii yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. Ebaahere oŋmɔ lɛ yiwala koni nibii babaoo ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ akafite.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the soil like a blanket. It holds moisture in the ground, protects roots from hot sun, stops soil from drying out quickly, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ atade Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when plants lack steady water. Extreme heat dries out the flower's pollen, stopping it from forming fruit, so regular watering during flowering is critical.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ agbi. ni okpa lɛ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo akaha No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he miihia.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning shade trees and clearing overgrown branches lets air and sunlight in to dry out wet pods and stop the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajie tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la agbi tsei ni efɔ lɛ ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients and light to build thick stems and heavy fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when rain stays on the farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water suffocates root tissues and encourages harmful fungi in wet soil to attack and decay the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start carrying heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can get destroyed by underground pests called nematodes or banana weevils. Supporting heavy bunches with wooden poles prevents wind from pushing over weakened trees.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Niji ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatswa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell underground groundnut pods are mature and ready for harvest without destroying the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanut ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni mifiteee miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Pull up two or three sample plants across the field and open the pods. If the inner pod walls have dark brown or black vein markings and the nuts have firm, colored skins, your farm is ready to harvest.
ga: Gbalamɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli gbogbo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewolo ni ma shi shiŋŋ lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish your maize plants and make them stronger.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha o-corn tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛhe awa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves to conserve water when there is no rain. The plant is not dead; it rests to survive the heat and will grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛto nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ejɔɔ ehe koni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa ni baai lɛ baafee ehee kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry conditions, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I stake them on sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ mikɛwo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they get full exposure to sunlight to make food, while also keeping the leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhoo nii yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbiɔ sweet potato baai lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack from the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa kɛmiijɛ shishifãi ni miigbɛ eshwa yɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter how deep I bury maize seeds when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ futuɔ mihe miwoɔ mli mihaa beni miduɔ lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, planting too deep makes the seed waste all its energy trying to push through the soil, while planting too shallow leaves the seed exposed to heat and birds.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ kɛ okpoi aná hulutsoo.

english: Why is it important to weed my maize field during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young maize seedlings have small roots and grow slowly. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crop gets all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients without competition.
ga: Abele dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why should I uproot my old cocoa trees instead of just leaving them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei momoi amli moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Old or unproductive cocoa trees take up valuable space and soil nutrients while giving you very few pods. Uprooting them allows you to plant fresh, high-yielding seedlings that will give you much better harvests in the future.
ga: Cacao tsei ni egbɔ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ yeɔ he ko ni jara wa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shi amɛhaa bo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Shishifãi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni baaha oná ŋmaa kpakpa kwraa wɔsɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my tree crops are too old and need to be uprooted and replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni ajie ni akɛtsake?

english: If your trees produce very little fruit season after season, have stunted growth, or suffer from persistent pests and diseases, it is usually a sign that they should be cleared out and replaced with healthy new seedlings.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ Dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ. Aloo ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ajie tso lɛ ni akɛ dumɔwu hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ato najiaŋ.

english: How long does it usually take for a new mandarin seedling to start bearing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mandarin dumɔwui heei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Mandarin trees grow slowly in their early stages and typically take about 3 to 5 years before they mature enough to start producing good yields of fruit.
ga: Mandarin tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛjeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afeemɔ shishi.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa and mandarins take so much longer to grow than food crops like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo kɛ mandarin heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa fe niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Tree crops are long-term plants that spend their first few years building deep root systems and strong trunks so they can support heavy harvests for decades, unlike fast-growing seasonal crops.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ji tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Koni enyɛ ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo aba afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ be mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ.

english: What does it mean to plant my tree seedlings properly on the field?
ga: Mɛni ji mi tso dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Proper planting involves digging the right size of holes, spacing the plants correctly so they do not crowd each other, and enriching the soil with compost so the young roots can spread easily.
ga: Nɔ ni fata dumɔ ni sa he ji bu ni dalɛ sa ni atsa. Gbɛ ni ja ni ka tsei ateŋ lɛ ji koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why is it better to buy nurse-grown seedlings instead of planting seeds directly in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grown in a nursery are carefully protected through their weakest early stage, giving them a much stronger root system and a higher chance of surviving when transplanted onto your farm.
ga: Abuɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shishijee, ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa waa, ni amɛnáa hegbɛ kpakpa ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow mandarin trees on the same farm land where I plant my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mandarin tsei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ kookoo yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, you can plant mandarins alongside cocoa as long as you maintain proper spacing so neither crop steals sunlight or water from the other.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu mandarin ŋmeii yɛ kookoo masɛi, kɛji akɛ okɛ he ni sa lɛ to he. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ko akaju hulu la loo nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli.

english: Do I need to dig out all the old root systems completely before putting in new seedlings?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafo shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, removing old roots completely clears away pests and fungal diseases that might be hiding in the dead wood, ensuring your new seedlings have clean soil to grow in.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi momo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ baajie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ ahi tso ni egbo lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ kwraa kɛya. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui heei lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do to prepare my land after I uproot old trees?
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei momoi lɛ, te esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: After clearing old trees, turn over the soil, remove leftover roots and weeds, and add organic compost or manure to enrich the land before digging holes for new seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei momoi lɛ, tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ojie shishifãi kɛ jwɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ. Dani obaafo bu kɛha dumɔwu hee

english: Why do my new cocoa seedlings struggle to survive if I plant them right where old trees were dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ni atsa tsei momo lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Old trees often exhaust the nutrients in the soil directly around them. Adding compost and giving the soil proper preparation revitalizes the earth so new seedlings get enough feeding to thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhi shi. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei lɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my maize crops dry up and die so fast when the Harmattan wind starts in December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya beni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ December mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind rapidly sucks moisture out of leaves and topsoil. Applying mulch around the crop roots helps trap moisture so your maize can withstand the dry breeze longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Mulching ni ooobɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni o-abele lɛ anyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during dry weather to reduce water loss and survive, but the roots under the ground will stay alive and start producing fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsɔɔ etsui mli ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ehi shi. Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baahi shi ni amɛbaabɔi baai heei feemɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from losing too much water faster than their roots can pull it from the ground; they usually recover as the temperature drops in the evening.
ga: yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: If I leave my farm land to rest for three years, why do crops grow much better when I plant on it again?
ga: Kɛji mishi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii etɛ Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow allows natural vegetation to rot and decay into organic matter, which restores essential nutrients to the soil and starves out soil pests that target farm crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbalaa amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ajie shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I change the type of crop I plant on the same plot of land from one season to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ be kome mli kɛya be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Rotating crops prevents specific pests and diseases from building up in the soil and stops the land from running out of the same nutrients year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree take about three to four years before it starts bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees spend their first few years developing strong root systems and sturdy trunks to store energy before they can support heavy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii kɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my corn plants produce tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving little energy for the plants to form large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my groundnut plants help my maize grow greener when I plant them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmei lɛ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ du amɛ ekomekomei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting like a built-in fertilizer for companion crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nanemɛi tsei tamɔ ŋmãa amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to the local environment, meaning their roots are extremely aggressive at taking up water and soil nutrients before crop seeds can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa waa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlimɔ mli dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to cut off the lower branches of my tomato plants as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pruning lower leaves stops them from touching damp soil where fungal diseases live, allowing the plant to send more water and energy up to growing fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hiɔ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo majeɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same land as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and provide heavy shade and soil moisture that cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa babaoo ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I trim or cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the tree, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa lɛ afee baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni mli wa.

english: Why are small green worms eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that hide in the center whorl of maize to eat soft leaves. Spraying early or applying neem extract stops them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ amɛhe ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ mra Loo akɛ neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Yam tubers grow deep underground. Soft, raised soil mounds give the tubers space to expand easily without fighting hard soil, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing leaf decay.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water stays trapped in the soil for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing underground rot caused by soil fungus and standing water.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot or when the plant suffers from sudden water stress. Regular watering during flowering helps the fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba tso lɛ nɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛyibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which protects the soil from hot sun, retains moisture in the ground, and stops weeds from taking nutrients away from your pepper plants.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow well right after I burn cleared bushes on my land, but grow poorly in the seasons after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ beni mishã brɔshi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛkɛ? Shi edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ no sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Ash from burning gives a fast, temporary boost of plant nutrients, but the high heat destroys long-term soil organic matter and beneficial organisms needed to keep soil healthy year after year.
ga: Ashwishwɛ ni jɛɔ shãa mli lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ oya, yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ.

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-drained soil where water does not collect in pools. If your soil is too hard or full of heavy clay, the roots will struggle to expand into big tubers.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni nu ebuaaa ehe naa yɛ nu ŋshɔ lɛ mli Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Why will my crops produce smaller harvest if I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong and produce well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is getting too much or too little water. Adding compost or the right fertilizer can help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to provide cover and retain soil moisture while they are still growing.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛtee ni akɛto ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach up high into the sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking the vines keeps leaves exposed to the sun, which helps the yam tuber under the ground grow bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Hulu la ni akɛwoɔ mli koni akɛfee niyenii aha sweet potato tsei lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist can help fix this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I wait after the very first rain of the year before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: The first rain often refreshes dry soil, but a long dry heat wave can follow soon after. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he jɔɔ. Shi hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Switching crops or planting beans helps restore nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes in corn leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on young leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended treatments can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do I still need to clear weeds even after my crops have grown big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light from your crops at all stages of growth. Clearing them regularly ensures all the soil nutrients go directly into making your crop produce more yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ amɛdalɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli. Kɛ́ ofɔ amɛhe daa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if a disease is attacking my cocoa trees before all of them die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hela dani amɛ fɛɛ amɛgboi?

english: Look out for early signs such as yellowing leaves, swollen shoots, or dark spots on the pods. Spotting these symptoms early helps you isolate or remove infected trees before the sickness spreads to the rest of your farm.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ baai ŋmɔŋ, ŋmeii ni efuu, loo hei ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Okadii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsiɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli loo ojieɔ amɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops get sick even when I clear the weeds and keep the farm clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi ni mikwɛɔ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse moŋ?

english: Crop diseases are often caused by tiny germs, fungi, or viruses carried by wind, rain, insects, or farm tools. Even a weed-free farm can get infected if these disease carriers enter from neighboring lands.
ga: Muawai bibii, ŋmei, loo muawai kɛ tsei helai baa. ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, loo okwaayeli nibii kɛbaa lɛ Okwaafoi ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ po baanyɛ aná hela kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ helai ahe nibii nɛɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ amɛbote mli.

english: Can I use the same cutlass on healthy trees after cutting down a diseased crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dagger nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ beni mifo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, using the same tool can transfer disease-causing sap or germs directly into healthy plants. Always clean your cutlass with fire or soap and water before working on healthy crops.
ga: Dabi, dɛŋdadei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu loo helai ni kɛ helai baa lɛ aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ la loo samla kɛ nu atsumɔ o-razor lɛ he dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ akɛ amɛ fĩ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods on time helps control it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni oookpa yɛ be kome mli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ niji lɛ.

english: Is it good to plant food crops like cassava or maize on land where cocoa died from disease?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela egbe ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like cassava or maize helps break the disease cycle because cocoa diseases usually cannot survive on these different plant types, giving the soil time to recover.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ. Akɛni bei pii lɛ, kookoo hela nyɛɛɛ ahi tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ anɔ hewɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: How long should I leave my land unused after a major crop disease wipes out my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛtsuuu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela ko ni naa wa efite miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving the land fallow or rotating with a completely different crop for at least one to two seasons starves the specific disease organisms living in the soil so they do not attack your new plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo atsake ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi kwraa kɛ hoo lɛ be kome loo bei enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha helai pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aye hɔmɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛtutuuu otsei heei lɛ.

english: Why does land that used to give good harvests stop producing well after many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kpaɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: I just inherited an old, neglected farm from my family; what is the first thing I should do to revive it?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni miná ŋmɔ momo ko ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ gboshinii kɛjɛ miweku lɛ dɛŋ. Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛwo mli ekoŋŋ?

english: First, inspect the land to identify and remove any diseased or dead trees. Then, clear heavy weeds and prune overgrown shade trees to bring sunlight and fresh air back to the farm.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ona tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo tsei ni egboi lɛ ni ojie amɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ ni ofolɔ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to plant young seedlings right next to old, dying cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi? Cocoa tso momo ni miigbo?

english: It is risky because old or dying trees often harbour pests and diseases that easily spread to young seedlings, which do not yet have the strength to survive an infection.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ loo ni egboi lɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛjɛ hela mli lɛ jɛɛhe.

english: What should I do with diseased plants after I cut them down from my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: You should carry them away from healthy plants and burn or bury them deeply. Leaving infected branches lying around allows the disease to spread back to healthy crops through wind and rain.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli ni oshã loo ofu amɛ shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei niji ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ agbele lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving larger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants give me smaller roots when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii shwereɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their stems compete with each other for sunlight above ground, and their roots fight for nutrients and water underground, leading to smaller crop yields.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. ni eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a vital food for leafy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) protects the soil from hot sun, helps it stay wet longer after watering, stops weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni awo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: You can plant them together because cowpeas actually feed the soil by trapping nitrogen from the air. This natural fertilizer helps the maize grow better without competing heavily for food.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome ejaakɛ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii he akaŋshii babaoo.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides and feeds inside the growing center of the maize plant. Applying safe natural treatments like neem seed extract early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagbai lɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ni eyeɔ nii yɛ he ni ŋmei tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli. Tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni oooye leebi lɛ baanyɛ akpa enɛɛmɛi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes water to collect in heavy soil, which starves the roots of air and allows fungal diseases to multiply and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛgboɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes for their vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce the food that gets sent down underground to grow large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ woɔ niyenii ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil, causing the plant to save its energy by shedding flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer so it doesn't hurt my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli koni amɛkaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool and the soil is damp, preventing the fertilizer from burning the plant roots in the hot sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni ekashã tso shishifãi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to mix my chemical thoroughly with water and shake it before spraying my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai futuɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni mihosoɔ dani mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: If you do not shake and mix the chemical properly, the concentrated chemical settles at the bottom of the spray tank. This causes some plants to receive pure water while others get a harsh, unmixed dose that burns and destroys the crop within days.
ga: Kɛji okɛ tsofai lɛ shwieee shi ni okɛfutuuu amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ spray tanki lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi náa nu ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei komɛi nine shɛɔ nu ni mli wa ni akɛfutuuu nɔ ni shãa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did my maize leaves turn brown and die right after I put fertilizer at the base of the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akɛ ŋmãa wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is like strong salt. Placing it directly against the stem causes 'chemical burn' on the roots and plant stem. Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away in the soil so the roots can safely draw in the nutrients.
ga: Fertilizer tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ‘Chemical burn’ aba Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it bad to spray pest chemicals on my crops during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ?

english: Yes, spraying under hot midday sun causes the chemical solution to evaporate too quickly or react with the intense heat, which scorches the plant leaves and reduces the chemical's ability to kill pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo ekɛ la ni naa wa lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã ni ebaa tsofa lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛgbeɔ koolooi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why did my vegetables dry up and die shortly after using a cheap pesticide I bought from an uncertified vendor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gĩ ni amɛgboi beni mikɛ tsofa ko ni jara waaa ni mihe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni bɛ hegbɛ lɛ tsu nii sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Uncertified or fake pesticides often contain dangerous, incorrect chemicals or improper concentrations that burn plant leaves instantly. Always purchase agrochemicals from licensed dealers who provide proper instructions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni teɔ shi woɔ mla, ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni bɛ he odaseyeli loo amalei amli. Aloo nɔ ko ni esaaa ni baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ agrochemicals kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ekɛ ŋaawoo ni ja haa lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Why does using muddy river water to mix my crop spray make the pesticide stop working?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ haaa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii lɛ?

english: Dirty or muddy water contains dirt particles and minerals that bind to the pesticide particles, neutralizing the active ingredient and making the spray useless against pests.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji lɛ mli muji kɛ minerals ni kpɛtɛɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ mli. Ehaa tsofa ni tsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I flush out my knapsack sprayer with clean water after spraying my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii lɛ nɔ beni mikɛshwie ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leftover chemicals dry inside the tank and nozzle, clogging the sprayer. Additionally, old chemical residue can mix unpredictably with new chemicals next time, causing damage to your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ tanki lɛ kɛ nozzle lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ afutu tsofai heei yɛ gbɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ be kroko. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when left under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and soft leaves that lose water rapidly under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas until their roots grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my planted seeds rotting in the dirt instead of growing into shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted too deep or in overly flooded soil where there is no air. Seeds need moisture, light soil cover, and air to sprout; too much water cuts off oxygen and suffocates them.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ fe nine ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nu babaoo ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are falling off because of a disease or because I applied too much chemical?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji hela loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsu nii lɛ hewɔ ni tsei ahe baai lɛ miigbee shi lɛ?

english: Chemical damage happens rapidly within 24 to 48 hours, leaving dry, crisp burn patches. Disease develops gradually over weeks, creating spreading spots, molds, or yellowing patterns.
ga: Tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa oya, yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli, ni ekɛ shãa ni egbi ni egbɔjɔ baa. Hela lɛ baa fiofio yɛ otsii komɛi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my crops still get eaten by insects even though I spray pesticide every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ nɔ daa otsi moŋ lɛ?

english: Spraying too frequently with the wrong chemical mixture can cause insects to build resistance. Using the correct chemical ratio at proper intervals is key to effective pest control.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ shwie shi shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi lɛ afee nɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Tsofa ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants use to grow green and strong. Adding compost, well-rotted animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer when the crops are young will help them turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa Koolooi ashishifã ni egbo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on wooden stakes so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. The more sunlight the leaves capture above ground, the larger the yam tubers grow under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei ahe bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee amɛ niyenii. Babaoo ni baai lɛ naa hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni sweet potato tuber lɛ daa lɛ, babaoo ni ebaada yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the deep center funnel of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest in Ghana that loves to hide and feed on the tender leaves inside the central funnel of maize. Applying recommended pesticides or neem leaf extract directly into the funnels early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni jɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ni eye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plants from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these small insects early with neem spray or soapy water helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem spray loo nu ni akɛ samla tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds even when they have green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai eŋɔli moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic pests called nematodes or banana weevil grubs eat away their underground root system, ruining their grip on the soil. Planting clean suckers and supporting fruiting stems with bamboo props prevents them from falling.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana weevils lɛ ye amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ yibii amli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays too wet for too long, especially in heavy clay or waterlogged land. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my ripe tomato fruits split open on the sides just as they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split open when the plant receives a sudden flush of water or heavy rainfall after a dry period. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch; keeping soil moisture steady with grass mulch helps stop this.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nu ni hoɔ trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch baakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni akpa enɛ.

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and moist under the hot sun, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into natural manure as the dry leaves decompose.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ, ni fiofio lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni baai ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the full rainy season truly begins. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young seedlings will dry out and die before the reliable rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my young cocoa trees fall off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the farm gets too dry, when shade is insufficient, or when tiny pests called mirids attack the blossoms. Keeping adequate shade trees and protecting the farm during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Without bigger shade trees or companion crops like plantain to block the direct sun, the leaves burn easily and the plant loses moisture faster than its roots can take it up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ shãa oya ni tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch and expanding tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a buaa ngmlɛfia a nya nɛ a duɔ ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling leaves is a protective survival mechanism. By curling its leaves inward, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing critical water loss through transpiration.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala hebuu gbɛ. Abɛi haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ waa kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my tomato plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme temperature spikes, dry winds, or inadequate pollination cause flower abortion. If temperatures get too high, the pollen dries out and becomes sterile, so the plant sheds the flower instead of wasting energy on unfertilized growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ fɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ebafeɔ nɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ dalɛ ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the center and tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a mobile nutrient, so when soil supplies are low, the plant draws nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ateŋ kɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes and powder like wet sawdust inside the middle funnel of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni powda ko tamɔ ŋmei ni efɔ lɛ yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is characteristic of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day, feeding on young leaf tissue and leaving behind coarse waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe su. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baa bibii amli fãji ni amɛshiɔ fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the hot afternoon even when the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually a sign of root rot or bacterial wilt. Fungal or bacterial pathogens attack the plant's root system, clogging the internal channels that carry water up the stem, causing the leaves to dry out despite moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ he okadi. Fungi loo bacteria ni gbeɔ helai lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ shishifãi. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ gbɛi ni kɛ nu yaa ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very thin stalks and small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ ŋmeii bibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Crowding forces plants to compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. When too close, individual plants cannot gather enough resources to build thick stems or fully develop large, healthy cobs.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Kɛ́ obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei aŋkroaŋkroi nyɛŋ abua nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse loo amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni he wa kwraa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my plot make my soil richer for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny root nodules containing friendly bacteria that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a usable food form. When the roots decay after harvest, they release natural nitrogen into the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii. kɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce small, misshapen tubers when I plant them in hard, unplowed ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii beni midu amɛ yɛ hei ni wa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, aerated soil to expand downward smoothly. Hard soil acts as a physical barrier, forcing the growing tuber to curve, deform, or stop growing altogether.
ga: Sweet potato yibii lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii. Ni anyɛɔ bulb ni miida lɛ nɔ koni ebɔle, efite, loo ekpa dalɛ kwraa.

english: This yellowing usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is a main food crops need to grow green and strong. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new green growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small leaves when weeds are growing next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli waa yɛ be mli ni jwɛi yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from your crops. When weeds surround a plant, the crop is forced to stretch upward to search for sunlight instead of growing thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, Abaanyɛ Dumɔwui anɔ ni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao hulu la. Mohu ɔ, e daa nɛ e he wa.

english: Why is it better to measure space between my cassava cuttings instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaasusu he ni yɔɔ ŋmei niji ateŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni ooodu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough underground room to expand into large tubers. Planting them too close forces the roots to fight each other for food and space, resulting in thin, woody roots instead of big cassava tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ he ko he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso shishifãi bibii Yɛ ŋmei shishifã agbo najiaŋ

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same land with my maize without damaging the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ ni mifiteee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as free natural fertilizer for your maize plants while suppressing weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ yɛ be kome too mli. kɛ jwɛi nɔyeli

english: Young cocoa plants act like human babies and cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Tall shade trees protect cocoa seedlings from intense heat and keep moisture in the air and soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers and stop producing pods during dry periods to conserve water and survive. Without enough soil moisture, the tree protects itself by shutting down fruit production until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ feemɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ aduawai ni amɛkpaa amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and greenish dirt inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and eats the young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why do my pepper stems turn dark brown and rot at the ground level after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a soil fungus that prospers in soggy, waterlogged ground. When water gathers around the base of the pepper plant without draining away, it creates the perfect condition for fungal rot to destroy the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ nu. Beni nu bua ehe naa kɛbɔleɔ Pepper tso lɛ shishi ni nu lɛ hoɔ. Ebaaha ŋmei lɛ agbo ni efite tso lɛ yitso lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my granular fertilizer on the farm just before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the topsoil into gutters and streams before the roots can absorb it. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, or buried slightly near the plant base so water dissolves it slowly into the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo afu fioo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli fiofio kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any tomatoes when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato blossoms. When pollen gets too hot, flowers fail to fertilize and fall off the plant without ever producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji pollen lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔmɔ nii ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings naturally grow under forest shade. Direct tropical sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly, so keeping shade trees or intercropping with plantains acts as a umbrella to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shade loo dumɔwui ni akɛduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that store starch in underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into full sunlight, allowing the plant to make maximum food through photosynthesis, which directly increases the size of the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ starch toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli. Staking baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Ehaa tsei feɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When maize lacks nitrogen, it extracts the remaining nutrient from its older, bottom leaves and sends it to feed the growing top leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow and die.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛmajeɔ ŋwɛi baa ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Extreme heat and high humidity cause pollination failure in tomatoes. When daytime temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy rather than trying to nourish fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa tomato pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and turning crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. The damage distorts leaf tissue as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni efite lɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water up from the soil. The plant temporarily droops to shrink leaf surface area and save moisture, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baajie amɛ baai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni efo baa lɛ nɔ ni ebu ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I find holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is the feeding behavior of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest crawls into the central funnel (whorl) of maize during the day to hide from heat and predators while chewing on tender, developing leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ niyenii yeli su. Kpluka nɛɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ faa (ring) lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni ekɛ ehe awo latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni ekɛ baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ yeɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right when the fruit bunches are growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that stay near the topsoil. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the center of gravity shifts, and wet soil or wind can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ aduawai akui babaoo dara lɛ Hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baatsake. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo ja tso nibii fiɔ osɛɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but only yield tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji babaoo ni eyɛ baai shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy stem and leaf tissue above ground instead of storing starch in the roots to make thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ baai ahe fãji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e toɔ starch ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nɛ mi wa.

english: Why does my land yield much less corn when I plant maize on the exact same field three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli bei etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?
