english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the topsoil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do crops like cucumbers produce fruit so much faster in a greenhouse than on my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kukumba woɔ yibii oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses create a controlled environment that protects crops from harsh weather and pests, allowing plants like cucumbers to grow rapidly and mature enough to be harvested every three days.
ga: Greenhouses haa shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei tamɔ kukumba ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ daa gbii etɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for setting up a greenhouse for vegetable production?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha aduawai akwɛmɔhe?

english: A location is suitable for a greenhouse if it has proper sunlight, good drainage, access to clean water, and flat ground, which allows fast-growing crops to thrive under controlled conditions.
ga: Akɛ he ko ni sa kɛha greenhouse lɛ haa kɛji akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyaa nu ni mli tse kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni haa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ daa yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Does growing vegetables in a greenhouse make the plants yield more produce than traditional farming?
ga: Ani aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei babaoo baa fe blema nibii ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, greenhouse conditions boost crop performance, causing plants to produce heavy yields continuously, which requires frequent harvesting every few days once production starts.
ga: Hɛɛ, greenhouse shihilɛi haa tsei lɛ anitsumɔ yaa hiɛ. Ha tsei awo yibii babaoo daa ni esa akɛ akpa shii abɔ Daa gbii fioo komɛi kɛji nibii afeemɔ je shishi.

english: How often will I need to pick my cucumbers once they start fruiting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafolɔ kukuji kɛji amɛbɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Cucumber plants in optimal conditions produce very quickly, meaning you will need to harvest mature fruits every 3 days to keep the plants productive and prevent over-ripening.
ga: Kukumba tsei ni yɔɔ shihilɛ ni sa mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa gbii etɛ koni tso lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii ni ekakwɛ̃ fe nine.

english: What will happen to my cucumber crop if I leave the mature fruits on the plant without harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi kukumba tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni mikpaaa?

english: If you do not harvest mature cucumbers every few days, the fruits become oversized and spoil, and the plant stops producing new flowers and young fruits.
ga: Kɛji okpaaa kukumba ni eda lɛ daa gbii fioo lɛ, aduawai lɛ baadara tsɔ ni amɛbaafite. ni tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei feemɔ.

english: Why do high-yielding vegetable crops require so much attention once harvest begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ aduawai ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ waa kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Fast-producing crops mature continuously, meaning large quantities of ripe produce build up rapidly every few days and must be picked immediately to avoid spoilage.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii oya lɛ baaya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nibii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa oya daa gbii fioo komɛi, ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkafite.

english: Why should I hold off on planting greenhouse crops if I haven't secured buyers yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ mli kɛji mibɛ mɔ ko ni baahe lolo?

english: Greenhouse crops like cucumbers produce large harvests every three days; without a ready market, your fresh produce will pile up rapidly and rot before you can sell it.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ kukumba lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo daa gbii etɛ kɛji akɛ jara ni yɔɔ klalo bɛ. Onibii heei ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baabua amɛhe naa oya ni amɛbaafite dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How fast do freshly harvested vegetables like cucumbers spoil after picking?
ga: Te aduawai ni akpa ehee, tamɔ kukumba lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Freshly picked cucumbers have high water content and spoil quickly in warm temperatures, which is why having buyers lined up before harvest is critical.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ kukumba ni ajie ehee lɛ mli, ni efiteɔ oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni aha mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ ahi line mli dani akpa nii lɛ.

english: Should I arrange my market connections before putting seeds in the ground or after harvesting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mato jarayeli he tsakpaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo beni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should always secure your market before planting, because once fast-yielding crops start producing every few days, you will not have enough time to search for buyers.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ojarayelihe lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be dani odu. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ tsei ni woɔ yibii oya lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo daa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, onaŋ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛtao mɛi ni baahe amɛ.

english: What is the biggest risk I face if my greenhouse crops perform extremely well?
ga: Mɛni ji osharai wuji ni mikɛkpeɔ kɛji mi-greenhouse tsei lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ waa?

english: The main risk of a very successful crop is production overload; if the yield is high and continuous but you lack buyers, you face heavy financial loss from rotting produce.
ga: Oshara titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye waa lɛ akwɛmɔ mli ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa fe nine. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni afee lɛ fa ni eyaa nɔ shi mɛi ni heɔ lɛ faaa lɛ Ehe baahia ni okɛ shika babaoo ni baafite kɛjɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpee.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, tender leaves that lose water very quickly under direct heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sunlight, the young plants burn and dry out before their roots can grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Does planting my cassava stems too close together affect how big the tubers will grow?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ baaná ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, when cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily with each other for space, water, and plant nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to form large, heavy tubers under the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shi waa koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: If too many small shoots grow around one main plantain tree, they steal food and water from the parent plant. Pruning extra shoots ensures the main plant gets all the energy it needs to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he lɛ, Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for growth. Adding manure or proper fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need to turn dark green and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves and clearings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni baai egbi ni ajie amɛhe?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter keeps the ground cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun. As those dry leaves rot, they turn into rich manure that feeds your crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ nakai baai ni egbi lɛ fite lɛ Ebaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha onibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crop help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally fertilize the soil and help neighboring crops grow stronger without extra chemical inputs.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛfɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. It also causes pests and diseases that attack maize to build up permanently in that field.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the center leaf tip to eat the tender growth. Detecting this early allows you to spray approved treatments before the worm destroys the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ koni eye tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli wa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra ni anaa Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo mli dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Bottom rot on tomatoes usually happens when watering is irregular or the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent and watering directly at the roots helps prevent the fruits from spoiling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be loo tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa yibii lɛ afite.

english: How do I know if the very first rain of the season is enough for me to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛdu midumɔwui lɛ?

english: The first rain often wet only the surface layer of soil, which can trick seeds into sprouting before they dry out and die in the dry days that follow. It is safest to wait until a few steady rains wet the soil deep below the surface before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ dani amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nɛɔ daa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds your maize, giving you a better harvest without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa kpakpa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its richness without sending it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori ko mli?

english: You can tell by watching leaf colors and crop growth. If lower leaves turn yellow early, plants stay unusually short, or yields drop year after year, your soil is running out of essential nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ahe su kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya Tso lɛ yɛ kuku yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. loo nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, cold, and overly shady conditions. Trimming extra branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods quickly keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he koni hulu la babaoo aba mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground usually happens when water sits around the roots in poorly drained soil, or when tiny soil worms called nematodes bite the tubers, allowing decay-causing fungi to enter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji nu ebɔle he. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii Atsɛɔ amɛ yitsoŋ ŋmeii. Ha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ abote mli.

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a hungry pest that hides in the funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early and spraying ash, neem leaf extract, or approved pesticides into the funnel protects the plant's growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ ni ji Neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo funnel lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ yitsei lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from heat. The plant is not dead; it is resting and will grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ehe ejɔɔ ehe ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato flowers and dries out the pollen, preventing them from forming fruit. Watering early in the morning and providing light shade helps the plant set fruit during hot periods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. prevent fruition Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and bushy under tree shade but give very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hulutsoo be mli shi ewoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to produce flowers and fruit. In deep shade, the plant uses all its energy to grow taller toward the light rather than growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ la lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eha tso lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know that my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvest without digging up every stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower stem leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni shishigbɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your plant lacks nitrogen, an important food for crop growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send the remaining nitrogen to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ aha koni amɛha tsei heei ni dara lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas can take nitrogen directly from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and turn hard during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot periods to trap moisture underneath and reduce water loss. It is the plant's natural shield to keep itself from drying out when the sun is too strong.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛmɔ nu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ enaa koni ekagbi kɛji hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Why do white, powdery spots appear on my garden eggs leaves when the morning weather is very foggy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ beni leebi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cool, humid morning air creates moisture on leaves, which helps tiny fungal germs grow. This fungal growth blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf surface and weakens the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ leebi lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ daa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack enough water. The plant panics under stress and sheds flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei sheɔ gbeyei yɛ haomɔ shishi ni amɛshwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big umbrella leaves that shade young cocoa trees until they are strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ ŋmeii agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha hulutsoo be fɛɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from around the stems of my young cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi-cassava bibioo lɛ tso lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for water, soil food, and sunlight. Clearing weeds ensures your cassava roots get all the water and nutrients they need to produce large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why produce smaller bunches of plantains when I plant the suckers very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ plantains akuu bibioo ko ahi shi lɛ? Beni aduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too closely, their roots fight each other for moisture and nutrients in the soil while leaves block light from reaching neighbors, resulting in smaller crop yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ ahe Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains develop mold when I store them in sacks right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize grains still contain moisture inside. If bagged immediately without proper sun-drying, that trapped moisture allows mold to grow and rot your grain.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ajieee lɛ kpo yɛ hulutsoo be mli jogbaŋŋ Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃ ni ŋmaa lɛ agbo.

english: Why do seeds from bought hybrid maize perform poorly if I save them and plant them again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni ahe lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛto ni midu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from two distinct parent plants to produce strong yields for one generation. Saving and replanting their seeds breaks that genetic blend, causing second-generation crops to grow weak and uneven.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ fɔmɔ nii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa ni egbɔjɔ ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: What happens to my maize crop if excess water collects and stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa ni edamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Excess standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off oxygen. This causes the roots to rot, the leaves to turn yellow, and eventually kills the plant because it cannot absorb essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does water flowing onto my farm from surrounding areas damage my crops?
ga: Te nu ni jɛɔ hei ni ebɔle mi lɛ boteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess water rushing across your land washes away the rich topsoil and nutrients your crops need. It also weakens the soil structure around the plant base, making crops easy to wash away or fall over.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaho sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni fa babaoo lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaho loo amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants fall over or get easily pulled out of the ground after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil becomes overly saturated with water, it loses its firmness and turns to mud. The plant roots lose their grip, making the crop unstable and prone to falling over or uprooting easily.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tse shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbee shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do the roots of my vegetable crops rot when the soil stays constantly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Roots need air to stay healthy. Soil that remains constantly wet creates a home for destructive fungi that attack tender plant roots, causing them to turn black, decay, and stop feeding the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ feɔ shihilɛhe kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni tutuaa tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛkpaa tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Can I grow coconut trees in an area of my farm that experiences frequent flooding?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmɔji amli hei ni nu shwieɔ shi yɛ jɛmɛ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: While full-grown coconut palms can tolerate short periods of wet soil, prolonged flooding damages young coconut roots, slows down their growth, and leads to poor nut production.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ gbɛ be kukuoo ko moŋ, shi nu afua ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baafite ŋmei shishifãi bibii lɛ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni ehiii

english: Why are my young coconut trees dropping their flowers and small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii bibii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Coconut trees drop young fruits when they experience environmental stress, such as root damage from standing water or sudden changes in water availability, to conserve their remaining energy.
ga: Kokoo tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ shishifãi ni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ efite loo nu ni yɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa. koni akɛto hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he

english: Is it good to plant large coconut trees right in the middle of my food crop field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmei tso agbo yɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Planting large coconut trees in the middle of food crops creates heavy shade and root competition. As the palm grows, its wide root network steals water and nutrients from smaller surrounding crops.
ga: Kokoo tsei wuji ni aduɔ yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ shishifãi ahe akaŋshii ni naa wa baa. Beni tso lɛ da Eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli.

english: Why are the crops I plant near the edge of my farm boundary growing much smaller than the rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ shwereɔ fioo kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Boundary crops often suffer because they compete with neighboring vegetation for sunlight and soil nutrients, or they receive water runoff coming directly from adjacent land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ husu naa lɛ naa amanehulu ejaakɛ amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. aloo enine shɛɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep failing even after I clear the land and replant new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ efiteɔ lɛ? Beni mijie jɛmɛ ni midu dumɔwui heei po sɛɛ.

english: If underlying problems like waterlogging, poor soil nutrients, or root diseases in the soil are not fixed first, new seeds will face the exact same conditions and fail to grow healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishijee naagbai tamɔ nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi kɛ niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifã hela ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ asaaa klɛŋklɛŋ Dumɔwui heei kɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baakpe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara waa.

english: How can I tell if heavy water damage has permanently ruined my farm's soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu afua ni efite lɛ efite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa?

english: Water-damaged soil often hardens into a thick crust when dry, smells bad when wet, and causes leaves on new plants to turn yellow quickly due to a lack of soil air and beneficial organisms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu efite lɛ mli waɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse kɛji egbi. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo kɛji edɔ Ni enɛ haa tsei heei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does water always gather in the same low spots on my farm whenever it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ shi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downhill to the lowest points of your land. These low-lying areas accumulate runoff water, creating moist zones that retain dampness much longer than higher ground.
ga: Nu hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛyaa he ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ nɛɛ buaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does falling rain actually change the condition of my farm's soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When raindrops hit bare soil, they act like tiny hammers that break apart soil clumps and cause particles to splash. Over time, this constant raindrop impact compresses the topsoil and reshapes the surface of your field.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaafee tamɔ hama bibioo. koni ekɛgbala shikpɔŋ sũ mli nibii bibii amli ni eha nibii bibii lɛ ajɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa nɛɛ mli baa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni etsakeɔ oŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Does a very heavy, forceful rain soak into my soil better than a light rain?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni naa wa lɛ boteɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo?

english: No, the strength or force of the water does not mean it penetrates better. Heavy downpours often beat down on the surface and run off quickly, while gentle, steady rains give the soil time to absorb the water deeply.
ga: Dabi, hewalɛ loo hewalɛ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ebaabote mli jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ ni ehoɔ oya. Beni nugbɔ miinɛ fioo ni eyaa nɔ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛnu nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plant leaves get covered in mud after a heavy rainfall, and is that bad for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ muji ehà mitso lɛ baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Ni ani no náa tso lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: When rain strikes bare earth, it splashes soil and water upward onto your crops. This mud splash can carry fungal spores and diseases from the ground directly onto your crop leaves, potentially causing rot or leaf damage.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Muji kɛ nu baashwie onibii anɔ. Nɛkɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baanyɛ ajie fungal spores kɛ helai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya otso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ agbo loo amɛfite.

english: What can I do to protect my land from getting damaged when heavy rains hit the dirt directly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekafite kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You can cover the bare ground with mulch, dry straw, or cover crops. This creates a cushion that absorbs the heavy impact of raindrops so the water soaks in gently without splashing dirt or washing away topsoil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, jwɛi ni egbi, loo okɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Enɛ haa kushin ko ni shwieɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni wa lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ mli blɛoo ni ekɛ muji shwieee shi loo ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my land has absorbed enough water for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ emɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You need to check below the dry surface layer. Scoop up soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it in your hand; if it holds together in a soft moist ball without dripping, the soil has absorbed enough rain for planting.
ga: Ehe miihia ni okwɛ akɛ shishigbɛ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ egbi. Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi amli ni okɛmimɔ oniji amli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe babɔ he ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eŋɔ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaadu nii.

english: Why do I see so many different types of insects and animals gathering around the wet areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi srɔtoi babaoo ni bua amɛhe naa yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water sources attract all kinds of wildlife and farm pests, even different species that do not normally group together. Moist areas give them a steady source of drinking water, cool shade, and a green feeding ground during warm periods.
ga: Nu jɛɛhei lɛ gbalaa koo mli kooloi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi srɔtoi fɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni bei pii lɛ amɛfeee kuu lɛ po He ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa nu ni amɛnuɔ daa, hulutsoo kɛ niyelihei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How do I keep pests from destroying my crops near the places where water gathers on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni nu eyi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can clear thick weeds around standing water, build simple drainage ditches to keep water moving, or plant natural pest-repellent crops along the wet borders to prevent insects from breeding near your farm's water spots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he lɛ, ni ofee nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. koni eha nu lɛ aya Aloo adu adebɔɔ mli tsei ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɛ ŋshɔi ni efɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni kooloi bibii akafɔ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Which crops should I put in parts of my field that tend to hold standing water after rain?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi ni bei pii lɛ nu damɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Crops like rice, sugarcane, or cocoyam prefer wet, saturated soil and do well in low areas. Crops like maize or cassava will suffer root rot if planted in land where water sits for days.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ omɔ, shɛ̃, loo kookoo sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baafite amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo.

english: Why does wet land seem to behave differently every season even if I plant the same crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛyaa be kroko mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ po.

english: Soil behavior changes based on rainfall patterns, seasonal water flow, and how the land retains moisture over time. Water constantly reshapes nutrients and soil tightness, affecting how crops grow from year to year.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ subaŋ tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ naa. nu ni hoɔ yɛ be mli kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Nu tsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ bɔ ni sũ lɛ mli edɔ ha lɛ be fɛɛ be. Enáa tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ daa afi.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce less harvest every year even though I work hard on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsu nii waa kɛha lɛ?

english: Over time, crop plants pull vital nutrients out of the soil. Without adding nutrients back through fertilizer or compost, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller harvests each passing year.
ga: Beni be hoɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has become tired and unproductive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ewooo yibii?

english: Tired soil often becomes hard or dry, crops grow slowly with pale or yellowing leaves, and harvest sizes drop continuously over several seasons despite normal rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ fɔɔ shiwoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. Ni ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi yɛ bei babaoo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can planting the exact same crop on the same land for many years ruin the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting only one crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases to build up, making future harvests smaller and smaller.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni aduɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ ajɛ mli kɛya nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli nikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛyaa bibioo.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to rot and spoil before I am able to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Spoilage before harvest is usually caused by fungal diseases like black pod disease or insect infestation, which spread easily when farms are overly shaded, crowded, or unpruned.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai, tamɔ black pod hela, loo ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tsɔ. Eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi. loo akafolɔ

english: What is the best way to prevent my harvested cocoa beans from going to waste?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite?

english: Harvested beans must be properly fermented under banana leaves for 5 to 7 days and dried evenly on raised bamboo mats in direct sunlight to prevent mold and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ atswa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ banana baai ashishi gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 ni agbi yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest if I don't clear them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji mikɛ jwɛi tsuuu nii daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving the main crop weak and unable to produce good fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: What can I do to make an old, unproductive farm plot fertile again?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni ŋmɔ mli shikpɔji ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ awo yibii ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore unproductive land by applying animal manure or compost, planting leguminous cover crops that fix soil nitrogen, or letting the land rest (fallow) for a few seasons.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni wooo yibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Legume ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni saa nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe Aloo ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe (egbee shi) bei fioo komɛi.

english: Why do some farmers clear fresh forest areas to start new farms instead of keeping old ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ koo mli shikpɔji heei koni amɛkɛje ŋmɔji heei shishi moŋ fe ni amɛaahi ŋmɔji momoi amli lɛ?

english: Fresh forest soil is naturally rich in decaying organic matter and nutrients, giving high crop yields initially without needing expensive fertilizers right away.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ hee lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa shishijee mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my old cocoa trees need to be cut down and replanted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni afo mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: If cocoa trees are over 25 to 30 years old, have thin canopies, show frequent disease signs, and yield very few pods for 3 or more years, it is time to cut them down and replant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, hela he okadii baa shii abɔ. ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ afii 3 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Be eshɛ ni esa akɛ afo lɛ ni adu ehee.

english: Will putting fertilizer on my farm automatically guarantee a big harvest?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmaa babaoo aba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer helps, but it only works well if the soil is properly managed, weeds are cleared, trees get sufficient rainfall, and diseases or insects are kept under control.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua, shi amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli, ni tsei lɛ ná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. kɛ helai loo kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ

english: Why should I start my coconut seeds in a nursery instead of planting them straight on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmei dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni makwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Raising seednuts in a nursery allows you to protect fragile sprouts from harsh sunlight, pests, and drought while ensuring you only select the strongest, healthiest seedlings to take to your main field.
ga: Odumɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ hɔmɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni ohala dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ni okɛdu yɛ oŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli.

english: How long does a healthy coconut nut usually take to sprout after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Under warm, moist conditions, a healthy coconut seednut typically takes between 1 to 3 months to show its first green sprout above the ground.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmei dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 1 kɛyashi 3 dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers talk about 'one-stage' nursery planting?
ga: Beni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ wieɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei lɛ ahe lɛ. Mɛni ji ‘gbɛ kome’ lɛ shishi?

english: One-stage' planting means growing sprouted seedlings in a single nursery bed and moving them directly to your main farm field without transferring them into polybags or a second nursery area first.
ga: Single-step’ dumɔ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ momo lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. ni oya oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ajie amɛ kɛya poly bag loo kusum he ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What is the benefit of using a 'two-stage' nursery system for crop seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ‘nibii enyɔ’ ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei amli lɛ he?

english: A two-stage system moves young sprouts into individual polybags or secondary beds, giving roots extra space and nutrition so seedlings develop a strong root ball that reduces shock when planted in the field.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ gbɛi enyɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ polybags loo saatso mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ babaoo kɛ niyenii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa, ni no haa shoofeemɔ baa shi kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: How can I tell which crop sprouts in my nursery are good enough to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select sprouts that emerged early, have thick and sturdy stems at the base, and show vibrant green leaves. Discard any weak, stunted, or late-emerging sprouts as they produce low yield.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Eyɛ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa yɛ shishigbɛ. ni ejie baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kpo Shĩ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egbɔjɔ loo ni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ yɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant crop seedlings on land where water is sitting on top of the soil?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Standing water can suffocate and rot young seedling roots. Unless the crop naturally thrives in flooded water, you should improve drainage or plant on raised mounds of earth to keep root systems healthy.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efite. Ja tso lɛ eda yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ oha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ loo odu yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How frequently should I water my sprouted seedlings in the nursery during dry weather?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Nursery beds need generous watering at least once a day, ideally early in the morning or late in the evening, to keep the soil consistently moist so young roots do not dry out.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, nu babaoo he miihia gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatsoi lɛ shikome daa gbi. Esa akɛ okɛ nu awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be Koni shishifãi bibii akagbi

english: How do I know the right age to transplant sprouted coconut seedlings to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afii ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ aya miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting around 6 to 12 months after sprouting, when they have developed 3 to 4 fully open green leaves and a well-established root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 12 yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ, beni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni egbele kwraa kɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ emuu lɛ.

english: How should I prepare the planting holes on my farm before bringing my seedlings from the nursery?
ga: Te esa akɛ asaa bu ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ dani ajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dig wide, deep holes well ahead of time and mix the dug-out topsoil with well-rotted manure or compost to create a loose, nutrient-rich base for the seedling roots.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni atsa lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli koni efee shishitoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: What steps can I take to prevent my young seedlings from wilting and dying right after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbo ni amɛkagbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Transplant during the cooler parts of the day or when rain is expected, keep as much intact nursery soil around the roots as possible, and water the seedlings immediately after planting.
ga: Akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ. Ha sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ eko abɔle ohe. shishifãi babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ ni okɛ nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, protecting young cocoa trees while keeping the soil cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔtɔ aba oya Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa ŋmɔtɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant is under water stress. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the base restores nutrients and helps the soil hold moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu mli haomɔ shishi. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: The first rain of the season often warms the soil without providing enough deep moisture. If a dry spell follows, seeds dry out underground; it is safer to wait until rains become regular before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baanɛ dani odu.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make the maize plants grow stronger and greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea ni mikɛ mi-corn lɛ duɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil plant food. The neighboring maize feeds on this extra nitrogen, resulting in greener leaves and better growth.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baaye nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off during periods of extreme afternoon heat or sudden dry spells. Watering the base of the plants regularly and providing light shade during the hottest part of the day helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli loo be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi trukaa lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shishi lɛ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids that transmit plant viruses. Spraying neem oil solution and removing heavily infested leaves stops the pests from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ haaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn soft and watery when I dig them up during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji atsa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb excess water during heavy rain periods, which reduces the starch content in the tubers. Harvesting during drier periods yields firm, starch-rich roots that store longer and taste better.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Nikpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch baa. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why should I remove the extra young shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for soil water and nutrients. Pruning away excess suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its energy into producing a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii. Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods signal ripeness through color change—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting pods at this stage ensures the beans inside have maximum sugar content for good fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshweremɔ kɛtsɔ su tsakemɔi anɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akpaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa.

english: When is the best time for me to prepare my land and plant seed yams?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yam requires a long period to mature and is best planted toward the end of the dry season (around December to February). Mound preparation during this time allows seed yams to sprout right as the main rainy season begins.
ga: Atomɔ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. ni esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee (Aaafee December kɛyashi February) Kɛ́ asaa ŋtayaa lɛ he yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋtayaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and produce food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer, animal manure, or compost helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfee niyenii. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow better when I leave some big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young and maturing cocoa trees get stressed under strong, direct heat. Larger shade trees protect them from harsh sunlight, cool down the field, and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ haoɔ yɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or pest damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the plants during extreme heat encourages flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up growing short and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow twisted when the soil is hard, compact, or filled with rocks that block the root path. Making deep, soft soil mounds or ridges allows the tubers to expand freely into straight, heavy yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi yɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni ja ni tsii.

english: What will happen to my cassava yield if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This results in plants with thin stems and small, poor-quality tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants stay alive during dry spells while my maize wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ye wala yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ gbo ni egbo lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have deep taproots that search for water buried far underground, and their leaves naturally conserve moisture, making them much more resistant to drought than maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛkɛtaoɔ nu ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni amɛbaai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ fe ŋmãa.

english: Why do my new plantain suckers struggle to grow if I plant them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need high moisture to grow strong roots and broad leaves. Without enough water, the plant goes into survival mode and stops growing until the rainy season begins.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo babaoo koni shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ adara. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni ekpaa dalɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why does grass and weed growth make my young rice plants stay weak and short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, sunlight, and water away from your rice. Clearing weeds early gives your rice plants full access to nutrients so they can grow tall and thick.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-rice tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Koni tso lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are my pepper fruits very small and turning red long before they reach full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he lɛ?

english: Peppers ripen early when the plant is stressed by lack of water or poor soil. The plant rushes to produce seeds before dying, which results in undersized, weak fruits.
ga: Peppers shwereɔ oya kɛji tsei lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ. Tsei kɛ oyaiyeli woɔ dumɔwui dani amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts under the dirt are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and dry up. You can pull up one test plant to check if the inside of the pods shows dark markings and firm seeds.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso ko ni akɛkaa mɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli diŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni wa yɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin, delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe kwraa. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that can pull free plant food (nitrogen) out of the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil so your maize can grow taller and produce larger cobs without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni baanyɛ ajie tse niyenii (nitrogen) ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaawo ŋmeii wuji ni ŋmeii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why are there small holes in my young corn leaves with brown crumbs that look like sawdust inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: That sawdust-like material is waste left by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hiding inside the central part of the corn plant. They eat the fresh leaves from the inside out, so finding them early helps you treat the crop before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ shĩɔ amɛshwieɔ shi. Amɛyeɔ baai heei kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mra be mli ni ana Enɛ baaha onyɛ ohere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and turn yellow when thick weeds cover the soil around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni jwɛi ni mli tse ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your pepper plants. They also block airflow around the stem, trapping extra dampness that encourages root diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ pepper tso lɛ mli. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ hu naa, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni woɔ shishifã hela he hewalɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy green leaves on top but produces only tiny, thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants get too much shade, the cassava sends all its food energy upward to grow leaves instead of downward into the tubers. Trimming excess leafy growth and avoiding heavy leaf-growing fertilizers helps the plant push energy down to swell the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Cassava tsuɔ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ baai moŋ fe ni eeeshi shi kɛya ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni ta baai lɛ anɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsiɔ shi koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and produce small cobs when I put four or five seeds in one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo dumɔ bu kome pɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread out wide and gather enough food to build strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa babaoo ni amɛbuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛfee tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during hot afternoons even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mibɛ amɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: On hot afternoons, water evaporates out of tomato leaves faster than the roots can drink it up from the dirt. The plant droops to protect itself from losing more moisture, and it will naturally stand tall again when the cool evening air returns.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tomato baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Ni tsei lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot during times of heavy rain mixed with hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa futu mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit when soil moisture swings rapidly between very dry and very wet. Keeping the water level in the soil steady helps the plant carry calcium to the tips of the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni faaa lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa calcium lɛ yaa tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do many of the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ babaoo egbi ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers and tiny pods than they can feed at one time. The tree intentionally sheds some young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—to save its energy for the remaining pods to grow full and healthy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni fe nɔ ni abaanyɛ atsɔse yɛ be kome mli Tso lɛ jwɛŋ ejie eshishifãi bibii lɛ ekomɛi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilt. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily after it grows a heavy bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo beni eda ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep, wooden roots like hard trees; their roots are shallow and soft. When a heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the top becomes heavy, allowing strong winds to easily push the tree over unless it is supported with a wooden Y-shaped pole.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni wa. Eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Kɛ́ tsei akui lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa tso lɛ shi. ja tso ni tamɔ Y fiɔ esɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help your maize gain back its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly pulls the exact same nutrients out of the soil every year and allows soil pests to multiply. Switching to legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the crop's roots can take it up. If applied to dry soil, fertilizer cannot be absorbed and can burn or damage the plant's roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer nyɛŋ aŋɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite tso shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big trees left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miigbi be mli ni tsei ni eda ko kwraa eshwɛɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees creates living shade that keeps the plants cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo mast tsei ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water sits around them because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main plant to produce bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the sun, which also prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la mli. Nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai hu anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and feeding help the plant hold its flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there is enough space on my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Even if there is space, weeds grow faster than your crops and steal light, soil water, and fertilizer away from them, leaving your crops weak and reducing your harvest.
ga: Kɛji he ko yɛ po Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ amɛmli. Ehaa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on crop leaves by moths. They hide inside the center leaves to eat the softest plant tissue, so checking your farm early and using recommended controls saves the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ tsei ahe baa lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ nibii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and burn after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Using more chemical than recommended on the bottle label scorches plant leaves because concentrated chemicals damage tender plant tissues instead of safely protecting them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai babaoo tsu nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ ejaakɛ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ moŋ fe ni eeebu ehe shweshweeshwe.

english: If I add double the amount of pesticide to my spray tank, will it kill the insects on my crops faster?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ Ani ebaagbe kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya?

english: Putting extra chemical in your tank does not kill pests any faster, but it risks burning your crop leaves, poisoning the soil, and wasting expensive inputs.
ga: Tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛfataa tanki lɛ he lɛ egbeee kooloi lɛ oya. Shi oshara baanyɛ aba akɛ abaashã ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai. Toxic kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nibii ni jara wa ni akɛfeɔ nii lɛ afitemɔ

english: How do I know if the damage on my maize leaves is caused by insects or by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo helai kɛ nɔ ni kɛ mi-abɛi lɛ efite lɛ baa?

english: Insects typically leave visible chew marks, holes, or saw-dust-like waste on leaves, while diseases usually show up as spreading spots, powdery spots, or rotting tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ ŋmeii ni anaa, bu, loo ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ hela lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ fãji ni egbɛ eshwa, fãji ni tamɔ powder, loo fãji ni miifite.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear away all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate young foliage and evaporates soil water faster than their small roots can absorb it.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thin stems and small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Eyɛ tsitsi bibioo ko kɛ yitso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for limited sunlight and nutrients, spending all their energy growing tall stems instead of building large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ moŋ fe bulb agbo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, forcing the plant to move remaining nutrients up to its top growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds in my garden cause my vegetables to produce smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mi-aduawai lɛ miifee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm by stealing soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your vegetables need to produce full, healthy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni he hiaa o-aduawai lɛ koni ewo yibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during very hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to preserve moisture and survive rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛbai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why must I measure water carefully when mixing spray chemicals instead of just guessing the tank level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu nu he jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ miifutu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu tanki lɛ he kɛkɛ lɛ

english: Using the wrong water-to-chemical ratio makes the mixture either too weak to kill farm pests or too strong, which harms the health of your crops.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nu kɛ tsofa ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbe ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ loo ebaafee nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ awui.

english: Why do my garden vegetables rot quickly during the continuous rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔbɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and damp conditions create the perfect environment for fungi and bacteria to grow and spread quickly across crop stems and leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their tender leaves burn under harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them protects them and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebuɔ tsei ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from water loss. It shrinks the surface area exposed to heat, keeping moisture inside the plant during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite. Ehaa he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. They feed on the plant's sap and can spread diseases that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do I see small holes chewed all over my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Miye mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni eyi obɔ?

english: This damage is commonly caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed inside the leaf whorls, which weakens the plant and reduces crop yields if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ yeɔ baa yibii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots allows the main tree to grow stronger and produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo plantain tsei wuji.

english: Yam vines need to spread leaves in the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. Lifting vines off the wet ground also prevents diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la he koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crops when I plant on it year after year without a break?
