ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ miduɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops remove natural nutrients from the soil every season. Without adding manure, compost, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot nourish new crops properly.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe daa be mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, feemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients very quickly. Early weeding prevents them from stealing food away from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ooojie mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out their pollen, preventing fruit formation. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its unused flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa Kɛji akɛ pollination ni yeɔ omanye bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ashwie.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, typically 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the specific variety used.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorched under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade from temporary plants like plantains or shade trees, the intense sun burns their tender leaves and dries out moisture, slowing down their growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei amli lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to produce thousands of flowers but drop most of them. The tree drops extra flowers if it lacks water, proper nutrients, or enough tiny insects like midges to pollinate them.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tso baafɔ̃ akpei abɔ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo baagbee shi. Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji nu bɛ ehe. Niyenii ni sa Aloo kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ yɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning low branches to let in air, and removing infected pods quickly helps keep the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. weeding Fɔlɔmɔ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Will cutting off branches from my cocoa tree hurt my final harvest?
ga: Ani niji ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: No, proper pruning actually improves your harvest. Removing weak or overgrown branches allows sunlight and air into the canopy, reducing disease risk and letting the tree focus its energy on producing big, healthy pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni oha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close together so I can fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ bɔni afee ni manyɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough resources and reduces the spread of diseases between trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are small brown patches and holes appearing on the young shoots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ buji yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is usually caused by mirid insects (capsids) that suck sap from young branches and pods. Spraying recommended treatments at the right time of year prevents them from weakening the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii babaoo (capsids) ni nuɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ tsei akui amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil has enough strength to support healthy cocoa growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shweremɔ?

english: Healthy soil for cocoa is rich in organic matter, dark in color, and holds moisture without staying waterlogged. If your trees grow slowly or have pale green leaves despite good rains, the soil needs compost or specific fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ, eyɛ su diŋŋ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo loo eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ cocoa dumɔwui heei yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is better to avoid cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots take up a lot of soil nutrients and water, competing directly with the cocoa trees. Plantain is a better companion crop for temporary shade.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ekɛ kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ji nanemɛi tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods grow much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries dissolved soil nutrients up into the tree, allowing pods to expand quickly. However, high humidity during the rainy season means you must monitor pods closely for fungal diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ yaa tsei lɛ aŋɔɔ. Enɛ haa pods lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya. Shi, bɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii ahe helai.

english: A pod is ready when its skin changes color completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures the beans inside have developed the sugars needed for good fermentation.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ hewolo lɛ tsake su kwraa—bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ mli Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ pɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding fertilizer like NPK or urea supplies this nitrogen to bring back healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen nɛɛ aba koni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves and grass around my crop roots keep the soil wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry organic matter on the soil, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from heating the earth. This stops ground moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps the roots cool during warm dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ. Enɛ haaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpea on my land help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpea is a legume plant that traps nitrogen from the air and stores it in small bumps on its roots. When the season ends, those roots break down in the ground and leave natural food in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ be lɛ ba naagbee. Nakai shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there small chewed holes and powdery dirt inside the top leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji ni tamɔ powda lɛ yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ aŋwɛi baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the tender growing center of corn plants. Catching them early and applying recommended pest control methods keeps them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni mli tse mli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and dry up when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Constant rain creates damp conditions where fungal diseases like leaf blight thrive. Tying tomato plants to wooden stakes keeps leaves off the wet ground, improving airflow and stopping fungal spores from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akagbee shi yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact spot where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he ni mibua ŋmeii anaa yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil diseases and pests. Rotating to a different crop family, like corn or beans, starves out the old pests left in the soil.
ga: Pepper kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii jɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛgbalaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ni atsakeɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii aweku kroko nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai momo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when exposed to harsh direct sunlight, dry conditions, or nutrient stress. Maintaining shade trees over cocoa creates a cooler environment that protects delicate flowers so they can mature into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall stems but produce very thin tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi eshishifãi lɛ yɛ bibioo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava planted too close together competes for sunlight, causing the plants to put all their energy into growing tall stems rather than expanding underground roots. Proper spacing leaves room for thick tubers to grow.
ga: Cassava ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha gbɛ aha ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: When too many shoots grow around one stem, they compete for water and soil food with the main tree. Pruning back excess shoots to keep only 2 or 3 ensures the main plant gets enough strength to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal sunlight, ground water, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early leaves all the water and nutrients available for your crops to produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ aná yibiiwoo ni fa.

english: What happens to my maize crops if there is too much heavy rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Excessive rain floods the soil and suffocates the roots by cutting off oxygen. This makes maize leaves turn yellow, stunts their growth, and can cause the roots to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall physically knocks blossoms off tomato plants and washes away pollen, which prevents the flowers from successfully forming fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over when we have heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain softens the soil around the roots, making the ground loose. Because plantains have shallow roots, strong storm winds can easily blow the heavy trees over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ Ahum ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ atswa tsei wuji ashwie shi oya.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rains come unpredictably?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje tsei afeemɔ shishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Rather than planting after the very first rainfall, wait until the soil stays consistently moist for several consecutive days so that seeds can germinate without drying out if the rain pauses.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during long periods of continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates cold, highly humid conditions that allow the Black Pod fungus to spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, blackpod fungus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain creates warm, soggy soil conditions that encourage soil bacteria and fungi to attack pepper roots, causing sudden plant wilt.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ woɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii shishifãi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbi trukaa.

english: Why do cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the soil stays waterlogged for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked for too long, cassava roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly, forcing the plant to drop its leaves to conserve energy.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil on my farm, and how does that hurt my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Topsoil holds most of the essential nutrients crops need to feed on. When heavy rain washes it away, crops are left in poor soil and produce very low yields.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ashiɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why do my yam mounds break down and wash away during big downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikɛto lɛ shwie shi ni eho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Loose soil in mounds easily dissolves under heavy rain if there are no drainage pathways or cover plants to slow down the flow of surface water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa. Kɛji akɛ nu homɔ loo tso ko bɛ ni baaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akaho oya lɛ,.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm right after a rainstorm than my crops do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb sudden rainwater and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to rapidly multiply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu ni baa trukaa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need shade from temporary crops like plantains to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil until their roots grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot produce the green color it needs to capture sunlight and grow big stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni amɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛdara lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: What is making small holes in my corn leaves, and why is the crop growing so slowly?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmã baa lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ tsei daa blɛoo nɛkɛ?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are often caused by pests like the fall armyworm eating the plant's leaves. When the leaves are damaged, the plant loses its ability to feed itself properly, which slows down its overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye tso lɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest if the roots are hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You can also carefully dig around one stem to check if the roots have grown thick and tuberous.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tuberous.

english: Why do I need to push long wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso kakadaŋŋ ko? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need light to make food for their underground tubers. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground with tall stakes exposes them to more sunlight and protects them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa la ni tsoɔ waa koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tsu nii kɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ebaatsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell that can dry out the soil completely. If you plant too early, the heat will scorch the newly sprouted seeds before the main, continuous rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ kwraa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dɔlɛ lɛ shãa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why is it good to cover the bare dirt around my crops with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents heavy rain from washing away the good topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Mulch haa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers say that planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decay, they leave that free fertilizer behind for crops like maize planted in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛshiɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets too stressed, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy so it can survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ babaoo shishi. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko hao lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: When a plantain tree produces too many young shoots, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough strength to produce a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ja ekome loo enyɔ pɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ plantains babaoo aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and bushy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the green color and helps the crop grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored food remains in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct, strong sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots grow deep enough to handle the heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ dɔlɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch light better and avoids fungal leaf diseases, which allows the yam root to grow much bigger underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ fungal leaf helai ahe. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Too many small shoots steal water and plant food from the main mother stem. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantains agboi babaoo ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the daytime heat is too extreme or when the plant does not get steady water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from harsh midday heat helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains last for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When water sits on top of the soil for too long without draining, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing underground rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away safely.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. haa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the sap from the back of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stops fruit growth from slowing down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch delicate young sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays wet enough for the seeds to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do crop diseases get worse if I plant the exact same crop in the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai lɛ mli woɔ wu kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same field year after year allows pests and soil diseases that target that specific crop to build up in large numbers. Changing to a different type of crop breaks their life cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yeɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tso kroko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha wala shihilɛ lɛ akpa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to plant my crop seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu tsei dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: The late afternoon or early evening, around 3 PM to 4 PM, is the ideal time to plant. The cooler evening temperatures allow the young plants to settle into the soil overnight without being stressed by harsh sunlight.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ, aaafee ŋmɛji 3:00 PM kɛyashi 4:00 PM ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei adumɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die when I plant them during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Scorching afternoon sun creates intense heat that rapidly dries out the soil and young roots before they can establish themselves. Planting under heavy sun causes severe dehydration and heat shock to the seedlings.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani amɛboteɔ shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be shishi lɛ baaha nu ni mli wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he shoofeemɔ aba dumɔwui lɛ anɔ.

english: How does hot and scorching weather affect newly planted crops on my farm?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Intense sun forces young crops to lose water through their leaves faster than their weak, newly planted roots can absorb it from the soil, causing wilting, stunted growth, or plant death.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ tsei bibii anɔ koni amɛjie nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Shishifãi ni adu ehee lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shwiemɔ Stunted dalɛ loo tso gbele

english: If I plant my crops late in the evening, how does it help them survive better?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei gbɛkɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua tsei ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting in the evening gives seedlings a cool night to absorb soil moisture and begin root growth without direct sun stress, making them strong enough to withstand the heat of the next day.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo gbɛkɛ koni amɛnu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ. Ni ebɔi shishifãi akwɛ̃mɔ ni hulu la kpɛɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔ enɔ jetsɛremɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Is it safe for me to water and plant my crops when the afternoon sun is beating down heavily?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mawo nu ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: It is not recommended because the hot sun causes rapid evaporation of soil water and can heat the surface soil, damaging fragile young roots. It is safer to wait until the sun lowers in the evening.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli adɔ. Efiteɔ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi hulu lɛ baanyɔ shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crops droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop leaves droop during peak afternoon heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant conserve water.
ga: Tse baai lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he

english: Why do I need to clear and till my land two or three times before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu nii shii enyɔ loo etɛ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Preparing land multiple times breaks up tough soil clumps, destroys deep-rooted weeds, and creates a soft soil texture that allows young plant roots to spread and catch moisture easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ yɛ gbɛ̀i babaoo nɔ bei pii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akumɔ Efiteɔ jwɛi ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ blɛoo ni haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell that my soil is finally ready and alright for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo yɛ naagbee ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Soil is ready when it is fine, loose, free of major weed roots, and sufficiently moist without being overly flooded or baked hard by the sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji ehi jogbaŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi shishifãi ni he hiaa bɛ mli. ni eyɛ fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa Ni hulu la ehiɛɛɛ nɔ loo hulu lɛ shãaa lɛ tsɔ.

english: How many times should I repeat my land preparation activities before putting seeds in the ground?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ he saamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Usually working the land two to three times is sufficient to clear unwanted vegetation, loosen the soil, and ensure proper field conditions for good crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛjieɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ. ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ni sa aha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why should I consult an agricultural officer about the specific planting time for my crop variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko agba be pɔtɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu mitso srɔtoi lɛ he sane lɛ?

english: Different crops and soil conditions require specific timing and heat management practices, so getting tailored guidance ensures you do not waste seeds or plant during unfavorable weather.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi biɔ be pɔtɛɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo he nifeemɔi. No hewɔ lɛ ŋaawoo ni sa ni ooona lɛ baaye abua bo ni okwɛ koni okashi dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight when they are small. They require shade plants like plantain or shade trees to cover them and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Is it fine for me to plant cassava alongside my cocoa trees on the same plot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cassava roots grow aggressively and suck away food and water from young cocoa plants. It is better to plant plantain or cocoyam instead, as they protect cocoa without competing heavily for nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛmuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Esa akɛ adu plantains loo cocoa moŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ejuuu niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɛɛ mli.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting cocoa before the tree starts producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani odu kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit in about two to three years, whereas older traditional varieties can take four to five years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal condition called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and humid weather. Clearing weeds and trimming overgrown branches lets sunlight and air dry out the pods to keep them healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects feeding on my fresh cocoa shoots and curling the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi-kookoo ŋmɔji heei lɛ ni amɛmiiha baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: These insects are common sap-sucking pests like capsids. They attack young shoots and weaken the tree, but they can be controlled using recommended sprays or neem-based treatments.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji kooloi ni fɔɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ tamɔ capsids. Amɛtutuaa ŋmeii bibii ni amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Shi abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ŋaa loo neem tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ akudɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is running out of nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa miduɔ nii lɛ bɛ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, leaves often turn pale yellow, and plant stems remain thin and weak. Adding compost or approved fertilizers restores the nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support as pods. Dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination can cause the tree to shed extra flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ ŋmeii amli. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo pollination ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ.

english: Will cutting or pruning branches off my cocoa tree reduce my yield?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ loo mifoɔ lɛ baaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually helps your tree produce more fruit. Removing extra branches allows the tree to send its energy directly to growing pods while reducing disease risk through better airflow.
ga: Tso lɛ ni oookpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa otso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akuɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I protect my crops from drying out during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the roots with dry leaves and organic mulch acts like a blanket, keeping soil moisture from evaporating quickly in dry weather.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi kɛ organic mulch woɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Enɛ haaa sũ mli nu lɛ atsɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Ripe cocoa pods turn bright yellow or orange depending on the variety. Harvesting green pods reduces quality, while leaving pods on the tree too long makes the beans sprout inside.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo akutu, ni enɛ damɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee fɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why does my new cocoa farm take a few years before I can harvest any pods from the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ he afii fioo komɛi dani minyɛ mikpa tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong root system, trunk, and branch network before they can support heavy fruit. Like a young child growing up, the tree must mature fully before it has the strength to produce cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛniji ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ. Taakɛ gbekɛbii bibii ji lɛ, esa akɛ tsei adara jogbaŋŋ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii. ni miida lɛ

english: How can cassava roots stay under the ground for many months without rotting like other harvested food?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei shishifãi ahi shikpɔŋ shishi nyɔji babaoo ni amɛgbooo tamɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are the plant's natural storage organs that stay alive as long as they remain attached to the main stem in dry, well-drained soil. This allows the plant to preserve its energy until you are ready to harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni ebaahi shi be fɛɛ be ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the food they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dried leaves and manure on my farm soil even if weeds are growing easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya.

english: Weeds can survive in poor soil, but food crops need rich soil to produce good yields. Spreading manure and dried leaves feeds beneficial soil bugs and returns vital nutrients into the earth so your crops grow bigger.
ga: Jwɛi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Shi niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ kpakpa koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni egbi ni ooogbɛ ashwã lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aye nii ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same farm plot without them spoiling each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two crops from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the delicate cocoa seedlings from direct sun while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster on my land than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to local weather and soil conditions over a long time, allowing them to absorb water and soil food faster than domesticated crop plants. Clearing them regularly ensures your crops get enough food to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsɔ amɛhe amɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔji lɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are tiny white insects gathering under my cassava leaves and causing them to curl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Those insects are whiteflies, and they curl the leaves by sucking out the sap and nutrients the plant needs to feed itself. Clearing surrounding weeds and applying organic treatments helps keep them away from your farm.
ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ. Ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛye ehe lɛ ni amɛmuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves when it is very hot to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from escaping too fast. They usually stand straight again in the cooler evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Amɛfɔɔ shidaamɔ ni ja ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly when packed in bags for transport to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo kotokui amli kɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked tomatoes produce heat and moisture as they breathe. Packing them tightly in closed bags traps heat and causes them to bruise and rot quickly, whereas packed crates with air holes keep them cool and fresh longer.
ga: Tomatoi ni ajie ehee Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa be mli ni emuɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo kotoku ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ. ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ bu yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛfee ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay green. The maize plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen from the older bottom leaves up to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up tightly into curls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The curling is the plant's physical reaction to insect damage and fluid loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Curling ji bɔ ni tso ko gbɔmɔtso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa kɛji kooloi fite lɛ ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my irrigated crop is getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: If a plant gets too much water, its leaves will turn pale yellow and start to droop or look limp even while the soil is wet. Excess water drowns the roots by blocking air, which prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaabɔi shwiemɔ loo amɛbaafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my maize plant produce powdery dust from the top while thread-like silks grow lower down on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ jieɔ sũ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni tamɔ kpãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is how maize reproduces. The top part (the tassel) produces male pollen dust, which drops down onto the sticky female silks below. Each silk thread connects to a single grain on the maize cob, so proper pollination forms a full cob.
ga: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni ŋmãa fɔɔ bii. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ (tassel) lɛ jieɔ pollen sũ, ni shwieɔ yoo siliki ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ŋmei kome ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ tsaa. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ pollination ni sa hewɔ lɛ, cob lɛ mli eyi kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the pods must grow underground. After pollination, the stems bend downward and push into the soil—a process called pegging—so the seed pod can safely develop underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fixation. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on as many leaves as possible to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to more sun and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la babaoo baa, ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ helai ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from sunburn and keep moisture in the soil until they are mature enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants, causing pollen to dry up so flowers cannot be fertilized. When pollination fails due to high temperatures, the plant sheds the flower to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. Anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my plantain crop slow down its growth and delay fruiting during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ daaa ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants require large amounts of water to build their heavy trunks and broad leaves. When water is scarce, the plant enters a survival state and pauses new growth until rainfall or irrigation resumes.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛfee tsei ni tsii kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Kɛ nu faaa Tso lɛ boteɔ wala shihilɛ mli ni ekpaa dalɛ hee kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ jeɔ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot under the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need well-drained soil so the roots can breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, oxygen is cut off, allowing rot-causing fungi in the mud to attack and decay the roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ebaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and stop growing after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash essential soil nutrients like nitrogen deeper into the ground where roots cannot reach them. Applying a top-dressing fertilizer helps restore the nutrients your maize needs to stay green and grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmãa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni ehiɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots tiny and thin even though the leaves above ground look very leafy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni baai yɔɔ mli waa ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the cassava plant to grow foliage instead of expanding its tuber roots. A balanced soil nutrient mix ensures the plant puts its energy into growing large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai yɛ tuber shishifãi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ja lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ bulb agboi ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy stems carrying heavy fruit bunches. Supporting them with strong wooden poles gives them stability so wind and rain won't knock them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni woɔ yibii ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ haaa ogbee shi.

english: Can I store my agricultural chemicals and sprays in the same room where I store harvested crops or live with my family?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ ato tsu kome mli ni mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ toɔ mli loo mikɛ miweku lɛ ahi shi?

english: No, agricultural chemicals release toxic vapors that can poison humans and contaminate food products. Chemicals must always be kept in a separate, secure, and well-ventilated space dedicated only to farm supplies.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ jieɔ lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ adesai anɔ, ni efiteɔ niyenii ni afee lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ srɔto, ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii pɛ.

english: Why does spraying weedicide on my farm during hot midday heat damage my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: High heat makes chemical sprays evaporate rapidly and drift onto crop leaves, causing severe burning. Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon ensures the chemicals work properly without harming your crops.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni efoɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ, ni ekɛ shãa ni naa wa baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is missing nutrients before I start planting my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adumɔ?

english: If your previous crops had pale leaves, slow growth, or low yield, your soil is likely depleted of nutrients. Adding compost or applying recommended fertilizers before planting restores the soil's strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these pests early protects your crop from stunt disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ahe.

english: Why does witchweed keep destroying my maize even after I clear all the weeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witchweed yaa nɔ efiteɔ mi-abele lɛ beni mikɛ minine jie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Witchweed attaches its roots directly to the maize plant underground and steals its nutrients before emerging above ground. Hand-weeding after it appears is often too late, so rotating crops or using resistant seed varieties is necessary.
ga: Witchweed lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni akɛ niji gbalaa beni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures are too high or when plants experience water stress from irregular rainfall. Providing consistent watering and light shade during hot spells helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni efɔɔɔ baa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no bigger leafy trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni baai yɔɔ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct heat. Taller shade crops like plantains or tree canopies act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air humid and protecting young plants until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi, ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying dark green during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks essential food, especially nitrogen. When the plant cannot draw enough nutrients from the earth, it steals food from its lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small root nodules. When these roots decompose, they naturally fertilize the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fite Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and form cracks when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Clay-rich soil expands when wet and shrinks as water evaporates under heat. Adding organic matter like compost or dried crop leaves helps hold moisture and keeps the soil soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛji edɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ be mli ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ahe baai ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with very tiny tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When cassava sticks are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plant spends all its energy fighting upward for light instead of storing energy in its roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my farm crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive root systems designed to steal water and food faster than domesticated farm crops. They react quickly to rain before your crops can absorb the moisture.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Amɛtsuɔ he nii oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they are stressed by dry spells, poor nutrients, or a lack of beneficial midges (tiny insects) that pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ha amɛhao. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ (koolooi bibii) ni haa fɔfɔii feɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop mostly when the plant starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ babaoo kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and bright petals that attract pests like thrips and pod borers, which feed on the delicate reproductive parts of the crop.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa mɔ fɔɔ lɛ

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to survive heat. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground during prolonged heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, preventing roots from breathing. Waterlogged soil creates ideal conditions for soil fungi to attack and rot the buried tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii ni afu lɛ.

english: Why do climbing weeds grow so quickly around my crop stems, and how do they harm my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɔɔ lɛ miida oya yɛ mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni te amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Climbing weeds wrap around your crop plants to reach sunlight, but in doing so, they choke the main stem, block light from reaching crop leaves, and steal essential nutrients from the soil, leading to poor crop yields.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɔɔ lɛ bɔleɔ otsei lɛ ahe koni amɛná hulu la. Shi nakai feemɔ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ atsĩ la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe. ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii

english: Why is it important to stake my yam and tomato plants instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato kɛ tomato tsei lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛshwie shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Staking keeps the plant's branches and leaves off the ground, controlling their direction of growth, improving airflow, and preventing ground pests and moisture from damaging developing fruit.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ niji kɛ baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kudɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaraa lɛ nɔ Eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni amɛkafite aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do young pods on my cocoa trees turn black and wither before they can fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods are soft and vulnerable, making them prime targets for fungal diseases like black pod and insect attacks. Without early protection and proper tree shade, these young pods die off early.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ he titri ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods kɛ kooloi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsei haaa amɛ hulutsoo lɛ, Nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ baagboi oya.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops much more aggressively once the plants start flowering and fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai shishi lɛ?

english: Flowers and young fruits are rich in sugars and nutrients that pests need. Pests target this reproductive stage because the plant tissues are soft and high in energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar kɛ niyenii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai taoɔ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kwɛɔ fɔmɔ be nɛɛ nɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants shed their flowers when stressed by pest damage, severe heat, or water shortages as a natural defense mechanism to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ hewalɛ he ni ahi wala mli.

english: Why do my crops sometimes grow tall with many green leaves but yield very small produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mitsei lɛ daa ni amɛyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When a plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or insufficient direct sunlight, it puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of directing nutrients to fruit or tuber development.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo hulu la ni fa tɛ̃ɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo aduawai loo ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Planting seeds too close creates intense competition underground for root space, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha shishifãi ahe he, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Why should I keep written records of my planting dates and harvests instead of just relying on my memory?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋma gbii ni miduɔ nii kɛ gbii ni mikpaa nii lɛ he saji awo wolo nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ mikaimɔi pɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Keeping simple records helps you know which crops bring the best income, track fertilizer schedules, and time your planting correctly with shifting weather patterns.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni haa shika baa. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ be ni akɛduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ naa.

english: How does letting cattle graze near my crop field damage the soil and my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsinai ni mikɛhaa amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ fiteɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Cattle can eat growing crop shoots and their heavy hooves pack the soil down tightly, making it hard for crop roots to absorb water and oxygen.
ga: Tsinai baanyɛ aye tsei ashishifãi ni miida. ni amɛnaji ni tsii lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ miimɔ shi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛ baa nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground right before harvest time during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water staying in waterlogged soil starves the underground cassava roots of oxygen, allowing soil fungi to multiply and cause root rot before you can harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why are my new cocoa seedlings struggling to grow on land where cocoa was planted years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui heei lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu kookoo yɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Replanting on old cocoa land is different from planting in fresh forest land. Over time, old trees draw out essential nutrients from the soil, and old pests or diseases might remain. The soil needs extra organic manure, fertilizer, and soil preparation to feed a new generation of cocoa.
ga: Esoro kookoo shikpɔŋ momo nɔ dumɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ dumɔ he. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei ni edara lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ekolɛ kooloi bibii loo helai momo yɛ jɛmɛ lolo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kroko ni akɛfataa he koni akɛdu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo.

english: Is planting crops on an old cleared farm different from clearing a fresh forest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ momo ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ koo hee ni ajieɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, virgin forest soil has rich topsoil full of organic nutrients from leaves and natural shade from big trees. Old farmland has lost much of its natural fertility and shade over time, so crops planted there require extra care, shade planting, and soil nutrients to thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ baai amli kɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli. Gbɛjegbɛi momoi lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Dumɔ kɛha hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha dalɛ

english: Why does land that produced large harvests many years ago no longer give me good yields today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni woɔ yibii waa afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired when crops continuously absorb nutrients year after year without those nutrients being replaced. Without adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizers, the soil nutrients get depleted and crop growth slows down.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛ́ tsei lɛ tee nɔ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii afi fɛɛ afi ni amɛkɛ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ etsakeee. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataaa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if a piece of land that previously had cocoa is still good for planting again?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ aduɔ kookoo yɛ nɔ lɛ hi lolo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo ehiii?

english: You can inspect the soil's color, depth, and ability to hold moisture, but old cocoa land almost always needs soil restoration. Preparing the land with organic matter or letting it rest (fallowing) helps bring back the nutrients needed for fresh plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ su yɔɔ ha, bɔ ni emli kwɔ ha, kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ehaa. Shi nɔ ni miihe ashɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni asaa kookoo ŋmɔji momoi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baasaa loo ahaa ejɔɔ ehe (tilling) lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei heei aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and shrink back even though I was told the variety is strong and heat-resistant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ minu akɛ nɛkɛ tso nɛɛ wa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa moŋ?

english: Even drought-tolerant crop varieties need adequate water and root space when they are young. If the soil is too hard, degraded, or dry during early growth, the plant will 'pull back' or stunt its growth to protect itself from dying.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ po he miihia nu kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ amɛji gbekɛbii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, efite loo egbi tsɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, tso lɛ ‘baatsi ehe kɛba sɛɛ’ loo ebaatsi edalɛ naa koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a crop variety can 'endure' harsh conditions?
ga: Kɛ́ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ tso henɔ ko baanyɛ ‘aŋmɛ’ shihilɛi gbohii ahiɛ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: It means the crop has traits that help it survive periods of dry weather or poor soil better than traditional varieties. However, 'enduring' does not mean it needs no care—it still requires proper planting, shade, and nutrients to produce a good harvest.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ sui ni haa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ‘ehiɔ shi daa’ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni adu nii jogbaŋŋ, aná hulutsoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai lolo koni aná yibii kpakpai.

english: What causes my crops to grow well at first and then suddenly stop growing or wither?
ga: Mɛni ha mitsei lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpa shweremɔ loo amɛgboi trukaa lɛ?

english: This often happens when young roots exhaust the top layer of nutrients or hit a hard, damaged subsoil layer. It can also be caused by root pests or sudden water shortages that force the plant to stop expanding.
