ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsu nii loo amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni amɛfite. Ebaanyɛ ejɛ shishifã mli kooloi loo nu ni faaa trukaa ni haa tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ naa lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: How can I tell if my crop is failing because of poor soil rather than a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ moŋ fe hela?

english: Poor soil usually causes widespread, slow, and uniform problems across the field, such as stunted growth or pale leaves. Diseases usually start on specific plants with distinct spots, rots, or sudden wilting before spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kɛ naagbai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, ni yaa nɔ daa baa shia lɛ mli fɛɛ, tamɔ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo baai ni mli tseee. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, ni egboɔ, loo egboɔ trukaa dani egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open sunlit field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. In natural forest conditions, canopy trees filter the sun. In open fields, you must plant temporary shade crops like plantains to protect the young seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. yɛ adebɔɔ mli koo mli shihilɛi amli Canopy tsei tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, ehe miihia ni odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: What special steps should I take before removing old cocoa trees to start a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi esa akɛ mafee dani mikɛ mi-kookoo tsei momo lɛ aya he kroko koni miyaje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Before replanting on old cocoa ground, you should clear out old diseased roots, break up hard soil, apply organic compost to replenish lost nutrients, and establish shade plants before putting your new seedlings into the ground.
ga: Dani obaadu ekoŋŋ yɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ momo nɔ Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ogbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. ni afee tsei ni haa hulutsoo dani akɛ dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why does the shade over my crops change position from the morning to the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsakeɔ egbɛhe kɛjɛɔ leebi kɛyashiɔ shwane lɛ?

english: The sun moves across the sky throughout the day. In the morning, shadows are long and fall in one direction, but as the sun reaches its peak at noon and moves into the afternoon, the shadows shift direction and size, changing how much shade your crops receive.
ga: Hulu lɛ nyiɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Leebi lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ shɛ eshishijee he yɛ shwane mli ni efã kɛtee shwane mli lɛ, Susumɔ lɛ baatsake gbɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni tsei lɛ náa lɛ falɛ

english: Why is shade more important for my young crops in the afternoon than in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo he hiaa mi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shwane mli fe leebi lɛ?

english: Morning sunlight is cool and mild, which helps crops start making food gently. In the afternoon, the sun carries intense heat that can scorch delicate leaves and dry out soil moisture rapidly, making shade crucial during those late hours.
ga: Leebi hulu la lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛhooɔ blɛoo. Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, hulu lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa hulutsoo he hiaa waa yɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nɛɛ amli.

english: Does the direction I plant my crop rows affect how much shade they give each other during the day?
ga: Ani gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni mikɛduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná bɔ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, planting rows from East to West allows sunlight to hit crops evenly throughout the day, whereas planting North to South causes the plants to cast shade on adjacent rows during the morning and afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli kɛjɛɔ bokagbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ kooyigbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ leebi kɛ shwane mli.

english: Why do my crops seem to wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest afternoon hours, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Wilting is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf surface area to save water until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu nu he kɛyashi hulu lɛ baaha edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin when they are planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni efeɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much shade, they stretch upward searching for direct sunlight. This causes the plant to waste energy growing a tall, weak stem instead of developing big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ zugba agbo ko nɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants change direction at different times of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ tsakeɔ gbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves follow the sun's path across the sky to catch maximum light when it is cool, and they may tilt or fold during intense afternoon sun to prevent overheating and water loss.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ nyiɛɔ hulu lɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni amɛná la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso. ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli loo abɔle ehe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi hulutsoo ni fe nine kɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ naa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and drop off while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As maize grows tall, the upper leaves block sunlight from reaching the lower leaves. Because the shaded bottom leaves can no longer catch light to make food, the plant discards them to focus energy on the sunny top leaves.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ da lɛ ŋwɛi baa lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ baa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii dɔŋŋ. Kɛkɛ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ ama baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my large shade trees are blocking too much light from my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei wuji miitsi la babaoo ni jɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: If your cocoa trees look slender with very few pods, or if the soil beneath them stays dark, wet, and mossy even without rain, the shade trees are blocking too much sunlight and need branch trimming.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli ewo duŋ lolo, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ miitsi hulu la babaoo naa, ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do I need to cover my nursery bed with palm fronds, and when should I reduce the shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tsei aha gbekɛbii ashihilɛhe lɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ okɛ hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi?

english: Seedlings are very delicate and burn under full daylight. Palm fronds provide temporary shade to protect them, and you gradually reduce the fronds as seedlings mature so they get used to full sunlight before transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ waaa waa ni ashãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Palm baai haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa koni ebu amɛhe, ni obaanyɛ okɛ baai lɛ aba shi fiofio be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ koni amɛtsɔse amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ dani okɛwo he kroko.

english: Will planting food crops under dense shade trees reduce the amount of yield I harvest?
ga: Ani niyenii ni miduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha nibii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, most food crops like maize and pepper need full sunlight to produce heavy yields. If shade is too thick throughout the day, the crops cannot create enough food power to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Ehe miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji aba.

english: When should I expect my crops to start showing flowers after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi kpojiemɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Depending on the crop, many fast-growing plants will begin to produce their first flowers around four weeks after planting, which marks the start of the reproductive stage.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni daa oya lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ aaafee otsii ejwɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Abuɔ enɛ akɛ fɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop is moving from just growing leaves to making food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejɛ baai ni mikwɛɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ kɛtee niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You will notice small flower buds beginning to form on the branches or stems, showing that the plant is shifting its energy from growing leaves to producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Obaana ŋmeii bibii. Ejeɔ shishi efeɔ yɛ tsei niji loo tsei akutsei anɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei miitsake hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli kɛmiiya fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: Why are flowers so important for getting a good harvest from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii he hiaa koni maná yibiiwoo kpakpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Flowers are the starting point for fruit development; without healthy flowers, the plant cannot form the seeds or fruits that you harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji he ni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ. Kɛji fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai ni okpaa lɛ.

english: What is pollination, and why do people say my farm crops need it?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ mi okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia lɛ?

english: Pollination is the transfer of pollen within a flower or between flowers, which fertilizes the plant so that the flower can successfully transform into a fruit.
ga: Pollination ji pollen ni akɛyaa fɔfɔi amli loo yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ atsake amɛhe amɛwo yibii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: How does pollination actually happen on my farm if I don't do anything?
ga: Te pollination baafee tɛŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mifeee nɔ ko?

english: Nature usually handles pollination through beneficial insects like bees carrying pollen as they collect nectar, or through the wind blowing pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ kudɔɔ pollination kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ wuobii, ni buaa pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli ni amɛbua nectar naa lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɛ pollen jɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my plants sometimes fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off without producing fruit if pollination did not happen, or if the plant is suffering from stress like extreme heat, poor soil, or lack of water.
ga: Kɛ́ pollination bɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is there any situation where I need to help pollinate my plant flowers myself?
ga: Ani shihilɛi komɛi yɛ ni ehe baahia ni mi diɛŋtsɛ maye mabua ni mikɛ fɔfɔii lɛ awo mli?

english: Yes, if there are few insects around or if you want a higher yield, you can manually transfer pollen between flowers using a soft brush or your fingers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ebɔle he. Fioo ko pɛ loo kɛji oosumɔ yibii babaoo Obaanyɛ okɛ onine atsɔ brɔsh ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo oniji anɔ okɛ pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ.

english: How long after flowering starts should I expect to see tiny fruits forming?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana aduawai bibii ni baaje kpo yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Once pollination is complete, small fruits usually start to appear gradually at the base of the flower within a few days to a couple of weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ egbe naa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo fiofio yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What does a flower look like when it has successfully been pollinated?
ga: Te fɔfɔi lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛye omanye yɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo mli lɛ?

english: The petals will usually dry up and drop off, leaving behind a small swollen green bump at the stem base that slowly swells into a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko pɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni fiofio lɛ ebaatsɔ aduawai

english: How long does it typically take for fruits to develop fully once they start showing?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa kɛji amɛje shishi amɛjie amɛhe kpo?

english: After the small fruits first appear, they grow gradually over a period of about 12 weeks until they reach full size and maturity for harvest.
ga: Yɛ yibii bibii lɛ asɛɛ Kɛ́ amɛje kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, amɛdaraa fiofio yɛ aaafee otsii 12 mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛshwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and dry up after I spray chemical medicine on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mixing agrochemicals stronger than recommended or spraying during hot afternoon sun scorches crop leaves. Always measure the exact water-to-chemical ratio and spray during cooler early morning or evening hours.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai ni mli wa fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutu mli loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashã. Susumɔ bɔ ni nu kɛ tsofai yɔɔ ha lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ be fɛɛ be. Ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Can I mix pest medicine and weed killer together in the same sprayer tank to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ jwɛi afutu yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing different chemicals without expert guidance can cause chemical reactions that destroy their power or create toxic liquids that burn your crops. Unless the product instructions specifically state they are compatible, spray them separately.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Kɛji ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ lɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni fiteɔ tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ aba loo ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ ashã onibii lɛ aba. Ja nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ kɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee, no lɛ ha amɛ srɔtoi.

english: Does it matter if I use muddy stream water to mix my chemical sprays?
ga: Ani ehe ehiaaa ni mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ efutu mli?

english: Yes, dirt and mud in water bind to active chemical ingredients, reducing their strength and clogging your spraying equipment. Always mix farm chemicals with clean water for effective results.
ga: Hɛɛ, muji kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kpãa gbee. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli hewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa onibii ni okɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, futumɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai kɛ nu ni mli tse koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: How long must I wait after spraying pest medicine on my vegetables before harvesting them to sell?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ eshwie aduawai anɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani akpa amɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Every chemical has a safety period, called a Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI), usually ranging from 3 to 14 days. Waiting for this period allows chemical residues to break down safely so the crops are safe for human consumption.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii dani akpaa nii lɛ (PHI). Bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ. Be nɛɛ ni mɛɔ lɛ haa tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai niyenii.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my cocoa pods even after I spray pest medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie amɛnɔ moŋ.

english: Using the same chemical repeatedly can make pests resistant to it, or you may be spraying at the wrong time when insect eggs are protected. Rotating different types of approved pesticides and spraying during active pest cycles ensures full control.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anyɛ atsu nii. Aloo ekolɛ oofɔse tsofa lɛ yɛ be ni esaaa mli beni abuɔ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ. Tsofai srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsakemɔ Kɛ shwiemɔ yɛ kooloi lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo be mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop treatment if heavy rain falls right after I finish spraying?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni migbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwiemɔ naa lɛ?

english: Rain washes away chemical medicine off plant leaves before the crops or pests can absorb it. If heavy rain falls within two hours of application, the treatment loses effectiveness and usually needs to be repeated.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofa lɛ ewo mli lɛ, Tsamɔ lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ ni bei pii lɛ ehe bahiaa ni afee lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the right time to spray medicine on my maize before worms destroy the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie ŋmãa nɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ akpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ?

english: Inspect your crops weekly by checking under leaves and inside young shoots for tiny holes or caterpillar eggs. Spraying early at the first sign of insects prevents major outbreaks before damage spreads.
ga: Kwɛmɔ onibii amli daa otsi kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ amli ni oookwɛ kɛji bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. loo ŋmeii akui ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra be mli Klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii emɔ mɔ lɛ ni anaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmeii wulu ko naa dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: If I double the amount of chemical fertilizer I put on my cassava, will it grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fa fe shii enyɔ lɛ, ani ebaada oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, excessive fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil that burn plant roots and stunt growth. Crops only absorb specific amounts of nutrients at a time, so applying extra wastes money and harms crop health.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni shãa tsei ashishifãi ni ehaaa amɛdara lɛ Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii komɛi pɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ shika kroko ni akɛfataa he ni afiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ ni yeɔ awui.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and dropping during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in severe sun to conserve water and prevent drying out. If they recover by morning, it is a normal heat reaction; if they stay curled, your soil lacks sufficient moisture.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ahi mli ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Kɛji ohe wa bo leebi lɛ Abuɔ enɛ akɛ eji thermal reaction ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛji amɛkoto Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are weeds hurting my tomato plants so much when they are growing in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ awui waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from tomato roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all available nourishment to produce healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tomato shishifãi amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Large trees provide shade and keep the air moist, protecting young cocoa from direct sun and heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Buu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Plantains grow quickly and have very broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas. They shield young cocoa plants from intense sun while also providing extra food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Amɛbuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding fertilizer or compost replenishes what the crop needs to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and lets pests build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil richness naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing at the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main parent plant. Removing most of the suckers and leaving only one or two leaves all the plant's energy focused on producing large fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ atsu yibii wuji ni ebaawo lɛ he nii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Keeping leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf rot and allows the plant to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaf. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading diseases that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbɛɔ helai ni haaa tsei adara lɛ amɛshwã.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This is typical damage from pests like the Fall Armyworm eating the tender leaves inside the crop's center. Checking plants early allows you to control them before they destroy the plant's growing point.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ fitemɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do farmers cut cassava stems into pieces and plant them slanted into the ground instead of upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ ŋmei niji bibii bibii lɛ? Ni adu lɛ ni etsi ehe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeedamɔ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slant buries more growing points beneath the soil, encouraging more roots to develop into thick, healthy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaafu he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants drop off without forming any tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out before they can be fertilized. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during peak sun helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, well-rotted manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore their green color and boosts plant energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea baawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ aná su ni ji eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha hewalɛ aya hiɛ aha tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without forming fruit when the weather is extremely hot, when watering is irregular, or when there are no bees around to pollinate them. Consistent watering and maintaining healthy soil can help plants hold onto their fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha tso lɛ afee pollin Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ yibii amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and dry winds. Leaving some shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantain creates a cool, humid environment that shields young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tso yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to more sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases and weed competition.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by viruses they spread. Spraying with neem leaf extract or soapy water helps control these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso mli nu loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because roots need air to stay healthy. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots do not suffocate and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ shwieee shi ni amɛgbooo.

english: If fall armyworms return to my maize farm after I spray them, what causes them to keep coming back?
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛni haa amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa?

english: Fall armyworms hatch continuously from eggs laid by flying moths, so one spray only kills the caterpillars present at that moment. Inspecting the center leaves weekly allows you to catch new batches early before they cause heavy damage.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ kome pɛ baagbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nakai beaŋ lɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa otsi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ eheei oya dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crop improve my soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil, providing free food for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soils, so they react faster to water and steal soil nutrients before your planted crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds while they are small keeps them from overwhelming your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ nu feɔ ekome oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei ni amɛduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni onibii lɛ akafee nɔ ni fe nine.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ fite beni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in warm, moist places where mold or insects damaged them, or if they were hybrid seeds that naturally lose vigor in the second generation. Storing dry seeds in sealed containers in a cool spot helps keep them alive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii loo kooloi fiteɔ amɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ eji dumɔwu ni akɛfee ekome ni efite ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy certified seeds when I can just use the seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Akɛni manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii hewɔ lɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to ensure high germination rates, disease resistance, and uniform growth. Saved seeds lose these strong qualities over time, leading to weaker crops and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa daa. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying the right fertilizer or compost will restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ ni amɛhe wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain or cassava alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantain provide living shade to protect young cocoa while giving you food to harvest while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii ni obaakpa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ miida lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in the center leaves of my maize plants with tiny green caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Mi-abɛi tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmei bibioo ni ji eŋɔli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed inside the growing shoot of maize plants, but early detection and spraying with approved organic or chemical solutions can save your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Shi mra ni ooona ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekwɛ onibii anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning curled and distorted with yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to stop it.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnuts make my soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to a plant family that captures nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. beni okpaa lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Will I get more harvest if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small, poor-quality produce.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: How do I know if my vegetable crop is receiving too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-vegetables lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their roots cannot breathe and begin to rot. Leaves will turn yellow, wilt even when the soil is wet, and plants may easily get pulled out of the muddy soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Egboɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Ni tsei baanyɛ ajɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli oya.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants face stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and good soil nutrients help flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How should I store my certified seeds so they stay good until the planting season begins?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ato koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ be lɛ baaje shishi?

english: Seeds should be stored in airtight containers placed in a cool, dry, and dark location. Moisture, heat, and sunlight will cause seeds to rot, lose their strength, or attract insects.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui awo tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni duŋ ewo. Fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ, kɛ hulu la baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo. hewalɛ ni baa shi loo egbalaa kooloi

english: Why is it important for me to space out my maize plants evenly instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majara ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Even spacing ensures that every plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong. When plants are crowded, they fight for nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller corn cobs.
ga: Gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ po haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ Ebaatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: How do I keep my crop rows straight when planting corn on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ afee tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can use a planting tool that marks the soil or use a guide string stretched across the field. Following these visible marks ensures neat, straight rows that make weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔ nii ni kadiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kpãi ni akpã mli yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Okadii ni anaa nɛɛ asɛɛdii yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa akɛ atoɔ he fɛo, ni ja. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do row markers help me know where to plant my next line of crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ line markers yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minaa he ni esa akɛ madu tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ?

english: A row marker creates a visible line or groove in the dirt parallel to the line you just planted. When you turn around to plant the next row, you simply follow that mark to keep all your rows evenly spaced.
ga: Row markers lɛ feɔ line loo furrows ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɛ line ni odu kɛkɛ nɛɛ kpãa gbee. Kɛji otsɔ ohe koni odu ŋwɛi ŋta ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ onyiɛ okadii lɛ asɛɛ kɛkɛ koni ŋta lɛ fɛɛ afee ekome.

english: Why do straight, spaced-out rows make it easier to weed my farm later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Straight rows leave clear, consistent pathways between crops. This allows you to walk through easily with a hoe without accidentally damaging the roots or stems of your growing corn.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ja haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli oya ni ofiteee ŋmei ni oduɔ lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why should I put corn seeds into the ground one by one instead of dropping several seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui komekomei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ.

english: Planting seeds one by one gives each plant its own space for root expansion. If too many seeds are dropped into one hole, the young shoots will compete with each other for food, leading to poor growth and smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ekomekomei lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui babaoo shwie bu kome mli lɛ, Young shoots lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa shweremɔ ayaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when I am planting maize on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize seeds should generally be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. Digging too deep prevents the seed from sprouting above ground, while shallow holes leave the seed exposed to heat and birds.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 nɔ. Kɛ́ akumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi.

english: What happens to my crop yield if my farm hands plant corn seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔ lɛ du ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, the growing corn plants shade each other from sunlight and tangle their roots. This causes thin, tall stalks that produce very small cobs or fall over easily in heavy wind.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Abɛi tsei ni miida lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ bibii bɔni afee ni amɛná ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛgbee shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How does using a hand planter tool help me when planting my corn field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni madu ŋmãa?

english: A hand planter opens the soil to the right depth and marks the distance to the next spot automatically. This speeds up planting, saves your back from constant bending, and keeps seed spacing uniform.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛ niji duɔ nii lɛ gbeleɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa kɛyashɛɔ he ni sa, ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ekadiɔ he ni jɛkɛmɔ kɛyaa he ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. This will help speed up planting. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be. ni oha sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ahi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ be fɛɛ be

english: What is the best way for two farm workers to work together to plant corn quickly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi enyɔ baanyɛ atsɔ nɔ afee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa oya?

english: One worker can lead by using a tool to dig or punch the holes and mark the distance, while the second worker follows right behind dropping the seeds into the open holes. Division of labor speeds up the process.
ga: Nitsulɔ kome baanyɛ atsɔ dɛŋdade ko ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔɔ gbɛ loo efo bu ni ekadi he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni nitsulɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ nyiɛ esɛɛ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwie bu ni agbele lɛ mli lɛ. Nitsumɔ mlijaa haa nifeemɔ lɛ yaa oya.

english: Is it better to plant corn using a standard cutlass or a hole-digging planter tool?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsɔ cutlass loo bu mli dɛŋdade ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ nɔ adu ŋmãa?

english: While a cutlass works for small gardens, a specialized planter opens holes to a uniform depth and measures row distance at the same time. It saves time, reduces physical exhaustion, and helps achieve a better yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ daggers hi kɛha abɔɔi bibii moŋ, Shi tsei tsɛnsii krɛdɛɛi gbeleɔ bu lɛ mli kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni amɛsusuɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ he yɛ be kome too mli. Ekɛ be baa shi Ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa nitsumɔ kpakpa

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from strong direct sunlight. Without shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, the young leaves burn and turn yellow.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he hulutsoo. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu he kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ, Baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps crop roots cool, and rots into natural food for your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni egboɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow dark green leaves. Adding manure or recommended fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil as natural fertilizer. This enriches the ground and helps neighboring crops grow stronger without buying extra inputs.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni jɛɔ sɛɛ mli baa lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛheee nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because they cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing much food when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light instead of developing strong stems and high yields.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛha la abote mli moŋ, ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch sunlight. Staking keeps leaves dry to prevent diseases and allows the plant to produce much bigger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when small insects attack the blooms. Keeping soil evenly moist helps the plant hold its flowers and make tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ tomato.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the amount of food I harvest from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baafee aha niyenii ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. If weeds are left in the field early in the season, your crops get starved and yield far less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: What causes small holes and chewed edges on the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Chewed holes on young maize leaves are usually caused by pest caterpillars, such as Fall Armyworm, hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Identifying them early helps you protect the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni ayɔseɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When the plant does not get enough nutrients from the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed the growing leaves on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with plenty of leaves but only produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are spaced too closely together, cassava uses all its food and energy to grow leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers and young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara?

english: Cocoa trees drop young pods (known as cherelle wilt) when they are stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or lack of shade. The tree naturally reduces its pod load to keep itself alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ Cherelle Wilt) kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo hulutsoo ni bɛ Tso lɛ baajie eshishifãi lɛ ayibɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ehi wala mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when excess nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on leaf growth instead of fruit formation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni amɛbaawo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but two or three healthy shoots ensures the main stem receives enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ, ja enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines into the light and keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni etsĩɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my groundnut plants bend down and push their flower stems into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miikoto shi ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ miitsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers pollinate above ground, but the actual nuts can only grow and mature in total darkness underground, where the soft soil protects them from dry heat and animals.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ ada ni amɛshwere yɛ duŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ pɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and getting hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from hot sun and rapid water loss, or as a symptom of a plant virus transmitted by small sap-sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ he. Aloo eji tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily at the stem whenever strong rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ baa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over (lodging) if seeds were planted too shallowly, if plants were overcrowded, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is needed to build strong, sturdy stalks.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai (wɔɔhe) kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ he miihia koni afee tso ni wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Standing water smothers weeds that compete with rice for sunlight and nutrients, while keeping the soil consistently moist so the rice roots can easily drink up plant food.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ aye tsei aniyenii mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant too many different types of crops on my small piece of farm at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? mi hu yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ

english: When you plant too many different crops closely together, they fight for the same water, light, and nutrients in the dirt. It also makes it easier for pests from one crop to move over and ruin another crop.
ga: Kɛji odu tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli lɛ baafã ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: If my maize crop fails this season, why is it a bad idea to plant maize again on the exact same plot right away?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ be nɛɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The pests and soil diseases that damaged your first maize crop will remain hidden in the soil. Planting maize again immediately gives those pests a continuous food supply to multiply and destroy your new crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni fiteɔ oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baakã he ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni ooodu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha nakai kooloi lɛ aná niyenii ni yaa nɔ koni amɛshwere ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: If I notice disease on one crop, why should I avoid touching healthy plants with my farm tools without washing them?
ga: Kɛji mina hela ko yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome nɔ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛfɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ he?

english: Diseases are often spread by tiny fungus spores or germs that stick to your cutlass, clothing, and hands. Touching a sick crop and then a healthy one directly transfers the sickness across your whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal spores loo helatsɛmɛi bibii gbɛɔ helai. Ekpɛtɛɔ dadei, atadei, kɛ oniji ahe. Kɛ́ ota tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ota tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aya oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp conditions. Leaving old infected pods on the tree allows the disease to jump to healthy young pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small holes all over their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central shoot during the day and feed on the growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ feɔ bu yɛ ŋmeii baa bibii amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my soil get hard and dry after I burn the bushes on my plot before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ saatso lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fire kills the good living organisms in the soil that keep it soft and fertile. Burning also removes natural mulch, leaving your topsoil exposed to the hot sun which bakes it hard.
ga: La gbeɔ nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ. Shãa hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Okɛ oshikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni no haa ewaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning light yellow while my neighbor's farm stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking important nutrients like nitrogen, or the crop is infected with a disease. Farm management practices like crop rotation and organic manure help keep soil rich.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. The plant sacrifices its flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa. Tsei kɛ amɛfɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay short and produce poor yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii miiba miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When weeds take over, your crops do not get enough food to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from direct sunlight while their roots establish. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide wide leafy shade that keeps the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwaa lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant produce food that travels down into the ground to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure will help the plants regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests with neem oil or proper spray helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. Consistent watering and putting dry grass mulch around the base of the plant helps retain soil moisture so flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nu daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. koni fɔfɔii lɛ afee aduawai

english: What is making small holes in my maize stalks and causing the tops of the plants to dry out?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni eha tso lɛ yiteŋ agbi?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that tunnel into the plant stem to feed. Applying targeted insect control early in the season prevents them from destroying the stalk and damaging your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need well-drained soil to breathe. When rain saturates the field without proper drainage, water sits around the roots and starves them of air, leading to fungal rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ. Nu baakpɛtɛ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi kɛ suffocate Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops hurt their overall harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ saa yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds during the early weeks of crop growth leaves all the nutrients and light for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kɛ la fɛɛ ni baaha otsei lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Fertilizer is most effective when applied a few weeks after planting when roots have formed to absorb it, and again before the plants start flowering to support fruit and grain formation.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ edara koni amɛŋɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. ni okɛfata he ekoŋŋ dani tsei lɛ aje fɔfɔii ashishi koni eye ebua aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni anáa lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans or cowpeas helps restore soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa crops yielding less even though I am planting at the same time I always have?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana have shifted over time, meaning the months that used to bring heavy rain might now be dry, leaving your young plants without enough water during critical growth periods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nyɔji ni tsutsu lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afee nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, otsei bibii lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees do not get enough water from rainfall, they shed their leaves to conserve moisture and protect themselves from dying of extreme heat and thirst.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kumai ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ he.

english: How does unpredictable weather affect the flowers on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ saa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Irregular rain and extended dry weather stress cocoa trees, causing them to drop their flowers early before they can turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa kookoo tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is crop irrigation and how will it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni te ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Irrigation is the artificial application of water to your land or soil, ensuring your crops get a steady water supply even when natural rains fail or become unreliable.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ji nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ po.

english: Will watering my cocoa trees during dry periods make them produce pods all year round?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baaha ewo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, giving your cocoa trees consistent water through irrigation stops them from drying out, allowing them to continuously flower and bear fruit regardless of the dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛ nu shwieɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ daa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni kookoo tso lɛ akagbi. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ekɔɔɔ he eko be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Is natural rainfall no longer enough to support cocoa farming in my area?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: Due to changing weather patterns, natural rainfall has become less predictable, making additional water sources like irrigation necessary to keep cocoa farms productive.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ No hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Enɛ haa nu jɛɛhei krokomɛi, tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ anɔ.

english: Will adding an artificial water system to my cocoa farm damage my trees or soil?
ga: Ani nu gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni akɛ niji fee ni mikɛbaafata mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baafite mitsei loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: No, proper irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone safely, helping the soil retain nutrients and keeping the trees strong and healthy.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ shweshweeshwe. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa farms in my region stay green during the dry season while mine dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni mi nɔ lɛ ŋmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Farms that stay green usually utilize irrigation systems to supply water continuously, protecting their trees from the harsh dry weather that affects farms relying only on rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha nu ni yaa nɔ. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa ni saa ŋmɔji ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I harvest cocoa pods outside the traditional main harvest season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ kusum naa kpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if your crops receive steady water and care throughout the entire year, the trees will keep producing cocoa pods outside the traditional harvest months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná nu kɛ kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsei lɛ baaya nɔ amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kusum naa ŋmaakpamɔ nyɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What steps can I take to protect my crops if the rainy season ends earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: Adopting an irrigation system allows you to supply water to your crops from secondary sources like wells or ponds whenever the rains stop unexpectedly.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu haa onibii kɛjɛɔ he kroko tamɔ nubu loo nubu. Be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa trukaa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni plantain bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like newborn babies—their leaves burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, acting like caring grandmothers who shield the young cocoa with shade until it grows strong enough to stand the heat.
ga: Kakao tso bibioo tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Beni efeɔ enii tamɔ nana ko ni kwɛɔ mɔ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: How do groundnuts help my cassava grow bigger when I plant them on the same mound?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava lɛ ni edara waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Groundnuts act like generous uncles in a family; they pull invisible food from the air and feed it into the dirt. Your cassava plants share that same dirt and eat that extra food, helping both crops grow healthy without fighting.
ga: Peanut feɔ enii tamɔ tsɛkwɛ̃ ko ni hiɛ tsui kpakpa yɛ weku lɛ mli. Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. O-cassava tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii ni eyeɔ nakai niyenii krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwuuuu amɛhe.

english: Why does my maize produce very small cobs when I plant it on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Just like a mother gets weak if she keeps giving birth without eating nutritious food, soil gets exhausted when maize drains the same food year after year. Rotating with beans or cowpeas feeds the soil back so it regains its strength.
ga: Nakai nɔŋŋ eji kɛha nyɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛji efɔ ni eyeee niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ hoɔ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: When a child goes hungry, their face looks pale and weak. Yellow leaves are your maize plants crying out from hunger because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food they need to build healthy green leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ hɔmɔ ye gbekɛbii lɛ, efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhiɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ji o-corn tsei ni miibolɔ kɛmiijɛ hɔmɔ mli ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a cool cloth placed on a hot forehead. It covers the soil so the scorching sun doesn't drink up all the underground water, keeping your pepper roots cool and hydrated through the heat.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ mama ni mli ejɔ ni akɛwo hiɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akanu shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni o-pepper shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with thin stalks when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Imagine sleeping five adults on one small sleeping mat; everyone fights for space and no one rests well. When seeds are planted too close, they stretch tall fighting each other for light and soil food instead of growing thick and sturdy.
ga: Susumɔ onukpai enumɔ ni ewɔ wɔɔhe bibioo kome nɔ lɛ he okwɛ. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ená he ko ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ejɔɔɔ ehe jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ la kɛ shikpɔŋ akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e daa nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do weeds lower my yam harvest even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are like greedy houseguests who eat all the food cooked for the children. Even with plenty of water, weeds steal the soil nutrients meant for your yams, leaving the tubers hungry and small.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ shia gbɔi hiɛjoolɔi ni yeɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni ohooɔ ohaa obii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛhaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why should I cut off some of the healthy-looking side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: If a parent has too many children to feed at once, none of them get enough food to grow strong. Trimming extra branches forces the tomato plant to focus all its strength on growing a few big, juicy fruits instead of many tiny ones.
ga: Kɛji fɔlɔi yɛ bii babaoo ni esa akɛ amɛtsɔse yɛ be kome mli Mɔ ko mɔ ko naŋ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛtsɔ niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tomato tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama aduawai wuji fioo komɛi ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe bibii babaoo.

english: Why do I suddenly find tiny holes in my cabbage leaves right after a short rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko trukaa lɛ? Yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ

english: Rain brings tender new leaves, which attract hungry insects just like a freshly cooked family meal attracts children to the table. Worms hatch quickly after rain to feast, so you must inspect the leaves early before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo baa. ni gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ Taakɛ weku niyenii ni ato ehee lɛ gbalaa gbekɛbii kɛbaa okpɔlɔ lɛ he lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ kooloi fɔɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni amɛha niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ baai lɛ amli mra. dani ekpãtãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the ground first?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Like a mother showing clear signs when it is time to give birth, cassava plants give signals: the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base starts to crack as the swell of heavy tubers pushes from below.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ tsuɔ okadii tamɔ nyɛ nɔ, ni etsɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛji be shɛ ni esa akɛ efɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni yitso agbo ko fũu kɛjɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving select shade trees protects the young leaves from drying out, keeps the soil moist, and reduces heat stress on the crop during its early years.
