ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ ni baa tsei anɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stem usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and fuels growth, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts work with tiny beneficial organisms in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Heavy rainfall washes away the fertilizer off the topsoil or pushes it deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, wasting your fertilizer and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot underground when the rains are too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields get waterlogged, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen and become vulnerable to fungal rots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛbaafee oshara akɛ amɛbaafite.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to direct sunlight so they can make more food for the plant, which leads to bigger yam tubers growing underground while keeping leaves off wet, disease-prone soil.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela baanyɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or erratic watering. When the plant gets too hot or dry, it drops blossoms to save water and survival energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni ejaaa ha amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ loo egbi tsɔ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato wala he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: If too many young suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for water, nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in smaller stems and small, light plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ plantain tsei bibii baa.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant my maize seeds too close together in the same line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: When maize plants are overcrowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for nutrients, soil moisture, and light, causing thin stalks and very small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwereɔ tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to filter the sun, the strong heat burns the leaves and dries out moisture, causing them to turn yellow and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baatsi hulu la naa lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers naturally when they are stressed by dry weather, lack nutrients, or lack small insects like midges that pollinate the flowers. Giving the soil proper nutrients and moisture helps more flowers stay on the tree to become pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it bad to spray chemical pesticides on my crops in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Spraying in the hot sun causes the liquid chemical to evaporate into the air before it can work on pests. The heat can also cause the chemicals to scorch and burn the plant leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ. Dɔlɛ hu baanyɛ aha tsofa ashã tso lɛ baai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do insects keep returning to my farm even after I have sprayed chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ po.

english: Insects return because eggs or pests hidden under leaves and in the soil may have survived the spray. Also, using the exact same chemical repeatedly can make pests resistant to it, so rotating different recommended chemicals ensures better control.
ga: Kplukai kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa ejaakɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ashishi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajo ŋmeii lɛ anaa foi. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Baanyɛ Eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akatsu nii No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai srɔtoi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ atsakeɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce huge leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leafy green stems instead of roots. Balancing the soil nutrients with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to build thick, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium toɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Nutrient-poor soil shows warning signs such as stunted growth, thin stems, or leaves turning yellow instead of deep green. Testing the soil or speaking with an extension officer can tell you exactly which plant foods are missing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ baajie kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii akpo, tamɔ dalɛ ni eyaaa hiɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, loo baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa loo sanegbaa ni okɛ extension nitsulɔ ko baagba lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo nɔ tuuntu ni ji tsei niyenii ni elaaje.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a larger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or missing maize cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to yield a full cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ni bɛ lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to multiply. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil health and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ helai babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air pass through the farm helps keep the pods dry and lowers the chance of rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hulutsoo. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ amɛbaafite lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and adapted to survive harsh conditions. They aggressively steal water, light, and nutrients from your crops, which is why clearing them early is essential for your crops to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, kane, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to plant maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Good soil for maize feels dark and crumbly, holds moisture without turning into sticky mud, and has organic matter from old leaves. If weeds grow green and thick on the land before clearing, it usually shows the soil has enough nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ baai momoi amli Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛjie amɛhe, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients maize needs to grow. It also lets soil pests and diseases that target maize build up, causing lower yields over time. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps restore the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Keeping taller trees or planting temporary plantains provides necessary shade and keeps the surrounding air cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛkwɛ shɔŋŋ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I trim or remove some of the side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie niji ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming extra shoots (suckers) directs the plant's food and water away from growing useless leaves and straight into producing bigger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe. ni ekɛ tomato yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on cassava usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, is getting too much water around its roots, or is being attacked by tiny pests like mealybugs or viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo virus tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why are insects eating small holes in my vegetable leaves, and does it really affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ buji bibii lɛ? yɛ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni ani enaa minitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's food factory by catching sunlight. When insects eat holes in the leaves, the plant cannot make enough food, which weakens its growth and reduces the amount of produce it yields.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi ye buji ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much rain or water in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nugbɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Too much water causes soil to stay waterlogged, suffocating plant roots. You will notice yellowing leaves, soft or rotting stems, and stunted growth because the roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients.
ga: Nu babaoo haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu. ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Obaana kaadi ni ji yellow card. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo egbo. kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, and when the inside lining of the shelled pods shows dark brown or black spots instead of being pale green or white.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. ni kɛ́ tso lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛŋ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen or that too much water is drowning the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer when the soil is damp helps the leaves turn deep green and resume healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo akɛ nu babaoo miiha shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce less corn every year even though I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and refreshes your land.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die after I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaf surfaces burn and their shallow roots dry out. Leaving some shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni baa lɛ hiɛ shãa ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ gbɛ́ɔ hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baadara.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes in my corn leaves and small worms tucked inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? ni akɛwo cone mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds heavily on the central leaves of growing maize. Checking your farm regularly and applying recommended botanical or targeted treatments early keeps the worms from destroying the plant's growth point.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil without proper drainage. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Can I just dig up any plantain shoot from my old farm and replant it in a new field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo plantain tsei kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Using random shoots can carry hidden root pests and diseases from your old farm into your new soil. It is best to select healthy maiden suckers with narrow, needle-like leaves and pare off any dark, damaged parts of the root before planting.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni baa trukaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ oŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ aba shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala yei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Ni ofolɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe hei ni edɔ ni efite lɛ dani odu.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them right after the very first day of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the top layer of dry, hot soil, which is not enough to support seed germination. Waiting for two or three steady downpours ensures the deeper soil is moist enough to keep the young seed alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. ni faaa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest and block out weeds?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo ni matsi jwɛi anaa?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and poor yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed while making it easier for you to clear weeds.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not flooded, ideally after a light rain. Placing the fertilizer in a small ring or hole near the crop's roots and covering it with soil prevents rainwater from washing it down the farm.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu efooo mli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo bu mli ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni akɛ sũ ha nɔ lɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer that forces leaf growth over fruiting. Mulching the soil to conserve moisture and providing balanced plant food helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ daa fe aduawai. Mulching ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛ tsei niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water when the sun is very hot. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu akafite kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives the roots the water they need before the sun gets strong, and prevents water from immediately evaporating into the hot afternoon air.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ dani hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I know if my cassava plants are suffering from too little water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nu fioo tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are thirsty, they naturally drop their lower leaves to save water for the main stem and underground tubers. Losing a few bottom leaves is normal, but losing most leaves means the crop is severely stressed.
ga: Kɛji kumai ye ŋmei tso lɛ Eshiɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ ebɔɔ su mli koni ekɛto nu kɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi ni laajeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni elaaje lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehao waa.

english: Why do the edges of my vegetable leaves turn brown and crisp even when I water the surface soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Brown leaf edges happen when water only moistens the surface without reaching the deep roots, or when hot winds dry out the leaves faster than the roots can drink up soil water.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji nu shwie nɔ shi eshɛɛɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha baai lɛ gĩ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up after several months of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni mikɛdara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing vines near the end of the season mean the plant is finishing its growth cycle and sending all its energy down into the underground tuber, showing that the yams are mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Wein tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbe edalɛ be lɛ naa. ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ amaje shi kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants form large outer leaves but fail to make a hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage plants fail to form heads when the weather is too warm or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces them to keep growing loose leaves instead of a tight center.
ga: Kaabaji tsei nyɛɛɛ afee yitsei kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni egbee shi yɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ masɛi?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin, but only producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa pɛ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They stretch thin to reach the sun, leaving them with too little energy to grow full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛgbalaa amɛhe bibii koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster in my field than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing their seeds to wake up faster and absorb water and nutrients quicker than domestic crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛjɛ fɔmɔ mli amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia dumɔwui.

english: Why do some types of maize make better dough for banku and etew than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi feɔ ashikishaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa banku kɛ etiu fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Maize varieties differ in starch structure and texture. White dent or soft local maize absorbs water easily and ferments well, producing the smooth, sticky texture required for foods like banku and etew, unlike hard flint or feed maize.
ga: Abɛi yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ srɔtoi. White bum loo maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni tamɔ banku kɛ etiu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa ni wa loo ŋmãa ni akɛyeɔ kooloi niyenii lɛ he.

english: Is it safe for me to save maize seeds from my current harvest to plant during the next season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted hybrid maize, saving seeds for the next season results in lower yields and small cobs because hybrid vigor drops after the first generation. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds or use improved open-pollinated varieties if you plan to save seed.
ga: Kɛji odu hybrid corn Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ejaakɛ hybrid hewalɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli. loo okɛ ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi ni agbele naa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii. Kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ koni ohere dumɔwui lɛ ayiwala

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without big cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply (about 15 centimeters deep) across a few steady rainfalls. Planting after just one early rain is risky because the soil can dry out quickly and kill germinating seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ (aaafee sɛntimita 15) yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ efite dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil. Planting them with maize improves soil fertility, controls weeds, and provides two different food harvests from the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, eyeɔ jwɛi anɔ, ni ehaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ jɛɔ he kome.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips of lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right stage will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillars hiding inside the top leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ nɔ Ekɛ ehe ewo baa lɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying an recommended insecticide early in the morning or late evening directly into the center funnel of the plant controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does a purple-flowered weed keep growing around my maize and causing the stalks to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Mi ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ afee bibioo.

english: This weed is called Striga (witchweed). It is a parasite that attaches its roots to maize roots to steal water and nutrients. Rotating your maize field with non-cereal crops like cassava or cowpea starves the weed seeds in the soil.
ga: Nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga (witchweed) lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Abele ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei baatsake lɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why does my stored maize grain turn into white powder and get tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛŋ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: This damage is caused by grain weevils that lay eggs inside dry corn seeds. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in airtight hermetic bags stops weevils from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Abele ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ewaa ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: Why is it harmful to harvest maize cobs while they are still wet and store them immediately in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mabua ŋmãa ŋmeii anaa be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo ni mikɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Storing wet maize creates moisture that allows dangerous fungi and moulds to grow. These moulds spoil the grain and produce invisible poisons called aflatoxins, which make the food unsafe for your family to eat.
ga: Abele ni akɛtoɔ he ni efɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsofai fɔji ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ. Enɛ haaa niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha oweku lɛ ni amɛye.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer flowers and pods than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo fe afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their natural strength declines, making it harder for the root system to absorb nutrients and support heavy flowering or pod production.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛye amɛbua fɔfɔi loo podi afeemɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and tired even when I clear the weeds around them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ amɛhe daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Over decades of continuous growth, cocoa trees drain specific nutrients from the soil, causing the trees to lose vigor from old age and nutrient exhaustion, which simple weeding cannot fix.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ Cocoa tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ amɛgbɔlɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa lɛ hewɔ. ni jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa tree has completely lost its strength and will not yield well again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tso ko he wa efo mli ni ewooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: If a cocoa tree consistently shows dry branches, yellowing leaves, and sparse flowering for several seasons despite good rainfall, it has lost its vigor and is reaching the end of its productive life.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso ko yɛ niji ni egbi, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ fɔfɔii ni egbɛ eshwã bei babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ efo mli ni eeshɛ eshihilɛ ni woɔ yibii lɛ naagbee.

english: If my cocoa farm is no longer yielding well, what food crops can I plant instead to get quick results?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ hu? Mɛɛ niyenii esa akɛ makwɛ moŋ koni maná yibii oya?

english: Switching to food crops like cassava, maize, plantain, or vegetables is ideal because these crops mature quickly within months or a year, giving you food and steady income while the soil recovers.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe tsakemɔ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ daa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi loo afi mli. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do food crops like maize and cassava produce food much faster than cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa woɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmãa tsei lɛ?

english: Food crops are short-cycle plants naturally designed to grow quickly and produce yield within a single season, unlike cocoa trees which take years to mature and produce pods.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni afee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo yibii yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ cacao tso, ni heɔ afii babaoo dani edaa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Is it better to clear my entire failing cocoa farm at once or replace it step-by-step with food crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie kookoo ŋmɔji ni efite lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo akɛ niyenii ŋmɔji awo amɛ najiaŋ fiofio fiofio?

english: Replacing old trees step-by-step allows you to clear the weakest parts of your farm first for food crops, securing immediate food and money while you manage the rest of the land.
ga: Tsei momoi ni oootsake amɛ fiofio lɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani amɛbatsɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii. ni oná niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What causes the flowers on my cocoa trees to dry up and fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni miiha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa flowers drop prematurely when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients, suffers from severe sun heat, or loses internal vigor due to old age and pest stress.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ he piŋmɔ loo mligbɛ hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ afii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Why does prolonged sunshine and hot weather affect old cocoa trees more than food crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe fe niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Old cocoa trees need consistent shade and high moisture to thrive, whereas crops like cassava have deep roots and tough leaves designed to survive heat and drought much better.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ latsaa babaoo koni amɛshwere. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni afee koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: What happens to the soil when cocoa trees grow on the exact same plot of land for nearly thirty years?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ aaafee afii nyɔŋmai etɛ?

english: Decades of cocoa farming continuously draw deep nutrients out of the soil, leaving the land tired and depleted unless organic matter or crop rotation is introduced.
ga: Afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛduɔ kookoo lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baa. ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsu nii.

english: Can growing food crops help restore my land after decades of cocoa farming?
ga: Ani niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni mikɛtsu kookoo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops—especially leguminous ones like beans or cowpeas—helps break the cycle of tree diseases and adds fresh nutrients back into the upper soil layers.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ. Titri lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa tso helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii heei baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when moisture stays trapped on the trees due to heavy shade or bushy farms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Fɛ̃i lɛ emɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil, or that too much water around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu yɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks become weak if the plants are planted too close together, if the soil lacks potassium, or if stem borer insects have eaten into the inside of the stalks.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Aloo kɛji stem borer kooloi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the daytime weather is too hot or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water, causing stress to the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and refusing to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Is it good for me to keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: No, planting the same crop on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients and builds up pests in the soil. Switching to crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Dabi, tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out so fast even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter to hold water. Adding compost or decomposed animal manure acts like a sponge, helping the soil keep water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha nu ahi mli lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping young fruits before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tsei lɛ woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees shed young fruit when they suffer from sudden dry spells, lack proper plant nutrients, or get attacked by fruit flies that pierce the small fruits.
ga: Citrus tsei woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe amɛ. Tso mli niyenii ni sa ni bɛ loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ aduawai bibii lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the bunches on my oil palm tree small and missing many palm nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ ji bibioo ni palm ŋmeii babaoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need proper pollination from beneficial insects or wind to form full bunches of nuts. If the tree lacks nutrients, water, or pollinators, many nuts fail to develop, leaving empty gaps on the bunch.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ aha amɛ ŋmeii ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, nu loo nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ Nuts babaoo ehiɛɛɛ. Enɛ haa he ko bɛ nɔ yɛ kuu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of the soil away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛjie shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stem center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant to eat soft young leaves, and they need to be treated early with recommended control measures before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii. ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ mra kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava rot usually happens when excess water stays trapped around the roots for too long, causing fungi to grow. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ehi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. haa ŋmeii shwereɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to produce enough energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the wet ground, which also prevents leaves from rotting and catching diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking jieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekafite ni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because the soil moisture keeps changing from too dry to too wet. Keeping the soil evenly watered helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juice out of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling tiny pests early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start producing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji amɛbɔi shweremɔ yɛ kui wuji amli pɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots to hold them firm, and tiny soil pests can weaken their shallow roots. Supporting the plants with strong wooden or bamboo poles prevents them from falling in wind or under heavy fruit weight.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. kɛ kooloi bibii ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo aduawai lɛ amli tsiimɔ mli.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, but not during heavy downpours. Crops need a little water to dissolve the fertilizer so roots can drink it, but heavy rains will wash it off the farm before plants can use it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi esaaa akɛ owoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Nu fioo he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ ŋmɔji amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Brown and falling leaves are usually a sign of a disease, like a fungal infection, or pest damage. When cocoa trees get sick, they drop leaves to survive, but spraying the right crop medicine stops the disease and allows fresh, healthy leaves to grow back.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji hela okadi, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tso lɛ Baai lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛhi shi. Shi tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ kpaa, ni ehaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spraying chemical medicine actually help my sick crops get better?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tɛŋŋ?

english: Spraying acts like giving medicine to a sick person. The chemical targets and kills the fungus or pest causing the problem, which stops the damage from spreading and lets your crop recover and produce new growth.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ tsofa ni akɛhaa helatsɛ ko. Tsofai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni kɛ naagba lɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni egbeɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni oye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná shweremɔ hee.

english: Can a cocoa tree that looks sick from disease ever grow healthy leaves again?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, if the main trunk and roots are still alive, treating the disease with the right spray destroys the infection, allowing the tree to bounce back and produce fresh, new growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Hela lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni sa tsuɔ he nii lɛ kpataa hela lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is a plant virus the same thing as a fungal disease on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani tsei amli helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji ekome?

english: No, viruses and fungi are different types of sicknesses. Fungal diseases usually cause pod rot or leaf spots and can be treated with sprays, while plant viruses often require extra care or removing the plant to keep it from spreading.
ga: Dabi, helai srɔtoi ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ pod rot loo baa lɛ mli tsɔi baa ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ biɔ tsamɔ krɛdɛɛ ko loo ajie tsei lɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Do I always have to cut down and uproot my cocoa tree if it gets sick?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ko ni mafolɔ mli be fɛɛ be kɛji hela mɔ lɛ?

english: No, you do not always have to uproot a sick tree. Many common diseases can be cured by applying the correct spraying medicine directly to the affected parts of the plant.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsa helai babaoo ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will my cocoa trees produce good pods again after being treated for a disease?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii kpakpai ekoŋŋ beni mitsa hela lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, once the disease is completely killed off by the chemical treatment, the tree regains its strength and directs its energy back into growing flowers and healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni ajie hela lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ nɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo fɔfɔi ni miida kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How long does it take to see new growth on my cocoa tree after spraying it?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mana shweremɔ hee yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once the spray effectively kills the fungus or disease, you will typically start seeing new green leaves and fresh shoots sprouting within a few weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbe ŋmeii loo hela jogbaŋŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaaje shishi ona baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: How do I know which spray medicine is the right one to buy for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male cacao spray ni sa kɛha mihemɔ lɛ?

english: Different sicknesses need different medicines—fungicides treat fungal diseases like black pod, while insecticides target bugs. An extension officer can help identify the exact disease on your farm so you buy the right product.
ga: Helai srɔtoi biɔ tsofai srɔtoi. Tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji, yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii anɔ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana hela pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni onyɛ ohe nɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak even when there are no obvious insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases caused by microscopic fungi or viruses can attack the inside of the tree or leaves without visible insects. Using an effective disease treatment destroys these hidden germs so the tree can regain its health.
ga: Hela nɛɛ, ni ŋmei bibioo ko loo helatsɛ ko kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ atutua tso lɛ mli loo baai lɛ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ bɛ mli. Helai ahe tsamɔi ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kpataa nɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ahiɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada ekoŋŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does a disease move from one tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through rain splashing, wind, infected tools, or insects crawling between plants. Spraying infected trees early kills the disease source before it can travel to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tsei ateŋ Ekɛ tsofa shwieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ mra Egbeɔ he ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ dani efãa gbɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the first rains start falling?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be too hot and dry. It is best to wait until you get two or three steady rains within a week so the soil holds enough moisture for the seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kaadu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lolo ni edɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too close together actually reduces your yield because the plants will compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow strong roots and yield larger fruits or tubers.
ga: Nibii ni ooodu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe baatswa akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full sun exposure; their leaves burn and they lose water rapidly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them provides a cool environment and protects them until their root systems mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Baai lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ aba ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering. Keeping the moisture in the soil consistent helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why does my shea tree produce a heavy harvest one year but almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shea tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni afeee nɔ ko kwraa?

english: Shea trees often practice alternate bearing, meaning they put so much energy into producing a huge yield one year that they need the following year to rebuild their stored nutrients before they can fruit heavily again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Shea tsei lɛ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi srɔtoi tsuɔ nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli aahu akɛ eheɔ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani amɛsaa amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What does it mean when people say my farmland soil has lost its strength or 'body'?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite hewalɛ loo ‘gbɔmɔtso’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Soil loses its strength when it has been farmed continuously without adding organic matter like compost or animal manure. Depleted soil cannot hold water or feed crops, causing plants to stay small and turn yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa kɛji akɛ atsu he nii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu loo eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the bottom up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow tall. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the skins of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting when the rainy season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: That is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cold conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight into the farm and improves airflow, which keeps the pods dry and stops the rot.
ga: No ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers under the ground are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves of the plant turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the growing tubers push outward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni miida lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, space, and nutrients far more aggressively than domestic crops. Covering the bare soil around your crops with dried leaves or mulch stops weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli waa fe shia tsei. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ ni okɛbaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I buy nursed cocoa seedlings from an extension officer instead of planting seeds directly from my old cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, a duɔ mɛ kɛ jeɔ kookoo tso momohi a mi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Nursed seedlings come from high-yielding, disease-resistant varieties that have already passed their most fragile growth stage. Planting them directly gives your crop a much higher chance of survival and faster growth compared to seeds taken straight from old pods.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni eho amɛdalɛ be ni waaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii momoi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant my new oil palm seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu oil palm dumɔwui heei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to plant oil palm seedlings is at the beginning of the main rainy season, usually around April or May in Ghana. This allows the roots to establish deeply in moist soil before the hot, dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu mu tso dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April loo May mli yɛ Ghana. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for planting cocoa or oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa thrives best in rich, well-drained forest soils with good shade protection and consistent rainfall, while oil palm is hardier, requires full open sunlight, and can tolerate flatter land with heavier clay soils.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ayɛ hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. yɛ be mli ni mu tso lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Ehe miihia ni hulu la ni mli tse lɛ aya nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: How much space should I leave between my oil palm seedlings when putting them in the ground?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm seedlings should be spaced about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern. Giving them this space ensures their large fronds do not block sunlight from each other, leading to maximum fruit production.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋmɛ oil palm dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ nɛɛ, ebaaha baai wuji lɛ atsĩii hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa babaoo.

english: What quick-yielding crops can I plant alongside my young cocoa trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: You can plant plantains, cassava, or cocoyams alongside young cocoa. Plantains are especially useful because their broad leaves provide essential shade for young cocoa while giving you food and cash within the first year.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain, ŋmei loo kookoo afata kookoo bibii ahe. Plantains he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ titri ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eha bo niyenii kɛ shika yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant oil palm trees and cocoa trees together in the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ mu tsei kɛ kookoo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is not recommended to plant cocoa and oil palm in the same space. Mature oil palms create heavy shade and have aggressive root systems that steal water and nutrients from cocoa trees, reducing cocoa yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu kookoo kɛ mu tso yɛ he kome. Mu tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Yellow or burnt leaves on young cocoa are usually a sign of excess direct sunlight without enough shade, or a lack of moisture in the soil. Adding shade trees or temporary plantain shade will protect the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni eshã yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu baai bibii ahe.

english: How can I protect my young seedlings from dying during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can protect seedlings during Harmattan by placing dry grass or leaves around the base of the stem (mulching) to keep moisture in the soil, and building small palm-frond shade covers over young trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui ahe yɛ Harmattan beaŋ kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi (mulch) lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmei tsei bibii afee hulutsoo Ha nɔ tso bibioo ko nɔ.

english: How long does a cocoa seedling take from planting before it starts producing pods and bringing me money?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛkɛ shika baa?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years with proper care, whereas traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years before producing their first harvest.
ga: Cocoa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani akpaa klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ.

english: How can income from a cash crop like cocoa help me expand into other types of farming?
ga: Te shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ mihe awo okwaayelii krokomɛi amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa provides a stable, long-term seasonal payout for decades. Farmers often use this steady income to buy new land, purchase livestock, or buy oil palm seedlings to create additional sources of income.
ga: Cocoa kɛ be mli nyɔmɔwoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ eha afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ shika ni amɛnáa daa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛheɔ shikpɔŋ hee, amɛheɔ kooloi loo amɛheɔ mu tso dumɔwui koni amɛkɛfee shika krokomɛi ni amɛbaaná.

english: Officer, I heard people talking about checking 'soil conductivity' when testing farm ground. What does that actually mean for my crops?
ga: Ofisa, minu ni mɔ ko miiwie sɛɛsaramɔ lɛ he. ‘Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɔne ni tsɔɔ tsɔne mli’ beni akaa ŋmɔ mli hei lɛ akwɛɔ Mɛni no tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil conductivity measures how well electricity passes through your soil, which tells us how many nutrients and salts are dissolved in it. When conductivity is in the right range, your crops can easily draw in food and water to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne ni tsɔɔ srawa hewalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni susuɔ bɔ ni srawa hewalɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ he. Etsɔɔ wɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa la lɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ agbala niyenii kɛ nu mli mlɛo koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to use well water that tastes a bit salty to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nubu ni mli edɔ fioo baawo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Salty water has high electrical conductivity, meaning it carries a lot of dissolved minerals. Using it regularly builds up salt in your soil, which traps moisture away from plant roots and can stunt or kill your vegetables.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ tsɔne ni haa srawa hewalɛ yaa hiɛ waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, shika tsuru ni mli edɔ babaoo yɛ nu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋoo tsu nii daa lɛ, ŋoo baabua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ jɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni ebaanyɛ eha aduawai lɛ afee shoo loo egbe amɛ.

english: I noticed a white crust forming on top of my soil during the dry season. What is happening to my farm land?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko miifee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Mɛni ba miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: That white layer is salt that came up to the surface as water evaporated. High soil conductivity shows that salt is building up, which can poison sensitive crops like tomatoes and peppers if it is not washed out with clean water.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmei ni teɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nu lɛ shwie shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni tsɔɔ la mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afee tsofa ni gbeɔ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ he.

english: Why do the tips of my maize leaves turn brown and dry up shortly after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo ŋmãa baa lɛ naagbee lɛ, efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when fertilizer increases the soil conductivity too fast, creating too much salt around the roots. Instead of feeding the plant, the heavy salt pulls water out of the roots, causing leaf burn.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii haa srawa hewalɛ ni sũ lɛ tsɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei babaoo bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei lɛ niyenii lɛ, Nu ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: When I mix liquid fertilizer with water to spray my crops, how can I be sure the mix is not too strong?
ga: Beni mikɛ nu futuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu koni mikɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli waaa tsɔ?

english: Extension officers measure the conductivity of the liquid mixture. If the conductivity reading is too high, the solution is too concentrated and will burn your leaves, so you need to dilute it with more fresh water.
ga: Extender lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli srawa hewalɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ conductivity nikanemɔ lɛ fa tsɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo awo mli.

english: Does adding dry cow dung or compost to my farm ground change how the soil feeds my crops?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni egbi loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, as compost breaks down, it releases rich minerals that raise the soil's natural conductivity in a healthy way. This helps the soil hold onto plant food longer so your crops get a steady supply of nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite Ejieɔ minerals ni jara wa ni haa sũ lɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ niyenii ni eduɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ daa.

english: Why are my plants looking weak and wilted even though I water the soil every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: If your soil has very high salt conductivity, it creates a barrier around the plant roots. Even when the ground is wet, the roots cannot suck up the water because the high salt concentration holds the water back.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni tsɔɔ ŋmei mli waa lɛ. Ehaa gbɛtsii nii ko baa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Shi shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ejaakɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow after heavy continuous rains fall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the soluble food and salts in your topsoil, dropping the soil conductivity. When these essential nutrients get leached deep into the ground, the plants starve and their leaves lose their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, srawa hewalɛ ni srawa hewalɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛji akɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni baai lɛ hu baafee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if my land has enough food for my crops before I spend money to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii dani mafite shika kɛdu amɛ?

english: An extension officer can test your soil's conductivity and nutrient levels using a simple meter. A healthy reading means good plant food is ready for your crop roots, while a low reading tells you to add compost or fertilizer first.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ mita ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo aka bɔ ni srawa hewalɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ bɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amɛkwɛ. Kanemɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ akɛ tso niyenii kpakpa yɛ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nikanemɔ ni baa shi lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: If I send my soil sample for a lab test, what does the total result tell me about my expected harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko maje koni aka lɛ akwɛ yɛ laboratori mli lɛ Mɛni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ fɛɛ baatsɔɔ mi yɛ mikpamɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ he?

english: The total test result combines measurements like conductivity, pH, and nutrient balance to show the overall health of your land. It tells you exactly what your soil lacks so you can apply the right inputs and get the maximum crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kaa lɛ hetooi lɛ fɛɛ he ji susumɔi tamɔ tsɔne ni tsɔɔ la mli, pH kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. koni etsɔɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ ha Ebaakɛɛ bo nɔ tuuntu ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ehiaaa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do certain wild grasses in the bush help my mother goats recover faster after giving birth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tooi nyɛmɛi ni amɛhe waa oya beni amɛfɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Some native wild grasses are naturally rich in essential minerals, water, and sugars that provide quick energy and promote healing and milk production for mother animals right after delivery.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ minerals ni he hiaa waa, nu, kɛ sugar babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa hewalɛ oya ni ehaa helatsamɔ kɛ mliki ni anáa kɛjɛɔ kooloi nyɛmɛi amli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ fɔmɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I grow wild bush grass on my farm to feed my livestock instead of searching the bush?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu koo mli jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii moŋ fe ni matao jwɛi?

english: Yes, you can collect seeds or stem cuttings of desirable wild fodder grasses and plant them in a dedicated pasture plot so you always have convenient, nutritious feed.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ obua koo mli kooloi aniyenii jwɛi ni ataoɔ lɛ dumɔwui loo niji anaa ni okɛdu yɛ kooloi alɛɛhei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli bɔni afee ni oná niyenii ni sa ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why shouldn't I let my animals graze my grass plot down to the bare dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihãaa kooloi aye mijwɛi lɛ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko?

english: Leaving a few inches of grass stem leaves enough food reserves in the roots, allowing the grass to regrow soft green leaves much quicker for future feeding.
