ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi tsei ni feɔ inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya kɛha niyenii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my farm animals prefer eating tender green leaves rather than dry mature stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ moŋ fe tsei ni egbi ni eda lɛ?

english: Young green shoots are soft, easy to digest, and rich in protein and moisture, whereas mature stems become tough, dry, and low in nutrients.
ga: Tsobii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛyeɔ oya, ni amɛmli protein kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ wa, amɛgbi, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa.

english: Why are the first two weeks after my seeds sprout so critical for their survival?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha amɛwala lɛ?

english: During the first two weeks, seedlings develop their initial roots and leaves; because these parts are so delicate, any drought, intense heat, or weed competition can easily kill the young plant.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ baajie eklɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi kɛ baai. Akɛni fãi nɛɛ waaa kwraa hewɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo jwɛi akaŋshii baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii lɛ mlɛo.

english: How often should I water my newly sprouted crops during their first two weeks?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mitsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: Newly sprouted crops need consistent moisture during their first two weeks, so light watering every day or two keeps the topsoil from drying out while tender roots establish.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo ni oooha daa gbi loo gbii enyɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akagbi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛma shi lɛ.

english: Why does feeding my young crops organic manure early make them yield better later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ mra lɛ? Ebaaha nifeemɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Early feeding gives seedlings immediate nutrients to build deep roots and sturdy stems, forming a strong foundation that supports heavy grain or fruit production later.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Haa dumɔwui lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Ebafeɔ shishitoo ni wa ni fiɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai babaoo ni baa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the right seeds from my harvest to grow good plants in the next generation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni sa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛwo tsei kpakpai ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Collect seeds from your healthiest mother plants that produced the biggest and best yields, as those strong traits will naturally carry over into the next planting season.
ga: Buamɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ fɔlɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii wuji ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ yaa shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I separate young suckers from the main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala tsei bibii kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli?

english: Separating young suckers stops them from stealing sunlight and soil nutrients from the parent tree, allowing both the mother plant and the new sucker to grow larger crops.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii lɛ amli gbalamɔ haaa amɛju hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsei wuji.

english: How do wild bush plants left on my fallow farmland improve the soil for future crops?
ga: Te koo mli tsei ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Wild plants draw deep soil minerals to the surface through their roots; when you clear them and let their leaves decay, they turn into rich natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Koo mli tsei gbalaa shika tsuru ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ojie lɛ ni oha ebaai lɛ fite Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I just plant the maize grains I buy from the local market as seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ akɛ dumɔwui?

english: Market grain is meant for eating and often carries diseases or produces weak crops. Certified planting seeds are specially treated and bred to produce strong, uniform, and high-yielding crops.
ga: Afee ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ koni adesai aye ni bei pii lɛ, ekɛ helai baa loo ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Akwɛɔ tsei dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni wa, ni yaa nɔ daa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow unevenly even when I plant all the seeds on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Using uncertified seeds or seeds saved from old harvests leads to uneven growth because the seeds have different strength levels. Good quality seeds germinate at the same rate and grow evenly.
ga: Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli loo dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee aba ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli ni amɛbaadara pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What actually happens to my maize if I cannot get fertilizer to apply to it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mawo mli ŋmãa?

english: Without fertilizer, crops quickly drain the natural food in the soil, leading to yellowish leaves, short plants, and small cobs with missing grains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni egbɔjɔ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for help showing the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food needed to build healthy green leaves and stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji bolɔmɔ ni akɛbiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Crops need fertilizer most when they are young and developing fast, and again just before they start producing flowers or ears of corn.
ga: Tsei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii fe fɛɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii ni amɛmiiya hiɛ oya lɛ. Ni ekoŋŋ dani fɔfɔi loo ŋmãa toi lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ.

english: Why are my plants growing very tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ miida ni efee mlɛo yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they stretch upward to fight each other for sunlight, resulting in weak stems that easily fall over in heavy wind.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Ebaakpã ehe koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural way of saving water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun so it doesn't dry out.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your soil before your crops can get them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná.

english: Is it better for me to plant a small farm with proper fertilizer or a big farm without any fertilizer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔ agbo ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli kwraa?

english: A smaller farm with enough fertilizer and proper care almost always yields more food and profit than a large field where crops are hungry and spread out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji bibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ fe ŋmɔji wuji ni hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce a smaller harvest now than it did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Farming the same soil every season without returning nutrients through organic manure or chemical fertilizer slowly starves the land, reducing its strength over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli daa afi ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kuuu sɛɛ kɛbaaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye hɔmɔ fiofio ni ehewalɛ hu baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my pepper leaves after a heavy rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity create a humid environment where fungal diseases spread easily. Water droplets splashing up from the mud carry ground spores onto the leaves, causing leaf spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. kɛ baai lɛ ahe tsɔi baa

english: Why do small caterpillars hide and eat inside the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft inner whorl of maize leaves where it is moist. Detecting them early allows you to apply recommended pest control treatments before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need shade from surrounding trees or crops like plantain to hold moisture and keep them cool during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetable crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot sun causes the water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots. Furthermore, water droplets left on leaves can focus sunlight and cause heat stress or leaf burn.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la lɛ afee ekome ni ekɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops on my small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mihe bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close causes overcrowding, forcing the plants to fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems and lower overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ kɛteke nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei wuɔ koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Weeds have strong root systems that grow faster than your crops, stealing the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants before the crops get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them unharvested for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni akpaaa lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots reach full maturity, wet soil conditions and underground pests begin to break down the roots, causing rot and loss of quality if left in the ground past their ideal harvest window.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baabɔi shishifãi lɛ afitemɔ. Ehaa fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛteke ŋmaakpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and can dry up easily. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings shade and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ.

english: Which direction should I point cassava stem cuttings when I push them into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the small buds or 'eyes' pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots will waste energy trying to grow around the stem to reach the sun, resulting in weak plants and fewer cassava roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ Shoots lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni obɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda yɛ amɛhe lɛ. tso lɛ mli koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmei shishifãi fioo pɛ baa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. Maize takes food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top when nitrogen levels in the soil are low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Abɛi kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛyeɔ ŋwɛi baa heei beni sũ mli nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves out in the air to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent rot and allows the plant to catch enough sunlight to produce big, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Atomɔ tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkafite ni ehaa tso lɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up into small balls and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. When the leaves curl, the plant cannot trap sunlight properly, which stops the tomatoes from growing large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi tomatoi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through the leaves of my cabbages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on cabbage leaves, which hatch into green caterpillars that feed on the fresh, tender leaf centers. Checking under the leaves early and applying safe neem-based sprays can stop them before they ruin the cabbage head.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. on cabbage leaves Enɛɛmɛi fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli ni yeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite kaaba yitsei lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as very hot sunny days without enough soil water, or too much fertilizer. Consistent watering during hot periods helps the plant keep its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ gbi ni edɔ waa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil richer for other crops later?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpea plants have special tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the cowpea plant dies after harvest, that stored nutrient stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ bɔɔt bibii. Tsei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsina tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut away the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stalk, they all fight for the same water and food in the soil. Keeping only one main plant and one small shoot ensures the main plant grows strong enough to yield a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii akwɛmɔ Tso titri kome baaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ená hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo aba.

english: Why do I need to trim old dead leaves and clean around the base of my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai momoi ni mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning dead oil palm leaves clears the path for insects that carry pollen from flower to flower, helping fruit clusters form better, while also preventing harmful pests from nesting close to the trunk.
ga: Oil palm tso lɛ baai ni egboi lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha kooloi ni hiɛɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ ahe ajɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai akui ni feɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara hu anaa koni amɛkafee amɛshĩai yɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ masɛi.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the rain season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains before planting. Sowing seeds after the very first light rain is risky because if a dry spell follows, the sprouted seeds will dry up and die in the soil.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa dani okɛdu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need plenty of direct sunlight to make food that feeds the tuber growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground catches more light, improves airflow, and prevents leaves from rotting on the hot soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha la babaoo aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil is running out of nitrogen. The corn plant copes by pulling nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves and sending it to support the fresh green leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsuɔ enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ koni eye ebua baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with maize in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil, helping the maize grow strong without relying entirely on costly fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaaye nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmãa ni jara wa nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the sun, traps moisture so crops don't dry out quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and turns into free plant food as it rots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la shishi. Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii akagbi oya Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ebafeɔ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛji egbo

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and shrivel up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet, humid weather. When rainwater settles on cocoa pods without drying off, the fungus penetrates the pod and destroys the beans inside.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ nu nɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni egbiko lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the top leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from under the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Inspecting the undersides of leaves early helps catch these pests before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishi loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: After about 12 to 15 months, cassava stops storing starch and begins converting its energy into tough plant fibers. Harvesting on time ensures the roots stay soft and easy to process into gari or fufu.
ga: Yɛ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei kpaɔ ŋmeii ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ ni ebɔi hewalɛ tsakemɔ ewoɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa amli. Kɛ́ akpa shishifãi lɛ yɛ be naa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaanyɛ afee amɛ kari loo fufu.

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, drought, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil damp and providing partial shade during very hot weather helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Which shoots should I cut off from my main plantain tree to get larger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli koni maná ŋmeii agbo?

english: You should remove thin, weak shoots called 'water suckers' and leave only one or two strong 'maiden suckers' with broad leaves. This stops the extra suckers from stealing water and nutrients away from the main fruiting tree.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ ‘nu ŋmeii’ lɛ ni oshi ‘ŋmei’ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to grow green and leafy, so applying urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the maize turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ baai. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps fix nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, scorching sunlight in their first two years. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates a shield that protects the tender seedlings from heat and keeps moisture in the ground.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shãa amɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily push out of the ground and fall over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have very shallow root systems. If tiny pests called nematodes weaken the roots underground, or if the soil gets too waterlogged, the roots can no longer hold the weight of the tree against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso lɛ muji lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the days get extremely hot, when there is too little water in the soil, or when insects are not visiting to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing gentle shade can prevent this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Be mli ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo baanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. These insects suck the plant's sap and can pass along plant viruses, so managing insects early prevents the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu kooloi ahe nii mra. Ebaatsi curling naa.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings suddenly rot and fall over right at the soil surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ Mine lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as damping-off, which happens when soil fungi attack weak seedling stems. It mostly occurs when seedbeds are kept too wet, overcrowded, or don't get enough sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ dampening, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutua dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baa mli babaoo kɛ́ he ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi, loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɛɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if heavy rains continue late into the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tee nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain stays in the soil for too long, air cannot reach the roots. The excess water causes underground fungi and bacteria to multiply, which rots the cassava tubers before harvest.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to reach maximum sunlight so they can make food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, preventing foliage diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ koni akɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: How do I know if it is safe to plant my seeds when the early rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: The very first rains after a dry season can be misleading; if you plant immediately, a dry spell might follow and destroy the germinating seeds. It is safest to wait until the top layer of soil remains consistently moist for several consecutive days.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dry magic baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni efite dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: How deep should I put seeds into the ground when sowing so they sprout properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Seeds need the right planting depth to sprout. If buried too deep, the young plant exhausts its energy before reaching sunlight, but if planted too shallow, birds will eat the seeds or the sun will dry them out.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Shi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Okpoi baaye dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, hulu la lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my crops turn out small and weak when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil, which prevents any of them from reaching their full, healthy size.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to sow my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them all over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sowing in rows ensures every plant gets equal space to grow and makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm, clear weeds, and apply fertilizer without damaging the crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ ooonyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, okɛ jwɛi awo mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni ofiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I saved from my previous harvest will actually grow before I sow them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu amɛ?

english: You can test seed viability by placing a small sample in a cup of water. Solid, healthy seeds usually sink to the bottom, while seeds that float are hollow or damaged and will not sprout.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shi aha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko ni okɛaawo nu kɔɔpoo mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ baafee ŋmeii loo amɛbaafite ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has good soil for growing crops or if the land is ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mikwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ miifite?

english: Good soil is dark, soft, and holds water well for plant roots. Soil that has been damaged by heavy digging, chemical runoff, or land destruction turns hard, loses its nutrients, and cannot support crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa tsei shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ ni tsofai ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni hoɔ babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings turn yellow and stop growing shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow seedlings are usually a signal that the crop is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that too much standing water is choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye dumɔwui kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to clear and loosen the topsoil before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafo mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the ground breaks up hard earth so that fragile young roots can easily push downward to find water and anchor the plant firmly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ anyɛ ashɛre shi kɛya shi koni amɛyatao nu ni amɛfi tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Should I water my soil immediately after sowing seeds or wait until I see green shoots?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji midu nii loo mamɛ kɛyashi mana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Seeds require moisture right away to wake up and begin the sprouting process, so the soil needs to be damp immediately after you sow them.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛte shi ni amɛje kwɛ̃mɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛji odu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How long does it typically take for crop seeds like maize to sprout above the ground after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Under good conditions with warm soil and sufficient water, healthy cereal seeds like maize will germinate and show green shoots above the ground within 4 to 7 days.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaná ŋmeii eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli.

english: Why do some delicate crop seeds need to start in a nursery before being moved to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aje dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ajie kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certain seeds produce very small, fragile seedlings that need extra shade, careful watering, and protection from harsh weather and pests until they grow strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi woɔ dumɔwui bibii, ni waaa ni biɔ hulutsoo babaoo. Nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Maize seeds require both sufficient moisture and loose, warm soil to germinate. If planted too deep or during a dry spell, germination will be delayed or the seeds may dry out completely.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahe sɛɛ loo dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my yam leaves curl up and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves curl during the hottest hours to minimize surface area exposed to the sun, reducing water loss through evaporation as a natural defense against heat.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni atsi adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ naa

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves begin turning yellow and dry up, and the inside of pulled sample pods turns dark with fully developed seeds.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni sample pods ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔ duŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ.

english: Will my crops produce more harvest if I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting too close forces plants to fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak crops with smaller overall yields compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ afata ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ shishi?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant roots and tissue; it should be applied in a ring or line a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai amli ni kɛ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants have ragged holes and tiny black dirt on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji diji bibii ni akɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing whorl of the plant and feed on young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-borne fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet conditions with excess shade and low airflow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ nu mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds lower leaves when it lacks nitrogen or experiences drought stress, dropping older foliage to preserve water and energy for the root tubers.
ga: Cassava baafite kɛji nitrogen bɛ ehe loo ekɛ hɔmɔ haomɔ kpe. Ekɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when day or night temperatures are too high, or when there is insufficient moisture, preventing successful pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Haa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ pollination awo mli

english: Why should I leave old plant stalks on my field instead of burning everything clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei akutsei momo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ehe tse lɛ?

english: Leaving old crop stalks on your soil acts like a natural cover that holds in water, keeps the ground cool, and slowly rots to feed your soil with valuable nutrients for the next planting season.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni egbɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away all the rich black soil on my sloped farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miiho shikpɔŋ diŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain falls on bare ground on a slope, water rushes downhill and drags topsoil with it. Planting crops across the slope or planting grass barriers slows the water down and protects your good soil.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu baatsɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛbaagbala shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni ooodu yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ loo jwɛi ni ooodu akɛ gbɛtsii nii lɛ baaha nu lɛ aba shi ni ebaabu oshikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are starving for essential plant nutrients like nitrogen or are stressed by water issues. Without proper nutrients, leaves lose green color and cannot make food to grow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu he naagbai miihao amɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni sa bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Because space is tight, every plant ends up weak instead of strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ejaakɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa No hewɔ lɛ tso fɛɛ tso bafeɔ gbɔjɔmɔ yɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too hot or don't get enough water. The plant panics under heat stress and drops flowers to conserve energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei sheɔ gbeyei yɛ dɔlɛ shishi ni amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛha wala.

english: Why do pests attack my fresh crops quickly if I leave old diseased plants in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ oya kɛji mishi tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bugs and plant diseases live and hide inside old infected stalks. If you leave old sick plants lying around, the pests simply move straight onto your new young crops.
ga: Kplukai kɛ tsei ahe helai hiɔ shi ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tsei akui momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji oshi tsei momo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛkã shi lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baafã tɛ̃ɛ kɛya odumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds sprout so much faster than my crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and sleep in the soil waiting for a tiny drop of rain. Once water hits them, they wake up faster than farm crops and steal water and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛmiimɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko. Kɛ nu tswa amɛ Amɛteɔ shi oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni ajuɔ

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive heat?
ga: Mulching around Te jwɛi ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Placing dry grass around the base of plants acts like a blanket over the soil. It traps water in the ground, prevents the hot sun from drying out roots, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Can I cut cassava stems and plant them straight into dry ground before rain starts?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ ŋmei tso ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Cassava stems need moist soil to push out new roots. If you plant stems in totally dry earth during hot weather, the stems will dry out and die before the rains come.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛtsi shishifãi heei kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ odu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or a nitrogen-based fertilizer helps restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome daa be ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: You should wait until the first few major rains have thoroughly soaked the soil deep down, rather than planting after the very first light shower, so the seeds have enough stable moisture to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi wuji fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops, like plantains, planted nearby to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When water sits in the soil without draining, it prevents air from reaching the roots, causing fungal rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha ŋmei lɛ agbo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes small insects to eat holes in my vegetable leaves, and how does it hurt my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te ebaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pests feed on leaves to get moisture and food, which weakens the plant because it uses leaves to make its own food from sunlight. Catching them early with proper pest control protects your yield.
ga: Kooloi yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ beni ekɛ baai lɛ feɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛji okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni obu onibii ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops can. Removing them early stops them from starving your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hɔmɔ akaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Watering deeply at the root zone helps them survive the heat.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ he okadii baa Nu ni awoɔ amɛ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How do I store my harvested maize safely so insects don't destroy it before I can sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Enɛ ji koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Maize must be dried completely in the sun until hard before storing in clean, airtight bags or silos to prevent weevils and mold from spoiling the grains.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛwo kotokui loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I make sure I get a good price and recover the money I spent on seeds and fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná jara kpakpa ni maná shika ni mifite yɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: To get a good return on investment, plan your harvest timing to avoid peak glut periods when market prices drop, and dry or process your harvest so it can be stored until prices rise.
ga: Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ nɔ nyɔmɔwoo kpakpa nɔ lɛ, too okpamɔ be lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni okpa be ni niyenii babaoo baa shi beni jara nɔ jara baa shi lɛ. ni agbiɔ loo atsuɔ he nii koni anyɛ akɛto kɛyashi be mli ni amɛjara baaya hiɛ.

english: Why should I split my fertilizer application into two or three small doses instead of applying it all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mi-fertilizer ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli bibii enyɔ loo etɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ fɛɛ baawo mli shikome lɛ

english: Crops take up nutrients gradually as they grow. Applying fertilizer in small split doses ensures the plants get a steady supply of energy when needed, without losing excess nutrients to heavy rainfall washing them away.
ga: Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nibii bibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ ehe miihia. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahewɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted directly under strong sunlight without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni plantains bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside provides living shade, retaining soil moisture and keeping the young cocoa cool until it matures.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi ebaada jogbaŋŋ

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main element crops use to build green foliage and produce energy for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost restores healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji nɔ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛhaa hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Planting cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each stem enough space under the soil to develop large tuber roots without competing with neighboring plants for sunlight, water, and nutrients.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops grow so small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha mi-vegetables lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them early leaves all the soil energy and moisture for your vegetables to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi koni o-vegetables lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme dry heat, lack of water, or uneven nutrients. Keeping soil moisture steady helps flowers convert into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi waa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ kpe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with plant material acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeping roots cool and preventing the sun from drying out the soil too quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ tsei ahe nibii woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa hulu la ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap and juice out of the leaves. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛmiɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally rebuilds nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake amɛ lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers store energy to survive dry periods. After a natural resting phase, internal signals tell the yam that it is time to grow again, causing sprouts to form in search of light and soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ toɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be sɛɛ Mligbɛ okadii tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda ekoŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmeii taoɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do crops grow so well in regions like Asante, but struggle in the soil in my own town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai tamɔ Asante nɔ shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mimaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil fertility varies across regions due to differences in natural forest cover, rainfall, and leaf decay. Forest regions like Asante often have thick, dark topsoil packed with natural nutrients, while drier or continuously farmed areas have thinner, less fertile soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa nɔ. Enɛ jɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kooi amli hei, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kooi amli hei tamɔ Asante lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee ni ehiii kwraa.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is fertile enough for farming before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli dani mabɔi nidumɔ?

english: Fertile land usually has dark, rich topsoil that holds moisture well and breaks apart easily in your hands. You can also tell by looking at the wild vegetation; land with tall, leafy green plants and broadleaf weeds typically has good soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni baa nii lɛ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsei eŋɔli ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa.

english: Is it true that clearing virgin forest land gives better yields than using old farmland?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe blema okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Yes, virgin forest land has accumulated thick layers of natural compost from fallen leaves over many years without being farmed, making it naturally rich in plant food compared to old farmland that has lost nutrients.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔshiimɔ koo lɛ ebua adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ baai ni egbee shi ni akwɛko nɔ afii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ he ni tsei niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ akɛto blema okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nii efite lɛ he.

english: Why do certain major crops like cocoa thrive in specific regions of Ghana instead of growing well everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni he hiaa tamɔ kookoo yɛ Ghana kpokpai komɛi anɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e waa saminya ngɛ he tsuaa he.

english: Crops need a specific combination of soil nutrients, rainfall pattern, and climate to thrive. Cocoa needs deep, nutrient-rich soil, high humidity, and stable rainfall, which are naturally present in forest zones but absent in drier regions.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ Cocoa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. hulutsoo be ni nɔ kwɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni yɔɔ kooi amli hei shi jeee hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to ask local elders about the history of a piece of land before I farm it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabi maŋ lɛ mli onukpai lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yinɔsane dani matsu he nii lɛ?

english: Elders know the history of the land, including how heavily it was farmed in the past, whether it gets flooded during heavy rains, and which specific crops failed or succeeded on that soil before.
ga: Onukpai lɛ le shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yinɔsane. ni bɔ ni okwaayeli lɛ mli wa ha yɛ Nu Afua ni eho lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ tsei ni egbo loo eye omanye yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani eba lɛ fata he.

english: Why do my maize crops grow well during the first year on new land but give lower yields in the second and third years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ kɛ etɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every time they grow and get harvested. If you do not add nutrients back using manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil gradually loses its food supply, leading to lower yields each year.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni abaakpa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ, fiofio lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients, particularly nitrogen, which plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost around the crop roots will feed the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni fiteɔ lɛ baawo Tse lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: What can I do to improve poor, sandy soil so that my crops can grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mafee shikpɔŋ ni ŋã bɛ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara babaoo?

english: You can improve poor soil by mixing in organic materials like poultry manure, compost, or dry leaves. These materials feed the soil, help it hold onto water longer, and release steady food for your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi afɔfɔi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egboi ni okɛbaafutu mli lɛ nɔ. Akɛ nibii nɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni ojie niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my farmland while my crops grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are adapted to surviving in poor soil with very little water. Farm crops are more sensitive and require nutrient-rich soil and space without competition to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ nu fioo nɔ. Okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he hiaa waa ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ he ko ni akaŋshii bɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the fertility of the soil on my farm?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away the top layer of dirt where all the nutrients are kept, a process called soil erosion. Rain can also wash nutrients deep into the ground beyond the reach of your crop roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, ni ji niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi. Nugbɔ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni tso shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build strong leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when water sits on the farm without draining properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ehi ŋmɔ ko mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot weather, dry soil, or receiving too much fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The disease prevents the leaves from trapping sunlight to make food, which leads to very small cassava roots.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji ŋmɔlɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Hela nɛɛ ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ haaa baai lɛ aná hulu la kɛha niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa.

english: Why do tiny holes appear in my harvested maize grains after storing them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli beni mikɛto kotokui amli sɛɛ?

english: Those holes are eaten by grain weevils, which are tiny insects that lay eggs inside the corn. If maize is not dried completely before storage or not stored in airtight containers, weevil eggs hatch and the young insects feed on the grain.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii, ni ji kooloi bibii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ yeɔ nakai bu lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo akɛtooo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same farm as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn and die under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop a dark, rotten patch on the bottom end while still on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when soil moisture changes wildly from very dry to very wet, preventing the roots from taking up calcium evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium daa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin, making them fall over during light wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe efee mlɛo bɔ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight and stretch upward too fast. This creates tall, weak stems that easily break or fall over when rain or wind hits the farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaagbala amɛhe oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants have plenty of green leaves but very few groundnuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they send pegs down into the ground to form nuts. If the soil is hard or compacted, these pegs cannot push into the earth, so the plant grows leaves above ground but produces few nuts below.
ga: Beni amɛfee ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Amɛtsuɔ ŋmeii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and dry up toward the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and dry up, it is a natural sign that the crop has finished growing. The vine moves all its stored energy down into the root tuber, signaling to the farmer that the yam is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃. Wein tso lɛ tsiɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kɛyaa shishifã lɛ shishi. Koni akɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my okro plants stop bringing out new flowers when I leave old okro pods on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei feemɔ kɛ́ mishi okra ŋmɔji momo lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: An okro plant produces fruit to make mature seeds. When old pods are left to dry on the stem, the plant thinks its job is done and stops making new flowers. Picking young pods regularly forces the plant to keep flowering and producing.
ga: Okra tso lɛ baawo yibii koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni eda lɛ aba. Kɛji ashi ŋmeii momo lɛ ni amɛgbi lɛ Tso lɛ baasusu akɛ egbe enitsumɔ lɛ naa ni ebaakpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantain bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide necessary shade and cool shade cover, acting like living umbrellas that protect the delicate young cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves available nitrogen to its upper leaves to support new growth, leaving the older, lower leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua dalɛ hee. Ha baai ni edara kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my pepper plant growth stay small and stunted even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth often happens when soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus, which helps roots grow deep, or when the soil is packed too hard for roots to spread out and take up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛŋɔ nu.

english: Leaf curling with yellow patches on cassava is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. It is caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck the sap from the green leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai eŋɔli amli lɛ

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy weather when air cannot flow freely through overgrown branches.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei niji ni edara fe nine lɛ amli oya lɛ

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers keep falling off without growing into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face heat stress, extreme dry periods, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to produce leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Early drying of yam vines usually occurs when foliage diseases like leaf spot attack the leaves, cutting off the leaf-made food supply needed to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbimɔ oya baa kɛji akɛ baai helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ tutua baai lɛ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛ baai ni he hiaa koni akɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my neighbors tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer that the maize can feed on.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily blow down during heavy rainstorms before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that grow near the top of the soil. When the bunch grows heavy, strong winds easily tip the tree over if the roots are shallow or damaged by microscopic worms called nematodes.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa tsei lɛ shi mlɛo kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ efite amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of afternoon heat or because of a root disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ hewɔ loo shishifãi ahe hela hewɔ?

english: If crops wilt during the hot sun but recover fresh green leaves by the cool morning, it is heat stress. If they remain wilted and drooping early in the morning, their roots are damaged or diseased.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Shi onine shɛɔ baai eŋɔli heei anɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ. No ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Kɛji amɛgbi lolo ni amɛgbee shi leebi lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ efite loo hela emɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before the whole farm dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ gbo?

english: Check your trees regularly for leaves turning yellow, dark spots forming on pods, or individual branches drying up. Catching these early signs allows you to treat the specific tree before the disease spreads across your farm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli daa koni ona kɛji baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ loo aniji aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ egbi? Kɛ́ omɔ mra be mli okadii nɛɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are some branches on my cocoa trees drying up and dying while the rest of the tree looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egboi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by fungal infections or pests attacking specific pathways inside the branch. When infected, the branch loses its ability to move water and food, causing that specific part to die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Beni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ Niji lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii kɛya he kroko. ha nakai fã lɛ agbo

english: What simple steps can I take to stop diseases from attacking my cocoa farm in the first place?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni helai akatutua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ?

english: Keep your farm clear of weeds, prune overgrown branches to let in light and fresh air, and immediately remove and bury sick or rotten cocoa pods so fungal spores cannot build up.
ga: Ha jwɛi akafee oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kpãa tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ amli koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu. Enɛ ji koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Can diseases spread to my cocoa farm from a neighbor's farm?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ ajɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli egbɛ eshwa mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, fungal spores and pests travel easily between farms through wind, rain splashes, insects, or even on dirty farm tools carried from one field to another.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fãa gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee po ni akɛyaa ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.
