english: If I see a dead or sick part on my cocoa tree, how should I apply medicine to treat it?
ga: Kɛji mina fãi ni egbo loo hela yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofa atsa lɛ?

english: First, cut off the dead or infected part with a clean cutlass or pruning tool slightly below the damaged area. Then, spray an approved fungicide on the wound and surrounding branches to protect the tree from further infection.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, okɛ tsɔne ni he tse loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ afo hei ni egbo loo hela lɛ emɔ lɛ yɛ he ni efite lɛ shishi fioo. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ pilamɔ lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ebɔle he lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ helai krokomɛi ahe.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray medicine on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaafɔ cacao tsei anɔ?

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool and calm. This stops the medicine from drying out too fast in the heat or getting washed away by heavy afternoon rains.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ dioo lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ latsaa be mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shwane mli lɛ akafɔ̃ lɛ.

english: Should I spray medicine on all my cocoa trees or only the ones that look sick?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse kookoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ loo nɔ ni tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: You should treat the sick trees directly, but also spray a protective coating on the healthy trees right next to them. Fungal spores are invisible and often spread to nearby healthy trees before you can see symptoms.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi esa akɛ afɔse nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he hu yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Anaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ, ni bei pii lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli dani onaa hela lɛ he okadii.

english: Is it better to cut down a dying cocoa tree or try to cure it with medicine?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofo cacao tso ni miigbo loo ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ tsofa atsa lɛ?

english: It depends on the disease. Viral infections like Cocoa Swollen Shoot cannot be cured and require cutting down the tree, whereas fungal diseases like Black Pod can be cured by trimming infected parts and spraying fungicide.
ga: Edamɔ hela lɛ nɔ. Anyɛɛɛ atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ ni ehe miihia ni afo tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Pod kɛtsɔ he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ ni afolɔ mli ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Cutting off infected pods immediately and keeping the farm pruned reduces the moisture that feeds the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I clean my cutlass after cutting off sick cocoa branches so I don't pass the disease to healthy trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ mi-knife lɛ he beni mifo kookoo niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ? Bɔni afee ni helai akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli?

english: Wipe or dip your tool in a mixture of bleach and water, soap, or rubbing alcohol after cutting sick branches. This kills any invisible spores on the blade before you cut healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Tsumɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe loo okɛwo bleach kɛ nu, samla, loo dãa ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli beni ofo tsei niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baagbe ŋmeii ni anaaa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ dani ofolɔ cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds produce very small, delicate seedlings that can easily get washed away by heavy rains or eaten by insects. A nursery allows you to shade, water, and protect them until they are strong enough to survive in the main farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ baawo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye lɛ mlɛo He ko ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ amɛhe woɔ hulutsoo mli, okɛ nu haa amɛ, ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die so quickly if I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ? Kɛji mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving large shade trees creates a cooler environment with high humidity that keeps the young plants safe.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it discards its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miiye amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay alive even when the dry season lasts for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food deep underground in its thick roots. During dry spells, it sheds its leaves to reduce water loss, entering a resting state until the rains return.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Eshwieɔ baai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni obote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize prioritizes new growth, so it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi sumɔɔ dalɛ hee. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say that planting cowpeas helps the next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have small nodules on their roots containing beneficial bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes grow huge bushy leaves but produce very small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When sweet potatoes get too much nitrogen fertilizer or very rich soil, the plant puts all its energy into making leafy branches above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛwo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil swings between very dry and soaked.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ miihoso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Why do harvested peppers spoil so much faster than harvested yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ?

english: Peppers have thin skins and high water content, making them soft and quick to decay under tropical heat. Yams have thick, woody skins and enter a dormant state after harvest, allowing them to store water and resist rot for months.
ga: Chili ŋmeii yɛ hewolo ni mli tseee, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Sweet potatoes yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ fitemɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do plantain trees snap and fall over easily during strong rains compared to mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ akɛto mango tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are not made of hard wood; they consist of soft, tightly wrapped water-filled leaf sheaths. Because their shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy, strong wind easily uproots or breaks them.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni wa fee plantain tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ mli ji tsɔji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ. Akɛni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tsii baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ loo akumɔ amɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, strong sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is mature enough to tolerate sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very thin and woody even after growing for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee tsei eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ ekwɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil and enough space to expand. If you plant stems too close together or in hard, unploughed ground, the roots cannot swell into thick, starchy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa Kɛji odu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere ni amɛfee bulb ni mli edɔ ni starch yɔɔ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight helps the leaves make food, which then travels down into the ground to build a large, heavy yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds just as the fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when bearing fruit. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy, fork-topped wooden pole gives the plant extra support to hold the heavy fruit until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni etse ehe lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye abua ni ehiɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli kɛyashi kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants have small holes eaten in them with tiny dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ani ayeɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide directly into the center funnel early in the morning or late evening destroys the caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying an appropriate insecticide early helps protect the young shoots from these destructive insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa Ebaabu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the blooms from pests helps the flowers successfully set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ, ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip indicate a shortage of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient maize needs for leafy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the plant base restores healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ebai eŋɔli lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every year when I plant maize on the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen naturally to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my chemical fertilizer on dry soil when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ miishɛ ohe lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in moisture for plant roots to absorb them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil under scorching heat can burn the plant roots and cause the nutrients to evaporate into the air, wasting your money.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ la ni naa wa shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots and stops them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo shwie shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava plant have lots of green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or if cassava stems are planted upside down, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves on top instead of storing food in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu ŋmei tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight each other for water and soil food, and their leaves block each other's sunlight. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small corn ears.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa baa.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow into strong plants while others stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida ni amɛmiitsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Suckers with narrow, blade-like leaves (called sword suckers) have stronger underground roots and produce heavy bunches, whereas suckers with broad leaves early on lack the root strength to grow big.
ga: Sucker ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ ŋmei. (ni atsɛɔ amɛ sword suckers) lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛdaraa yɛ kui wuji amli. Yɛ be mli ni suckers ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Shishifãi hewalɛ ni bɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the heat gets too intense or when the soil dries out completely. The plant drops its flowers to save water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up or droop in the middle of the day even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. They temporarily wilt to shrink their surface area and save water, usually bouncing back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsi amɛhe yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛye amɛbua koni nu akafite. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ kuɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if insects are eating my vegetable leaves or if a sickness is attacking them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloi bibii miiye mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ loo hela mɔ mi?

english: Insects usually leave clear physical marks like chewed edges, holes, or visible slime trails, while diseases cause the leaves to develop yellow spots, brown patches, or powdery dust without actual bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli, bu, loo ŋmeii okadii ni anaa. Be mli ni helai srɔtoi Ebaaha baai lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ. ŋmɔtɔ loo sũ ni ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ ko bɛ he

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally tough and adapted to local soil and weather conditions, so they steal available water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Underground crops like yam signal they are mature when the vines and leaves above ground naturally start turning yellow and drying up, showing that the plant has finished transferring all its energy into the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei, tamɔ sweet potatoes, tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara beni wain tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do seed sellers coat maize and cowpea seeds in dark powder or colorful chemical before selling them to us?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ powda ni tsuɔ loo tsofai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi woɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ dani amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛhaa wɔ lɛ?

english: That dark or colored powder is a protective medicine called seed dressing. It prevents fungi, mold, and soil insects from eating or rotting the seed while it is buried underground, ensuring the seedling sprouts healthy.
ga: Pauda loo su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed dressing. Ehaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ yeɔ loo amɛkafiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers smear dark coal tar or thick paste on tree branches after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ loo mu ni mli ewo muji woɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ beni amɛfo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you cut a branch, it leaves an open wound on the tree. Smearing dark coal tar or pruning paste seals the cut so that rain rot, fungi, and destructive insects cannot enter the stem and make the rest of the tree sick.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso nine Ebaashi ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tar ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ wo he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi pilamɔ lɛ naa bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akabote tso lɛ shishi ni amɛha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ hela aba.

english: Is there a quick chemical spray that can cure a crop disease instantly like malaria medicine cures a person?
ga: Ani tsofa ko yɛ ni ajieɔ oya ni baanyɛ atsa ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ tamɔ bɔ ni atiridii tsofa baanyɛ atsa gbɔmɛi lɛ?

english: Crop sprays can stop active fungal or bacterial infections from spreading, but damaged plant leaves cannot instantly heal. The plant needs time to absorb nutrients and grow fresh, healthy replacement leaves.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Shi anyɛɛɛ atsa tso baai ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Be he miihia tsei koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni baaye amɛ najiaŋ ni yɔɔ ehee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do farmers soak or wash plantain suckers in warm water or liquid chemicals before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ plantain tsei lɛ woɔ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofai ni ji nu mli loo amɛfɔɔ amɛhe dani amɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Soaking plantain suckers cleans off hidden microscopic worms called nematodes and weevil eggs living inside the roots. Cleaning them before planting ensures you do not introduce pests into your fresh field.
ga: Plantains ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes kɛ weevil ŋmeii ni hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. He ni oootsu he nii dani odu lɛ haa okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baaa o-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people mix black charcoal dust or wood ash into the farm soil before planting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ ŋmeii diji loo tso sũ futuɔ sũ mli yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Black charcoal dust and wood ash act like sponges in the soil. They hold onto water and plant food so heavy rains do not wash them away, while also reducing soil sourness (acidity) to help roots grow.
ga: Sũ mli sũ diŋ kɛ tso sũ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Amɛtoɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa shi. (acidity) ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa

english: Why can't I inject chemical medicine directly into the trunk of my tree instead of spraying all the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ tsofai awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trunk injection is sometimes used for large trees, but spraying leaves is usually faster and safer because leaf pores take in liquid medicine and distribute it quickly throughout the whole tree through its sap stream.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsei ashishi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei wuji anɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yaa oya ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ŋɔɔ tsofa ni ji nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ oya kɛtsɔɔ emli nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves drop off during severe heat to save water. Plants lose moisture through their leaves, so shedding them during hot weather helps the plant stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How does spraying chemical liquid on top of plant leaves kill insects that are hiding down near the roots?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Some sprays are 'systemic,' meaning the plant drinks the liquid through its leaves and circulates it inside its sap. When insects bite into any part of the plant, including the roots, they consume the medicine and die.
ga: Spray komɛi ji ‘systemic’, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ tso lɛ fã ko, ni shishifãi lɛ fata he. Amɛbaaye tsofa lɛ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and light green instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant cannot produce its green color, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores its health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does dark manure help crops grow safely, but white chemical fertilizer burns my crops if I put too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe lɛ? Shi tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛŋ lɛ baashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ babaoo fata he.

english: Dark manure releases its nutrients slowly over time, making it gentle on roots. Chemical fertilizer is very concentrated, like concentrated salt; if applied too close or in large amounts, it sucks moisture out of roots and burns the plant.
ga: Manɔ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Ehaa efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa, tamɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli tsɔ loo akɛwo mli babaoo lɛ, ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã tso lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields, but their special traits break down after the first harvest. Replanting saved hybrid seeds usually results in weaker plants and much lower yields compared to fresh seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwu lɛ sui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui heei.

english: What does it mean when a seed is called a 'hybrid', and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni atsɛɔ dumɔwui akɛ ‘hybrid’ lɛ shishi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A hybrid seed is produced by crossing two different strong plant varieties to combine their best traits, such as high yield and disease resistance. They give maximum output, but only for the first generation you plant.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛtsɔ tsei henɔi enyɔ ni wa ni afɔɔ amɛ koni akɛ amɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ afata he. Nibii ni anáa babaoo Shi kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ ni oduɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem weaker and more easily attacked by pests when grown from saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya kɛji akɛ akwɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ?

english: Replanted seeds from hybrid crops lose the strong genetic protection engineered into fresh seeds. As a result, the second-generation plants stress more easily and become more vulnerable to common field pests and diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ fɔmɔ nii ahebuu ni mli wa ni amɛhaa dumɔwui heei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni ji yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ haoɔ amɛhe oya, ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: What will happen if I take stalks or seeds from my harvested crop at home and plant them again?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tso ko ni mikpa yɛ shia lɛ shishifãi loo dumɔwui lɛ du ekoŋŋ?

english: Plants grown from saved harvest material will not perform like the original crop. You will notice uneven growth in your field, weaker plants, and a major drop in total harvest quantity.
ga: Nibii ni adu kɛjɛ ŋmaa nibii ni ahere lɛ amli lɛ efeŋ amɛnii tamɔ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Obaana shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ ba shi waa.

english: Why don't crops grown from saved seeds grow uniformly in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ akwɛɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops pass on a random mixture of traits to their offspring. In the second generation, some plants will grow tall, some short, and many will fail to produce full fruits, leading to an uneven field.
ga: Hybrid tsei jieɔ sui srɔtoi akpo. Yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei komɛi baafee kakadaji, ekomɛi hu baafee kukuji, ni babaoo nyɛŋ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ mɔ yaa hei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee

english: How much crop yield can I lose if I replant saved hybrid seeds instead of buying fresh ones?
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ ayibɔ enyiɛ manyɛ mafite kɛji midu dumɔwui ni akɛto hybrid mli yɛ dumɔwui heei ni mahe lɛ najiaŋ?

english: You can lose a massive portion of your harvest—sometimes up to 70% of your potential yield—because second-generation hybrid seeds lack the vigor and genetic strength of fresh seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofite yibiiwoo babaoo—bei komɛi lɛ, eshɛɔ yibiiwoo ni baanyɛ aba lɛ mlijaa 70—ejaakɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ ni ji hybrid dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yɔɔ dumɔwui heei amli lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from any crop on my farm, or does it depend on the crop type?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo ani edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Traditional or open-pollinated crop varieties can often be saved and replanted, but hybrid varieties must be bought fresh every planting season if you want to get good yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ ato blema tsei srɔtoi loo tsei ni agbele naa lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ. Shi esa akɛ ohe hybrid henɔi lɛ ehee yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ kɛji oosumɔ ni oná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling us to buy new seeds every season instead of using our own saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔhe dumɔwui heei daa be mli yɛ dumɔwui ni wɔ diɛŋtsɛ wɔtoɔ lɛ ni wɔkɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Officers recommend fresh seeds not to make farmers waste money, but because fresh certified seeds guarantee full plant strength, high yields, and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds lose those qualities quickly.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ okwaafoi akafite shika yɛ dumɔwui heei ahe. Shi akɛni dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ, yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ oya.

english: Is it really worth spending money on fresh certified seeds for every planting season?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ abaafite shika yɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he kɛha be fɛɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, because the extra money spent on fresh hybrid seeds is usually recovered through a much larger, healthier harvest, whereas saving money on seeds often leads to poor yields and lost income.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, awoɔ shika kroko ni fata he ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, shika ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii kɛ shika ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: If I want high crop yields all the time, what is the best practice for getting my planting materials?
ga: Kɛji miitao ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo be fɛɛ be Mɛni ji nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa tsei ahe nibii?

english: To maintain consistently high yields every season, you should purchase fresh certified seeds from trusted seed dealers for each planting rather than saving seeds from your previous harvest.
ga: Koni akwɛ nibii ni afee lɛ babaoo nɔ daa be fɛɛ be. Esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahɔ̃ɔlɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ dɛŋ kɛha dumɔ fɛɛ dumɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: How can I make sure my livestock have enough food to eat during the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mikooloi lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can plant dedicated fodder grass on your farm during the rainy season. This gives you a reserved field of nutritious feed that keeps your animals healthy when natural bushes dry up.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu jwɛi ni akɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni haa okooloi lɛ náa hewalɛ beni adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ egbi lɛ.

english: Why should I deliberately plant grass on my farm instead of relying on wild bushes for my animals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijɛɔ mihe miwoɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ koo mli jwɛi anɔ koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Planted fodder grass grows much faster, yields a larger amount of foliage, and contains higher nutrition than wild bush, protecting your animals from starving when the Harmattan dry season hits.
ga: Forage jwɛi ni adu lɛ daa oya kwraa. Ha baai babaoo. ni eyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe koo mli tsei Ye obua ni obu okooloi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What can I do to keep my planted pasture grass green for as long as possible into the dry period?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-prairie jwɛi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni manyɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Applying animal manure to the soil and leaving a good root base when cutting helps the grass retain soil moisture and stay green much longer into the dry months.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli ni ashi shishitoo kpakpa beni afoɔ jwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua jwɛi lɛ ni ehiɛ sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni ehi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I start planting high-yield pasture grass on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi jwɛi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can plant pasture grass easily by burying stem cuttings with healthy joints (nodes) at an angle into moist soil at the start of the rains, where they will quickly shoot out roots and new green leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ prairie jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ fãi ni mli wa (nodes) ni ooofu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be shishijee mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Will pasture grass grow back on its own after I cut it for my animals?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ beni mifolɔ miha mikooloi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, fodder grasses are fast-regrowing plants. As long as you cut them a few inches above the soil level and do not damage the roots, they will shoot up new stems repeatedly after every rain.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, forage jwɛi ji tso ni daa oya. Shii abɔ ni obaafo lɛ inchi fioo ko kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofiteee shishifãi lɛ. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei shii abɔ. Yɛ nugbɔ fɛɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Why does my planted fodder grass turn hard, tall, and woody over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛyeɔ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni kɛlɛ, ni efeɔ tso yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Grass naturally puts its energy into growing hard stalks and seeds as it matures. If you leave it uncut for too long, it loses its soft leaves and becomes harder for your animals to digest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo tsei ni wa kɛ dumɔwui be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji oshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni okɛkpako lɛ, Baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ ni ehaa ewaa ahaa kooloi akɛ amɛaaye amɛ.

english: Can planting grass on my farm help prevent my soil from washing away during heavy rains?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, the dense and tangled root systems of fodder grasses anchor the topsoil tightly, stopping heavy rain from washing away your farm's rich soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ji forage jwɛi lɛ shishifãi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akpa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to let my animals walk directly into the grass field to eat, or should I cut it and bring it to them?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mahã kooloi lɛ anyiɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya kooloi alɛɛhe kɛkɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mafolɔ ni mikɛbahã amɛ?

english: Cutting the grass and bringing it to your animals (cut-and-carry) is better because it stops livestock from trampling the roots, wasting feed, and compacting the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni ooofo ni okɛha okooloi lɛ (Ofolɔ ni otsi) lɛ hi fe no ejaakɛ ehaa kooloi shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, amɛfiteɔ niyenii ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the best height or time to cut the grass for my animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo loo be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mikooloi lɛ ajwɛi lɛ?

english: The best time to cut is when the grass reaches waist height before flowering. At this stage, the leaves are full of vitamins, soft, and easy for the livestock to chew.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo ji be mli ni jwɛi lɛ shɛɔ etsitsi he, dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, baa lɛ eyi kɛ vitamini, eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha kooloi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: How much of my grass field should I cut at one time for feed?
ga: Jwɛi enyiɛ esa akɛ mafo yɛ be kome mli koni mikɛha lɛ niyenii?

english: You should cut only a small portion that your animals can finish in a day or two. This keeps the remaining field fresh and allows the cut portions time to regrow in stages.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ fãi bibii pɛ. ni okooloo lɛ baanyɛ agbe naa yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ afee ehee ni eha ŋmeii lɛ aná be ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why should I clear my farm land without burning the bushes before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni mishãaa jwɛi lɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bushes destroys important soil nutrients, beneficial micro-organisms, and organic matter. Clearing without burning allows dead plants to decompose naturally, enriching the soil and keeping it moist for your crops.
ga: Tsoi ni he tse ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ baaha tsei ni egboi lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that act as living natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa crops the shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I put fertilizer into the soil immediately when planting seeds, or wait until after they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ loo mamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait until 2 to 3 weeks after seeds sprout before applying initial fertilizer. Very young seeds do not have developed roots yet to absorb nutrients, and strong fertilizer put directly on fresh seeds can burn them.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli. Dumɔwui ni darako kwraa lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ lolo. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ni etse. Yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves of maize plants during the day and eat the tender growth, requiring early pest control measures to prevent crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni ato gbɛjianɔi ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insect pests early prevents the virus from spreading across your entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away because the soil loses air and fungi multiply. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni efooo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ faa babaoo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers stay on the plant long enough to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment available in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my yam seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Yam seeds should be planted right after the first major rains when the soil is warm and moist. Soil that is too dry can scorch seed yams, while planting right at the onset of rains encourages rapid root sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water. The plant is not dying; it goes dormant to protect its tubers underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gbooo, eyaa wɔɔhe koni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees experience heat stress and dehydration without shade. Large forest trees protect cocoa from harsh afternoon sun, maintain soil moisture, and create a cooler microclimate needed for heavy flowering and pod growth.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ kookoo tsei amli lɛ bɛ hulutsoo lɛ, amɛkɛ haomɔ kpeɔ. Koo mli tsei wuji buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ pod dalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow starting from the tip in a V shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ V-shape ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early will help the leaves green up again.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels too hot or thirsty, it drops its flowers to save energy for survival rather than spending energy making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ wo mli. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ loo kumai miiye lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines high up off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli ni makwɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy to swell the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and away from soil-borne diseases that thrive in moist shade.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they transmit. The feeding distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from flowering properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Niyenii haa tso lɛ baa lɛ dalɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever strong wind and heavy rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (lodging) when planted too closely together or when roots are weak. Planting at proper distances and mounding soil around the base gives the roots strong support against wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi (amɛjɔɔ amɛhe) kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ni sa ni akɛ sũ toɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bunches on my plantain trees getting smaller every year even though the farm is still the same?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ? Ani ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nakai nɔŋŋ lolo?

english: As plantain plants grow, they produce multiple suckers around the base. If you don't cut extra suckers away, they steal nutrients and water from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara Ebaawo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛji ofolɔko ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers look healthy at first, but then end up full of small worms that destroy the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ebafeɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ni fiteɔ pod lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers attract pod-boring moths that lay eggs right inside the blossoms. As soon as the eggs hatch, the larvae feed on the young developing pods, so protective measures must be taken right at flowering.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa lɛ he nii kɛji amɛfɔ fɔfɔi pɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow well near some farm trees but die or stay small when planted near Eucalyptus trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei komɛi ahe shi amɛgboiɔ loo amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ eucalyptus tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Different trees interact with soil differently. Trees like Eucalyptus draw immense amounts of water from the soil and shed leaves that release chemicals inhibiting other plants, while beneficial trees enrich the soil.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Tsei tamɔ eucalyptus gbalaa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ, ni no jieɔ tsofai ni tsiɔ tsei krokomɛi anaa lɛ kpo. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to make green leaves and grow strong, so adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea can restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of tubers. To get big roots, cassava needs soil rich in potassium, which helps the plant store energy underground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia Cassava, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that likes to hide inside the central leaves of maize plants. Spraying early in the morning or late evening when they come out to feed helps keep them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛ tsofa lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves getting white powdery dust on them and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ hiɛ sũ yɛŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads when the weather is humid and air cannot flow well between plants. Spacing your plants properly and picking off infected leaves helps keep the rest of the farm clean.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli atse.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have a special ability to capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize and keeps your soil healthy for longer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight over water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This causes all the plants to stay small and yield less harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. High heat destroys the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from turning into a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. Tsi enaa koni ekatsɔ tomato.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds away from my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that young cocoa trees desperately need to establish deep roots. Clearing them removes competition so your cocoa can grow faster and healthier.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa diɛŋtsɛ ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ atswa shishifãi lɛ mli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii baa shi bɔni afee ni o-cocoa lɛ anyɛ ada oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of plant leaves much faster than roots can pull water from dry soil. The tree drops its leaves on purpose to reduce water loss and protect itself from dying completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele kwraa he.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture after the first rain for me to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy, steady rains before sowing. Planting after only the very first light rain is risky because if the sun stays hot for a few days after, the young germinating seeds will dry up in the soil and die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ dani odu dumɔwui. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created by crossing two strong parent plants to produce maximum yield. If you replant seeds saved from that harvest, the new plants will lose those special traits, growing unevenly and giving you a much smaller harvest.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ nyɛ tsei enyɔ ni he wa ni akɛfoɔ mli koni ená yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei lɛ baafite nakai sui lɛ. uneven growth Ni ehaa okpaa nii babaoo fioo.

english: Why do I have to keep buying fresh maize seeds from the shop every year instead of saving my own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ obaahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli daa afi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaakpa?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds only give their best strength and highest yield in their very first generation. Buying certified fresh seeds every season guarantees that all your plants grow uniform, resist diseases, and give you heavy cobs.
ga: Jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baaha hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be lɛ haa otsei lɛ fɛɛ daa daa. Enyɛɔ helai ahe ni ewoɔ cob yibii ni tsii.

english: What is the difference between my local traditional seeds and these hybrid seeds officers talk about?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mimaŋ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ ni onukpai lɛ wieɔ he lɛ ateŋ?

english: Local traditional seeds allow you to save and replant seeds from your farm year after year, but they naturally produce smaller yields. Hybrid seeds give much bigger yields and resist diseases better, but they must be bought fresh every planting season.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli, shishijee dumɔwui lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni okɛduɔ ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi. Shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ. Shi esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei daa be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why did my neighbor's corn crop grow uniform and tall while mine from saved seeds grew with mixed sizes and small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ ni ekwɛɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni minɔ ni jɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni efutu kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Your neighbor planted fresh hybrid seeds which carry uniform, high-energy traits. Saved seeds break down genetically in the second generation, causing some plants to grow tall, others short, and most to bear small cobs.
ga: Okutsoŋnyo lɛ duɔ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ekomɛi feɔ kuku, ni amɛteŋ babaoo woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do some of the seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved at home often suffer hidden damage from weevils, mold, or heat during storage. Certified seeds bought from agro-dealers are treated and quality-tested so almost every single seed sprouts strongly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ naa fitemɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo dɔlɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jalɔi adɛŋ lɛ anɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛhi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu kwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: Why are the new maize seeds I bought coated in bright pink or green powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni mli tse loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ewo ŋmãa hee ni mihe lɛ he lɛ?

english: That colored powder is a protective chemical treatment that stops soil insects, birds, and fungal diseases from attacking or rotting the seed before it gets a chance to grow.
ga: Pigments ji tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛtsi kooloi bibii, okpoi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua loo amɛfite dumɔwui dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How does storing my harvested corn in a warm or damp room ruin its ability to grow as seed?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ baafite nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaatsɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Heat and moisture weaken or kill the tiny living embryo inside the seed, and attract insects like weevils. If the embryo dies inside the grain while in storage, it will rot in the ground instead of growing.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa haa fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo egbeɔ amɛ ni egbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ gbo yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, Lala lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants struggle to grow well if I drop three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds sprout in one small hole, their roots fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. Planting the correct distance apart gives each stalk room to grow thick and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, sũ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu mli tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient in the soil. Feeding the crop with the right fertilizer early gives it the power to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia onibii lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaha tsei mra Ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: If I plant yellow corn next to white corn on my farm, why do I find mixed colored grains on the same cob?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ masɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ minaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sui ni efutu yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants pollinate through the wind carrying dust from the flowers. If two different types are planted close together, dust from the yellow corn will land on the white corn, resulting in cobs with mixed grains.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ woɔ abɛi tsei amli. Kɛji akɛ adu henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, sũ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni mli efutu lɛ feɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves with tiny worms hiding inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ayɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ. Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. The worms feed on young growing leaves inside the central whorl; applying recommended pesticides or organic treatments like neem extract directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up like small cups and turning sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves. They suck out essential plant sap and can spread viruses that stop the plant from flowering properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni haaa tsei lɛ aná fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli edɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight because their leaves are tender. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow at once forces them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing extra shoots so that only two or three healthy ones remain ensures the main stem produces larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Ni aaaha ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ shikome Enɛ baaha amɛwuu kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ashi ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow much bigger tubers underground when I stake them with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji babaoo beni mikɛ tsei kakadaji fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture food. That extra energy is stored underground, resulting in larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. Akɛ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick foliage, but yield tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. High nitrogen encourages leafy growth above ground, whereas potassium is needed to swell the roots into large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa baa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa. Yɛ be mli ni potassium he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to put chemical fertilizer on my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa mli?

english: Fertilizer works best in split doses: apply your first basal fertilizer (like NPK) about one to two weeks after germination to help root development, and top-dress with nitrogen fertilizer (like Urea) four to six weeks after planting when the crop grows rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mlijaa mli: Okɛ shishijee nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli (tamɔ NPK) awo mli aaafee otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ sɛɛ beni eshishifãi lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) awo nɔ yɛ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu tso lɛ beni tso lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants take up moisture before the heat of the day sets in, and any excess water on the leaves dries off quickly, reducing the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ. Ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbi oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why can swamp rice grow in standing water, but my maize turns yellow and dies if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Shi mi ŋmãa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛji nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice roots have special internal air channels that allow oxygen to flow down to the roots even underwater. Maize roots do not have these channels, so standing water drowns the roots and stops them from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ nu shishi po. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight causes their leaves to burn and dries out the soil moisture. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that protects the young trees while they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa. Yɛ be mli ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots and leaves from my cocoa trees if they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree, which stops moisture from building up and spreading fungal diseases. It also ensures the tree directs its food energy into growing big pods instead of just growing leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu koni tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ lɛ amaje ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores the nutrients your crops need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai ni wa aba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield fewer bags of corn every year even when the rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Farming the same piece of land continuously drains the soil of its natural nutrients. Resting the land periodically or rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli loo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it helpful for me to plant cassava together with maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a great strategy because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava takes longer to mature. This allows you to harvest food twice from the same plot of land without wasting space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei heɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ofiteee he ko.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs and a lower total yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa cob lɛ feɔ bibioo ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Removing infected pods right away and keeping the farm clear of overgrown weeds stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni oha jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that your main crops receive all the water and nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni otso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to protect themselves from losing too much water. Providing light shade and watering early in the morning helps the plants keep their blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ha tso lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and turn to dust in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ebatsɔ sũ yɛ nitoohe?

english: Insects like weevils feed on harvested grain if it is stored while still damp or kept in open containers. Thoroughly drying your grain under the sun and storing it in airtight bags protects your harvest from pest damage.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baaye dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsɛnsii ni agbele mli loo awo mli. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for growth. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet for too long, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stems with small tubers instead of thick, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni tsii ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water when it gets hot and dry. However, leaf curling can also be caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu akafite fe nine kɛ́ edɔ ni amɛgbi. Shi kɛlɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ ŋmei loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees around them?
