ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade from larger trees like plantains or forest trees, the sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can establish.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantain loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when plants experience extreme dry spells followed by sudden heavy watering. Excess nitrogen fertilizer can also cause plants to produce flowers that drop instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa bei ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa ni nu ni mli wa trukaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and bend when the soil underground is hard, stony, or compacted. When the growing tip of the tuber hits hard ground, it changes direction to keep growing.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo ebɔle ehe, kɛ kɛ́ tsei niji ni miida lɛ anaagbee lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Ebaatsake gbɛtsɔɔmɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why are white powdery spots appearing on my garden egg leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai anɔ yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew. It spreads quickly when plants are crowded together and air cannot circulate well around the leaves during warm, humid weather.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe. ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cowpea seeds not sprouting after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea seeds usually fail to sprout because the soil is either too dry for germination, planted too deep in the soil, or eaten underground by insects and rotting fungi before they can break through.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cowpea dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃. ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛboteɔ mli.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains kuu lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fruits become plump and full, lose their sharp edges, and the top leaves on the plant start turning yellow.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔ ni eyi obɔ, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ laajeɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my maize right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmã lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are adapted to grow aggressively in local soil. They wake up quickly with rain and take up water and fertilizer faster than young crop roots can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ maŋ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Amɛteɔ shi oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. ni eŋɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their leaves from intense direct sunlight and heat. Without larger trees or plantains nearby to provide shelter, the young cocoa plants dry out and burn before their roots can spread deep enough into the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji tsei wuji loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni akɛbaafee abobaahe ko bɛ lɛ Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa dani amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to lift and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight, which helps the leaves manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases and allowing maximum sunlight to build larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa ni oha hulu la babaoo aba bɔ ni ooonyɛ ni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key food element in the soil. When nitrogen is low or washed away by heavy rain, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick stems but producing only tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are grown too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves to reach light. Because energy is diverted upward, less food is sent down to form large root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛmɔ la lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ajieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. No hewɔ lɛ atsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni efee shishifãi wuji fioo komɛi.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas help my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha shweremɔ be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with friendly soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvested, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish crops like maize planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa tsei lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress or sudden changes in water, such as a long dry spell followed by sudden heavy rain. Stress prevents successful pollination, causing the flower to fall off instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Haomɔ tsiɔ pollination naa. ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii

english: Why do some plantain trees produce small bunches while others produce very large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains komɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ekrokomɛi hu woɔ ŋmeii wuji waa lɛ?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one main plantain plant, they compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away weak suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to build a heavy, healthy plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Dumɔwu titri kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei bibii ni tsii ni wa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close together on the land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and nutrition to grow strong and yield larger, healthier produce.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects, causing distorted and stunted leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ etsakeɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops droop and wilt during hot afternoons even when the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water up from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to protect themselves from water loss, usually bouncing back by evening as temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni nu akafite. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my rice plants turning yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Rice leaves often turn yellow when standing water washes away nitrogen from the soil or prevents the roots from breathing properly, which starves the plant of essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwie nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo etsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why does my rice crop grow very tall with plenty of leaves but produces very few grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ nɛkɛ lɛ? Baai babaoo shi dumɔwui ayitsei fioo?

english: When rice plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of forming grain panicles.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmãa babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ wu tue.

english: Why do some parts of my rice field mature and turn yellow faster than other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Uneven maturity happens when the land is not level, causing water and fertilizer to gather in lower areas while higher spots dry out faster and mature earlier.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ebɔle ehe. Enɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ. yɛ be mli ni hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛhooɔ oya.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my rice so the grains don't fall off on the farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa nii? No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛŋ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the main stems turn golden yellow, and the grains at the base of the head are hard rather than milky.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa yɛ mliki najiaŋ.

english: Why does my rice field dry out so quickly even after I trap water in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu lɛ eto?

english: Sandy soil or cracked clay allows water to drain away fast; building low soil boundaries (bunds) around the field and compacting the soil helps keep water standing long enough for the rice roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo shikpɔŋ sũ mli egbɛ eshwa lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ husu ni baa shi (bundle) ni afee ni bɔleɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa nu hiɔ jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi.

english: Why do my citrus trees drop most of their flowers before any oranges form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani orange lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop flowers when they experience dry spells during flowering or when the soil lacks nutrients like boron and potassium needed to hold the young fruit buds.
ga: Orange tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna be ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ boron kɛ potassium ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi bibii lɛ ahi shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my orange trees curling up and becoming sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are caused by small sap-sucking insects like aphids or mealybugs, which feed on the leaves and leave behind a sugary substance that attracts mold.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my oranges small and sour even when the tree looks full and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: When a citrus tree carries too many fruits at once, it spreads its water and nutrients too thin, resulting in small, sour fruits unless you prune some off early.
ga: Kɛji citrus tso bua aduawai babaoo naa yɛ be kome mli Ebaagbɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashwã tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ daraaa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Ja ofo ekomɛi amli kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Can I plant rice between my young citrus trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, planting rice between young citrus trees works well during the first two years because the young trees are small enough that they will not shade out the rice crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ daraaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster around my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients faster than crop seedlings, so feeding the soil helps the weeds grow rapidly unless you clear them right before fertilizing.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha sũ lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua jwɛi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ja ojie jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a major food plants need to grow. When the plant cannot find enough nitrogen in the soil, it moves what little it has from its older bottom leaves to nourish the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants wilt on hot afternoons even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water out of the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to close their tiny pores and save moisture, usually standing back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛŋa ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ni amɛha nu ahi mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, eteɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rain falls continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave standing water in the farm, the soil becomes waterlogged, suffocating the roots and allowing soil fungal diseases to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee nu. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni amɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: What can I do with all the left-over cocoa pod peels after I remove the fresh beans?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie dumɔwui heei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa peels do not cause any harm on the farm if managed properly. You can leave them to break down naturally into rich compost for the soil, or gather them to produce local black soap and animal feed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii kɛ naagba ko baaa. yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Obaanyɛ oha amɛfite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. aloo abua naa koni akɛfee maŋ lɛ mli Jatropha kɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Is there a specific way I should gather my cocoa beans so I don't ruin them during harvest?
ga: Ani gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mikɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ato koni ekafite yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Gathering cocoa beans is clean and easy when done right. You should open the pods with a blunt wooden mallet instead of a sharp cutlass so you do not cut the fresh beans or make a mess with the pulp.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ he tse ni ebɛ mlɛo kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni mli tseee agbele pod lɛ mli moŋ fe ni okɛ tsɔne ni mli wa baatsu nii. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okafolɔ ŋmeii heei loo okafee basabasa.

english: Why does cocoa farming feel like continuous, stressful work that never ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔ tamɔ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni haa mɔ haoɔ ni bɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa farming requires ongoing tasks like weeding, pruning, and timely harvesting. If you stop doing these tasks even briefly, the work piles up quickly and becomes much more stressful to handle later.
ga: Cocoa okwaayeli biɔ nitsumɔi ni yaa nɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni ato lɛ mli Kɛji okpa nitsumɔi nɛɛ kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli po lɛ, Nitsumɔ lɛ buaa ehe naa oya ni haomɔi babaoo yɛ ni esa akɛ otsu he nii sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to prune extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air through. This stops excess moisture from building up, which reduces black pod disease and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do extension officers insist on tying up and bagging dried cocoa beans tightly before sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ akpɛtɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tying up dried cocoa securely in clean jute sacks prevents moisture, dirt, and insects from getting inside, ensuring the beans stay dry and high quality for the market.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ kookoo ni egbi lɛ fĩ jute kotoku ni mli tse mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ, muji kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ koni kookoo yibii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jarayeli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa beans are fully dry and ready to be put into sacks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ akɛwo baagi mli?

english: Well-dried cocoa beans will crackle when you squeeze a handful together. They should have a rich brown color and low moisture so they do not rot or mold after you tie them up.
ga: Kookoo ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fãa kɛji okɛ onine kome shwie nɔ. Esa akɛ amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa. Enɛ baaha amɛkafite loo amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ beni okɛ amɛ ebɔ he sɛɛ.

english: How do I tell when a cocoa pod on my tree is ready to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie?

english: As cocoa pods mature, their color changes from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange. This color change shows that the beans inside are fully developed and ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwere lɛ Su lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree experiences stress from extreme heat, dry weather, or pest attacks like mirids. Giving the trees moderate shade and proper care helps them retain flowers to form pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi, hulutsoo ni akɛhaa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leafy shades that protect young cocoa trees from heat stress during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baai wuji ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is fermentation an essential step before drying cocoa beans in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni he hiaa waa dani hulu lɛ shɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fermenting wet cocoa beans under banana leaves removes the sweet pulp, kills the seed germ, and develops the chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni mli edɔ yɛ banana baai shishi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. Gbemɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ ni oná tsokolate kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their shallow roots. Leaving a few large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides the shade cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ egbiɔ. Tsei wuji fioo komɛi ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ hu haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying poultry manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the season will help the plant stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-corn lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, giving the neighboring maize plants free nutrients to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa niyenii ni he ehiaaa ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the central shoot of my young maize plants with little black droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu ni etse amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ bibioo ko yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the maize funnel to feed on young leaves. Applying targeted biopesticides or a mixture of clean sand and neem powder into the funnel early in the infestation destroys the worms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo ŋã ni mli tse kɛ neem powda ni akɛfutu mli lɛ wo funnel lɛ mli mra yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eba lɛ, ebaakpata tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that transmit leaf curl viruses. Spraying the underside of the leaves with soapy water or appropriate organic treatments helps clear the insects.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ eshwaa Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high off the ground using tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ atswa mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to feed the tuber underground. Keeping the leaves off the wet soil also prevents fungal leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil food. Leaving only one strong follower sucker allows the main tree to devote its energy to producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa ni ji sucker lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: How does covering the soil around my garden crops with dry grass help them survive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from evaporating moisture out of the earth. It keeps the ground moist for much longer and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and watery if I leave them in the soil after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains start, the cassava plant uses the energy stored in its tuberous roots to grow new green stems and leaves. This drains starch from the roots, making them watery, light, and less sweet.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni eha amɛfee nu, amɛhe ejɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or the soil lacks consistent water, which stresses the plant. Watering your tomatoes deeply at the base and planting shade crops nearby helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Okɛ nu awo tomato mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ ni okɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ adu. Ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stunted when the soil is hard and packed tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyi lɛ obɔ lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard and compact, crop roots cannot spread out or reach deep down to swallow water and nutrients, which causes the leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo amɛbote mli ni amɛmi nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich and ready for planting without using expensive tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni ehi kɛha dumɔ ni akaaa mihe shika babaoo?

english: Good, healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and has earthworms crawling in it.
ga: Okwaafoi ashishi ni hi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ ni kɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender like seedlings and cannot handle full direct sunlight; they need shade from larger trees or plantains to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo tamɔ dumɔwui, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, which weakens the leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their blossoms to preserve their own water and energy instead of feeding new fruits.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas capture invisible natural plant food from the air and store it in the ground, which feeds the neighboring maize plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei aniyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ, he ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots very small even though the leaves on top are bushy and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or get too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize is fully ripe to harvest before the rains spoil it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nikpamɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn dry and brown, and a small black spot forms at the point where the corn grain connects to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ. Cob lɛ egbi ni eyɛ asarasu. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ he ni ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ŋmãa lɛ kpaa gbee yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yams start rotting or producing green shoots soon after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ loo eyɛ ŋmeii eŋɔli beni mikpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest; keeping them in warm, damp, or poorly ventilated places triggers them to sprout or attract fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgbala ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes soften and spoil so quickly when packed in sacks for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui amli koni akɛmaje lɛ?

english: Tomatoes generate heat and continue to ripen after picking; packing them tightly in hot, unventilated sacks causes heat to build up, crushing them and causing rapid decay.
ga: Tomato haa dɔlɛ baa ni eyaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa. Efoɔ oya ni efiteɔ.

english: Why is cocoa considered such an important crop to farm in Ghana compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni esa akɛ adu yɛ Ghana kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa grows exceptionally well in Ghana's tropical climate and rich forest soils. It is a reliable cash crop with a steady demand both locally and internationally, providing farmers with a dependable source of income year after year.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ titri yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ nɔ. Eji shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni abiɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ maŋsɛɛ fɛɛ. Ehaa okwaafoi lɛ náa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, intense sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantains to protect them from heat and help the soil hold moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are flowers growing directly on the main trunk of my cocoa trees instead of on the thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers directly on the thick trunk and main branches. This unique trait gives the tree a sturdy frame capable of supporting the weight of heavy cocoa pods as they develop and mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ amɛniji wuji anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Su nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing near the ground on my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ mi-koko tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, you should prune those extra shoots, often called suckers or chupons. They steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk, which reduces the number of cocoa pods your tree can produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ nakai tsei krokomɛi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ suckers loo suckers. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii ni otso lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why are some of the small cocoa pods on my tree turning shriveled and black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: Small pods can turn black due to natural thinning, where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot support, or because of fungal diseases like black pod disease during wet weather. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and badly diseased pods helps protect the remaining crop.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee ediŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ. aloo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, dark forest soil that drains water easily while remaining moist. If rainwater forms standing pools on your land for days, the soil retains too much water, which can rot cocoa roots.
ga: Cocoa shwereɔ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ fee ŋmeii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod on my tree is fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange. Tapping the pod lightly will also produce a hollow sound, showing that the beans inside have detached from the inner wall.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ otswa pod lɛ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji aba Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejie ehe kɛjɛ mligbɛ gbogbo lɛ he.

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin trees and lower yields. It also creates a damp, crowded environment where diseases spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ hu baa he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Dropping leaves during hot, dry weather is a natural survival response. It reduces the amount of water the tree loses through its leaves, allowing it to conserve moisture until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni tsei shwieɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain and cassava together on the same land with my cocoa?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava. Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-Cocoa lɛ agba he kome?

english: Yes, especially when the cocoa trees are young. Plantains provide useful shade for young cocoa trees, but crops like cassava should be planted with enough space so their roots do not compete directly with cocoa roots for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, titri lɛ beni cacao tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Plantains haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi esa akɛ adu tsei tamɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha kookoo shishifãi kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: If I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land, will they fight for food in the soil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ Ani ebaatswa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ?

english: Maize grows fast and takes nutrients early from the topsoil, while cassava grows slowly at first and feeds deeper later. Planting them together allows them to share the soil nutrients at different times and depths without killing each other.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ edaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ. Hefatalɔi ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ haa amɛjaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli kɛ hei ni mli kwɔ ni amɛgbeee amɛhe.

english: If I plant shade trees in my farm alongside my food crops, won't the tree roots steal all the water from my crops?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, Ani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ejuŋ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Deep-rooted shade trees drink water from far underground, while crops like cocoa or vegetables draw water closer to the surface, so they naturally share the soil without competing for the same water.
ga: Shade tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo aduawai gbalaa nu kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjaraa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ nu kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil better for the maize I plant after them on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ sɛɛ mli yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have special root nodules that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This leaves behind natural fertilizer that nourishes the next crop planted on that plot.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I keep fast-growing plantain trees beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ to amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow broad leaves quickly that act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa the exact shade and moisture needed to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela oya. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the forest trees around them grow too thick and dense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo lɛ? Edaa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: While cocoa needs moderate shade when young, mature cocoa trees still need sunlight to make flowers and pods. When shade trees become too thick, they block out the light and cause pod production to drop.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kookoo biɔ hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ hu he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Ebaatsi la naa ni ebaaha pod feemɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and turn yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight heat is severe and soil water is low, pepper plants curl their leaves to save moisture and prevent sun damage, showing that they need irrigation or temporary shade.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nɔ ni hulu lɛ baanyɛ afite lɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo hulutsoo be kukuoo he miihia amɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop take almost a full year before I can harvest the tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ ni ekɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cassava spends its first few months building strong stems and leaves above ground to gather sunlight energy, and only then uses that energy to swell and grow the roots underneath.
ga: Yucca heɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ ni ekɛmaa tsei ahe tsei kɛ baai ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbua hulu la hewalɛ naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of lying on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekã shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb higher to reach open sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves high and clean, allowing the plant to collect energy to feed the growing yam tubers in the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehe tseɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ buaa hewalɛ naa koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop harvests get smaller every year when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot without rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the topsoil. Rotating different crops or letting the land rest allows the soil to naturally rebuild those depleted nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ Aloo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ama nakai niyenii ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the food crops I carefully plant on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly capture light, space, and soil water under harsh conditions, allowing them to outgrow domestic crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛmɔ la, ŋwɛi, kɛ nu oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya fe shia tsei kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip along the middle vein, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to feed properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛtee amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and heavy rain. Clearing extra shade trees and pruning lower branches helps sunlight dry out the pods and prevent the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Tsei ni afolɔ koni amɛná hulutsoo babaoo kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: You will notice the lower leaves yellowing and dropping off, soil cracking around the stem base, and the crop reaching between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that are often weakened by tiny soil pests like nematodes or stem borers. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, the weak roots cannot anchor the plant in soft, wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips living under the leaves and sucking out plant juice, which can also spread small plant viruses.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala hela lɛ eshwa tsei bibii hu amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too high, when the soil drops too dry, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer encouraging leaf growth over fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ni haa baai lɛ daa fe bɔ ni aduawai lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to collect maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant produce food that goes down to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛbua hulu la babaoo naa bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji shwereɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a big rain comes or after?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer on moist soil after a light rain. If you put it down right before a heavy downpour, the rain will wash the fertilizer away before the plants can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛji okɛto dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves fold up or curl during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants fold or roll their leaves during the hottest part of the day as a natural survival trick to reduce surface area exposed to the sun and save water from escaping.
ga: Tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ebaa lɛ loo efoɔ ehe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he teemɔŋ sane Koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekaje kpo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when the rains start late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen. When dry soil prevents roots from absorbing nutrients properly, the plant cannot get enough food until steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa.

english: Maize takes away nutrients from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, which refreshes the land for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ehee kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to cover them, the heat dries out their leaves and damages their young roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni efite amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When water sits in flooded soil for too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing harmful fungi and bacteria to multiply and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce food that goes down into the earth to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yaa shikpɔŋ koni bulbs lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Curling tomato leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread plant sicknesses, which stops the plant from making normal fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor nutrients, causing it to shed flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛná hewalɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plantain tree, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil, which results in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he lɛ, Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is moist instead of dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in moisture before plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots or leave the nutrient powder wasted on top of the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi loo eshi niyenii mli hewalɛ powda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yields so fast if I do not clear them early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi oya kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly away from your plants, causing your crops to remain small and produce less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does the buyer weigh all my harvested crops together before sorting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ he ekome dani amɛhalaa lɛ?

english: Weighing everything at the beginning gives an accurate record of your total farm harvest weight. Sorting happens afterward so the buyer can determine how much of that total weight belongs to each quality level.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he saji awo mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baaba sɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ nɔ ni shwiili lɛ fɛɛ baafee kɛha shwiili lɛ mli shwiili lɛ eko fɛɛ eko.

english: Why is it better for my produce to be measured on a scale rather than by the bag or bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ sɛkɛl baasusu minibii lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni mikɛ baagi loo baagi baasusu lɛ?

english: A scale measures exact weight fairly regardless of container size. Measuring by bags can be inaccurate because bags can be packed loosely or tightly, leading to unfair pricing for your hard work.
ga: Sɛkɛl lɛ susuɔ tsiimɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni kɔɔɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ dalɛ he. Ekolɛ susumɔi ni akɛ kotokui tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ kotokui awo mli ni etse loo ni etsilɛ. Enɛ haa awoɔ bo nyɔmɔ ni ejaaa yɛ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops weigh less when I take them to the market a few days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi kɛ́ mikɛtee jara nɔ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops naturally lose water and dry out over time through evaporation. As the water evaporates into the air, the physical weight of the crop drops.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Beni nu shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔmɔtsoŋ tsiimɔ baa shi.

english: What does crop grading actually mean when I sell my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ shishi kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔ̃ɔ?

english: Crop grading is the process of inspecting your produce and grouping it into different quality levels based on size, cleanliness, moisture, and freedom from insect damage or disease.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ onibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli ni abua amɛ naa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai srɔtoi amli yɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ, amɛhe tsemɔ, amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ bɔ ni kooloi fiteɔ nii loo helai bɛ amɛhe lɛ naa.

english: What does a category like Class 8 mean when my produce is being sorted?
ga: Mɛni ji kui tamɔ Kuu 8 lɛ shishi kɛji mihala mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Quality classes are numbers or names used to group crops by condition. A lower class or specific grade number indicates produce that might be smaller, slightly discolored, or damaged compared to premium top-class produce.
ga: Quality level ji yibɔ loo gbɛi ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ shihilɛ ko naa. Yibɔi ni yɔɔ shishi loo grade pɔtɛɛ tsɔɔ nibii ni baanyɛ afee bibioo. Su lɛ tsake fioo. loo efite kɛ akɛto nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe

english: Why do buyers separate insect-damaged produce from good produce right after weighing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ gbalaa nibii ni kooloi efite lɛ kɛjɛɔ nibii kpakpai amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛsusu amɛhe lɛ?

english: Damaged or infested crops can quickly spread mold, rot, and insects to healthy crops nearby. Separating them immediately protects the rest of the good harvest from spoiling.
ga: Tsei ni efite loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ mli oya lɛ, ebuɔ nibii kpakpai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: What causes my harvested crops to be placed in a low quality grade during inspection?
ga: Mɛni ha abu mikpamɔ lɛ akɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ?

english: Crops get low grades mainly if they have insect holes, mold, high moisture levels, dark spots, or if there is a lot of dirt, sticks, and stones mixed in with the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ baaná grade ni baa shi titri kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, hulutsoo babaoo, ŋmeii diji, loo muji, tsei tsei, kɛ tɛi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I prepare my crops on the farm so they receive a higher quality grade from buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ mli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ koni maná nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Sort out damaged or rotten produce at the farm, remove soil and debris, and ensure your crops are properly dried before taking them to the buyer. Clean, uniform crops always get higher grades.
ga: Gbalamɔ nibii ni efite loo efite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jiemɔ sũ kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. Ni kwɛmɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛya mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aŋɔɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni he tse ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baaná nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How does drying my harvested grain or cocoa properly affect the final grade I get?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo kookoo ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa naagbee grade ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper drying removes excess water that causes mold and rotting during storage. Buyers reward well-dried crops with top grades because they can be stored safely for a long time.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa beni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɔmɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai ejaakɛ abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do higher crop grades bring in more money per kilogram than lower grades?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa anáa shika babaoo yɛ kilogram kome mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ?

english: Higher grade crops look better, store longer, taste better, and meet strict quality standards required by major food processors and exporters, making buyers willing to pay more for them.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafee fɛo. Amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, amɛŋɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshɛɔ shishitoo mlai ni mli wa ni niyenii ahe nitsulɔi wuji kɛ mɛi ni kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ eto lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves and strong stems. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure around the crop base helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia otso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni wa kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmeii ni egbo ni bɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni eha amɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant plantains or cassava next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui loo ŋmei yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso hee

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting tall, fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava provides living shade that cools the ground and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my tomato plant leaves to curl up into small tubes and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni okpa dalɛ

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread crop viruses, or by extreme heat and lack of soil moisture. Controlling sucking insects early and mulching to hold soil moisture prevents leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I put it into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds or bumps on the stem cutting. These buds must point upwards toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to emerge, resulting in weak growth and small tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ Esa akɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaakumɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: How do specialty crops like Monkey Head or oyster mushrooms grow if they do not produce seeds like maize?
ga: Te tsei krɛdɛɛi tamɔ ŋmei yitso loo ŋmei ŋmei baafee tɛŋŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji amɛwooo dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Mushrooms are fungi, not flowering plants, so they grow from microscopic spores or prepared 'spawn' mixed into organic material like dried sawdust or agricultural waste. They feed on decaying organic matter in cool, damp, shaded environments rather than requiring open soil and full sunlight.
ga: Mushroom ji ŋmeii. jeee tso ni woɔ fɔfɔi No hewɔ lɛ amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ‘spawn’ ni asaa ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbi efutu mli. loo okwaayeli mli jwɛi Amɛyeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaasumɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ hulu ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds to grow right around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from the soil that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds from the root zone ensures your crop receives full nutrients and grows much faster.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo ni amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: If I put three or four seeds into one hole, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot causes crops to crowd each other and compete for soil nutrients and sunlight. Proper spacing allows each individual plant to grow strong roots and yield larger, healthier produce.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ he kome lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee babaoo ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ baatswa akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and fold in the afternoon even though I watered them a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli beni Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu wo nɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Plants fold or droop their leaves during intense heat as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss through their pores. As long as the soil beneath stays damp, leaves usually recover once the sun sets and temperatures drop.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛjieɔ amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts that can burn tender plant stems and roots if applied directly against them. It is safer to place fertilizer in a small ring or pocket a few inches away from the stem where feeding roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo kotoku bibioo ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni shishifãi ni kɛ niyenii lɛ haa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: How can I tell if my maize grains are dry enough to harvest and store in my barn without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni akɛto mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli ni egbooo?

english: Maize is sufficiently dry when the outer cob husks turn completely straw-brown and dry, and the kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them. Storing grain that retains too much moisture leads to mold and insect damage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ jwɛi ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo. Dumɔwui ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii afite.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have a high water content and continue to ripen after picking. Storing them in closed plastic sacks under the hot sun speeds up rotting, so placing them in ventilated crates under shade keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ tomato mli ni eyaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto plastic kotokui ni aŋã mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli yɛ hulutsoo be shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to harvest for selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa koni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall but producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize needs proper spacing and nitrogen fertilizer. If planted too close together, crops compete for sunlight and nutrients, spending energy growing tall instead of filling out big cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ni aná he ko ni sa kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baafata he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during heat to protect themselves from losing water. Mulching the soil around the base helps keep the soil moist and reduces heat stress on the crop.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ awo mli la koni nu akafite. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient needed for healthy green growth and strong crop development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal infection that spreads in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods promptly prevents the rot from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do small insects destroy my stored maize grains even after I put them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ baagi mli moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils breed quickly in grains that still hold moisture. Drying maize completely under the sun before bagging and using airtight storage sacks keeps insects away.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu mli dani awoɔ mli Ni akɛ vacuum bags baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that shade each other out if planted too close, forcing the roots to fight for soil nutrients and resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bibioo

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my watermelon plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Watermelons produce male flowers first, which drop naturally. If female flowers fall off too, it is usually because there are not enough bees for pollination or the soil is too dry.
ga: Watermelons baawo fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ ni baagbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ hu gbee shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ.

english: Why are my bean seeds taking a long time to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean seeds need moisture to soften their outer coat and trigger sprouting. If planted in dry soil, the seed remains dormant until adequate water is provided.
ga: Beans he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha ekwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. kɛyashi ebaaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen food in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost helps the leaves turn dark green so the plants can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye sũ lɛ nitrogen loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry hot weather to save water and survive the heat. Once the rainy season starts again, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa, ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi ekoŋŋ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa seedlings are getting too much direct sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ?

english: When young cocoa seedlings get scorched by the sun, their leaves turn brown and crispy at the tips and edges. Growing temporary shade crops like plantains near them protects the tender seedlings from sunburn.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ shã kookoo tsei bibii lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaa kɛ amɛnaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually because the soil is too dry, temperatures are extremely high, or tiny insects are attacking the blossoms. Keeping the soil moist encourages the flowers to stay and produce fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. hulutsoo ni mli wa waa Aloo kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I check if my yam tubers are growing big under the ground without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ efoŋ?

english: You can judge underground yam growth by looking at the vines and leaves above ground. Strong, thick, dark green vines with plenty of leaves show that the plant is making enough food to grow large tubers below.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛtsɔ wain tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Wein tso ni mli wa ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops whenever it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally absorb water and food from the soil faster than domestic crops can. Clearing weeds quickly after it rains keeps them from stealing sunlight and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkajuɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn completely black and dry up while hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ beni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pods turn black when infected by black pod disease, a fungal sickness that spreads fast in wet, humid conditions. Removing infected pods from the tree and clearing thick weeds helps keep damp air away and protects healthy pods.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛji akɛ black pod hela lɛ mɔ amɛ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ajie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ naa ni ebu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my plantain sucker taking so long to produce a bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?
