english: Plantains require huge amounts of water and rich nutrients to build a thick trunk before they can hold a heavy fruit bunch. If the soil lacks compost or manure, the plant will delay flowering until it gets enough strength.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ niyenii kpakpa he miihia plantains koni efee ŋmeii ni mli tse dani enyɛ etsu aduawai akui ni tsii ahe nii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tso lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi ebaaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough to give me a good yield before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani madu?

english: Healthy soil feels soft and crumbly, holds moisture without becoming swampy, is dark in color, and contains living creatures like earthworms. If your soil is hard, pale, and dry, mixing in organic manure restores its strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ, eyɛ su ni tsuɔ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbi lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato stems bending over and rotting right near the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgboi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tomato stems rot near the ground when the soil stays waterlogged or when damp fungi attack the plant base. Heap soil around the base, build drainage mounds, and tie the stems to sticks to keep them dry and upright.
ga: Tomato tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo loo be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli efɔ lɛ tutua tso lɛ shishi. Okɛ sũ ato shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni ofee nu homɔ he ko. ni okɛ tso lɛ afĩ tso nine ko he koni ehi shi ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade to survive. Strong direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil, making it hard for the young roots to take up water and nutrients.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant narrow-leaf plantain suckers instead of broad-leaf ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui ni baa bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni baa mli lɛɛ lɛ?

english: Narrow, sword-shaped suckers have stronger underground corms and establish deep roots quickly. Broad-leaved suckers are usually weaker and take much longer to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers ni tamɔ klante ni mli tse lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ daa oya. Broadleaf tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds when the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You should wait until the soil remains wet for two or three consecutive days after a heavy rain. Planting after a single light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if the sun returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ lolo gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why am I seeing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark specks inside the stem center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii diji lɛ? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central growing whorl of the maize plant during the daytime and feed on the soft, developing leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but giving me tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil contains too much nitrogen or uncomposted animal manure, cassava uses its energy to build leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo kooloi aŋmei ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fa babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ starch baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa mi-sweet potato tso lɛ he adafi lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the wet soil to catch maximum sunlight and reduce leaf diseases. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food to feed the expanding tuber underneath.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ekɛ folier helai aba shi. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii ni miigbɛ amɛshwãa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism tomato plants use to minimize water loss during intense heat. If the leaves uncurl once the evening cools down, the plant is safe and healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off onto the ground before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme temperatures, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents the blossoms from dropping.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer granules directly against the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer touching the plant stem directly can burn the outer tissue and kill feeder roots. It is safer to place fertilizer in a small ring or side-band a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã fãji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo sɛɛ ŋtayaa ko ni kɛ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting a heavy crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa babaoo sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides immediate, fast-growing shade that protects the young cocoa and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni daa oya ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You should always look at the small buds on the stem cutting and make sure they are pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the plant to waste energy growing upward from below, resulting in weak plants and very few tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, yɛ tso ni afo lɛ nɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ daa kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni edaa kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɛ bulb fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend putting wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ akɛ tso ko ama mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make their tubers using sunlight trapped by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ feɔ bulbs. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ babaoo ni ekɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Which plantain sucker is best to dig up and plant when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker henɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ kɛji aje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: It is best to choose a 'sword sucker,' which has narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong root base. These grow much faster and produce stronger stems and larger bunches than 'maiden suckers' with broad leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ afee ni ahala ‘Sword sucker’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni wa. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni wa kɛ kui wuji fe 'tsei bibii' ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize farm turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to make food and stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted poultry manure will quickly turn the crops green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ oya.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps my soil for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the ground to feed the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and gives crop-specific pests a permanent home. Rotating maize with beans or cassava helps the soil recover and starves crop pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni baahi shi daa. Akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Watering regularly at the base of the plant during dry spells helps stress-free flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni haomɔ bɛ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying a natural neem leaf solution can help keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem tso ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable garden in the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ nu woɔ o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering under hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate before it reaches the roots, and water drops left on leaves can magnify heat and damage the plant. It is best to water early in the morning.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo lɛ aya hiɛ ni efite tso lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot take intense direct sunlight or heat. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees above them, the sun dries out their leaf moisture faster than the roots can replace it, causing the leaves to burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu La haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsake lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant steals whatever food is left in its older bottom leaves and sends it up to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Abele tsei juɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyakwɛ̃ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and covered in a sticky white powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ powda yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or whiteflies. As they suck the liquid out of the leaves, they weaken the cassava plant and leave behind a sweet juice that turns into mold, causing the leaves to curl and stunt root growth underground.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies. beni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Ehaa ŋmei tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni eshiɔ wuo ni bafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden surge of water after being dry for a while, such as a heavy rainfall after a dry period. The inside of the tomato fills up with water and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Nu eyi tomato lɛ mli obɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight, and that food is what expands the tuber underground. Raising the vines on tall sticks spreads the leaves out to catch full sunlight and keeps them away from wet ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii. Ni nakai niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ baagbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni etsĩ helai anaa koni ekaba shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are my bean plants dropping all their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Beans often drop flowers when attacked by tiny pests like thrips, or when exposed to extreme heat and drought. Protecting the flowers from pests early on allows the plant to form full pods instead of shedding the buds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ eshɛ latsaa kɛ hɔmɔ he Fɔfɔi ahe ni abuɔ mra kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃.

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they steal food, water, and light away from the main plant. Pruning them down to leave only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main plant grows a massive, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) daraa yɛ plantain wulu lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ kane kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli tsei 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly drop dead even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbo trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ miida moŋ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This usually happens because of root rot or bacterial wilt caused by too much standing water or poorly drained soil. Damp soil allows destructive soil microbes to attack and kill the roots, stopping the plant from absorbing water even if the ground is soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why does planting my rice in neat, straight rows give me a bigger harvest than scattering the seeds across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every single rice plant gets equal space, air, and sunlight without crowding its neighbors. It also makes it easy to walk through and clear weeds that would otherwise steal food from the crop.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni akutsoŋbii lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo mli Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu akɛ aaatsɔ mli ni agbe jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why is it wasteful to put fertilizer on my farm right when heavy rains are about to fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miiba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the top of the soil and down into waterways before the roots have time to drink it in. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil after rain, giving roots time to absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa nu gbɛi amli dani shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does the weight of my harvested maize bag get lighter after sitting in my barn for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kpamɔ ŋmãa kotoku lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi beni mita ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains a lot of trapped water inside the seeds. As the maize dries out over time, that water evaporates into the air, making the grain lighter even though the bag looks just as full.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu babaoo ni ekã ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa gĩ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Nu lɛ baaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni kotoku lɛ eyi obɔ moŋ.

english: Why do buyers pay less money for my cocoa beans if they are not completely dry when weighed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi-kookoo lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji akɛ kookoo lɛ egbiko kwraa kɛ́ asusu he lɛ?

english: Wet cocoa beans carry extra water weight that will disappear once dried, and they rot or grow mold very quickly in storage bags. Buyers pay lower prices because wet weight is not real bean weight, and moldy beans cannot be sold to chocolate factories.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ. ni baaje mli kɛji egbi Ni ebaagbo loo ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ oya waa kɛ akɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni baa shi ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ jeee ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ aha tsokolate nitsumɔhei.

english: When I take my paddy rice to the milling machine, why do I get fewer kilos of white rice than the weight of raw paddy I brought?
ga: Be ni akɛbaawo ŋmãa lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ nɔ fioo fe ŋmãa ni mikɛba lɛ tsiimɔ?

english: Paddy rice has a hard outer husk and bran layer that the machine strips away during milling. That outer shell makes up about thirty percent of the crop's weight, so the final clean eating rice will always weigh less than the raw paddy.
ga: Paddy rice yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛ bran ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni akɛhaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ tso lɛ tsiimɔ mlijaa oha mlijaa nyɔŋmai etɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, naagbee ŋmãa ni atsuu he lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi fe ŋmãa ni ahoko lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does my cassava produce much less gari when I harvest and mill it during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ Gari fioo kwraa kɛ́ mikpa ni mikɛmiikpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, cassava roots soak up large amounts of water from the soil, which lowers their starch content. When you roast the cassava paste into gari, that extra water evaporates away, leaving you with fewer kilos of solid gari.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ashikishaŋ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Kɛ́ oshã ŋmei lɛ yɛ gari lɛ mli lɛ Nakai nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, obaaná gari ni mli wa fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly like drinking straws during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward to protect themselves from intense heat and slow down the amount of water escaping from their leaves. It is the plant's natural way of saving water during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms onto the ground instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miishwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as hot dry spells, insufficient soil water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni naa wa he, tamɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nitrogen fertilizer ni fa fe nine Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni ato lɛ.

english: If I add extra fertilizer to my cassava plants, will it automatically give me bigger tubers and more money?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha ŋmeii wuji kɛ shika babaoo aba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not always. Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the cassava plant to grow huge, thick stems and leaves above ground while keeping the tubers underneath very small, watery, and light.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tsei lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha bulb lɛ ahi shi bibioo waa, nu yɔɔ mli ni ekpɛ.

english: How do I know if the new fertilizer advice an officer gives me is actually working on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaawoi heei ni onukpai lɛ kɛha lɛ kɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can test the advice by applying the fertilizer to only half of your crop row while leaving the other half untreated. If the treated side produces healthier foliage and heavier harvests at scale, then the advice is good for your soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋaawoi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fã pɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ, ni oshi fã kroko lɛ ni okɛtsuuu nii. Kɛji akɛ fã ni atsa lɛ lɛ woɔ tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmaa ni mli kwɔ ni tsii Nakai ŋaawoo lɛ hi kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more crops from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani jeee mi nɔ ni?

english: No, when plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the plants tall and weak, resulting in smaller individual fruits and a lighter overall harvest weight.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa aduawai aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ feɔ bibii, ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why does my local maize variety take four months to yield while my neighbor's improved seed takes only three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa henɔ lɛ heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ dani ewoɔ nii lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, wɔkutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔwui ni asaa lɛ he nyɔji etɛ pɛ.

english: Improved seed varieties are specifically bred to grow faster and flower early. This allows the crop to produce full grain heads in a shorter window, helping the farmer harvest successfully before dry spells begin.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo fɔfɔi oya. Gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni eyi obɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛyeɔ omanye yɛ kpamɔ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How can I be sure that the crop medicine I buy from the market is genuine and will actually cure my farm's disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ebaatsa hela ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Genuine crop medicines have registered EPA labels, batch numbers, and clear instructions written on the container. Buying directly from licensed agro-input dealers ensures you receive authentic products that safely treat your crops without destroying your soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ EPA wolo nɔ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ nɔmba, kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni aŋmala awo nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɔ nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni kwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shweshweeshwe ni eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ awui lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of day to spray medicine on my cabbage and pepper crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ okɛshwie mi-cabbage kɛ mi-pepper lɛ nɔ?

english: The best times to spray crops are early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Spraying during the hot afternoon sun causes the liquid to evaporate too quickly before taking effect and can burn the wet crop leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ji leebi loo shwane. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or pests like fall armyworms are feeding on the plant. Applying the right fertilizer or approved pest medicine early will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms miiye tso lɛ. Nibii ni sa loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots grow.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge green leaves above ground but produces very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy leaves instead of building tubers. Using a balanced fertilizer with higher potassium encourages the plant to store its food underground into large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agboi amli.

english: Why are my tomatoes cracking open right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitswa dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when they get a sudden surge of water after a dry period, which causes the inside of the fruit to grow faster than the skin can stretch. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching prevents this from happening.
ga: Tomato baagbala kɛji nu lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the fruits are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy, leaving them vulnerable to strong winds and root pest damage. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole holds the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops grow very tall in one part of my farm but remain stunted in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi amɛyaa nɔ amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality and nutrient levels vary across a single piece of land due to past erosion or crop feeding. Applying organic compost or getting a basic soil test done helps balance out the weak areas so all your crops grow uniformly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ayeɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic compost loo shikpɔŋ nɔ shishijee kaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ afee ekome bɔni afee ni onibii fɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early in the first three to four weeks gives your planted crops enough space and nutrients to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ ohe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha odumɔi lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do holes suddenly appear in my pepper leaves right after a heavy rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainy and humid weather encourages insects like beetles and caterpillars to hatch and feed on fresh leaf growth. Checking under leaves regularly and applying recommended pest controls early protects your foliage before insect populations multiply.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be woɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛye baai heei lɛ. Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ daa kɛ ŋaawoo akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ebu obaai lɛ ahe dani kooloi ayibɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa. Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Yellowing leaves mean the plant is heat-stressed, so planting temporary shade crops like plantain or banana nearby protects cocoa leaves from sun scorch and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantain loo banana yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground, boosting sunlight exposure and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When land stays flooded with standing water, the roots drown, suffocating the plant and attracting harmful rot-causing fungi; planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread sideways rather than going deep into the dirt. When a heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop prevents it from uprooting in high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa afãi moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes through the inner leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that targets the tender central leaves of young maize plants. Applying recommended treatments directly into the center leaf whorl early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or transmitting viruses. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or insecticidal soap reduces these pests and allows new leaves to grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛdara ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when air temperatures get too hot or when soil water changes drastically from wet to dry. High heat damages flower pollen, preventing fruit development, so watering consistently and providing light shade during extreme heat helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Etsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa No hewɔ lɛ, ha nu daa ni oha hulutsoo fioo. Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and thin if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil moisture, and essential plant food. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. Applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the energy it needs to build strong leaves and stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kompost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is harsh. It is a natural way for the plant to reduce water evaporation, but if the leaves remain curled into the evening, it means the plant needs more water at its base.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ ebɔle amɛhe kɛyashi gbɛkɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nu babaoo yɛ eshishigbɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa trees from sun damage and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni fiteɔ amɛ lɛ he. Ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and thin with very few leaves when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ amɛdu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Plants need sun to make their food. When planted under heavy shade, a crop stretches upward as fast as it can to reach the light, making its stem long, weak, and thin instead of strong and bushy.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and shallow instead of deep and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmli ekɔɔɔ shi moŋ ni amɛmli kwɔ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when they hit hard, packed soil or stones underneath the ground. Building high, loose soil mounds or ridges allows the yam root to push downward without obstacle, producing long, straight tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eja.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce plenty of green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen (often from raw manure), the cassava plant spends all its energy building leaves above ground instead of storing food in its roots below. Using balanced nutrients encourages the plant to direct food down to the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ mli) Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii amaje shi kɛya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from heavy heat helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees drop tiny green fruits onto the ground before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Citrus trees drop extra fruit if they do not have enough water and food to support all of them, or if fruit flies attack the young fruits. Deep watering during dry spells and using fly traps can prevent the tree from dropping its fruit prematurely.
ga: Orange tsei baawo yibii krokomɛi kɛji amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua aduawai bibii Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ amɛnɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmeii atsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkashwie amɛyibii lɛ oya.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds rot in the soil without sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted in soil that is too wet or buried too deep where air cannot reach them. Planting seeds at a finger's depth in moist, well-drained soil helps them breathe and sprout quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ loo afu amɛ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ muɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings take a long time to sprout when I plant them upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni afo lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small buds that grow pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots must bend all the way around underground to find the light, which drains the cutting's strength and slows down growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛi Esa akɛ abɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe. shikpɔŋ shishi koni ena la Enɛ baaha tso nine lɛ hewalɛ aba shi ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides living shade and holds moisture in the air, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores nutrients and turns the leaves green again so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat or dry soil as a way to save energy. Giving your tomatoes consistent water during hot dry spells keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Plantains have shallow roots rather than deep ones, making it hard for them to hold up a heavy fruit bunch in strong wind. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden Y-sticks holds the weight and stops the tree from snapping.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaamɔ aduawai akui ni tsii amli. yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ Y ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish the next crops you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: How do weeds lower my crop yield even if I leave enough space between plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi? Kɛji mishi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ po.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal underground water and soil food right away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up long wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the energy that fills up the tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases live.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ ayiɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field. Switching crops breaks pest cycles and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my field right before a huge rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ ni naa wa ko aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes the fertilizer off the field or buries it too deep before the roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so the roots absorb it immediately without waste.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo efuɔ lɛ tsɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni eshiŋ jwɛi ko kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to make food. When the soil runs out of nitrogen or when heavy rains wash it away, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed new growth, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ fo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ lɛ. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. If the weather is too hot or the soil dries out suddenly, the plant saves its energy by dropping flowers instead of trying to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa lɛ Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing more leaves to the sun while protecting them from fungal diseases that thrive on wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a clear, open field with no trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni tsei bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and excessive heat. Without larger shade trees or plantain plants to filter the direct sunlight, the heat burns the young leaves and dries out the roots before the cocoa can establish itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ bɛ. Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani kookoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stalks and small maize cobs instead of strong plants with large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e ngɛ tso agbo nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain saturates the field and water cannot drain away, the roots get waterlogged, run out of air, and begin to rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmɔji lɛ amli fũuɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ aho kɛje mli. Nu baatsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli, kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli, ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year if I plant it on the exact same plot without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients every season. Planting it in the same spot continuously exhausts those specific nutrients, leaving the soil tired and unable to support good yields without rest or crop rotation.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo daa be mli. Dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help improve the soil for my next crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays behind, fertilizing the soil naturally for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and will drink the fertilizer water and absorb the soil nutrients before your crop's roots can reach them, leaving your crops hungry despite the added fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo. Amɛbaa nu nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars appear in the center of my maize plants right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Warm weather and early rain cause pest eggs, such as Fall Armyworm, buried in the soil or weeds to hatch. The young caterpillars seek out the soft, tender inner leaves of young maize plants to feed on.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi amli lɛ fɔɔ. Kplukai bibii taoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai bibii lɛ koni amɛye.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the field has too much standing water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out small and tough even though the plant leaves look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil is packed too hard or contains excess nitrogen, the cassava plant spends its energy growing thick leaves above ground instead of expanding tubers below. Loosening the soil into raised mounds or ridges helps the roots grow fat.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo bulbs yɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ ni efee gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɔ babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when soil moisture swings between too dry and too wet, or when temperatures get very high. Mulching around the plant base with dry grass helps keep soil moisture even so flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ po.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly and look weak when I plant the same crop in the same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows specialized soil pests to build up. Rotating different crops each season gives the soil time to recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi krɛdɛɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛhe nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my tree turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms. Trimming excess branches from surrounding trees to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli Ha hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses as they feed. Spraying the undersides of leaves early with organic neem leaf extract controls these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra. Eyeɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground happens when heavy rain collects in low spots without draining, attracting soil bacteria and beetles. Planting on tall ridges or mounds allows excess water to flow away cleanly from the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa bua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Egbalaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainy season even when the wind is not strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain stems become very top-heavy when bearing fruit, while small root worms weaken their underground grip. Supporting fruiting stems with sturdy bamboo props prevents the heavy plants from collapsing.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ amli tsii kɛji amɛwo yibii. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ haa amɛhe ni amɛmɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnuts make my land better for growing maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnuts have special root nodules that draw nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decay after harvest, that natural plant food feeds the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, tso niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my mature oil palm leaves develop bright orange spots and turn brown early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya lɛ?

english: Orange spots on oil palm leaves indicate a lack of potassium nutrient in the soil. Spreading empty palm fruit bunches or wood ash around the tree base returns potassium to the roots and keeps leaves green.
ga: Oil palm tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Palm aduawai akui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo tso sũ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa potassium kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli.

english: What is NPK fertilizer and why is it so important for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium, which are the main foods plants need. Just like people need good food to be strong, NPK supplies essential nutrients that help all types of crops grow well and stay healthy.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha Nitrogen, Phosphorus kɛ Potassium, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛhe awa lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ NPK kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to put on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Every crop and soil type requires a specific quantity of fertilizer. Applying too little will not feed the plant enough, while applying too much can waste your money and burn the plant roots, so you must measure according to recommended guidelines.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaahaa tso lɛ niyenii bɔ ni sa, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko wo mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite oshika ni esha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ osusu he yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni atsɔɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Will applying NPK fertilizer help all the different crops on my farm, or only specific ones?
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi pɛ?

english: NPK fertilizer is generally beneficial for almost all crops because every plant needs nitrogen for green leaves, phosphorus for strong roots, and potassium for fruits and grains.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ he miihia nitrogen kɛha amɛbaai eŋɔlii lɛ. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai kɛ ŋmaa.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my field harm my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, over-applying fertilizer can damage your crops by burning their roots and stems. It is essential to follow recommended quantities so the plants get just what they need to thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite onibii kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni eshãa lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni atsu tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ he nii koni tso lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing slowly and looking pale even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crops to grow well. Plants also need soil nutrients to build stems and leaves, so pale or slow-growing plants are usually a sign that the soil lacks food like NPK.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei hu taoɔ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee tsei kɛ baai. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ NPK bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What actually happens to my plants after I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli?

english: When you apply fertilizer, plant roots absorb the dissolved nutrients from the soil, allowing the crop to build stronger stems, greener leaves, and larger fruits or grains faster.
ga: Beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni wa. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji daa oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough plant food from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Healthy crops receiving enough nutrients will have dark green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady growth. Weak stems, yellowish leaves, or small fruits indicate the crop needs more nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni naa niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaná baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Tso lɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, baai ni tsuɔ, loo aduawai bibii tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia tso lɛ.

english: How does feeding my crops properly affect the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Te niyenii ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ saa niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Well-fed crops produce larger yields and bigger produce, ensuring that your household has enough food to eat and extra left over to sell at the market.
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oshia lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛye kɛ agbɛnɛ hu niyenii ni eshwɛ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do some crops seem to need more nutrients from the soil than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe hiaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different crops produce different types of food; heavy-feeding crops like maize need lots of nitrogen for fast growth, while tubers or fruit crops need different amounts of nutrients to develop properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi woɔ niyenii srɔtoi. Nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he miihia nitrogen babaoo koni amɛdara oya, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa loo aduawai ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia niyenii srɔtoi babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to place fertilizer so my crops can actually use it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni anyɛ akɛtsu nii?

english: Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away from the plant stem and covered lightly with soil so rain doesn't wash it away, allowing the roots to easily drink up the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3, ni akɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Koni nugbɔ lɛ akaho Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo

english: Why is it difficult to use a mechanical planter on my field immediately after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ mishia lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain turns the soil into thick mud. Machinery like planters will sink, get stuck, and clog up with wet mud, which prevents seeds from dropping properly and damages the soil structure.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo muji. Tsɔnei tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baagbee shi. Ekɛ muji ni efɔ lɛ ebɔ he ni ekɛ ehe ewo mli Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ agbee shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii.

english: How long should I wait after rain stops before using a planter on my land?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii?

english: You should generally wait one to two days until the excess water drains away. A good test is to squeeze a handful of soil; if it squeezes out water or forms a sticky ball, it is still too wet for machinery.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ kɛyashi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaho. Kaa kpakpa ji ni ajie sũ fioo ko kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji ekɛ nu lɛ shwie shi loo ebatsɔ bɔɔlu ni shwieɔ shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo kɛha tsɔne lɛ.

english: What happens if I force my planting machine to work on very wet, muddy soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji minyɛ mɔ ni duɔ nii lɛ nɔ koni etsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Forcing heavy equipment on muddy soil compacts the earth into hard clods when it dries. This leaves airless pockets around seeds and forms a hard surface crust that young shoots cannot break through.
ga: Nibii ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ nɔ ko ni wa kɛ́ egbi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmei ni wa ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does soil stick to and clog up my planting tools when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa midumɔ nibii lɛ tsiɔ naa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: Wet soil contains water that acts like glue between small soil particles and metal or plastic surfaces. This causes mud to build up on planter wheels and seed chutes, blocking seeds from falling into the ground.
ga: Nu ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ glu ni yɔɔ sũ mli nibii bibii kɛ dade loo plastic nibii ateŋ lɛ yɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ mli. Enɛ haa sũ buaa ehe naa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shwiili lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ashwiemɔ he lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkagbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant by hand with a hoe when the soil is very wet?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ minine baadu nii kɛ ŋmei be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting by hand is safer when the ground is very wet because human feet cause much less soil compaction than heavy machinery, allowing you to place seeds at the right depth without ruining the soil structure.
ga: Hɛɛ, nine ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, adesa naji kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo kwraa fe tsɔnei ni tsii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ he ni sa ni ofiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii.

english: Why do seeds rot in the ground when I plant them during prolonged heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as moisture to germinate. When rain floods the soil, water replaces all the air spaces, essentially suffocating the seeds and causing fungi to rot them before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Should I plant my seeds shallower or deeper in the soil when it has been raining heavily?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa?

english: You should plant slightly shallower in very wet soil. Placing seeds too deep in wet ground keeps them away from warmth and air, increasing the risk of seed decay.
ga: Esa akɛ odu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ fioo. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baafite lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does planting my farm manually with casual laborers cost so much more than using a planter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ shika babaoo akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be baatsu nii kɛkwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ fe okwaafoi ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ?

english: Manual planting requires hiring multiple workers who are paid a daily rate, and human labor takes several days to cover large fields. A planter finishes the same work in a fraction of the time, saving money on daily wages.
ga: Nine ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ biɔ ni nitsulɔi babaoo ni awoɔ amɛ nyɔmɔ daa gbi lɛ atsu nii. ni adesai anitsumɔ heɔ gbii babaoo dani anyɛɔ atsuɔ he ko ni da tamɔ nɛkɛ he nii. Okwaafoi gbeɔ nitsumɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ naa yɛ be fioo ko mli. Ekɛ shika toɔ daa gbi nyɔmɔwoo mli

english: How can I manage my planting costs when rain keeps delaying my daily farm workers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ?

english: You can prepare your fields and mark out planting spots ahead of time during dry days so that when workers arrive, they can drop seeds quickly and finish more acres in a single day.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ni okadi hei ni abaadu nii yɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. koni kɛ́ nitsulɔi lɛ bashɛ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie dumɔwui oya ni amɛdu acreage babaoo yɛ gbi kome mli.

english: Why does my crop sprout unevenly when I use casual workers to plant by hand during rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ beni mikɛ be kukuoo mli nitsulɔi tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ amɛ kɛ niji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Casual laborers working in wet, difficult conditions may push seeds to different depths using hoes or cutlasses. Seeds planted deeper take longer to emerge than seeds planted near the surface, causing uneven growth across your field.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni mli wa amli lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ spade loo dagger atsu nii ni amɛkɛtsi ŋmaa lɛ kɛya hei srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fe dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety, like Colombia maize, to get a good harvest in my area?
ga: Mahala tso henɔ ni sa, tamɔ Colombia ŋmãa. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii kpakpai yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred to suit specific soil types, rainfall patterns, and maturity times. Selecting a tested variety suited to your region ensures your plants grow strong, resist local pests, and give you a higher yield.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ dalɛ be Kaa tso ni sa kɛha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ halamɔ baaha otsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Where is the best place for me to buy genuine crop seeds and inputs so I do not waste my money?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ koni mikafite mishika?

english: It is best to buy inputs from certified agro-dealers or authorized community connectors. Purchasing from reliable sources guarantees that seeds have high germination rates and that agrochemicals are authentic and safe for your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe saji kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Kɛ́ ohe kɛjɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ waa, ni akɛ agrochemicals lɛ ji anɔkwale ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I correctly measure and mix liquid products like Vital Five before applying them to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu nibii ni ji nu tamɔ Vital Five lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛfutu mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Liquid fertilizers and treatments must be diluted with the exact amount of clean water recommended—such as mixing a specific dose per 5 liters of water. Proper dilution prevents chemical burns on leaves and ensures plants absorb nutrients safely.
