ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nu ni mli tse awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nu mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli kɛyashɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nu litai 5 mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni shãa tsei lɛ baa lɛ naa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my plants if I apply too much chemical or fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Using more chemical than recommended can scorch the leaves, burn the root system, and stunt crop growth. Over-application damages soil health and wastes money without increasing your yield.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã, eshã shishifãi lɛ, ni etsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa. Kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ shika ni ekɛ yibiiwoo lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops leaves turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can indicate that fertilizer was applied when the soil was too dry, preventing nutrient absorption, or that the plant is receiving too much or too little of a specific nutrient. Proper soil moisture is necessary for plants to take up food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ. etsĩɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa Aloo tso lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa he miihia koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: How do I know the right time of the month or season to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa yɛ nyɔŋ loo be mli ni mikɛbaaha mitsei lɛ niyenii?

english: Crops require nutrients at specific stages of development, such as right after early growth or just before flowering. Applying fertilizer when soil moisture is right during monthly rainfall cycles helps plants absorb nutrients when they need them most.
ga: Tsei he hiaa niyenii yɛ amɛdalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli, tamɔ beni amɛdara oya sɛɛ loo dani amɛwo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant according to the natural rainy season schedule?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa nugbɔshiimɔ be he gbɛjianɔtoo naa lɛ?

english: Crops rely naturally on moisture to dissolve nutrients in the soil so roots can absorb them. Planting in harmony with natural rainfall patterns allows crops to establish deep roots without suffering from heat stress or drought.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛjie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ ko enaaa amɛ.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off before turning into fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when crops experience stress from irregular watering, high heat, or lack of key nutrients. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing balanced feeding during the flowering stage helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital nutrients and sunlight from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on the behavior and health of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajeŋba kɛ amɛhewalɛ?

english: Inspecting your farm at least once a week allows you to notice early signs of nutrient deficiencies, pest attacks, or leaf diseases so you can treat the crops before major damage occurs.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo helai ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mra bɔni afee ni onyɛ otsa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani efite waa.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when I want them to produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi? Be ni miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes weak, diseased, or excess branches so the tree doesn't waste energy on leaves that don't produce. It opens up the tree to sunlight and fresh air, which boosts pod growth and prevents fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni afeee lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe amɛhaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa pod lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii helai tamɔ pod diji lɛ tsiɔ naa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They need shade trees or nurse crops like plantains planted alongside them to shade them and keep the soil cool until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa amɛbii, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ajɔɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa

english: How can I keep my crops from drying out during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your soil by covering the ground around your plants with dried leaves, straw, or grass—a practice called mulching. Mulch traps moisture in the ground, shields the soil from hot sun, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai ni gboi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi ni oooha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Why do my crops shed their leaves when the weather gets hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves. Shedding leaves is a natural way for a plant to save moisture and stay alive during long dry spells until the rains return.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Can I use waste from my chicken coop to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina shĩa mli jwɛi aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, chicken manure is very rich in nitrogen and helps crops grow strong green leaves. However, you should mix it with soil or dry leaves and let it age (compost) first, because fresh manure is too hot and can burn plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmei mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni egbi afutu ni oha egbɔ (compost) klɛŋklɛŋ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii hee baanyɛ adɔ tsɔ ni eshã tso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Why do crops planted near farm animals seem to grow faster than crops further away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil near animal housing often receives organic waste from manure and leftover feed, which naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that feed nearby plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ kooloi ashihilɛhei lɛ naa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi aniyenii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I leave paths and wide spaces between my crops instead of planting everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛjegbɛi wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors. Clear paths also make it easy to walk through for weeding, spraying, and harvesting without trampling plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Gbɛi ni mli tse lɛ hu haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ mli kɛha jwɛi shwiemɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei anɔ.

english: Why do crops planted along my farm boundary sometimes grow poorly compared to those in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Boundary lines often suffer from shade from neighboring tall trees, hard soil packed down by people walking past, or roots from neighboring vegetation taking away water and soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa husui lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni gbɔmɛi nyiɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli etse. loo shishifãi ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: Is burning dry grass on my farm before planting good or bad for my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: While burning clears the land fast, it burns away good organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the soil. Over time, burning weakens the soil, making it hold less water and fewer nutrients for your crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya moŋ, shi eshãa nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hu ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni akɛtoɔ lɛ faaa, ni niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ hu faaa.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ maje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels moist and crumbly, contains earthworms, and has healthy wild plants growing on it. If plants on the uncultivated land look pale or weak, the soil may lack key nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ fɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii titrii bɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is ready to be harvested using a machine instead of by hand?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛ tsɔne baakpa moŋ fe ni akɛ niji baakpa?

english: Maize is ready for machine harvesting when the leaves turn brown, the cobs droop downward, and the grains are hard and dry enough that pressing them with your thumbnail leaves no mark.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwie shi, ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ mli wa ni egbi bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ oshishifã lɛ anyɛ nɔ koni amɛkashi okadi ko kwraa.

english: Will using a combine harvester damage my corn grains compared to picking them by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baafite mi-ŋma lɛ kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛkpaa lɛ he?

english: If the machine is set correctly and the corn is fully dry, it will not damage the grains. However, if the corn is harvested when it is still wet or soft, the machine can crush or split the kernels.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato tsɔne lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ abele lɛ mli efɔ lolo loo eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, efiteee dumɔwui lɛ. Mashiŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ loo agbala dumɔwui amli.

english: Why does my corn field need to be cleared of big tree stumps before a harvester can enter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii wuji kɛjɛ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmaakpalɔi lɛ abote mli lɛ?

english: Combine harvesters have heavy tires and low-hanging metal blades. Hidden tree stumps and large rocks can bend or break the cutting blades and ruin the expensive machinery.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkpaa nii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ tai ni tsii kɛ dade ni shwieɔ shi ni shwieɔ shi. Tsoi akutsei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tɛi wuji baanyɛ aha tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ atsɔ loo efo. ni ebaanyɛ efite tsɔnei ni jara wa

english: Why do large combine harvesters refuse to harvest small or oddly shaped corn fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔnei wuji ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakpa ŋmãa ŋmɔji bibii loo ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ?

english: Harvesters are big machines that need wide spaces to turn around smoothly. On small or irregular fields, the machine spends more time turning than harvesting, which wastes fuel and time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ji tsɔnei wuji ni biɔ he ko babaoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. yɛ hei bibii loo hei ni ejaaa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsɔne lɛ heɔ be babaoo ni ekɛtsakeɔ ehe fe bɔ ni ekɛkpaa nii. ni fiteɔ fuɛl kɛ be

english: Does the way I space my corn plants when planting affect whether a harvesting machine can work on my farm?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ toɔ he ko kɛji miduɔ lɛ saa kɛji ŋmaakpalɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, harvesting machines move along straight rows set at fixed distances. If your corn rows are planted unevenly or too close together, the machine will run over nearby plants instead of harvesting them properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nikpamɔ tsɔne lɛ nyiɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ato he. Kɛji akɛ adu o-abele ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsɔne lɛ baajo foi kɛho tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekpa amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants fall over in strong winds, and can a machine still harvest them if they fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ? Ni ani tsɔnei baanyɛ akpa nii lolo kɛji amɛgbee shi?

english: Corn plants fall over if their roots are shallow or stems are weak from overcrowding. Combine harvesters struggle to scoop up corn that is lying flat on the ground, so fallen crops usually have to be harvested by hand.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Mɛi ni kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ naa naagba yɛ ŋmãa ni ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni akɛ niji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbee shi lɛ.

english: Why do some cobs on my farm grow big full grains while others on the same field stay small and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi miidu ŋmaa wuji lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cobs grow smaller or empty grains if the soil in that part of the field lacks water or nutrients, or if weeds were competing with the crop for sunlight and food while the grains were forming.
ga: Cob lɛ baatsɔ dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ fã lɛ mli lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Aloo kɛji akɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why does my maize rot faster if I harvest it right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Corn grains absorb rain moisture quickly. Harvesting wet corn traps that water inside the storage bags or machine bins, creating a damp environment where mold and bacteria multiply rapidly.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔshiimɔ oya. Ni akɛ nu woɔ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui loo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmãa kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa oya.

english: Why do I lose so many corn grains on the ground when I harvest late in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikpaa ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When corn stays on the stalk too long in hot, dry weather, the cobs become very brittle. Any shaking during harvest causes the dry grains to shatter and drop into the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi waa. Kpokpomɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to leave my corn to dry on the stalk in the field or harvest it early to dry at home?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ tsei ni egbi nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo makpã mra ni magbi yɛ shia?

english: Leaving corn on the stalk saves labor, but it exposes the cobs to attacks by birds, pests, and mold. Harvesting early and drying the cobs on clean tarpaulins at home protects the quality of your grain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Shi enɛ baaha okpoi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii atutua cob lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra Ni ooogbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ yɛ shia lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which acts as food for healthy green growth. Adding organic compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow pepper?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ?

english: Healthy soil for pepper feels dark, loose, and drains water easily without creating long-lasting puddles. If water sits on top of your land for a long time after rain, mixing in dry animal manure or compost will help loosen the soil and improve drainage.
ga: Pepper shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ oya ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Koolooi ashishifãi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha nu lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas together with my cassava in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ cowpea kɛ cassava adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer. Planting them alongside cassava keeps your soil rich and gives you two different crops to harvest from one piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ odu yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi enyɔ ni obaanyɛ okpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen in the soil. Giving your plants consistent moisture around their roots during dry days helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli fũuɔ Shishifãi lɛ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to capture sunlight and make food, which gets stored underground as the yam tuber. Raising the vines on stakes gets leaves off the hot ground and opens them to maximum sunlight for bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai tamɔ hulu la tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. kɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha sweet potatoes wuji.

english: When maize seeds are planted too tightly together, the growing plants compete for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This causes thin, weak stems and very small ears of corn instead of full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekomekomei tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa baa yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Curled, yellow-patterned leaves are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this by planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties and clearing infected plants early.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small round holes into my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni oyeɔ kɛ́ oye kaabe baai ni buji bibii yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. Spraying a natural mixture made from crushed neem seeds or using safe, approved crop sprays protects the leaves from being eaten.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ tso lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛ neem dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ fee lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni akaye amɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my main crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds while your crops are still young ensures your plants get all the nourishment they need to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi be mli ni onibii lɛ darako lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating my dried beans after I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Bean weevils multiply quickly when stored grains contain moisture or are left in open sacks. Drying your beans completely under the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) suffocates the insects naturally without chemical powders.
ga: Pea ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli edɔ loo ashi amɛ yɛ kotokui ni agbele mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni akɛwo kotoku ko ni mli ewo muji mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why is it important for me to test my farm soil before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi tsei adumɔ?

english: Testing your soil reveals what nutrients are already in the ground and what is missing, preventing you from wasting money on the wrong fertilizers or applying chemicals your land does not need.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kpo kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa loo tsofai ni he ehiaaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does a portable soil testing kit work when I use it on my field?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A soil testing kit uses simple chemical liquids or test strips mixed with a small soil sample to show color changes that indicate your soil's pH balance and main plant nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa nibii kɛ tsofai ni ji nu folo loo kaa nibii ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko efutu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ su tsakemɔi ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ pH kɛ tsei amli niyenii titrii lɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: What is soil acidity, and how does it stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ acid? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soil acidity (or pH) measures how sour the land is; if soil is too acidic, crop roots cannot absorb food from the ground, even if you put fertilizer there.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acid (loo pH) lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛsusuɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli acid yɔɔ ha lɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo jɛmɛ po.

english: Why do crops on one side of my farm grow tall while crops on another part stay yellow and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ afã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality and nutrient levels can vary across small distances on the same plot of land, meaning different sections may require different soil treatments to produce healthy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ atsake yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛ fioo. yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fãi lɛ Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii srɔtoi koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I know the exact fertilizer my land needs for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ koni ekpa nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soil testing measures the levels of key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, allowing an extension officer to give you an exact fertilizer recipe tailored to your land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa susuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium lɛ falɛ he. Enɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I just guess the amount of fertilizer to put on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji misusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Guessing can lead to over-fertilizing, which burns crop roots and pollutes nearby water, or under-fertilizing, which leaves plants weak and lowers your total crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni asusuɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aha afɔ mɔ fe nine. Enɛ shãa tsei ashishifãi ni efiteɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ afata he Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ aba shi.

english: What are the signs on crop leaves that show my land is lacking good nutrients?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kpakpa bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean a lack of nitrogen, while purplish leaves or stunted roots usually point to a lack of phosphorus, showing that your land needs specific nutrients added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo shishifãi bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields keep reducing every year even when I farm the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ ŋmɔji kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ moŋ?

english: Every harvest removes nutrients from the ground, and continuously farming without replacing those missing minerals causes the soil to become exhausted and lose its natural power.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni okwaayeli ni aya nɔ ni akɛ shika tsuru ni elaaje lɛ tsakeee lɛ haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ehewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Where can I get soil information for my farm if testing tools are not available in my area?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana shikpɔŋ he saji kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ? Kɛji akɛ kaa dɛŋdade ko bɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office, where officers maintain regional soil maps and historical data to give reliable advice for your locality.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Wɔ nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ he mfoniri kɛ yinɔsane mli saji anɔ koni amɛkɛ ŋaawoi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ aha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use regional soil data from nearby farms to guide my planting decisions?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kpokpaa nɔ shikpɔŋ he saji ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ akudɔ yiŋkpɛɛi ni kɔɔ dumɔ he?

english: Yes, regional soil data gives a very good general guide on common soil types and nutrient needs in your district, helping you choose the right crops and fertilizers when personal testing isn't possible.
ga: Hɛɛ, kpokpaa nɔ shikpɔŋ he saji haa gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa beni anyɛɛɛ aka bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe okwɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain saturates the soil and drowns the roots, stopping them from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii

english: Why does my farm land produce less maize every year if I plant it in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop feeds on. It also gives pests and diseases that prefer that crop a permanent place to live and multiply in your field.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ yeɔ lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ hu naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings shed their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan wind brings dry air that pulls moisture out of leaves faster than young roots can drink from the soil. Shedding leaves is the seedling's defense to save water and keep its main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow so rapidly right after the first major rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rains wake up beneficial microbes in the dry soil. These organisms quickly break down old leaves and organic matter, releasing a natural surge of nitrogen that acts like instant fertilizer for your seeds.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ teɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ fiteɔ baai momoi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ oya. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee klalo kɛha odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light, using up energy that should have gone into making large maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛfee ŋmãa ni fa babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a very small bunch when I leave all the suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mihaa ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Nakai plantain tso lɛ

english: The small suckers act like extra mouths feeding from the same roots, taking water and nutrients from the main stem. Pruning away excess suckers leaves all the food for the mother plant to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabu krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ shishifãi komekomei lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii fɛɛ kɛhaa tso nyɛ lɛ koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to create energy for the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive until growing conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rain right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa dani kpamɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. Excessive rain fills all those air spaces with water, causing the roots to drown and encouraging rot organisms to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ewoɔ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and feeling sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ kɛji mita he lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled leaves mean tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are hiding underneath, sucking out the sap and leaving behind a sweet liquid that attracts mold and weakens the plant.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle, ni wa tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi. Ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshiɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa tso lɛ mli ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when water sits on my farm field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like people do. When water sits on your farm for many days without draining away, it starves the roots of air, causing them to drown, rot, and stop feeding the plant.
ga: Tse shishifãi muɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi muɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu hiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Hɔmɔ baaye kɔɔyɔɔ mli shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛkpaa tsei lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow seeds right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, be lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: The first light rain only wet the top surface of the soil. If a dry spell follows immediately, your newly sprouted seeds will dry out and die because there isn't deep soil moisture yet to keep them alive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I avoid planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ yɛ he kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he?

english: Growing the same crop every season steals the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. It also allows specific soil diseases and pests to build up in that plot, making your harvest smaller each year.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi komɛi hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital food they need to stay strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi eshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants show they are ready when their lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, leaving bare stems. For most local varieties, this happens between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Yucca tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. Kɛha maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi babaoo Enɛ baaba yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛ 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by high heat or sudden changes in water—like going from very dry soil to very wet soil. The plant drops flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plants like plantains grown right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ he hiaa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the soft shade and cool soil they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants yield small fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving them proper space helps each plant grow big and produce plenty of large peppers.
ga: Beni pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when my soil is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast thieves that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds share the field, your crops get less food and cannot build thick stems or good yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ jaa ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii fioo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo tsei ni mli tse loo amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I see tiny holes chewed into my maize leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Okɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ atsu nii leebi.

english: Tiny holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by early-stage pests like Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the center funnel of the plant during the hot day and come out at night or early morning to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mra, tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the topsoil or waterlogs the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ewaa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leafy tops instead of sending energy down to build thick, starchy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ etso kɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e pee sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ e ngɛ powder.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans in my field help the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without tall crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a shield against heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo he tsɔne yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: What is causing the ragged holes and sawdust-like leaves in the center of my young corn stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the growing center of the corn plant. They feed on fresh leaves before they unfold, leaving holes and waste behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai heei dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛtsɔ bu kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of calcium in the soil, which prevents the flowers from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots growing around my plantain tree to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Midumɔwui lɛ yɛ biɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main plantain tree. Removing most suckers leaves all the food for one main stem, resulting in larger bunches.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ fɛɛ ahi tso lɛ yitso titri kome nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa kuu wulu ko.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch more sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first small rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil, which quickly dries out if dry weather returns for a few weeks. Seeds that germinate will wither and die because their tender roots cannot find deeper moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Enɛ baagbi oya kɛji shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsii fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my field always grow much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants adapted to local soil and climate conditions over many years. They naturally germinate faster and absorb available soil nutrients and water more aggressively than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When water collects around cassava roots without draining, it starves the roots of air and allows harmful fungi to grow. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu efooo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ada. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How can I prevent water from settling around my crops and causing them to rot during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu naa koni ekabɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni eha amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can create raised beds or mounds instead of planting on flat ground or in deep holes. This lets heavy rain flow away from the plant stem and roots, keeping them safe from standing water.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee saatsoi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo bu ni mli kwɔ mli. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ahe. Ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ he.

english: What is the best way to plant crops in low-lying or marshy areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: In marshy areas, build high ridges or mounds so the main root system stays above the water level. This gives the crops access to soil moisture without letting water drown the plant.
ga: yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ Feemɔ ŋshɔkpɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko bɔni afee ni shishifã titri lɛ ahi nu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni nu lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: If I dig a very deep hole to plant my seeds, will it help them grow better?
ga: Kɛ́ mifo bu ko ni mli kwɔ waa koni mikɛdu dumɔwu lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, digging too deep can trap water inside the hole like a pit, causing seeds or roots to rot before they sprout. Seeds should be planted at a shallow depth where they get air, warmth, and just enough moisture.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akuɔ mli tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ nu yɛ bu lɛ mli tamɔ bu. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ loo shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa, dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers rot after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers often rot if water collects at the bottom of the planting hole. Digging a hole with loose, well-draining soil and refilling it slightly with topsoil prevents standing water from suffocating the base.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ dumɔ bu lɛ shishi. Bu ni akɛ sũ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ baatsu nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋwɛi sũ fioo afata he koni nu akafee ekome yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Should I plant my yam crops on flat ground or build mounds for them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo matswa gɔji maha amɛ?

english: Building mounds is better for yams because it loosens the soil for tuber growth and prevents water from pooling around the yam, which protects it from rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni ama lɛ hi fe ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni bulbs lɛ adara. Ni ehaaa nu abɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I bury the stem of my cocoa seedling too deep in the soil when transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ kɛ́ mikɛmiidu shi?

english: Burying the stem too deep exposes tender stem tissues to wet soil, inviting fungal diseases that cause the stem to rot. The seedling should be planted at the same soil level it had in its nursery bag.
ga: Kɛ́ afu tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ fã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpo. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ baa. Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to turn yellow and drop after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves after rain usually mean the soil is waterlogged. When roots sit in trapped water for too long, they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, causing the plant to shed leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ hi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ha tsei ajie amɛbaai lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has poor water drainage before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ dani madu nii?

english: If puddles stay on the surface for hours after rain, or if the soil feels sticky like heavy clay and smells sour, your soil has poor drainage and needs raised ridges before planting.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehe miihia ni awó nɔ dani adu.

english: Can planting seeds right before a heavy downpour harm my crop?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, heavy rain immediately after planting can wash away topsoil, expose seeds, or bury them inside waterlogged mud pits where they rot instead of germinating.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ. ni ejieɔ dumɔwui lɛ akpo Aloo fuu amɛ yɛ muji bu ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli he ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa anáa wɔɔhe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and air to produce a healthy crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps turn the leaves green and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps improve soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny helpers in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When the plant grows and breaks down, it leaves behind natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ yelikɛbualɔi bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛfite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I drop chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated chemical fertilizer can burn the soft stem and destroy delicate feeding roots. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring or side-groove a few inches away from the stem where roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo sɛɛ ŋmei lɛ kɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on wooden poles instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow big tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal rot and diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya hiɛ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo aba nɔ. ni ji hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on the soil around my garden vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Mi abɔɔ mli aduawai?

english: Covering the ground with dry materials, called mulching, protects the soil from hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps weeds from sprouting and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms usually drop off when temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Regular, even watering helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack open as the tubers grow bigger beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efuɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaf. Spraying a mild soap or neem oil mixture under the leaves helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows with spaces between them instead of planting them close together everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ahi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ.

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from stealing sunlight, water, and soil food from each other, which helps every plant grow strong and produce more yield.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Applying fertilizer like Urea helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer to my farm during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash the fertilizer away into streams or deep underground before the plant roots have a chance to drink it up, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Covering the ground with mulch keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from drying out quickly under the sun, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu la shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys corn shoots. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening stops them before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii. Akpaa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning black and rotting underground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water collects in the soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the flowers from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Lifting yam vines up on poles allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and yellow leaves from the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pruning lower leaves stops dirt and disease from splashing onto the plant during rain and helps the plant send its strength directly into producing larger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni muji kɛ helai akashwie tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ehaa tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo tomatoi wuji.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants lack deep root systems and cannot handle direct sunlight or high temperatures. Without shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees, intense sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn purple or pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ purple loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, while purple leaves point to a phosphorus deficiency. Applying balanced fertilizers like NPK restores these essential nutrients so the corn can grow tall and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ adara ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, the crop roots fight each other underground for nutrients and water, while their upper leaves block sunshine from neighbor plants. Proper plant spacing gives each crop enough food, light, and air to produce maximum harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni amɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa niyenii, la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in wet soil, choking the roots of oxygen during heavy rain seasons. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are fall armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the plant's central leaf funnel during the hot day and eats the tender leaves at night. Spraying targeted controls early in the morning or late evening reaches them while they feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii gbɛkɛ. Targeted control spraying ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baashɛ amɛhe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods suddenly turn black and shrivel during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that multiplies in damp, dark, and cool conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning thick branches lets sunlight in and lowers moisture, preventing the fungus from spreading across the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ baaha hulu la lɛ akpɛ yɛ mli ni ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by soil-borne germs or root pests that clog the plant's water tubes from the inside. Rotating your tomato fields with different crops like corn or cassava starves out these soil pests over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli helai loo shishifã mli kooloi ni miitsi tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa kɛmiijɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Tomato ŋmɔji ni atsakeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I trim off the small branches growing directly out of the stem on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: These extra shoots, called chupons, consume water and plant food without growing cocoa pods. Trimming them off directs all the tree's energy into main branches that bear large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ kɛ nu baatsu nii ni amɛkwɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ he ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa niji titrii lɛ anɔ, ni kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do farm officers encourage me to plant groundnuts together with my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli onukpai lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, groundnuts naturally feed nitrogen into the soil, acting as a natural food source for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why should I stop burning crop remains on my field after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ ashãmɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Burning crop stalks destroys good soil nutrients and kills helpful earthworms and soil organisms. Leaving dry leaves to decay naturally creates a protective cover that keeps soil cool, retains water, and transforms into natural manure.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ baai ni egboi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for crop growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help bring the deep green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my yam mounds make the yams grow much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your yams need to grow. When you clear the weeds, all the soil nutrients go straight into feeding the yam roots, allowing the tubers to expand.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ Nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my cassava stem cuttings when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the rain has wet the soil deeply for a few continuous days. Planting cassava in dry soil causes the stem cuttings to lose moisture and die before they can produce roots.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi tɛ̃ɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ afee shoo ni amɛgboi dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: If you plant maize seeds too deep, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy dirt and may die underground. Planting them about the depth of your thumb knuckle gives them the best chance to sprout quickly.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ odu amɛ tamɔ bɔ ni otsitsi bibioo lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe fɛɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing funnels of maize plants. Applying approved treatments directly into the center of the leaf funnel early in the morning or late in the evening will control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper fruits rotting and dropping to the ground before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fruit rot in peppers is often caused by fungal diseases that spread in damp weather or by insect bites that let rot inside. Clearing fallen leaves, spacing plants for airflow, and removing infected fruits keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ loo ŋmeii ni kɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ajiemɔ Shi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛ aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They temporarily droop to conserve water and will naturally bounce back when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛbaakoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu nu he. ni ebaaku esɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground directly around the base of the main stem begins to crack from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting the soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a plant family that naturally captures nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. This enriches the ground and provides free plant food for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: How do I know when my rubber trees are old enough to start tapping for latex?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi rɔba tswaa?

english: Rubber trees usually need 5 to 6 years of proper growth to become mature enough for tapping. Tapping them before this age weakens the tree stem and permanently lowers the amount of latex you can collect over its lifetime.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei biɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 6 ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atswa amɛ. Nɛkɛ gbee ni tswaa oya nɛɛ baaha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa latɛs ni obaanyɛ obua naa yɛ owala be fɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What will happen to my rubber farm if I start harvesting latex after just two years?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi rɔbɔt ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mibɔi latɛs ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ naa yɛ afii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvesting at two years damages young stems because they are not strong enough. It stunts the tree's overall growth, causes severe wound scarring, and can shorten the lifespan of your trees.
ga: Nikpamɔ beni eye afii enyɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii bibii lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa bɔ ni sa. Etsiɔ tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ naa. ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni naa wa baa ni ehaa tsei awala be feɔ kuku.

english: Apart from counting years, how can I tell if a rubber tree trunk is ready for tapping?
ga: Kɛfata afii lɛ akanemɔ he lɛ Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ rɔba tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha gbee?

english: You can measure the thickness around the trunk. A rubber tree is generally ready for tapping when its trunk circumference reaches about 50 centimeters at a height of one meter from the ground.
ga: Ebaanyɛ esusu ŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle gbɔmɔtso lɛ he lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ miihe ashɛ sɛntimita 50 ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ miihe ashɛ mita 1.

english: How often am I supposed to collect latex from my rubber trees without hurting them?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mabua latɛs ni jɛ rɔbɔt tso mli lɛ naa ni miyeee lɛ awui?

english: Rubber trees need sufficient time to rest and rebuild fluid inside their bark. Tapping every single day causes extreme stress to the crop, so trees need at least 24 to 48 hours of rest between each collection.
ga: Rɔba tsei he miihia be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfee nu ekoŋŋ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Daa gbi ni akɛtswaa tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ, no hewɔ lɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abua naa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ.

english: Why does my rubber tree stop dripping latex a few hours after I make a fresh cut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rubber trees naturally seal their cuts to protect themselves from losing too much fluid and drying out. This is normal plant behavior, which is why the tree must rest before you make another light cut.
ga: Sapwood lɛ tsiɔ he ni afo lɛ naa koni ebu ehe koni nu babaoo akaje mli ni ekagbi. Enɛ ji tsei asubaŋ ni yaa nɔ daa. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe dani ogbe kane lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Is there a specific month or season in the year when I should open the rubber tapping season?
ga: Ani nyɔŋ loo be pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ rɔbɔt tswamɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Farmers typically open the main tapping season around January during dry conditions. Heavy rains can wash away dripping latex and cause fungal infections in the fresh bark cuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ gbeleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ be titri lɛ naa yɛ January be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ latɛs ni hoɔ lɛ he ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba tso lɛ yibii heei lɛ amli.

english: Why are my rubber trees developing big rough scars on their bark after tapping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ beni etswa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Scars form when bark is cut too deeply into the wood underneath or when young trees are tapped before they are mature enough to heal properly. Safe tapping only cuts the outer bark layer.
