ga: Scarring baa kɛji akɛ afo tso lɛ yibii lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ afo tsei bibii dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsa jogbaŋŋ. Hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ pɛ ji he ni afoɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why does the cut bark on my rubber trees take so long to regrow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afo yɛ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Bark regrows slowly if the tree is tapped too frequently without enough rest, or if cuts are made too deep. Giving the tree enough resting days allows the bark to heal cleanly and smoothly.
ga: Bark lɛ baafee ehee fiofio. Kɛji otswa tsei shii abɔ tsɔ ni onaaa hejɔɔmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa, loo kɛji ofolɔ mli tsɔ Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ hejɔɔmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he atse ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can tapping a tree too early or too frequently cause it to dry up and die?
ga: Ani tso ni atswaa oya loo shii abɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha egbi ni egbe lɛ?

english: Yes, extracting fluid continuously without resting periods starves the tree of essential nutrients, leading to disease, permanent bark damage, and eventual death of the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni no baaha hela aba tso lɛ nɔ ni ebaafite tso lɛ yibii lɛ daa. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ.

english: What should I do if I already tapped my young rubber trees too early and caused scarring?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mifo rɔbɔt tso ko oya tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ba?

english: You should stop tapping them immediately and allow the trees to rest for a season or two. Giving them time without cuts helps the bark heal and allows the trunk to gain full strength.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa tso lɛ tswaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni oha tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be kome loo bei enyɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ be ni amɛfooo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ shɛɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to grow green and healthy; when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Treating the crop for pests early helps prevent the leaves from shrinking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the cocoa can survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do extended farmers advise planting cowpeas or beans between rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi wuji woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, which naturally fertilizes the soil for maize. Their leaves also cover the ground to block weeds and keep water in the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Baai lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli ni nu akahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant three or four maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole causes the plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stalks that produce very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why should I cover my newly planted yam mounds with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi aha sweet potato ni adu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mulching yam mounds with dry grass shields the buried seed yam from excessive sun heat, prevents heavy rainfall from washing away the soil mound, and helps retain soil moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ha ŋmeii ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ fe nine ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli baa lɛ he. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ sũ ni abua naa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: What is eating holes in my maize leaves and leaving saw-dust like material inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ amli ni ashiɔ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feed on the soft inner leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why are all the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or if the soil is given too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough regular water during flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lowest leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the lower fronds on my oil palm trees turn brown and hang down during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees shed or drop lower leaves during dry spells to conserve water. The tree cuts off moisture to older outer leaves so it can send remaining water to the growing shoot in the center.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛtsɔɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛya tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow when it stops raining for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain stops, the soil quickly loses moisture. Crops need water to draw up nutrients from the soil; without enough water, the leaves cannot make food, causing the plant to stress, turn yellow, and wilt to conserve water.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei hia nu koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu faaa lɛ Baai nyɛŋ afee niyenii. kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he

english: If crops don't get enough water, their leaves curl, dry up, or wilt during the dry afternoon heat. If they get too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, roots rot in muddy soil, and the plant stops growing.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ, loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ muji lɛ mli. ni tsei kpaɔ shweremɔ

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the plant before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when water supply is uneven—such as a dry period followed by heavy watering or rain. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ be ni sa mli, tamɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi ni nu ni mli wa loo nugbɔ nɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Is it safe for me to pump water straight from a river like the Afram to water my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo nu tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ faa ko tamɔ Afram mli koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu?

english: Yes, natural river water carries good minerals for crops. However, you should make sure the water is free from dangerous chemical runoffs or illegal mining pollution before using it on your food crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shika tsuru ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ faa mli nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ koni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo mujiwoo ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko yɛ nu lɛ mli. dani okɛwo oniyenii tsei lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady water, especially when forming flowers and cobs. When water is scarce, the plant focuses on surviving rather than feeding the seeds, leading to small or incomplete cobs.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa daa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa wala mlihilɛ nɔ fe amɛdumɔwui lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant and harvest crops all year round if I have a water source nearby?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nii ni makpa nii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ miyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi hu?

english: Yes. By using simple irrigation to supply water during dry periods, you do not have to wait for the rains. You can grow and harvest crops two or three times a year when market prices are highest.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛhaa nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ. Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ afi mli beni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do crops in northern Ghana need different watering plans compared to crops in the south?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ he hiaa ni ato nu he gbɛjianɔi srɔtoi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: The north has a single, shorter rainy season with long dry periods, while the south gets two rainy seasons. Crops in the north lose water faster due to intense heat, so they require planned irrigation to survive dry spells.
ga: Kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei enyɔ yɔɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ato nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What is irrigation and how does it help my farm compared to waiting for rain?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛtoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mɛmɔ he?

english: Irrigation is the practice of artificially bringing water from river streams, wells, or dams to your farm through pipes, pumps, or channels. It keeps your crops growing continuously without depending on unpredictable weather.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ji nu ni jɛɔ faa, nu bu, loo faa mli kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ paipii, pɔmpii, loo gbɛi ni akɛfee lɛ nɔ. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara daa ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ.

english: How can government irrigation projects in my area directly benefit my small farm?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ nu shwiemɔ nitsumɔ ko ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Government projects build shared canals, dams, and water channels near farm areas. This brings reliable water close to your land, making it cheaper and easier for you to water your crops continuously.
ga: Nɔyeli nitsumɔi maa faai, nu ŋshɔi kɛ nu gbɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ okwaayeli hei. Enɛ baaha nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ abɛŋkɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ehaa ejara waaa ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does watering my crops at their base work better than splashing water over all the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu yɛ eshishigbɛ fe ni oooha eshishigbɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots are what actually absorb water for the plant. Directing water to the soil at the base feeds the roots directly, reduces water loss from evaporation, and prevents wet leaves from developing fungal diseases.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni shwieɔ nu diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa tso lɛ. Nu ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ. Tsɔ nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ lasu mli lɛ shi ni otsi baa ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akaba

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees when starting a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe beni mijeɔ shikpɔŋ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full sun. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil moist while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes showing up in my young maize leaves, and why are caterpillars hiding in the center of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ. Ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the leaves and feed on the growing point of the plant, which stops the maize from developing healthy cobs if not managed early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa afee ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make my maize grow better when I plant it the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This leaves nutrient-rich soil behind for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and droop in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In extreme sun, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves curl to reduce water loss, which is normal as long as the plant recovers when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa, be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my garden pepper plants before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from sudden heat spikes or dry soil. The plant casts off its flowers to protect itself and save energy until moisture and temperature balance out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ trukaa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baajie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa baafee ekome.

english: Why do yam leaves need to climb up tall wooden stakes instead of just growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Staking gets the leaves off the wet ground to capture maximum sunlight for food production while protecting the plant from soil-borne leaf diseases, leading to bigger yam tubers underneath.
ga: Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni emɔ hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli tsei ahe helai ahe. Enɛ haa sweet potato tuber agbo ko baa shishi.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully formed under the soil without digging up the whole stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sũ eyi ŋmei shishifãi amli obɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: As cassava reaches full maturity (usually between 9 to 12 months), the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop naturally. You can gently clear the soil near the main stem to inspect root thickness.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa (bei pii lɛ, yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ) lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Obaanyɛ Ojie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso wulu lɛ fiofio koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ha.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with dark green leaves but produce very little fruit when I put too much manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen from excessive manure makes the plant put all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves, forgetting to form flowers and fruit. Plants need a balanced mix of nutrients to produce food.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ ŋmeii babaoo mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni amɛhiɛ kpaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa koni amɛná niyenii.

english: Why do tall weeds near my crops make my crops produce tiny yields even when rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. Even with good rain, the weeds steal food away from the crop's roots, causing the crop to starve.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around one plantain stem to get big bunches?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii enyiɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ dumɔwu kome he koni maná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: It is best to leave only one main flowering plant, one medium follower stem, and one small shoot. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi fɔfɔi tso titri kome pɛ. 1 fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ 1 ŋmɔshi nibii bibii - ni ashiɔ ŋmɔji babaoo tsɔ lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and build strong stalks, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni wa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. If the soil gets too dry or too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the growing tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them off the wet ground where diseases and insects spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ baai lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ la mli, ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, he ni helai kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the insects early stops the leaves from crumpling.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ helai yɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai ahe tsamɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water drowns the soil and deprives roots of air, allowing waterborne fungi to attack. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi ni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plants die, this trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ bibii bibii. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are growing a small distance away?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo po?

english: Weed roots spread quickly underground to drink up soil water and steal nutrients before your crops can reach them, starving your plants even if they look separate above ground.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛnu shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he moŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out and scorch in direct sunlight. Big trees provide shade and keep the air cool, acting as natural shields while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibi be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to get a deep rain before putting seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu dumɔwui?

english: Seeds need a steady soak of moisture to break open their hard outer shell and sprout. Planting in hot, dry soil keeps seeds inactive or leaves them vulnerable to insects and birds.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛgbala amɛhewolo ni wa lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akatsu nii loo ebaaha kooloi kɛ okpoi anyɛ aye amɛ oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the funnel-like center of young maize leaves because it is dark, moist, and tender to eat. Checking the funnels early helps you treat them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ni tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ ediŋ, amɛmli edɔ, ni amɛhe yɛ blɛoo kɛ aye amɛ. Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil has run out of key nutrients like nitrogen. Mixing organic matter, animal manure, or natural compost into the soil restores these nutrients so the leaves can turn green and feed the plant again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if insect pests are attacking my crops or if the plants are just suffering from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Insect attacks leave visible marks like holes in leaves, chewed stems, or sticky fluids, whereas heat stress causes the entire plant to wilt evenly or curl its leaves without any parts being eaten.
ga: Koolooi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ shiɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ bu yɛ baai amli, tsei ni aŋɔ, loo nu ni kpɛɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ajaraa baai lɛ amli loo abɔleɔ amɛhe ni ayeee fã ko kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up during the hottest time of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces its leaf surface to prevent losing too much water in intense heat. If the leaves unfold by evening, the crop is managing the heat well.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ dɔlɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I put wood ash from my kitchen fire onto my farm soil to help my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ ni jɛɔ shĩa la mli lɛ afata sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, wood ash supplies potassium to the soil and helps reduce soil acidity, making it easier for crops like cassava and vegetables to absorb nutrients and grow strong roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ haa potassium baa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ aduawai akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛwaje amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant cassava on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmei wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How does covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass help them during dry spells?
ga: Bɔ ni jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the dirt by shielding it from the harsh sun, keeping the soil cool and reducing how often you need to water.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ebuɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is under stress, which is often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients needed for fruit formation.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ ni bɛ

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout quickly if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the ground is packed too hard, or if there is not enough moisture to trigger the seed to wake up and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ate shi ni amɛdara lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my garden leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mibɔɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black spots during wet weather are usually fungal diseases that thrive in high humidity. Spacing your plants further apart allows wind to blow through and dry the leaves, slowing down the spread.
ga: Black spot yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaha gbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Weeds are wild plants with naturally strong roots designed to aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients ahead of cultivated crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni afee koni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ aju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani amɛdu tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: High heat, lack of water, or a shortage of tiny insect pollinators cause cocoa trees to shed flowers. The tree drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself when it feels stressed.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nibii bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ Haa kookoo tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji amɛmiihao.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, exposing them to light and preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces them to steal food and water from the main plantain tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only 2 or 3 strong ones, ensuring the main tree produces a large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛná ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi koni tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting maize too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss through their foliage. This is a natural defense mechanism that helps the plant survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why is my maize remaining short and yellow even after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli po lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can soak it up. If applied on very dry ground or if weeds absorb it first, the maize plant cannot take in the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo hei ni egbi waa loo kɛji akɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Abɛi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and steal the soil food, water, and sunlight your plants need. Clearing weeds early ensures all nutrients go straight to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when the plant experiences irregular watering while the tomatoes are forming.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ naa nu ni ejaaa be mli ni tomatoi lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do small green worms appear inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miije kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on young leaves. They prefer feeding on the soft, growing heart of the maize plant where it is dark and moist.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai bibii anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛ ye ŋmei tso lɛ tsui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni edɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or by a plant virus they carry. These insects feed on leaf sap, causing the young leaves to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ mites loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli nu. haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ shoo

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain plants next to them when I clear a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Beni mijieɔ ŋmɔ hee ko mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the cool shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small when I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close to each other, their roots compete under the soil for nutrients, water, and space. Giving each plant enough room allows the roots to expand freely and swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my maize yield get worse if I plant it on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ kɛji midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land removes the same soil nutrients repeatedly and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating your maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ shii abɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa ekoŋŋ ni ekpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plants before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extremely hot days helps the flowers stay on the plant and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛhi tso lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun but look normal again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during hot afternoons as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much water in the heat. As long as the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is managing the heat, but it shows the crop needs regular watering.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ shwieee shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikwɛ dɔlɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nɔ nu daa.

english: What causes my maize stems to fall over easily whenever there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are shallow or weak, often caused by shallow planting or loose soil. Mounding up soil around the base of the maize stalks as they grow gives the roots stronger anchor support against wind.
ga: Abɛi baashwie eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛbɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛbaa ji dumɔwui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee. Shikpɔŋ ni ooobɔle ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi beni edaa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the younger top leaves, indicating it is time to apply nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil while the crop is actively growing, usually a few weeks after planting and right before flowering. Applying fertilizer to very dry soil can burn roots, while applying it during heavy rains causes it to wash away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops actually reduce my final harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ baa shi ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the nutrients and moisture in the soil go directly into growing your crops rather than feeding unwanted plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkwɛ tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei ni he ehiaaa amɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my watermelons start rotting from the bottom side while still attached to the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi shi ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ wain tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in watermelons happens when the fruit sits directly on wet soil or when the soil lacks balanced moisture and calcium. Placing dry straw under growing melons keeps them dry and prevents soil rot from starting.
ga: Butt rot ni yɔɔ watermelon mli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ aduawai lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ calcium bɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo melon ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha melon lɛ agbi ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, a severe viral infection spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. It causes branches to swell, reduces pod yield, and can eventually kill the tree.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi titri. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa pod lɛ yibiiwoo baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Is there any chemical spray I can buy to cure my cocoa trees if they get swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe koni mikɛtsa mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe?

english: Currently, there is no chemical cure or medicine for Swollen Shoot disease. The only effective way to stop it from spreading to your healthy trees is to cut down and remove the infected trees.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa loo tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa fãji ni efuu lɛ. Gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli ji ni ofolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ojie amɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa trees to suddenly stop bearing pods and slowly die off?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ fiofio?

english: A major cause of sudden decline and death in cocoa trees across Ghana is Swollen Shoot disease. It weakens the tree's system over time, stopping pod production before killing the plant.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ kookoo tsei ni baa shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ baa ji bud swelling hela. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ekpaa pod feemɔ dani egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Where can I get reliable young cocoa plants to start or expand my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana cacao tsei bibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni mikɛje ŋmɔ shishi loo mikɛgbala mli?

english: You can obtain healthy, high-quality cocoa seedlings directly from the government's Seed Production Division or through local agricultural extension officers who distribute approved varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kookoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni hɔ̃ɔ kookoo srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I get cocoa seedlings from the government instead of planting seeds from my own harvested pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maná kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ dɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, bo diɛŋtsɛ okpaa?

english: Government seedlings raised by the Seed Production Division are specially bred hybrid varieties that grow faster, produce more pods, and have better natural strength against common diseases compared to regular farm seeds.
ga: Nɔyeli dumɔwui ni Dumɔwui Ahe Nitsumɔhe lɛ duɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome ni daa oya. Ha pods babaoo ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves look soft and reddish before they turn green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ oblahii kɛ etsuru dani amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: New cocoa leaves produce a natural reddish color to protect their tender young tissue from harsh sunlight. As the leaf grows stronger and matures, it naturally turns deep green.
ga: Kookoo baai heei feɔ su tsuru ko ni buɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Beni baai lɛ mli wa ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa.

english: Why are some of my cocoa trees producing pods after just two years while old trees took much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni cacao lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe nakai.

english: Modern high-yield cocoa varieties distributed today are bred to mature very quickly, often bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties naturally took 4 to 5 years to start producing.
ga: Atsɔse ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya waa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ feemɔ shishi.

english: Who can I report to if I notice strange disease symptoms on my cocoa farm that I don't understand?
ga: Kɛji ona okadi ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli ni minuuu shishi Namɔ manyɛ mabɔ amaniɛ?

english: You can visit or contact your local agricultural extension officer or the nearest Seed Production Division office. Their officers are available to inspect your farm and give you advice.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara loo oyatswa okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ loo Seed Production Division nitsumɔhe ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ. Amɛ nitsulɔi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwo bo ŋaa.

english: Can the government help me get new cocoa trees if I have to cut down my old diseased farm?
ga: Ani nɔyeli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná kookoo tsei heei? Ni kɛji akɛ ehe bahia ni mafo ŋmɔ momo ko ni hela emɔ mli lɛ hu?

english: Yes, agricultural officers help farmers clear infected farms and can assist you in getting fresh, disease-free seedlings from government nurseries to replant your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli he onukpai yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛgbeɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oná dumɔwui heei ni hela bɛ mli kɛjɛ nɔyeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei lɛ koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the cocoa seedlings I am buying are safe and free from diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni hela bɛ mli?

english: The safest way to get healthy seedlings is to receive them directly from recognized government bodies like the Seed Production Division, where young plants are raised under strict health conditions.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ji ni ana kɛjɛ maŋ nɔyeli nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui afeemɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛnamɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa shishi.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or when the ground is too flooded with water, which drowns the roots and stops them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa niyenii yeli.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time or different plants to restore its richness.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ekɛ be haaaa sũ lɛ loo tsei krokomɛi koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛwo nii

english: Why do I need to loosen the soil before planting seeds instead of just poking a hole in the hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie sũ lɛ dani adu dumɔwui lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil creates space for soft young plant roots to spread quickly, breathe air, and absorb water easily so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. emuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ Ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi mlɛo koni eha tsei adara waa.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants and very small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when they are exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and weak root systems that burn easily in direct sun; they need shade trees around them to keep them cool and moist while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why did the leaves on my crops dry up and burn after I put fertilizer on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts; putting them directly on the leaves or too close to the stem can burn the plant tissue. Fertilizer should be placed in the soil a short distance away from the plant stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: Why is it wasteful to spray pest chemicals on my crops right before it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the plant leaves into the soil before it has time to work, leaving your crops unprotected against insects and wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛtsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ahe, ni ehaa oshika hu fiteɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars and bugs suddenly attack my farm after the first heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tutua miŋmɔ lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The warm, wet weather after early rains creates ideal conditions for insect eggs to hatch, and the soft new leaves on young crops provide abundant food for young pests.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ba kɛha kooloi bibii lɛ ni amɛfɔ. Ni baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo.

english: How do simple weeds actually harm my cassava plants if there is enough land for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mi yucca tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the soil that your cassava needs to build big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems and branches from my crop bushes if I want more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ jwɛi mli kɛji miitao aduawai babaoo?

english: Removing excess leaves and non-producing branches forces the plant to send all its water and nutrients directly into making bigger, healthier fruit instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow healthy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores soil nutrients and stops the yellowing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ebaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the ground, while groundnuts and beans are leguminous crops that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil through their roots, making the soil rich for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji ŋmei ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat. Keeping larger trees or planting shade crops like plantains around them protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for water, light, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce larger and healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo aduawai akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: Those holes are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the plant. Applying approved pest treatments or recommended organic solutions early in the morning or late evening helps eliminate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, aphids, or thrips sucking the sap from leaves. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, aphids, loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Excess water staying in the ground deprives cassava roots of oxygen, causing them to decay and rot. Digging proper drainage channels allows surplus rainwater to flow away from the root zone.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni atsa lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha obɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because afternoon heat evaporates water before the roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets left on leaves can burn the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, water supply is irregular, or there are few insects around to pollinate them. Consistent watering and planting flowers that attract bees can improve fruit setup.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni baanyɛ afee pollination. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ fɔfɔii ni aduɔ koni akɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground so they capture maximum light and stay free from leaf spot diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛmɔmɔ la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛhi shi ni baa lɛ nɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to intense heat and direct sun. They need shade plants like plantains or gliricidia during their first two years to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to help retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo glicidia yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves lifted off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. When vines climb stakes, the leaves make more energy, leading to larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha hewalɛ babaoo aba. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen to feed the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil with free plant food for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Too many side shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, resulting in bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo loo afã tsei lɛ kɛ tso nyɛ titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain jwɛi lɛ bafee agbo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow thin and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving the main crops starved and stunted regardless of rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ baa shi ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the sap beneath young leaves, or by plant viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves with green droppings in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni ŋmeii eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls inside the growing central funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh foliage away from daylight.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects. Without proper moisture and pollination, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ fɔfɔi ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: If I plant my cassava stem cuttings slanted instead of straight up in the ground, how does it affect growth?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ooodu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ Te ebaaná dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant (around 45 degrees) encourages roots to grow deeper in search of moisture while keeping tubers grouped together near the soil surface, making harvest easier.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ŋmeii lɛ afee ekome kɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa ekpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant them under plantain trees or tall shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ dumɔwui loo tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living canopy shade and traps moisture in the air, creating a soft microclimate that keeps the delicate cocoa leaves from burning while roots get established.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsiɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa koni ekashã yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow along the middle vein?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting along the central vein usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaves and fast growth. This happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or heavy rains wash nitrogen out of reach of the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi edaa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nitrogen lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall and bushy above ground but produce very small tuber roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ?

english: When the soil is too hard or contains too much leaf-building nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing upper foliage. For healthy tubers, cassava needs loose, mound-ploughed soil so the roots can expand easily and store food underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo ni feɔ baai lɛ fa babaoo. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa eŋwɛi baai lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛha yitso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Cassava he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms drying up and falling off before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli ewo fɔfɔi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii fata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This provides free natural fertilizer to neighboring crops like maize and keeps the soil healthy for next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa yaka, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes instead of creeping along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all their leaves to build food for the growing tuber under the dirt. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to air and light while preventing leaf mold and rot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni ehaa eboteɔ mli lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ hu naa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshwieee shi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon sunshine, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves curl to protect themselves from losing more moisture, and they usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow short and thin even when I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the plant food and water go directly into making your crops grow big.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei aniyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do the roots of my garden vegetables turn black and rot when water sits on my land after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the field for too long, air gets trapped out of the soil, causing the roots to drown and fall victim to fungal rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgbeeɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I harvest smaller maize cobs when I put many seeds closely together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa bibii toɔ lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fataa he Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Placing seeds too close together forces the growing plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each crop its own area to gather resources, leading to bigger plants and larger cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni miida lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛbua nibii anaa. Enɛ haa tsei wuji kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the heavy July rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi yɛ July mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains in July can wash away key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and clog the roots with too much water. When roots drown, they cannot feed the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ July mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu babaoo atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli lɛ Enyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii aha tsei lɛ Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What farm work should I focus on when heavy rain in July keeps me from clearing the land?
ga: Mɛɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔ esa akɛ ama nɔ mi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ July mli? Ani ehaaa anyɛ ajie jɛmɛ?

english: During wet months like July when field work is difficult, you should focus on post-harvest activities, preparing grain stores, cleaning equipment, or processing harvested cassava into shelf-stable foods like gari.
ga: Yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa, tamɔ July, be mli ni ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ wa lɛ, Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ nitsumɔi anɔ. Nibii ni akɛsaa ŋmaa shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ahe saamɔ loo ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni efee niyenii ni anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi tamɔ gari.

english: How can I store my harvested maize in bags without insects eating all of it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ baagi mli ni kooloi yeee fɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp environments. Dry your maize thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are hard before putting them into airtight bags (hermetic bags), which suffocate any insects trying to enter.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli. (Vacuum bag) ni haa kooloi bibii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil within just two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots continue to breathe and lose water rapidly once cut from the stem. Because they lack a thick protective skin, air causes them to rot quickly unless they are processed or buried in wet sawdust.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji akɛ, nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni mli wa bɛ. No hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa egboɔ oya, ja atsu he nii loo afu yɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ amli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the light, making them tall and weak instead of developing thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse ni wa.

english: Why am I supposed to put fertilizer a few inches away from the plant stem instead of right against it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 moŋ fe ni mabɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the stem can burn the soft plant tissue, whereas placing it a few inches away allows the roots to safely draw in the nutrients from the wet soil.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ toɔ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its power to grow crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei dɔŋŋ?

english: If your crops look stunted, have light green leaves, or produce smaller yields than in previous years despite good rain, the soil has run out of nutrients and needs compost, manure, or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ awo mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, leaving plenty of room for the slower cassava to grow and expand later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo haa ŋmei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the living shade and soil moisture needed for cocoa trees to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight the main mother tree for nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers gives you healthier plants and larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha oná tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newest leaves at the top to survive, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha ni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for other crops?
