ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, they release that nitrogen back into the soil, feeding the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long because the roots cannot breathe without air in the soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry heat wave that bakes the ground. If seeds germinate after that single rain, the heat will dry out and kill the young seedlings before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbeɔ tsei bibii dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a sign that tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies are feeding on the underside of the leaves and spreading plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies lɛ he okadi. Niyenii taomɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tso mli helai ni haa shweremɔ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during hot dry periods or sudden changes in water availability stress the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to preserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni edɔ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ mli haomɔ tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet leaves touching the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ni efɔ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds cause my maize crop to produce small and light cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-abele lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, ground moisture, and sunlight away from your crop. When maize has to fight weeds, it lacks the energy to fill out the corn cobs completely.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni hulu la lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni esa akɛ ŋmãa kɛ jwɛi awui lɛ ŋmãa bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Cassava tubers need well-drained soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits in the ground without draining, it suffocates the roots and causes fungal rots to develop underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛmu. Beni afu nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong rainstorms hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ahum ni naa wa ko tswa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy weight at the top when bearing fruit. Heavy rains soften the soil, making it easy for strong winds to push the top-heavy plants out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ́ amɛmiiwo yibii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ akɛ ebaatsi tsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if there is no rain during the time it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli?

english: Maize requires steady moisture during flowering to form grains. A dry spell at this stage prevents proper pollination, leading to empty cobs or missing kernels on the cob.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi be mli koni ewo dumɔwui. Shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo loo dumɔwui bɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans alongside my main crop makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. As the plant grows and breaks down, it releases this nitrogen into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for nearby crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛgboi Ebaajie nitrogen nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm seem to grow much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt very quickly to local soils, allowing them to absorb available water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect activity needed to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting shoots in storage before I even take them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break their resting phase when humidity and air temperature rise in storage, signaling to the tuber that it is time to start growing again.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baatsɔ hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ nitoohe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when the soil holds too much water, preventing the plant's roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the leaves. These pests suck the sap out of the young leaves, causing them to twist, wrinkle, and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival. They act like unwanted guests that steal the water, soil nutrients, and sunlight that your crops need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the air gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. High heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔii agbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my papaya trees produce flowers but never grow any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male papaya trees only produce flowers to pollinate other trees, but they will never produce fruit themselves.
ga: Papaya tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Papaya tsei hii fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛwo tsei krokomɛi amli pɛ. Shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwoŋ yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with water for too long without proper drainage. Heavy clay soil during heavy rains suffocates the roots, allowing rot fungus to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to guide and tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔɔ gbɛ ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to spread their leaves in the sun. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily and helps the plant trap maximum sunlight to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seed right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry hot spell. Planting too early means the seeds might germinate, but the hot dry soil will dry out and kill the young seedlings before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbiɔ ni egbeɔ tsei bibii dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on dry soil when there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔtsi wɔhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant's roots can drink it up. If you put dry fertilizer on dry soil in hot sun, it cannot feed the plant and can actually burn and damage the roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei niyenii. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ashã ni efite.

english: Why do plantains growing in my backyard look different from the ones planted on large forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Backyard plantains often receive continuous water, shade, and kitchen waste rich in organic nutrients, which helps them grow steadily. In open forest fields, crops face more direct sunlight, stronger winds, and competition from wild weeds, which changes how quickly they mature and how much care they require.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ naa nu, hulutsoo, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ daa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛshwereɔ. yɛ kooi amli hei ni agbele naa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ koo mli jwɛi amli lɛ kpeɔ. Enɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain shoots when planting on a large plot of land?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafee mi-plantains lɛ he gbɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ he ko ni da?

english: Plantains need about 3 meters (10 feet) of space between each plant. Giving them enough distance prevents their broad leaves from blocking sunlight from each other and ensures their shallow roots get enough soil nutrients to yield large bunches.
ga: Plantains he miihia aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaatsi baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant too many plantain suckers on a small piece of land near my house?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he bibioo ko? Ani ebɛŋkɛ shia?

english: Yes, crowding too many plantain suckers on a small plot causes them to fight for water, sunlight, and soil food. This competition results in thin, tall plants that produce small fruit bunches or fall over easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain tsei babaoo yɛ he bibioo ko. Enɛ haa amɛshiɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ ha tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ ni amɛfee mlɛo aahu akɛ amɛwo aduawai bibii loo amɛgbee shi oya.

english: Why do crops grow so fast when I first clear a forest plot for farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya nɛkɛ? Be ni mijie koo mli shikpɔŋ kɛha okwaayeli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Forest soil has accumulated fallen leaves and decaying organic material over many years, creating a thick layer of natural plant food (humus) that gives newly planted crops a powerful boost in early growth.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ buaa baai ni egbee shi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (humus) ni mli tse ni haa tsei ni adu ehee lɛ hewalɛ ni haa amɛdaraa mra lɛ baa.

english: Should I burn the cut bush and trees when clearing forest land to plant crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ beni mijieɔ koo mli shikpɔŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but intense heat destroys essential soil nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms. Clearing without burning leaves organic matter to rot, which naturally feeds your plantain roots over time.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ he ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Enɛ baaha o-plantain shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my plantain plant keep sprouting extra small shoots around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni bɔle Eshishitoo lɛ he ji be fɛɛ be

english: Plantains naturally reproduce by growing baby shoots called 'suckers' from their underground corm. Leaving too many suckers starves the main stem, so you should prune extra shoots and keep only one or two strong ones.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘ŋmeii’ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ akumɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1-2 pɛ ato.

english: Do plantains prefer growing in full sunlight or under heavy tree shade?
ga: Ani plantains sumɔɔ ni adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ tsei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ashishi?

english: Plantains grow best in bright, open sunlight once established. While young shoots tolerate partial shade, heavy shade slows down their leaf production and prevents big bunches from forming.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛji etswa shi pɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii lɛ kpɛɔ hulutsoo fã ko naa moŋ. Shi hulutsoo ni tsii baaha tsei lɛ ahe afee mlɛo ni ebaatsi kui wuji anaa koni amɛkafee.

english: Why do plantain plants bend or fall over when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are soft and their roots stay near the soil surface. When a bunch becomes heavy, wind or weight can easily pull the stem down, so supporting heavy bearing trees with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles is necessary.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ loo tsiimɔ baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ shishi oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa afi tsei ni woɔ muji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why does my plantain yield get smaller after growing plantains on the same land for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi beni mikɛ afii babaoo edu yɛ he kome lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains consume large amounts of soil nutrients like potassium and nitrogen. Continuous planting without adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer drains the soil energy, leading to smaller fruit yields over time.
ga: Plantains yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ haa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I grow plantains alongside other crops like young cocoa or vegetables on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ kookoo bibii loo aduawai ahe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, plantains work well alongside young cocoa or shade-loving crops. Their fast-growing, wide leaves provide temporary shade and retain soil moisture, protecting young seedlings while providing early harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii loo tsei krokomɛi ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii mra.

english: How can my soil continue to feed crops even when the rain stops falling for a long time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Soil that is rich in organic matter acts like a sponge deep underground. It stores water from previous rains and keeps it in the root zone so crops can keep drinking even during a dry period.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Emɔɔ nu ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ tsutsu lɛ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii anu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: What should I do with dead grass and leaves after clearing my land to keep moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko?

english: Instead of burning cleared vegetation, spread it over your soil as mulch. This cover shades the ground from the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating, and slow-cooks into rich food for your crops.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã tsei ni ajie lɛ Ha akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehooɔ blɛoo koni ekɛfee niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some crops take up to two or three years before I get a good harvest from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ afii enyɔ loo etɛ dani mináa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Long-term crops like cocoa, oil palm, or cassava spend their early years building deep root systems and strong trunks. Once established after two or three years, they produce heavy harvests for a long time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei fɔ loo ŋmei heɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ hejɔɔmɔ. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa Kɛji ato amɛ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ Amɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How long will it take for me to know if the money and effort I put into my new farm will pay off?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani male kɛji shika kɛ mɔdɛŋ ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii?

english: For quick crops like maize or vegetables, you see results in a few months, but for major land improvements or tree crops, it takes two to three years to see the full financial return on your investment.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai Obaana nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi kɛha shikpɔŋ loo tsei ahe tsakemɔi wuji Ekolɛ ebaahe afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani ona shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ mli nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has good soil that will support crops for multiple years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ afii babaoo?

english: Good soil is typically dark in color, crumbly to the touch, holds moisture well when squeezed, and has visible signs of life like earthworms and decomposing leaf litter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɔ mli ni enaa wala he okadii, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Can I keep planting crops on the same fertile land for three years in a row without damaging it?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni mifiteee?

english: You can, provided you rotate different crop types—like putting legumes after maize—or regularly add manure to replace the nutrients the plants draw out of the ground each year.
ga: Obaanyɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmãa ni okɛbaafata ŋmãa he lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he daa koni ekɛye niyenii ni tsei lɛ gbalaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it better for us to gather as a family group to farm a large piece of land instead of working alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ wɔɔto wekui akui koni wɔtsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔji wuji anɔ moŋ fe ni wɔkome too wɔbaatsu nii lɛ?

english: Group labor allows heavy tasks like land clearing and planting to be finished quickly before the weather changes, saving individual energy and reducing high labor costs.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa anyɛɔ agbeɔ nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anaa oya dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ mɔ diɛŋtsɛ hewalɛ toɔ he ni ehaa nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo ni nɔ kwɔ baa shi

english: If I have a piece of land that is very wide, is it wise to plant the same crop across the entire field?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni da waa lɛ, ani esa akɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: It is safer to divide wide land among different crop varieties. Planting everything in one crop increases the risk of a single pest or disease wiping out your entire farm.
ga: He ni yɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ateŋ lɛ mlijaa babaoo. baafee shweshweeshwe Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela kome loo hela kome baafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Which crops are best to plant if I am worried that the rains will be poor this season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu kɛji nugbɔ gbonyo ni nɛɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ he miihao mi?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpea, millet, and sorghum are ideal because their roots go deep or they require very little water to complete their growth cycle.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ loo amɛhe ehiaaa nu fioo koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa.

english: What are these new or special farming methods officers talk about, and will they really give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni he nɛkɛ okwaayeli gbɛi heei loo krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ onukpai lɛ wieɔ he? Ni ani amɛbaahã mi yibiiwoo ni da fe no diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Modern techniques—such as correct seed spacing, line planting, and targeted composting—help crops use soil nutrients and light more efficiently, often doubling your harvest compared to traditional broadcasting methods.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ la tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛfeɔ nɔ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ toi enyɔ kɛ akɛto blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atswaa adafitswaa lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to plant cassava on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava prefers loose, well-drained sandy loam soil where its roots can easily expand underground, and it struggles in heavy clay or waterlogged soil where the tubers will rot.
ga: Cassava sumɔɔ ŋã ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eshishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya. ni esa akɛ ebɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni eyitso baagboi lɛ nɔ.

english: Does the part of the cassava stem I choose to plant affect how many tubers I will harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni mihalaa akɛ madu lɛ saa ŋmeii ayibɔ ni abaakpa lɛ he?

english: Yes, using healthy cuttings from the middle portion of mature cassava stems produces stronger roots and higher yields compared to using soft young tops or dry old bases.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmeii bibii ni egbi loo shishifãi momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Can I plant groundnuts between my cassava plants without damaging my cassava yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ ni mifiteee mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, groundnuts cover the ground to prevent weeds and fix nitrogen into the soil which nourishes the cassava, and groundnuts can be harvested early before the cassava leaves grow large enough to block light.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli koni jwɛi akaje mli ni ekɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Ni obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii mra. Dani ŋmei baai lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni baatsi kane lɛ naa lɛ,.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the leaves on top grow very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dara waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together or using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of sending food down to swell the underground roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsu hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: This is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that weakens the plant and reduces the size of your final harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does cassava survive dry seasons better than crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and relies on its deep root system, allowing the plant to go dormant until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ. Ha tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some cassava varieties taste bitter while others taste sweet when boiled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ŋɔɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ŋɔɔ kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ?

english: Bitter cassava contains higher amounts of natural plant chemicals that protect it from wild animals and pests, which means it requires extra processing like soaking or fermenting before it is safe to eat.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ koo mli kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni atsu he nii yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, tamɔ ni akɛwo nu mli loo ni akɛwo mli, dani abaanyɛ aye lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi duŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Once removed from the soil, cassava roots stop receiving nutrients from the plant stem and react quickly to air exposure, causing internal spoilage within two to three days unless processed.
ga: Kɛji ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii oya kɛji amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Amɛfiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli ja atsu he nii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and digging up a sample stem shows fully formed, thick tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Tso lɛ shishifomɔ tsɔɔ yitso ni mli tse ni eye emuu.

english: Is it better to leave cassava in the soil until I find a buyer or dig it all up at once?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooshi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaana mɔ ko ni baahe loo obaafo mli fɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature cassava unharvested in the ground acts as natural storage for several extra months, keeping the tubers fresh until you have a confirmed buyer or market ready.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpako lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli he ni akɛ nibii toɔ nyɔji babaoo. Ha tubers lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛyashi obaaná mɔ ko ni baahe loo jara ni ama nɔ mi akɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water logs your field, it starves the roots of air and prevents them from taking up nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu ni fa fe nine ho kɛtee oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa.

english: Is it a good idea to dig channels through my farm when heavy water gathers on the field?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafo nubu kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nu eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yes, digging drainage channels helps direct standing water away from your crops. Removing trapped water prevents root rot and keeps the soil healthy enough for crop roots to breathe and spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ odɛŋ lɛ he gbɛi ni oootsɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli. Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why shouldn't I dig or work my farm soil when it is completely soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ loo matsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Digging wet soil destroys its natural structure and creates hard lumps when it dries out. This hardened soil makes it very difficult for young crop roots to push through and grow deep into the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni akuɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni wa baa kɛji egbi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɛɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers make raised mounds or ridges before planting cassava in low-lying areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaafoi awo gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ dani amɛdu ŋmei yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges raise crop roots above the ground level, keeping them out of standing water while providing loose, well-drained soil that allows tubers to expand properly.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ woɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi nu jɛɛhei ni damɔ shi lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni baaha bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops need water when the top of the soil looks dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Dig down about two to three inches into the soil with your fingers or a cutlass. If the soil at that depth feels dry and crumbles easily, your crops need water; if it feels damp and sticks together, there is still enough moisture for the roots.
ga: Kɛ onine loo stiletto knife atsu nii ni okɛfo sũ lɛ mli 2-3 inch kɛji sũ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nakai shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. Nu he miihia onibii lɛ. Kɛji enu he akɛ edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the middle of the day even when there is moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon sun, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Drooping is the crop's natural way of protecting itself by reducing leaf area exposed to the sun, and the leaves usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ he ni ebaa ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ebaa shi lɛ nɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ he waaa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crop roots when the underground water level rises during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ tee ŋwɛi yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: When the water level under the ground rises close to the surface, crop roots stop growing downward and instead spread outward near the topsoil, making the plant dependent on surface moisture and easy to fall over in heavy winds.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ tee hiɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ damɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Which food crops grow well in areas of my farm that stay flooded for weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he ko ni nu ewo mli otsii babaoo?

english: Crops like swamp rice and sugarcane are adapted to survive in standing water, whereas crops like maize, peppers, and cassava quickly develop root rot and die if submerged for too long.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Atsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo oya ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do crop diseases spread so fast when there is high water and moisture on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ be mli ni nu babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria thrive in warm, wet conditions. Water droplets splashing off wet soil carry disease germs directly onto plant leaves and stems, allowing infections to spread quickly across the farm.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Does heavy rain wash away the fertilizer I apply to my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaje mli?

english: Yes, heavy rainfall causes fertilizer to wash away over the surface or sink too deep into the ground beyond the reach of roots. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, rather than right before a heavy rain storm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo dani ahum ni naa wa aba.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong and green. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps feed the plant so it can produce healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket (called mulch) over the soil. It blocks the harsh sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly so the plant roots stay moist longer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Mulch (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch) ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting and smelling bad inside the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long, it chokes the roots and allows water-loving fungi to attack, causing the tubers to rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa hydrophilic fungi lɛ tutuaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and removing affected plants stops the disease from spreading to healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are there tiny ragged holes and powdery brown dirt inside the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing tip of the corn plant and eats the leaves. Applying neem leaf extract or recommended treatments into the center whorl can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyeɔ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry conditions, lack of nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) around to fertilize the flowers properly.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kplukai (pollinators) lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong wind blows, even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that carry heavy bunches of fruit. Microscopic worms (nematodes) or stem borers can weaken the roots, causing the tree to lose its grip in the soil during windstorms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Nibii bibii ni shwieɔ shi (Nematodes) loo tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground—which prevents leaf diseases—and ensures the foliage gets enough light to grow big tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ—ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai anaa—ni ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ená la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their young green peppers right after they start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ pepper bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje shishi amɛfee lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruits when they experience sudden heat stress or when soil moisture swings drastically from very dry to very wet, causing the plant to protect itself by dropping fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe trukaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe kɛtsɔ aduawai ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and wither when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight. Large canopy trees protect cocoa from excessive heat and water loss, providing the filtered light and humidity cocoa plants need to thrive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he. Ha cacao tso lɛ la ni atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my young mango trees dropping all their flowers before fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flower dropping usually happens when the tree experiences water stress during dry spells, or when pests like thrips and fungal diseases attack the blossoms. Giving young trees steady water during flowering and controlling pests helps flowers stay on to become fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips kɛ fungal helai tutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ yaa nɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the food plants use to make green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from old bottom leaves up to feed new top growth, showing you it needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni tsei lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the afternoon heat even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon sun, plants lose water through leaves faster than roots can drink it up. Drooping is the plant's way of curling away from the intense sun to save moisture, and it will bounce back when the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Drooping ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni tsei lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn pale right after heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ trukaa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Too much standing water fills up all the tiny air holes in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots. Roots need oxygen to breathe and pull up food, so flooded plants turn pale and stop growing until the soil drains.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛjie niyenii. Tsei ni nu ewo amɛmli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and turning yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted and mottled cassava leaves are a sign of mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that bite the plant. Using healthy, disease-free stems for planting stops the disease from taking over your field.
ga: Cassava baai ni etsake ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji mosaic hela he okadii. Whiteflies bibii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii beni oduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my seeds come up nicely from the ground and then suddenly fall over and die a few days later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ̃ trukaa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛkɛ ni egbee shi ni egbo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off,' which happens when soil fungi attack tiny stems at ground level because the soil is too wet or crowded. Spacing seeds properly and not overwatering helps young seedlings stay strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutua tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil food, while their leaves block each other's sunlight. This competition makes all the plants grow tall, thin, and weak, producing smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ daraa, amɛdaraa, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haaa amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is my watermelon vine producing lots of flowers but no actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ebɛ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons have separate male and female flowers, and insects like bees must carry pollen from male to female flowers for fruit to grow. If heavy spraying drives bees away, female flowers dry up without forming fruits.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Ni esa akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛya yei anɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai akwɛ̃. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ waa lɛ baashwie ŋmeii lɛ kɛya. Fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are mature and ready to pull up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ agbala?

english: Groundnuts show maturity on top when leaves begin turning yellow and shedding. Underground, if you pull up a test plant and the inside shell walls are dark with full, firm seeds, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, kɛji ogbala tso ko ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ ni emli ŋmei lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ efee duŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers bend and stay small when they hit hard, rocky, or unplowed soil underground. Building soft, deep soil mounds allows tubers to stretch downward easily and grow long, smooth roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibii kɛ́ amɛtswa shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa bulb lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I nurse my seeds in a small nursery bed before planting them in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli dani madu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursing seeds gives delicate young plants a protected environment with soft soil, shade, and regular watering. Once the seedlings grow strong roots and leaves, they can withstand the harsher sun, pests, and weather in the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ náa he ko ni abuɔ he ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ. Enyɛɔ edamɔ hulu la, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know when my crop seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are usually ready for transplanting when they have grown 3 to 4 true leaves and developed a firm stem. Moving them too early makes them weak, while waiting too long can cause their roots to get overcrowded.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ otsi amɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbɔjɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha eshishifãi lɛ afee tsɔ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to grow uniformly, resist common local diseases, and produce higher yields. Saved seeds often lose their vigor over time and can carry diseases from the previous season into your new soil.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aya oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni miwo amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they are too old, stored in hot conditions, buried too deeply in the soil, or infected by rot. Good seeds need oxygen, gentle moisture, and proper depth to wake up and grow.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ Afuɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo egboɔ Dumɔwui kpakpai he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa ni baaha ete shi ni eda.

english: Why are some of the seeds I buy covered in a bright pink or blue powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ ekomɛi amli powda ni mli tse loo bluu yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: That colorful coating is a protective treatment made of fungicides and insecticides. It prevents soil insects and fungi from eating or rotting the seed before it has a chance to germinate.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii feɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaye loo amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually harm my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. When weeds compete with your plants, your crops grow slower, become weaker, and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ miitswa akaŋ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo, amɛbaafee gbɔjɔmɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops start turning yellow during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is stressed due to a lack of water or nutrients like nitrogen. Without enough water in the soil, the crop cannot pull up food, causing its leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak instead of short and sturdy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ kukuji ni ehe wa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When crops do not receive enough direct sunlight, they stretch rapidly upwards searching for light. Giving your crops full sunlight and proper spacing keeps them strong and sturdy.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya kɛtaoɔ la. Kɛ́ okɛ hulu la babaoo ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for root space, air, light, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to thrive and prevents diseases from spreading easily between leaves.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi, kɔɔyɔɔ, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã baai lɛ ateŋ mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before any fruit or pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani aduawai loo ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Crops drop flowers when they experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or insect damage. When the plant feels under stress, it sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ lɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over or bend down to the ground when strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛkotoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (called lodging) when their root systems are weak or planted too shallowly. When strong winds blow heavy crops, weak roots cannot hold them upright. Heap soil around the base of the stems (hilling) to anchor the roots firmly into the ground.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa) kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo adu amɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ Beni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ ni ja. Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (tillage) koni shishifãi lɛ atswa shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crop stems growing thin and weak, making the plants bend sideways instead of standing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ? Ha tso lɛ abɔle ehe kɛya afã moŋ fe ni eeedamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: When plants lack essential soil nutrients like potassium or phosphorus, their stems remain soft and cannot support their own weight as they grow taller. Adding well-decomposed manure or the right fertilizer strengthens stem walls so plants stay upright.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium loo phosphorus. Tso lɛ baaya nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ nɔ beni edaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ gbogboi lɛ afee shiŋŋ. Tso lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why are all my young plants leaning to one side instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ miitsi ehe kɛmiiya he kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally bend towards light when they are planted too close together or shaded by larger trees. Giving each plant enough space during planting ensures they get even sunlight and grow straight.
ga: Tsei baakoto amɛhe kɛya la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo tsei wuji tsi amɛnaa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha enine ashɛ hulu la po nɔ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I be worried if I see a few crops in my field drooping while the rest look healthy?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahao kɛji mina akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Yes, drooping or bent crops are often early warning signs of root rot, stem borers, or water shortages. Checking these signs early allows you to fix the issue before it spreads to the rest of your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni shwieɔ shi loo amɛkotoɔ lɛ ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo. trunk borer loo nu ni faaa Okadii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ osaa naagbai dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why does my plantain stem bend so low to the ground when it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: As a plantain bunch grows bigger, the stem struggles under the heavy weight of the fruit. Farmers use sturdy wooden or bamboo forks to prop up the stem so it does not break before the fruit matures.
ga: Beni plantains kuu lɛ dara lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ tso yibii lɛ ni tsii lɛ shishi. Okwaafoi kɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni mli wa tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛkakumɔ dani aduawai lɛ agbɔ.

english: What causes my cassava stems to look bent and wilted even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbo ni amɛgboi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Diseases like cassava bacterial blight or underground pests eating the roots prevent water and nutrients from moving up the stem. This makes the plant wilt and bend down even in wet soil.
ga: Helai tamɔ cassava bacteria leaf blight loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po.

english: Can applying too much chemical fertilizer cause my crops to fall over easily?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbo oya?

english: Yes, too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants grow tall leaves very quickly while leaving the stem thin and soft. This makes the plant top-heavy, causing it to bend or snap easily.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ atsɔ baai kakadaji oya waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishi hu feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ blɛoo. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo Efoɔ loo efoɔ oya.

english: Why do my yam vines bend down and crawl on the ground if I do not put sticks for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ miiho yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Akɛni mikɛ nitsumɔhe nine ko efɔɔɔ jɛmɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are naturally soft climbers that need vertical support to get enough sunlight. Staking them with tall wooden sticks keeps the leaves off the ground, preventing fungal diseases and encouraging larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ji tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni biɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fĩ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and turn downwards during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shi yɛ shwane mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Leaves droop and curl downwards in extreme heat to reduce moisture loss and protect themselves from burning. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the roots cool and moist, reducing heat stress.
ga: Ha amɛgbee shi ni amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ la ni naa wa waa mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ shãa he. Organic mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi

english: Why do my crops pull out of the ground and lean over whenever there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkotoɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: If the farm soil is too loose or shallow, heavy rains soften the dirt around the roots until they lose grip. Clearing land properly and planting on ridges or mounds gives roots deeper anchorage.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli etse tsɔ loo ekɔɔɔ he eko Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ ŋshɔkei loo gɔji anɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I use wooden poles to mark out my land before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei akadi shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Using poles to measure and align your plot ensures equal space between crop rows, preventing plants from crowding each other and competing for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsei tsu nii kɛsusu ni okɛto oshikpɔji lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa gbɛ po kã ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ ateŋ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee ekome kɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant too many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight over the same nutrients in the soil and their leaves block sunlight from one another, causing weak growth and poor yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Why do crops like yam need wooden poles or stakes to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes he hiaa tsei loo tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Climbing crops use poles to lift their vines toward the sunlight and keep foliage off the damp ground, which prevents soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akwɔɔ lɛ kɛ tsei tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo wain tsei anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ mli ni amɛha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: How does setting up a shared nursery with other farmers help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi to ŋmɔ ko ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A shared nursery allows farmers to pool materials like shade poles and water supplies, reducing costs while protecting delicate young plants until they are strong enough to transplant.
ga: Nurseries ni ajaa lɛ haa okwaafoi buaa nibii tamɔ shade poles kɛ nu mli nibii anaa. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni abuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical or fertilizer to apply to one hectare of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛwo hectare 1 mli?

english: Input amounts are calculated based on total field size; applying the specified dose per hectare ensures crops receive full protection or nutrition without burning the roots.
ga: Akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ yibɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ wo hectare kome mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ buɔ ehe loo enáa niyenii kpakpa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shãaa.

english: If the pests on my farm do not die after spraying, should I immediately increase the chemical dose?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbooo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ani Esa akɛ mawo tsofa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: You should not increase chemical doses on your own, as over-application can burn leaves, pollute soil, or cause pests to build resistance to the treatment.
ga: Esaaa akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. ekɛ mujiwoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ama shi ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofafeemɔ

english: Why is it risky to measure crop chemicals by eye instead of using exact measuring tools?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ hiŋmɛi baasusu tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he moŋ fe ni akɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Estimating chemical amounts by eye often leads to over-dosing, which wastes money and damages crops, or under-dosing, which leaves pests alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ hiŋmɛi bu tsofai lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa lɛ, ekɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine baa. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. loo tsofai fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How do I make sure I am mixing liquid inputs with water in the correct proportion?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ nu kɛ nu ni sa miifutu?

english: Agrochemical labels specify exact milliliter or gram amounts per liter of water; following these ratios ensures the mixture is strong enough to work without harming the crop.
ga: Agrochemical woji lɛ tsɔɔ mililita loo gram ni yɔɔ nu lita kome mli lɛ falɛ. Nɛkɛ ratios nɛɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ haa nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni etsuɔ ​​enitsumɔ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui.

english: How can I accurately measure my farm to know how many hectares I own?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu miŋmɔ lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ koni male hectares enyiɛ ni miyɔɔ?

english: You can measure farmland by using standard measuring tapes or marked ropes to define boundaries, where one hectare equals roughly 2.5 acres or 10,000 square meters.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe loo kpã ni akadi lɛ asusu oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni okɛtsɔɔ husui lɛ, ni hectare 1 lɛ feɔ aaafee acre 2.5 loo sqɛɛ mitai 10,000.

english: Why are my crop yields dropping each year even though I plant on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil; varying your crops or replenishing nutrients helps maintain long-term soil fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. Tsakemɔi ni ooofee yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do pests and wild animals attack my crops more when my farm is near a forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ koo mli kooloi babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ koo ko lɛ?

english: Forests are natural habitats for insects and wild animals. When crops like corn are planted next to forest land, pests easily cross over into your field because young crops provide a rich and easy source of food.
ga: Kooi ji adebɔɔ shihilɛhe kɛha koolooi kɛ koo mli kooloi. Kɛji oodu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ kooi amli hei ni bɛŋkɛ kooi amli lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ afo kɛbote oŋmɔji lɛ amli oya ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ji niyenii ni fa babaoo ni anyɛɔ anáa oya.

english: Why is something eating my corn plants so quickly in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ko miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ oya yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Corn leaves and stalks are tender and nutritious, making them attractive to fast-feeding pests like fall armyworms and rodents. If left unchecked, these pests multiply fast and can destroy a field within days.
ga: Abɛi baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii oya tamɔ cutworms kɛ rodents lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ waa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ayi fa oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite he ko yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray pest medicine on my cornfield?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ afɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon. During these cooler hours, insects come out to feed on leaves, and the liquid medicine will not dry up too fast in the sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Yɛ fɛ̃i be nɛɛ mli lɛ, kooloi baaje kpo ni amɛbaaye baai lɛ. Ni tsofai ni akɛ nu fee lɛ egbiɛɛ oya tsɔ kɛ́ akɛwo hulu la mli.

english: How fast should crop medicine work after I spray it on pests eating my corn?
ga: Te esa akɛ tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ atsu nii oya aha tɛŋŋ beni mikɛshwie mi-ŋmãa-yelɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fast-acting contact pesticides start killing pests within 15 to 30 minutes of touching them, while systemic medicines take a day or two as the insects need to feed on the sprayed leaves first.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tsuɔ nii oya lɛ jeɔ shishi egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ minitii 15 kɛyashi 30 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ekɛ amɛ kpeɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ baahe gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ ejaakɛ esa akɛ kooloi lɛ aye baai ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How can I tell if insects or larger animals are destroying my corn leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii loo kooloi wuji miifite mi-abele baai lɛ?

english: Insects usually chew small holes, leave ragged edges, or leave droppings on leaves. Larger animals bite off whole stalks, dig around roots, or trample plants down across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ŋmɔɔ bu bibii. Shi ŋmeii ni etse loo shi ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Koolooi wuji ŋmɔɔ tsei ashishifãi muu fɛɛ, amɛfoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, loo amɛnyiɛɔ tsei anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn brown and chewed up right before the cobs form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Insects target corn leaves right before cob formation because the plant is soft and full of nutrients. Losing leaves at this stage starves the plant of energy, preventing big, full cobs from growing.
ga: Kplukai shwieɔ ŋmãa baai anɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ darako ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Baai ni baafite yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ. Etsiɔ cob lɛ naa koni ekafee agbo tsɔ.

english: Why do I need to inspect my field regularly even after I have already sprayed pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ nibii ni midu lɛ amli daa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ shi moŋ.

english: New insect eggs can hatch after spraying, or new pests can move in from surrounding bushland. Regular visits help you catch fresh infestations early before they cause major farm loss.
ga: Kplukai akui heei baanyɛ afɔ yɛ be mli ni ashwie amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai heei Baanyɛ aba kɛjɛ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Saramɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona helai ni hiɛ ka lɛ mra. dani ekɛ fitemɔ kpele baaba ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to use strong liquid medicine to clear pests off my food crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni ji nu baatsu nii kɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yes, but only if you use approved agricultural pesticides, mix them in correct dosages, wear protective clothing, and wait for the recommended safety period before harvesting crops for food.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii pɛ. Okɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ afutu mli. Wo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he ni omɛ shweshweeshwe be ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ dani okpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii.

english: Should I spray my corn as soon as I see a few insects, or wait until there are many?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ ŋmãa nɔ kɛji mina kooloi fioo komɛi pɛ loo mamɛ ni kooloi babaoo aba?

english: It is better to act as soon as you spot early damage. A small group of crop pests can lay thousands of eggs and spread across your entire farm within a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee nɔ ko kɛji ona nɔ ko ni efite mra pɛ. ŋmeii akuu bibioo Amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii akpei abɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What can I do along the edges of my farm to stop pests from entering my cornfield?
ga: Mɛni mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Clearing a clean buffer zone around the borders of your farm removes hiding places for insects and animals, making it much harder for them to cross from the forest directly into your crops.
ga: Buffer zone ni he tse ni ebɔle Oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baajie hei ni kooloi kɛ kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaafo kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya oŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods this year compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crop yields naturally fluctuate from year to year depending on rainfall patterns, heat, and soil nutrients. If the previous year had better rainfall during the flowering stage, the harvest will be much bigger than in a year with dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi. Edamɔ nugbɔ, dɔlɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaahi jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nikpamɔ lɛ fa kwraa fe afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is the difference between the main harvest season and the light crop season?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nikpamɔ be titri lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ fioo lɛ ateŋ?

english: The main crop season occurs after the major rainy season and produces the largest yield of bigger pods. The light crop season occurs during minor rains, yielding smaller pods and a lower total harvest.
ga: Be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ sɛɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ baa. Be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo lɛ baa be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why did my trees flower heavily but end up giving me very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry winds, or pest attacks during the pod-setting stage cause flowers and tiny pods to fall off prematurely, resulting in a disappointing harvest despite heavy early flowering.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shwereɔ. fall off prematurely Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni nijiaŋjewui baa yɛ fɔfɔi ni baa mra tsɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning brown and looking like they were burnt by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive sunlight and lack of soil moisture cause water stress in plants, which scorches the leaf edges and makes them look burnt or withered even without actual fire.
