ga: Hulu la ni fa fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa. ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã loo egbo eyɛ mli akɛ la diɛŋtsɛ bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Can strong sunshine damage mature crop pods while they are still on the tree?
ga: Ani hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni eda lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, prolonged harsh sunlight without adequate shade canopy can scorch pods, dry out their internal moisture, and reduce the overall weight and quality of the beans inside.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni naa wa be kakadaŋŋ ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha pod lɛ ashã. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. ni eha kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tsiimɔ kɛ amɛhe fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I protect my crops from burning during extreme dry heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Planting shade trees, leaving a moderate canopy, and covering the soil around roots with organic mulch helps retain moisture and shields crops from destructive sun heat.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛha hulutsoo Shimɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ teŋgbɛ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Why do the crops growing at the outer edges of my farm dry out faster than the ones in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops at the edges face direct exposure to strong winds, hot sun, and clearing heat from surrounding land, making them lose moisture much quicker than sheltered plants inside the field.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: What causes the border drying effect that local farmers refer to as 'nsugya'?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi tsɛɔ lɛ ‘nsugya’ lɛ baa?

english: Nsugya' refers to border scorching caused when extreme heat, hot dry winds, or heat radiated from nearby bush clearing dries up soil moisture along the unshaded perimeter of your farm.
ga: Nsugya’ tsɔɔ husu nɔ shãa ni baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi Aloo, la ni tsoɔ waa kɛjɛɔ brɔshi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naagbee ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ he.

english: How do I stop bushfire heat from destroying the crops along my farm boundary?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ koo mli la mli baa lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Creating a clean firebelt—a cleared strip of bare soil around your farm perimeter free of dry weeds—prevents ground fires and intense heat from reaching your crops.
ga: La ni he tse ni ooofee—shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ naa ni jwɛi ni egbi bɛ mli lɛ—baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ nɔ la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa akashɛ onibii ahe.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my crops past their maturity time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpamɔ be sɛɛ fe be ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops on the tree too long exposes them to pod rot, pest infestation, over-ripening, and moisture loss, which reduces the final weight and quality of your yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Pest ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni laajeɔ. Enɛ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ amli tsiimɔ kɛ naagbee kpakpa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady rainfall for at least two to three consecutive days and stays moist below the surface, rather than sowing immediately after the very first light shower.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What should I do to protect my young crops if the rain suddenly stops after I have already planted?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to trap moisture in the ground and shade the young roots from scorching heat until the rains return.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebu shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkadɔ fe nine kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and drying up even when there is moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves despite moist soil often signal a soil-borne fungal disease or root rot, which happens when water cannot drain properly or when plants lack vital soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ po lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni shikpɔŋ loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: How can I tell if a plant sickness on my farm is minor or a serious disease that can kill all my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji hela bibioo ko loo hela ko ni naa wa ni baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Minor sickness only affects a few lower leaves without stopping growth, while serious diseases spread fast, cause dark rotted spots, wilt whole stems, or stunt the entire crop.
ga: Hela ni waaa lɛ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ fioo pɛ nɔ ni ekpaaa dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oyayaayai. ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ. loo ŋmɔshi nibii muu fɛɛ ni efiteɔ.

english: What causes white spots and rotted patches on my crop pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Excess moisture and high humidity create a perfect environment for fungal diseases to grow on pods, especially if the farm is overgrown and air cannot circulate between the crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii helai ni baakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I delay clearing weeds from my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwie sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops after rain and will steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops, causing your crops to become weak and yield poorly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai.

english: What important farm tasks must I complete immediately after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni magbe ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni he hiaa lɛ anaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Clear any blocked drainage pathways so standing water doesn't drown crop roots, check for washed-away fertilizer, and inspect leaves for newly appeared pest attacks or mold.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛi ni nu tsɔɔ nɔ ni atsĩ naa lɛ koni nu ni ekã shi lɛ akagbe tsei shishifãi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ efo. Ni okwɛ baai lɛ amli kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai heei eba.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for nutrients and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small harvests; proper spacing gives every plant room to yield fully.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu ni miida lɛ woɔ eyibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with many leaves but fail to produce big fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa kɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo aduawai wuji loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of flowering and building strong pods or fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a fɔɔ fɔfɔi nɛ a woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant crops like beans together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baafata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is good because beans pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves your total harvest from one land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ hi ejaakɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stalks into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce their pods underground. After pollination, the flower stem bends downward and pegs itself into the soil so the nut can safely develop underground away from heat and sunlight.
ga: Peanuts woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ pollination sɛɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ he ko ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la shɛɛɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my groundnut crop turning yellow even though rain has been falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a nutrient deficiency like nitrogen, or a viral disease such as groundnut rosette. Excess waterlogging can also damage the root system, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ ŋmei rose bɛ mli. Nu babaoo baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ. ni haa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ

english: Why do tiny green insects always hide underneath my crop leaves instead of sitting on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi Be fɛɛ be moŋ fe ni amɛaata amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Insects hide under leaves to protect themselves from the direct heat of the sun and to avoid predators like birds while feeding on the softer tissue on the leaf's underside.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛ koni ajie kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe beni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if insects in my field are actually damaging my crop or just resting on the plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo eta tso ko nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Pest damage usually shows up as chewed holes, curled leaves, sticky substances on stems, or wilting. Useful insects, like ladybugs, do not eat the plant; they search for and eat the harmful pests instead.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jeɔ kpo tamɔ bu ni ashɛreɔ, baai ni ebɔle, kɛ nɔ ko ni kpɛtɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. loo ni egboɔ Kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ladybugs lɛ, yeee tsei. Mohu ɔ, a naa koolohi nɛ yeɔ awui nɛ a yeɔ mɛ.

english: Why are dark brown spots spreading fast across my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa mitsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Damp and humid weather allows fungal spores to multiply. Raindrops splash these fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves, causing spot diseases to spread across the field.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli edɔ lɛ haa fungal spores lɛ shwereɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hela ko ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is one side of my farm wilting while the rest of the crops look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome miigbo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Wilting in patch patterns usually means a soil-borne fungus, root-eating pest, or localized water drainage issue is attacking the roots in that specific area of the field first.
ga: Wilting in patches Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni afɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi loo nu homɔ he naagba pɔtɛɛ ko ni tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he pɔtɛɛ ko klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: What makes my young maize leaves look twisted and yellow-striped instead of broad and green?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etsake ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Twisted and yellow-striped leaves in young maize are typically caused by viral infections spread by sap-sucking insects like leafhoppers, or by severe nutrient deficiencies early in growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ leafhoppers lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsake kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ niyenii ni esaaa ni naa wa ni ayeɔ yɛ shishijee dalɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients and water faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to outgrow young seedlings quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ basabasa. ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui bibii.

english: Can weeds still reduce my harvest yield if my crop plants are already tall and big?
ga: Ani jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi lolo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛdara momo?

english: Yes, mature crops still lose valuable water and fertilizer to thick weeds. Overgrown weeds also trap humidity near the stem, creating ideal conditions for diseases and pests to spread.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni eda lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lolo kɛyaa jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight. They stretch upwards rapidly to reach the light, spending energy on height rather than building thick stems or yielding good produce.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei ni mli tse loo eeewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaves so the plant can feed itself and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye amɛhe niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the young plants I planted directly under full sunlight dry up so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni miduɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Young crops like cocoa or tender vegetables have delicate roots and thin leaves that lose water rapidly in strong sunshine. They need partial shade from taller plants, like plantains, to keep the surrounding air and soil moist while they grow strong roots.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo loo aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni baaha nu afite oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Flowers usually drop when the plant is stressed by hot, dry weather or a lack of water and soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers until peppers form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. aloo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready for harvest without digging up the whole bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: As cassava roots mature and expand underground, they push against the earth and cause visible cracks in the soil around the base of the stem, signaling that the tubers are large enough to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Etsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmei ni anaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ bulb lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow big and produce healthy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun, traps soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests multiply in the dirt. Changing crops or planting beans restores nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds in my farm make my crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than farmed crops, so they steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ dani otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in the middle of my maize leaves, and how does it hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? ŋmãa baa teŋgbɛ Ni te eyeɔ tso lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in leaf centers are typically caused by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, eating the young leaves. Damaging leaves reduces the plant's ability to make food from sunlight, which stunts overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Foji ni efite lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my vegetable leaves after a period of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetable baa lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity and leaves moisture sitting on plant leaves, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to grow. Spacing plants properly allows air to flow and dry leaves quickly after rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni eshiɔ hulutsoo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ adalɛ. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore leaf color and crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni tsei lɛ hu ada.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry plant grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi haa he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Dry grass protects the soil from hot sun, helps moisture stay in the ground longer, reduces weed growth, and eventually breaks down into rich organic manure.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa

english: Why do my pepper leaves look weak and droopy in the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon weather makes plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant naturally wilts to save water and will refresh itself once the air cools in the evening.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, tso lɛ sumɔɔɔ ni ekɛ nu toɔ, ni ebaaná hejɔɔmɔ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduuu tomato?

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, often by extreme midday heat, erratic watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Consistent watering and adding wood ash or phosphorus fertilizer helps fruits form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tso sũ loo fɔsfɔs ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunshine and hot dry winds. Planting plantain trees alongside cocoa provides living canopy shade that protects the young trees until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: How far apart am I supposed to space cassava stem cuttings when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋmei niji lɛ ateŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings about one meter apart ensures the roots have enough space underground to form thick tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava niji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward sunlight so the plant can make maximum energy, which directly results in much larger yam tubers growing under the mound.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo. Enɛ saa sweet potato tsei ni dara kwraa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with green powdery stuff left inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ powda ŋmɔŋ bibii ni eshwɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant funnel. Treating the crop early in the morning or late in the evening with proper organic or chemical remedies destroys the worms before they ruin the whole farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tsei akutsei lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa loo tsofai ni sa tsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting saved maize seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced for high yields, uniform growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose these special traits, resulting in lower yields and weaker plants in the next generation.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekome kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ Dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomatoes need proper moisture, gentle temperatures, and insects like bees to shake pollen inside the flower. If it gets too hot, too dry, or if there are no helpful insects around, the flowers drop off without making fruit.
ga: Tomato he miihia ni hulutsoo be ni sa aba mli. hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni baatsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli Kɛji edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pest chemicals on my farm when my crops are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Bees and other helpful insects visit open flowers to feed and carry pollen that makes fruits grow. Spraying chemicals during flowering kills these beneficial insects, which leads to fewer flowers turning into healthy produce.
ga: Wuobii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Amɛbaasara fɔfɔi ni agbele naa lɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do tiny bugs gather under my pepper leaves and make them curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Those tiny pests suck the juices and nutrients directly out of the tender leaves. This loss of plant juice causes the leaves to wrinkle, curl, and fail to feed the rest of the plant properly.
ga: ŋmeii bibii Mɛi ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nu ni tso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot where my previous crop died from disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he ni hela gbo mitsutsu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tiny disease germs that attacked your previous crop can stay alive hidden in the soil long after the dead plant is removed. Planting the same crop in that spot gives those hidden germs a direct chance to attack the new roots immediately.
ga: Muawai bibii ni tutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtee amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ beni ajie tsei ni egboi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ haa helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi heei lɛ.

english: What causes my maize leaves to turn yellow and dry up before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow early when the soil runs out of essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when the roots cannot get enough water. Soil pests damaging the roots can also stop the plant from drinking water and food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ hu baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkanu nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farm give me a smaller harvest every year even when rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every time they grow. If you plant on the same piece of land continuously without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed new crops.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji oya nɔ odu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo ni tsei heei nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When heavy water covers the farm without draining away, it chokes the roots, preventing them from breathing and causing them to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu, tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu afua lɛ ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense heat. Direct sunlight dries out their leaves faster than the young roots can pull water from the soil, causing the plant to burn and dry up.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and aggressive at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because they grow faster than farm crops, they will quickly starve and crowd out your crops if you do not remove them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ basabasa yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jumɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Hɔmɔ baaye amɛ oya ni amɛbaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ kɛji ojieee amɛ oya.

english: Why do some of the seeds I buy fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, if the soil is too dry, or if the seeds were spoiled by heat or moisture before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji dɔlɛ loo fɛ̃i fite dumɔwui lɛ dani adu.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and burn easily. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy of shade that lowers temperatures and keeps soil moist for the cocoa roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo shishifãi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, a vital food for plants. The maize moves whatever nitrogen is left to its newer leaves, causing the older leaves at the bottom to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ Abele lɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, helping to naturally restore soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to place cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem; they should always point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the new shoots to grow sideways or downward, making the plant weak and reducing root growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ yɛ afã loo shishi. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra sucker shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain tree, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Pruning them leaves energy for the main plant to yield a much larger bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, Dumɔwu kome baaju nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure so the plant can feed its growing tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni tsei anyɛ aye abua bulb ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and sticky sawdust-like dirt inside the top funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on young leaf shoots inside the plant. Identifying these signs early helps you apply targeted treatments before the pest destroys the whole field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Okadii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akpãtã he fɛɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or a virus they transmit. These insects drink the leaf sap, causing the leaf tissue to twist and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli nu. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or dry soil, which stresses the plant. Ensuring consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch keeps flowers on the vine to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Can I grow rice on dry sloping land, or does it only grow in flooded muddy water?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ gɔji ni egbi nɔ loo abaanyɛ adu yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ pɛ mli?

english: There are different varieties of rice: Upland rice thrives on normal rain-fed soil like maize, whereas Lowland rice requires stagnant or flooded water in valley bottoms to grow successfully.
ga: Omɔ henɔi srɔtoi yɛ: Omɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ, yɛ be mli ni omɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ biɔ nu ni damɔ shi loo nu afua yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, working like a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their blossoms when they are stressed by drought, lack nutrients, or are attacked by tiny pests like mirids (capsids) that suck sap from the delicate flower stems.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli nu lɛ tutua amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow during the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or banana root weevils destroy their root systems under the soil, weakening their anchor.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much water during heavy rains, causing waterlogging and fungal infections that destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look dead in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi moŋ.

english: Hot afternoon heat causes plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink water from the soil, so they wilt temporarily to protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, sunken spots on the bottom of the fruit as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebote shishi kɛji ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering patterns.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting white shoots in the barn even when I want to store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii yɛŋ shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miisumɔ ni mahi shi moŋ

english: Yam tubers naturally enter a rest period after harvest, but once their internal biological clock finishes dormant rest, they automatically sprout to try to grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ amɛmli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ kpa hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, Ebaakwɛ̃ ehe yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni ekwɛ wain tso hee mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crop right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep or wide root systems that can steal rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo amɛmli kwɔ ni baanyɛ aju nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Sir, why do my maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the rainfall becomes very heavy?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Yellowing leaves mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. Heavy rains flood the soil, preventing roots from breathing and absorbing food, while also washing away soluble nutrients deeper into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afɔseɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars start chewing the center leaves of my young corn plants as soon as the weather becomes dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ aŋmɔmɔ shishi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ egbi pɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. Warm, dry weather speeds up their hatching, and they hide deep inside the tightly rolled center leaves of corn plants where hot sun and chemical sprays cannot easily reach them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya. Ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni abɔle amɛhe waa lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he mlɛo.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my cassava help make the soil better for my farm?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that have natural plant nodules on their roots. These nodules pull nitrogen gas out of the air and convert it into rich fertilizer in the ground, sharing nutrients with nearby crops like cassava.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Sir, why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. Shrinking its exposed leaf area reduces the amount of water lost through evaporation, protecting the plant from drying out until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie he ni baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ kpo lɛ, nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi. Buu tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do all the flowers drop off my tomato plants without forming fruits when there is a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When tomato plants experience high heat and water shortages, they go into survival mode. They shed their flowers to save water and energy for staying alive, rather than spending resources on growing fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ na amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, Tomato baaya shihilɛ mli. Amɛ duɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha amɛ wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: How can I know that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when its bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, and cracks begin to form in the topsoil around the base of the stem as the growing roots push upward.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bɔi feemɔ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni shishifãi ni miida lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Sir, why do wild weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rain?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely hardy and lie dormant in the soil waiting for moisture. Because wild weeds are aggressive survival experts, their root systems drink up soil water and fertilizer much faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ejaakɛ koo mli jwɛi ji wala yibii ahe nilelɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kwraa fe shia tsei.

english: Why does my stored corn turn moldy in the room even though I harvested it during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsu lɛ mli lɛ? Ani akpaa yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Corn kernels retain hidden moisture inside the core of the cob even when the outside looks dry. If you do not spread the corn under the sun to dry completely before bagging, trapped heat creates internal moisture that causes mold.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli, kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ po. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwieee shi kwraa ni egbi dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa baa emli ni ehaa ŋmãa baa.

english: Sir, if I plant my plantain suckers very close to each other, won't I get a bigger harvest from my piece of land?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, kɛji midu plantain tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa. Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces the suckers to compete over sunlight, groundwater, and food. Instead of many big fruits, you will harvest tall, thin trees that bear very small and light bunches.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa aduawai wuji babaoo lɛ, obaakpa tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni niji bibii waa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do dark black spots spread rapidly over my cocoa pods during damp and foggy mornings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso ni afua miiye lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, moist, and shady conditions. Fog and water droplets on the pods help the microscopic fungal spores swim and infect healthy plant tissues.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Afua kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant my maize in neat rows with equal spacing instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu abele yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ

english: Planting in straight rows gives every crop enough room to catch sunlight and draw water and nutrients from the soil without competing with its neighbors. It also leaves clear pathways for you to walk through to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest easily.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ. Gbɛ ko hu yɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ kɛya jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: If I put two or three seeds into the exact same hole, won't I get double or triple the crops during harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ wo bu kome mli Ani maná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Placing too many seeds in one spot makes the plants fight each other for food, water, and sunlight. Instead of getting many big fruits or cobs, you will end up with weak, thin plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo he kome lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Yɛ aduawai wuji loo ŋmeii babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, amɛgbeɔ naa kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster when my crops are planted wide apart?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa kɛ́ adu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced too far apart, sunlight directly hits the bare ground between them, which encourages weed seeds in the soil to sprout. Proper row spacing allows mature crop leaves to cover the soil, creating shade that naturally slows down weed growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ Hulu la lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ woɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa tsei ahe baai ni edara lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa.

english: How does using a planter attached to a tractor help my crops grow better than planting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso tsɛnsi ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ trakta he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ niji duɔ lɛ?

english: A tractor planter drops seeds at the exact same depth and distance apart across the entire field in one pass. This ensures all your seeds germinate at the same time and grow evenly, making your field uniform and easy to manage.
ga: Trakta lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ha onibii ni odu lɛ afee ekome ni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo akɛ oookwɛ nɔ.

english: Will using heavy tractors on my land make the soil too hard for my crop roots to push through?
ga: Ani traktɔ agbo ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli?

english: If heavy machines drive over wet soil repeatedly, they squeeze the soil particles tightly together, a process called compaction. This makes it difficult for crop roots to breathe and stretch deep to find water, so it is best to operate heavy machinery when the soil is dry enough.
ga: Kɛji tsɔnei ni tsii tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii bibii lɛ afee ekome. Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ kɔmpakshin. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii atsu nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I calculate the amount of seed bags I need to buy for my size of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui kotokui ayibɔ ni esa akɛ mahe lɛ he akɔntaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ naa?

english: The amount of seed you need depends on your total land size and the recommended spacing for that specific crop. Extension officers use your land acreage to calculate the exact weight of seeds required so you do not under-plant your farm or waste money buying extra.
ga: Dumɔwui abɔ ni he hiaa bo lɛ damɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ kɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ nɔ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni he hiaa lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni ehe akahia ni odu tsei fioo tsɔ loo ofite shika ni okɛhe babaoo.

english: Does having a larger acre of land mean I will automatically harvest more bag loads than someone with a small farm?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni da ni miyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ makpa baagi babaoo yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe fe mɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ bibioo?

english: Not necessarily. A smaller, well-spaced farm that is properly weeded and fertilized will often produce more food per acre than a huge farm where crops are neglected, crowded, or choked by weeds.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ jogbaŋŋ ni jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa niyenii babaoo baa yɛ acre kome mli fe ŋmɔji wuji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ, ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi, loo jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my seeds under the ground if I bury them too deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply use up all their stored energy trying to push up through the thick layer of earth. Most will run out of energy and die underground before their shoots can reach the surface and sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ. Hewalɛ ni amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baaho ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why are some plants in the middle of my farm growing tall and green while others nearby remain small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ekomɛi daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo.

english: Uneven growth usually happens when seeds were planted at different depths, or when soil nutrients and moisture are not spread evenly across the field. Proper land preparation and uniform planting ensure every crop gets an equal start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ejaraaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ ni sa kɛ dumɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: How many days should I wait for my seeds to sprout after planting before I know they have failed?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ ni esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ koni male akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ŋ?

english: Most grain crops like maize germinate within 4 to 7 days if the soil has good moisture. If nothing comes up after 10 to 14 days, the seeds may have dried out, rotted from too much rain, or been eaten by insects, meaning you need to replant.
ga: Ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nɔ ko baaa yɛ gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hewɔ. loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that the roots are suffocating from too much standing water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Aloo nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or dry, as extreme heat and water stress prevent the flowers from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants grow big green leaves but produce very few nuts underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes groundnuts focus all their energy on growing leafy branches instead of sending down pegs to produce pods underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei niji ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu ŋmeii kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Curling leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects that suck sap from the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when there is too much shade and bad air movement around the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fɔŋ nyiɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do small holes appear all over my cowpea leaves shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Holes in young leaves are caused by chewing pests like leaf beetles and caterpillars that feed on tender plant leaves right after germination.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ tsei bibii tamɔ baa mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ beni amɛje kpo etsɛɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the ground was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: Pepper plants wilt during peak heat because they lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil, though they recover when the air cools down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ amɛshwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhe baajɔ amɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: Yam tubers become small and distorted when the soil is too hard and compacted for the root to push through, or when microscopic soil pests called nematodes damage the young tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface of the soil, making the tall plants top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over when the heavy fruit bunches mature.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa enɔ beni aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava too close to my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa bibii tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava branches spread wide and develop aggressive roots, which block sunlight and steal water and nutrients away from neighboring maize plants.
ga: Cassava niji gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni boteɔ mɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are insects suddenly attacking my maize field after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii batutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Early rains trigger fresh crop leaves to sprout, which attracts hungry pests like fall armyworms. The humid weather after rain also helps pest eggs hatch faster and spread across young plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa tsei ahe baai kwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ afɔ̃ɔ oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do pests keep coming back to my farm even after I weed and clean the entire field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mijie jwɛi ni mijie he fɛɛ he lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: Pests often hide in surrounding bushes, wild plants, or crop leftovers from the previous season. When new crops start growing, these pests fly or crawl back onto your farm searching for fresh food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ jwɛi ni bɔle koo mli tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii heei bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baafo loo amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyatao niyenii hee.

english: Why is my new maize crop growing so weak on land where I harvested cassava last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa henɔ hee lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava draws a massive amount of nutrients from deep in the soil. If you do not add manure or compost before planting a heavy feeder like maize, the soil will be too tired to feed the new crop.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he dani okɛ niyenii agbo tamɔ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei.

english: Why do groundnut plants have lush green leaves but very few nuts under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from over-using fertilizers or previous leafy crops—the groundnut plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of developing underground pods.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo tsei ni tsutsu lɛ amɛyɛ baai lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Peanut tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ shishi pods lɛ

english: Why does the cocoa buyer offer me a low price even when my harvest yield is large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Buyers inspect beans for moisture, mold, insect damage, and proper fermentation. High quantity does not earn top market prices if the quality of the dried beans fails inspection standards.
ga: Mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ baa kwɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmei, kɛ koolooi ebote mli. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa Nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ baaa jara nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ mlihilɛ hoɔ kwɛmɔ he mlai lɛ ahe.

english: How do I inspect my field early to catch diseases before my whole farm gets ruined?
ga: Mikwɛɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ana helai dani akpata ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ?

english: Walk through your farm early in the morning and inspect the undersides of leaves, young stems, and roots for yellow spots, fine webbing, or wilting, which are early signs of disease.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okwɛ baai, tsei bibii, kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi yɛ. fibers kpakpai loo ŋmɔlɔ ni ji hela lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy rainfall causes severe stress to pepper plants. To save water and survive, the plant drops its flowers instead of feeding growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ nu ato ni ehi shi No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii ni miida.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny whitefly insects that spread viral diseases, or by excessive heat paired with low water and lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛji kɛ baa lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwaa loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni nu ni faaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ mli.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast when I plant my crops very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Tight crop spacing traps moisture and prevents sunlight and fresh air from circulating between plants. Damp, shaded leaves create an ideal home for fungi to multiply rapidly.
ga: Tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ bibioo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akabɔle tsei lɛ ateŋ. Baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛshwere oya.

english: How do I know if it is better to sell my harvested yams immediately or store them for later?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mikɛto kɛha sɛɛ mli?

english: Selling immediately provides quick cash but yields lower profits during harvest peak. Storing undamaged yams in a well-ventilated barn allows you to sell later when market supplies drop and prices rise.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ haa shika oya shi sɛɛnamɔi baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ohɔɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli beni jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Maize plants turn yellow when they lack nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the leaves return to a healthy dark green color.
ga: Abɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for your maize and giving you a better harvest.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa, ni ehaa onáa ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my plants with dry grass or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or straw is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you do not have to water as often, and stops weeds from taking over your land.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaye oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and prevent the whole tree from dying. Providing shade trees on your farm helps protect the cocoa from direct sun and keeps the soil moist longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi tso muu lɛ fɛɛ naa koni ekagbo. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time, leading to fungal infections. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. kɛ fungal infection baa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too strong or when the plant does not get enough water consistently. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving the plants partial shade during extreme heat helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha tso lɛ he hulutsoo fioo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know if worms are damaging my young maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miifite mi-baby corn tsei lɛ?

english: If caterpillars like the fall armyworm are present, you will see ragged holes in the young central leaves and small brownish droppings. Catching them early by applying safe, recommended treatments inside the plant leaf funnel stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Obaana bu ko ni etse ehe yɛ baa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil food and water they need to grow tall and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ anɔ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients, leading to small plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two strong shoots allows the main tree to produce much larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa Kɛ́ ooohiɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall sticks, or stakes, so their leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight. The sunlight helps the leaves make food, which travels down to build big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ niji ni kɛlɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee yam ŋmeii agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my crops dry up and die even when there is a river near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ faa ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops can only use water if it reaches their roots regularly. Having a river nearby is not enough unless you actively channel or carry the water to your field using simple pumps, ditches, or watering cans during dry spells.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ nu atsu nii kɛji eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ pɛ. Faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ No pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Ja okɛ pɔmp, nubu, loo nu tsɛnsi tsu nii kɛpomɔ loo okɛ nu tee ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: When crops get too little water, their leaves curl up, turn brown, or wilt during the day. When they get too much water, the leaves turn yellow and soft, and the roots rot because soggy soil prevents them from breathing.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu fioo tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo egboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo. Ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa amɛmuɔ.

english: Is it possible for me to grow crops in Ghana during the dry season without waiting for the rains?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni mimɛɛɛ nugbɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow crops year-round during the dry season by practicing small-scale irrigation, using water from streams, wells, or ponds, and covering the soil with dry grass to retain moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu bibioo ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu ni jɛ faa, nubu, loo nubu mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why does my land produce less food now compared to when I first started farming it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the soil. If you do not replenish those nutrients using compost, animal manure, or fertilizers, the soil becomes tired and weak, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nakai niyenii lɛ fataaa he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What causes some farmers to harvest far more food than others even when they plant on the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaafoi komɛi kpaɔ niyenii babaoo fe mɛi krokomɛi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Higher yields come from using improved seed varieties, protecting crops from weeds and pests early, feeding the soil with the right nutrients, and ensuring plants get a steady supply of water throughout their growth.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe mra Ni akɛ niyenii ni sa aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: If I leave a piece of my land unplanted for a season, will it help my crops grow better later?
ga: Kɛ mishi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni miduuu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, letting land rest—known as fallowing—allows the soil to naturally rebuild its organic matter, moisture, and plant food so it can produce healthier crops when you plant again.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Ale lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ tsei aniyenii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji koni enyɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ odu ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light and food to grow strong and produce heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba amɛhe su kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better?
