ga: Nɔ hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the ground, keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from popping up, and saves water for the plant roots.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu toɔ tsei shishifãi ahe

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my main crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil food faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early stops them from starving your main crops of the water and nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: What is the best season to plant new cocoa seedlings in my field?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant cocoa seedlings at the start of the major rainy season so the young roots can establish themselves firmly in wet soil before the dry harmattan season arrives.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ dani harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, dark, well-drained soil that stays moist without holding stagnant water, and in areas that receive good rainfall throughout the year.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa nu shwieɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli kɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is getting too much shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo?

english: If your cocoa trees get too much shade, they will grow tall and skinny with thin leaves and yield very few pods because they cannot get enough direct sunlight to make food.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo Cacao tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune the extra branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or diseased branches, allowing light and air to pass through the tree, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the plant put energy into growing cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔjɔ, ni egboi, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ naa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around the base of my cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from young cocoa trees, which slows down their growth and can cause young plants to dry out and die.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli Enɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during damp, rainy weather when water stays on the pods for long periods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. ni nu eshwɛ yɛ pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean the plant is exposed to too much direct sunlight without shade, or the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ he. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: How do capsid insects damage my cocoa trees?
ga: Te capsid ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Capsid insects bite into young cocoa stems and green pods to suck out sap, leaving dark spots that cause the leaves to dry up and young branches to die back.
ga: Capsid kooloi ŋmɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni niji bibii lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose many of their tiny pods right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifite amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii asɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods when they do not have enough water or soil nutrients to nourish all the developing pods to full maturity.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashi eda.

english: How does applying fertilizer help my older cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Over time, mature trees use up the nutrients in the dirt. Adding fertilizer replaces those missing nutrients, giving the tree energy to grow new flowers and fill out cocoa pods.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ baafite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi heei kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ eyiɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip, your soil usually lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build strong leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the new growth at the top, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, no lɛ ekolɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni mli wa. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ nɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do farmers tell me to plant beans or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that pull plant food (nitrogen) directly from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant them with or before maize, they feed the soil naturally so your maize grows stronger without needing as much expensive artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa tsu nii loo dani okɛ ŋmãa du lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa afee.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tight and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the juices out of the underside of the leaves. As they feed, they cause the leaf to warp, wrinkle, and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Amɛhaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rain, even when they have big bunches of food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji niyenii babaoo yɛ po

english: Plantains often fall over because invisible worms called nematodes or stem borers have eaten away their roots underground. Without a deep, strong root anchor, the heavy fruit stem pulls the whole tree down when rain makes the soil soft.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ eye amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa bɛ tso lɛ yibii ni tsii lɛ gbalaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping all their flowers instead of producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the air gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get steady water. When the plant feels heat or drought stress, it drops its flowers to save energy so the main stem doesn't die.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Kɛ tsei nu dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ akagbo

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain stays on the farm for too long without draining away, the water fills all the air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing water rot fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to carry pollen from flower to flower before a pod can form. If the farm is too dry, lacks natural shade, or if strong chemicals have killed these tiny helper insects, the flowers drop without turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges, ni amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ dani pods baanyɛ afee. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo bɛ. Aloo, kɛji tsofai ni mli wa gbe nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛbuaa nɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my seed yams take several weeks to sprout out of the ground after I plant them in mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural sleeping period called dormancy after harvest. If you plant them while they are still in this resting phase, or if the soil mound is too hot and dry, the yam will wait until the conditions are right before pushing out leaves.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ wɔɔhe. Kɛji akɛ odu be mli ni ehi shi lolo, loo kɛji akɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ, Sweet potatoes baamɛ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa dani ekɛ baai lɛ baaje kpo.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or companion crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas until their branches grow thick enough to protect themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi amɛniji lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why does my maize turn weak and thin when weeds grow close around the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your crops. When weeds surround young maize, they drink up the food first, leaving the maize starving and struggling for light.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle ŋmãa bibii ahe lɛ Amɛbaanu amɛ niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha ŋmãa lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebɔi la he mɔdɛŋ.

english: Why are my harvested maize cobs light in weight instead of heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he waaa moŋ fe ni eeetsii lɛ?

english: Maize cobs become heavy when the plant gets enough nutrients and water during the grain-filling stage. If the plant lacks food or strength at this crucial time, the grains inside will not fill out completely, leaving the cob light.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛji tsei lɛ ná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo hewalɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa nɛɛ mli Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyimɔɔɔ kwraa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ.

english: How does food from the soil actually get into my corn to make the grains grow big?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ boteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli koni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Just like a mother converts nutrients into milk for her baby, a crop takes up nutrients through its roots and stem and pumps that energy straight into the cob to build thick, plump grains.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni nyɛ ko tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ mliki mli ehaa ebi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ni mli edɔ.

english: How can I ensure my corn cobs are full of heavy grains rather than soft or empty spaces?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii? Mohu ɔ, e ji he ko nɛ ngɛ blɛoo loo he ko nɛ e be nɔ́ ko.

english: Giving your crop adequate fertilizer and water right when the cobs start forming gives the plant the extra strength it needs to fill every kernel with starch, making the cobs solid and heavy.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo otsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni oha amɛ nu beni ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛfee lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ kroko ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii fɛɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni etsii.

english: How does feeding the soil help the crop produce bigger grains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmaa wuji?

english: Fertilizer feeds the roots, which act as the plant's engine. A well-fed root system pumps strength upward through the stalk directly into the growing grains, making them grow large and full.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ tsɔne. Shishifã ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa dumɔwu ni miida lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛyiɔ obɔ.

english: Is there a specific short period when my maize needs the most support to grow quickly?
ga: Be kuku ko yɛ. Nɛgbɛ ji he ni yelikɛbuamɔ he hiaa mi ŋmãa lɛ fe fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya?

english: Yes, there is a key window of about 10 days during the early cob-forming stage where proper water and nutrients make the biggest difference in helping the crop grow fast and strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, be ko ni he hiaa waa yɛ ni ji aaafee gbii 10 yɛ cob tsumaa be lɛ mli. No ji he ni nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa yɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhe wa lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to help my crops gain maximum strength?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛshɛ hewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ he?

english: Applying top-dress fertilizer right before and during the flowering and cobbing stage ensures the plant has maximum food available exactly when it is working hardest to produce grains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli dani ewo fɔfɔii kɛ be mli ni efoɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii waa fe fɛɛ koni ekɛwo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants need extra care right after they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Flowering marks the start of grain development. This is the period when the plant directs all its strength into feeding the cob, so any lack of nutrients or water during these days will reduce your final yield.
ga: Fɔfɔii ni shwereɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee. Enɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛlɛɔ ŋmei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nu ni bɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops look weak even though I planted good quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Good seeds carry the potential for a high yield, but they still require rich soil with enough strength and nutrients to feed the growing plant and nourish the crop to full size.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Shi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tsei ni miida lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia lɛ lolo.

english: What makes some maize cobs grow very large while others on the same farm stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa henɔi komɛi daa waa nɛkɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Cobs grow large when individual plants receive enough nutrients, sunlight, and water without competing with weeds or overcrowded neighboring plants during their critical growth period.
ga: Cob daa babaoo kɛ́ tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. ni ekɛ jwɛi akaŋ akaŋ loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ fe nine yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my maize plant has enough strength to support heavy ears of corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ abele toi ni tsii lɛ anɔ?

english: Healthy maize plants have thick, sturdy stems and deep green leaves. If the stalk is thin or the leaves are pale yellow, the plant lacks the strength needed to form heavy, full cobs.
ga: Abele tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse, ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli tseee loo baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmei ni tsii ni baa yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my neighbor's maize plants growing tall and deep green while mine on the same land stay short and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ji kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants turn yellow and stay stunted when the soil lacks nitrogen and essential nutrients. Your neighbor's soil might have more organic matter, fertilizer, or better rotation practices that feed the crops properly.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year when I keep planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen and life back into the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen kɛ wala aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bibii ni amɛhe tseee lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close to each other, their roots fight under the ground for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your main crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a heavy yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii titri lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a living umbrella that shields the young cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much moisture to the air. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛtoɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant hold onto flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants develop dark spots and turn yellow after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves, causing leaf spot disease. Trimming lower leaves and spreading dry grass or mulch on the ground prevents rainy soil from splashing onto the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. cause leaf spot disease Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ sũ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and chupons from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ tsei bibii krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted shoots and overcrowded branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the tree. This prevents fungal pod diseases like black pod and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni ataooo kɛ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa, ni akudɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do seeds I save from my last tomato harvest produce weaker crops than certified seeds from the office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee tomato kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni nitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often carry hidden diseases from previous seasons and lose their strength over time. Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to resist local diseases, germinate uniformly, and give higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. They act like natural fertilizer, feeding your maize and keeping the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Tall shade trees act like giant umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from harsh heat and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow big enough to handle direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo jwɛi lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it really necessary for me to use wooden stakes to support my growing yam vines?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ akɛ mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ atsu nii kɛfi miwein tsei ni miida lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for growth while keeping them away from damp soil diseases, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing small bunches even though the trees look tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ moŋ

english: When too many young suckers grow around the base of a mother plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main stem to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same plant family and share the same diseases and soil pests. Planting them consecutively in the same spot allows sleeping pests in the soil to immediately attack the new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ he kome yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do small green caterpillars appear inside the top leaf funnel of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miije kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched worms hide deep inside the soft leaf funnel to feed on the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: Flower dropping usually occurs when plants face heat stress, drought, or lack of water. The plant sheds flowers to preserve water and energy so that the rest of the plant survives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni bɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ koni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 8 to 12 months. Key signs include the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil swelling or cracking around the base of the stem as tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii hiɔ shi nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ. Okadii ni he hiaa lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the dirt if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the ground dries back out quickly, killing the newly germinated seeds before steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and can easily dry out or burn. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from direct sunlight while keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi loo amɛshã oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava too close to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that spreads its roots aggressively and absorbs a lot of water and nutrients from the soil. If planted too close, it will starve young cocoa trees of the food and water they need to grow strong.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa oya ni eŋɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip and moving down the middle in a V-shape usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for leaf growth. It can happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the dry, hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in heat is a survival mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excess water from evaporating from the plant tissue.
ga: Baai ni dɔlɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tsei amli fãji amli.

english: This is typically caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in overly shady, cool, and damp environments. Trimming extra tree branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry out moisture and protect the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni shade yɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to measure specific distances between my plantain suckers instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ masusu bɔ ni plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to yield big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ amɛhe koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee kui wuji.

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and will quickly steal soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all available resources to build strong stem structures.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei bibii lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ni amɛkɛmaa tso lɛ shishitoo ni wa.

english: Why should I rotate my land and avoid planting maize on the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains specific nutrients like nitrogen out of the soil and allows maize-specific pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to sow my maize seeds right after the first major rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need reliable moisture to soften their outer shells and germinate. Sowing right after the first major rain allows young seedlings to build deep roots before any brief dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛkwɛ̃. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are mature enough to be harvested for food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛha niyenii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, leaving a bare main stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open due to the expanding tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Shi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ni ehi shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ bulb ni mli elɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Shade trees protect the young seedlings from heat stress, help the soil stay moist, and create a cool climate for the plants to build strong roots during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni efee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip inwards even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbee mli kɛyaa mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil is short of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Rain alone cannot feed the plant if the soil lacks nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Nugbɔ pɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei niyenii kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts actually capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, restoring fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii? No hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. When applied to dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer sits against the roots and can actually scorch or burn them, damaging the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã loo ashã. ni baanyɛ afite tsei

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground if heavy rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the ground with water, it drives out oxygen from the soil. Cassava roots need oxygen to stay healthy, so flooded soil causes the tubers to suffocate and rot quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cassava shishifãi he miihia oxygen koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni amɛto tsei ahe tsei koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the growing underground tubers using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Koni akɛtsi baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination. When the flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward into small cups and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni eha tso lɛ akpa dalɛ

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from fresh leaves and transmitting viruses, which damages the leaf structure and stops growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I put four or five seeds in one hole instead of just two?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ beni mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli moŋ fe enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the plants compete fiercely with each other for space, light, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough resources to form full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná he ko, la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwu ko bɛ ni yɔɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo dumɔwu ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow together, they steal water and food from the main plant. Keeping only one main plant and one or two strong follow-up suckers ensures large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ suckers kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shwiili.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani anyɛɔ akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil fast due to heat and bruising, which accelerate decay and bacteria growth. Harvesting them early in the morning when temperatures are cool and packing them gently in ventilated plastic crates instead of heavy sacks keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ. ni haa fitemɔ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ yɛ leebi he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni okɛwo plastic adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli blɛoo yɛ kotokui ni tsii amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize cobs rotting while they are still standing on the stalks in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ miifite lɛ? Ani odamɔ toi ko nɔ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize rots on the stalk when rainwater gets trapped inside the husk leaves during heavy downpours. Bending the cobs downward (a practice called doubling) once the crop matures prevents rainwater from entering the husk until harvest day.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bote ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ ŋmei lɛ shii enyɔ) lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ ŋmei lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔɔ gbi lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from getting soft and rotting in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when exposed to damp ground, direct sunlight, or poor airflow. Storing them on raised bamboo shelves in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn prevents heat buildup and moisture damage.
ga: Sweet potato yibii fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛ tee hei ni efɔ, hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii atoohe ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why are wild animals destroying my young cassava plants, and how can I protect my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi miifite mi-cassava tsei lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Pests like grasscutters target young cassava because the fresh shoots are soft and sweet. Keeping a clean, weed-free perimeter around your farm border removes hiding spots for animals and makes physical barriers or deterrents far more effective.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ. Ni oooha kpokpaa lɛ he atse ni jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akafee nɔ ko Oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hei ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. ni eha gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii loo gbɛtsii nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungal infection that spreads in wet, dark, and damp conditions. Regular pruning of overhanging tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm floor and stop the fungal spores from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ fɔ́ kɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. ni etsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from severe heat stress, often combined with insect attacks like aphids. Light watering at the base of the plant early in the morning helps lower plant stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa lɛ fataa he lɛ, nu fioo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi leebi lɛ baaye abua ni eha haomɔ ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of a growing bunch during windstorms. Supporting the main stem with sturdy wooden or bamboo props (staking) gives the plant the physical stability it needs.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ (staking) lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa gbɔmɔtsoŋ shifimɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with large green leaves but producing very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive excessive nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, they direct all their energy into stem and leaf growth instead of flowering. Using balanced fertilizers rich in phosphorus encourages blooming and fruit development instead of leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli Hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ shishifã kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahe hewalɛ yɛ baai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when tiny insects like thrips feed on the delicate blossom joints, or when the plant experiences extreme heat. Controlling flower-eating pests early in the blooming stage allows the flowers to turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ye fɔfɔi lɛ ahe fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop seedlings after the first major rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in dry soil and germinate instantly with the first moisture, competing aggressively for nutrients. Early land preparation and weeding within the first three weeks of planting gives your young crops a head start.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. ni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehaa otsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay thin when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper spacing allows all of them to get enough nutrients to grow tall, green, and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara, amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant cover crops before putting my main food crops in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cover crops act like a natural blanket for your land. They block unwanted weeds, protect the soil from drying out under the hot sun, and add rich nutrients back into the dirt so your main crop grows much stronger.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛtsiɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni otso titri lɛ adara babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up during the hottest time of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural way of protecting itself from losing water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct heat, preserving moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni ahiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava take much longer to grow tubers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifã lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani edaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally slows down its growth when water is scarce to conserve its energy. Without sufficient soil moisture to move nutrients up from the roots, the plant enters a resting phase until the rains return.
ga: Cassava baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu bɛ ni baaha hewalɛ akafite. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baabote hejɔɔmɔ be mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do insect pests know when my crops are weak or suffering?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ leɔ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmiipiŋ?

english: When crops lack water or food, they release faint chemical scents into the air. Pests can smell these signals from far away and target weak crops because the plants are too stressed to defend themselves.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei bɛ nu loo niyenii Kɛji adu tso lɛ pɛ lɛ, ejieɔ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ fioo kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ anu okadii nɛɛ ahe kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ atswa amɛ ojo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ he miiwo wu tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ebu ehe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees scorch and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting taller crops like plantains near young cocoa provides living shade that cools the plant and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the lower leaves on my tomato bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing lower leaves allows fresh air to blow through the plant, which keeps fungal diseases away. It also forces the bush to spend its energy producing large, healthy tomatoes instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Enyɛɔ jwɛi lɛ hu anɔ koni amɛfite hewalɛ koni amɛkɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the leaves on top are bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil is packed too hard or contains too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of pushing deep into the earth to build thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ebaai lɛ akwɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ lɛ kɛ wo zugba a mi kɛ ya shɔŋŋ konɛ e pee bulb nɛ mi wa nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already naturally present in large numbers in the soil and are adapted to sprout instantly when exposed to rain and sun. Planted crops need extra care and time to establish roots before they can compete.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni abaanyɛ atsake koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ Tsei ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye akaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my previous harvest every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over many seasons gradually lose their strength and resistance to local diseases. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures your crops grow uniformly and produce high yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ be babaoo mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ ni baa shi kɛ helai ni teɔ shi ewoɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo daa be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of a deep green color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or because waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from breathing. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Nɔ titri ni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ji nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a wide open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the seedling and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ebaaha hɔɔŋ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your main crops can absorb them, effectively starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, drought, or irregular watering, which prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi akawo yibii.

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium, usually caused by irregular watering that prevents roots from taking up nutrients continuously.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa, ni haaa shishifãi lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Will trimming off some healthy leaves on my tomato plants help me get bigger fruits?
ga: Ani baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná aduawai wuji?

english: Yes, removing lower or overcrowded leaves helps the plant direct its water and nutrient energy into growing larger fruits rather than maintaining extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni dalɛ faaa loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ baai nɛ piɛɛ he ɔ kɛ to he.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines start curling up and getting brown spots in the middle of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive moisture creates high humidity, which promotes fungal diseases that attack and curl crop leaves. Proper spacing helps air flow through and dry the leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo baa. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest yield much less grain than the seeds I bought from the dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are special hybrids bred for high yields in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these strong parental traits and produce lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ babaoo ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ fɔlɔi asui ni mli wa nɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi.

english: Why do tiny beetles damage my harvested maize grains even when stored in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni aŋã mli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid on the grain while it is still drying in the field. They hatch inside storage unless the grain is properly dried and sealed in airtight bags or treated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmaa nɔ be mli ni egbi lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛfɔɔ yɛ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ mli ja agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo amɛ vacuum kotokui amli loo atsa amɛ.

english: What does cocoa rehabilitation actually mean for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kookoo ni anáa lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa rehabilitation means cutting down very old, diseased, or unproductive cocoa trees on your land and replacing them with new, fast-growing, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings so your farm can yield much more cocoa in the future.
ga: Kokoo ni aku sɛɛ akɛbaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaafolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni wooo yibii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni akɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni daa oya, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ awo amɛ najiaŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔ lɛ awo kookoo babaoo wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and the stems swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and yellowing leaves are signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Once a tree is infected, it stops producing properly and eventually dies, so it must be removed to protect neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji tso lɛ he hela lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo jogbaŋŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture to help young cocoa seedlings survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni eye ebua kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let in air and light, clearing weeds, and spraying approved fungicides will help protect your pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ mli, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛbaashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off excess branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can pass through. This keeps the tree dry, stops fungal diseases from spreading, and encourages the tree to send its nutrients into growing big, healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ Ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ ni ekanyaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amaje tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni mli wa lɛ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your cocoa leaves are pale, growth is slow, and trees produce very few small pods, the soil has likely run out of essential food. Applying approved cocoa fertilizer during the rainy season gives the trees the nutrients they need to yield more.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ ahe su etsake lɛ, edaa fiofio ni tso lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo, ni tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my cocoa tree without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers but can naturally only feed a fraction of them into full pods. However, heavy flower drop can also happen if the tree lacks water, suffers from insect attacks, or isn't getting properly pollinated.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, fɔfɔi fã ko pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kpluka ko emɔ lɛ loo afeee lɛ pollin jogbaŋŋ

english: Should I cut down all the large forest trees on my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: No, mature cocoa trees still require partial shade to protect them from extreme heat, keep the ground moist, and shelter them from strong winds. Leaving selected economic shade trees on the farm keeps the cocoa healthy.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulutsoo fioo lolo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baajɛ mli aba Shika helɛtemɔ he hulutsoo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni kookoo lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young seedlings have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep groundwater during dry weather. Without temporary shade, mulching around the roots, or regular watering, the dry wind strips moisture from their leaves until they dry out.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo bɛ lɛ, ha shishifãi lɛ loo nu lɛ nɔ daa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn deep orange. Harvesting at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully mature, rich, and easy to ferment.
ga: Pod lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa beni ehiɛ su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ waa. Nɛkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fã nɛɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ kwraa, ehiɛɔ shi, ni ehiɛɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees are getting too old to produce good pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees usually reach peak production between 10 to 20 years of age. After this period, trees naturally begin to produce fewer pods and become more vulnerable to diseases unless properly managed or replanted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛyibii babaoo he beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 lɛ. Yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi feemɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni helai baanyɛ aba enɔ oya. ja akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yield drops usually happen due to aging trees, soil nutrient depletion, poor rainfall, or hidden disease attacks that prevent the tree from feeding its pods properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ, loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haaa tso lɛ aná eshishifãi lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I cut down my old cocoa trees and plant new ones if they stop producing pods?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo cacao tso momo lɛ ni madu ehee kɛji cacao tso lɛ kpa ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Yes, if old trees consistently produce very low yields despite good care, replacing them with modern high-yielding hybrid seedlings will dramatically improve your harvest over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tso lɛ egbɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa be fɛɛ be kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ tsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can diseases on my farm cause my cocoa yields to keep dropping every year?
ga: Ani helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-cocoa ni mifeɔ lɛ aba shi afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Yes, progressive diseases like Black Pod disease or Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus weaken trees over successive seasons, causing a continuous decline in pod production if not controlled.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ni baa mɔ nɔ tamɔ black pod hela loo cocoa bud virus lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, pod feemɔ baaya nɔ aba shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ.

english: What are the common signs that my cocoa trees are sick?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Common signs include blackening or rotting pods, yellowing leaves, swollen branches, or small pods dying off rapidly before reaching maturity.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe ji ŋmeii ni etsɔ ediŋŋ loo amɛgboi, baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei niji ni efuu, loo ŋmeii bibii ni gboiɔ oya dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do small young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This can be caused by natural self-thinning (cherelle wilt) when the tree lacks energy, but excessive loss is usually caused by pest damage or early fungal attacks.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ ajɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ. (Cherel gboɔ) Kɛ́ tso ko bɛ hewalɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, nibii ni laajeɔ fe nine lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mra lɛ ahewɔ.

english: How often should I spray my cocoa farm to prevent diseases from ruining my pods?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akafite ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Fungicide spraying should generally start at the onset of the rainy season and be repeated every three to four weeks during high-risk months to protect growing pods.
ga: Esa akɛ aje tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashwiemɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli ni afee lɛ daa otsii 3-4 yɛ nyɔji ni oshara yɔɔ mli waa lɛ amli koni akɛbu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: How does a sudden change in rainfall patterns affect my cocoa production?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ saa bɔ ni mifeɔ kokoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Irregular rain or prolonged dry spells cause cocoa flowers to drop and young pods to wither, severely reducing the total crop yield for that season.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ ba shi kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need fertilizer if they have been growing fine in the same soil for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe hiaa ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo nɛ?

english: Over the years, cocoa trees pull essential nutrients out of the soil to produce pods; fertilizer restores those nutrients so the trees can maintain strong production.
ga: Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nakai niyenii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to prune my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ cacao tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in air and sunlight, which reduces humidity inside the farm and prevents disease-causing fungi from thriving on your pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni kɛ hela baa lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ o-pods lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields of maize every year even when I clear and weed it properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli moŋ.

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time you harvest them. If you plant the same crop repeatedly without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil runs out of food for the plants, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa amɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn the dry weeds and bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning grass destroys organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and soil organisms that keep the soil soft and rich. It leaves the ground dry and unable to hold rainwater effectively.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ ato jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main plant food responsible for making leaves green, healthy, and able to produce food for quick growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli, amɛhe wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara oya.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. They have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant there.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks so the roots get big?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni shishifãi wuji aba?

english: Planting cassava about one meter apart gives the roots enough space in the ground to expand without competing with nearby plants for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my maize seeds after the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply at least two or three times. Planting after the very first light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell immediately follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up, shrink, and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. They suck out the plant juices and spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haaa tsei adara lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young or exposed cocoa trees lose water quickly through their leaves under direct sunshine. Without shade trees to cover them, extreme heat causes the leaves to dry up, burn, and fall off to protect the trunk.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii loo ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ, amɛshãa, ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ yitso lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of holding fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai moŋ fe ni eeekpa aduawai.

english: How can I stop my plantain trees from falling over when they carry heavy bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi beni miwóɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle under heavy weight and strong winds. Mounding soil tightly around the base of the stem and supporting the plant with a branched wooden pole will hold it upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ muji ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni ooobɔle tso lɛ shishi shiŋŋ ni okɛ tsei ni akɛ tsei niji yɔɔ mli fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plant leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to reduce their surface area and save moisture. It is a natural defence against heat, but if the leaves stay rolled up in the cool morning, it may be a sign of pest attack or lack of water.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lolo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ebatutua loo nu bɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn light green or yellow after continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?
