english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, preventing plant roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients like nitrogen. When nitrogen cannot reach the leaves, they lose their deep green colour and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyiɔ. Etsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ́ nitrogen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Ebaaje eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Stress prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the flower to protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ oya tsɔ nɔ. Haomɔ tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four maize seeds in one single hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunshine. This competition makes all of them thin and weak, resulting in small ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ feɔ shwilafo ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is done, these roots decompose and leave free nitrogen in the soil, which helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu agbe naa Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yeɔ nii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look pale and yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ amɛ moŋ lɛ? Ani oooha nu daa gbi?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil has run out of essential plant nutrients, especially nitrogen, which helps plants stay green. Water alone is not enough; the soil needs plant food like well-rotted manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsei niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and put sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni mikɛ niji afata he koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to make big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the main stem starts to crack due to the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshwɛ tso ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ fũuɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What is causing the small holes and chewed edges on the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ ŋmei ni atsɔ mli lɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in the dry season to reduce the amount of water escaping from the tree. Planting shade trees around cocoa helps keep the farm cool and reduces this dry season leaf loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Tsei ni aduɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo yɛ Cocoa he lɛ haa ŋmɔji lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baa ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my vegetables grow better than planting in an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli?

english: A greenhouse is a light structure covered with clear plastic or net that protects crops from extreme heat, heavy rain, and destructive pests. It creates a controlled environment where vegetables like tomatoes and peppers grow faster, stay healthier, and yield higher-quality produce year-round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋloo ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Ehaa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ he ni aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni ofee nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do crops growing inside a greenhouse require much more daily care than my open-field crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi fe miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Plants inside a greenhouse rely entirely on you for water, ventilation, and food since natural rain is blocked out. Because heat and humidity build up quickly in an enclosed space, missing a few days of care can cause soil drying or disease outbreaks very fast.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ o-greenhouse lɛ damɔ onɔ kɛha nu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa amɛhe naa oya yɛ hei ni atswa amɛhe naa lɛ. Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya loo ekɛ hela ko aba.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when plants face heat stress, extreme sun, or lack of water and nutrients. When the air is too hot or the soil is too dry, the plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, hulu la ni naa wa, loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baawo yibii lɛ, amɛhaoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that feed on young leaves. It can also be caused by a plant virus carried by insects or by sudden changes in weather and water availability.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Tse mli helai ni koolooi hiɛɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa loo nu shihilɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow even though I am watering them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ waa daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns the roots by pushing out air from the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food. It also washes away essential nutrients like nitrogen, which the plant needs to keep its leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛbaajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye nii. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu.

english: Why should I use plastic crates instead of sacks or traditional woven baskets to transport my harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ plastic adekai atsu nii yɛ blema kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni akpɛ lɛ najiaŋ kɛwo tomato ni akpa lɛ mli?

english: Rigid plastic crates prevent vegetables at the bottom from getting crushed during transport, unlike soft sacks or rough baskets. Keeping fruit unbruised prevents quick rotting, preserves appearance, and allows you to demand higher prices from buyers.
ga: Plastic adekai ni wa tsiɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Etamɔɔɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo tsɛnsi ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ atsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ oya naa. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa obiɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables wilt so fast when I pick them in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ akpa amɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: During the hot afternoon, plants are actively losing moisture to the air to stay cool. Harvesting under full heat speeds up water loss in the picked crop, whereas harvesting in the cool early morning keeps the produce firm, crisp, and fresh much longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yeɔ emuu ni akpaa lɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahala lɛ amli lɛ yaa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ehee be babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact right stage to harvest my peppers so they stay fresh during a long journey to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ? Enɛ ji koni chili lɛ ahi shi ehee yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni akɛyaa jara lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Peppers should be harvested when they reach full size and firm texture, just as their color starts to change. Harvesting them slightly mature rather than fully soft allows them to ripen safely during transport without easily bruising or spoiling.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii beni amɛshɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee loo ni wa, beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ fioo moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛko kwraa lɛ, ehaa amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ ni amɛfiteee loo amɛfiteee.

english: Why does the selling price of my vegetables drop so low during the main harvesting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers in your area harvest and sell the exact same crop at the same time, the market gets flooded with more food than buyers need. When supply is higher than demand, prices drop, which is why out-of-season or greenhouse farming can yield higher profits.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpaa ŋmɔshi nii kome ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Niyenii babaoo baayi jara lɛ nɔ obɔ fe bɔ ni he hiaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ, jara baa shi, no hewɔ ni okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ be ni be lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen, a major food plants need for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea at the right growth stage helps the leaves regain their deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa shaded and moist while it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks to get big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ odu ŋmei kɛjɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni onine ashɛ bulbs wuji anɔ?

english: Cassava needs about one meter of space on all sides so the roots have enough room underground to swell into big tubers without competing with nearby plants for soil food.
ga: Cassava he miihia he ko ni miihe ashɛ mita 1 yɛ efãi fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ebɔi akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning light yellow even though it has been raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. Rain alone isn't enough; applying a nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure will restore the green color and help the maize grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli Nugbɔ pɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo organic fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plants experience stress, such as sudden hot dry spells or poor nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers until pepper fruits form.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ trukaa, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ waa. loo niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafee.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves coming out of the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni miijɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel. Catching them early and applying an approved insect spray or dropping clean wood ash into the funnel destroys the worms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize ears turn into fine dust inside my barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa toi ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ bibioo yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called grain weevils tunnel into stored maize to eat the inner part of the seeds. Properly drying the maize until it snaps easily and storing it in airtight bags or treating it with safe storage dust keeps the weevils out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa lɛ mli nibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaakumɔ oya, ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛto vacuum bag loo sũ ni akɛbuaa sũ naa lɛ mli shweshweeshwe koni ŋmãa lɛ akabote mli.

english: How can I tell if the farm chemicals I buy at the market are real and safe to use?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Genuine agrochemicals have sealed caps, clear expiration dates, legible English or local language labels, and official registration numbers from regulatory authorities. Buying from certified input dealers protects you from fake products.
ga: Agrokemikal diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tsitsii ni akɛfiɔ he. clear expiration date Woji ni akaneɔ mlɛo yɛ Blɔfo loo maŋ lɛ mli wiemɔ mli kɛ nɔmba ni aŋmalaa awoɔ wolo nɔ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ Hemɔ kɛjɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ amale nibii ahe.

english: Why is it better to buy fresh hybrid maize seed instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛ hybrid fee lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye kpami nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ mi.

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yields and uniform growth. Seeds saved from past harvests lose that special vigor, resulting in smaller plants and fewer cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛdara daa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛmli ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds come back so quickly right after I clear and burn my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mishã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping deep inside the soil for years. When you clear and burn the land, sunlight hits the exposed soil and triggers those hidden seeds to sprout immediately.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo. Kɛ́ ojie he ko ni oshã lɛ Hulu la lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture after the early rains to plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: Scoop up a handful of topsoil and squeeze it tightly. If it forms a ball that holds together but easily breaks apart when you touch it, the ground has enough moisture for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fioo ni okɛtswa shi shiŋŋ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he shi efoɔ oya kɛji ota he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small tool or your fingers, instead of waiting for tiny insects to do it. It guarantees that more flowers turn into pods, which can greatly increase your crop yield.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. loo onine Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni kooloi bibii afee nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi babaoo baatsɔ ŋmeii, ni baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do so many of my cocoa flowers fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo miiho ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop naturally within a day or two if insects do not pollinate them. Because natural insects are often few, many flowers go unpollinated and simply fall to the ground.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo bɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: Do I need special tools to do hand pollination on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná dɛŋdadei krɛdɛɛi ni mikɛ miniji aaawo mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: You can use basic tools like small tweezers, forceps, or even soft cushions made from palm fronds to hold delicate flower parts without damaging them, though simple careful hand techniques also work.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ tweezers bibii, pliers, loo kushin ni yɔɔ blɛoo po atsu nii. Akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fee koni akɛmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli ni efiteee amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ waaa moŋ, shi niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii.

english: Should I try hand pollination on my whole cocoa farm at once or start with just a small section?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maka nine ni mikɛwo kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ shikome loo mikɛ fã bibioo ko aje shishi?

english: It is best to start on a small portion of your farm first. This allows you to practice the technique, see the results with your own eyes, and manage your labor and expenses before expanding to the rest of the farm.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni oje shishi bibioo. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ Ehaa okɛ ŋaa gbɛi tsuɔ nii Naa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ kɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ohiŋmɛii. ni ekwɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shika nɔ dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli.

english: How do I decide which cocoa trees on my farm I should pollinate first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ cacao tsei ni esa akɛ mawo amɛmli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ahe?

english: Choose healthy, mature cocoa trees that produce many fresh flowers and receive good sunlight. Avoid sick, heavily shaded, or very old trees until you have restored their health with pruning and fertilizer.
ga: Halamɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni woɔ fɔfɔi heei babaoo ni hulu la kpakpa shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ hulutsoo waa, loo ni egbɔ waa lɛ ahe kɛyashi obaaha amɛhewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ nɔ.

english: What time of the day is best for pollinating cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji gbi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Early morning between 6:00 AM and 10:00 AM is the best time because cocoa flowers are fresh, open, and wet with pollen before the midday sun dries them out.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa ni yɔɔ leebi ŋmɛji 6:00 kɛyashi 10:00 teŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ehee, amɛgbele amɛhe, ni amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli dani hulu lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: How long does a successfully pollinated cocoa flower take to grow into a ripe pod?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi ni afee amɛ pollin yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda?

english: After successful pollination, it takes about 5 to 6 months for the flower to grow from a tiny green pod into a mature, ripe cocoa pod ready for harvest.
ga: Yɛ pollination ni ye omanye sɛɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli. Etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods turn black and dry up shortly after forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cocoa pods bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi beni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ.

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It happens when a tree has more pods than it can feed or lacks water and nutrients, so it naturally sacrifices smaller pods to keep the remaining ones alive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Ebaa kɛji tso ko yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaasha pod bibioo lɛ afɔle. koni eha pods ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi

english: Will my cocoa trees need extra fertilizer if I pollinate them by hand?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ baabi ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛji mikɛ minine wo amɛmli?

english: Yes, because hand pollination creates many more pods than usual, the tree works much harder to feed them all. Giving your trees adequate fertilizer and water keeps them healthy and prevents them from getting weak.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atsu nii waa koni amɛkwɛ amɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha otso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha egbɔjɔ.

english: Can I hand pollinate older cocoa trees, or does it only work on young ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ miniji awo kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ? Aloo ebaatsu nii yɛ kookoo tsei bibii pɛ anɔ?

english: Hand pollination works on trees of any age as long as they are flowering and healthy, but older trees usually produce better results if you prune them well and fertilize them beforehand.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni eye afii fɛɛ mli lɛ anɔ, kɛji amɛmiiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Shi tsei ni edara lɛ fɔɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji ofolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani be shɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and turning watery inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni nu miiho yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long during heavy rains. The excess water suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to attack and break them down.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛkpãtãa amɛhiɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade trees, like plantain or banana, to protect their tender leaves and retain soil moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Koni abu baai bibii ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat and dry conditions stress the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Yam plants grow as vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground allows them to catch maximum light to manufacture food, which helps the tuber beneath the ground grow large.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa tamɔ wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on the sap and spreading viral diseases that stunt leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli ni tsiɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people say planting beans alongside my maize will make the maize yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha mi-ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have natural bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plant.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Adebɔɔ mli helai yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: If I put fertilizer on my crop field without weeding first, will my crops grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔ mli ni migbeee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, because weeds have faster-growing roots than most crops and will absorb most of the fertilizer before your crops can reach it, making the weed problem even worse.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya fe tsei babaoo. Ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ he naagba lɛ mli woɔ wu.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain only wets the top layer of dirt, which dries out quickly. If seeds germinate without deeper moisture in the soil, the young sprouts will dry up and die under the hot sun.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ, ni egbiɔ oya kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my fertilizer to my maize field at the exact same time I plant the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young seeds cannot absorb a full load of fertilizer at once, and heavy rains can easily wash the unused nutrients away. Splitting the application feeds the crop gradually as it grows big enough to actually use the food.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwraa yɛ be kome mli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ oya. Nibimɔ mligbalamɔ yaa nɔ fiofio. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii beni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii diɛŋtsɛ akɛ niyenii.

english: Will putting extra chemical fertilizer on my land make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, crop roots can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients at a time, and applying too much chemical fertilizer can burn the roots, damage your soil, and waste your money.
ga: Dabi, tsei ashishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be kome mli. Ni tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ shika

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni miida lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient the plant needs to build green leaves and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce smaller cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up competing against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which prevents any of them from reaching full strength.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ni haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for all my seeds to be buried at the exact same depth in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds buried at the same depth get equal heat and moisture, allowing them to sprout at the same time so no early plants block sunlight or steal food from late starters.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ naa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. kwɛ̃ɔ dumɔwui yɛ be kome mli No hewɔ lɛ tsei komɛi bɛ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa loo amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishijee ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if the dirt stays completely dry after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to soften their outer shell and trigger growth; without water in the soil, the seed remains asleep or dries up and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha amɛdara. Kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi loo amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Should I spray my weedkiller chemical before or after my crop shoots come out of the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo beni amɛje kpo sɛɛ?

english: It depends on the chemical type: some sprays are made to stop weed seeds before your crop comes up, while spraying the wrong chemical after your crop sprouts can burn and kill your leaves.
ga: Enɛ damɔ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ: Afeɔ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ koni akɛkpa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛshwieɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite otso lɛ tsei lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my young seedlings much more than the older, bigger crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ tutuaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ babaoo fe mi tsei wuji lɛ?

english: Young shoots are soft, tender, and easy for insects to chew, whereas older plants develop tougher leaves and stronger natural defenses against pests.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ baai ni wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I break up the hard ground before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ mifo shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates air spaces and makes it easy for soft young roots to push deep down to find water and food during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni darako lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the ground, but beans and groundnuts put vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally, restoring nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Beans are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil through their roots. When the bean roots decompose after harvest, they leave that extra nitrogen behind to fertilize the next crop.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my bean plants climb and wrap around wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ kwɔɔ ni amɛbɔleɔ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Climbing bean varieties have soft, weak stems that cannot support heavy pods on their own. They naturally twist around support sticks to reach higher up for sunlight, which keeps their leaves healthy and prevents the pods from rotting on wet ground.
ga: Climbing bean henɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the flower buds dropping off my bean plants without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii komɛi efeee lɛ?

english: Beans drop their flowers when the plants experience extreme heat stress, dry soil during flowering, or insect attacks from pests like thrips that feed on the delicate blossoms.
ga: Peas lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: How can a new plant grow from just a piece of stem cutting without using any seeds?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso henɔ hee ko akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso kome ni afo lɛ mli ni akɛ dumɔwui tsuuu nii?

english: Stems contain hidden growth buds and natural plant hormones. When you place a healthy stem cutting into moist soil, those hormones tell the plant to sprout fresh roots from the buried nodes and leaves from the top nodes.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tso mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Beni okɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afo lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ. Nakai tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ lɛ kɛɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekwɛ shishifãi heei kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni afu lɛ amli, ni ebaajɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my stem cuttings turn soft and rot in the dirt instead of growing roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miniji lɛ ekomɛi yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shishifãi ni baakwɛ̃ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings rot when the soil is kept too wet, when the cut ends are infected with dirt bacteria, or when the stems were taken from weak, sick parent plants.
ga: Niji fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Beni muji mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ emɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ naa loo be mli ni ajie tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛjɛ tso nyɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hela mɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which part of the stem I cut when I want to plant cassava or yam cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo beni aduɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ?

english: Yes, mature and firm stems from the middle of a healthy plant work best. The soft green tips dry out too quickly, while the very tough bottom stems are too old to form new roots easily.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni eda, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni jɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tips ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ tsei ni wa waa lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee shishifãi heei mlɛo.

english: Why should I buy improved bean seeds from the research institute instead of saving seeds from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmei dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he ko moŋ fe ni mabua dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa?

english: Improved seeds from research institutes are carefully bred to resist common local diseases, survive short dry spells better, and yield more produce than old seeds that have weakened over many seasons.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ ekwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Amɛ nyɛɔ amɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni egbɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ bei babaoo mli

english: How do agricultural scientists create crop varieties that grow faster than our traditional crops?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya fe wɔ shishijee tsei lɛ?

english: Scientists look for wild or local plants with desirable traits, like fast growth or large pods, and cross-pollinate them over many plant generations to select and combine only the strongest features into one seed variety.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi taoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli loo tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni yɔɔ sui ni amɛsumɔɔ, tamɔ tsei ni daa oya loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii wuji. kɛ cross-pollination ni akɛ tsei ayinɔi babaoo feɔ lɛ koni akɛhala sui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ni akɛfee dumɔwu kome.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning light yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, excess water drowning the plant roots, or root pests preventing the crop from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together result in a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing all of them to stay small and produce fewer, smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like small tubes when the afternoon sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water when heat is high. It is the plant's natural way of reducing its surface area in the sun, showing that it is thirsty or trying to survive intense heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa ehiɛ shi kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye lɛ loo eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: When crops experience heat and lack of water, they get stressed and save their energy just to stay alive. Dropping flowers stops new peppers from forming when there is not enough water in the soil to feed them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kpe Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ. Fɔfɔi ni egbee shi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii heei ni baa lɛ anaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I pour water on them early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli yɛ leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb the water before the sun heats up. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the air, and wet leaves under hot sun can easily get scorched or diseased.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ni baai ni efɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo hela aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: If I use pipes and machines to pour water on my crops every day, will they grow faster than depending only on rain?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ paipii kɛ tsɔnei tsu nii kɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli nu daa gbi. Ani tsei baakwɛ̃ oya fe kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, giving your crops a steady supply of water prevents them from slowing down their growth during dry periods. However, you must be careful not to flood them, as roots need a balance of water and air in the soil to grow properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee mlɛo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni nu atsɔ amɛnɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni shishifãi lɛ aná nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I pour water directly on the stems of my crops or around the soil surrounding them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse nu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔle amɛhe? Ani shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji no?

english: It is best to water the soil around the plant where the root tips spread out. Pouring water directly onto the stem can cause the stem to rot, while watering the surrounding soil encourages the roots to grow wide and strong.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ nu. tso ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ eshwã Nu ni afɔseɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha egbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooshwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does water sit on top of my field for days instead of sinking down to feed my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote mli koni ekɛye mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Water stays on top when the soil is packed too tightly or has heavy clay that blocks water flow. Mixing organic matter like compost into the ground helps break up hard soil so water can easily reach the crop roots.
ga: Nu hiɔ ŋwɛi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa yɛ jɛmɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ sũ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa sũ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nu lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe oya.

english: Why do officers advise me to cover the soil around my crop stems with dry grass after watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu wo mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the hot sun so the water you poured does not dry up quickly, keeping your crops hydrated for longer.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu ni okɛshwieɔ mli lɛ akagbi oya. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted in the afternoon but stand up fresh again the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi eku esɛɛ eba kɛ hejɔɔmɔ enɔ jetsɛremɔ.

english: During the hot afternoon, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. At night, when the heat drops, the roots catch up and refill the leaves with water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. gbɛkɛ Beni latsaa lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baafata baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning yellow even though I am giving them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Too much water can fill up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they fail to take up plant food, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Nu babaoo baanyɛ ayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Be ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Enyɛŋ eye tsei niyenii. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my young crop seedlings are getting sick from too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ nu babaoo mli?

english: When seedlings get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow, feel soft or mushy, and the stem near the soil may turn dark and snap easily. Healthy seedlings need moist soil, not wet or muddy soil.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ani enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ? Ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee duŋ ni amɛkumɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ. Jeee ŋmɔtɔ loo muji

english: How do I know that my maize is completely ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can tell your maize is ready when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard. If you press a kernel with your thumbnail and it does not dent easily, the maize has reached full maturity and is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ o-corn lɛ efee klalo kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe. Cob lɛ egbi ni eyɛ asarasu. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛji okɛ ŋmei nyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni amɛkuuu oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: What happens if I leave my ripe maize on the farm for too long without harvesting it?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa?

english: Leaving ripe maize in the field exposes it to rain, insects, birds, and mold. The grains can start germinating on the cob or rotting, and pests like weevils will begin attacking the crop, leading to significant loss of yield and market value.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aba enɔ. Dumɔwui baanyɛ aje shishi akwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo amɛgboi. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii baabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii tutuamɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni afee lɛ kɛ jara ni jara wa lɛ fiteɔ babaoo.

english: Is it bad to harvest my maize when rain is falling?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ abaakpa ŋmãa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting during rain introduces unwanted moisture into the harvested cobs. High moisture encourages mold and fungal growth, which can ruin the grain quality and make it unsafe for human or animal consumption.
ga: Hɛɛ, nikpamɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni esaaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite omɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni eha efee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɔ loo kooloo niyenii.

english: Why do some farmers bend the maize stalks downwards before harvesting the cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Bending the maize cobs downward, often called doubling, prevents rainwater from collecting inside the husk while the grain finishes drying on the stalk. It also makes it harder for birds and pests to attack the ears.
ga: Ale ŋmãa ni akɛbaa shi lɛ hu akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛbaa shi shii enyɔ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa lɛ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa okpoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu akɛ amɛbaatutua toi lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to dry my harvested maize in the sun before putting it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Sun drying removes excess moisture from inside the maize kernels. If you bag maize that is still moist, mold and fungi will grow quickly inside the sack, generating heat and causing the entire bag of grain to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji oowo ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ Mold kɛ mildew daa oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni ehaa dumɔwui kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: How do tiny insects like weevils get into my stored maize, and how can I stop them?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Weevils often lay microscopic eggs on the maize while it is still in the farm, which hatch later in storage. You can prevent them by drying your grain thoroughly, cleaning your store room, and storing the maize in airtight hermetic bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmãa bibii bibii yɛ ŋmãa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Enɛ baafo koni akɛto sɛɛ mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni oooha egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he ni okɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo vacuum kotoku mli

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves before maturity usually indicate that your plants lack essential nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or NPK helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani edara lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will my maize grains keep growing or ripening if I cut down the stalk too early?
ga: Ani mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ baaya nɔ adara loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji mifo ŋmeii lɛ amli mra tsɔ?

english: No, once the stalk is cut down early, the plant stops supplying food and water to the cob. Harvesting too early results in shriveled, small kernels that produce less flour and spoil easily.
ga: Dabi, beni afo tso lɛ shishi mra lɛ. Tsei lɛ kpaɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmei lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii ni egbɔjɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi, ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete heavily with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows every individual plant to get enough light and food to grow strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring soil fertility naturally for your next crop season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees and plant them alone in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ ni mikome too midu amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains around young cocoa trees provides crucial shade and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ni aduɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the trunks of some of my cocoa trees swelling up and stopped producing good pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread between trees by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because there is no cure once a tree is infected, the swollen trees must be safely removed to protect the remaining healthy cocoa trees on your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, tsamɔ ko bɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie tsei ni efuu lɛ shweshweeshwe koni akɛbu kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my maize crop give me a huge harvest in the first year, but gives very small cobs if I plant maize on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi hu?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of these essential nutrients, leaving future plants weak unless you rotate the field with legumes or add compost and fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ayi obɔ fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Ja otsake ŋmeii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu komɛi. Ani akɛtee baai lɛ amli?

english: Your maize is being attacked by Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that eats the growing point of the plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical treatments early in the morning or late evening targets the pests while they feed.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ miitutua o-corn lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbaatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatswa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahiɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder with little insect holes a few months after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ etsɔ powda ni eyɛ kooloi bibii amli ŋmeii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack dried maize when moisture remains inside the kernels or when storage containers are not sealed. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun and using airtight storage bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ehi dumɔwui lɛ amli loo kɛ́ atsĩii nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ ogbala o-abele lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akajo foi ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, shrinking, and turning yellowish-green instead of growing broad and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using stem cuttings from healthy, disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this virus from taking over your crop.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni afo lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out thin and small when I plant several seed yams together on one small mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni mikɛ sweet potato dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ gɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When too many plants share a single mound, their roots compete heavily for light, nutrients, and room to spread. Giving each yam seed its own space and mound allows the tubers to grow larger and healthier.
ga: Kɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná la, niyenii kɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. He ni akɛhaa kɛ sweet potato dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi ni atoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my pepper and tomato plants turn yellow while the leaves at the top remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that excessive water is choking the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich compost or well-rotted manure around the plant helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever growing into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience heat stress and shed their blossoms to conserve water and energy. Providing light shade and consistent watering during hot spells helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help improve the soil for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to naturally fertilize whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei fɛɛ ni oya nɔ odu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them from high heat and preserve moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains grow rapidly and develop broad leaves that act like living umbrellas. They protect delicate young cocoa plants from sun scorch while providing you with food and quick income while waiting for cocoa to yield.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Amɛbuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize typically show a lack of nitrogen in the soil, or signify that heavy rains have waterlogged the roots, preventing the plant from drawing up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ amli ewo nu. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, uneven watering, or excess nitrogen fertilizer, which pushes the plant to grow leaves rather than nourish fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ tsirɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ koni amɛwo baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral infections spread by insects that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ kpaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell that can bake the soil and kill fragile germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rainfall pattern becomes regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa, ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ ashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ni waaa lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa.

english: What happens to my maize if I leave it standing in the farm for too long after it has matured?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature maize unharvested exposes the cobs to field pests like weevils, mold from sudden late rains, and rot, which ruins the quality and weight of your grain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaaa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ naa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli. kɛ fitemɔ Enɛ baafite dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready for harvest so they don't spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni no hewɔ lɛ amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is generally mature when the main leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. Leaving tubers in wet ground too long after maturity makes them woody, watery, and easy to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei, nu ni amɛbaafite oya.

english: Why should I buy new certified maize seeds every year instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the second generation, leading to uneven growth and much smaller yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines must climb high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to feed the root system. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees and plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei wuji kɛ plantains fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains or leaving shade trees creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ kookoo ni ji gbekɛ lolo yɛ shishijee mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava crops are fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem becomes firm. You can also carefully dig up one plant to check if the tubers are mature before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ baawa Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome hu ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base of the plants will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa ni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmãa ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce less maize if I plant it on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil, keeping your land fertile.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot, or when the plants receive irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni afɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow while ground cover from cowpeas keeps weeds away.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni tsina ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to grow strong leaves and produce large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the damp ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay free from fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ, ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my crops grow slow and weak when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni jwɛi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the planting season gives your crops full access to food and room to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii babaoo kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap beneath the leaves. Spraying your plants with neem oil extract or recommended bio-pesticides will help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch germinating seeds in the hot soil. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady before sowing your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: How long does it usually take for cassava to mature before I can harvest it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa ŋmei?

english: Cassava usually takes between 9 to 12 months to mature, depending on the variety. Harvesting too early results in small, watery roots, while waiting too long can make the roots woody and hard to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee tso ni eyeɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive quickly in local soils, so they consume water and light faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds in the first 4 to 6 weeks gives your young crop the chance to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi oya yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ nu kɛ la tsuɔ nii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat, which causes them to lose water quickly and dry up. Tall trees or shade crops like plantain protect the young cocoa until its own canopy develops.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni egbiɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ ŋwɛitsu.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce water loss. It is a natural defence mechanism, but if the soil stays dry for too long, the plant will stop growing and drop its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ Tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni efɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips, or viral infections they carry. These pests feed on the plant's sap, weakening it and stopping proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ baa. loo hela ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ hela Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why are there small holes chewed into the leaves and stems of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni mikɛyeɔ nii?

english: Holes in young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves of the plant. If left untreated, they can destroy the growing tip and stop the maize from producing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni amɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and thin but producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: When maize is planted too close together or lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, the plants fight each other for sunlight and food. This causes them to stretch upwards instead of putting energy into filling out big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baawo ŋmei ni da lɛ mli.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miishi mi-pepper tso lɛ ni pepper ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant receives too much or too little water, or when there are not enough nutrients in the soil to support fruit production.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing crooked and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to expand easily downwards. Hard, compacted soil or rocky ground blocks the growth of the tuber, causing it to bend and stay small.
