ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ tuber dalɛ naa. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo.

english: Will planting cowpea together with my cassava affect how my cassava grows?
ga: Ani cowpea ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baaná edalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cowpea actually helps cassava because it captures nitrogen from the air and feeds the soil. As long as you give them proper spacing, cowpea covers the soil to prevent weeds without disturbing cassava root development.
ga: Cowpeas yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Shii abɔ ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli bɔ ni sa. Akɛ muji woɔ tsina ŋmeii amli koni ebu he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe ni ekɛtsiii ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines. When you give them wooden stakes to climb, their leaves catch more sunlight and air, which helps the plant manufacture more food to build big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ oha mɔ ko tso ni ekɛkwɔ Amɛbaai lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as free natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni shwapoi lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for high yield, disease resistance, and strength. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time through cross-pollination in the field, making the next generation weaker.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai akamɔ amɛ, ni amɛhe wa. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛtsɔ cross-pollination ni yaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and dry winds. Without temporary shade crops like plantains, the intense heat dries out the leaves faster than the roots can suck up water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni niyenii baatsu kɛya shi koni ekɛdu ŋmeii lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers falling off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or dry because heat stresses the flower and prevents proper pollination. High heat or lack of water signals to the plant to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo edɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, latsaa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ, ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ ejie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and droop during the hot afternoon even if it rained yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ nyɛ moŋ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a defense mechanism crops use to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the burning sun, helping them save moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni akpɛ́ɔ lɛ ji hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green worms inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The parent moth lays eggs in the young maize shoot, and once caterpillars hatch, they hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on tender leaf tissue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ŋmei ni woɔ wui yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (rings) koni eye baai bibii lɛ amli fãji.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops so much even after I have applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive roots that steal water, light, and fertilizer faster than your crops can take them in, effectively starving your plants of the food you added.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni okɛwo mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs plant food before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni aye tsei niyenii dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Tired soil often looks pale or reddish, gets hard quickly when dry, drains water too fast or too slow, and produces weeds with pale yellow leaves. Healthy soil is usually darker, crumbly, and rich in decaying organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsuru. Ewaa oya kɛji egbi Okɛ nu lɛ afɔ oya loo blɛoo tsɔ. ni ekɛ jwɛi ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli ewo duŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nibii ni fiteɔ babaoo yɛ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to clear and prepare my land before the rainy season starts in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni misaa he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, land should be prepared during the dry months, usually between December and March, so that the soil is ready as soon as the main rains begin in April. Early preparation ensures seeds catch the early rain needed for fast germination.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa December kɛ March teŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo kɛji nugbɔ titri lɛ je shishi yɛ April mli pɛ. Hesaamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ naa nugbɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ oya koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Can I plant any crops during the dry season around December, or should I wait until the April rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nɔ ko yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni miihe ashɛ December lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi April nugbɔ lɛ aba?

english: Planting rain-fed crops in December is very risky because the soil lacks moisture during the Harmattan dry season. Unless you have access to river irrigation or a watering system, it is best to wait for the major rainy season in April.
ga: Nibii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ December mli lɛ adumɔ yɛ oshara waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Ja oyɛ faa mli nu loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he gbɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ yɛ April mli.

english: How do I know if my land is fully prepared and ready for planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Your land is ready when weeds and tree stumps are removed, the soil has been loosened up so roots can easily spread, and planting beds or rows are made right before the first reliable rains fall.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji ajie jwɛi kɛ tsei akutsei lɛ pɛ. Aŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. ni ofee shikpɔji loo dumɔwui akui dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Is it better to burn dried weeds on my farm or clear them without fire when preparing my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo majie jwɛi ni la bɛ mli beni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the farm or tilling them into the soil is better than burning. Burning destroys beneficial soil nutrients, whereas leaving organic material helps retain soil moisture during hot periods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo sũ ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ hi fe shãa. Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops die when the rains suddenly stop shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are short and stay near the surface. If rain stops suddenly, the hot sun rapidly dries out the top layer of soil, scorching fragile roots before they can grow deeper to find groundwater.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛbɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Eshãa shishifãi ni waaa lɛ dani amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: If it rains heavily just once in March, should I plant my seeds immediately?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa kome pɛ nɛ yɛ March mli Ani Esa akɛ Madu amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. A single early rain in March is often followed by a long dry spell, which will dry up the ground and kill young seeds that have just sprouted.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome yɛ March mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm if the weather changes and rains become unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake ni nugbɔ nɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by covering the soil with dried leaves or straw (mulching) to preserve moisture, planting drought-tolerant crop varieties, and staggering your planting dates so you don't lose all crops at once.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ni oookɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. ni okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ atsake bɔni afee ni akawo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ shikome.

english: What can I put on my farm soil to keep it cool and moist when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni eha edɔ ni edɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa?

english: You can cover the ground around your plants with dry grass, crop leftover stalks, or leaves. This practice, called mulching, acts like a shade cover that stops the sun from evaporating water out of the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha he ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ. tso loo baai ni eshwɛ lɛ Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism against heat and drought. By curling, the leaf presents less surface area to the sun, helping the plant save water and survive hot hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli.

english: Which crops grow best when the rainy season is short and unpredictable?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli?

english: Fast-maturing crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or early-maturing maize varieties work best during short rainy periods because they finish growing and yield fruit before the soil dries up.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli. Ejaakɛ edaa ni ewoɔ yibii dani shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs extra nutrients for my cocoa trees to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi koni cacao tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow slowly, produce yellowing leaves, or drop their flowers before forming pods, it usually means the soil is exhausted and needs fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ, no lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ, loo fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiikwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eje kpo ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: Yellowing leaves are a common sign that your cocoa tree is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that it is getting too much harsh sunlight without enough soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ he akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen miiye lɛ loo enine eshɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa nɔ tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, humid conditions when air cannot flow freely through overgrown cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ cacao tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: How does disease spread from one infected cocoa tree to healthy ones on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Diseases spread through rain splashes, wind, infected harvesting cutlasses, and pests carrying fungal spores from sick pods to healthy ones.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa nii ni hela emɔ mli lɛ anɔ. kɛ kooloi ni hiɛɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can a small disease outbreak kill my whole cocoa farm if I leave it untreated?
ga: Ani hela bibioo ko ni baa lɛ baanyɛ agbe mi-kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ?

english: Yes, common cocoa diseases like swollen shoot virus or black pod can spread rapidly across your entire farm over a few seasons if infected trees are not treated or removed early.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ bud swollen loo pod black virus baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ loo ajieee amɛ mra lɛ,.

english: Why is my old cocoa farm producing fewer pods now compared to seven years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii kpawo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce less as they age, especially if the soil loses nutrients over time or if minor diseases slowly weaken the trees over many years.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Aloo kɛ́ hela bibioo ko ha tso lɛ gbɔjɔ fiofio? afii babaoo nɛ

english: What causes my cocoa pods to grow much smaller than usual this season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Pods grow small when trees suffer from dry spells during flowering, or when sap-sucking insects like mirids weaken the tree's ability to feed the growing pods.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo be mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ iris lɛ, fite nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛhaa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off the tree without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by extreme heat, lack of rain, or insect attacks, causing the tree to save its energy by shedding blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo kooloi ni baatutua lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Ha tsei ato hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ

english: How does cutting off dead or extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Te niji ni egboi loo niji krokomɛi ni akɛfata he lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes useless branches that steal water and nutrients, allows sunshine to reach the trunk, and improves airflow to prevent disease.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that burn quickly in harsh sun; they need temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Look for 'sword suckers' which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base attached to the mother plant. These grow faster, stronger, and produce much bigger bunches than 'water suckers' which have broad leaves and weak bases.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛ tso nyɛ lɛ he. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya, amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji fe ‘suckers’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishi ni bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches producing very small fruits instead of large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa yɛ yibii wuji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Small bunches usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like potassium, or the tree is competing with too many extra suckers. Clear away excess suckers so only two or three grow with the main tree, and add compost or poultry manure to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium, loo tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni fata he lɛ miitswa akaŋ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ akwɛ̃ kɛfata tso titri lɛ he. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How long does it take for a plantain tree to produce fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tso woɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: In Ghana, a plantain tree typically takes between 11 to 15 months from the day you plant the sucker until the fruit bunch is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ gbi ni oduɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛkui lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How can I stop animals like cane rats from destroying my young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Clear a wide strip of land around the boundary of your farm to remove hiding places for rodents. You can also construct simple wire mesh fences around vulnerable beds or spray natural pepper solutions along the edges of the farm to repel them.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ he ko ni da ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ koni ojie hei ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ otswa waya ni akɛfee ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo hu obɔle he. saatso ni ŋmeii yɔɔ nɔ Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli pepper spray afɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni oshwie amɛ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to snap or fall over easily before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi mlɛo dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Trees fall over when stem borers or root nematodes weaken the root system underground. Clean your suckers properly before planting and heap rich soil and mulch around the base of the tree to build a deep, strong root foundation.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli loo shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsumɔ oshishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ dani odu ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ato he koni efee shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa.

english: Can I grow plantains together on the same field with oil palm trees?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ oil palm tsei?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantains with oil palms during the first three to four years. The plantains provide food and shade while the young oil palm trees develop, allowing you to earn income before the palm trees start fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu mu tso dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli. Plantains haa niyenii kɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni mu tsei hu kwɛ̃ɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika dani o-palm tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: How do I know when oil palm nuts are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akpa oil palm ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Oil palm bunches are ripe when their color changes to a bright reddish-orange and a few loose fruits naturally detach and fall to the ground beneath the tree.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji amɛhe su lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ekomɛi baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: What is the best way to prevent harvested palm nuts from spoiling before I extract the oil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani ajie mu lɛ?

english: Store harvested palm bunches in a dry, shaded place raised off the bare soil, and try to process the nuts into oil within two to three days after harvest to stop them from turning sour.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni egbi, ni shade yɔɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Ni bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfee fɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen or that the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage. Adding organic compost or poultry manure helps restore nitrogen and strengthens the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha baai lɛ afee hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to support heavy crops like plantain and oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ plantains kɛ oil palms?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged, and contains organic matter like decaying leaves and earthworms. If your soil is sandy or pale, mix in manure or cover crops to build up its fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã loo ŋmɔtɔ Futumɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full tropical sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing cassava about 1 meter apart gives the roots enough room under the soil to swell into large tubers without fighting neighboring plants for nutrients and water.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for healthy growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green growth and increases yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen can stress pepper plants, causing flowers to fall off prematurely. Consistent watering and partial shade during hot days helps set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha chili tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes plant leaves to evaporate water faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Adding mulch around the stem keeps the soil cool and retains water longer.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mulching around Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the hot sun and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds lower the amount of food my farm produces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa niyenii ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving your plants and lowering harvest yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ anɔ ni oha kpamɔ yibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are pests like fall armyworms that lay eggs on leafy crops. Inspecting plants early and applying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides prevents them from destroying the crop's growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai anɔ lɛ. Tsei amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my tomato plants while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji komɛi be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: Pruning extra side branches directs the plant's energy and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on excess stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ koni etsɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong green growth. Adding a balanced fertilizer helps restore their green color and healthy energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ni hi aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves, but the cassava tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much leaf-growing nutrient (nitrogen) or lacks space, it puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ niyenii babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli (nitrogen) loo he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I remove all the large trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantain to cover them, the intense sun burns their leaves and starves the plant.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni daa oya bɛ ni baaha nɔ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ hɔmɔ aba.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the heavy rains do not wash it away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ tsei lɛ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Covering the fertilizer slightly with soil keeps it in place near the roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is usually caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which often happens when the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked suddenly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, etsɔ nu trukaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my field before I plant maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts naturally capture good food from the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil later, the maize feeds on those leftover nutrients to yield bigger cobs.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts baamɔ niyenii kpakpa komɛi. kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmãa wuji.

english: What will happen to my maize if I put three or four seeds in one hole instead of spacing them out properly?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: When too many seeds are crowded in one hole, the plants fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. This struggle leaves all of them thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Ta nɛɛ haa amɛhe feɔ shoo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when there is plenty of rain during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively drink up the nutrients and water from the soil, starving your main crops underground even if rain is plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛnuɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ babaoo nɛ po.

english: Having too many shoots around one main plantain stem forces the parent plant to share its food with all of them, which leaves less energy to produce a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Plantain ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle tso titri kome he lɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ plantain lɛ fɛɛ agba niyenii. Enɛ baabi hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ koni akɛfee plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow well. When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil is low in nitrogen, so the plant is moving nutrients to its newer leaves.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa baai heei amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field help my maize grow better the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, soil that is too dry or too wet, or a lack of calcium in the soil during flowering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo efɔ tsɔ. loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark powdery dust inside the center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and dark waste (frass) are clear signs of pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender inner leaves of the maize plant.
ga: bu ni ekumɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli ewo duŋ Abɛi tsei (bulbs) ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworm caterpillars ni yeɔ abele tsei amli baai bibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rain pools around the base in poorly drained soil, creating damp conditions that allow fungal diseases to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa bua amɛhe naa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly into a ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or as a physical reaction by the plant to protect itself from excessive heat and water shortage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo eji nɔ ko ni tsei gbɔmɔtso lɛ feɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he?

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees or plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso loo plantain ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains provides temporary canopy shade and retains soil moisture while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ adumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward sunlight, allowing the plant to generate more energy to grow large, healthy tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ haa baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ kpeɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots coming out around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ he lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Removing extra shoots (suckers) prevents them from stealing food and water from the main mother plant, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my young oil palm seedlings dry out even when I water them on the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ po lɛ?

english: Oil palm roots grow deep quickly, so light surface watering only wets the top layer of soil without reaching the deep roots, causing the plant to dry out in heat.
ga: Mu tso shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshɛɛɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Tsei ni akɛ la miigbi

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from excessive heat and save water. By rolling up, less leaf area is exposed to the strong sun, which stops the plant from drying out too fast during hot periods.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛji okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa baashɛ Less leaf area lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crops are suffering from lack of water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miihe nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava plants show water stress by dropping their lower leaves and drooping their stem tips. If the leaves turn yellow and drop early, the plant is trying to save water to keep its underground tubers alive.
ga: Cassava tsei jieɔ nu he haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi oya Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miitao ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young vegetable plants wilt and fall over during the hottest part of the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme sun, young plants lose water through their leaves faster than their tender roots can suck it up from the soil. They usually bounce back in the evening when the heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baatsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfite nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. Under dense shade, the plant wastes all its energy stretching upwards to reach light instead of growing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Yɛ ŋmeii ni amɛaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my cowpea plants before they turn into full bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heavy heat stress, sudden dry spells, or insect damage. Without steady moisture and pest protection during flowering, the plant cannot support pod growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe bɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the sunlight so they can make food for the tuber below. It also keeps leaves off the wet soil, preventing diseases and rot.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa

english: Which fast-growing food crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting for cocoa trees to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain, cocoyam, maize, and cassava are ideal because they produce food within 3 to 12 months. Plantain and cocoyam also provide necessary shade to young cocoa seedlings while they grow.
ga: Plantain, cocoa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 12 mli. Plantain kɛ cocoa hu haa cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my green crops turn pale yellow right after heavy rains pass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen—the main plant nutrient responsible for dark green leaves—deeper into the soil where roots cannot reach. Adding compost or fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii titri ko ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli waa lɛ kɛyaa. Yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily underground for water and soil food. This competition leaves each plant weak and produces smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shi waa kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm help the next crop grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When harvested, they leave this natural fertilizer behind for future crops to use.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akpa Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ koni akɛtsu nii yɛ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves, showing that you need to apply nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he.

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop finishes, that stored nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive intense direct sunlight. Forest trees or tall crops like plantains act as umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from heat stress and keeping moisture in the soil during dry spells.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Koo mli tsei loo tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Will cutting off lower green leaves from my oil palm tree help it produce more palm fruit?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo palm yibii babaoo?

english: No, green leaves make the food that feeds the growing fruit bunches. Removing healthy green leaves starves the tree, so you should only trim leaves that are completely dead, dry, or blocking harvest.
ga: Dabi, baai eŋɔli ji niyenii ni haa aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni egboi kwraa, ni egbi, loo nɔ kroko ni tsiɔ kpamɔ lɛ naa lɛ pɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. When vines lie flat on the wet soil, leaves get shaded and rot from diseases, which leads to small, poor-quality tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaagbo kɛjɛ helai srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings suddenly from dry to wet. Covering the soil with straw mulch and watering regularly helps keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie nɔ ni akɛ nu shwie nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or suitable insecticides prevents insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite nii.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the young shoots grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Having too many shoots causes them to fight with the main tree for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots and keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Nibii ni shwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahi ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why do groundnut flowers push themselves down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally form their pods underground. After the flower is pollinated, the plant grows a long stem called a peg that pushes into the soil where the actual nut develops safely.
ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni ajie fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli he ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is August usually recommended as a good month for planting late-season crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ August yi akɛ eji nyɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: August falls within the minor rainy season in many southern areas, providing the right amount of rain and cooler soil for seeds to germinate without getting flooded.
ga: August ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo yɛ kooyigbɛ hei babaoo. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni nu shwieee amɛnɔ.

english: How does planting in July instead of August affect how my crops grow?
ga: Te dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ July mli yɛ August najiaŋ lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting in July allows crops to make the most of the early rains and build strong root systems before the drier periods set in, but it requires enough early rainfall so seeds do not dry out.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ July mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni etswaa shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa. Shi esa akɛ nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa mra bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do crops planted during the minor season need tighter planting schedules than major season crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ dumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa fe shishijee be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season is shorter and less predictable, so planting within a specific window ensures crops mature before the dry harmattan season begins.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ yɛ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ samflɛ ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛshɛ shweremɔ he dani harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ aje shishi.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them in late August and the rains stop early?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu yɛ August naagbee gbɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: If the rain stops early, crops planted late in August may suffer from water stress, leading to stunted growth, smaller harvests, or crop failure.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra lɛ Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ August naagbee gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ana nu he naagba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni kpamɔ fioo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why do farmers in coastal regions plant their crops earlier than those living further inland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔnaa hei lɛ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Coastal areas often experience slight changes in rainfall patterns due to ocean breezes and humidity, making July or early August the ideal time for coastal soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔnaa hei naa tsakemɔi fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋshɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo hewɔ. Enɛ haa July loo August shishijee feɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋshɔnaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do neighboring towns sometimes plant the exact same crop in different months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Local weather conditions, proximity to bodies of water, and differing soil types mean rain arrives at slightly different times even in nearby communities.
ga: maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ He ni bɛŋkɛ Nu jɛɛhei kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nugbɔ baa yɛ bei srɔtoi fioo amli. Yɛ akutsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po amli

english: How do I know if my coastal farm soil is ready for planting late-season crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋshɔnaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ naagbee be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Your soil is ready when it is consistently damp a few inches below the surface after early rains, showing it can support seed germination without drying out quickly.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ po yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi 2-3 inches yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ baanyɛ aye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ehaaa amɛgbi oya.

english: Is there a strictly fixed date in August when I must finish planting my crops?
ga: Ani gbi ko yɛ ni ato pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ August mli ni esa akɛ magbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adumɔ naa?

english: No, planting dates are flexible guidelines rather than strict rules. You should focus on current rainfall and soil dampness rather than a fixed calendar date.
ga: Dabi, gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ moŋ fe mlai ni mli wa. Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amrɔ nɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ moŋ fe kalanda gbii pɔtɛɛ.

english: Can I adjust my planting schedule if the rains start earlier or later than expected?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsake midumɔ be lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: Yes, farmers should adapt to actual rain patterns rather than set dates, planting when the rains consistently start to avoid loss.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi atsake amɛhe kɛya nugbɔshiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ nɔ moŋ fe gbii pɔtɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi ebaa daa koni nɔ ko akafite.

english: Should I follow my community's traditional planting months or rely strictly on modern calendar dates?
ga: Ani esa akɛ manyiɛ akutso lɛ mli bii akusum nifeemɔi amli nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ asɛɛ loo mikɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kalanda gbii lɛ atsu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Traditional planting months are based on generations of local climate observation, so combining local wisdom with modern weather forecasts gives the best results.
ga: Kusum nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ yinɔi ni kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli nilee kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he gbalɛi fata he lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the tubers to grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni edaa babaoo

english: How do groundnuts end up forming under the soil when the flowers grow above ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above the ground, the plant grows long stems called 'pegs' that bend down and push themselves deep into the soil, where the nuts safely develop underground.
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibii womɔ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Propping them up with strong wooden poles or building high soil mounds around the stem base gives them the support they need.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ loo kɛtsɔ gɔji ni kwɔlɔ ni amamɔ ebɔleɔ he lɛ nɔ. Trunk shishitoo lɛ baaha yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea restores their natural green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha e-ŋmei su ni ji adebɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable garden in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Midday heat causes applied water to evaporate quickly before roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch the plant. Watering early in the morning or late evening allows the roots to absorb the water properly.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots suffocate and rot when trapped in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Spraying the leaves early with neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Neem baai loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stem without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or poor pollination can cause tomato plants stress, leading flowers to fall off before fruit can form. Regular watering and providing light shade during extreme heat helps save the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa daa Loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf funnels of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibi lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender growth heart of the maize. Finding them early and applying wood ash or approved crop protection products directly into the funnels keeps them from destroying the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni dalɛ tsui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra kɛ tso sũ loo tsei ahebuu nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite tso lɛ.

english: Why do the young pods on my cocoa trees shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods shrivel due to black pod disease, nutrient competition, or lack of shade management. Pruning excess tree branches to improve airflow and applying recommended fungicides prevents this loss.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii loo hulutsoo be mli kwɛmɔ ni bɛ Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield pods only at specific times of the year instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to seasonal weather patterns in Ghana, such as rainfall and temperature changes, which naturally trigger flowering and pod development during specific main and minor crop seasons.
ga: Cocoa tsei tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii yɛ Ghana, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli shweremɔ be pɔtɛɛ mli.

english: What short-term crops can I plant to get food and money while waiting for seasonal crops like cocoa to produce?
ga: Mɛɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni maná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ kookoo lɛ koni amɛwo yibii?

english: You can plant quick-maturing crops like vegetables, maize, or legumes, which grow in a few months and provide continuous food and income during the cocoa off-season.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai, abele, loo ŋmãa. ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli ni ebaaha niyenii kɛ shika aya nɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: How does eating healthy crops grown on my farm help prevent sickness in my family?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni miyeɔ lɛ tsiɔ hela naa yɛ miweku lɛ mli?

english: Freshly harvested crops are rich in essential nutrients and vitamins that build your immune system, acting like natural medicine to keep your body strong against diseases.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛ vitamini ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ yaa hiɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ he waa kɛshiɔ helai srɔtoi.

english: Can I grow traditional medicinal herbs on the same land where I grow my food crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu maŋbii tsofai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, many traditional medicinal plants can be grown alongside food crops or along farm borders without interfering with your main crops' growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu blema tsofafeemɔ tsei babaoo yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe loo yɛ ŋmɔji husui ahe. ni ekɛ ehe wooo otsei titrii lɛ adalɛ mli

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color distinctly—green pods turn yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow—indicating that the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su jogbaŋŋ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives during rainy periods when moisture gets trapped around the trees without enough sunlight to dry it out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ebɔle ehe Tsei ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni haa amɛgbiɔ

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted branches lets air flow freely and allows sunlight to reach the tree, which lowers disease risk and directs the plant's energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do plantain trees help young cocoa seedlings grow better during their early stages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under harsh sunlight; plantain trees grow fast with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and roll up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water through high heat, helping the plant conserve internal moisture until it gets water again.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enine shɛɔ nu nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow faster and stronger in dark soil compared to dry, light-colored soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli tse lɛ he lɛ?

english: Dark soil contains decayed leaves and organic matter that hold moisture and supply essential plant food, acting as a natural food supply for growing crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei ni miida.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field with no big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to harsh direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees around them acts as a protective shield, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mango flowers fall off the tree before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebafeɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop off easily when the tree faces sudden dry spells, strong winds, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the trees well-watered and managing pests early helps flowers develop into full fruits.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuamɔ. Esa akɛ aha tso lɛ nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ mra. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: If I put a lot of fertilizer on my cassava plants, why do I get huge leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ baai shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava focus all its energy on growing tall stems and thick leaves above ground, leaving very little energy to develop thick, starch-filled roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ ekome ni ekwɛɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni akɛbaatsu shishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil. When the plant leaves decay, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso baai lɛ fite Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants developing ragged holes and yellow spots early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and early leaf yellowing are typical signs of pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the growing center of the plant. Catching this behavior early helps stop the insects before they destroy the whole farm yield.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tso lɛ he ni edaa lɛ he. Su nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa kooloi bibii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly turn brown and droop even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ trukaa ni egbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden drooping is often caused by fungal or bacterial wilt diseases living in the soil. The disease blocks the plant's internal tubes, preventing water from traveling up from the roots to the leaves even if the soil has water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal loo bacteria wilt ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa nɛɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa nu ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ anɔ, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu po.

english: Why do extension officers measure and force us to leave wide spaces between cocoa trees instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ sɔlemɔtsui ahe hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ wɔ nɔ koni wɔshi he ko ni da yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing allows air to flow freely between trees and ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients. When cocoa trees are crowded together, moisture gets trapped, creating a perfect environment for black pod disease to spread.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ, Moisture baamɔ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crops do not retain their strength in the second generation. Planting saved hybrid seeds will produce uneven plants, smaller cobs, and weaker crops that get attacked easily by pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi amɛhewalɛ mli yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ato ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee aba. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya.

english: Why do commercial buyers and export agents reject my tomatoes if they have small black spots on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nibii kɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ kpooɔ mi-tomato lɛ kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ? yɛ tomato lɛ shishi

english: Black spots on tomato bottoms are caused by calcium deficiency or irregular watering, known as blossom-end rot. International buyers and formal markets reject them because these spots shorten shelf life and cause the fruit to rot quickly in storage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Maŋsɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ kpoo lɛ ejaakɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ ashihilɛ be feɔ kuku, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop a white powdery mold while stored inside my warehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ná white powdery mildew be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Storing maize before it is completely dry traps excess moisture inside the storage bag. That damp environment encourages mold and dangerous toxins to grow, making the grain unsafe for human consumption or export.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmãa ni fa fe nine lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa kotoku lɛ mli. He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii loo kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ.

english: Why does rice need so much water on the field compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in flooded soil because their roots can still take in air through special channels in their stems. The standing water also acts as a natural barrier that stops common weeds from growing and stealing food from the rice.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ hu baanyɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛtsɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: How does breaking up hard soil with machinery help my crop grow better roots?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛgbalaa sũ ni wa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kpakpai aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard, packed soil acts like a wall that tender crop roots cannot push through. Loosening the soil creates air pockets, makes it easy for roots to spread deep to find water, and allows rainwater to sink down to root level.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa nugbɔ nu lɛ ni efoɔ kɛyashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: If I bury my seeds very deep into the soil, will they grow stronger roots?
ga: Kɛ mifu dumɔwu ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa Ani dumɔwu lɛ baakwɛ shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: No, seeds only carry a small package of energy to get started. If planted too deep, the shoot exhausts all its energy trying to reach sunlight and dies underground before it can sprout.
ga: Dabi, hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛjeɔ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ hulu la he ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani enyɛɔ edaa.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce tiny yields instead of healthy plants with full grains or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ e ngɛ wuhi loo yiblii tsuo.

english: Why do my crops planted under big shade trees stay small and produce little grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui fioo lɛ?

english: Crops use direct sunlight on their leaves to make their own food. Shade from large trees starves the crop of light, while the tree's massive roots absorb all the food and water from the soil around it.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai anɔ lɛ feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo lɛ haa hulu baaa. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the crop is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, which builds green leaf power. It can also happen when the roots are drowning in flooded soil without air.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baa eŋɔli lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I plant the exact same crop on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. It also allows pests and diseases that love that specific plant to stay in the soil and attack your new crop immediately.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa onibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal food and water faster than cultivated crops. They react quickly to any sunlight or moisture, which is why they must be cleared early so they do not choke your young crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii oya kɛji hulu la loo ŋmɔtɔ ba amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. Bɔni afee ni okafite oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why is heavy rain bad for my crops when they start to open flowers?
