ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ náa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers are how crops like rice and maize produce grains. Heavy rains wash away the fine pollen needed for grain formation or destroy delicate blossoms, leading to empty heads at harvest time.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji bɔ ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa woɔ dumɔwui. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni he hiaa kɛha dumɔwui afeemɔ loo efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ feɔ efolo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my tall rice plants fall flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, which happens when rice grows very tall and top-heavy with heavy grains. Strong winds, rain, or excess fertilizer can cause the stems to bend or snap under the weight.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ eda waa ni dumɔwui lɛ hu tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, nugbɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ loo amɛkumɔ yɛ muji lɛ shishi.

english: How do I know if my seedlings in the nursery are ready to be transplanted to the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Your seedlings are usually ready to move when they have developed 3 to 4 strong, true leaves and stand about finger-length tall. Moving them at this stage ensures their roots are tough enough to survive the move without dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, odumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ kroko kɛji amɛyɛ baai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji anɔkwale, ni amɛdamɔ shi aaafee inchi kome. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shimɔ lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo.

english: Is it better for me to plant crop seeds directly into the soil or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔi amɛ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Tiny or delicate seeds like tomatoes, peppers, and cabbage do best in a nursery where you can protect them from heavy rain and pests. Larger, tough seeds like maize, beans, and okra grow better when planted directly into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii loo ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kaabe hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui wuji ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ okra daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji adu amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds sprout within a few days while others take very long to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be kakadaŋŋ waa dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds sprout at different speeds based on their size, hardiness, and soil moisture. Good quality seeds planted at the right depth in warm, moist soil sprout quickly, while dry soil, buried seeds, or old seeds delay germination.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ bɔ ni amɛda ha lɛ naa. hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Dumɔwui kpakpai ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni afu loo dumɔwui momo baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough plants designed to survive harsh conditions. They absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why you must clear them early before they starve your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni ojie amɛ mra lɛ. Dani amɛbaagbe otsei bibii lɛ hɔmɔ

english: How can I tell if weeds are already harming my crop's growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ momo?

english: When weeds are stealing your crop's food and light, your plants will look thin and tall, their leaves may turn light green or yellow, and they will grow much slower than expected.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Otso lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ kakadaŋŋ. Ebaai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ eŋɔli loo wuɔfɔ. ni ebaada blɛoo kwraa fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray weed control chemicals on my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when there is no strong sun or wind. High heat causes the chemical to evaporate too fast, and wind blows it away from the target plants.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse ji leebi loo shwane mli. he ni hulu loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɛjɛɔ tso ni akɛmamɔ ehiɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow or burn after I apply liquid chemical fertilizer or pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efata he lɛ?

english: Leaf burning usually happens if the chemical mixture was made too strong, sprayed during the hottest part of the afternoon, or applied directly onto delicate young leaves without proper dilution with water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashãa baa kɛji tsofa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ. Okɛshwie nɔ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo okɛwo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ nu efɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long after I spray chemical on my crops should I hope it doesn't rain?
ga: Be enyiɛ eho kɛjɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Ani esa akɛ mahiɛ ahi nɔ akɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Most farm chemicals need about 2 to 4 hours of bright weather after application to enter the plant's leaves or soil. Heavy rain right after spraying washes the medicine away before it can work.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse ŋmɛlɛtswai 2 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni ebote tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaho tsofa lɛ dani etsu nii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Plants curl or droop their leaves in strong heat to protect themselves from losing too much water into the hot air. As long as they stand strong again by morning, it is normal crop behavior.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ yɛ latsaa be mli. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shi ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ. Eji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe subaŋ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer as soon as I put my seeds in the ground or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ ni mikɛwo mli loo mamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait until seeds sprout and grow their first true leaves—usually 1 to 2 weeks after planting. Seeds carry their own food to sprout, so fertilizer applied too early can burn tiny roots before they are ready to absorb nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛjie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ kpo—bei pii lɛ, otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Dumɔwui yeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii aba. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding manure or NPK fertilizer gives the crop the food it needs to regain its deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer. Planting them with maize enriches the soil and gives you two harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ aba kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly a day or two after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast when direct sunshine hits it. Covering the soil between your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the ground cool and traps moisture longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji hulu la shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ onibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ onibii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open on the farm right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikpaa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when they get a sudden surge of water after a hot dry period. Keeping a steady watering routine and mulching soil helps prevent the fruit skin from breaking.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be ko ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso yibii lɛ ahewolo lɛ akakumɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or soapy water keeps these pests away and lets leaves grow flat again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do insect pests swarm my cowpea crops the moment flowers start to show?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ bɔi kpojiemɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that attracts pests like thrips and pod borers. Protecting the crop with organic sprays just as flower buds appear keeps insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Kɛ́ okɛ organic spray tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ bu onibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite onibii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by harsh heat, dry weather, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Keeping overhead shade trees and controlling pests helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds when the bunch is getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni niji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Supporting the trunk with a strong forked wooden stick helps hold the weight so wind does not blow it down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ haa efeɔ tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa tso lɛ mli muji lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams start growing sprouts in the storage barn before the planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ be lɛ?

english: Seed yams sprout early when stored in hot, poorly ventilated places because warmth signals to the yam that it is time to grow. Keeping your yam barn shaded, cool, and well-ventilated delays sprouting until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, latsaa lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃. Kɛ o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ ato he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli. Ha eda fiofio. kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Feeding the soil with manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay green and fill out the maize ears properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or peanuts on my land make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays behind in the earth, feeding the maize crop that follows.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ baakã he ahi je lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and twisting into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etsɔ amɛhe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus carried by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and removing twisted plants stops the sickness from spreading to healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ ji vector. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra kɛ tsei ni efite lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam seed tubers rot underground before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot when planted in soil that holds too much water, or when cut seed pieces are planted fresh without drying first. Fungi in wet soil enter the cuts and destroy the seed before it can grow shoots.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni afo lɛ ehee ni agbiko amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and small fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young flowers and fruits when they get heat-stressed, when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly, or when tiny insect pests suck juice from the flower stalks.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii kɛji dɔlɛ ha amɛmiifee basaa. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli oya Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii miimu nu kɛjɛ fɔfɔi tsei amli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moisture in the soil while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: Why should I make my planting ridges across a sloped land instead of up and down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Ridges built across the slope act like small barriers that catch heavy rainwater. This prevents the rain from washing away your topsoil, fertilizer, and seeds down the hill during downpours.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛtsii nii bibioo ko. ni fiɔ nugbɔ nu ni naa wa sɛɛ Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ akafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow when left in the sun before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Cassava stems store moisture inside to sprout new shoots. When exposed to harsh direct sunlight, the stems dry out internally and lose the living energy needed to push out root shoots.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu yɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, tso lɛ mli tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛtsi tso lɛ shishi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their blossoms without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they feel stressed by drought, poor shade, or insect attacks like mirids (capsids). Keeping proper shade and protecting flowers from insects helps them turn into young cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hɔmɔ hao amɛ. ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ, tamɔ iris (capsid). Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain suckers turning yellow and drying up before the crop flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ lɛ?

english: Early leaf drying in plantains is usually caused by leaf spot fungi or roots standing in waterlogged soil. Clearing dry leaves and ensuring good water drainage keeps the plant healthy enough to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ plantains mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ mra lɛ ji leaf spot fungus loo shishifãi ni damɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni egbi lɛ amli gbalamɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ panicles babaoo baa.

english: Can I use the same spray or organic fertilizer on my coffee plants that I use on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kɔfi tsei anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ cacao tsei amli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, certain general sprays and organic fertilizers can be used on both cocoa and coffee because both are perennial tree crops with similar nutrient needs, though you must always check the right application rate for each specific crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi atsu nii yɛ kookoo kɛ kɔfe fɛɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni niyenii he hiamɔ nii tamɔ amɛhe. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii aha tso fɛɛ tso be fɛɛ be moŋ.

english: What does it actually mean when a farm treatment is labelled as organic certified?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ aŋmala tsofa ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ akɛ eji tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni aŋmala nɔ?

english: Organic certified means the input is made from natural materials and has been tested and officially approved to be safe for crops, soil, and humans without using harmful synthetic chemicals.
ga: Organic he odaseyeli tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii fee nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. ni aka lɛ akwɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ehi kɛha tsei, shikpɔŋ kɛ gbɔmɛi, ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why do farmers in my community use local names like 'zinc and cabbage' for crop chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi tamɔ ‘zinc kɛ cabbage’ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Farmers often create local nicknames based on packaging colors, pictures, or past results to make them easy to remember, but it is best to check the original bottle label with an extension officer to know the real chemical name.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ gbɛi krokomɛi woɔ amɛ akutso lɛ mli hei lɛ yɛ sui, mfonirii loo nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ni eho lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛhiɛ akai nɔ oya. Shi esa akɛ okɛ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛ shishijee niŋmaa ni yɔɔ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ole tsofa lɛ gbɛi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How do I know if a treatment is appropriate for a disease affecting my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko ni miigba mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ tsamɔ sa?

english: An appropriate treatment is one that specifically targets the exact pest or disease affecting your cocoa—such as black pod or capsids—without harming the tree, young leaves, or developing pods.
ga: Tsamɔ ni sa ji nɔ ni kɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela ni saa o-cocoo lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black pods loo capsids lɛ he. Eyeee tso lɛ, baai bibii lɛ, loo eshishifãi lɛ awui.

english: Why is it important to apply treatments to my cocoa farm quickly as soon as I notice a problem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai awo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya kɛji ana naagbai komɛi pɛ?

english: Fungal diseases and insect pests spread rapidly in cocoa farms due to shade and humidity, so acting quickly prevents infections from spreading to healthy surrounding trees.
ga: Fungal helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afee nɔ ko oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need micronutrients like zinc to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii bibii tamɔ zinc he hiaa mi-cacao tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Zinc helps cocoa trees build strong branches, produce chlorophyll for healthy green leaves, and support proper pod development during the flowering and fruiting stages.
ga: Zinc yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni enáa niji ni mli wa. Ehaa klorofil baa koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa pod lɛ shweremɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli.

english: Is there one single chemical that can cure all the different problems on my cocoa farm?
ga: Tsofa kome yɛ ni baanyɛ atsu naagbai babaoo ahe nii. Ani abaanyɛ afee enɛ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No single product can cure everything; while some organic treatments improve general health, specific problems like fungal black pod and insect pests like mirids require targeted treatments.
ga: Nɔ kome pɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai komɛi ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ, Shi naagbai pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii ni etsɔ diŋ ni jɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids lɛ amli lɛ biɔ tsofafeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Do coffee plants get sick from the same diseases that affect cocoa trees?
ga: Ani helai ni cacao tsei yeɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ miiye kɔfi tsei?

english: Coffee and cocoa share some general fungal issues and soil needs, but coffee also suffers from unique pests like the coffee berry borer that require specific control measures.
ga: Kɔfi kɛ kookoo kɛ naagbai ni kɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ he nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Shi kɔfe hu naa amanehulu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ srɔto, tamɔ kɔfe yibii fɔji. ni biɔ gbɛjianɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni akɛkudɔɔ lɛ

english: Will using certified organic inputs make my cocoa beans sell for a better price?
ga: Ani nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni aŋmala he odaseyeli akɛtsu nii lɛ baaha mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Yes, using certified organic inputs keeps your soil healthy and produces chemical-free beans, which allows you to sell to premium specialty buyers who pay extra for clean cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli ni aŋmala he odaseyeli akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eha kɔfi yibii ni tsofai bɛ mli lɛ aba. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ ohaa mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni jara wa waa ni woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛhaa kookoo ni he tse lɛ.

english: Should I apply crop treatments right after harvesting my cocoa pods?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe tsofai atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Applying protective sprays shortly after harvest helps heal the wounds on branches where pods were cut off, preventing fungi and insects from invading the trees during the recovery period.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ wo tsei niji ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsa pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei niji ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkatutua tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ shi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop needs fertilizer or if my soil is already rich enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii bɔ ni sa?

english: If leaf colors turn pale green or yellow, growth slows down, or your yield drops compared to previous seasons, your soil is short on nutrients. Testing the soil or showing leaf symptoms to an extension officer can help identify the exact fertilizer your farm needs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ahe su tsake kɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo Aloo onibii ni ofeɔ lɛ eba shi kɛ akɛto be ni eho lɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooka okwɛ loo baa lɛ he okadii ni ooojie lɛ kpo otsɔɔ extension nitsulɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ona ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that water is sitting at the roots for too long without draining. Applying the right nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving field drainage can help bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu ko ehi shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and produce less fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early and regularly ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni daa lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stems and a much lower total harvest than if the plants were given enough proper space to expand.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ hulu la he. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi fe he ni sa ni anáa kɛha tsei lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves get burnt and dry out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops cannot handle strong, direct sunlight without enough soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or using mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and protects tender young leaves from scorching.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo mulch ni aduɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai bibii lɛ shãaa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Adding mulch around the base of the plant helps keep moisture in the soil longer so the leaves stay firm.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ baai lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Does cutting off branches from my cocoa tree hurt it, or does it help it produce more?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Removing weak, dead, or crowded branches—called pruning—helps the tree by allowing sunlight and fresh air to reach the main stem. This reduces diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ebaaye ebua tso lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni eeeha eshɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers and small pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? dani eda

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers and young pods (known as cherelle wilt) when they lack water or soil nutrients, or when pests attack. Proper pruning and applying the correct fertilizer helps the tree retain its pods until harvest.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt) kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua lɛ Tso lɛ he tsemɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa tso lɛ.

english: Why do bugs keep coming back to attack my farm even after I spray chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛbatutua miŋmɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ

english: Insects return if chemicals are applied at the wrong time or at incorrect amounts, or if old infected pods and heavy weeds are left on the farm. Combining proper sanitation with scheduled spraying keeps pests away longer.
ga: Kplukai baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo yɛ bɔ ni esaaa mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii momo ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ jwɛi ni tsii eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hetsemɔ ni sa kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and cool conditions. Removing infected pods from the tree and pruning dense branches lets in sunlight to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei amli ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni afolɔ tsei aniji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la aba mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or struggling in waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or making sure water drains properly will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo eebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo akwɛ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my soya bean plants dropping their flowers before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani efee pods lɛ?

english: Soya beans drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, a lack of rain, or insect attacks during flowering, which prevents the crop from setting seeds.
ga: Soybean dumɔwui lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo kooloi tutua amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieee dumɔwui.

english: How do soya beans help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soy haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soya beans have tiny nodules on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Soybean lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why does maize grow better when I plant it where soya beans grew last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ he ni adu soybeans yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soya beans leave behind natural nutrients in the soil, which gives the next maize crop a quick growth boost and reduces your need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Soybeans shĩɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa oya. ni ebaa tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe hiamɔ shi

english: When maize plants are packed too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small, empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my chicken coop directly onto my growing crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ tsina shĩa lɛ mli lɛ afata miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and hot for tender crops and can burn their roots. It is best to let the manure dry and decompose for a few weeks before mixing it into your farm soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ashã Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to absorb water and soil food very quickly, whereas crop seeds need extra care and warm, prepared soil to get started.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛje shishi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei amli lɛ amli

english: This leaf damage is caused by caterpillars known as Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing funnel of the maize plant and chew on tender young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ afitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural protection trick crops use to shield themselves from harsh sunlight and trap moisture inside so they do not dry out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli koni amɛkagbi.

english: How do I know when my soya beans are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybean lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Soya beans are ready to harvest when the leaves dry up and fall off, the pods turn tan or brown, and you can hear the seeds rattling inside the pods when you shake the stem.
ga: Soybeans lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Pods lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. Ni obaanyɛ onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miitswa yɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ he kɛ́ otsi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa seedlings from excessive heat and holding moisture in the soil.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of a maize plant mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color, so adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaves and increases crop yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When rain saturates the soil without draining properly, air cannot reach the roots. This waterlogged soil allows fungi to grow quickly and rot cassava tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii daa oya ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the days get excessively hot or when plants face dry conditions. The heat causes severe stress to the plant, preventing proper pollination and making flowers drop off to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa loo beni tso lɛ yɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Dɔlɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to hold my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hia mi koni mikɛfi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to trap as much sunlight as possible with their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves dry and exposed to the sun, allowing the plant to make more food and develop larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects, such as aphids or mites, are feeding on the underside of the leaves. Treating the plants with organic neem spray or recommended pesticides helps clear the insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ he okadi. Ekɛ niyenii miiye yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji organic neem spray loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ tsu tso lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi lɛ ajie amɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow from one plantain stem, they fight over soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring the main stem produces big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ jɛ tso kome mli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shady environments. Pruning cocoa tree branches lets sunlight into the canopy and circulates fresh air, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kookoo tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my maize farm need so much water right when the flowers appear at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni fɔfɔii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: The moment maize produces tassels at the top, it is beginning to form grains on the cob. If the plant lacks water during this flowering period, cob growth stops, leading to missing kernels or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ gbá ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ baabɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ feemɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ Akpaa ŋmei lɛ dalɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni bɛ loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baa.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts store natural nitrogen from the air into their roots. When the plant harvest finishes, that stored nitrogen enriches the soil, feeding the next crop you plant in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpamɔ naa lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the direct sun, the leaves dry out and burn, which slows down the plant's growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaashã. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my plant leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is intense. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Shi ni ebɔle ehe koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off before growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but they drop excess flowers if the tree lacks enough water, nutrients, or proper insect pollination. The tree sheds what it cannot support so it can focus its strength on growing a smaller number of healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu ni sa, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kooloi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tso jieɔ nɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo ni baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce a huge harvest this year but very little the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ shi ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A very large harvest uses up almost all the energy and food stored inside the tree. The tree then needs a rest period during the next season to rebuild its strength and nutrients before it can produce heavy crops again.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo kɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni ato yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ekoŋŋ dani amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Heavy rains and high humidity create the perfect conditions for a fungal disease called Black Pod. Excess dampness and lack of airflow in the farm allow the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop look scorched and dry as if fire touched them when there was no fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbi, tamɔ la ni tswa amɛ be mli ni la bɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like mirids (Akate). They bite into the young shoots and leaves to feed, leaving toxic spots that cause the branches and leaves to dry up and look burned.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ nu, tamɔ mirids (akate) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai kɛha niyenii. Eshiɔ hei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa tsei niji kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: How does cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ni mi cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Extra or unwanted branches consume water and food that the tree could use to make pods. Pruning removes these useless branches, letting sunlight reach the tree trunk and directing all the plant's energy into growing bigger fruit.
ga: Niji ni fata he loo ni ataooo lɛ heɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛfee ŋmeii. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa nɛɛ. Ha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds growing around the base of my cocoa trees reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa cacao ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds act like hidden thieves in your farm; their roots aggressively steal water and fertilizer from the soil before your cocoa roots can reach them, leaving your cocoa trees hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kookoo shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye o-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is worn out and unable to feed my crops properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni enyɛɛɛ eha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Worn-out soil usually causes crops to grow very slowly, with leaves turning light green or yellow instead of deep green, and the plants producing smaller fruits or pods than usual.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo kwraa. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii loo ŋmeii ni baa shi fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight for the same small amount of soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or banana next to them provides shade and moisture to keep the young cocoa leaves cool and healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba koni eha kookoo baai bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop staying small and pale yellow even when I water it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow and stunted maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK will help the leaves turn dark green and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Spacing them properly gives the roots enough room under the ground to expand into large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the heat is too high or water is irregular. Watering your plants consistently at the base early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Catching them early and applying safe neem oil sprays or targeted control measures will protect the young crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai babaoo aba. Ni kɛ akɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe.

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Wait until the rain has soaked deep into the ground consistently for a few days. Planting after only the first short rain can cause seeds to germinate and then die if the dry weather returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into the soil. This enriches the land naturally, giving extra food to nearby maize plants without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ekɛ niyenii krokomɛi haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, shaded farms. Pruning overgrown cocoa branches lets sunlight and wind through, which dries the pods and reduces the spread of the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant the leftover seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ yɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests often produce weaker plants and lower yields over time. Using certified hybrid or fresh improved seeds ensures stronger resistance to pests and higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhaa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid loo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops the best chance to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni juɔ adebɔɔ mli hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani onibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do cocoa buyers reject my cocoa beans if they find dirty or moldy ones inside my sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ kpooɔ mi kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji amɛna kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Buyers inspect beans carefully because dirty or moldy beans contaminate the entire batch, ruining the flavor of chocolate and failing to meet the clean quality standards required for export.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii akui muu lɛ fɛɛ. Efiteɔ tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ ni eshɛɛɛ shishitoo mlai ni he tse ni he hiaa kɛha tsɔne ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ he.

english: Why must I clean my storage room and sacks thoroughly before putting my harvested maize inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ nitoohe lɛ kɛ kotokui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: Cleaning your storage space and sacks removes hidden insect eggs, dirt, and old mold spores that would otherwise spread onto your fresh grain and spoil your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ otsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ kɛ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ, ebaajie kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, muji, kɛ ŋmeii momo ni ekolɛ egbɛ eshwa oŋmaa hee lɛ mli lɛ. ni efite onitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear away old rotten cocoa pods from the farm ground before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni egboi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Rotten pods carry the Black Pod fungus. Leaving them on the ground allows rain droplets to splash the disease onto healthy leaves and pods, contaminating your new crop.
ga: Pods ni egboi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ blackpod tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni hoɔ lɛ ashwie hela nɔ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baafite onibii heei lɛ.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested cocoa beans on raised bamboo mats instead of directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying beans off the ground keeps them clean from soil dirt, animal waste, and groundwater dampness, allowing fresh air to flow around them so they dry evenly without molding.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ muji, kooloi ashishifãi, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli nu mli. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, kɔfi yibii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do the young leaves on my newly planted cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and lose water faster than their roots can take it in. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them protects their leaves from scorching heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa, ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape along the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape shows that the plant is starving for nitrogen. The maize is pulling nutrients from its lower leaves to keep growing, signaling that the soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Su ni tamɔ V ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi lɛ miigbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or severe dry weather. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with tiny roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They waste all their energy growing upward to reach the light instead of building large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: How does leaving harvested yam tubers exposed under direct sunlight damage them before market day?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ dani akɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Direct sunlight overheats the flesh of harvested yams, causing sunburn cracks and soft spots that allow rot bacteria to enter and spoil the tuber quickly.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ loo lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why do small holes in my cabbage leaves cause market women to offer me lower prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu lɛ ji bibioo lɛ? yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ, ni no haa yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi.

english: Holes mean insects have damaged the crop, which allows bacteria to enter and cause rot, reducing the shelf life and appearance that consumers demand.
ga: Bu tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ehaa shɛlɛf wala kɛ hiɛ su ni jarayelɔi sumɔɔ lɛ baa shi

english: How do I know if the soil on my new farmland is fertile enough for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa?

english: Dark, rich soil filled with decaying leaves and organic matter usually holds water well and has plenty of nutrients. If weeds and native plants on the land are growing dark green and bushy, it is a strong natural sign that the soil is healthy for maize.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni ehiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔji, Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young pepper plants droop and look weak during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon heat makes leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from dry soil. Drooping is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce heat exposure, showing that the soil needs more water or light shade to keep the plant strong.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa dɔlɛ ni baa shi lɛ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo hɔnɔ babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight each other underground for water, air, and plant food. This leaves you with small, thin tubers instead of large, healthy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmei shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni mli wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Can I plant beans on the same piece of land alongside my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe?

english: Yes, beans and maize grow very well together. Beans pull nitrogen from the air into the soil to feed the maize, while tall maize stalks give climbing bean vines a natural pole to grow on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli. Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Abɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bean wain tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tso ni akɛduɔ nii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant suffers from sudden water shortage. Heat and lack of moisture stress the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu ni faaa trukaa. Heat kɛ humidity ni bɛ haomɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii ni akɛtoɔ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale green and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors on your farm. They steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need, leaving your crops hungry, weak, and pale.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii lɛ amli. Shi onibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes are usually caused by tiny caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves. Checking under the leaves early in the morning helps you catch these pests before they eat the growing center of the cabbage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛye kaaba ni miida lɛ tsui lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same spot season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot completely drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abɛi lɛ mli lɛ baaho kwraa. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for my crop yield if I water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up moisture before the heat evaporates it. It also lets the leaves dry quickly in the sun, preventing leaf fungi and rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ hu ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why did many of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni adu lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were buried too deep in the dirt, if the soil was too dry for them to wake up, or if field insects and birds ate the seeds before they could grow roots.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ete shi. Aloo kooloi bibii kɛ loofɔji ni yɔɔ ŋa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛnáa shishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or gliricidia trees planted alongside them to act as natural sunshades until their roots grow deep enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo gliricidia tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advice me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and provides free food for the corn plants growing next to them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii yaka.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the soil when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects around them because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which feed on the tender growing core of corn plants. Identifying them early and applying organic or recommended sprays inside the leaf funnel keeps the plant's growing point healthy.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua ni ewo tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden dry spells. Keeping the root zone cool with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close to each other, won't I get a larger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and smaller yields. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce a heavy crop.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How does allowing weeds to grow in my farm slow down the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal essential plant food, water, and light. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ la ni he hia. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Staking yam vines spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight and protects the leaves from damp soil diseases. This allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛbu baa lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell that my maize is completely ready for harvest so it doesn't rot during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a dark spot appears at the base of the kernel where it meets the cob, showing that the grain has stopped taking in food.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni he diŋ ko jeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekpa niyenii yeli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily and can die under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have wide leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the cocoa until it grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and tall with tiny ears when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light, using up energy that should have gone into making big, healthy maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii koni ekɛfee ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases can rot them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ, ni helai baanyɛ ekɛba lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Ebaanyɛ egbo

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ he lɛ? Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ

english: All the young shoots, called suckers, share food and water from the same root system. Cutting away extra suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its nutrients into producing one large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii bibii. Jaa niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ shishifã kome mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. As the plant grows, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei dara lɛ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when it rains heavily for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves the soil flooded for a long time, air is blocked out, causing the roots to drown and decay underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ tsiɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot, the heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form seeds. The plant drops these useless flowers to save its water and energy.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ebɔ dumɔwui. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa nɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding deep inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the plant, and once hatched, the caterpillars crawl inside the funnel of young leaves because it is dark, safe from birds, and full of tender food.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ ji enɛɛmɛi. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ baai bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ duŋ, okpoi nyɛŋ afee amɛ shweshweeshwe, ni niyenii ni mli tse eyi mli obɔ.

english: Pepper leaves usually curl up when tiny insects like thrips or mites hide under the leaves and suck out the juices, or when insects pass a plant virus that deforms new growth.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites tee amɛhe amɛwo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmu nu lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tsɔ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ hee lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top remains green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. When food is low, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top, signaling that your soil needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ Tso lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, long dry spells, or too much water. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it can survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli. be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak heavy soil and trap water around cassava roots, cutting off air and allowing water molds to rot the tubers underground. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni bɔleɔ ŋmeii shishifãi ahe lɛ, ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy windstorms?
