ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay near the surface while carrying heavy, water-filled trunks and fruit clusters. Because their roots are not deep enough to anchor them, banking soil around the base and using wooden props prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ aduawai akui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha shishigbɛ lɛ he ni okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ shishigbɛ.

english: My cocoa trees have plenty of healthy green leaves, so why are they not producing many pods?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ ekɛ pods babaoo baaa lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees get too much shade or excessive nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight to hit the main trunk, which triggers flower and pod development.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Amɛbaakɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu baai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he nii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to survive tough local conditions and absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and food from your young crops.
ga: Adebɔɔ naa jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and gives crop-specific pests a permanent home. Alternating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil nutrients and breaks insect life cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni baahi shi daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot weather as a self-defense trick to reduce their exposed leaf surface and slow down water loss. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the roots cool and reduces leaf curling.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ebaa lɛ hiɛ shi ni ekɛ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ aba shi. Organic mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create a cool living umbrella, shielding delicate young cocoa trees from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Buu cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my watermelons turning black and rotten while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of watermelons is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Waterin the crop consistently helps the vine deliver calcium smoothly to the growing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ watermelon shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium baa tso yibii ni miida lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a main food crops need to stay healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight and high heat because their leaves and roots are still tender. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects them from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Ejaakɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ darako lolo Odumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ masɛi Enɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are caterpillars like the fall armyworm, which hide inside the growing center of maize plants to eat tender leaves. Catching them early and applying appropriate natural or chemical controls prevents them from destroying your entire harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni tamɔ cutworm ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets two or three good, heavy rains so the soil holds moisture deep down. Planting after just one light rainfall can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes back strong for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni naa wa waa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba kɛ hewalɛ gbii fioo komɛi krokomɛi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the cassava tubers and drowns them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni boteɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and put it back into the soil. This feeds the neighboring maize plants and keeps your land healthy for longer.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ aye nii ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weeds steal soil food, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing them while your crops are young ensures your plants get all the resources they need to start off strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to put long wooden poles next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akakwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking allows the leaves to gather energy from the sun, which directly helps the tuber underground grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛbuaa hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too severe or when the plant receives uneven amounts of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade trees nearby helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ ná nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from the maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures strong growth and a much bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do agricultural officers sometimes ask us to stop using certain crop chemicals we are already comfortable with?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ biɔ wɔ ni wɔkpa tsofai komɛi ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli ni wɔle momo lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, pests can build resistance to older chemicals, making them useless. Also, ongoing safety reviews reveal if certain chemicals harm the soil, beneficial insects, or human health long-term, requiring them to be replaced with safer and more effective alternatives.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atswa tsofai momo ni teɔ shi woɔ amɛ lɛ ama shi. making them useless Kɛfata he lɛ, shweshweeshwefeemɔ he niiamlitaomɔi ni yaa nɔ lɛ ejie lɛ kpo akɛ tsofai komɛi yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui. ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Aloo adesa hewalɛnamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ? Ebiɔ ni akɛ nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ato amɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to keep using the exact same pesticide every single season on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii daa afi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Using the same pesticide repeatedly allows the strongest insects to survive and reproduce. Over time, those insects build immunity to the chemical, rendering your spray ineffective and wasting your money.
ga: Tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Ehaa kooloi ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nakai kooloi lɛ náa hewalɛ ni tsiɔ tsofai lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa o-spray lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni eji oshika fitemɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops, like plantains, to act as umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the heat gets very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, which prevents proper pollination. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to conserve its energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and turn pale during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viruses transmitted by whiteflies. These pests multiply rapidly in warm, dry weather and suck the vital sap from young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ faa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli. ni ekɛ nu ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ shwieɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs high amounts of nitrogen to stay green, and heavy rains can easily wash this nutrient below the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛya he ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy bushes above ground but very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or excess water early on, the plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves instead of storing starch in its underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo nu babaoo nɔ mra lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmei baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do cowpea crops grow green and strong even when I do not apply chemical fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he moŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work together with natural bacteria in the soil. These bacteria take nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural plant food right at the roots.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tso adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant groundnuts or beans on the land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni wɔkpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize drains nitrogen from the soil, while beans and groundnuts put nitrogen back into it. Rotating these crops keeps the soil fertile naturally without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ lɛ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from agro-dealers instead of replanting seeds stored from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and often carry seed-borne diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially bred to germinate evenly, resist local diseases, and produce higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni bei pii lɛ amɛkɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa kɛjɛɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long or if the ground is too hard and compact. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the growing tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes keeps the leaves exposed to the sun and off the damp soil, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hulu lɛ nɔ, ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ hu shɛɛɛ he. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the trees are stressed by excessive heat, dry winds, or a lack of moisture. Planting shade trees nearby shields young cocoa from harsh afternoon sun and keeps the air humid enough for pods to set.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni pods lɛ anyɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and can get top-heavy if too many suckers grow around the main stem. Cutting away extra suckers and piling soil around the base of the main stem strengthens its root grip in the ground.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni tsii kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ato he. base of main trunk Ebaaha shishifãi ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ mli awa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again and supports grain growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does my groundnut crop need loose soil around the stems after it flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Tso lɛ tso lɛ beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant sends down peg-like stems into the dirt where the nuts actually grow. If the soil is hard and packed down, these pegs cannot push into the ground, and no groundnuts will form.
ga: Beni tso lɛ ekɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ peg tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni afɔɔɔ ŋmeii ko kwraa.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get tiny holes in them before the seeds inside are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Tiny holes are caused by pod borer insects that eat into the young pods to feed on the sweet seeds. Spraying the crop with natural neem tree extract or organic pesticides during flowering prevents these insects from laying eggs.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ koni amɛye dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso mli nu loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akawo amɛwui.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken spots on the bottom while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ shishi ni ebote mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your crop steadily so the soil stays evenly moist helps the plant move calcium smoothly to the growing fruit.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Nu ŋmɔshi nibii daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray keeps the new leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my young crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, keeping moisture from evaporating under the hot sun and preventing weeds from taking over. Over time, the grass rots and turns into rich natural food for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baafite ni ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: No, planting too close causes the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This results in tall, thin stalks with tiny cobs or no cobs at all. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli loo ŋmeii bɛ mli kwraa lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and drop off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds suck moisture out of plants quickly. Cocoa trees curl their leaves to hold onto water, but if the dry spell lasts long, they drop leaves to protect their main branches from drying out completely.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ahi mli. Shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu niji titrii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when I plant them too close to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has strong, wide roots that quickly absorb nutrients and water from the dirt. When planted too close, the cassava starves the maize of nitrogen, which is the nutrient maize needs to keep its leaves deep green and healthy.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛji adu Cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye lɛ kɛjɛ nitrogen mli. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers keep getting smaller every year on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava removes a large amount of food from the soil to form its tubers. If you plant it repeatedly in the same spot without adding manure or growing crops like beans that rebuild the soil, the ground loses its fertility and produces smaller yields.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji odu shii abɔ yɛ he kome ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni saa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi, ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and preventing fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi aduawai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf juices and spreading plant viruses. This weakens the plant so much that it cannot produce full-sized peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ waa aahu akɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ tomato ko baaa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of bees to pollinate the blooms. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and stay alive until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be kpe. Aloo ŋmeii ni baahã fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi wala mli kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough for growing groundnuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Groundnuts need loose, sandy soil because after the flowers are pollinated, they must push downward into the earth to grow nuts underground. Heavy clay soils are too hard for the pegs to penetrate, leading to low yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmei ejaakɛ kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollination sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ ashɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni pin nyɛŋ abote mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi

english: Why did some of my maize seeds fail to come up after I planted them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, or if ants and soil insects eat them before they sprout. Planting at the right depth after a good rain helps them come up evenly.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Removing those extra shoots, called suckers, forces the plant to send its water and nutrients directly to developing big fruits instead of wasting energy on useless extra branches.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yaa aduawai wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist, protecting the seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛŋmɛɔ hulu la naa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves spread high in the sunlight to produce energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sun and ventilation, which leads to bigger yam tubers and prevents leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo aba mli. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow and drying up from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-decomposed animal manure will help your plants regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii, loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize after these crops, the maize feeds on that leftover nitrogen, reducing your need for commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Kɛji odu ŋmãa taakɛ tsei nɛɛ tsɔɔ lɛ ŋmãa baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same spot rapidly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target maize to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cassava or legumes keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and strange caterpillar droppings in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack, a pest whose caterpillars hide in the central whorl of young maize plants to feed on new leaves. Early detection and spraying targeted pesticides or recommended bio-control methods directly into the center funnel of the leaves will protect your crop.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai heei. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ ni anaa mra ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Aloo, gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown, rot, and develop white dust on them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛshiɔ sũ yɛŋ yɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excessive wetness. Pruning shade trees and extra branches allows sunlight and wind to dry the farm, while picking off infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ tsei niji krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haaa hulu lɛ agbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does the soil around my garden vegetables dry out and crack so quickly even after I water it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very rapidly because heat from the sun evaporates the water directly from the ground. Spreading dry grass, straw, or leaves around the bases of your plants (mulching) shades the soil, keeps it cool, and holds moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai abɔle otsei lɛ ashishi (mulch) he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, eye ebua ni eha edɔ, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the first rainy day after a dry season means it is time to start planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi?

english: The very first light rain after a dry spell only dampens the top surface of the soil, which can cause seeds to sprout and then wither when hot days return. It is safer to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy, steady rains that wet the soil deep down before planting.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani aduɔ nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and tasteless when I harvest them late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei ni amɛbɛ ŋmɔlɔ beni mikpaa amɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are meant for storing starch, but if left in the ground past their ideal maturity age (usually 9 to 12 months depending on the variety), the plant converts the starch into tough wood fiber. Harvesting at the right age ensures the tubers remain soft and good for eating.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi toɔ starch. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛteke afii ni sa (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ), tso lɛ baatsake ŋmeii lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni wa. Nikpamɔ yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi bɔdɔɔ ni ehi kɛha niyeli.

english: Why did the chemical I sprayed on my farm fail to work even though I covered the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ hei fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ?

english: Chemicals can fail if they are applied at the wrong time (such as right before heavy rain), mixed with dirty or hard water, used at the wrong dosage, or if the pests have developed resistance to that specific product.
ga: Tsofai baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli (tamɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa) ni akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni wa futu mli. Kɛ yibɔ ni ejaaa atsu nii loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nakai tsofa lɛ

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so quickly on my land even after I spray herbicide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miidara oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can remain hidden underground for years; clearing or spraying the surface leaves buried seeds untouched, which then sprout as soon as sunlight and water reach them.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Kɛ́ afɔ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ anɔ loo afɔse nɔ lɛ, ehaa mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahe. ni baakwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la kɛ nu bashɛ shi pɛ.

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the farm turn a golden-yellow color and the lower leaves of the stems begin to turn brown.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does using a machine to harvest rice help me compared to doing it by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni akɛ niji kpaɔ lɛ he?

english: A harvesting machine cuts and threshes the rice much faster, reduces grain loss in the field, lowers labor costs, and ensures your crop reaches the market before weather damages it.
ga: Nikpalɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni eshwieɔ lɛ oya kwraa. Tsɔ dumɔwui ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shi Tsɔ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo shi ni oha nɔmimaa akɛ onibii lɛ baashɛ jara nɔ dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ afite amɛ.

english: Why does rice grow well in flooded water while my maize crops die if water sits on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu hi mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when trapped in flooded soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, which can be corrected by applying the right fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni abaanyɛ atsake kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa ni edaa lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer when my soil is dry or after rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist; if applied to dry soil, the nutrients cannot be absorbed by the roots, and if applied in heavy rain, the nutrients will be washed away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ akɛwo nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ, Nutrients lɛ hoɔ.

english: What is the difference between buying certified seeds and using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist diseases, mature faster, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over time and often yield fewer and smaller crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai, amɛshwere oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ni bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii bibii bibii

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get insects inside the bags while in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fite loo ŋmeii yɛ kotokui lɛ amli beni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage if they are bagged before drying properly, because moisture creates heat and humidity inside the bag, which attracts insects and promotes mold growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani agbi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo kɛ latsaa baa kotoku lɛ mli. ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and develop yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow spots are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies; planting disease-resistant stem varieties is the most effective way to prevent it.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni kɛ hela baa lɛ Adumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning brown in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to draw extra water. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the cocoa leaves from sunburn and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kroko kɛfata he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when we get continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When rainwater collects and sits in the ground without draining away, it suffocates the roots, causing fungal rot to set in underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni afuɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens to my crops if my watering system suddenly shuts off for a few days during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mi nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ kpa nitsumɔ trukaa gbii fioo komɛi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When water supply stops in hot weather, crops close the tiny pores on their leaves to save moisture, which halts their growth. If water cuts off during flowering, plants may drop their flowers to survive, reducing the harvest.
ga: Kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ kpa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaŋmɛ buji bibii lɛ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni baaha amɛdalɛ akpa lɛ ahi shi Kɛji nu bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Tsei baanyɛ agbee shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat combined with inconsistent soil moisture. Giving plants a steady supply of water helps them hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ fata he. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs water before the heat of the sun causes evaporation, and wet leaves dry quickly in daylight, preventing leaf fungus.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ baagbi oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni akafee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain bunches become small when many shoots grow out from the base of the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Pruning away excess suckers leaves more food and energy for the main plant to produce large plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo plantain tsei wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same spot on my land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize continuously in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth. Rotating with beans or cowpeas restores fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so leaves can catch maximum sun and stay free from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo, ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when I plant them in an open, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa creates a natural umbrella that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching until the trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need tall sticks so their leaves can spread out high in the sunlight to make food. When yam leaves catch maximum sunlight, the plant sends more energy down into the ground to build bigger, heavier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia amɛ niji ni kɛlɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Be mli ni sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base when the plants are knee-high restores their green color and boosts corn yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ebaakwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishitoo lɛ nɔ kwɔ aaafee tsitsi nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmãa yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain tree fight with the mother plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi babaoo ni ebɔle ehe Dumɔwu kome kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why does my maize crop yield so much better when I plant it on land where I grew groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed your next crop of maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmei lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmei ni obaakpa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding deep inside the middle leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ etee amɛhe amɛwo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which crawl deep into the central funnel of the plant to hide from predators and sunlight while eating the tender leaves. Applying targeted pest treatments directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning kills them before they destroy the growing plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ kɛ hulu la he be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ wo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛfite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like small cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ekpaa dalɛ hee?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites living underneath the leaves. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with mild neem oil or soapy water destroys these pests so the leaves can expand normally.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaakpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ. koni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft while still hanging on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when soil water levels jump from very dry to very wet. Giving tomato plants steady, regular watering and adding wood ash to the soil prevents this rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwere kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Tomato tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii daa Nu daa Ni tso sũ ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Once cassava roots are dug out of the soil, they react rapidly with oxygen in the air, causing them to spoil quickly. To keep them fresh, leave cassava unharvested in the ground until you are ready to sell or process them into gari immediately.
ga: Kɛji ajie ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, efiteɔ oya. koni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shimɔ ŋmei lɛ ni akpaaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo okɛtsu nii ni okɛfee curry ŋmei.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable garden during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering in the hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets on leaves can burn the plant. Watering early in the morning allows the soil to hold moisture so the crops stay hydrated all day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What causes some of my cocoa pods to look gnawed on and broken while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Squirrels, monkeys, and rodents chew through cocoa pods to reach the sweet pulp inside, leaving behind damaged, open pods that quickly rot and attract pests.
ga: Akpɔlɔi, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ kookoo ŋmeii koni amɛná ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni efite ni ajie lɛ kpo ni fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I see more wild animals biting into my cocoa pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa koo mli kooloi babaoo ni ŋmɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, water sources dry up, driving wild animals to seek moisture by biting into juicy cocoa pods and green crop tissues to stay hydrated.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Nu jɛɛhei lɛ baagbi. Wo koo mli kooloi hewalɛ ni amɛtao nu kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo nu kɛ tsei eŋɔli ni amɛyeɔ koni nu ahi amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up shortly after an animal bites them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ beni kooloo ko ŋmɔ mi lɛ?

english: Animal bites open wounds on the pod skin, allowing fungal spores like Black Pod disease to enter easily, destroy the beans, and rot the whole pod.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔɔ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ hewolo nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ baabote mli, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die suddenly after insects chew on their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni kooloi bibii eye amɛshishifãi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When pests chew into the stem tissue, they cut off the plant's water and nutrient pipelines, preventing food from reaching the roots and causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ amli lɛ Efoɔ tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ paipii lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa niyenii ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Will building a wooden fence around my farm keep animals from destroying my young cocoa trees?
ga: Tso gbogbo ni atswaa kɛbɔleɔ he Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baatsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkafite mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Fences stop large animals like goats or bush pigs, but small pests like squirrels and rats easily climb over or squeeze through, requiring extra traps or farm clearing to keep them away.
ga: Fɛnsi ni akɛbaakpa kooloi wuji tamɔ tooi loo koo mli tsinabii Shi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɔ loo amɛmimɔ amɛhe oya. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsɔnei krokomɛi atsu nii loo ajie ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkabote mli.

english: Should I use wooden sticks to support my young cocoa saplings when they start leaning?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fiɔ kookoo tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ mibɔi shwiemɔ?

english: Tying leaning saplings to supportive wooden stakes helps them develop straight stems and strong root systems, preventing them from snapping under heavy rain or wind.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni ja kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekakumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Can I plant tall barrier trees along my farm edge to protect my cocoa from heat and wind?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei kakadaji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni mikɛbu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he?

english: Planting tall windbreak trees around your farm borders creates a cooler microclimate and blocks harsh winds that can break branches and dry out young cocoa leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu tsei kakadaji ni ooodu yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ aba ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei aniji ni eha kookoo baai bibii lɛ agbi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat forces cocoa trees into survival mode, causing them to shed flowers and young pods to preserve water and guard their core health until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛbii bibii lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the branches of my cocoa trees snap so easily during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso niji fãa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Extended dry weather combined with stem-boring insects weakens the internal wood structure, making cocoa branches brittle and prone to snapping under the weight of pods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fataa he lɛ haa tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo niji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ efo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tsiimɔ hewɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drooping during sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Intense sun overheats the surface soil and dries out shallow roots, causing tender young plants to lose water faster than they can absorb it from the ground.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ egbiɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ejie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip when the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can feed its growing cob.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ beni tsei lɛ he hiaa nitrogen lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava stakes very close together, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil, which results in thin leaves and tiny roots. Spacing them about one meter apart gives each plant enough room to grow large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii baa. Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee mita kome, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi baa.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Mulching the soil and watering regularly during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their small roots can drink. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Akɛni amɛbaai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛduɔ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper leaves curl up during extreme heat to hide from the sun and reduce water loss. Watering early in the morning and putting dried grass around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and reduces leaf curling.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in the young leaves of my maize, and why is the leaf center covered in saw-dust-like powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa eyi baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot and chews on young leaves. Checking the farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract kills them before they ruin the cob.
ga: Cutworms ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã ŋmei lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my maize yield better when I plant it there next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant harvested, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground and acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but standing water blocks oxygen and causes soil bacteria to attack the roots. Planting cassava on mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers don't drown.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ naa, ni ehaa sũ mli helai tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni oyitso akabote nu mli

english: If I harvest good hybrid maize, why shouldn't I save those seeds to plant again next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa hybrid ŋmãa kpakpa Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to give a high yield only in the first generation. Saving and replanting seeds from that harvest causes the next generation to produce smaller cobs and uneven plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni abuɔ he ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for the ground to get thoroughly soaked by rain before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds need to absorb water to trigger germination and soften their hard outer shell. Planting in dry soil can cause the seeds to dry out, rot, or get eaten by insects before they have the chance to sprout.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aŋɔ nu koni eha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛha kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli awa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo koolooi aye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is good enough for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize crops need well-drained soil that does not hold stagnant water. If rainwater stays sitting on your land for days after rainfall, the roots of the maize will rot and the leaves will turn yellow because they cannot get air.
ga: Abɛi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi mli. Kɛji nugbɔ nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Abɛi lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ emu.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall stems with leaves but give me small tubers inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava grows in soil with too much nitrogen or under heavy shade, the plant puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɔɔ nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in severe heat to stop water from escaping. However, if the leaves remain yellow and curled in the early morning, it means sap-sucking insects like whiteflies have infected the crop with a virus.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu akajɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni amɛbɔle amɛhe leebi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ, kɛ hela nɛɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and wind into the farm, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience heat stress or lack water. Without enough soil moisture, the plant cannot support new fruits, so it drops the flowers to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ yibii heei lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell the right time to harvest my yams so they don't spoil quickly in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii? Bɔni afee ni ekafite oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ.

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. Harvesting too early leaves the tuber full of excess water, which makes it rot quickly after digging.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ayi ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ baaha egbo oya beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get tiny holes and turn into dust after a few weeks in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ sũ beni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ?

english: Weevils bore into stored maize to feed and lay eggs. If maize is not dried completely until the grains are very hard before storage, or if airtight sacks are not used, these insects will multiply rapidly.
ga: Weevils shwieɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani akɛto Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ vacuum bag tsuuu nii Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ faa oya.

english: What makes cassava roots go dark and turn bad just two days after I dig them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, harvested cassava has no protective skin, so air enters the damaged root right away and causes a natural breakdown that spoils the tuber within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, ŋmei ni akpa lɛ bɛ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shishifãi ni efite lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ baa, ni no fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Are there good crops I can grow that do not require heavy land clearing and digging?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu ni biɔ ni ajie ŋmɔji ni mli wa ni atsa?

english: Crops like cowpeas and vegetables can be grown using zero-tillage methods where you clear weeds with light cutting or mulch instead of digging deep ridges, making them easier to manage if you have physical limitations.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsɔ zero-tillage gbɛi anɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ aduawai. Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ooofolɔ loo jwɛi ni oookɛwo mli fioo lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ooofo ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsu he nii kɛji akɛ oyɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagbai.

english: How does covering the soil with dry leaves help my crops grow better with less work?
ga: Te baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ kɛ nitsumɔ fioo pɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, blocks sunlight so weeds cannot sprout easily and keeps soil moisture from evaporating, meaning you spend far less effort on weeding and watering.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Jwɛi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ mlɛo ni atsĩɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ jwɛi kɛ nu.

english: Why should I plant beans in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Beans are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When grown alongside maize, they act as a natural food supplier, helping the soil stay rich without buying expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii halɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How deep into the ground should I push my bean seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-beans lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Bean seeds should be planted about two to three centimeters deep. If you push them too far into the soil, the young plant will waste all its energy trying to push through the dirt and may die before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Kɛji otsi lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I grow crops on it every single year without letting it rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ daa afi ni mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Soil is like a human worker—if it works continuously without a break, it gets exhausted. Leaving the land to rest or planting green cover crops allows the soil to rebuild its strength and nutrients naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ nitsulɔ. Kɛji otsu nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ohe wooo mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does covering the soil with dried leaves help my crops survive hot days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots acts like a cool blanket over the dirt. It blocks the scorching sun, keeps the ground moist for much longer, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni mli ejɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant all my seeds on the very same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in small batches a week or two apart means your crops will mature at different times. This protects you from losing everything if a dry spell hits at a bad moment, and allows you to harvest continuously.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ kui bibii amli Otsi kome loo enyɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ baabu ohe koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akaje odɛŋ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko ba yɛ be ni ehiii mli. ni eye ebua bo ni okpa nii daa

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved will actually grow before planting them in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Wrap ten sample seeds in a wet cloth and keep it damp in a warm spot for a few days. If eight or more sprout shoot roots, your batch of seeds is strong and ready for field planting.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui nɔkwɛmɔnɔ 10 awo mama ni mli efɔ mli ni oshi amɛ ni amɛfee fɛ̃i yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛji shishifãi ekpaa loo nɔ ni fe nakai ekwɛ̃ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa shoots wither and die when the sun gets too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops lose water through their fresh leaves much faster than their tiny roots can pull it from the ground. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby to shield them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai heei anɔ fe shishifãi bibii. Hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa oya kwraa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ. Koni akɛbu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my plant leaves turn pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, which happens when the land has been farmed repeatedly without giving back food through compost or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tsei kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni baa kɛji atsu okwaayeli shii abɔ lɛ. Amɛyeee nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: When is the right time to feed fertilizer to my crops so the rain doesn't carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ lɛ akashwie shi?

english: Apply fertilizer when the ground is damp and the plant is actively growing, but not right before a heavy downpour. Putting it a few inches away from the stem allows roots to drink it safely without washing away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛto tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ he lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu shweshweeshwe ni amɛshwieee nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested beans turn moldy or get eaten by insects when stored in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ kɛ́ akɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans hold hidden water inside them after harvest. If they are not completely sun-dried until they are hard before storage, leftover moisture creates mold and attracts small pests that eat through the store.
ga: Beans kɛ nu toɔ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nii yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small worms eating the middle of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ye nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that attacks young maize. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they destroy your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and keeping the field free of weeds helps prevent the disease from spreading.
