ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Control Ni kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my pepper fruits turn black and rot at the tips before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is often blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular water. Keeping the soil moisture steady with regular watering or mulching helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo amɛnáa nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni sa.

english: Why do I need to make raised soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil so their roots can expand into big tubers. Mounding loosens tough soil, prevents water from collecting around the tubers and rotting them, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooobɔle he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ yitso he ni efiteɔ Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to plant if I want a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ ofolɔ ni odu kɛji oosumɔ ni owo yibii kpakpai?

english: It is best to use the mature middle section of a healthy stem, cut to about 20 to 30 centimeters long. Avoid the very soft top or the hard bottom, as the middle section sprouts faster and builds stronger roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ baatsu nii. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo waa loo shishi ni wa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaafee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed, stay healthy, and produce larger fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii. Ha ohe ajɔ bo ni owo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps make the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots in the soil. When you plant maize or vegetables in that same soil later, they use that stored food to grow bigger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, Amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ baatsu nii koni amɛdara ni amɛkɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is weak and needs fertilizer before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale yellowish leaves instead of deep green, or produced very small harvests despite getting rain, your soil is low in nutrients and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up and turning brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa creates living shade to protect them until they grow big and tough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka aba koni ebu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do I need to remove weeds early instead of waiting for my crops to grow big first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will steal water, fertilizer, and light from your young plants. Clearing weeds early in the first three to four weeks gives your crops the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ebaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green growth. When nitrogen in the soil gets low, the plant moves what little it has left from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a virus spread by those insects. As the sap is drained, the leaf loses its shape and twists.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ mliki lɛ ho lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings sharply between very dry and very wet. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed unpollinated blossoms to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Excessive leaves with few pods happen when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, often from using the wrong fertilizer. High nitrogen pushes the plant to focus on stem and leaf growth instead of putting energy into flowers and pods.
ga: Baai babaoo kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama shishifã kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ awo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: When planted too closely, maize stalks compete aggressively for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch tall to outgrow their neighbors for light, leaving very little energy to develop big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu Abɛi tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛdara fe amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ yɛ la taomɔ mli. Hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why should I cut off extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food directly from the main plantain mother tree. By keeping only one or two strong suckers and removing the rest, all the soil nutrients go into making a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine loo suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ojie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ. Nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔ plantain agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and turn brown when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot take up water fast enough to withstand harsh, direct heat. They require shade trees or plantains nearby to block excess sun and keep the air humid until their roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I lift them onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni miwoɔ amɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes all the yam leaves to maximum sunlight, which allows the leaves to manufacture more food through photosynthesis. This extra food travels down into the ground to feed and swell the growing tuber.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Niyenii ni fa nɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eyaye niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains flood the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, it pushes out all soil oxygen, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungi to attack and break them down.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants spreading out wide leaves instead of forming a tight, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miigbɛ baai babaoo eshwa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when temperatures are consistently too hot or when watering is irregular. Warm weather tells the plant to keep growing leafy foliage instead of wrapping its inner leaves tightly into a head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitso kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ be fɛɛ be loo kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛɛ tsei lɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛ baai lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ tsohi nɛ a ngɛ mi ɔ kɛ fɔ̃ɔ yi ɔ mi saminya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is highly concentrated, and touching the stem directly can cause chemical burns to tender plant tissues. Placing it a short distance away in a ring allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients as rain dissolves them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli babaoo ni kɛ́ ekɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofa ashã tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Ni akɛaawo ŋwɛi ŋta mli be kukuoo ko Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ shweshweeshwe beni nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their tender leaves dry out and burn. Leaving mature shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides the shelter and moisture young trees need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ aná wɔɔhe kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high toward sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and encouraging higher yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha yibii babaoo aba.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when water sits around the roots for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops each year if I grow on the same piece of land without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every crop season, plants draw vital nutrients out of the earth to grow. Planting continuously without resting the land or adding organic manure exhausts the soil's natural fertility over time.
ga: be fɛɛ be ni aduɔ nii lɛ Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeli?

english: Ragged holes in the center whorl of corn plants are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. Detecting them early allows you to apply recommended pest control before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ ahe ŋaa lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from crinkling and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress or sudden changes between dry soil and heavy watering. Mulching around the base keeps soil moisture steady and helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ waa lɛ teŋ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water. Pruning away weaker suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa dumɔwui wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crops on the extension demonstration farm yield so much better than the crops on my own land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Demonstration plots show the full potential of crops when precise seed spacing, correct fertilizer timing, and proper weeding are combined. Following these specific steps on your own farm instead of traditional methods will help you get similar high yields.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii aha kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ fata he. Be ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ jwɛi ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ Gbɛi pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ ni ooonyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli yɛ blema gbɛi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear and till my land deeply before I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Tilling loosens hard soil so young crop roots can easily spread and reach food and water deep underground, while clearing removes aggressive weeds that compete with young crops for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, won't I harvest more cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in weak plants with thin, small roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crops after the first rain falls in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu mitsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil stays consistently moist for several consecutive days after the initial rain. Planting after just one isolated rain leaves seeds vulnerable to drying out and dying if a sudden dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while I wait for them to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea early in the crop's life restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did the fertilizer I applied end up burning and killing my crops instead of helping them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ shãa baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is concentrated plant food. Placing it too close to the main stem or applying too much in dry soil sucks moisture out of the plant roots and burns them. Always apply fertilizer a few inches away from the stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Fertilizer ji tsei aniyenii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã shishifãi lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die as soon as the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out quickly under harsh sun and dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects them from the intense heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests every year even though I put in the same hard work on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mitsu nii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nakai nɔŋŋ po?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year exhausts specific nutrients in the soil. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, no baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing on the leaves of my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in crop leaves are typically caused by leaf-eating pests like caterpillars or beetles. Checking your farm early and regularly allows you to control these pests before they damage the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baai, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu baa tso baai amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni ooofee nakai daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni oye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when heavy rains leave standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water chokes the roots by cutting off oxygen, allowing fungal diseases to attack and rot the root system.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ha ni fungal helai atutua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why does my maize seem to grow fine on its own while other crops need extra plant medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi biɔ tsofa kroko ni akɛfataa he lɛ?

english: Maize is a tough crop with strong roots that naturally pulls nutrients from healthy soil quickly, whereas delicate crops like tomatoes or cabbages have soft stems and leaves that attract pests and diseases much more easily.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli wa ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato loo cabbage yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ helai oya.

english: What do people mean when they talk about giving 'medicine' to my farm crops?
ga: Mɛni gbɔmɛi tsɔɔ kɛ amɛmiiwie ‘tsofa’ ni akɛhaa mi okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he?

english: Plant medicines are special products like fertilizers that feed hungry crops to grow bigger, or pesticides that kill insects and sicknesses that attack your plants.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ ji nibii krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akɛhaa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara. loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni tutuaa otsei lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or that heavy rains have washed the plant food away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia oŋmɔshi nii lɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell the right amount of chemical medicine to mix for my crops so I don't damage them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? koni mikafite lɛ

english: Every chemical medicine has specific mixing rules based on the size of your sprayer tank; putting too much can burn the plant leaves, while putting too little will not kill the pests.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ mlai pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he, ni damɔ bɔ ni o-spray tanki lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo pɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why are some crop seeds covered in bright colored powder when I buy them from the dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni mli tse haa dumɔwui komɛi ahe beni miheɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: That colored coating is a protective medicine put on the seeds to stop insects and rot in the soil from eating them before they can sprout into healthy plants.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ji tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni kooloi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbo lɛ akaye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it dangerous for my health if I spray crop medicine without covering my mouth and nose?
ga: Ani ebaaye gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ awui loo ebaayeee mɔ awui? Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa shwie tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛhaaa onaabu kɛ ogɔŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, crop medicines contain strong chemicals that can make you sick if you breathe them in or get them on your skin, so you should always protect your body while applying them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa yɛ tsei amli tsofai amli ni baanyɛ aha oná hela kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ mu loo okɛ ohewolo kpe. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ obu ogbɔmɔtso lɛ he be fɛɛ be beni okɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Can putting too much chemical fertilizer on my maize hurt the crop instead of helping it grow?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer at once creates too much salt in the dirt, which burns the roots of the crop and causes the leaves to dry up and die.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ shãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes inside the center leaves of my growing maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa ni miida lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Those worms are called Fall Armyworms, which hatch from tiny eggs laid by moths on young maize leaves and feed on the soft growing parts of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. he ni ŋmei ŋmɛɔ ŋmei baa bibioo ko nɔ ni eyeɔ tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ahe nibii.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil food, causing them to stretch high for light instead of growing thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ la moŋ fe ni amɛaada kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know if a pest insect is actually damaging my crops or if it is harmless?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo eji nɔ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui?

english: Harmless insects usually just sit on the plant, while harmful pests leave visible signs like chewed leaves, holes in the stems, sticky liquid, or curling leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeee mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ tsei anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shiɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni atsɔ mli, bu yɛ tso lɛ shishi, nu ni shwieɔ shi, loo baai ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Why do my mango trees seem to pull so much water out of the ground during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ gbalaa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Mango trees have deep root systems and large leafy canopies that act like giant straws. In hot weather, water travels up from the soil through the trunk to cool the leaves and support fruit growth.
ga: Mango tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi wuji. yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha baai lɛ amli ajɔɔ ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How does water actually move from the soil up to the leaves at the top of a tree?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: Trees suck up water through their roots into tiny tubes in the wood. As water evaporates from the leaves into the air, it creates a continuous pull that brings fresh water and nutrients up from the roots to the topmost branches.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli kɛyaa paipii bibii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ amli. Beni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, Ekɛ ŋmiŋmi ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa ni egbalaa nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can pouring too much water around my mango tree end up damaging the roots?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ nu wo mango tso nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, overwatering can drown the roots by replacing the air in the soil with water. Without air, roots rot and can no longer draw up water or nutrients, causing the tree leaves to turn yellow and droop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu ni akɛbaatsake kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ wuɔfɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to water my fruit crops so the water doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mahã mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ nu koni mikafite nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because temperatures are cooler. This allows the roots time to absorb the soil moisture before the hot afternoon sun causes it to evaporate.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: How can I keep the moisture in the soil around my trees from drying out so fast?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni amɛkagbi oya?

english: You can place a layer of dry grass, crop leaves, or wood chips around the base of the tree trunk. This organic cover, called mulch, shades the soil from direct sunlight and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tso ŋmɔtɔ abɔle he. tso lɛ shishi Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo

english: Why do my tree leaves dry up and fall off when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: When water in the soil becomes scarce, the tree drops leaves to save moisture. With fewer leaves, the tree loses less water to the hot air, helping it survive until the rains return.
ga: Kɛ́ nu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shi. Beni baai lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baafite nu fioo kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my mango tree before they can turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mango tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by irregular watering, sudden heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping moisture levels steady while flowers form helps the tree hold onto them until fruit sets.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. hulutsoo trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi daa be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ yibii lɛ woɔ.

english: Will trimming some branches off my mango tree help it survive with less water?
ga: Ani mango niji lɛ ekomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua lɛ ni ehi shi kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, selective pruning reduces the total number of leaves on the tree. Since leaves let out water into the air, having fewer leaves means the roots need less water to keep the tree healthy during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ahala tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ jieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ he hiaa shishifãi lɛ koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: How do I know if my tree crop is getting enough water in the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: A healthy tree with enough water will have firm, bright green leaves and steady growth. If leaves wilt, roll inward, or turn brown at the edges, the tree is under water stress and needs moisture.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná baai ni mli edɔ. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ gboi ni amɛbɔle amɛhe kɛtee mli loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi ni ehe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ aba mli.

english: Why are my tree crops growing slowly even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: If water is available but growth is slow, the soil may lack essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus, or the soil may be too compacted for roots to expand and feed the plant properly.
ga: Kɛ́ nu yɛ lɛ, edalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo. Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus. Aloo, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas put natural food back into the soil through their roots, helping to refresh the land after heavy feeding crops like maize have used up the soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ beni tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ eye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.
